source_text:
Verse: O Prophet! Struggle against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be firm with them. Hell will be their home. What an evil destination!

Tafsir: O Prophet struggle against the disbelievers with the sword and the hypocrites with words and definitive arguments and be harsh with them through rebuke and aversion towards them; for their abode will be Hell an evil journey’s end an evil resort it is!

hype_questions: What are the consequences of being a disbeliever?
How should one deal with hypocrites?
What awaits those who reject faith?
propositions: Struggle against disbelievers and hypocrites.
Use sword and words to combat them.
Be firm and harsh towards them through rebuke and aversion.
Hell is their destination.
Their abode will be Hell.
It is an evil journey's end and evil resort.

source_text:
Verse: They swear by Allah that they never said anything ˹blasphemous˺, while they did in fact utter a blasphemy, lost faith after accepting Islam, and plotted what they could not carry out. It is only through resentment that they pay Allah and His Messenger back for enriching them out of His bounty! If they repent, it will be better for them. But if they turn away, Allah will torment them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no one on earth to protect or help them.

Tafsir: They the hypocrites swear by God that they said nothing of the defamation that has reached you as being from them; but they did indeed say the word of disbelief and did disbelieve after their submission to God they did indeed manifest disbelief after having manifested submission to God. And they purposed that which they never attained in the way of assassinating the Prophet on the night of al-‘Aqaba upon his return from Tabūk — there were about ten to twenty of them and ‘Ammār b. Yāsir struck the faces of their riding camels when they came against him and were thus repulsed; and they were only spiteful they detested that God and His Messenger should have enriched them of His bounty by way of spoils when they had been in dire need the meaning is that this was all that they attained from him which is nothing to be spiteful about. So if they repent of hypocrisy and believe in you it will be better for them; but if they turn away from belief God will chastise them with a painful chastisement in this world by having them killed and in the Hereafter in the Fire and they have none on earth as protector to guard them from Him or helper to defend them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject Allah after accepting Islam?
Can repentance save someone from the punishment of Allah?
How will Allah treat those who are spiteful towards Him and His Messenger?
propositions: They swore by Allah that they never said anything blasphemous, but they did in fact utter a blasphemy.
Those who lost faith after accepting Islam and plotted against the Prophet will be punished by Allah.
If someone repents of hypocrisy and believes in Allah, it is better for them; otherwise, Allah will chastise them with a painful punishment.

source_text:
Verse: And there are some who had made a vow to Allah: “If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity and be of the righteous.”

Tafsir: And some of them have made a covenant with God saying ‘If He gives us of His bounty we will give voluntary alms la-nassaddaqanna the original tā’ of natasaddaqanna has been assimilated with the sād and become of the righteous’ this was Tha‘laba b. Hātib who asked the Prophet s to supplicate on his behalf so that God would give him wealth of which he would give every needy person his due. He the Prophet thus supplicated for him and he became wealthy but stopped attending the Friday prayer and congregational prayers and refused to pay the alms-tax as God exalted be He says

hype_questions: What happens if someone makes a vow to Allah and fulfills it?
How does one become of the righteous through charity?
Can making a covenant with God guarantee wealth?
propositions: Some people made vows to Allah, promising to spend in charity if He gave them from His bounty.
Tha\u201claba b. H\u2013H\u2013tib made a covenant with God, asking Him to give him wealth so he could help the needy.
God exalted be He says that those who fulfill their vows and give charity are of the righteous.

source_text:
Verse: But when He gave them out of His bounty, they withheld it and turned away indifferently.

Tafsir: Yet when He gave them of His bounty they became niggardly with it and turned away from obedience to God in aversion.

hype_questions: What happens when we withhold blessings from others?
How does disobedience to God affect our relationship with Him?
Can we truly say that we are thankful for the blessings we receive?
propositions: God gives people blessings out of His bounty.
When people receive blessings, they often become niggardly and ungrateful.
Disobedience to God can lead to turning away from Him in aversion.

source_text:
Verse: So He caused hypocrisy to plague their hearts until the Day they will meet Him, for breaking their promise to Allah and for their lies.

Tafsir: So He made the consequence in their case hypocrisy fixed in their hearts until the day they meet Him that is God on the Day of Resurrection because they failed God in what they promised Him and because of that concerning which they lied he Tha‘laba then brought the payment of his alms to the Prophet s who said to him ‘God has forbidden me to accept it from you’; so he Tha‘laba began to throw earth on his head in remorse. He then approached Abū Bakr with it who did not accept it. He then went to ‘Umar b. al-Khattāb who also did not accept it. He went to ‘Uthmān b. ‘Affān but he did not accept it; he died during the latter’s reign.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who fails to fulfill their promise to Allah?
How does one show remorse for lying to Allah?
Can a person accept charity from the Prophet (s) after being told not to?
propositions: He caused hypocrisy to plague their hearts until the Day they will meet Him.
God has forbidden me to accept it from you.
The payment of his alms was brought to the Prophet (s).
Tha‘laba began to throw earth on his head in remorse.
Abū Bakr did not accept the payment of his alms.
'Umar b. al-Khattāb also did not accept it.
'Uthmān b. ‘Affān did not accept it either.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not know that Allah ˹fully˺ knows their ˹evil˺ thoughts and secret talks, and that Allah is the Knower of all unseen?

Tafsir: Did they the hypocrites not know that God knows their secret what they conceal within themselves and their confidential talks what they confide in each other and that God is the Knower of the hidden things? what is concealed from the eyes.

hype_questions: Does God not know our deepest secrets?
Can we truly hide anything from God's all-knowing eyes?
Is there something hidden from God that will be revealed in the end?
propositions: Allah knows their evil thoughts and secret talks.
God is the Knower of all unseen things.
There is nothing concealed from God's sight.

source_text:
Verse: ˹There are˺ those who slander ˹some of˺ the believers for donating liberally and mock others for giving only the little they can afford. Allah will throw their mockery back at them, and they will suffer a painful punishment.

Tafsir: When the verse concerning ‘voluntary alms’ Q. 975 was revealed a man came and gave a large amount as voluntary alms so the hypocrites said ‘He is merely showing off!’ Another man then came and gave a moderate measure of food and so they said ‘God has no need of this man’s charity!’ The following was then revealed Those who alladhīna is the subject find fault with defame the believers who offer alms voluntarily performing supererogation and such as find nothing to offer but their endeavours nothing but what they are capable of and offer it; and deride them and the predicate of the mentioned subject is the following — God Himself derides them He has requited them for their derision and theirs will be a painful chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens to those who mock believers for their charitable donations?
Why do hypocrites ridicule those who give generously to charity?
How does Allah respond to the mockery of believers who offer voluntary alms?
propositions: Those who slander believers for donating liberally and mock others for giving only what they can afford will be mocked by Allah.
God Himself derides those who find fault with believers who offer voluntary alms, performing supererogation.
The hypocrites' mockery of believers who give generously to charity will be requited by Allah, resulting in a painful chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It does not matter˺ whether you ˹O Prophet˺ pray for them to be forgiven or not. Even if you pray for their forgiveness seventy times, Allah will never forgive them. That is because they have lost faith in Allah and His Messenger. And Allah does not guide the rebellious people.

Tafsir: Ask forgiveness for them O Muhammad (s) or do not ask forgiveness for them this leaves the choice of asking forgiveness or refraining up to him; the Prophet s said ‘I have been given the choice and I made it’ meaning the choice to ask forgiveness as reported by al-Bukhārī. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times God will not forgive them it is said that the ‘seventy’ is intended to express by hyperbole a great frequency of asking forgiveness. In the Sahīh of al-Bukhārī there is a hadīth which states ‘If I was sure that were I to ask more than seventy times God would forgive them I would have done so’. It is also said however that the very number seventy is actually meant on account of this other hadīth of his ‘I shall ask more than seventy times’ whereupon it was made clear to him the Prophet that the matter regarding forgiveness had been concluded by the verse Q. 636 Alike it will be regarding them whether you ask forgiveness for them or you do not ask forgiveness for them God will not forgive them; that is because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger; and God does not guide the wicked folk.

hype_questions: Can asking forgiveness for someone guarantee their forgiveness?
What is the significance of praying seventy times for forgiveness?
How does faith in Allah and His Messenger affect one's chances of forgiveness?
propositions: It does not matter whether you pray for them to be forgiven or not.
Even if you pray for their forgiveness seventy times, Allah will never forgive them because they have lost faith in Allah and His Messenger.
God does not guide the rebellious people.

source_text:
Verse: Those ˹hypocrites˺ who remained behind rejoiced for doing so in defiance of the Messenger of Allah and hated ˹the prospect of˺ striving with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. They said ˹to one another˺, “Do not march forth in the heat.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “The Fire of Hell is far hotter!” If only they could comprehend!

Tafsir: Those who were left behind from the journey to Tabūk rejoiced at remaining behind the Messenger of God and were averse to striving with their wealth and their lives in the way of God. And they said that is they said to one another ‘Do not go forth do not set off to join the fight in the heat!’ Say ‘The fire of Hell is hotter than Tabūk and more worthy for them to guard against by not staying behind did they but understand’ this they would not have stayed behind.

topics: Striving in the cause of Allah
hype_questions: Would staying behind from a military campaign be a better option than risking one's life and wealth?
How does the Prophet's message compare to the prospect of physical hardship?
What would have happened if those who stayed behind had understood the gravity of their decision?
propositions: Those who remained behind rejoiced at not joining the military campaign.
They were averse to striving with their wealth and lives in the cause of Allah.
The Prophet warned that the Fire of Hell is hotter than Tabūk.
If only they could comprehend, they would have understood the gravity of their decision.

source_text:
Verse: So let them laugh a little—they will weep much as a reward for what they have committed.

Tafsir: But let them laugh a little in this world and weep much in the Hereafter as a requital for what they used to earn the sentence is predicative of their state expressed in the form of an imperative.

hype_questions: What will be the reward for those who laugh a little in this world?
How much will they weep in the Hereafter as a requital for their actions?
What is the sentence that awaits them due to their past earnings?
propositions: Let them laugh a little in this world.
They will weep much in the Hereafter as a requital for what they used to earn.
Their state is such that it deserves a certain punishment.

source_text:
Verse: If Allah returns you ˹O Prophet˺ to a group of them and they ask to go forth with you, say, “You will not ever go forth or fight an enemy along with me. You preferred to stay behind the first time, so stay with those ˹helpless˺ who remain behind.”

Tafsir: So if God brings you back from Tabūk to a party of them of those hypocrites who stayed behind in Medina and they ask leave of you to go forth with you on some other campaign say to them ‘You shall never more go forth with me and you shall never fight with me against an enemy. You were content to stay behind the first time so stay behind with those who stay behind’ away from military campaigns such as women and children and others.

hype_questions: Can a hypocrite ever be trusted to fight alongside the Prophet?
What is the significance of staying behind in Medina?
How does Allah's mercy apply to those who stay behind?
propositions: If Allah returns you to a group of them, they will not go forth with you.
You preferred to stay behind the first time, so stay with those who remain behind.
You shall never fight with me against an enemy.

source_text:
Verse: And do not ever offer ˹funeral˺ prayers for any of their dead, nor stand by their grave ˹at burial˺, for they have lost faith in Allah and His Messenger and died rebellious.

Tafsir: When the Prophet s prayed over the dead body of ‘Abd Allāh Ibn Ubayy the following was revealed And never pray over any one of them when he is dead nor stand over his grave at a burial or as a visit; lo! they disbelieved in God and His Messenger and died while they were wicked they died disbelieving.

hype_questions: What happens when someone dies in a state of disbelief?
Can we offer prayers for the deceased, and is it permissible to visit their graves?
How does one's faith affect their fate after death?
propositions: It is not permissible to offer funeral prayers for anyone who has died in a state of disbelief.
Standing by someone's grave during burial or as a visit is also forbidden.
Those who die in a state of disbelief will be punished for their wickedness.

source_text:
Verse: And let neither their wealth nor children impress you ˹O Prophet˺. Allah only intends to torment them through these things in this world, and ˹then˺ their souls will depart while they are disbelievers.

Tafsir: And let not their wealth and their children please you; God desires only to chastise them thereby in this world and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.

hype_questions: What happens to those who prioritize material wealth over their faith?
How does Allah's chastisement manifest in the lives of disbelievers?
Can children or wealth ever bring a person closer to God?
propositions: Allah only intends to torment individuals through their wealth and children in this world.
The souls of disbelievers depart while they are still living.
Wealth and children cannot please Allah, as He desires to chastise them.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever a sûrah is revealed stating, “Believe in Allah and struggle along with His Messenger,” the rich among them would ask to be exempt, saying, “Leave us with those who remain behind.”

Tafsir: And when a sūra that is a section of the Qur’ān is revealed saying ‘Believe in God and strive with His Messenger’ the affluent among them ask leave of you saying ‘Leave us to be with those who sit at home’.

hype_questions: What is the response of the affluent when a sûrah is revealed stating, 'Believe in Allah and struggle along with His Messenger?'
How do the rich react when a sūra is revealed saying 'Believe in God and strive with His Messenger'?
Why do the wealthy ask to be exempt from participating in the struggle?
propositions: A sûrah stating, ‘Believe in Allah and struggle along with His Messenger,’ is revealed.
The affluent among them ask leave of you saying 'Leave us to be with those who sit at home'.
They want to be exempt from participating in the struggle.

source_text:
Verse: They preferred to stay behind with the helpless, and their hearts have been sealed so they do not comprehend.

Tafsir: They are content to be with those who stay behind khawālif is the plural of khālifa meaning the women who ‘stay behind’ takhallafna at home and a seal has been set upon their hearts so they do not understand what is good.

hype_questions: What does it mean to stay behind in the context of Islamic history?
How do the women who stayed behind contribute to the overall narrative of the Quran?
What is the significance of having one's heart sealed in this context?
propositions: The women who stayed behind are content with their decision.
A seal has been set upon their hearts preventing them from understanding what is good.
Khawālif refers to the women who 'stay behind' at home.

source_text:
Verse: But the Messenger and the believers with him strived with their wealth and their lives. They will have all the best, and it is they who will be successful.

Tafsir: But the Messenger and those who believe with him strive with their wealth and their lives for them are the good things in this life and in the Hereafter; those they are the successful the triumphant.

hype_questions: What does it mean to strive with one's wealth and life?
How will believers be rewarded in this life and the Hereafter?
What is meant by 'the successful' and 'the triumphant'?
propositions: The Messenger and his followers struggle with their resources.
Believers who follow the Messenger strive with their wealth and lives for worldly benefits and rewards in the afterlife.
Those who are successful and triumphant are those who have strived with their wealth and lives.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has prepared for them Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever. That is the ultimate triumph.

Tafsir: God has prepared for them Gardens underneath which rivers flow to abide therein that is the supreme triumph.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate destination of those who have been chosen by Allah?
How will they be rewarded for their faith and good deeds?
What is the nature of the Gardens that Allah has prepared for them?
propositions: Allah has prepared Gardens underneath which rivers flow.
They will abide in these Gardens forever.
This is the supreme triumph.

source_text:
Verse: Some nomadic Arabs ˹also˺ came with excuses, seeking exemption. And those who were untrue to Allah and His Messenger remained behind ˹with no excuse˺. The unfaithful among them will be afflicted with a painful punishment.

Tafsir: And those Bedouins who had an excuse al-mu‘adhdhirūn the original tā’ has been assimilated with the dāl in other words it would usually be read as al-mu‘tadhirūn which itself is a variant reading those of them who were excused came to the Prophet s asking for leave to stay behind on account of their excuses and so he gave them leave to do so. And those who lied to God and His Messenger by feigning belief those hypocrites among the Bedouin stayed behind refraining from coming to give their excuses — a painful chastisement shall befall those of them who disbelieve.

hype_questions: What happens to those Bedouins who had excuses and asked the Prophet for leave to stay behind?
Why did the unfaithful among them get a painful punishment?
How do hypocrites among the Bedouin react when they are called upon to give their excuses?
propositions: Some nomadic Arabs came with excuses, seeking exemption.
Those who were untrue to Allah and His Messenger remained behind with no excuse.
The unfaithful among them will be afflicted with a painful punishment.
Those Bedouins who had an excuse came to the Prophet s asking for leave to stay behind on account of their excuses and so he gave them leave to do so.

And those who lied to God and His Messenger by feigning belief those hypocrites among the Bedouin stayed behind refraining from coming to give their excuses — a painful chastisement shall befall those of them who disbelieve.

source_text:
Verse: There is no blame on the weak, the sick, or those lacking the means ˹if they stay behind˺, as long as they are true to Allah and His Messenger. There is no blame on the good-doers. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: As for the weak such as the old and the sick the blind and the chronically ill and those who find nothing to expend for the struggle no blame no sin falls upon them should they stay away from it if they remain true to God and to His Messenger when they stay behind by not spreading false rumours or impeding others from joining the struggle but by adhering to obedience. There is no way of blame no way of reproach against those who are virtuous through such behaviour. And God is Forgiving Merciful to them by granting them such leeway in this matter.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are unable to participate in the struggle due to illness or financial constraints?
Can one be blamed for staying behind from the struggle if they remain loyal to God and His Messenger?
How can virtuous individuals avoid blame for their behavior when staying behind?
propositions: There is no blame on those who are weak, sick, or lacking in means as long as they are true to Allah and His Messenger.
God is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful towards those who remain loyal to Him and His Messenger.
Staying behind from the struggle without spreading false rumors or impeding others does not incur blame or reproach.

source_text:
Verse: Nor ˹is there any blame on˺ those who came to you ˹O Prophet˺ for mounts, then when you said, “I can find no mounts for you,” they left with eyes overflowing with tears out of grief that they had nothing to contribute.

Tafsir: Nor against those who when they came to you so that you might give them a mount to ride with you on the raid — these were seven men of the Ansār; but it is also said that they were the Banū Muqrin — you having said to them ‘I cannot find a mount whereon to mount you’ this last sentence is a circumstantial qualifier turned back this is the response to the clause beginning with idhā ‘when’ that is they departed their eyes flowing pouring with tears min al-dam‘i min is explicative for sorrow that they could not find the means to expend for the campaign struggle.

hype_questions: What happened to the Ansār when they came to the Prophet for a mount?
Why did the Banū Muqrin leave with tears in their eyes?
How did the Prophet respond to those who couldn't find a mount?
propositions: Those who came to the Prophet for a mount left because he said he could not find one.
The Ansār were seven men who came to the Prophet for a mount to ride with him on the raid.
The Banū Muqrin were those who departed with their eyes overflowing with tears due to their inability to contribute to the campaign.

source_text:
Verse: Blame is only on those who seek exemption from you although they have the means. They preferred to stay behind with the helpless, and Allah has sealed their hearts so they do not realize ˹the consequences˺.

Tafsir: The way of blame is only against those who ask leave of you to stay behind when they are rich. They are content to be with those who stay behind and God has set a seal on their hearts so that they do not know a similar statement has already been made.

hype_questions: What is the condition for someone to be exempt from blame?
Why do some people prefer to stay behind with others despite having the means?
How does Allah's seal on their hearts affect their understanding?
propositions: Blame is only on those who seek exemption from you although they have the means.
They preferred to stay behind with the helpless,
Allah has sealed their hearts so they do not realize the consequences.

source_text:
Verse: They will make excuses to you ˹believers˺ when you return to them. Say, “Make no excuses, ˹for˺ we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us about your ˹true˺ state ˹of faith˺. Your ˹future˺ deeds will be observed by Allah and His Messenger as well. And you will be returned to the Knower of the seen and unseen, then He will inform you of what you used to do.”

Tafsir: They will make excuses to you for having stayed behind when you return to them from the campaign. Say to them ‘Do not make excuses; we will never believe you! God has already told us tidings of you that is He has already informed us of your true status. And God will see your work and so will His Messenger then you will be returned through resurrection to the Knower of the unseen and the visible meaning to God and He will tell you what you used to do’ and requite you for it.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who make excuses when they return from the campaign?
How will Allah and His Messenger observe our future deeds?
What will we be requited for in the afterlife?
propositions: They will make excuses to you when you return.
We will not believe your excuses.
Allah has informed us of your true state of faith.
Your future deeds will be observed by Allah and His Messenger.
You will be returned to the Knower of the seen and unseen.
God will see your work.
His Messenger will also observe your work.
We will be requited for our actions in the afterlife.

source_text:
Verse: When you return, they will swear to you by Allah so that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone—they are truly evil. Hell will be their home as a reward for what they have committed.

Tafsir: They will swear to you by God when you turn back when you return to them from Tabūk that they had genuine excuses for staying behind so that you may leave them be refraining from reproaching them. So leave them be for they are an abomination filth on account of their inner vileness and their abode shall be Hell as requital for what they used to earn.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of not leaving people alone who have genuine excuses?
How does Allah's justice work in relation to those who are truly evil?
What is the ultimate reward for those who commit evil deeds?
propositions: When you return, they will swear to you by God that you may leave them alone.
Hell will be their home as a reward for what they have committed.
They are truly evil and an abomination due to their inner vileness.
You should refrain from reproaching them so that you may leave them be.
Their abode shall be Hell as requital for what they used to earn.

source_text:
Verse: They will swear to you in order to please you. And even if you are pleased with them, Allah will never be pleased with the rebellious people.

Tafsir: They will swear to you that you may be satisfied with them; but if you are satisfied with them God will surely not be satisfied with the wicked folk that is with them your satisfaction is of no avail in the face of the wrath of God.

hype_questions: What happens when someone swears to please you?
Can human satisfaction make up for the wrath of God?
How does Allah respond to those who swear to please others?
propositions: They will swear to you.
Allah will never be pleased with the rebellious people even if you are pleased with them.
Your satisfaction is of no avail in the face of the wrath of God.

source_text:
Verse: The nomadic Arabs ˹around Medina˺ are far worse in disbelief and hypocrisy, and less likely to know the laws revealed by Allah to His Messenger. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: The Bedouins the Arab nomads are more intense in unbelief and hypocrisy than the city-dwellers on account of their harshness and crude nature and their being too remote to hear the Qur’ān and are more likely not to know the bounds of what God has revealed to His Messenger in the way of rulings and legal prescriptions; and God is Knower of His creatures Wise in what He does with them.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of being a nomadic Arab in terms of their relationship with Allah?
How do harsh living conditions affect an individual's understanding of divine laws?
Can city-dwellers be more knowledgeable about Allah's revelations than nomadic Arabs?
propositions: The nomadic Arabs are far worse in disbelief and hypocrisy.
Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
The Bedouins are more intense in unbelief and hypocrisy due to their harshness and crude nature.
God is Knower of His creatures Wise in what He does with them.

source_text:
Verse: And among the nomads are those who consider what they donate to be a loss and await your misfortune. May ill-fortune befall them! And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Tafsir: And of the Bedouins there is he who takes what he expends in the way of God as a penalty as a liability and a financial loss because he does not aspire to be rewarded for it but expends it out of fear these were Banū Asad and Banū Ghatafān; and awaits for you evil turns of fortune the fortunes of time for you that these should turn against you and so be rid of you. Theirs shall be the evil read as al-sū‘ or al-saw‘ turn of fortune that is chastisement and destruction shall turn on them not on you. And God is Hearer of the sayings of His servants Knower of their actions.

hype_questions: What happens to those who consider their charitable donations as a loss?
How do the Bedouins perceive their acts of charity towards Allah?
What is the consequence for those who fear Allah and spend in His way?
propositions: Those who donate to Allah consider their act as a loss.
The Bedouins take what they expend in the way of God as a penalty as a liability and a financial loss.
God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

source_text:
Verse: However, among the nomadic Arabs are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and consider what they donate as a means of coming closer to Allah and ˹receiving˺ the prayers of the Messenger. It will certainly bring them closer. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: And of the Bedouins there is he who believes in God and the Last Day such as men from among the tribes of Juhayna and Muzayna and takes what he expends in the way of God as pious offerings to bring him nearer to God and as a means to secure the prayers the supplications of the Messenger for him. Surely these the expenditure of such men will bring them nearer read qurubatun or qurbatun to Him. God will admit them into His mercy His Paradise. Truly God is Forgiving to those who obey Him Merciful to them.

hype_questions: What is the significance of donating to Allah in Islam?
How can one bring themselves closer to Allah through their actions?
What happens to those who obey Allah and show mercy?
propositions: Those who donate to Allah will be brought closer to Him.
Allah admits those who believe in Him into His mercy.
God is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: As for the foremost—the first of the Emigrants—and those who follow them in goodness, Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. And He has prepared for them Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. That is the ultimate triumph.

Tafsir: And the first to lead the way of the Emigrants and the Helpers namely those who were present at the battle of Badr or it means all the Companions and those who follow them up to the Day of Resurrection by being virtuous in deeds God will be pleased with them for their obedience of Him and they will be pleased with Him for His reward to them; and He has prepared for them Gardens — with rivers flowing beneath them a variant reading adds min min tahtihā ‘beneath which’ — to abide therein forever that is the supreme triumph.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate triumph for those who follow in goodness?
How will Allah be pleased with His servants?
What reward does God have in store for virtuous individuals?
propositions: Allah is pleased with those who follow in goodness.
God will be pleased with His servants for their obedience to Him.
He has prepared Gardens under which rivers flow for them to stay forever.

source_text:
Verse: Some of the nomads around you ˹believers˺ are hypocrites, as are some of the people of Medina. They have mastered hypocrisy. They are not known to you ˹O Prophet˺; they are known to Us. We will punish them twice ˹in this world˺, then they will be brought back ˹to their Lord˺ for a tremendous punishment.

Tafsir: And among those around you O inhabitants of Medina of the Bedouins there are hypocrites such as the tribes of Aslam Ashja‘ and Ghifār and among the townspeople of Medina there are also hypocrites who are obstinate in hypocrisy engrossed in it and persisting in it. You do not know them — an address to the Prophet s — but We know them and We shall chastise them twice by disgracing them or having them killed in this world and by way of punishment in the grave then they will be returned in the Hereafter to a terrible chastisement namely the Fire.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of hypocrisy in this world?
How will hypocrites be punished in the Hereafter?
Can one know who is a hypocrite?
propositions: Some nomads around you are hypocrites.
The people of Medina, including Bedouins and townspeople, have mastered hypocrisy.
We will punish them twice in this world and then they will be brought back to their Lord for a tremendous punishment.

source_text:
Verse: Some others have confessed their wrongdoing: they have mixed goodness with evil. It is right to hope that Allah will turn to them in mercy. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: And there are others ākharūn is the subject another folk who have confessed their sins for having stayed behind i‘tarafū bi-dhunūbihim is an adjectival qualification of it the subject and the predicate is the following khalatū ‘amalan sālihan they have mixed a righteous deed that is their former participation in the struggle or the their confession of their sins or otherwise with another that was bad which is their having stayed behind. It may be that God will relent to them. Truly God is Forgiving Merciful this was revealed regarding Abū Lubāba and a group of men who tied themselves to the walls of the mosque after they heard what had been revealed regarding those who stayed behind; they swore that only the Prophet s would untie them which he did when this verse was revealed.

hype_questions: Can Allah ever forgive someone who has committed a grave sin?
What is the significance of staying behind during the struggle in Islam?
How can one seek mercy from Allah after committing a mistake?
propositions: Some others have confessed their wrongdoing: they have mixed goodness with evil.
It is right to hope that Allah will turn to them in mercy.
God will relent to those who have confessed their sins.
The Prophet s untied the men who tied themselves to the walls of the mosque after hearing about those who stayed behind.

source_text:
Verse: Take from their wealth ˹O Prophet˺ charity to purify and bless them, and pray for them—surely your prayer is a source of comfort for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Tafsir: Take of their wealth some alms to purify them and to cleanse them thereby of their sins; he thus took a third of their wealth and gave it away as charity; and pray for them that is supplicate for them; truly your prayers are a comfort a mercy for them it is also said to mean reassurance for them that their repentance has been accepted. And God is Hearer Knower.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of giving charity to others?
How does prayer benefit those who receive it?
Can prayer bring comfort and reassurance to those in need?
propositions: Take from their wealth charity to purify and bless them.
Your prayer is a source of comfort for them.
Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not know that Allah alone accepts the repentance of His servants and receives ˹their˺ charity, and that Allah alone is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful?

Tafsir: Do they not know that God is He Who accepts repentance from His servants and takes accepts the voluntary alms and that God is He Who is the Relenting to His servants by accepting their repentance and the Merciful? to them the interrogative is intended as an affirmative statement and is meant to incite them to offer repentance and charity.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's acceptance of repentance?
How does God respond to the voluntary alms of His servants?
What is the essence of God's mercy towards His servants?
propositions: Allah alone accepts the repentance of His servants.
God is He Who accepts repentance from His servants.
Allah alone receives the voluntary alms of His servants.
God is He Who takes the voluntary alms.
God is He Who is the Relenting to His servants by accepting their repentance.
God is He Who is the Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: Tell ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Do as you will. Your deeds will be observed by Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the seen and unseen, then He will inform you of what you used to do.”

Tafsir: And say to them or to people in general ‘Act as you will for God will surely see your actions and so will His Messenger and the believers and you will be returned through resurrection to the Knower of the unseen and the visible that is to God and He will tell you what you used to do’ and so requite you for it.

hype_questions: What will happen to us after we die?
Will Allah judge us based on our actions?
What is the purpose of resurrection?
propositions: God will see your actions.
His Messenger and believers will observe your deeds.
You will be returned to God through resurrection.
God will inform you of what you used to do.

source_text:
Verse: And some others are left for Allah’s decision, either to punish them or turn to them in mercy. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And there are others from among those who stayed behind who are deferred read murja’ūna or murjawna whose repentance is delayed to God’s command concerning them according to His will whether He chastises them by causing them to die without their having made any repentance or relents to them; and God is Knower of His creatures Wise in what He does with them. These others mentioned are the three who will be mentioned afterwards Murāra b. al-Rabī‘ Ka‘b b. Mālik and Hilāl b. Umayya. They stayed behind out of laziness and their inclination for peace and quiet not out of hypocrisy. Unlike the others however they did not excuse themselves before the Prophet s and so the matter regarding them was suspended for fifty days during which time people avoided them until it was later revealed that God had relented to them.

hype_questions: What is the fate of those who stayed behind during the Hijrah?
How does Allah's mercy manifest in the lives of those who were deferred?
Can one excuse themselves from their duties to Allah?
propositions: Some individuals are left for Allah’s decision, either to punish them or turn to them in mercy.
The repentance of murja’ah is delayed until God’s command concerning them according to His will.
God is Knower of His creatures Wise in what He does with them.
Murāra b. al-Rabī‘, Ka‘b b. Mālik, and Hilāl b. Umayya stayed behind out of laziness and their inclination for peace and quiet.
The Prophet s did not excuse himself from his duties to Allah.
People avoided Murāra b. al-Rabī‘, Ka‘b b. Mālik, and Hilāl b. Umayya during the fifty-day period.
God had relented to Murāra b. al-Rabī‘, Ka‘b b. Mālik, and Hilāl b. Umayya.

source_text:
Verse: There are also those ˹hypocrites˺ who set up a mosque ˹only˺ to cause harm, promote disbelief, divide the believers, and as a base for those who had previously fought against Allah and His Messenger. They will definitely swear, “We intended nothing but good,” but Allah bears witness that they are surely liars.

Tafsir: And among them those who have chosen a mosque — these were twelve men from among the hypocrites — by way of harm to cause distress for those of the mosque of Qubā’ and disbelief since they built it on the orders of the monk Abū ‘Āmir as a sanctuary for him so that whoever comes from his side may stay there he had gone to the Byzantine Emperor qaysar to bring troops to fight against the Prophet s and to cause division among the believers who pray in the mosque of Qubā’ by having some of these pray in their the hypocrites’ mosque and as an outpost an observation post for those who waged war against God and His Messenger before that is before it was built — meaning the above-mentioned Abū ‘Āmir — they will swear ‘We desired nothing by building it but to do good’ by way of kindness towards the poor in times of heavy rain or extreme heat and in order to provide a place of worship for the Muslims; and God bears witness that they are truly liars in this claim of theirs. They had asked the Prophet s to perform prayers in it and so the following was revealed

hype_questions: What is the purpose of building a mosque that causes harm and division among believers?
How do hypocrites justify their actions by claiming to have done good?
Why did the Prophet s refuse to perform prayers in a mosque built for a specific individual?
propositions: Some individuals set up mosques with the intention of causing harm and promoting disbelief.
Hypocrites will swear that they intended to do good, but Allah bears witness that they are liars.
The Prophet s was asked to perform prayers in a mosque built for a specific individual, but it was revealed that this was not acceptable.

source_text:
Verse: Do not ˹O Prophet˺ ever pray in it. Certainly, a mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy of your prayers. In it are men who love to be purified. And Allah loves those who purify themselves.

Tafsir: Never stand never perform prayer there and so he sent a group of men to destroy and burn it and in its place they left a refuse pit where decaying cadavers would be dumped. A mosque which was founded one whose foundations were built upon piety from the first day constructed the day you arrived in Medina dār al-hijra — this was the mosque of Qubā’ as mentioned in Bukhārī — is worthier than that other one for you to stand to perform prayer therein; in it are men namely the Ansār who love to purify themselves; and God loves those who purify themselves muttahhirīn the original tā’ of mutatahhirūn has been assimilated with the tā’ that is He will reward them. Ibn Khuzayma reported in his Sahīh by way of an isnād from ‘Uwaym b. Sā‘ida that ‘The Prophet s came to them at the mosque of Qubā’ and said “God exalted be He has praised handsomely the way you purify yourselves in the story about your mosque so what is this purification which you perform?” They said “By God O Messenger of God all that we know is that we used to have Jews in our vicinity and they used to wash their behinds after defecation and so we began to wash in the way they did”’. According to one hadīth reported by al-Bazzār they said ‘We use stones to scrape off remnants and follow this with water’; to which he the Prophet said ‘That is the way for proper purification. Let this be your way’.

hype_questions: What is the significance of purification in Islam?
How did the Ansār develop their unique method of purification?
Why does Allah love those who purify themselves?
propositions: A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy of your prayers.
The Prophet s came to the mosque of Qubā’ and praised the way the Ansār purified themselves.
Proper purification involves using stones to scrape off remnants and following with water.

source_text:
Verse: Which is better: those who laid the foundation of their building on the fear and pleasure of Allah, or those who did so on the edge of a crumbling cliff that tumbled down with them into the Fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

Tafsir: Is he who founded his building upon fear of God and in hope of beatitude from Him better or he who founded his building upon the brink the edge of a bank an overhang that is crumbling about to collapse read juruf or jurf so that it toppled with him so that it collapsed taking with it the one who built it into the fire of Hell? this is an excellent similitude for building upon that which constitutes the opposite of fear of God and for what it leads to; the interrogative is meant as an affirmative in other words the former is the better which is the likeness of the building of the mosque of Qubā’ while the latter is the likeness of the mosque of ‘harm’ masjid al-dirār. And God guides not the evildoing folk.

hype_questions: What is the better foundation for building one's life: fear and hope in Allah, or reckless abandon?
How does building on shaky ground compare to building on a solid foundation of faith?
Can someone who builds their life on fear of God be said to have built it on solid ground?
propositions: Those who founded their buildings upon fear of God and in hope of beatitude from Him are better than those who did so on the brink of a crumbling cliff.
Building on shaky ground is like building on the edge of a bank that is about to collapse.
God guides not the evildoing folk.
The former is the better, which is the likeness of the building of the mosque of Qubā’.
The latter is the likeness of the mosque of ‘harm’ masjid al-dirār.

source_text:
Verse: The building which they erected will never cease to fuel hypocrisy in their hearts until their hearts are torn apart. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: The buildings which they have built will never cease to be a misgiving a point of doubt in their hearts unless their hearts are cut torn to pieces such that they die; and God is Knower of His creatures Wise in what He does with them.

hype_questions: What can fuel hypocrisy in the hearts of people?
How will the buildings built by humans affect their faith?
Can God's wisdom be questioned?
propositions: The building erected by humans will never cease to be a source of hypocrisy in their hearts.
Humans' doubts and misgivings about their creations will persist until they are torn apart by internal conflict.
God is All-Knowing and All-Wise, and His actions cannot be questioned.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has indeed purchased from the believers their lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah and kill or are killed. This is a true promise binding on Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran. And whose promise is truer than Allah’s? So rejoice in the exchange you have made with Him. That is ˹truly˺ the ultimate triumph.

Tafsir: Indeed God has purchased from the believers their lives and their possessions that they expend it in obedience of Him — for example by striving in His way — so that theirs will be the reward of Paradise they shall fight in the way of God and they shall kill and be killed this sentence is independent and constitutes an explication of the above-mentioned ‘purchase’; a variant reading has the passive verb come first sc. fa-yuqtalūna wa-yaqtulūn ‘they shall be killed and shall kill’ meaning that some of them are killed while those who remain fight on; that is a promise which is binding both wa‘dan ‘promise’ and haqqan ‘binding’ are verbal nouns and are in the accusative on account of their omitted implicit verbs upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur’ān; and who fulfils his covenant better than God? that is no one is better in fulfilling it. Rejoice then there is a shift from the third to second person here in this bargain of yours which you have made for that bargain is the supreme triumph the one that secures the ultimate goal.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate triumph in Islam?
How do believers receive a reward for their actions?
What is the nature of God's promise?
propositions: Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise.
The believers fight in the cause of Allah and kill or are killed.
God's promise is truer than any other promise.
Believers expend their possessions in obedience to God.
Those who remain after some have been killed will continue to fight on.
Rejoicing in this bargain secures the ultimate goal.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It is the believers˺ who repent, who are devoted to worship, who praise ˹their Lord˺, who fast, who bow down and prostrate themselves, who encourage good and forbid evil, and who observe the limits set by Allah. And give good news to the believers.

Tafsir: Those who repent al-tā’ibūna is in the nominative as a laudative the subject being implicit from idolatry and hypocrisy those who worship who devote their worship sincerely to God those who give praise to Him in every state those who fast those who bow those who prostrate themselves that is those who perform prayers those who enjoin decency and forbid to indecency those who maintain God’s bounds His rulings by implementing them and give good tidings to the believers of Paradise.

hype_questions: What are the characteristics of a believer?
How can one maintain God's bounds and rulings?
What is the reward for believers in Paradise?
propositions: Believers repent.
Believers worship sincerely to God.
Believers fast.
Believers bow down and prostrate themselves.
Believers encourage good and forbid evil.
God gives good tidings to believers.

source_text:
Verse: It is not ˹proper˺ for the Prophet and the believers to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives, after it has become clear to the believers that they are bound for the Hellfire.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding the Prophet s asking forgiveness for his uncle Abū Tālib and some of the Companions asking forgiveness for their idolatrous parents It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the idolaters even though they be kinsmen relatives after it has become clear to them that they are inhabitants of the Hell-fire for having died as disbelievers.

hype_questions: Can believers ask for forgiveness for their polytheistic relatives after they have died as disbelievers?
Is it permissible for the Prophet to seek forgiveness for his idolatrous family members?
What are the consequences of being a polytheist and dying without accepting Islam?
propositions: The Prophet cannot ask for forgiveness for polytheists, even if they are close relatives.
Believers should not seek forgiveness for their polytheistic parents after it becomes clear that they are destined for Hellfire.
Polytheism is a grave sin that leads to eternal punishment in the afterlife.

source_text:
Verse: As for Abraham’s prayer for his father’s forgiveness, it was only in fulfilment of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to Abraham that his father was an enemy of Allah, he broke ties with him. Abraham was truly tender-hearted, forbearing.

Tafsir: Abraham’s prayer for the forgiveness of his father was only because of a promise he had made to him when he said to him I will ask my Lord forgiveness for you Q. 1947 in the hope that he would submit to God; but when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God upon his death as an disbeliever he declared himself innocent of him and refrained from asking forgiveness for him; truly Abraham was soft of heart making frequent entreaty and supplication to God forbearing enduring harm patiently.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Abraham's prayer for his father's forgiveness?
How did Abraham respond when he realized his father was an enemy of Allah?
What is the meaning of 'soft of heart' in the context of Abraham's character?
propositions: Abraham made a promise to his father that he would ask for forgiveness on his behalf.
Abraham broke ties with his father when he realized he was an enemy of Allah.
Abraham was patient and forbearing, making frequent entreaty and supplication to God.

source_text:
Verse: Allah would never consider a people deviant after He has guided them, until He makes clear to them what they must avoid. Surely Allah has ˹full˺ knowledge of everything.

Tafsir: And God would never send a people astray after He had guided them to Islam until He had made clear to them that which they should be wary of in the way of deeds but when they are not wary of it then they deserve to be sent astray. Surely God is Knower of all things including who deserves to be sent astray or to be guided.

hype_questions: What are the signs that Allah is guiding a people towards righteousness?
How does Allah make clear to His servants what they must avoid in their deeds?
Can a person ever be truly astray if Allah has guided them?
propositions: Allah guides a people until He makes clear to them what they must avoid.
If Allah has not made clear to a people what they should avoid, then they are not truly guided.
A person can only be sent astray if they ignore the warning signs given by Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, to Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And besides Allah you have no guardian or helper.

Tafsir: Surely to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and of the earth. He gives life and He makes to die; and you do not have O mankind besides God that is other than Him any protector to preserve you from Him or helper to defend you against His hurt.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's power over creation?
Can humans rely on anyone besides Allah for protection?
How does Allah's sovereignty impact human existence?
propositions: Allah belongs to no one else but Himself.
Allah gives life and causes death.
Humans have no protector or helper besides Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has certainly turned in mercy to the Prophet as well as the Emigrants and the Helpers who stood by him in the time of hardship, after the hearts of a group of them had almost faltered. He then accepted their repentance. Surely He is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to them.

Tafsir: God has truly relented that is He has truly perpetuated His relenting to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship that is during the time of this hardship which was their predicament during the raid at Tabūk where two men would share a single date ten men would take turns on one camel and where the heat became so intense that they resorted to drinking filth; after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated read either as tazīghu or yazīghu had almost inclined away from following him in favour of staying behind due to the hardship that afflicted them then He relented to them by making them steadfast. Truly He is Gentle Merciful to them.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Allah's mercy towards the Prophet and his companions?
How did the Prophet and his companions overcome hardship during their journey to Tabūk?
What role did perseverance play in the story of the Emigrants and Helpers?
propositions: Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet.
The hearts of a group of them had almost faltered.
He then accepted their repentance.
God has truly relented that is He has truly perpetuated His relenting to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship.
after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated
Truly He is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to them.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹Allah has also turned in mercy to˺ the three who had remained behind, ˹whose guilt distressed them˺ until the earth, despite its vastness, seemed to close in on them, and their souls were torn in anguish. They knew there was no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them in mercy so that they might repent. Surely Allah ˹alone˺ is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: And He relented to the three who were left behind formerly denied His relenting to them for the same reason as those mentioned above when the earth was straitened for them for all its breadth that is despite its vastness so they could find no place wherein to feel secure and their souls that is their hearts were straitened for them because of the anxiety and their sense of alienation resulting from the delay of God’s relenting to them with mercy such that they their souls could not find happiness or solace; until they thought they were certain that read the softened an there is no refuge from God except in Him. Then He turned relenting to them He made them successful in finding repentance that they might also turn in repentance. Truly God is the Relenting the Merciful.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah turns in mercy to those who have been denied it?
How do the three individuals who remained behind feel after being left out of God's relenting to them?
Can there be any refuge from Allah except in Him?
propositions: Allah has turned in mercy to the three who had remained behind.
The earth seemed to close in on them due to its vastness.
Their souls were torn in anguish until they knew there was no refuge from Allah except in Him.
He turned to them in mercy so that they might repent.
Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: O  believers! Be mindful of Allah and be with the truthful.

Tafsir: O you who believe fear God by refraining from acts of disobedience to Him and be with those who are truthful in their faith and covenants by adhering to sincerity.

hype_questions: What is the importance of being truthful in one's faith and covenants?
How can believers show their obedience to Allah?
What are the consequences of disobeying Allah?
propositions: Believers should fear God by refraining from acts of disobedience.
Being with those who are truthful in their faith and covenants is important.
Adhering to sincerity is a key aspect of being truthful.

source_text:
Verse: It was not ˹proper˺ for the people of Medina and the nomadic Arabs around them to avoid marching with the Messenger of Allah or to prefer their own lives above his. That is because whenever they suffer from thirst, fatigue, or hunger in the cause of Allah; or tread on a territory, unnerving the disbelievers; or inflict any loss on an enemy—it is written to their credit as a good deed. Surely Allah never discounts the reward of the good-doers.

Tafsir: It is not for the people of Medina and for the Bedouins who dwell around them to stay behind God’s Messenger when he sets out on a campaign and to prefer their lives to his life by guarding them against hardships which he the Prophet is content to suffer himself this statement is a prohibition expressed as a predicate; that prohibition against staying behind is because neither thirst nor toil nor hunger afflicts them in the way of God nor tread they any tread mawti’an is a verbal noun meaning wat’an that enrages the disbelievers nor gain any gain from the enemy of God be it through slaughter capture or plunder but a righteous deed is therefore recorded for them that they may be rewarded for it. Truly God does not leave the wage of the virtuous to go to waste that is the wage of those mentioned rather He rewards them.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who stay behind during a campaign?
Can avoiding hardships be considered a good deed?
How does Allah reward the virtuous?
propositions: The people of Medina and the nomadic Arabs around them should not avoid marching with the Messenger of Allah.
Whenever they suffer from thirst, fatigue, or hunger in the cause of Allah, it is written to their credit as a good deed.
Allah never discounts the reward of the good-doers.

source_text:
Verse: And whenever they make a donation, small or large, or cross a valley ˹in Allah’s cause˺—it is written to their credit, so that Allah may grant them the best reward for what they used to do.

Tafsir: Nor expend they therein in the way of God any sum small even if it be a single date or great nor do they cross a valley during a campaign march but it is recorded for them as a righteous deed that God may reward them the best of what they used to do that is the due reward thereof.

hype_questions: What happens when we make a donation in the name of Allah?
How does Allah reward us for our good deeds?
Can small acts of charity still earn us a great reward?
propositions: Whenever someone makes a donation, it is written to their credit.
Allah records every righteous deed, no matter how small.
The best reward for our actions is the one we will receive in the afterlife.

source_text:
Verse: ˹However,˺ it is not necessary for the believers to march forth all at once. Only a party from each group should march forth, leaving the rest to gain religious knowledge then enlighten their people when they return to them, so that they ˹too˺ may beware ˹of evil˺.

Tafsir: When the Prophet s was about to dispatch a raiding party — after they certain Muslims had been reproached for staying behind — all of them went forth and so the following was revealed It is not for the believers to go forth on a raid altogether why should not a party a group of every section of every tribe of them go forth while the others remain behind so that they those who remain behind may become learned in religion and that they may warn their folk when they return to them from the raid by teaching them some of the rulings which they have come to learn so that they may beware? of God’s punishment by adhering to His commands and prohibitions. Ibn ‘Abbās said that this verse is specifically intended for raiding parties while the previous one is specifically to prohibit any individual staying behind when the Prophet s sets out on a campaign.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of sending out a party from each group during a raid?
How can believers ensure they are following God's commands and prohibitions?
What happens to those who remain behind after a raid?
propositions: Believers do not need to march forth all at once.
A party from each group should march forth, leaving the rest to gain religious knowledge.
Those who remain behind should warn their folk when they return from the raid by teaching them some of the rulings they have learned.
The purpose is for believers to beware of God's punishment by adhering to His commands and prohibitions.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Fight the disbelievers around you and let them find firmness in you. And know that Allah is with those mindful ˹of Him˺.

Tafsir: O you who believe fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you that is the nearest followed by the next nearest of them and let them find harshness in you that is severity in other words be harsh with them and know that God is with the pious helping and granting them victory.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be firm in faith?
How can one show severity towards disbelievers?
What role does God play in the lives of the pious?
propositions: Believers should fight those who are near them first, followed by the next nearest.
Being harsh with disbelievers means showing severity and firmness in faith.
God is present with those who are mindful of Him and helps the pious.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever a sûrah is revealed, some of them ask ˹mockingly˺, “Which of you has this increased in faith?” As for the believers, it has increased them in faith and they rejoice.

Tafsir: And whenever a sūra of the Qur’ān is revealed there are some of them that is the hypocrites who say to their companions mockingly ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ and God says As for those who believe it has increased them in faith because they accept that it is true and they rejoice because of it.

hype_questions: Does revelation increase faith in believers?
How do hypocrites react to the revelation of a sūra?
What is the response of God to those who question the effect of revelation on faith?
propositions: Whenever a sûrah is revealed, some people ask mockingly which of them has increased in faith.
For believers, the revelation of a sūra increases their faith.
God responds that it is those who believe that have increased in faith because they accept its truth.
Believers rejoice upon receiving the revelation of a sūra.

source_text:
Verse: But as for those with sickness in their hearts, it has increased them only in wickedness upon their wickedness, and they die as disbelievers.

Tafsir: But as for those in whose hearts is sickness a weakness of faith it only adds abomination to their abomination that is it only adds disbelief to their disbelief since they disbelieve in it and they die while they were disbelievers.

hype_questions: What happens to those who have sickness in their hearts?
How does faithlessness affect an individual's spiritual state?
Can a person's disbelief lead to spiritual death?
propositions: Those with sickness in their hearts increase their wickedness.
Faithlessness leads to abomination and disbelief.
Disbelievers die as disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not see that they are tried once or twice every year? Yet they neither repent nor do they learn a lesson.

Tafsir: Do they not see that is the hypocrites in which case read a-wa-lā yarawna; or if read a-wa-lā tarawna ‘do you O believers not see’ that they are tested afflicted every year once or twice? with drought and diseases. Still they do not repent of their hypocrisy nor do they remember nor do they heed admonition.

hype_questions: Do you O believers not see that they are tested afflicted every year once or twice?
Do they not see that is the hypocrites in which case read a-wa-lā yarawna;
Still they do not repent of their hypocrisy nor do they remember nor do they heed admonition.
propositions: They are tested afflicted every year once or twice.
The hypocrites are those who do not repent.
Believers should see that the hypocrites are being tested.
Hypocrisy is a state of not repenting.
Drought and diseases are part of their testing.
Admonition is ignored by the hypocrites.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever a sûrah is revealed, they look at one another, ˹saying,˺ “Is anyone watching you?” Then they slip away. ˹It is˺ Allah ˹Who˺ has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not comprehend.

Tafsir: And whenever a sūra is revealed wherein is mention of them and the Prophet s recites it they look at one another desiring to flee and saying ‘Will anyone see you?’ if you get up and flee? and so if no one can see them they get up and leave otherwise they stay put. Then they turn away persisting in their disbelief. God turns their hearts away from guidance because they are a folk who do not understand the truth for they do not reflect on it.

hype_questions: What happens when a sūra is revealed and the Prophet recites it?
Why do people look at one another when a sūra is revealed?
How does God respond to those who turn away from guidance?
propositions: Whenever a sûrah is revealed, they look at one another.
Allah has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not comprehend.
God turns their hearts away from guidance because they are a folk who do not understand the truth for they do not reflect on it.

source_text:
Verse: There certainly has come to you a messenger from among yourselves. He is concerned by your suffering, anxious for your well-being, and gracious and merciful to the believers.

Tafsir: Verily there has come to you a messenger from among yourselves that is one of you — Muhammad (s) — for whom it is grievous hard that you should suffer that is your suffering your experiencing hardship and encountering harm is hard on him; who is full of concern for you that you should be rightly guided; to the believers full of pity profoundly compassionate merciful desiring good for them.

hype_questions: What is the nature of a messenger sent by Allah?
How does a prophet experience hardship due to human suffering?
What is the role of compassion and mercy in guiding believers?
propositions: A messenger has come from among yourselves.
It is hard for Muhammad (s) that you should suffer.
He desires good for the believers.

source_text:
Verse: But if they turn away, then say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah is sufficient for me. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. In Him I put my trust. And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”

Tafsir: So if they turn away refraining from believing in you say ‘God suffices me. There is no god except Him. Upon Him I rely in Him have I put my trust and in none other and He is the Lord of the Tremendous Throne’ al-‘arsh al-azīm the kursī which is singled out for mention because it is the greatest of all things created. Al-Hākim reported in al-Mustadrak by way of an isnād from Ubayy b. Ka‘b that he Ubayy said ‘The last verse to be revealed was from Verily there has come to you a messenger… to the end of the sūra’ sc. Q. 9128-129.

hype_questions: Does Allah's sufficiency guarantee salvation?
Can one rely solely on Allah for guidance?
What is the significance of the 'Lord of the Tremendous Throne' in Islamic theology?
propositions: Allah is sufficient for me.
There is no god worthy of worship except Him.
I put my trust in Him.
He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.

source_text:
Verse: Alif-Lãm-Ra. These are the verses of the Book, rich in wisdom.

Tafsir: Alif lām rā’ God knows best what He means by these letters. Those namely these signs are the signs of the wise Book that is the Qur’ān the genitive annexation āyāt al-kitāb has the meaning of min sc. min āyāti’l-kitāb ‘from among the verses of the Book’ which has been made clear.

hype_questions: What is the meaning of Alif-Lãm-Ra in the Qur'ān?
How does God relate to the verses of the Book?
What are the signs of the wise Book?
propositions: The Book is rich in wisdom.
God knows best what He means by these letters.
These signs are from among the verses of the Book that has been made clear.

source_text:
Verse: Is it astonishing to people that We have sent revelation to a man from among themselves, ˹instructing him,˺ “Warn humanity and give good news to the believers that they will have an honourable status with their Lord.”? Yet the disbelievers said, “Indeed, this ˹man˺ is clearly a magician!”

Tafsir: Is it for the people the people of Mecca this interrogative is meant as a disavowal; the preposition li- ‘for’ and its dependent genitive noun al-nās ‘the people’ constitute a circumstantial qualifier of His saying a wonder ‘ajaban read in the accusative as a predicate of kāna; or if read in the nominative ‘ajabun as its subject its predicate which is also its subject if read according to the former accusative reading is the following an awhaynā that We have inspired a man from among them Muhammad (s) saying an ‘that’ is explicative ‘Warn threaten the people the disbelievers with chastisement and give good tidings to those who believe that they have a prior a preceding promise of truth with their Lord’? that is a preceding fair reward in return for the deeds they have sent forward. The disbelievers say ‘Truly this Qur’ān that comprises all of that mentioned is manifest sorcery’ a variant reading for la-sihrun has la-sāhirun ‘a sorcerer’ where it is the Prophet s to whom they are referring as being ‘a manifest sorcerer’.

hype_questions: Does the Quran contain sorcery?
Is the Prophet Muhammad a magician?
Can humans be warned and given good news by God?
propositions: God sent revelation to a man from among themselves.
The people of Mecca are being disavowed as the intended audience of this verse.
God will give good tidings to those who believe that they have a prior promise of truth with their Lord.
The disbelievers say that the Quran is manifest sorcery.
The Prophet Muhammad is referred to as a 'manifest sorcerer' by the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: Surely your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne, conducting every affair. None can intercede except by His permission. That is Allah—your Lord, so worship Him ˹alone˺. Will you not then be mindful?

Tafsir: Truly your Lord is God Who created the heavens and the earth in six days of the days of this world that is in the same measure of time since there was no sun or moon then had He willed He could have created them in an instant but the reason for His not having done so is that He wanted to teach His creatures to be circumspect; then He presided upon the Throne a presiding befitting of Him directing affairs among creatures. There is no mā min indicates a relative clause intercessor to intercede for anyone save after His permission a refutation of their saying ‘The idols intercede for us!’; that Creator and Director is God your Lord so worship Him affirm His Oneness. Will you not remember? tadhakkarūna the original tā’ of tatadhakkarūna has been assimilated with the dhāl.

hype_questions: Does Allah allow any intercession without His permission?
What is the reason behind Allah's creation of the world in six days?
How does Allah want His creatures to be circumspect?
propositions: Your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days.
None can intercede except by Allah's permission.
Worship Allah alone.
Allah wanted to teach His creatures to be circumspect.
Allah presided upon the Throne directing affairs among creatures.
There is no mā min indicates a relative clause intercessor to intercede for anyone save after Allah's permission.
That Creator and Director is Allah your Lord so worship Him affirm His Oneness.
Will you not remember?

source_text:
Verse: To Him is your return all together. Allah’s promise is ˹always˺ true. Indeed, He originates the creation then resurrects it so that He may justly reward those who believe and do good. But those who disbelieve will have a boiling drink and a painful punishment for their disbelief.

Tafsir: To Him exalted be He is the return of all of you God’s promise in truth both wa‘da and haqqan are verbal nouns and in the accusative because of the verbs implicit in them. Truly He read innahu as a new sentence or annahu with an implied lām sc. li-annahu ‘Because He’ originates creation that is He began it by originating it then recreates it through resurrection that He may requite reward those who believe and perform righteous deeds justly. And those who disbelieve for them will be a draught of boiling water and a painful chastisement because they disbelieved.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reward for those who believe and do good?
What will happen to those who disbelieve?
How does Allah originate and resurrect creation?
propositions: Allah's promise is always true.
He originates creation and then resurrects it to reward those who believe and do good.
Those who disbelieve will have a boiling drink and a painful punishment for their disbelief.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who made the sun a radiant source and the moon a reflected light, with precisely ordained phases, so that you may know the number of years and calculation ˹of time˺. Allah did not create all this except for a purpose. He makes the signs clear for people of knowledge.

Tafsir: He it is Who made the sun a radiance that is emitting light and the moon a light and determined it with respect to its movement in stations 28 stations in 28 nights every month becoming concealed for two nights when a particular month has 30 days or concealed for one night when it has 29 days so that you might know thereby the number of the years and the reckoning. God did not create that which is mentioned save in truth not in vain exalted be He above such things. He details read yufassilu or nufassilu ‘We detail’ the signs for a people who know who reflect.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Allah's creation?
How does Allah make signs clear for people of knowledge?
What is the significance of the moon's phases?
propositions: Allah created the sun as a source of light.
The moon was determined to have precisely ordained phases.
God did not create anything in vain.
Allah makes signs clear for people who know and reflect.

source_text:
Verse: Surely in the alternation of the day and the night, and in all that Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, there are truly signs for those mindful ˹of Him˺.

Tafsir: Truly in the alternation of night and day in their coming and going increasing and diminishing and in what God has created in the heavens of angels sun moon stars and other things and in the earth of animals mountains seas rivers trees and other things there are signs indications of His power exalted be He for a people who fear Him and so believe He singles these out for mention because they are the ones to benefit from them such signs.

hype_questions: What are the signs of Allah's power in the universe?
How do people who fear Allah benefit from the signs of nature?
Why does Allah single out certain individuals for mention?
propositions: There are signs of Allah's power in the alternation of day and night.
Allah has created many things in the heavens and earth, including angels, sun, moon, stars, animals, mountains, seas, rivers, and trees.
People who fear Allah will benefit from the signs of nature.
Allah singles out certain individuals for mention because they are the ones to benefit from the signs.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us, being pleased and content with this worldly life, and who are heedless of Our signs,

Tafsir: Truly those who do not expect to encounter Us through resurrection and are content with the life of this world instead of the life the Hereafter since they reject the truth of it and feel reassured feel secure in it and those who are heedless of Our signs of the proofs of Our Oneness neglecting to ponder them

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the truth of the Hereafter?
How do those who are content with worldly life prepare for their own death?
Can one truly feel secure in a life that is not based on faith?
propositions: Those who do not expect to meet Us are pleased and content with this worldly life.
They reject the truth of the Hereafter and feel reassured and secure in it.
Those who are heedless of Our signs neglect to ponder them.

source_text:
Verse: they will have the Fire as a home because of what they have committed.

Tafsir: those their abode will be the Fire because of what they used to earn in the way of practising idolatry and performing acts of disobedience.

hype_questions: What will be the fate of those who practice idolatry?
How will the Fire serve as a home for those who disobey Allah's commands?
What consequences will those who perform acts of disobedience face?
propositions: Those who commit sins will have the Fire as their abode.
The Fire is a consequence of practicing idolatry and performing acts of disobedience.
Idolatry and disobedience lead to a terrible fate.

source_text:
Verse: Surely those who believe and do good, their Lord will guide them ˹to Paradise˺ through their faith, rivers will flow under their feet in the Gardens of Bliss,

Tafsir: Truly those who believe and perform righteous deeds their Lord will guide them He will lead them through their faith in Him by appointing for them a light with which they will be able to find their way on the Day of Resurrection. Rivers will flow beneath them in the Gardens of Bliss

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal for those who believe and perform righteous deeds?
