What happens to those who reject Allah's messengers?
propositions: Worship Allah and shun false gods.
God guides some people to believe in His Oneness, while others are destined for error.
Traveling through the land will show you the fate of those who deny their messengers.

source_text:
Verse: Even though you ˹O Prophet˺ are keen on their guidance, Allah certainly does not guide those He leaves to stray, and they will have no helpers.

Tafsir: If you O Muhammad (s) are eager for them to be guided when God has already made them go astray you will not be able to achieve this For God does not guide read passive lā yuhdā ? or active lā yahdī he whom He has already sent astray he whom He desires to send astray and they will have no helpers no protectors from God’s chastisement.

hype_questions: Can a person be guided if they are already astray?
What happens to those who are left to stray by Allah?
Is there any protection from Allah's chastisement for those who stray?
propositions: Allah does not guide those He leaves to stray.
God has already made them go astray.
He whom God desires to send astray will be sent astray.
They will have no helpers or protectors from God's chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: They swear by Allah their most solemn oaths that Allah will never raise the dead to life. Yes ˹He will˺! It is a true promise binding on Him, but most people do not know.

Tafsir: And they swear by God their most earnest oaths in other words with their utmost earnestness therein that God will not resurrect the dead. God exalted be He says Nay He will resurrect them it is a promise binding upon Him both wa‘dan and haqqan are verbal nouns used for emphasis and are in the accusative because of the verbal actions implicit in them; in other words He promised that and made it a binding truth but most people that is the people of Mecca do not know that.

hype_questions: Will Allah raise the dead to life?
Is God's promise of resurrection a binding truth?
Do people in Mecca understand the true nature of Allah's promise?
propositions: Allah will not resurrect the dead.
God exalted be He says Nay, He will resurrect them.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He will do that˺ to make clear to them what they disagreed on, and for the disbelievers to know that they were liars.

Tafsir: That He may make clear to them li-yubayyina is semantically connected to an implied yab‘athuhum ‘He will resurrect them’ what they differ with believers in of matters of religion by punishing them and rewarding the believers and that the disbelievers may know that they were liars when they denied the Resurrection.

hype_questions: Will the Resurrection be a reality?
What happens to those who deny the Resurrection?
How will God punish and reward believers?
propositions: God will resurrect the dead.
The disbelievers are liars for denying the Resurrection.
Believers will be punished and rewarded by God.

source_text:
Verse: If We ever will something ˹to exist˺, all We say is: “Be!” And it is!

Tafsir: All that We say to a thing when We will it that is when We will that it come into existence qawlunā is a subject the predicate of which is what follows is to say to it ‘Be’ and it is in other words and that thing is a variant reading for fa-yakūnu has fa-yakūna as a supplement to naqūla. The verse is intended as an affirmation of the power of God to resurrect.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's will in bringing something into existence?
How does God's affirmation of power relate to resurrection?
Can anything be said about the process of creation itself?
propositions: God says 'Be!' when creating a thing, and it exists.
The act of saying 'Be!' is what brings a thing into existence.
God's power is not limited to resurrection alone.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who emigrated in ˹the cause of˺ Allah after being persecuted, We will surely bless them with a good home in this world. But the reward of the Hereafter is far better, if only they knew.

Tafsir: And those who emigrated for God’s cause to establish His religion after they had been wronged through harm those from among the people of Mecca — these were the Prophet s and his Companions — truly We shall lodge them in this world in a goodly lodging namely Medina and the reward of the Hereafter that is Paradise is surely greater grander did they but know that is the disbelievers — or those who stayed behind and did not emigrate — did they but know the honour that belongs to emigrants they would have followed them.

topics: Reward in this world and the Hereafter
hype_questions: What is the reward of emigrating for God's cause?
How will those who stay behind be treated if they knew about the honour of emigrants?
Can staying behind in Mecca guarantee a better life than emigrating?
propositions: Those who emigrated for Allah after being persecuted will receive a good home in this world.
The reward of the Hereafter is far better than what can be received in this world, if only they knew.
Medina is a goodly lodging for those who emigrated for God's cause.
Paradise is greater and grander than what can be received in this world, if only they knew.
Those who stayed behind and did not emigrate would have followed the Prophet s and his Companions if they knew about the honour of emigrants.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It is˺ they who have patiently endured, and in their Lord they put their trust.

Tafsir: They are those who endure the harm inflicted by the idolaters and endure the emigration in order to make manifest the religion and put their trust in their Lord so that He provides for them whence they do not reckon.

hype_questions: What is the significance of patience in Islam?
How does emigration relate to manifesting the religion?
What role does trust play in a Muslim's life?
propositions: They endure harm inflicted by idolaters.
They endure emigration to manifest the religion.
They put their trust in their Lord for provision.

source_text:
Verse: We did not send ˹messengers˺ before you ˹O Prophet˺ except mere men inspired by Us. If you ˹polytheists˺ do not know ˹this already˺, then ask those who have knowledge ˹of the Scriptures˺.

Tafsir: And We did not send before you anything other than men to whom We revealed and sent not angels ‘So ask the followers of the Remembrance those knowledgeable in the Torah and the Gospels; if you do not know’ that then they know it and you are more likely to believe them than the believers are to believe Muhammad (s)

hype_questions: What is the nature of the messengers sent before Prophet Muhammad?
Who should be consulted for knowledge of the Scriptures?
Why are believers more likely to believe in the prophets than in Muhammad?
propositions: We did not send messengers before you except mere men inspired by Us.
Ask those who have knowledge of the Scriptures, if you do not know this already.
The followers of the Remembrance are knowledgeable in the Torah and the Gospels.

source_text:
Verse: ˹We sent them˺ with clear proofs and divine Books. And We have sent down to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Reminder, so that you may explain to people what has been revealed for them, and perhaps they will reflect.

Tafsir: We sent them with clear signs bi’l-bayyināt is semantically connected to an omitted verb namely We sent them with clear arguments and the Books and We have revealed to you the Remembrance the Qur’ān that you may make clear to mankind what has been revealed to them therein in the way of what is lawful and unlawful and that perhaps they might reflect upon this and take heed.

hype_questions: What are the clear arguments sent by God to guide humanity?
How can humans understand the Remembrance (Qur'ān) and its teachings?
What is the purpose of reflecting on divine guidance?
propositions: We sent them with clear signs.
We have revealed to you the Remembrance (Qur'ān).
You may explain to people what has been revealed for them.

source_text:
Verse: Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them? Or that the torment will not come upon them in ways they cannot comprehend?

Tafsir: Do they feel secure those who have schemed evil schemes against the Prophet s at the Council Assembly schemes such as detaining him killing him or banishing him as mentioned in sūrat al-Anfāl Q. 830 that God will not cause the earth to swallow them as God did with Qārūn Q. 2881 or that the chastisement will not come upon them whence they are not aware of? that is in a way which would not occur to them. Indeed they were destroyed at Badr even though they had never anticipated it.

hype_questions: Will Allah punish those who plot against the Prophet?
Can those who scheme evil against others feel secure?
How will Allah deal with those who are unaware of their fate?
propositions: Those who devise evil plots do not feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them.
The torment will not come upon them in ways they cannot comprehend.
God did with Qārūn
God did with Qārūn
Indeed they were destroyed at Badr even though they had never anticipated it.

source_text:
Verse: Or that He will not seize them while they go about ˹their day˺, for then they will have no escape?

Tafsir: Or that He will not seize them in their going to and fro during their travels for commerce whereupon they will not be able to escape? whereupon they will not be able to elude the chastisement.

hype_questions: Will Allah seize us while we are traveling for commerce?
Can we escape from Allah's chastisement?
What happens if Allah does not seize us during our daily activities?
propositions: Allah will not seize them while they go about their day.
If Allah does not seize them, then they will have no escape.
They will not be able to elude the chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Or that He will not destroy them gradually? But your Lord is truly Ever Gracious, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: Or that He will not seize them amid growing fear? amid a gradual diminishing of their numbers little by little until all are destroyed ‘alā takhawwufin is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb God or the object. Indeed then your Lord is Gentle Merciful insofar as He does not hasten for them their punishment.

hype_questions: Will Allah destroy us gradually?
Is Allah gentle and merciful towards His servants?
What is the nature of Allah's mercy?
propositions: Allah will not destroy them gradually.
Your Lord is truly Ever Gracious, Most Merciful.
Allah does not hasten for them their punishment.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not considered how the shadows of everything Allah has created incline to the right and the left ˹as the sun moves˺, totally submitting to Allah in all humility?

Tafsir: Or have they not observed the things which God has created which cast a shadow such as trees or a mountain how their shadows incline to the right and to the left shamā’il is the plural of shimāl in other words towards both sides at the beginning of the day and at its end prostrating to God sujjadan is a circumstantial qualifier that is to say subservient to Him with respect to what is required of them and how they the shadows are subject? humbled they the shadows are likened to rational beings in this description.

hype_questions: Do shadows have a tendency to incline towards both sides?
How do the shadows of created objects behave in relation to Allah?
Can shadows be likened to rational beings?
propositions: The shadows of everything Allah has created incline to the right and the left.
God's creations cast a shadow that inclines towards both sides at the beginning and end of the day.
Shadows are subject to submission to God, subservient to Him with respect to what is required of them.

source_text:
Verse: And to Allah ˹alone˺ bows down ˹in submission˺ whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of living creatures, as do the angels—who are not too proud ˹to do so˺.

Tafsir: And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of living creatures that is of every single thing that moves thereupon; in other words to Him it everything is subservient in terms of what is required of it — most of what is given by way of example is non-rational since these are the more numerous — and the angels also prostrate — these are singled out for mention because of their merit — and they are not arrogant they do not disdain to worship Him.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate authority that all living creatures bow down to?
How do angels demonstrate their devotion to God?
What is the significance of prostration in Islam?
propositions: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of living creatures bows down to Allah.
The angels also prostrate before Allah, demonstrating their merit and humility.
All living creatures are subservient to Allah in terms of what is required of them.

source_text:
Verse: They fear their Lord above them, and do whatever they are commanded.

Tafsir: They that is the angels fear yakhāfūna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person governing the verb yastakbirūna ‘they are not arrogant’ their Lord from above them min fawqihim is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the suffixed pronoun -hum of fawqihim in other words they fear their Lord being High above them with the power to subjugate and they do what they are commanded to do.

hype_questions: What happens when an individual fears their Lord above them?
How does one demonstrate humility in their actions?
What is the consequence of obeying a higher power?
propositions: They fear their Lord being High above them with the power to subjugate.
They do what they are commanded to do.
The angels fear their Lord from above them.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah has said, “Do not take two gods. There is only One God. So be in awe of Me ˹alone˺.”

Tafsir: And God has said ‘Do not choose two gods ithnayn is for emphasis. Truly there is only One God — He has added this statement to affirm His Divinity and Oneness — so be in awe of Me alone’ fear Me to the exclusion of anyone else — herein is a shift from the third person to the first.

hype_questions: What does it mean to fear Allah alone?
How does the concept of monotheism relate to human behavior?
What is the significance of affirming Divine Divinity?
propositions: Allah has said, 'Do not take two gods.'
There is only One God.
So be in awe of Me alone.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him ˹alone˺ is the everlasting devotion. Will you then fear any other than Allah?

Tafsir: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth as possessions creatures and servants. And to Him belongs the religion the obedience that endures the one everlasting wāsiban is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-dīn ‘the religion’ and is operated by the sense of the adverbial clause. Will you then fear any other than God? when He is the True God other than Whom there is no god the interrogative is a statement of rejection and rebuke.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's devotion?
How does obedience relate to one's relationship with God?
What is the significance of rejecting other deities?
propositions: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.
The everlasting devotion belongs to Allah alone.
Will you then fear any other than Allah?
Allah is the True God, other than Whom there is no god.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever blessings you have are from Allah. Then whenever hardship touches you, to Him ˹alone˺ you cry ˹for help˺.

Tafsir: Whatever grace you have it is from God none but He brings it mā ‘whatever’ is either a conditional or relative particle. Then when misfortune poverty or illness befalls you to Him you cry for help to Him you raise your voices with pleas for help and supplications and you do not call upon any other than Him.

hype_questions: What is the source of blessings?
How should one respond to hardship?
Who should be called upon for help in times of need?
propositions: Whatever blessings you have are from Allah.
When misfortune, poverty, or illness befalls you, you cry out to Him for help.
You do not call upon any other than Him.

source_text:
Verse: Then as soon as He removes the hardship from you, a group of you associates ˹others˺ with their Lord ˹in worship˺,

Tafsir: Then when He has rid you of the misfortune behold a group of you attribute partners to their Lord

hype_questions: What happens when hardship is removed?
How do people respond after being freed from misfortune?
What does it mean to attribute partners to one's Lord?
propositions: When hardship is removed, some individuals associate others with their Lord in worship.
After being freed from misfortune, a group of people attribute partners to their Lord.

source_text:
Verse: only returning Our favours with ingratitude. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.

Tafsir: in order to deny that grace which We have given them. So enjoy that consent of yours to worship idols an imperative meant as a threat for soon you shall know the consequence of this.

hype_questions: What happens when we deny Allah's favours with ingratitude?
Will we face a consequence for our actions towards idols?
How will we understand the outcome of our worship?
propositions: We have given them Our favours but they return with ingratitude.
Enjoy yourselves now, for you will soon know the consequence of your actions.
Your consent to worship idols is an imperative that carries a threat.

source_text:
Verse: And they ˹even˺ assign to those ˹idols˺—who know nothing—a share of what We have provided for them. By Allah! You will certainly be questioned about whatever ˹lies˺ you used to fabricate ˹against Allah˺.

Tafsir: And they that is the idolaters assign to what they do not know that they cause harm and cannot benefit them — namely the idols — a portion of that which We have provided them with of crops and cattle saying that ‘this is for God and this is for our partners’. By God you will indeed be questioned a questioning of rebuke; there is a shift herein from the third to the second person about what you used to fabricate against God such as claiming that He commanded you to do this.

hype_questions: What is the nature of idols and their role in human life?
How do people justify claiming that idols are for God when they know nothing about them?
Will individuals be held accountable for fabricating claims against Allah?
propositions: Idols cause harm but cannot benefit humans.
Humans assign a portion of the provision given to them to idols, despite knowing nothing about them.
By Allah, you will be questioned about whatever lies you used to fabricate against Allah.

source_text:
Verse: And they attribute ˹angels as˺ daughters to Allah—glory be to Him!—the opposite of what they desire for themselves.

Tafsir: And they assign to God daughters by claiming that the angels are the daughters of God — Be He glorified! — a declaration that He is exalted above that which they claim — while they will have what they desire namely sons the status of this sentence is either independent nominative or that of an accusative object of the verb yaj‘alūna ‘they assign’. The meaning is that to Him they assign daughters to whom they are averse when in any case He is exalted beyond having offspring while to themselves they assign sons of their own choosing so that the best is theirs exclusively — like where God says Now ask them are daughters to be for your Lord while sons are to be for them? Q. 37149.

hype_questions: Do angels have daughters?
What is the status of angels in Islamic theology?
Can humans assign sons to God?
propositions: They attribute angels as daughters to Allah.
God is exalted above having offspring.
Humans assign sons to themselves, but not to God.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever one of them is given the good news of a baby girl, his face grows gloomy, as he suppresses his rage.

Tafsir: And when one of them is given the tidings of a girl that will be born to him his face becomes darkened transformed like that of one suddenly struck by grief and he chokes inwardly filled with anguish so how is it that daughters are attributed to Him exalted be He?

hype_questions: How can a being of immense power and wisdom experience grief over the birth of a daughter?
Why does the face of one who receives news of a girl's birth become darkened?
What is the nature of the anguish that fills the heart of one who is given tidings of a girl's birth?
propositions: When someone learns they are having a baby girl, their face becomes gloomy.
The face of someone who receives news of a girl's birth darkens and they choke inwardly with anguish.
It is not possible for God to experience grief or anguish over the birth of a daughter.

source_text:
Verse: He hides himself from the people because of the bad news he has received. Should he keep her in disgrace, or bury her ˹alive˺ in the ground? Evil indeed is their judgment!

Tafsir: He hides disappearing from people that is from his people out of distress at the tidings given to him fearing mockery unsure what to do with it the newborn shall he retain it — refrain from killing it — in humiliation enduring shame and disgrace or trample into the dust by burying it alive. Verily wretched is what they judge evil is this judgement of theirs in which they ascribe to their Creator that His are the daughters who have such a lowly status in their eyes.

hype_questions: Should one keep a newborn in disgrace, or bury it alive?
What is the appropriate course of action for someone who has received bad news and is unsure what to do with it?
Is it wretched to judge someone as evil based on their status?
propositions: He hides himself from the people because of the bad news he has received.
The newborn should be retained, not killed.
Humiliation and disgrace are worse than burying the child alive.
Their judgment is evil and ascribes a lowly status to Allah's daughters.

source_text:
Verse: To those who disbelieve in the Hereafter belong all evil qualities, whereas to Allah belong the finest attributes. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter namely for the disbelievers there is an evil description in other words theirs is the most evil attribute meaning the most vile which is their burying alive of newborn girls despite the fact that they are needed for the purposes of marriage; and the loftiest description belongs to God His is the attribute most sublime namely that there is no god except Him. And He is the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His creation.

hype_questions: What is the nature of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter?
How do the actions of disbelievers reflect their true attributes?
What is the most sublime attribute that belongs to God?
propositions: To Allah belong the finest attributes.
The loftiest description belongs to God.
There is no god except Him.

source_text:
Verse: If Allah were to punish people ˹immediately˺ for their wrongdoing, He would not have left a single living being on earth. But He delays them for an appointed term. And when their time arrives, they cannot delay it for a moment, nor could they advance it.

Tafsir: And if God were to take mankind to task for their wrongdoing wrongdoing through acts of disobedience He would not leave upon it that is upon the earth any living being any single living thing moving upon it; but He gives them respite until an appointed term; and when their term comes they will not defer from it by a single hour nor advance it.

hype_questions: What would happen if Allah were to punish people immediately for their wrongdoing?
Why does Allah give humans respite before punishing them?
What will happen when a person's appointed term arrives?
propositions: If Allah were to punish people immediately for their wrongdoing, He would not have left a single living being on earth.
Allah gives humans respite until an appointed term.
When a person's appointed term arrives, they cannot delay it for a moment nor could they advance it.

source_text:
Verse: They attribute to Allah what they hate ˹for themselves˺, and their tongues utter the lie that they will have the finest reward. Without a doubt, for them is the Fire, where they will be abandoned.

Tafsir: Still they assign to God what they dislike for themselves — such as daughters partners in power and the mistreatment of messengers. And their tongues despite this relate tell the lie which is that theirs will be the best reward with God namely Paradise as He God states in their words elsewhere ‘And in case I am returned to my Lord I will indeed have the best reward with Him’ Q. 4150. But God exalted be He says Without any doubt — verily — theirs shall be the Fire and they shall be abandoned therein or it mufratūn means that they shall be foremost in entering it a variant reading for mufratūn has mufritūn meaning that ‘they transgress the bounds’.

hype_questions: What happens to those who attribute false attributes to Allah?
Will those who deceive themselves about their reward be rewarded in Paradise?
How do those who transgress the bounds of Allah end up?
propositions: They attribute to Allah what they hate.
Their tongues utter the lie that they will have the finest reward.
Without a doubt, for them is the Fire, where they will be abandoned.
God exalted be He says Without any doubt — verily — theirs shall be the Fire and they shall be abandoned therein.

source_text:
Verse: By Allah! We have surely sent messengers to communities before you ˹O Prophet˺, but Satan made their misdeeds appealing to them. So he is their patron today, and they will suffer a painful punishment.

Tafsir: By God We verily sent to communities before you messengers. But Satan adorned for them their deeds their evil deeds so that they considered them to be good deeds and therefore they denied the messengers. So he is their patron the guardian of their affairs today that is now in this world and for them there will be a painful chastisement in the Hereafter. It is also said that by al-yawm ‘today’ is meant the Day of Resurrection narrating the events as though they are taking place now. In other words they have no guardian other than him in other words Satan and as he is incapable of helping himself how could he possibly help them?

hype_questions: What is the role of Satan in tempting humans?
How do messengers get rejected by communities?
What will be the punishment for those who deny the messengers?
propositions: Allah sent messengers to communities before you.
Satan made their misdeeds appealing to them.
They considered their evil deeds as good deeds and denied the messengers.
Satan is their patron today, guardian of their affairs in this world.
There will be a painful chastisement for those who deny the messengers in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: We have revealed to you the Book only to clarify for them what they differed about, and as a guide and mercy for those who believe.

Tafsir: And We have not revealed to you O Muhammad (s) the Book the Qur’ān except for the purpose that you may make clear to them to mankind that wherein they differ in the matter of religion and as a guidance wa-hudan is a supplement to wa-li-tubayyina ‘and that you may make clear’ and as a mercy for a people who believe in it.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the Quran?
How does the Quran guide people in matters of religion?
What is the role of mercy in the Quran?
propositions: We have revealed to you the Book only to clarify for them what they differed about.
And We have not revealed to you O Muhammad (s) the Book the Qur'an except for the purpose that you may make clear to mankind that wherein they differ in the matter of religion and as a guidance.
wa-hudan is a supplement to wa-li-tubayyina 'and that you may make clear' and as a mercy for a people who believe in it.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah sends down rain from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death. Surely in this is a sign for those who listen.

Tafsir: And God sends down water from the heaven and therewith revives the earth with plants after its death after its drying up. Surely in that which is mentioned there is a sign indicating the truth of the Resurrection for a people who listen listening and then reflecting.

hype_questions: What is the significance of rain in bringing life to the earth?
How does the Quran relate to the concept of Resurrection?
What role do plants play in the process of creation?
propositions: Allah sends down rain from the sky.
The earth dies after its death, but is revived with plants.
There is a sign indicating the truth of the Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: And there is certainly a lesson for you in cattle: We give you to drink of what is in their bellies, from between digested food and blood: pure milk, pleasant to drink.

Tafsir: And truly for you there is in the cattle a lesson an example to learn from. We give you to drink — this introduces the explanation of the ‘lesson’ — of that which is in their bellies the cattle’s bellies from min indicates a new subject and is semantically connected to nusqīkum ‘We give you to drink’ between the refuse the intestinal waste and the blood pure milk uncontaminated by either the refuse or the blood neither in its taste odour or colour even though it the milk is situated between the two palatable to drinkers easily passing down their throats not causing any choking.

hype_questions: What is the lesson we can learn from cattle?
How do we benefit from drinking milk from cattle?
Why is pure milk from cattle considered pleasant to drink?
propositions: We give you to drink of what is in their bellies.
The milk is situated between the refuse and the blood.
It is palatable to drinkers easily passing down their throats not causing any choking.

source_text:
Verse: And from the fruits of palm trees and grapevines you derive intoxicants as well as wholesome provision. Surely in this is a sign for those who understand.

Tafsir: And of the fruits of date-palms and vines comes forth a fruit from which you draw an intoxicant a wine that intoxicates — it the wine is referred to by the verbal noun sakaran ‘intoxicant’ and this verse came before it was prohibited — and goodly provision such as dates raisins vinegar and molasses. Surely in that which is mentioned there is a sign indicating His power exalted be He for a people who understand a people who reflect.

hype_questions: What is the intoxicant mentioned in this verse?
Why was the intoxicant prohibited later on?
What are some examples of wholesome provision derived from palm trees and grapevines?
propositions: You derive intoxicants and wholesome provision from the fruits of palm trees and grapevines.
The intoxicant mentioned in this verse is referred to by the verbal noun sakaran.
Allah's power is exalted, and there is a sign indicating His power for those who understand.

source_text:
Verse: And your Lord inspired the bees: “Make ˹your˺ homes in the mountains, the trees, and in what people construct,

Tafsir: And your Lord revealed to the bee a revealing effected through inspiration saying an ‘that’ is either explicative or relates to the verbal noun ‘Choose among the hills habitations to which you can resort and among the trees also habitations and among the trellises which they raise that is the places which humans build for you — for otherwise it the bee would not resort to these places.

hype_questions: What are the suitable places for bees to make their homes?
Why do bees choose certain locations over others?
How do humans contribute to the bee's decision on where to build its habitat?
propositions: Your Lord inspired the bees to make their homes in mountains, trees, and human-built structures.
The bee was instructed by its Lord to choose habitations among hills, trees, and trellises.
Humans provide suitable locations for bees to build their habitats.

source_text:
Verse: and feed from ˹the flower of˺ any fruit ˹you please˺ and follow the ways your Lord has made easy for you.” From their bellies comes forth liquid of varying colours, in which there is healing for people. Surely in this is a sign for those who reflect.

Tafsir: Then eat from every kind of fruit and follow enter the ways of your Lord follow His paths in seeking pastures ways made easily accessible’ dhululan is the plural of dhalūl and is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-subul ‘the ways’ in other words those paths disposed for you such that they pose no difficulty for you even if it should be rough terrain and such that you would not lose your way when returning therefrom even if it be far away; it dhululan is also said to be a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person of the pronominal suffix of fa’slukī ‘you follow’ meaning in this case follow those paths in compliance with what is required of you. There comes forth from their bellies a drink namely honey of diverse hues wherein is a cure for mankind from all ailments; it is also said that it means that it is a cure only for some ailments as indicated by the indefinite noun shifā’un ‘a cure’; or that it is a cure for all ailments when supplemented with some other remedy; or without these other remedies but with the resolve niyya to get better. The Prophet s used to prescribe it for anyone suffering from stomach pains as reported by the two Shaykhs Bukhārī and Muslim. Surely in that there is a sign for a people who reflect upon God’s handiwork exalted be He.

hype_questions: What is the significance of following one's Lord's paths in seeking pastures?
How does honey from different fruits contribute to human health?
What role does resolve (niyya) play in recovery from ailments?
propositions: Eat from every kind of fruit and follow your Lord's ways.
There is healing in the liquid that comes forth from their bellies.
The Prophet s prescribed honey for stomach pains when accompanied by resolve.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has created you, and then causes you to die. And some of you are left to reach the most feeble stage of life so that they may know nothing after having known much. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Most Capable.

Tafsir: And God has created you when you were nothing then He takes you in death when your terms of life are concluded; and there are some among you who are relegated to the most abject stage of life that is the most diminished because of old-age and senility so that he knows nothing after having possessed some knowledge. ‘Ikrima said ‘Whoever recites the Qur’ān will not come to such a predicament’. God is Knowing of how to manage the affairs of His creation Powerful in doing what He will.

hype_questions: What happens to us after we die?
How does old age affect our knowledge and abilities?
Can reciting the Qur'an prevent a decline in mental capacity?
propositions: Allah creates humans when they are nothing.
Allah takes humans away when their life terms are concluded.
Some people are left with minimal knowledge after old age due to senility.
Reciting the Qur'an can prevent a decline in mental capacity.
God is All-Knowing and Powerful in managing His creation's affairs.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision. But those who have been much favoured would not share their wealth with those ˹bondspeople˺ in their possession, making them their equals. Do they then deny Allah’s favours?

Tafsir: And God has favoured some of you above others in respect of provision thus some of you are poor some are rich some owners others are owned. Now those who have been more favoured namely the masters would not hand over their provision to those slaves whom their right hands possess that is they would not assign that wealth and other things which We have given them as something to be shared equally between them and their slaves so that they that is the slaves and their masters become equal partners in respect thereof. The meaning is they do not have partners from among their slaves in respect of their wealth so how can they make certain of God’s servants partners of His? Is it then the grace of God that they deny? that they reject when they ascribe partners to Him?

hype_questions: Do the wealthy deny God's favours by not sharing their wealth with others?
Can those who are favoured by God truly claim to be equal partners with their slaves in terms of wealth?
Is it possible for someone to reject God's grace while ascribing partners to Him?
propositions: Allah has favoured some individuals over others in provision.
Those who have been much favoured will not share their wealth with those in their possession, making them equal.
The wealthy do not assign their wealth and other things given by Allah as something to be shared equally between themselves and their slaves.
The slaves and their masters become equal partners in respect of their wealth only if they are truly partners with Allah.
It is not possible for someone to reject God's grace while ascribing partners to Him.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah has made for you spouses of your own kind, and given you through your spouses children and grandchildren. And He has granted you good, lawful provisions. Are they then faithful to falsehood and ungrateful for Allah’s favours?

Tafsir: And God made for you mates from your own selves thus He created Eve from Adam’s rib and created all mankind from the seminal fluids of men and women and made for you from your mates children and grandchildren and He provided you with the good things of all kinds of fruits seeds and animals. Is it then in falsehood in the idol that they believe and in the grace of God that they disbelieve? when they associate others with God?

hype_questions: Do people believe in falsehood and disbelieve in God's grace?
Is it wrong to associate others with God?
Does God provide good things for us?
propositions: Allah made spouses of one's own kind.
Eve was created from Adam's rib.
Mankind is created from seminal fluids of men and women.
Children and grandchildren are from mates.
God provides good provisions.
People believe in falsehood and disbelieve in God's grace when they associate others with God.

source_text:
Verse: Yet they worship besides Allah those ˹idols˺ who do not afford them any provision from the heavens and the earth, nor do they have the power to.

Tafsir: And they worship besides God that is other than Him what has no power to give them any sort of provision from the heavens such as water and the earth such as plants shay’an ‘anything’ is a substitute for rizqan ‘provision’ nor do they have the capacity nor are they able to do anything — and these are the idols.

hype_questions: What is the nature of idols worshipped by non-believers?
How do idols provide for their worshipers?
Can idols grant any sort of provision?
propositions: They worship besides Allah other deities that have no power to provide them with provisions from the heavens or earth.
Idols are unable to give their worshipers any form of sustenance.
These idols possess no capacity for action or ability.

source_text:
Verse: So do not set up equals to Allah, for Allah certainly knows and you do not know.

Tafsir: So do not strike any similitude for God do not ascribe to God likenesses and then associate them with Him in power. Truly God knows that there is nothing like Him and you do not know this.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of ascribing likenesses to God?
Can anything be compared to the power and attributes of God?
How does one understand the limits of human knowledge when it comes to God's nature?
propositions: Do not strike any similitude for God.
Ascribe not to God likenesses.
Associate not with Him in power those things which He has created.

source_text:
Verse: Allah sets forth a parable: a slave who lacks all means, compared to a ˹free˺ man to whom We granted a good provision, of which he donates ˹freely,˺ openly and secretly. Are they equal? Praise be to Allah. In fact, most of them do not know.

Tafsir: God strikes a similitude mathalan this is substituted by the following ‘abdan mamlūkan a slave who is a chattel mamlūkan an adjective to distinguish him this type of slave from a free man who is the servant of God alone having no power over anything since he has no mastery and one on whom man is an indefinite noun adjectivally qualified in other words a free man We have bestowed a fair provision from Us such that he spends thereof secretly and openly that is disposing of it as he wishes the first similitude is for the idols while the second is His exalted be He. Are they equal? the powerless slaves and the dispensing free men? No. Praise belongs to God alone. But most of them that is the people of Mecca do not know the chastisement they will come to and so they associate others with God.

hype_questions: Does one who is enslaved to God have the same level of freedom as someone who has wealth and power?
Can a person truly be equal to another if they have different levels of provision from God?
What happens to those who do not recognize the power and chastisement of God?
propositions: Allah sets forth a parable: a slave who lacks all means, compared to a free man to whom Allah granted a good provision.
Most of the people of Mecca do not know the chastisement they will come to and so they associate others with God.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah sets forth a parable of two men: one of them is dumb, incapable of anything. He is a burden on his master. Wherever he is sent, he brings no good. Can such a person be equal to the one who commands justice and is on the Straight Path?

Tafsir: And God strikes a similitude mathalan this is substituted by the following rajulayn two men one of whom is dumb from birth having no power over anything as he cannot understand nor be understood and who is a liability burdensome to his master — the legal guardian of his affairs — wherever he directs him he does not bring therefrom any good he does not succeed and this is the similitude of the disbeliever. Is he that is the dumb one mentioned equal to one who enjoins justice that is to one who is able to speak of benefit to people since he enjoins it justice and encourages others to it and follows a path a way that is straight? — this being the second man the believer — No he is not equal to him. It is also said that this last similitude is a similitude of God while the similitude of the dumb one is of the idols so that the preceding verse contains the similitude of the disbeliever and the believer.

hype_questions: Can a person who brings no good be equal to one who commands justice and follows the Straight Path?
Is it possible for someone who is burdened on their master to be considered equal to one who enjoins justice and encourages others to do so?
What is the similitude of God compared to that of a disbeliever?
propositions: Allah sets forth a parable of two men: one of them is dumb, incapable of anything.
The dumb man is a burden on his master and brings no good wherever he is sent.
One who commands justice and follows the Straight Path is not equal to the dumb man.
The similitude of the disbeliever is the dumb man.
God strikes a similitude that is substituted by two men: one of whom is dumb from birth.

source_text:
Verse: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs ˹the knowledge of˺ the unseen in the heavens and the earth. Bringing about the Hour would only take the blink of an eye, or even less. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: And to God belongs the Unseen of the heavens and the earth in other words the knowledge of what is hidden in them. And the matter of the Hour is but as the twinkling of an eye or it is even nearer since it takes place as a result of the words ‘Be’ and it is kun fa-yakūn. Truly God has power over all things.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's knowledge of the unseen?
How does the Hour relate to Allah's power?
What is the significance of the words 'Be' and 'kun fa-yakūn' in understanding the Hour?
propositions: Allah possesses knowledge of the unseen in the heavens and earth.
The Hour is near, occurring as a result of Allah's words 'Be'.
God has power over all things.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing, and gave you hearing, sight, and intellect so perhaps you would be thankful.

Tafsir: And God brought you forth from the bellies of your mothers while you did not know anything the statement lā ta‘lamūna shay’an ‘while you did not know anything’ is a circumstantial qualifier and He gave you hearing and sight and hearts that perhaps you might give thanks to Him for this gift and become believers.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of being given hearing, sight, and intellect?
How should one respond to these gifts from Allah?
What does it mean to be thankful to Allah?
propositions: Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers.
He gave you hearing, sight, and intellect.
Perhaps you would be thankful.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not seen the birds glide in the open sky? None holds them up except Allah. Surely in this are signs for those who believe.

Tafsir: Have they not observed the birds how they are made subservient disposed to be able to fly in the air of heaven? that is in the air between the heaven and the earth. Nothing holds them when they draw in their wings or open them lest they fall except God by His power. Indeed in that there are signs for a people who believe the signs which are that they have been created in a way that enables them to fly as well as the creation of the air in such a way that it allows for flight and the holding of them up in the air so that they do not fall.

hype_questions: What is the reason behind birds' ability to fly?
How do birds stay suspended in the air without falling?
What enables birds to glide effortlessly through the sky?
propositions: Birds are made subservient and disposed to be able to fly in the air of heaven.
Nothing holds birds when they draw in their wings or open them except God by His power.
There are signs that birds have been created in a way that enables them to fly, and the creation of the air allows for flight.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah has made your homes a place to rest, and has given you tents from the hide of animals, light to handle when you travel and when you camp. And out of their wool, fur, and hair He has given you furnishings and goods for a while.

Tafsir: And it is God Who has made for you your homes as a place of rest a place that you can inhabit and He has made for you out of the skins of the cattle homes such as tents and pavilions which you find light to carry on the day of your migration your travel and on the day of your halting; and of their wool that is the sheep’s and their fur that is the camels’ and their hair that is the goats’ He has made for you furniture chattels such as rugs and blankets and wares for you to use for a while until they perish.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Allah's provision for believers?
How does Allah provide for the needs of His servants?
What are some examples of Allah's blessings in everyday life?
propositions: Allah has made homes a place to rest.
Allah has given tents from animal hides that are easy to carry.
Allah has provided furnishings and goods from wool, fur, and hair.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah has provided you shade out of what He created, and has given you shelter in the mountains. He has also provided you with clothes protecting you from the heat ˹and cold˺, and armour shielding you in battle. This is how He perfects His favour upon you, so perhaps you will ˹fully˺ submit ˹to Him˺.

Tafsir: And it is God Who has made for you from what He created of houses trees and clouds shade zilāl is the plural of zill to protect you from the heat of the sun; and He has made for you in the mountains places of refuge aknān is the plural of kinn which is a places where one can seek shelter istakanna such as a cave or a tunnel; and He has made for you garments shirts that protect you from the heat that is and also from the cold and garments that protect you from your mutual violence your warring in other words to protect you from stabbed or struck during these instances garments such as coats of mail and armour plates. So in the same way that He has created these things He perfects His favour — in this world — to you by creating that of which you have need so that you O people of Mecca might submit that you might affirm His Oneness.

hype_questions: What are some ways Allah has provided for our protection?
How does Allah perfect His favour upon us?
What is the ultimate goal of submitting to Allah?
propositions: Allah has provided shade from what He created.
Allah has given shelter in the mountains.
Allah has provided clothes protecting us from heat and cold.
Allah has provided armour shielding us in battle.
Allah perfects His favour upon us by creating things we need.

source_text:
Verse: But if they turn away, then your duty ˹O Prophet˺ is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.

Tafsir: But if they turn away if they reject Islam your duty O Muhammad (s) is only to convey the Message plainly — this was revealed before the command to fight the disbelievers.

hype_questions: What is the duty of a prophet when people reject his message?
How should a prophet convey his message to those who refuse to listen?
What happens if a prophet's message is not accepted by the people?
propositions: If they turn away, then your duty O Prophet is only to deliver the message clearly.
Your duty O Muhammad (s) is only to convey the Message plainly when people reject Islam.
The command to fight the disbelievers was given after the revelation of the Message.

source_text:
Verse: They are aware of Allah’s favours, but still deny them. And most of them are ˹truly˺ ungrateful.

Tafsir: They recognise God’s grace that is they affirm that it comes from Him and then deny it by associating others with Him and most of them are ungrateful.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's favours?
How do people respond to Allah's grace?
What is the consequence of denying Allah's favours?
propositions: They recognise God’s grace.
God’s grace comes from Him.
Most of them are ungrateful.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Consider, O  Prophet,˺ the Day We will call ˹a prophet as˺ a witness from every faith-community. Then the disbelievers will neither be allowed to plead nor appease ˹their Lord˺.

Tafsir: And mention the day We shall raise up from every community a witness and this will be it that community’s prophet to bear witness for it and against it and this day is the Day of Resurrection; then the disbelievers will not be given permission to make excuses nor will they be asked to make amends that is nor will they be asked to repent and return to that which pleases God.

hype_questions: What will be the role of a prophet on the Day of Resurrection?
Will disbelievers be given a chance to make excuses or repent on the Day of Resurrection?
How will the community's prophet bear witness for and against it on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: The Prophet will be called as a witness from every faith-community on the Day of Resurrection.
Disbelievers will not be allowed to plead or appease their Lord on the Day of Resurrection.
The community's prophet will bear witness for and against its community on the Day of Resurrection.
The Day of Resurrection is the day when all individuals will be held accountable for their actions.
Disbelievers will not be given permission to make excuses or asked to repent and return to God's pleasure on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: And when the wrongdoers face the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺.

Tafsir: And when those who did wrong those who disbelieved behold the chastisement the Fire it shall not be lightened for them the chastisement nor will they be granted any respite any deferment from it when they see it.

hype_questions: Will the punishment of the wrongdoers be lightened for them?
Can they be granted any respite or deferment from the punishment?
What will happen to those who disbelieve when they see the chastisement?
propositions: When the wrongdoers face the punishment, it will not be lightened for them.
The Fire is a chastisement that shall not be lightened for those who did wrong and those who disbelieved.
Those who disbelieve shall see the chastisement and know that they will not be granted any respite or deferment from it.

source_text:
Verse: And when the polytheists see their associate-gods, they will say, “Our Lord! These are our associate-gods that we used to invoke besides You.” Their gods will throw a rebuttal at them, ˹saying,˺ “You are definitely liars.”

Tafsir: And when the idolaters behold their associates of devils and others they will say ‘Our Lord these are our associates whom we used to invoke whom we used to worship besides You’. But they will fling to them the saying that is they will say to them ‘You are indeed liars!’ when you say that you used to worship us — as is stated by them in another verse ‘It was not us that they worshipped’ Q. 2863; and also in the verse They will deny their worship of them Q. 1982.

hype_questions: What happens when polytheists see their associate-gods?
Why do the gods of polytheists reject their worship?
How do polytheists respond to being called liars by their gods?
propositions: Polytheists will invoke their associate-gods when they see them.
The gods of polytheists will deny their worship of those associate-gods.
Polytheists are liars if they claim to worship the same gods as before.

source_text:
Verse: They will offer ˹full˺ submission to Allah on that Day, and whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them.

Tafsir: And they will offer submission to God on that day that is they will have surrendered to His judgement and that which they used to invent in the way of claiming that their gods intercede for them will fail forsake them.

hype_questions: Will people be able to offer true submission to God on the Day of Judgement?
How will people's fabricated gods fail them on that day?
What happens to those who claim their gods intercede for them?
propositions: They will offer full submission to Allah on that Day.
Whatever gods they fabricated will fail them.
Their claims of godly intercession will be forsaken.

source_text:
Verse: For those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, We will add more punishment to their punishment for all the corruption they spread.

Tafsir: Those who disbelieve and bar people from the way of God from His religion them We shall add chastisement to their chastisement that chastisement which they have merited for their disbelief — Ibn Mas‘ūd said ‘Their chastisment will consist of scorpions whose fangs are as long as the tallest palm trees’ — because of the corruption they used to cause by their barring people from belief.

hype_questions: What happens to those who disbelieve and hinder others from the Way of Allah?
How will the punishment be added for those who spread corruption?
What is the chastisement that awaits those who bar people from belief?
propositions: For those who disbelieve, We will add more punishment to their punishment.
Those who disbelieve and bar people from the way of God from His religion shall have added chastisement to their chastisement.
Their chastisement consists of scorpions whose fangs are as long as the tallest palm trees.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Consider, O  Prophet,˺ the Day We will call against every faith-community a witness of their own. And We will call you to be a witness against these ˹people of yours˺. We have revealed to you the Book as an explanation of all things, a guide, a mercy, and good news for those who ˹fully˺ submit.

Tafsir: And mention the day We shall raise up from every community a witness against them from among themselves and this will be their that community’s prophet and We shall bring you O Muhammad (s) as a witness against these namely your people. And We have revealed to you the Book the Qur’ān as a clarification of all things that people might need concerning the Law and as a guidance from error and a mercy and good tidings of Paradise to those who submit those who affirm the Oneness of God.

hype_questions: What is the significance of being a witness in Islam?
How does the Quran serve as a guide for humanity?
What are the consequences of not submitting to God's will?
propositions: The Day of Judgment will call every faith-community against themselves a witness from among their own.
The Prophet Muhammad (s) will be called upon to testify against his people on the Day of Judgment.
The Quran has been revealed as an explanation, guide, mercy, and good news for those who submit to God's will.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Allah commands justice, grace, as well as courtesy to close relatives. He forbids indecency, wickedness, and aggression. He instructs you so perhaps you will be mindful.

Tafsir: Indeed God enjoins justice — that is affirmation of His Oneness or actually being fair and virtue performance of the religious obligations or that you should worship God as if you were able to see Him as reported in the hadīth; and giving to kinsfolk — He has singled it kinship out for mention by way of highlighting its importance — and He forbids lewdness fornication and abomination with regard to the stipulations of the Law abomination such as disbelief and acts of disobedience and aggression wrongdoing against people — He also singles this out for mention by way of showing its importance; just as He began with the mention of ‘lewdness’ in this way He admonishes you through commands and prohibitions so that you might remember that you might be admonished tadhakkarūna ‘you might remember’ the original tā’ of tatadhakkarūna has been assimilated with the dhāl. In the Mustadrak of al-Hākim al-Naysābūrī it is reported from Ibn Mas‘ūd that he said ‘This verse is the most comprehensive verse in the Qur’ān in terms of what is good and what is evil’.

hype_questions: What is the importance of justice in Islam?
How does Allah define fairness and virtue?
What are some examples of abomination in Islam?
propositions: Allah commands justice.
Justice means affirmation of His Oneness or being fair.
God enjoins giving to kinsfolk as a religious obligation.
He forbids lewdness, fornication, and abomination.
Disbelief and acts of disobedience are considered abomination.
Aggression is wrongdoing against people.
Allah instructs you so that you may be mindful.

source_text:
Verse: Honour Allah’s covenant when you make a pledge, and do not break your oaths after confirming them, having made Allah your guarantor. Surely Allah knows all you do.

Tafsir: And fulfil God’s covenant effected by way of pledges of allegiance and oaths and in other ways when you made a covenant and do not break your oaths after pledging them and having made God surety over you that you will fulfill the covenant for you have sworn the oath by Him the sentence wa-qad ja‘altumu’Llāha ‘alaykum kafīlan ‘and having made God surety over you’ is a circumstantial qualifier. Truly God knows what you do — this is a threat for them.

hype_questions: What happens when you break your oaths after making a pledge?
How does Allah feel about being surety for someone's covenant?
What is the consequence of not fulfilling one's covenant?
propositions: Honour Allah’s covenant when you make a pledge.
Do not break your oaths after confirming them, having made Allah your guarantor.
You have sworn the oath by Him and God knows what you do.

source_text:
Verse: Do not be like the woman who ˹foolishly˺ unravels her yarn after it is firmly spun, by taking your oaths as a means of deceiving one another in favour of a stronger group. Surely Allah tests you through this. And on the Day of Judgment He will certainly make your differences clear to you.

Tafsir: And do not be like her who undoes spoils her yarn that which she has spun after having made it strong having set and spun it breaking it up into fibres ankāthan is a circumstantial qualifier ankāth is the plural of nikth and means that which is undone yunkathu — this was an imbecile Meccan woman who used to spin all day and then undo it — by making tattakhidhūna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person of the verb takūnū ‘do not be like’ in other words what is meant is ‘do not be like her by making’ your oaths a means of deceit dakhal is what enters yadkhulu into something but does not belong to it in other words as a means of causing mischief or as trickery between you by breaking these oaths so that one group may become more numerous than another group. They used to enter into an alliance with a given group but if they encountered another more numerous and more powerful group they would renege on their alliance with the former and forge a new alliance with these latter. God only tries tests you thereby in other words by that which He enjoins in the way of fulfilling the covenant so that He may observe the obedient and the disobedient among you or when it is the case that one group is more numerous than another that He may observe whether you fulfil your obligation to them or not; and certainly He will make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that wherein you used to differ during the life of this world with regard to covenants and otherwise by punishing he who reneged and rewarding he who was faithful to his covenant.

hype_questions: What happens when we use oaths as a means of deceiving others?
How does Allah test us through our actions and covenants?
What will happen to those who reneg on their alliances and what about those who are faithful?
propositions: Do not take your oaths as a means of deceiving one another.
Allah tests you by making you fulfill or renege on your covenants.
God will punish those who reneged on their alliances and reward those who were faithful.

source_text:
Verse: Had Allah willed, He could have easily made you one community ˹of believers˺, but He leaves to stray whoever He wills and guides whoever He wills. And you will certainly be questioned about what you used to do.

Tafsir: For if God had willed He could have made you one community people of a single religion but He leads astray whom He will and guides whom He will and you will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection a questioning of rebuke about what you used to do so that you might be requited for it.

hype_questions: Is God's will the ultimate authority over human destiny?
Can humans truly choose their own path in life?
What happens to individuals after death, according to Islamic teachings?
propositions: Had Allah willed, He could have easily made you one community of believers.
He leaves to stray whoever He wills and guides whoever He wills.
You will certainly be questioned about what you used to do.

source_text:
Verse: And do not take your oaths as a means of deceiving one another or your feet will slip after they have been firm. Then you will taste the evil ˹consequences˺ of hindering ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, and you will suffer a tremendous punishment.

Tafsir: And do not make your oaths a means of deceit between you — He repeats this here for emphasis — lest a foot should slip that is lest your feet should slip off the path of Islam after being steady having been set upon it and lest you should taste evil that is chastisement forasmuch as you barred people from the way of God in other words for your refraining to fulfil covenants or barring others from doing this since your custom once established will be followed by others and there be a tremendous chastisement for you in the Hereafter.

topics: Consequences of hindering others from the Way of Allah
hype_questions: What happens when we deceive others with our oaths?
How will we be punished if we hinder others from following the way of Allah?
What consequences will we face in the Hereafter if we bar others from the path of God?
propositions: Do not take your oaths as a means of deceiving one another.
Your feet will slip after they have been firm if you deceive others with your oaths.
You will taste the evil consequences of hindering others from the Way of Allah.
You will suffer a tremendous punishment if you hinder others from following the way of Allah.
If you bar others from the path of God, your custom once established will be followed by others.
There will be a tremendous chastisement for you in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: And do not trade Allah’s covenant for a fleeting gain. What is with Allah is certainly far better for you, if only you knew.

Tafsir: And do not sell God’s covenant for a small price of this world so that you break it in return for this small price. For truly what is with God of reward is better for you than all that is in this world — if you should know this then do not break it.

hype_questions: What is the value of keeping Allah's covenant?
Is breaking Allah's covenant worth it for material gain?

source_text:
Verse: Whatever you have will end, but whatever Allah has is everlasting. And We will certainly reward the steadfast according to the best of their deeds.

Tafsir: That which is with you of the things of this world will come to an end will perish but that which is with God remains it is everlasting. And He shall surely pay read la-yajziyanna or la-najziyanna ‘We shall surely pay’ those who were patient in fulfilling their covenants their reward according to the best of what they used to do ‘the best’ here means ‘the good’.

hype_questions: What happens to worldly possessions in the afterlife?
How is one rewarded for their faithfulness?
What does it mean to fulfill one's covenants?
propositions: Whatever you have will end.
Allah has everlasting things.
We shall surely pay those who were patient in fulfilling their covenants their reward according to the best of what they used to do.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever does good, whether male or female, and is a believer, We will surely bless them with a good life, and We will certainly reward them according to the best of their deeds.

Tafsir: Whoever acts righteously whether male or female and is a believer him verily We shall revive with a goodly life. This is said to be life in Paradise; or it is life on earth when it is one of contentedness or one of wholesome halāl provision. And We shall surely pay them their reward according to the best of what they used to do.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who act righteously?
How will Allah bless believers with a good life?

propositions: Whoever acts righteously, regardless of gender, and is a believer, will be blessed with a good life.
The reward for righteous actions will be paid according to the best of what they used to do.
Life in Paradise or contented/halāl provision on earth are considered good lives.

source_text:
Verse: When you recite the Quran, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed.

Tafsir: And when you recite the Qur’ān that is when you intend to recite it seek refuge in God from Satan the outcast in other words say a‘ūdhu bi’Lllāhi min al-shaytān al-rajīm ‘I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan’.

hype_questions: What is the significance of seeking refuge when reciting the Quran?
How does reciting the Quran relate to one's intention and faith?
What is the difference between Satan as described in the Quran and other connotations of the word?
propositions: When you recite the Quran, seek refuge with Allah from Satan.
Reciting the Qur'an implies an intention to do so and a desire for protection from Satan.
Satan is referred to as 'the accursed' in the Quran, emphasizing his malevolent nature.

source_text:
Verse: He certainly has no authority over those who believe and put their trust in their Lord.

source_text:
Verse: When We replace a verse with another—and Allah knows best what He reveals—they say, “You ˹Muhammad˺ are just a fabricator.” In fact, most of them do not know.

Tafsir: And when We exchange a verse in place of a different verse by abrogating it and revealing another for the welfare of God’s servants — and God knows best what He reveals — they say that is the disbelievers say to the Prophet s ‘You are just a fabricator’ a liar making it up yourself. Nay most of them do not know the true nature of the Qur’ān and the benefit to God’s servants of abrogation.

hype_questions: Does the Quran abrogate previous verses?
What is the nature of the Quran and its benefits for believers?
Can the Prophet Muhammad be trusted to interpret the Quran?

source_text:
Verse: Say, “The holy spirit has brought it down from your Lord with the truth to reassure the believers, and as a guide and good news for those who submit ˹to Allah˺.”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘The Holy Spirit Gabriel has revealed it from your Lord with truth bi’l-haqq this is semantically connected to nazzala ‘he Gabriel has revealed it’ to confirm the faith of those who believe by their believing in it when it is revealed and as guidance and good tidings for those who have submitted to God’.

hype_questions: What is the role of the Holy Spirit in revealing divine messages?
How does faith come about through submission to God?
What are the benefits of submitting to God's guidance?
propositions: The holy spirit has brought it down from your Lord with the truth.
Gabriel has revealed it from your Lord with truth.
This is good news for those who submit to God.

source_text:
Verse: And We surely know that they say, “No one is teaching him except a human.” But the man they refer to speaks a foreign tongue, whereas this ˹Quran˺ is ˹in˺ eloquent Arabic.

Tafsir: And verily wa-laqad is for confirmation We know that they say ‘It is only a human that is teaching him the Qur’ān’ — this was a Christian blacksmith whom the Prophet s used to frequent. God exalted be He says The tongue the language of him to whom they refer to whom they incline with the accusation that he is the one teaching him is foreign’; while this Qur’ān is in a clear Arabic tongue one of lucidity and clarity so how can a foreigner be teaching him?

God exalted be He says that the tongue of the one they refer to is foreign.
This Qur'an is in eloquent Arabic.

source_text:

hype_questions: Will those who reject Allah's revelations ever be guided?

source_text:
Verse: No one fabricates lies except those who disbelieve in Allah’s revelations, and it is they who are the ˹true˺ liars.

It is they who are the liars.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after their belief—not those who are forced while their hearts are firm in faith, but those who embrace disbelief wholeheartedly—they will be condemned by Allah and suffer a tremendous punishment.

Tafsir: Whoever disbelieves in God after having affirmed his faith — except for him who is compelled to pronounce a statement of unbelief and so pronounces it while his heart is at rest in faith man ‘whoever’ is either a subject or a conditional and so the predicate of this subject or the response to this conditional is an implied lahum wa‘īdun shadīd ‘there is for them a severe threat of chastisement’; this is indicated by the statement that follows — but he who opens up his breast to unbelief that is he who opens it up and expands it with unbelief meaning that his soul is content with it upon such shall be wrath from God and there is a great chastisement for them.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who disbelieves in Allah after having affirmed their faith?
How does one's heart respond when they are compelled to pronounce a statement of unbelief?

propositions: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after their belief will be condemned by Allah and suffer a tremendous punishment.
The heart of one who is compelled to pronounce a statement of unbelief is at rest in faith.
He who opens up his breast to unbelief shall be wrath from God.

source_text:
Verse: This is because they prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter. Surely Allah never guides those who ˹choose to˺ disbelieve.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who emigrated after being compelled ˹to renounce Islam˺, then struggled ˹in Allah’s cause˺, and persevered, your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful after all.

Verse: ˹Honouring˺ the Sabbath was ordained only for those who disputed about Abraham. And surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their disputes.

Tafsir: The Sabbath was only prescribed in other words its consecration was made obligatory only for those who differed concerning it with their prophet — these were the Jews. They were commanded to devote themselves solely to worship on Friday but they said ‘We do not want it’ and chose Saturday; consequently thereon the observance of it was enforced strictly on them; and lo! your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ with regard this matter of the Sabbath by rewarding the obedient and chastising the one who disobeyed by his violating its sanctity.

Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their disputes.

source_text:
Verse: Invite ˹all˺ to the Way of your Lord with wisdom and kind advice, and only debate with them in the best manner. Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided.

source_text:
Verse: Glory be to the One Who took His servant ˹Muhammad˺ by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque whose surroundings We have blessed, so that We may show him some of Our signs. alone is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

Tafsir: Glory be to Him — an affirmation of God’s transcendence — Who carried His servant Muhammad (s) by night laylan is in the accusative as an adverbial qualification; isrā’ means ‘to travel by night’; what is instructive about this mention of laylan ‘by night’ is that through its being indefinite there is an indication of the brevity of its duration from the Sacred Mosque that is Mecca to the Farthest Mosque the Holy House of Jerusalem so called because of its distance from the former; the environs of which We have blessed with fruits and rivers that We might show him some of Our signs the marvels of Our power. Indeed He is the Hearing the Seeing that is to say the Knower of the Prophet’s s sayings and deeds. Thus He God was gracious to him by way of carrying him on the night journey which comprised his encountering the other prophets his ascension to heaven and the sight of the marvels of the Divine Realm and His communion exalted be He with him. For he the Prophet s said ‘I was brought al-Burāq a white animal larger than a donkey but smaller than a mule; it was able to place its hoof back towards its extremity and so I mounted it. It set off carrying me until I reached the Holy House of Jerusalem. There I fastened the animal to the ring where the prophets fasten their animals. I then went in and prayed two units inside it. As I came out Gabriel came to me with a jug of wine and a jug of milk and so I chose the milk. Gabriel said to me “You have made the right choice by choosing the primordial nature fitra”.’ He the Prophet continued the narration ‘We then ascended to the heaven of this world whereat Gabriel asked to be let in. Someone asked “Who are you?”. He replied “Gabriel” “And who is with you?” “Muhammad (s)” he said. “Has he been sent for?”. “Yes he has been sent for”. Then it was opened for us and lo! Adam stood before me; he greeted me and prayed for well-being for me. We then ascended to the second heaven and Gabriel asked to be let in. Someone asked “Who are you?”. He replied “Gabriel” “And who is with you?” “Muhammad (s)” he said.

hype_questions: What was the purpose of Muhammad's night journey?
Who did Adam greet during Muhammad's ascension to heaven?
What was Gabriel carrying when he met Muhammad?
propositions: God took His servant Muhammad by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque.
The environs of the Holy House of Jerusalem were blessed with fruits and rivers.
Muhammad saw the marvels of God's power during his journey.
Gabriel brought wine and milk to Muhammad during his ascension.
Adam greeted Muhammad in heaven and prayed for well-being.

source_text:
Verse: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guide for the Children of Israel, ˹stating:˺ “Do not take besides Me any other Trustee of Affairs,

Tafsir: God exalted be He says And We gave Moses the Scripture the Torah and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel saying that they should not choose beside Me any guardian to whom they delegate their affairs a variant reading for yattakhidhū ‘they should not choose’ is tattakhidhū ‘you should not choose’ thus turning away from the third person address in which case the particle an ‘that’ is extra and the ‘saying’ is implicit.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Torah in Islamic theology?
How does Islam view the concept of a 'Trustee of Affairs'?
What is the role of Moses in receiving the Scripture?
propositions: God gave Moses the Torah as a guidance for the Children of Israel.
The Children of Israel should not choose any guardian to whom they delegate their affairs besides God.
God exalted be He says that the Torah is a guidance and not a choice.

source_text:
Verse: ˹O˺ descendants of those We carried with Noah ˹in the Ark˺! He was indeed a grateful servant.”

Tafsir: descendants of those whom We carried with Noah in the Ark. Indeed he was a grateful servant giving thanks to Us frequently and offering praise in whichever state he found himself.

hype_questions: What is the significance of gratitude in Islam?
How did Noah demonstrate his faith through his actions?
What can we learn from Noah's experience about showing appreciation to Allah?
propositions: The descendants of those whom We carried with Noah in the Ark were grateful servants.
Noah frequently gave thanks to Allah and offered praise in all states.
Allah is frequently thanked by His servants, including Noah.

source_text:
Verse: And We warned the Children of Israel in the Scripture, “You will certainly cause corruption in the land twice, and you will become extremely arrogant.

Tafsir: And We decreed We revealed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture the Torah ‘You shall indeed work corruption in the land the land of Syria through acts of disobedience twice and you shall indeed become great tyrants’ you shall perpetrate grave injustice.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of disobedience for the Children of Israel?
How will the Children of Israel become tyrants?
What is the nature of grave injustice?
propositions: We warned the Children of Israel in the Scripture that they would cause corruption in the land twice.
The Children of Israel were decreed to work corruption in the land through acts of disobedience twice.
The Children of Israel will become great tyrants and perpetrate grave injustice.

source_text:
Verse: When the first of the two warnings would come to pass, We would send against you some of Our servants of great might, who would ravage your homes. This would be a warning fulfilled.

Tafsir: So when the time for the first of the two prophecies the first of the two occasions for corruption came We roused against you servants of Ours of great might men who are strong in war and assault who ransacked who came and went seeking you out through your habitations in the very midst of your homes in order to slay you and take others among you captive and it was a promise fulfilled. Their first act of corruption was their slaying of the prophet Zachariah. So Goliath and his army were roused against them and they slew them and took their children captive and destroyed the Holy House of Jerusalem.

hype_questions: What is the first warning that God sends to humanity?
How do the servants of God respond to this warning?
What is the consequence of the servants' actions?
