propositions: When the time for the first of the two prophecies comes, God will send some of His servants against humanity.
These servants are strong in war and assault and will ravage homes.
The first act of corruption is the slaying of a prophet.
God's promise is fulfilled when the servants destroy a holy place.
The destruction of Jerusalem is a consequence of the servants' actions.

source_text:
Verse: Then ˹after your repentance˺ We would give you the upper hand over them and aid you with wealth and offspring, causing you to outnumber them.

Tafsir: Then We gave you back the turn the rule of the state and victory to prevail over them one hundred years later by having Goliath slain and We aided you with children and wealth and made you greater in number in clan.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Goliath's defeat?
How did Allah aid the Prophet in terms of wealth and offspring?
What was the outcome of the Prophet's increased number in clan?
propositions: Allah gave back to the Prophet the turn of ruling the state.
The Prophet prevailed over his enemies one hundred years later after Goliath's defeat.
Allah aided the Prophet with children and wealth.
The Prophet was made greater in number in clan.

source_text:
Verse: If you act rightly, it is for your own good, but if you do wrong, it is to your own loss. “And when the second warning would come to pass, your enemies would ˹be left to˺ totally disgrace you and enter the Temple ˹of Jerusalem˺ as they entered it the first time, and utterly destroy whatever would fall into their hands.

Tafsir: And We said ‘If you are virtuous through acts of obedience you are being virtuous to your own souls since the reward thereof is for them your souls; and if you do evil by way of working corruption it is for them’ your evildoing. So when the time the occasion for the other prophecy comes We will raise them forth that they might ravage you make you grieve through their slaying and taking captive of you a grief that will be manifest on your faces and that they might enter the Temple the Holy House of Jerusalem and destroy it just as they entered it and destroyed it the first time and that they might destroy lay waste all that they conquered all that they gained ascendancy over utterly with an utter wasting. They indeed wrought corruption a second time when they slew the prophet John. Thus Nebuchadnezzar was roused against them and so he slew thousands of them and took their children captive and destroyed the Holy House of Jerusalem.

hype_questions: What happens when an individual acts virtuously?
How will the consequences of evil be measured?
Will the people who destroyed Jerusalem be punished?
propositions: If you act rightly, it is for your own good.
The reward of virtuous actions is for one's soul.
When the time comes for another prophecy to be fulfilled, those who have done evil will be raised forth to ravage and destroy.
Those who destroyed Jerusalem will enter the Temple and destroy it again.
Nebuchadnezzar was roused against them and slew thousands of them and took their children captive.

source_text:
Verse: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you ˹if you repent˺, but if you return ˹to sin˺, We will return ˹to punishment˺. And We have made Hell a ˹permanent˺ confinement for the disbelievers.”

Tafsir: And We said in the Scripture It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you after the second time if you were to repent; but if you revert to working corruption We too will revert to punishment. And assuredly they did revert by denying the Prophet s and so he was given power over them through the slaying of the Banū Qurayza the expulsion of the Banū Nadīr and the exacting of the jizya-tax from them; and We have made Hell a dungeon for the disbelievers a place of detention and a prison for them.

hype_questions: Will Allah show mercy to those who repent?
What happens if someone reverts to sin after repenting?
Why is Hell a place of detention for disbelievers?
propositions: If you repent, your Lord may have mercy on you.
We will return to punishment if you revert to sin.
Hell is a permanent confinement for the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: Surely this Quran guides to what is most upright, and gives good news to the believers—who do good—that they will have a mighty reward.

Tafsir: Truly this Qur’ān guides to that to that way which is straightest most upright and correct and gives tidings to the believers who perform righteous deeds that there is a great reward for them.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of the Quran?
How do believers who perform righteous deeds benefit from their actions?
What can be expected as a reward for those who follow the teachings of the Quran?
propositions: The Quran guides to what is most upright.
Good news is given to the believers who do good.
There is a great reward for those who perform righteous deeds.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹it warns˺ those who do not believe in the Hereafter ˹that˺ We have prepared for them a painful punishment.

Tafsir: And it this Qur’ān informs that those who do not believe in the Hereafter We have prepared for them a painful chastisement namely the Fire.

hype_questions: What is the punishment for those who do not believe in the Hereafter?
How will Allah deal with those who reject the concept of an afterlife?
What can be expected from those who refuse to acknowledge the existence of a hereafter?
propositions: We have prepared a painful punishment for those who do not believe in the Hereafter.
The Qur’ān informs that the Fire is the chastisement prepared for those who do not believe in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: And humans ˹swiftly˺ pray for evil as they pray for good. For humankind is ever hasty.

Tafsir: And man prays for ill against himself and his family when he is frustrated as avidly as he prays for good. And mankind is ever hasty to pray against himself without contemplating the consequence thereof.

hype_questions: What happens when humans pray for evil instead of good?
Why do people get frustrated and pray against themselves?
How does humanity's hasty nature affect its prayers?
propositions: Humans pray for evil as they pray for good.
Man prays for ill against himself and his family when he is frustrated.
Mankind is ever hasty to pray against himself without contemplating the consequence thereof.

source_text:
Verse: We made the day and night as two signs. So We made the sign of the night devoid of light, and We made the sign of the day ˹perfectly˺ bright, so that you may seek the bounty of your Lord and know the number of years and calculation ˹of time˺. And We have explained everything in detail.

Tafsir: And We made the night and the day two signs both indicators of Our power. Then We effaced the sign of the night extinguishing its light with darkness so that you might repose therein the annexation āyata’layli ‘the sign of the night’ is explicative and made the sign of the day sight-giving in other words one in which it is possible to see because of the light; that you may seek therein bounty from your Lord by earning your livelihood and that you may know by both day and night the number of years and the reckoning of the times of the day and everything that might be needed We have detailed very distinctly We have explained clearly.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of having day and night as signs?
How does the Quran explain the concept of time?
What can we learn from the Quran about seeking bounty?
propositions: We made the day bright so that you may seek the bounty of your Lord.
The sign of the night is devoid of light, but it serves as a sign of Our power.
We have explained everything in detail.

source_text:
Verse: We have bound every human’s destiny to their neck. And on the Day of Judgment We will bring forth to each ˹person˺ a record which they will find laid open.

Tafsir: And We have attached every person’s omen — his deeds — for him to carry upon his neck — this site is singled out for mention because fastening something to it is much more severe; Mujāhid b. Jabr al-Makkī said ‘There is not a child born but it has a leaf around its neck in which it is decreed that the child will be either fortunate or damned’ — and We shall bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book in which his deeds are recorded and which he will find wide open yalqāhu manshūran both are adjectival qualifications of kitāban ‘a book’.

hype_questions: What is the significance of every person's omen being attached to their neck?
How will a person's deeds be recorded on the Day of Resurrection?
What does it mean for a child to have a leaf around its neck with a decree about its fate?
propositions: We have bound every human’s destiny to their neck.
On the Day of Judgment We will bring forth to each person a record which they will find laid open.
We have attached every person’s omen — his deeds — for him to carry upon his neck.
There is not a child born but it has a leaf around its neck in which it is decreed that the child will be either fortunate or damned.

source_text:
Verse: ˹And it will be said,˺ “Read your record. You ˹alone˺ are sufficient this Day to take account of yourself.”

Tafsir: And it will be said to him ‘Read your book! This day your soul suffices as your own reckoner’.

hype_questions: What is the significance of being one's own reckoner?
How does self-sufficiency relate to accountability?
What happens when an individual takes responsibility for their actions?
propositions: It will be said, 'Read your record.'
You alone are sufficient this Day to take account of yourself.
Your soul suffices as your own reckoner.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever chooses to be guided, it is only for their own good. And whoever chooses to stray, it is only to their own loss. No soul burdened with sin will bear the burden of another. And We would never punish ˹a people˺ until We have sent a messenger ˹to warn them˺.

Tafsir: Whoever is guided is guided only to the good of his own soul because the reward of his guidance will be for him; and whoever goes astray goes astray only to its his soul’s detriment because the sin thereof will be held against it. No burdened no sinful soul shall bear the burden of another soul. And We never chastise anyone until We have sent a messenger to make clear to him that which is his obligation.

hype_questions: What happens when someone chooses to follow the right path?
Can a person's sin affect another person?
How does guidance benefit an individual?
propositions: Whoever chooses to be guided will only benefit from it.
No one can bear the burden of another's sin.
We will not punish anyone until we have sent a messenger to warn them.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever We intend to destroy a society, We command its elite ˹to obey Allah˺ but they act rebelliously in it. So the decree ˹of punishment˺ is justified, and We destroy it utterly.

Tafsir: And when We desire to destroy a town We command its affluent ones those inhabitants of its who enjoy the graces of God meaning its leaders We command them to obedience by the tongue of Our messengers; but they fall into immorality therein rebelling against Our command and so the Word is justified concerning it that it should be chastised and We destroy it utterly We annihilate it by annihilating its inhabitants and leaving it in ruins.

hype_questions: What happens when a society's elite refuse to obey Allah?
How do We justify destroying a town that rebels against Our command?
What is the ultimate fate of a town that is destroyed by Us?
propositions: Whenever We intend to destroy a society, We command its elite to obey Allah.
The decree of punishment is justified when a society's elite refuse to obey Allah.
We annihilate a town by annihilating its inhabitants and leaving it in ruins.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We have destroyed after Noah! And sufficient is your Lord as All-Aware and All-Seeing of the sins of His servants.

Tafsir: How many — in other words many — generations communities We have destroyed since Noah! And your Lord suffices as One Informed and Beholder of the sins of His servants Knower of the hidden and manifest aspects of these sins bi-rabbika ‘your Lord’ is semantically connected to bi-dhunūb ‘of the sins’.

hype_questions: How many communities has Allah destroyed since the time of Noah?
What is the significance of Allah being aware and seeing the sins of His servants?
Can Allah's knowledge of a person's sins be hidden from Him?
propositions: Allah has destroyed many peoples after Noah.
Your Lord suffices as One Informed and Beholder of the sins of His servants.
Bi-rabbika 'your Lord' is semantically connected to bi-dhunūb 'of the sins'.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever desires this fleeting world ˹alone˺, We hasten in it whatever We please to whoever We will; then We destine them for Hell, where they will burn, condemned and rejected.

Tafsir: Whoever desires through his deeds the hasty world that is the life of this world We hasten for him therein whatever We will for whom We please such a hastening li-man nurīd ‘for whom We please’ is a substitute for lahu ‘for him’ with the repetition of the genitive particle li-. Then We appoint for him in the Hereafter Hell to which he will be exposed to which he will be admitted condemned blameful and rejected banished from God’s mercy.

hype_questions: What happens when one prioritizes worldly desires over spiritual growth?
How does Allah's will determine one's fate in the afterlife?
Can human actions influence their destiny in the Hereafter?
propositions: Allah hastens in the fleeting world whatever He pleases for whoever He wills.
Desiring the hasty world through deeds leads to a destination of Hell.
One's fate is determined by Allah's will, and they will be condemned and rejected in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it accordingly, and is a ˹true˺ believer, it is they whose striving will be appreciated.

Tafsir: And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort that is he performs the deeds worthy of it being a believer wa-huwa mu’minun is a circumstantial qualifier — for such their effort will find favour with God that is their effort will be accepted and rewarded.

hype_questions: What are the necessary efforts required to strive for the Hereafter?
How does a believer's striving find favour with God?
What happens to a person's effort when it is accepted and rewarded?
propositions: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it accordingly, and is a true believer, it is they whose striving will be appreciated.
And whoever desires the HereAfter and strives for it with the necessary effort that is he performs the deeds worthy of it being a believer wa-huwa mu’minun
their effort will find favour with God

source_text:
Verse: We provide both the former and the latter from the bounty of your Lord. And the bounty of your Lord can never be withheld.

Tafsir: Each of the two parties We supply We give to these and to those hā’ūlā’ wa-hā’ūlā’ is a substitute for kullan ‘each’ from min is semantically connected to numiddu ‘We supply’ from your Lord’s bounty in this world. And your Lord’s bounty therein is not confined it is not forbidden to anyone.

hype_questions: Can God's blessings be withheld?
What are the limits of God's bounty?
Is it permissible for anyone to deny God's blessings?
propositions: We provide both the former and the latter from the bounty of your Lord.
The bounty of your Lord can never be withheld.
Your Lord's bounty in this world is not confined, nor is it forbidden to anyone.

source_text:
Verse: See how We have favoured some over others ˹in this life˺, but the Hereafter is certainly far greater in rank and in favour.

Tafsir: See how We have given preference to some of them over others in provision and renown. And truly the Hereafter is greater grander in degrees and greater in preferment to this world and so one ought to devote one’s attention to it the Hereafter to the exclusion of the other.

hype_questions: What is the significance of favoritism in this life and the Hereafter?
How does provision and renown relate to one's spiritual growth?
What is the ultimate goal that should be prioritized over worldly concerns?
propositions: We have given preference to some individuals over others in terms of provision.
The Hereafter is greater than this world in terms of rank and favor.
One ought to devote their attention to the Hereafter rather than the world.
True fulfillment lies in the Hereafter, which surpasses the grandeur of this world.

source_text:
Verse: Do not set up any other god with Allah, or you will end up condemned, abandoned.

Tafsir: Do not set up another god besides God or you will sit blameworthy forsaken with no one to assist you.

hype_questions: What happens if I worship other gods besides Allah?
Can I be forgiven if I reject Allah's oneness?
Will I have any support or assistance if I abandon Allah?
propositions: Do not set up another god besides God.
You will sit blameworthy forsaken with no one to assist you.

source_text:
Verse: For your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. And honour your parents. If one or both of them reach old age in your care, never say to them ˹even˺ ‘ugh,’ nor yell at them. Rather, address them respectfully.

Tafsir: And your Lord has decreed He has commanded that you worship none save Him and that you show kindness to parents by being dutiful to them. If they should reach old age with you one of them ahaduhumā is the subject of the verb or both a variant reading for yablughanna has yablughān ‘both should reach’ in which case ahaduhumā would be substituting for the dual indicator alif of yablughān then do not say to them ‘Fie’ read uffan or uffin uffa or uffi a verbal noun meaning tabban ‘perish!’ or qubhan ‘evil!’ nor repulse them but speak to them gracious words fair and gentle words.

hype_questions: What is the Islamic principle of showing respect to parents?
How should one address their elderly parents?
What are the consequences of speaking harshly to one's parents?
propositions: Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him.
Honour your parents, especially when they reach old age in your care.
Never say 'ugh' or yell at your parents, and instead address them respectfully.

source_text:
Verse: And be humble with them out of mercy, and pray, “My Lord! Be merciful to them as they raised me when I was young.”

Tafsir: And lower to them the wing of humility show them your submissive side out of mercy that is on account of your affection for them and say ‘My Lord have mercy on them just as they had mercy on me when they reared me when I was little’.

hype_questions: What is the significance of humility in Islam?
How does mercy play a role in human relationships?
Can we expect divine retribution if we show compassion to others?
propositions: Be humble with them out of mercy.
Lower to them the wing of humility.
Show them your submissive side out of mercy.
Say, 'My Lord, have mercy on them just as they had mercy on me when I was little'.

source_text:
Verse: Your Lord knows best what is within yourselves. If you are righteous, He is certainly All-Forgiving to those who ˹constantly˺ turn to Him.

Tafsir: Your Lord knows best what is in your hearts in the way of what may be concealed of dutifulness or disobedience to parents. If you are righteous obedient to God then truly to those who are penitent those who return to obedience of Him He is Forgiving of any slip that might have issued on their part regarding their duty to the parents so long as they do not conceal within themselves any disrespect towards them.

hype_questions: What is the condition for God's forgiveness?
How can one show obedience to God and still be forgiven?
What happens when someone returns to obeying their parents?
propositions: Your Lord knows best what is in your hearts.
If you are righteous, He is certainly All-Forgiving to those who turn to Him.
He is Forgiving of any slip that might have issued on their part regarding their duty to the parents so long as they do not conceal within themselves any disrespect towards them.

source_text:
Verse: Give to close relatives their due, as well as the poor and ˹needy˺ travellers. And do not spend wastefully.

Tafsir: And give the kinsman his due of dutifulness and kindness and the needy and the traveller as well; and do not squander by expending for any purpose other than in obedience to God.

hype_questions: What is the importance of giving to close relatives and the poor?
How can one ensure they are not wasting their resources?
What is the purpose of spending money in obedience to God?
propositions: Give to close relatives their due.
Give the needy and travellers their due.
Do not spend wastefully.

source_text:
Verse: Surely the wasteful are ˹like˺ brothers to the devils. And the Devil is ever ungrateful to his Lord.

Tafsir: Indeed squanderers are brothers of devils that is they follow their way and the Devil was ever ungrateful to his Lord extremely rejective of His graces likewise his brother the squanderer.

hype_questions: Does being wasteful make someone a devil's brother?
Why is the Devil ungrateful to his Lord?
What happens when someone rejects their Lord's graces?
propositions: The wasteful are like brothers of devils.
The Devil is ever ungrateful to his Lord.
The Devil was extremely rejective of His graces.

source_text:
Verse: But if you must turn them down ˹because you lack the means to give˺—while hoping to receive your Lord’s bounty—then ˹at least˺ give them a kind word.

Tafsir: But if you have to overlook them that is the kinsmen and the others mentioned and do not give to them seeking mercy from your Lord a mercy which you expect in the future that is you do not give to them because of a request for provision which you are waiting to come to you from your Lord before you give to them then speak to them gentle words pleasant and reasonable words promising them that you will give to them when the provision from God arrives.

hype_questions: What is the best way to respond when we can't afford to give charity to our relatives and friends?
How can we show kindness to those who are in need without compromising our financial stability?
What promise can we make to those who are waiting for us to provide for them?
propositions: If you must turn someone down, at least give them a kind word.
You should not give charity to your relatives and friends expecting mercy from God in return, unless you expect God's provision to arrive first.
When you can afford to give charity, speak to those who are waiting for it with gentle and reasonable words, promising them that you will provide when the time comes.

source_text:
Verse: Do not be so tight-fisted, for you will be blameworthy; nor so open-handed, for you will end up in poverty.

Tafsir: And do not keep your hand chained to your neck in other words do not withhold it completely from expending nor open it in order to expend completely or you will sit blameworthy — this refers to the first case — and denuded cut off having nothing — this refers to the latter case.

hype_questions: What happens if I am too tight-fisted with my resources?
How will I be affected if I am too open-handed with my spending?
Can being too generous lead to poverty?
propositions: You should not withhold your resources completely.
You should not expend all of your resources completely.
Being tight-fisted can lead to blame.
Being too open-handed can lead to poverty.
Expending all of one's resources completely is not recommended.

source_text:
Verse: Surely your Lord gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills. He is certainly All-Aware, All-Seeing of His servants.

Tafsir: Truly your Lord expands provision He makes it abundant for whomever He will and He straitens He restricts it for whomever He will. Indeed He is ever Aware and Seer of His servants Knower of what they hide and what they manifest giving them provision in accordance with their welfare.

hype_questions: Does Allah's provision for us depend on His will alone?
Can Allah be unaware of our needs and circumstances?
Is Allah's knowledge limited to what we manifest, or does He also know what we hide?
propositions: Allah gives abundant provisions to whoever He wills.
Allah expands provision for whomever He wills and restricts it for whomever He wills.
Allah is ever Aware and Seer of His servants.
Allah knows what His servants hide and manifest, giving them provision in accordance with their welfare.

source_text:
Verse: Do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Surely killing them is a heinous sin.

Tafsir: And do not slay your children by burying them alive fearing penury poverty. We shall provide for them and for you. Slaying them is truly a great sin.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of prioritizing material wealth over the well-being of one's children?
How does Islam view the act of killing one's own children?
What is the Islamic perspective on poverty and its impact on family decisions?
propositions: Killing children due to poverty is a heinous sin.
God provides for both parents and their children.
Slaying children is considered a great sin in Islam.

source_text:
Verse: Do not go near adultery. It is truly a shameful deed and an evil way.

Tafsir: And do not come anywhere near fornication — this form of expressing it is more effective than saying ‘Do not commit it’. It is indeed an indecency an abomination and it is an evil way.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of committing adultery?
How does fornication affect one's relationship with Allah?
Can indecency and abomination be forgiven?
propositions: Adultery is a shameful deed.
Fornication is an indecent and abominable act.
It is evil to engage in such behavior.

source_text:
Verse: Do not take a ˹human˺ life—made sacred by Allah—except with ˹legal˺ right. for they are already supported ˹by law˺.

Tafsir: And do not slay the soul whose life God has made inviolable except with due cause. Whoever is slain wrongfully We have certainly given his heir the one inheriting from him a warrant a sanction to retaliate against the slayer; but let him not commit excess let him not overstep the bounds in slaying by slaying other than the killer of the one slain or by other than that instrument with which he the slain was killed; for he is supported by the Law.

hype_questions: What are the circumstances under which taking a human life is considered acceptable?
How does Islam handle situations where someone is killed unjustly?
What rights do individuals have when it comes to defending themselves or their loved ones?
propositions: Taking a human life is only permissible with legal right.
God has made certain lives inviolable and subject to legal sanction.
Those who are wrongfully slain have the right to retaliate against the slayer, but must do so within the bounds of the law.

source_text:
Verse: Do not come near the wealth of the orphan—unless intending to enhance it—until they attain maturity. Honour ˹your˺ pledges, for you will surely be accountable for them.

Tafsir: And do not come anywhere near an orphan’s property except in the fairest manner until he comes of age. And fulfil the covenant should you make a covenant with God or with people in general. Indeed the covenant will be enquired into.

hype_questions: What happens to an orphan's property when they come of age?
How should one handle an orphan's wealth?
What is the consequence of breaking a covenant with God or people?
propositions: Do not approach an orphan's wealth unless intending to improve it until they reach maturity.
Honour your promises, as you will be held accountable for them.
Fulfill any covenant made with God or people, as it will be scrutinized.

source_text:
Verse: Give in full when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is fairest and best in the end.

Tafsir: And give full measure complete it when you measure and weigh with a right balance with an even balance that is better and fairer in return.

hype_questions: What does the Quran say about fairness in trade?
How should one measure and weigh goods to ensure a fair transaction?
What is the Islamic perspective on fairness and balance?
propositions: Give full measure when you measure.
Weigh with an even balance.
That is fairest and best in the end.

source_text:
Verse: Do not follow what you have no ˹sure˺ knowledge of. Indeed, all will be called to account for ˹their˺ hearing, sight, and intellect.

Tafsir: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed the hearing and the sight and the heart — of each of these it will be asked of that person what he did with them.

hype_questions: What happens to our knowledge when we die?
How are we held accountable for our actions?
Can we be forgiven for mistakes made with our senses?
propositions: Do not follow what you have no knowledge of.
It will be asked of each person what they did with their hearing, sight, and intellect.
The heart will also be questioned about its actions.

source_text:
Verse: And do not walk on the earth arrogantly. Surely you can neither crack the earth nor stretch to the height of the mountains.

Tafsir: And do not walk in the earth exultantly that is exultant with pride and conceit. Indeed you will not rend the earth you will not pierce it and reach its depths with your pride nor attain the mountains in height the meaning is that you shall never attain such ends so how can you be so arrogant?

hype_questions: Can I achieve something greater than what is physically possible?
How can I be so arrogant when I know my limitations?
What drives people to act with excessive pride and conceit?
propositions: You should not walk on the earth with arrogance.
You cannot crack the earth or stretch to the height of the mountains.
Your pride and conceit will not allow you to pierce the earth's depths or attain the heights of the mountains.

source_text:
Verse: The violation of any of these ˹commandments˺ is detestable to your Lord.

Tafsir: All of that which has been mentioned — the evil of it is hateful in the sight of your Lord.

hype_questions: What are the commandments that are detestable to Allah?
How does Allah feel about violating these commandments?
What is the nature of evil according to Allah's sight?
propositions: The violation of any commandment is detestable to your Lord.
All of that which has been mentioned is hateful in the sight of your Lord.

source_text:
Verse: This is part of the wisdom which your Lord has revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺. And do not set up any other god with Allah ˹O humanity˺, or you will be cast into Hell, blameworthy, rejected.

Tafsir: This is part of the wisdom the admonition which your Lord has revealed to you O Muhammad (s). And do not set up with God any other god or you will be cast into Hell blameworthy abandoned banished from God’s mercy.

hype_questions: What happens if I worship other gods besides Allah?
Can I avoid Hell by not setting up other gods?
How can I ensure God's mercy and forgiveness?
propositions: Your Lord has revealed to you part of the wisdom.
Do not set up any other god with Allah.
You will be cast into Hell if you set up other gods.

source_text:
Verse: Has your Lord favoured you ˹pagans˺ with sons and taken angels as ˹His˺ daughters? You are truly making an outrageous claim.

Tafsir: Has your Lord then preferred you has He distinguished you exclusively O Meccans with sons and chosen for Himself females from among the angels? as daughters for Himself in the way that you are wont to claim. Truly by saying this you are speaking a monstrous word!

hype_questions: Does your Lord have a preference for certain groups of people?
Are angels considered as daughters in Islamic theology?
What does it mean to claim that one's Lord has chosen females from among the angels?
propositions: Your Lord has not favoured you with sons.
Angels are not chosen by your Lord as daughters.
Claiming that one's Lord has chosen females from among the angels is a monstrous word.

source_text:
Verse: We have surely varied ˹the signs˺ in this Quran so perhaps they may be mindful, but it only drives them farther away.

Tafsir: And verily We have dispensed We have elucidated in this Qur’ān similitudes promises of reward and threats of retribution so that they may remember that they may be admonished but it that elucidation only increases them in aversion to the Truth.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of varying signs in the Quran?
How does the Quran's elucidation affect people's perception of truth?
What is the ultimate goal of the Quran's promises and threats?
propositions: We have varied the signs in this Quran.
The Quran's elucidation increases aversion to the Truth.
People may be admonished through the Quran's promises and threats.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Had there been other gods besides Him—as they claim—then they would have certainly sought a way to ˹challenge˺ the Lord of the Throne.”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘If there were with Him that is with God other gods as they say they would in that case have sought against the Lord of the Throne that is against God some path some way in order to fight Him off.

hype_questions: Would other gods have sought a way to challenge God if they existed?
How would polytheistic beliefs affect their relationship with God?
What would be the consequences of challenging the Lord of the Throne?
propositions: If there were other gods besides God, they would seek a path to fight Him off.
The existence of other gods is not supported by the ability to challenge God.
Challenging the Lord of the Throne is against God.

source_text:
Verse: Glorified and Highly Exalted is He above what they claim!

Tafsir: Glory be to Him — an affirmation of His transcendence — and exalted be He above what they say in the way of His having associates greatly!

hype_questions: Does Allah have any partners or equals?
Can Allah be associated with anything?
Is Allah's transcendence absolute?
propositions: Allah is above what they claim.
Glory be to Him, an affirmation of His transcendence.
He is exalted above what they say in the way of His having associates greatly.

source_text:
Verse: The seven heavens, the earth, and all those in them glorify Him. There is not a single thing that does not glorify His praises—but you ˹simply˺ cannot comprehend their glorification. He is indeed Most Forbearing, All-Forgiving.

Tafsir: The seven heavens and the earth and all that is therein proclaim His praise they affirm His transcendence. And there is not a thing among things created but proclaims enwrapped in His praise in other words everything says subhāna’Llāh wa-bi-hamdihi ‘Glory and praise be to God’; but you do not understand their glorification because it is not proclaimed in your language. Lo! He is Forbearing Forgiving for He does not hasten to bring about your punishment.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's glorification?
How does everything in creation proclaim praise to God?
Why can humans not comprehend the full extent of God's praise?
propositions: The seven heavens, the earth, and all that is therein proclaim His praise.
There is not a thing among things created but proclaims enwrapped in His praise.
God is Forbearing Forgiving for He does not hasten to bring about your punishment.

source_text:
Verse: When you ˹O Prophet˺ recite the Quran, We put a hidden barrier between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter.

Tafsir: And when you recite the Qur’ān We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier that is one that hides you from them so that they cannot see you — this was revealed regarding those who wanted to assassinate him s the Prophet.

hype_questions: What is the barrier that Allah puts between the Prophet and those who do not believe in the Hereafter?
How does this barrier protect the Prophet from those who want to harm him?
What is the significance of the hidden barrier in the Quran?
propositions: When you recite the Quran, Allah puts a hidden barrier between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter.
This barrier hides you from them so that they cannot see you.
The Prophet was protected by this barrier because some people wanted to assassinate him.

source_text:
Verse: We have cast veils over their hearts—leaving them unable to comprehend it—and deafness in their ears. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Quran, they turn their backs in aversion.

Tafsir: And We place upon their hearts veils covers lest they should understand it lest they should understand the Qur’ān in other words and so in this way they do not understand it and in their ears a deafness a heaviness thus they cannot hear it. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’ān they turn their backs in aversion to it.

hype_questions: What happens when someone mentions God alone in the Quran?
Why do people turn their backs when hearing about God in the Quran?
How does the Quran affect those who are deaf to its message?
propositions: We have cast veils over their hearts.
They are unable to comprehend it.
There is a deafness in their ears.
When you mention your Lord alone in the Quran, they turn their backs in aversion.

source_text:
Verse: We know best how they listen to your recitation and what they say privately—when the wrongdoers say, “You would only be following a bewitched man.”

Tafsir: We know best what they listen to the reason for which they listen to it in order to mock it when they listen to you to your recital and when they are in secret counsel holding secret talks among themselves in other words when they talk when idh substitutes for the preceding idh ‘when’ the evildoers say in their secret conversation ‘You are only following a man bewitched one duped his mind overcome’.

hype_questions: Does listening to the Quran lead to mocking its message?
Can a person be deceived by someone's words and actions?
What is the nature of secret conversations among people?
propositions: They listen to the Quran to mock it.
The wrongdoers are deceived by someone's bewitching words and actions.
Secret conversations among people can be misleading.

source_text:
Verse: See how they call you names ˹O Prophet˺! So they have gone so ˹far˺ astray that they cannot find the ˹Right˺ Way.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says Look how they strike similitudes for you such as your being bewitched a soothsayer or a poet and they go astray thereby from the path of guidance and cannot find a way a path to it!

hype_questions: What happens when people call you names?
How do people go astray from the right path?
Can people find their way to guidance?
propositions: God exalted be He says that people strike similitudes for him such as being bewitched by a soothsayer or a poet.
People go astray from the path of guidance when they strike similitudes for God.
The path to guidance is not found by those who strike similitudes for God.

source_text:
Verse: And they say ˹mockingly˺, “When we are reduced to bones and ashes, will we really be raised as a new creation?”

Tafsir: And they say in denial of the Resurrection ‘What when we are bones and fragments shall we really be raised up in a new creation?’

hype_questions: Will we be raised as a new creation after being reduced to bones and ashes?
What will happen to our physical bodies after death?
Is there an afterlife where we are resurrected in a new form?
propositions: They say that when they die, their bodies will be reduced to bones and ashes.
The Resurrection is a reality that will occur after death.
We will be raised up in a new creation after being resurrected.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹Yes, even if˺ you become stones, or iron,

Tafsir: Say to them ‘Be stones or iron

hype_questions: If I were to lose all my physical form, would I still be able to fulfill my duties as a prophet?
How can I demonstrate patience in the face of adversity?
What is the significance of sacrifice in Islam?
propositions: Even if you become stones or iron, you will still be able to fulfill your duties.
You should be willing to undergo any transformation that may be required of you.
Sacrifice is an essential aspect of Islamic faith and practice.

source_text:
Verse: or whatever you think is harder to bring to life!” Then they will ask ˹you˺, “Who will bring us back ˹to life˺?” Say, “The One Who created you the first time.” They will then shake their heads at you and ask, “When will that be?” Say, “Perhaps it is soon!”

Tafsir: or some creation yet greater in your breasts something yet far less able to accept life aside from bones and fragments a spirit will undoubtedly be made to exist in you to bring you back to life. They will then say ‘Who shall bring us back?’ to life. Say ‘He Who originated you created you the first time when you had not been anything in existence because the One Who is able to initiate creation is also able to repeat it indeed this repetition is easier than the initiation. Then they will shake their heads at you stupefied and they will say mockingly ‘When will it be?’ that is the Resurrection. Say ‘Maybe it is near!’

entities: The One Who created you the first time
hype_questions: When will we be brought back to life?
Who will bring us back to life?
What is the nature of the Resurrection?
propositions: The One Who created you the first time will bring you back to life.
He Who originated you is able to repeat creation.
The Resurrection is near.

source_text:
Verse: On the Day He will call you, you will ˹instantly˺ respond by praising Him, thinking you had remained ˹in the world˺ only for a little while.

Tafsir: The day He calls you the day He calls out to you from your graves by the tongue of the archangel Isrāfīl you will respond you will answer His call from your graves with His praise by His command — it is also said to mean that you will respond ‘and praise be to Him’ — and you will think that you have remained in this world only a little because of the terror of what you will see on that day.

hype_questions: What happens when the archangel Isrāfīl calls out to you from your graves?
How will you respond to God's call on the Day of Judgment?
What will you think about when you see what awaits you on that day?
propositions: You will respond by praising God when He calls you.
God will call out to you from your graves using the tongue of the archangel Isrāfīl.
You will answer His call with His praise, as commanded by Him.
You will think that you have remained in this world only a little while due to fear of what you will see on that day.

source_text:
Verse: Tell My ˹believing˺ servants to say only what is best. Satan certainly seeks to sow discord among them. Satan is indeed a sworn enemy to humankind.

Tafsir: And tell My servants the believers to speak to disbelievers that word which is finer. For Satan indeed incites ill feeling he makes trouble between them and Satan is indeed man’s manifest enemy his enmity is evident. The ‘finer word’ is to say this

hype_questions: What is the best way to respond to a disbeliever?
How can believers maintain harmony with one another?
What is the nature of Satan's relationship with humanity?
propositions: My servants should speak only what is best.
Satan seeks to sow discord among My servants.
Satan incites ill feeling and makes trouble between My servants.
Satan is a sworn enemy to humankind.
The 'finer word' means saying this

source_text:
Verse: Your Lord knows you best. He may have mercy on you if He wills, or punish you if He wills. We have not sent you ˹O Prophet˺ as a keeper over them.

Tafsir: Your Lord knows you best. If He will He will have mercy on you by way of granting you repentance and faith or if He will for you to be chastised He will chastise you by having you die in disbelief. And We did not send you to be a guardian over them and so compel them to embrace faith — this was revealed before the command to fight them.

hype_questions: Will Allah show mercy to me if I repent?
What is the consequence of not believing in Allah?
Is it my responsibility to force others to believe in Allah?
propositions: Your Lord knows you best.
If He wills, He may have mercy on you by granting you repentance and faith.
If He wills, He may chastise you by having you die in disbelief.
We did not send you to be a guardian over them.

source_text:
Verse: Your Lord knows best all those in the heavens and the earth. And We have surely favoured some prophets above others, and to David We gave the Psalms.

Tafsir: And your Lord knows best all who are in the heavens and the earth thus endowing them each one with what He will according to the measure of their states. And verily We have preferred some of the prophets above others endowing each of them with a particular merit Moses with being spoken to; Abraham with Friendship; and Muhammad (s) with the Night Journey; and We gave David the Psalms.

hype_questions: What is the measure of a prophet's merit?
How do different prophets receive divine favor?
What is the significance of the Night Journey for Muhammad (s)?
propositions: Your Lord knows best all who are in the heavens and the earth.
We have preferred some of the prophets above others endowing each of them with a particular merit.
Moses was spoken to by God.
Abraham was chosen for friendship with God.
Muhammad (s) underwent the Night Journey.
David was given the Psalms.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Invoke those you claim ˹to be divine˺ besides Him—they do not have the power to undo harm from you or transfer it ˹to someone else˺.”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘Call on those whom you assumed to be gods besides Him such as the angels Jesus and Ezra ‘Uzayr; yet they have no power to rid you of misfortune nor to transfer it to persons other than you.

hype_questions: Can invoking gods besides Allah undo harm?
Can these gods transfer misfortune to others?
What is the nature of divine power?
propositions: There are no gods besides Allah.
Invoking other deities does not rid one of misfortune.
No one can transfer misfortune to another but the individual themselves.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Even˺ the closest ˹to Allah˺ of those invoked would be seeking a way to their Lord, hoping for His mercy, and fearing His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s torment is fearsome.

Tafsir: Those whom they call gods they themselves seek a means to their Lord they seek nearness by way of obedience which of them ayyuhum substitutes for the third person indicator wāw of the verb yabtaghūna ‘they seek’ in other words even he seeks it this nearness the one who is nearer to Him so how much more is it sought in the case of others?; and they hope for His mercy and fear His chastisement just like others so how can you call them gods? Truly your Lord’s chastisement is a thing to beware of.

hype_questions: What happens when we seek nearness to Allah through obedience?
How can we hope for Allah's mercy and fear His punishment at the same time?
What is the nature of Allah's chastisement, and how should we approach it?
propositions: Even the closest of those invoked would be seeking a way to their Lord.
They seek nearness by way of obedience.
Your Lord’s torment is fearsome.

source_text:
Verse: There is not a ˹wicked˺ society that We will not destroy or punish with a severe torment before the Day of Judgment. That is written in the Record.

Tafsir: There is not a town — its inhabitants are the ones meant — but We shall destroy it before the Day of Resurrection through death or chastise it with terrible chastisement by killing its inhabitants or otherwise. That has been inscribed in the Book the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz.

hype_questions: What is the fate of a society that disobeys God?
How will the world be punished before the Day of Judgment?
Will all towns be destroyed on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: There is not a town — its inhabitants are the ones meant — but We shall destroy it before the Day of Resurrection through death or chastise it with terrible chastisement by killing its inhabitants or otherwise.
That has been inscribed in the Book the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz.

source_text:
Verse: Nothing keeps Us from sending the ˹demanded˺ signs except that they had ˹already˺ been denied by earlier peoples. And We gave Thamûd the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wrongfully rejected it. We only send the signs as a warning.

Tafsir: Nothing prevented Us from sending the signs requested by the people of Mecca except that the ancients denied them when We sent such signs and so We destroyed them if We were to send them to these people of Mecca they would deny them and would thus deserve destruction. However We have judged that they be given respite so that the mission of Muhammad (s) be completed. And We gave Thamūd the she-camel as a sign that was apparent one that was clear and evident but they wronged they disbelieved it and were therefore destroyed. And We do not send signs miracles except for deterrence to servants so that they might believe.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of sending signs to humanity?
How do people typically respond to miracles and warnings from God?
Can miracles alone lead to belief in God?
propositions: Nothing prevented Us from sending the signs requested by the people of Mecca except that the ancients denied them.
We only send the signs as a warning.
And We do not send signs miracles except for deterrence to servants so that they might believe.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember, O  Prophet˺ when We told you, “Certainly your Lord encompasses the people.” And We have made what We brought you to see only as a test for the people. We keep warning them, but it only increases them greatly in defiance.

Tafsir: And remember when We said to you ‘Truly your Lord encompasses mankind’ in knowledge and power over them such that they are within His grasp so deliver the Message to them and do not fear anyone because God will protect you from them. And We did not appoint the vision that We showed you before your very eyes during the Night Journey except as a test for people for the people of Mecca — since they denied it and some of them even apostatised when he the Prophet informed them of it — and likewise the tree cursed in the Qur’ān namely the tree called Zaqqūm Q.3762ff that issues from the very root of the Blazing Fire of Hell; We made it a test for them because they said ‘Fire consumes trees so how can it cause it the Zaqqūm tree to issue forth?’. And We seek to deter them with it but it Our deterrence only increases them in gross insolence.

hype_questions: Does God protect the Prophet from harm?
What is the purpose of the vision shown to the Prophet during the Night Journey?
How does the Zaqqūm tree relate to the Blazing Fire of Hell?
propositions: God encompasses mankind in knowledge and power.
The Prophet must deliver the Message to all people despite fear for himself.
The vision shown to the Prophet was a test for the people of Mecca.
The Zaqqūm tree is a test for those who deny its existence.
God's deterrence only increases insolence in those who reject it.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” so they all did—but not Iblis, who protested, “Should I prostrate to the one You have created from mud?”

Tafsir: And mention when We said to the angels ‘Prostrate yourselves before Adam’ a prostration of salutation by inclining oneself and so they all prostrated themselves except Iblīs he said ‘Shall I prostrate myself before one whom You have created from clay?’ tīnan is in the accusative because the operator of the oblique min ‘of’ has been omitted in other words it would normally be min tīnin.

hype_questions: Does the Quran emphasize the importance of obedience to God's commands?
Can humans be held accountable for their actions in this life and the next?
What is the significance of Iblis' refusal to prostrate before Adam?
propositions: God commanded the angels to prostrate themselves before Adam.
Iblis refused to prostrate himself before Adam, questioning God's creation.
The act of prostration is a form of salutation and submission to God's will.

source_text:
Verse: Adding, “Do you see this one you honoured above me? If you delay my end until the Day of Judgment, I will certainly take hold of his descendants, except for a few.”

Tafsir: Said he ‘Do You see — in other words inform me this one whom You have honoured whom You have preferred above me? by commanding that prostration should be made before him when ‘I am better than him. You created me from fire while him You created from clay’ Q. 712. If la-in the lām is for oaths You defer me to the Day of Resurrection I shall verily eradicate his seed by leading them astray all save a few’ of them of those whom You have given divine protection.

hype_questions: Will I be rewarded for my good deeds if others are more deserving?
Can I trust in Allah's justice and fairness?
What happens to those who are favored by Allah over me?
propositions: Allah created the speaker from fire, while another was created from clay.
The speaker is better than another whom Allah has honored above him.
If Allah delays the speaker's end until the Day of Judgment, He will take hold of his descendants except for a few.

source_text:
Verse: Allah responded, “Be gone! Whoever of them follows you, Hell will surely be the reward for all of you—an ample reward.

Tafsir: Said He exalted be He to him Iblīs ‘Begone deferred to the time of the First Blast of the Trumpet. Whoever of them follows you — indeed Hell shall be your requital both yours and theirs a requital that is indeed ample sufficient and complete.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of following Iblis?
Will Hell be a reward for those who follow Iblis?
Is the reward for following Iblis ample and sufficient?
propositions: Allah responded, 'Be gone!'
Whoever follows Iblis will receive Hell as their reward.
Hell is an ample and complete reward for those who follow Iblis.

source_text:
Verse: And incite whoever you can of them with your voice, mobilize against them all your cavalry and infantry, manipulate them in their wealth and children, and make them promises.” But Satan promises them nothing but delusion.

Tafsir: And tempt dupe whomever of them you can with your voice by your calling them with songs and pipes and with every invitation to acts of disobedience; and rally incite against them your cavalry and your infantry namely those who ride and walk in acts of disobedience and share with them in wealth that is illicit such as usury and extortion and children from acts of adultery and make promises to them’ to the effect that there will not be any resurrection or requital. And Satan promises them thereby nothing but delusion falsehood.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of following Satan's temptations?
How can one avoid falling prey to Satan's deception?
What is the nature of the promises made by Satan to those who follow him?
propositions: Satan tempts people with their voice through songs and pipes.
Satan rallies people against each other through acts of disobedience.
Satan makes promises that lead to delusion and falsehood.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Allah added,˺ “You will truly have no authority over My ˹faithful˺ servants.” And sufficient is your Lord as a Guardian.

Tafsir: ‘Truly as for My servants the believers you shall have no warrant’ no sway or ability. And Your Lord suffices as a guardian as a protector for them against you.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's authority over believers?
Can non-believers have any sway or influence over faithful servants?
How does Allah's guardianship protect His servants from harm?
propositions: You will truly have no authority over My faithful servants.
Your Lord suffices as a guardian for them against you.

source_text:
Verse: It is your Lord Who steers the ships for you through the sea, so that you may seek His bounty. Surely He is ever Merciful to you.

Tafsir: Your Lord is He Who drives for you the ships upon the sea that you may seek of His bounty exalted be He through engaging in commerce. Truly He is ever Merciful towards you by disposing these ships for you.

hype_questions: Does Allah guide us in our navigation through the sea?
Can we seek Allah's bounty by engaging in commerce?
Is Allah Merciful towards us?
propositions: Your Lord steers the ships for you through the sea.
He drives for you the ships upon the sea that you may seek of His bounty.
Truly He is ever Merciful towards you by disposing these ships for you.

source_text:
Verse: When you are touched with hardship at sea, you ˹totally˺ forget all ˹the gods˺ you ˹normally˺ invoke, except Him. But when He delivers you ˹safely˺ to shore, you turn away. Humankind is ever ungrateful.

Tafsir: And when distress difficulty befalls you at sea such as fear of drowning those whom you are wont to invoke are no longer present those whom you are wont to worship of gods are no longer present and so you do not call on them — except Him exalted be He for on Him alone you do call because you are suffering a distress which only He can remove. But when He delivers you from drowning and brings you to land you are rejective of God’s Oneness for man is ever ungrateful ever denying God’s graces.

hype_questions: What happens when you're in a desperate situation at sea?
Why do people turn away from their faith when they're in trouble?
How can we cultivate gratitude and faith in the face of adversity?
propositions: When hardship strikes, one forgets all other deities except God.
God is the only deity worthy of invocation during times of distress.
Man's ingratitude towards God's blessings is a recurring theme throughout history.
Faith and gratitude are essential for navigating life's challenges.

source_text:
Verse: Do you feel secure that He will not cause the land to swallow you up, or unleash upon you a storm of stones? Then you will find none to protect you.

Tafsir: Do you feel secure that He will not cause a side of the earth in other words the land to swallow you up as He did with Korah Qārūn or unleash upon you a squall of pebbles? that is hurl a shower of stones upon you as He did with the people of Lot. Then you will not find for yourselves any guardian any protector from Him.

hype_questions: Will Allah protect me from the earth swallowing me up?
What will happen if Allah unleashes a storm of stones upon me?
Can I find protection from Allah in times of need?
propositions: He will not cause the land to swallow you up.
He will unleash upon you a squall of pebbles.
You will not find for yourselves any guardian or protector from Him.

source_text:
Verse: Or do you feel secure that He will not send you back to sea once again, and send upon you a violent storm, drowning you for your denial? Then you will find none to avenge you against Us.

Tafsir: Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it that is to the sea a second time and unleash upon you a shattering gale that is a violent wind that shatters everything in its path to destroy your ship and drown you for your ungratefulness? And then you will not find for yourselves any redresser of this against Us any helper or advocate to demand restitution from Us for what We will have done to you.

hype_questions: Will I be punished if I deny Allah?
What will happen to me if I am ungrateful to Allah?
Can anyone help me against Allah?
propositions: Allah will not return you to the sea a second time.
Allah will unleash upon you a shattering gale that is a violent wind.
You will not find any redresser of this against Us.
We will have done what We will have done to you.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We have dignified the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea, granted them good and lawful provisions, and privileged them far above many of Our creatures.

Tafsir: And verily We have honoured We have preferred the Children of Adam above other creation by giving them knowledge speech and their being a creation of even proportions amongst other things including their means of purification after death and carried them over land on animal-back and sea in ships and provided them with good things and We have preferred them above many of those whom We created such as livestock and wild animals with a marked preferment the min of mimman ‘of those whom’ has the sense of mā ‘of what’ or something close to it and includes the angels the purpose being to give preference to the angelic genus; there is no requirement to give explicit preference to the individuals of this category of being since they angels are superior to mankind excepting the prophets.

hype_questions: What are the benefits granted to humans by Allah?
How does Allah prefer humans over other creations?
What is the significance of angels in Islam?
propositions: Allah has dignified the children of Adam.
Allah has carried them on land and sea.
Allah has granted them good and lawful provisions.
Allah has privileged them above many of His creatures.
The Children of Adam are a creation of even proportions amongst other things.
The Children of Adam have been given knowledge, speech, and means of purification after death.
Angels are superior to mankind excepting the prophets.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Beware of˺ the Day We will summon every people with their leader. So whoever will be given their record in their right hand will read it ˹happily˺ and will not be wronged ˹even by the width of˺ the thread of a date stone.

Tafsir: Mention the day when We shall summon all men with their leader their prophet and it will be said ‘O community of so-and-so’; or it bi-imāmihim means ‘with the record of their deeds’ in which case it will be said ‘O one of good deeds O one of evil deeds!’ this is on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever from among them is given his book in his right hand these being the fortunate those possessors of understanding in this world — those will read their book and they will not be wronged they will not be diminished of their deeds so much as a single date-thread.

hype_questions: What will be the state of those who are given their record in their right hand on the Day of Resurrection?
How will those who possess understanding in this world be treated on the Day of Resurrection?
What is the significance of being given one's book in one's right hand?
propositions: The Day of Resurrection will summon all men with their leader, their prophet.
Those who are given their record in their right hand will read it happily and will not be wronged even by the width of a date stone.
The Day of Resurrection is a time when individuals will be accounted for their deeds.

source_text:
Verse: But whoever is blind ˹to the truth˺ in this ˹world˺ will be blind in the Hereafter, and ˹even˺ far more astray from the ˹Right˺ Way.

Tafsir: And whoever has been in this that is in this world blind to the truth will be blind in the Hereafter to the path of salvation and the reciting of the Qur’ān and even further astray from the right way more removed from the road that leads to it.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of being blind to the truth in this world?
How does blindness to the truth affect one's path to salvation?
What happens when one is further astray from the right way?
propositions: Whoever is blind to the truth in this world will be blind in the Hereafter.
Blindness to the truth in this world leads to blindness to the path of salvation and the reciting of the Qur'ān.
Being further astray from the right way means being more removed from the road that leads to it.

source_text:
Verse: They definitely ˹thought they˺ were about to lure you away from what We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺, hoping that you would attribute something else to Us falsely—and then they would have certainly taken you as a close friend.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding the tribe of Thaqīf for they had asked him the Prophet s to declare their valley inviolable and implored him to grant them this request And indeed wa-in the particle in is softened they were about to they nearly did beguile you away from that which We revealed to you so that you might invent against Us something other than that; and then had you done that they would have taken you as a friend.

hype_questions: Would the Prophet be deceived by the tribe of Thaqīf's request?
How would the Prophet respond to the tribe of Thaqīf's plea for their valley to be declared inviolable?
What would have happened if the Prophet had invented something against Allah?
propositions: The Prophet was about to be deceived by the tribe of Thaqīf.
The tribe of Thaqīf asked the Prophet to declare their valley inviolable.
If the Prophet had invented something against Allah, they would have taken him as a friend.

source_text:
Verse: Had We not made you steadfast, you probably would have inclined to them a little,

Tafsir: And if We had not made you stand firm upon the Truth by way of divine protection ‘isma certainly you might have you nearly inclined to them a little because of the extent of their deception and their persistence. This statement is explicit about the fact that the Prophet s neither inclined nor came close to doing so.

hype_questions: Would I have been swayed by their deception if not for divine protection?
How did the Prophet's steadfastness on Truth impact his relationship with them?
What would have happened to me if I had wavered in my faith?
propositions: The Prophet was made steadfast upon the Truth by divine protection.
If not for this protection, he might have been inclined to their deception.
The Prophet's steadfastness on Truth prevented him from being swayed by their persistence.

source_text:
Verse: and then We truly would have made you taste double ˹punishment˺ both in this life and after death, and you would have found no helper against Us.

Tafsir: Then had you inclined We would have surely made you taste a double chastisement in life and a double chastisement upon death in other words twice the chastisement that any other person would receive in this world and the Hereafter. Then you would not have found for yourself any helper against Us anyone to shield you from it.

hype_questions: Would I be able to escape the double punishment if I had been more obedient?
What would happen to me if I didn't have anyone to help me in this life and the hereafter?
Can I find any way to avoid the chastisement that Allah has planned for me?
propositions: Allah would have made you taste double punishment in this life.
You would have found no helper against Allah in this life and the hereafter.
The chastisement is not just limited to one lifetime, but also extends to the afterlife.

source_text:
Verse: They were about to intimidate you to drive you out of the land ˹of Mecca˺, but then they would not have survived after you ˹had left˺ except for a little while.

Tafsir: When the Jews said to him ‘If you are a prophet then make your way to Syria for it is the land of prophets’ the following was revealed And indeed wa-in the particle in is softened they were about to provoke you out of the land the land of Medina to expel you from it but then had they expelled you they would not have remained after you in it except a little while after which they would have been destroyed.

hype_questions: What would have happened if the Jews had succeeded in expelling Prophet Muhammad from Medina?
How long would the Jews have remained in power after expelling Prophet Muhammad?
What would have been the ultimate fate of the Jews if they had succeeded in expelling Prophet Muhammad?
propositions: The Jews were about to intimidate Prophet Muhammad to drive him out of Mecca.
If the Jews had expelled Prophet Muhammad from Medina, they would not have remained in power for a long time.
Prophet Muhammad was prophesied to be destroyed if he left Medina.

source_text:
Verse: ˹This has been˺ Our way with the messengers We sent before you. And you will never find any change in Our way.

Tafsir: That is the way in the case of those whom We have sent from among Our messengers before you that is to say that is Our way of dealing with them their enemies destroying those who expel them Our messengers. And as regards Our established way you will not find any change any alternative manner.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's way with His messengers?
How do Allah's enemies treat those who expel His messengers?
Is there any change in Allah's way with His messengers?
propositions: Allah has a fixed way with His messengers.
Those who expel Allah's messengers are destroyed by their enemies.
There is no change in Allah's way with His messengers.

source_text:
Verse: Observe the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night and the dawn prayer, for certainly the dawn prayer is witnessed ˹by angels˺.

Tafsir: Establish prayer from the sun’s decline that is from after midday until the dark of night until its darkness has fallen in other words perform prayers at noon in the afternoon at sunset and at night and the recital of the Qur’ān at dawn the morning prayer. Verily the dawn recital is ever witnessed it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

hype_questions: What is the recommended time for performing prayers?
At what time of day does the dawn prayer take place?
Who witnesses the recital of the Qur'ān?
propositions: Perform prayers from the sun's decline until the darkness of night.
The dawn prayer is witnessed by angels.
Recite the Qur'ān at dawn and perform prayers at noon.

source_text:
Verse: And rise at ˹the last˺ part of the night, offering additional prayers, so your Lord may raise you to a station of praise.

Tafsir: And for a part of the night keep vigil perform prayer therewith with the Qur’ān as a supererogatory devotion for you as an extra obligation for you to the exclusion of your community or it means as extra merit for you on top of the other obligatory prayers. It may be that your Lord will raise you to establish you in the Hereafter in a praiseworthy station one for which the first and last of mankind will praise you — and this is the station of intercession which will take place during the passing of the Final Judgement.

hype_questions: Will my Lord raise me to a station of praise in the Hereafter?
What is the station of intercession that will take place during the passing of the Final Judgement?
How can I earn extra merit with Allah through supererogatory prayers?
propositions: Rise at the last part of the night to offer additional prayers.
Perform prayer therewith with the Qur’ān as a supererogatory devotion.
Your Lord may raise you to establish you in the Hereafter in a praiseworthy station.

source_text:
Verse: And say, “My Lord! Grant me an honourable entrance and an honourable exit and give me a supporting authority from Yourself.”

Tafsir: And say ‘My Lord make me enter Medina with a veritable entrance an entrance that is satisfying one in which I do not see what I dislike and bring me out of Mecca with a veritable departure a departure such that my heart will not care to turn back to look at it yearningly. And grant me from Yourself a favourable authority’ grant me strength with which You render me victorious over Your enemies.

hype_questions: What is the ideal way to enter a city after migrating?
How can one avoid feeling nostalgic about their old life when leaving it behind?
What kind of authority does Allah grant to His servants?
propositions: Say, 'My Lord, grant me an honourable entrance.'
Grant me an honourable exit.
Give me a supporting authority from Yourself.
Make me enter Medina with a veritable entrance.
Bring me out of Mecca with a veritable departure.
Grant me strength with which You render me victorious over Your enemies.

source_text:
Verse: And declare, “The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish.”

Tafsir: And say upon your entry into Mecca ‘The Truth Islam has come and falsehood has vanished away disbelief has come to nothing. Truly falsehood is ever bound to vanish’ ever bound to fade away and disappear. Indeed the Prophet s entered it Mecca and there were 360 idols which had been placed around the Sacred House sc. the Ka‘ba. He the Prophet then set about thrusting at them with a stick he was carrying saying those words until they had all been toppled as reported by the two Shaykhs Bukhārī and Muslim.

hype_questions: Does the arrival of Islam mark the end of falsehood?
Can disbelief be eradicated from society?
How did the Prophet handle idolatry in Mecca?
propositions: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished.
Falsehood is bound to vanish away.
The Prophet entered Mecca and toppled 360 idols around the Sacred House.

source_text:
Verse: We send down the Quran as a healing and mercy for the believers, but it only increases the wrongdoers in loss.

Tafsir: And We reveal of min here is explicative the Qur’ān that which is a cure from error and a mercy for believers thereby; though it only increases the evildoers the disbelievers in loss because of their disbelief in it.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the Quran?
How does the Quran affect non-believers?
Can faith bring healing?
propositions: The Quran was sent as a healing and mercy for believers.
The Quran only increases wrongdoers in loss due to their disbelief.

source_text:
Verse: When We grant people Our favours, they turn away, acting arrogantly. But when touched with evil, they lose all hope.

Tafsir: And when We are gracious to man the disbelieving man he is disregardful of giving thanks and turns aside turning his face away in arrogance; but when an ill such as poverty or hardship befalls him he is in despair despondent of God’s mercy.

hype_questions: What happens when a person is granted favors by God, but then turns away in arrogance?
How does a disbeliever respond to God's blessings?
What is the state of a person who faces poverty or hardship and loses hope?
propositions: When people are granted favors, they turn away arrogantly.
A disbeliever is disregarding when he is grateful.
Poverty or hardship befalls a person, and he becomes despondent of God's mercy.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Everyone acts in their own way. But your Lord knows best whose way is rightly guided.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Everyone including us and you acts according to his own character his own manner of conduct and your Lord knows best who is better guided as to the way’ as to the path he follows and He will reward him accordingly.

hype_questions: Does Allah have a plan for each individual's life?
Can humans make choices that affect their fate?
How does Allah reward or punish individuals?
propositions: Everyone acts in their own way.
Your Lord knows best whose way is rightly guided.
The path one follows will be rewarded accordingly.

source_text:
Verse: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the spirit. Say, “Its nature is known only to my Lord, and you ˹O humanity˺ have been given but little knowledge.”

Tafsir: And they will question you that is the Jews concerning the Spirit from which the body receives life. Say to them ‘The Spirit is of the command of my Lord that is it belongs to His knowledge about which you know not. And of knowledge you have not been given except a little’ relative to His knowledge exalted be He.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Spirit?
How does the body receive life from the Spirit?
What is the relationship between the Spirit and God's knowledge?
propositions: The Prophet was asked about the Spirit.
The Spirit's nature is known only to God.
Humans have been given little knowledge compared to God's exalted knowledge.

source_text:
Verse: If We willed, We could have certainly taken away what We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺—then you would find none to guarantee its return from Us—

Tafsir: And if la-in the lām is for oaths We willed We could take away what We have revealed to you in other words take away the Qur’ān by erasing it from the hearts of men and from the written copies. Then you would not find in respect thereof any guardian for yourself against Us;

hype_questions: Can the Qur'ān be erased from human hearts and written copies?
Who can guarantee the return of the Qur'ān to its original state?
What would happen if the Qur'ān were to be taken away?
propositions: We could have certainly taken away what We have revealed to you.
If We willed, We could take away the Qur'ān by erasing it from the hearts of men and from the written copies.
Then you would find none to guarantee its return from Us.

source_text:
Verse: had it not been for the mercy of your Lord. Indeed, His favour upon you is immense.

Tafsir: it is only — but We have let it remain — as a mercy from your Lord. Truly His favour to you is ever great tremendous for He has revealed to you and granted you the praiseworthy station as well as other kinds of merit.

hype_questions: What is the immense favour of Allah upon His servants?
How has Allah revealed Himself to His servants?
What is the praiseworthy station granted by Allah?
propositions: Had it not been for the mercy of your Lord,
Indeed, His favour upon you is immense.
It is only — but We have let it remain — as a mercy from your Lord.
Truly His favour to you is ever great tremendous for He has revealed to you and granted you the praiseworthy station as well as other kinds of merit.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If ˹all˺ humans and jinn were to come together to produce the equivalent of this Quran, they could not produce its equal, no matter how they supported each other.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Verily should mankind and jinn come together to produce the like of this Qur’ān the like thereof in terms of clarity and rhetorical excellence they could not produce the like thereof even if they backed one another’ even if one was an assistant of the other. This verse was revealed as a refutation of their statement ‘If we wish we can speak the like of this’ Q. 831.

hype_questions: Can humans and jinn produce a text as clear and eloquent as the Quran?
How would the combined efforts of humans and jinn affect their ability to create something like the Quran?
What would happen if humans and jinn worked together to produce a text with similar clarity and excellence?
propositions: Humans and jinn cannot produce a text as clear and eloquent as the Quran, even if they work together.
The Quran's clarity and rhetorical excellence are unmatched by any human or jinn effort.
Assistance from one another would not improve the ability of humans and jinn to create something like the Quran.

source_text:
Verse: And We have truly set forth every ˹kind of˺ lesson for humanity in this Quran, yet most people persist in disbelief.

Tafsir: And verily We have dispensed explained for people in this Qur’ān every kind of similitude min kulli mathalin this is an adjectival qualification of an omitted clause in other words ‘We have dispensed a similitude from every kind of similitude’ that they might be admonished; but most people that is the people of Mecca insist on disbelieving on denying the truth.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the Quran's lessons for humanity?
Why do most people persist in disbelief despite being admonished with similitudes?
How does the concept of Mecca relate to the theme of disbelieving in truth?
propositions: We have set forth every kind of lesson for humanity in this Quran.
We dispensed a similitude from every kind of similitude to admonish people.
Most people of Mecca insist on disbelieving the truth.

source_text:
Verse: They challenge ˹the Prophet˺, “We will never believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us,
