source_text:
Verse: And warn them ˹O Prophet˺ of the Day of Regret, when all matters will be settled, while they are ˹engrossed˺ in heedlessness and disbelief.

Tafsir: And warn them threaten O Muhammad (s) the disbelievers of Mecca of the Day of Regret namely the Day of Resurrection on which the sinner will regret not having been virtuous in the life of this world when the matter will be decided for them thereupon that they be chastised while they in this world are yet heedless of it and do not believe in it the Day of Resurrection.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the Day of Regret?
Will the sinner regret not being virtuous in this life?
How will the disbelievers be chastised on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: The Day of Regret is a future event that will settle all matters.
The disbelievers of Mecca will be threatened by Muhammad (s) on the Day of Regret.
The sinner will regret not being virtuous in this life on the Day of Resurrection.
The matter will be decided for them on the Day of Regression.
They will be chastised on the Day of Regression while they are yet heedless of it.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, it is We Who will succeed the earth and whoever is on it. And to Us they will ˹all˺ be returned.

Tafsir: Indeed We innā nahnu a repetition of the first person for emphasis shall inherit the earth and all who are on it of rational beings and others by destroying them and to Us they shall be returned thereon on the Day of Resurrection for requital.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who are on the earth after it is inherited?
Who will inherit the earth and all its inhabitants?
What is the purpose of the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: We will succeed the earth.
All beings on the earth will be returned to Us.
The earth and all its inhabitants will be destroyed before being returned to Us.

source_text:
Verse: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Abraham. He was surely a man of truth and a prophet.

Tafsir: And mention to them in the Book Abraham that is mention his tale. Indeed he was a truthful one the intensive form siddīq means ‘extremely truthful’ a prophet the following statement substitutes for the preceding predicate.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be a truthful prophet?
How did Abraham's truthfulness impact his prophetic role?
Can truthfulness be an essential characteristic of a prophet?
propositions: The Prophet is mentioned in the Book.
Abraham was a man of truth and a prophet.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember˺ when he said to his father, “O dear father! Why do you worship what can neither hear nor see, nor benefit you at all?

Tafsir: When he said to his father Āzar ‘O my father! the final tā’ here of abati has replaced the possessive yā’ of genitive annexation sc. of yā abī; the two however are never used together — he Abraham’s father used to worship idols. Why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees and is of no avail to you suffices you not in any way? whether in terms of benefit or harm.

hype_questions: Does worshiping idols bring any benefit or harm to a person?
Can idols hear or see, and do they have any impact on human life?
Is it sufficient for humans to rely solely on idols for their well-being?
propositions: Abraham's father used to worship idols.
Idols neither hear nor see and are of no avail to humans in terms of benefit or harm.
Humans should not rely solely on idols for their well-being.

source_text:
Verse: O  dear father! I have certainly received some knowledge which you have not received, so follow me and I will guide you to the Straight Path.

Tafsir: O my father! Indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you. So follow me that I may guide you to a path a route that is right that is straight.

hype_questions: What guidance can be received from the Quran?
How does one find the right path in life?
What is the significance of following a guide on the Straight Path?
propositions: I have received knowledge that you have not.
Follow me to receive guidance.
The Straight Path is the correct route.

source_text:
Verse: O  dear father! Do not worship Satan. Surely Satan is ever rebellious against the Most Compassionate.

Tafsir: O my father! Do not worship Satan by obeying him through your worship of idols. Truly Satan is disobedient the intensive form‘asiyyan means ‘one given to disobedience’ to the Compassionate One.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Satan's rebellion?
How does one worship idols in a way that obeys Satan?
What is the meaning of 'one given to disobedience'?
propositions: Do not worship Satan.
Satan is ever rebellious against the Most Compassionate.
Obeying Satan through worship of idols is considered disobedience.

source_text:
Verse: O  dear father! I truly fear that you will be touched by a torment from the Most Compassionate, and become Satan’s companion ˹in Hell˺.”

Tafsir: O my father! I do fear lest a chastisement from the Compassionate One should befall you if you do not repent and then you become an ally of Satan an assistant and a comrade of his in the Fire.

hype_questions: What happens if I don't repent?
Can I avoid becoming Satan's companion?
How can I escape the Fire?
propositions: If you do not repent, a chastisement from the Compassionate One will befall you.
You will become an ally of Satan and his assistant if you do not repent.
The Fire is the destination for those who become Satan's companions.

source_text:
Verse: He threatened, “How dare you reject my idols, O  Abraham! If you do not desist, I will certainly stone you ˹to death˺. So be gone from me for a long time!”

Tafsir: He said ‘Are you renouncing my gods O Abraham? so that you are denouncing them in this way? If you do not desist from criticising them I shall surely assail you with stones or with evil words so beware of me; and stay away from me for a long time’.

hype_questions: What happens if you reject the idols of a pagan community?
How will the pagan community react to criticism of their false gods?
What is the consequence of rejecting the idols of a pagan community?
propositions: Abraham rejected the idols of his pagan community.
The pagan community threatened Abraham with stoning if he did not desist from criticizing their false gods.
Abraham was commanded to stay away from the pagan community for a long time.

source_text:
Verse: Abraham responded, “Peace be upon you! I will pray to my Lord for your forgiveness. He has truly been Most Gracious to me.

Tafsir: He said ‘Peace be to you from me — in other words I shall not cause you any harm. I shall ask forgiveness of my Lord for you. Truly He is ever gracious to me hafiyyan from hafiyyun meaning bārrun ‘kind’ answering my prayers. And indeed he Abraham fulfilled his above-mentioned promise as described in sūrat al-Shu‘arā’ And forgive my father Q. 2686; but this was before it became clear to him that he Abraham’s father was an enemy of God as mentioned in sūrat Barā’a Q. 9114.

hype_questions: What does it mean to ask for forgiveness from God?
How can Abraham's promise be fulfilled?
What is the significance of Abraham's father being an enemy of God?
propositions: Abraham said, 'Peace be upon you! I will pray to my Lord for your forgiveness.'
God is ever gracious to me.
Abraham fulfilled his promise as described in sūrat al-Shu‘arā’.

source_text:
Verse: As I distance myself from ˹all of˺ you and from whatever you invoke besides Allah, I will ˹continue to˺ call upon my Lord ˹alone˺, trusting that I will never be disappointed in invoking my Lord.”

Tafsir: And I shall shun you and that which you call upon that which you worship besides God. I will supplicate I will worship my Lord — hopefully in calling upon in worshipping my Lord I shall not be wretched’ as you have become wretched by your worship of idols.

hype_questions: What happens when one stops worshipping idols and focuses on the one true God?
How does calling upon Allah alone differ from invoking other deities?
What is the outcome of trusting in Allah's sovereignty?
propositions: I will distance myself from you and whatever you invoke besides Allah.
I will shun you and that which you call upon that which you worship besides God.
I will supplicate my Lord alone, hoping to avoid wretchedness.

source_text:
Verse: So after he had left them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and made each of them a prophet.

Tafsir: And so after he had shunned them and that which they worshipped besides God by having set off to the Holy Land We gave him two sons for him to find solace in Isaac and Jacob and each of the two We made a prophet.

hype_questions: What is the significance of prophethood in Islam?
How did Allah provide solace to Prophet Ibrahim after he left his polytheistic community?
Who are Isaac and Jacob, and what role do they play in Islamic theology?
propositions: Prophet Ibrahim left his polytheistic community.
Allah granted Prophet Ibrahim two sons, Isaac and Jacob.
Each of the two sons, Isaac and Jacob, became prophets.

source_text:
Verse: We showered them with Our mercy, and blessed them with honourable mention.

Tafsir: And We gave them all three of them out of Our mercy wealth and offspring and We assigned for them a worthy repute one that is lofty sublime namely We assigned fair praise of them among all the members of the Abrahamic religions.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's mercy?
How does Allah bless His servants with honourable mention?
What is the significance of fair praise among all Abrahamic religions?
propositions: Allah showered them with mercy.
Allah blessed them with wealth and offspring.
Allah assigned a worthy repute to them, which includes fair praise among all members of the Abrahamic religions.

source_text:
Verse: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Moses. He was truly a chosen man, and was a messenger and a prophet.

Tafsir: And mention in the Book Moses. Indeed he was devoted to God read either as mukhlisan to mean ‘one sincerely devoted to worship of God’; or read mukhlasan to mean ‘he was delivered’ as in God had delivered him from defilement and he was a messenger a prophet.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be a chosen man in the context of Islamic theology?
How did Moses' devotion to God impact his role as a messenger and prophet?
What does it mean for someone to be 'delivered' by God, according to Islamic interpretation?
propositions: Moses was a chosen man.
Moses was a messenger and a prophet.
God delivered Moses from defilement.

source_text:
Verse: We called him from the right side of Mount Ṭûr, and drew him near, speaking ˹with him˺ directly.

Tafsir: And We called him — with the words ‘O Moses! Verily I am God’ Q. 279 — from the right side of the Mount al-Tūr is actually the name of a mountain that is from the side to the right of Moses as he was approaching the Mount from Midian; and We brought him near in communion as God exalted be He made him hear His speech.

hype_questions: What was the name of the mountain from which God called Moses?
How did God communicate with Moses on Mount Ṭûr?
Who is the one who called Moses from the right side of Mount Ṭûr?
propositions: God called Moses from the right side of Mount Ṭûr.
The name of the mountain is al-Tūr, which is to the right of Moses as he approached it from Midian.
God brought Moses near in communion and made him hear His speech.

source_text:
Verse: And We appointed for him—out of Our grace—his brother, Aaron, as a prophet.

Tafsir: And We gave him out of Our mercy Our grace his brother Aaron Hārūn either a substitution for akhāhu ‘his brother’ or an explicative supplement thereof likewise a prophet nabiyyan a circumstantial qualifier constituting the import of the ‘gift’ to Moses which was in response to his Moses’s request that He God send forth his brother with him; he Aaron was older in years than him.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Aaron's prophethood in Islamic theology?
How does mercy play a role in the appointment of prophets?
What does it mean for Moses to have his brother sent with him as a prophet?
propositions: God appointed Aaron as a prophet out of His grace.
Aaron was Moses's brother and was sent with him as a prophet.
The appointment of Aaron as a prophet was in response to Moses's request.

source_text:
Verse: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Ishmael. He was truly a man of his word, and was a messenger and a prophet.

Tafsir: And mention in the Book Ishmael. Indeed he was true to his promise — he never promised anything which he did not fulfil; he once waited for three days for someone whom he had promised to meet; or it is said that he waited an entire year until that person finally returned to the place in which he Ishamel was supposed to have met the former; and he was a messenger to the tribe of Jurhum a prophet likewise.

hype_questions: What is the story of Ishmael in the Quran?
How did Ishmael fulfill his promises?
What was Ishmael's role as a prophet?
propositions: Ishmael was a man of his word.
Ishmael fulfilled all his promises.
Ishmael was a messenger to the tribe of Jurhum.

source_text:
Verse: He used to urge his people to pray and give alms-tax. And his Lord was well pleased with him.

Tafsir: He used to enjoin upon his kinsfolk that is his people prayer and the payment of alms and he was pleasing to his Lord mardiyyan ‘pleasing’ is actually marduwwun but both wāw letters have been changed to two yā’ letters while the kasra vowel has also been changed to a damma vowel.

hype_questions: What is the importance of enjoining prayer and alms-tax on one's family?
How does one demonstrate their obedience to Allah by performing these acts?
What are the rewards for following the example of a righteous person?
propositions: He used to urge his people to pray.
He used to enjoin upon his kinsfolk that is his people prayer and the payment of alms.
His Lord was well pleased with him.

source_text:
Verse: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Enoch. He was surely a man of truth and a prophet.

Tafsir: And mention in the Book Idrīs who was Noah’s great-grandfather. Indeed he was a truthful one a prophet.

hype_questions: What is the story of Enoch in the Quran?
Who was Idris and what is his significance in Islamic history?
How does the concept of truthfulness relate to prophethood?
propositions: The Prophet Muhammad mentioned Enoch in the Book.
Idrīs was Noah's great-grandfather.
Enoch was a truthful one and a prophet.

source_text:
Verse: And We elevated him to an honourable status.

Tafsir: And We raised him to a high station — he is alive in the fourth or sixth or seventh heaven or he is in Paradise into which he was admitted after he was made to experience death and brought back to life and he has not exited therefrom.

hype_questions: What is the status of a person who has been raised to a high station?
Can a person experience death and be brought back to life?
Is Paradise accessible only once after experiencing death?
propositions: We elevated him to an honourable status.
He is alive in the fourth or sixth or seventh heaven.
He is in Paradise into which he was admitted after being made to experience death and brought back to life.
He has not exited Paradise from there.

source_text:
Verse: Those were ˹some of˺ the prophets who Allah has blessed from among the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried with Noah ˹in the Ark˺, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those We ˹rightly˺ guided and chose. Whenever the revelations of the Most Compassionate were recited to them, they fell down, prostrating and weeping.

Tafsir: Those ūlā’ika is the subject to whom God has been gracious alladhīna an‘ama’Llāhu ‘alayhim is an adjectival qualification of it of the subject from among the prophets mina’l-nabīyyīna an explication of it of the subject functioning like an adjectival qualification in terms of import. That which follows it mina’l-nabīyyīna ‘from among the prophets’ up to where the conditional sentence begins constitutes an adjectival qualification of al-nabīyyīna ‘the prophets’; and so His saying … of the seed of Adam namely Idrīs and of those whom We carried with Noah in the Ark namely Abraham — who is the son of his Noah’s son Shem Sām — and of the seed of Abraham namely Ishmael Isaac and Jacob and of the seed of Israel — who is Jacob — namely Moses Aaron Zachariah John and Jesus and from among those whom We guided and chose that is to say from among their number the predicate of ūlā’ika ‘those’ is the following idhā tutlā … when the signs of the Compassionate One were recited to them they would fall down prostrating and weeping these sujjadan and bukīyyan constitute the plural forms of sājid ‘prostrate’ and bākin ‘weeping’ respectively in other words what is meant is be you like them bukiyyun is originally formed from bakūyyin but the wāw is changed into a yā’ and the damma vowel into a kasra.

hype_questions: What are some of the prophets who Allah has blessed?
How did the prophets react when they heard the revelations of the Most Compassionate?
Who were some of the individuals guided and chosen by Allah?
propositions: Allah has blessed some of the prophets from among the descendants of Adam.
The revelations of the Most Compassionate were recited to the prophets, causing them to fall down prostrating and weeping.
Allah guided and chose some individuals from among the descendants of Abraham and Israel.

source_text:
Verse: But they were succeeded by generations who neglected prayer and followed their lusts and so will soon face the evil consequences.

Tafsir: But there succeeded after them a posterity who neglected the prayer by abandoning performance of it a posterity such as the Jews and the Christians and followed their lusts in the way of acts of disobedience. So they shall soon encounter Ghayy — a valley in Hell — that is they shall fall into it;

hype_questions: What are the consequences of neglecting prayer?
How will those who follow their lusts be punished in the afterlife?
What is Ghayy, and what happens to those who fall into it?
propositions: Generations succeeded each other, neglecting prayer and following their lusts.
A posterity neglected the performance of prayer by abandoning its obligation.
The Jews and Christians followed their lusts in acts of disobedience.
Those who follow their lusts will soon encounter Ghayy, a valley in Hell.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who repent, believe, and do good, it is they who will be admitted into Paradise, never being denied any reward.

Tafsir: whereas those who repent and believe and act righteously — such shall enter Paradise and shall not be wronged they shall not be diminished in any way in their reward;

hype_questions: What is the condition for entering Paradise?
How are those who repent and believe rewarded?
Can one's reward be diminished in Paradise?
propositions: Those who repent, believe, and do good will be admitted into Paradise.
Repentance, belief, and righteous action are necessary for entering Paradise.
The reward of those who repent and believe is not diminished in Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They will be in˺ the Gardens of Eternity, promised in trust by the Most Compassionate to His servants. Surely His promise will be fulfilled.

Tafsir: they shall enter Gardens of Eden as a place of residence jannāti ‘Adnin substitutes for al-janna ‘Paradise’ which the Compassionate One has promised to His servants a promise in the Unseen bi’l-ghaybi a circumstantial qualifier in other words a promise made while they do not see it. Indeed His promise that is to say that which He promises is ever fulfilled meaning that it always arrives the original form of ma’tiyyan is ma’tūyun; or what is meant by His promise here is Paradise to which those deserving of it shall arrive.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Paradise promised by Allah?
How does Allah fulfill His promises to His servants?
What are the characteristics of those who will enter Paradise?
propositions: Allah has promised Paradise to His servants.
Paradise is a place of residence for those deserving of it.
Allah's promise is ever fulfilled and always arrives in its original form.

source_text:
Verse: There they will never hear any idle talk—only ˹greetings of˺ peace. And there they will have their provisions morning and evening.

Tafsir: Therein they shall not hear anything that is trifling of talk but they shall hear only a greeting of ‘Peace!’ from the angels to them or from some among them to others. And therein they will have their provision morning and evening in other words according to the equivalent measure of these two in the life of this world since there is no day or night in Paradise only everlasting light and illumination.

hype_questions: What kind of environment do the righteous enjoy in Paradise?
How are their provisions provided for in Paradise?
What is the nature of time in Paradise?
propositions: They will never hear any idle talk—only greetings of peace.
Therein they shall have their provision morning and evening.
In Paradise, there is no day or night only everlasting light and illumination.

source_text:
Verse: That is Paradise, which We will grant to whoever is devout among Our servants.

Tafsir: That is the Paradise which We shall give as inheritance which We shall grant and in which We shall lodge those of Our servants who are God-fearing through their obedience of Him.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Paradise in Islam?
How does Allah grant inheritance to His servants?
What qualities are required for a person to be considered God-fearing?
propositions: Paradise is an inheritance granted by Allah.
Allah shall lodge those who are God-fearing among His servants in Paradise.
Devotion and obedience to Allah are key characteristics of God-fearing individuals.

source_text:
Verse: “We only descend by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs whatever is before us, and whatever is behind us, and everything in between. And your Lord is never forgetful.

Tafsir: When the Revelation did not come for a number of days the Prophet s said to Gabriel ‘What prevents you from visiting us more often than you do?’ and so the following was revealed And We do not descend except by the commandment of your Lord. To Him belongs all that is before us namely ahead of us of the affairs of the Hereafter and all that is behind us of the affairs of this world and all that is between those two namely all that takes place from this point in time until the coming of the Hour in other words to Him belongs knowledge of all of those things. And your Lord is never forgetful meaning that He is never neglectful of you even when the Revelation is postponed from being sent to you.

hype_questions: What prevents the Prophet from receiving more frequent revelations?
Who has knowledge of all future events?
When will the Hour be revealed?
propositions: We descend by the command of your Lord.
Your Lord belongs to everything before us, behind us, and in between.
Your Lord is never forgetful.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is the˺ Lord of the heavens, and the earth, and everything in between. So worship Him ˹alone˺, and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of anyone equal to Him ˹in His attributes˺?”

Tafsir: He is the Lord the Owner of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them. So worship Him and be steadfast in His worship in other words continue to perform it patiently. Do you know of anyone who could be His namesake? anyone named with that same title? No!

hype_questions: Is there anyone who can be considered equal to Allah in terms of His attributes?
Can anyone be named after Allah?
Who is worthy of worship and devotion?
propositions: Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them.
Worship Allah alone and be steadfast in His worship.
No one can be considered equal to Allah in terms of His attributes.
No one can be named after Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Yet ˹some˺ people ask ˹mockingly˺, “After I die, will I really be raised to life again?”

Tafsir: And man the denier of the Resurrection — namely Ubayy b. Khalaf or al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra concerning whom the verse was revealed — says ‘When read a-idha either pronouncing the second hamza or not but inserting an alif between the two hamzas in both readings I am dead shall I then be brought forth alive?’ from the grave as Muhammad (s) says? the interrogative here statement is meant as a denial in other words he means to say I shall not be brought forth alive after death; mā of mā mittu ‘I am dead’ is extra for emphasis likewise extra is the lām of la-sawfa ‘shall I then’. He God then responds to him with the following saying of His exalted be He

hype_questions: Will I be raised to life again after death?
What happens to a person who denies the Resurrection?
How will God respond to someone who questions their fate?
propositions: Some people ask if they will be raised to life again after death.
The denier of the Resurrection, Ubayy b. Khalaf or al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, asks if he will be brought forth alive from the grave.
God responds that a person who denies the Resurrection is dead and will not be brought forth alive.
The extra words 'I am dead' and 'shall I then' are used for emphasis.
God's response to the denier of the Resurrection is His exalted saying...

source_text:
Verse: Do ˹such˺ people not remember that We created them before, when they were nothing?

Tafsir: Does not man then remember yadhdhakaru is actually yatadhakkaru but the tā’ has been changed to a dhāl and assimilated with the other dhāl; a variant reading leaves it as yadhkuru that We created him before when he was nothing? and thus infer from the first act of creation the possibility of resurrection.

hype_questions: Can humans remember their past existence before being created?
Does the concept of creation imply the possibility of resurrection?
What is the significance of remembering one's past in Islamic theology?
propositions: Humans were created before existing.
The act of creation implies the possibility of resurrection.
Remembering one's past existence is significant in Islamic theology.

source_text:
Verse: By your Lord ˹O Prophet˺! We will surely gather them along with the devils, and then set them around Hell on their knees.

Tafsir: For by your Lord We will surely gather them namely the deniers of the Resurrection and the devils that is to say We shall gather every one of them with his devil bound together in a chain; then We shall bring them around Hell around the outside of it crouching on their knees jithiyyan is the plural of jāthin and is originally formed as jathawuwwin or jathawiyyun deriving from the verb jathā imperfect tense yajthu or yajthī two variant forms.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who deny the Resurrection?
How will the devils be punished in the afterlife?
Will the Prophet be present during the gathering of all souls?
propositions: By your Lord, We will gather them along with the devils.
We will gather every one of them with his devil bound together in a chain.
Then We shall bring them around Hell around the outside of it crouching on their knees.

source_text:
Verse: Then We will certainly begin by dragging out of every group the ones most defiant to the Most Compassionate.

Tafsir: Then We shall pluck out from every party every sect whichever of them was most hardened in disdain in insolence of the Compassionate One.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Most Compassionate?
How does the Most Compassionate respond to defiance?
What is the ultimate fate of those who are hardened in disdain?
propositions: We will drag out of every group the ones most defiant to the Most Compassionate.
The Most Compassionate responds to insolence with disdain.
Those who are hardened in disdain will be dealt with by the Most Compassionate.

source_text:
Verse: And We truly know best who is most deserving of burning in it.

Tafsir: Then indeed We shall know best those most deserving of it most worthy of being in Hell the most hardened of them and others like them for the burning for the admission into it and the scorching therein and We shall start with them siliyyan is originally formed as salawiyyun from the verb saliya or salaya.

hype_questions: What are the characteristics of those most deserving of Hell?
Who will be the first to enter Hell?
What is the nature of Jahannam?
propositions: We shall know best those most deserving of Hell.
Those most deserving of Hell are the most hardened of them and others like them.
Jahannam was originally formed as salawiyyun from the verb saliya or salaya.

source_text:
Verse: There is none of you who will not pass over it. ˹This is˺ a decree your Lord must fulfil.

Tafsir: There is not one of you but shall come to it that is but shall enter Hell. That is an inevitability already decreed by your Lord something which He made inevitable and which He decreed; He will not waive it.

hype_questions: What happens to those who do not fulfill the decree of Allah?
Can one's fate be changed after it has been decreed by Allah?
What is the nature of the inevitability decreed by Allah?
propositions: There is none of you who will not pass over it.
A decree must be fulfilled.
One shall come to it and enter Hell.
This is an inevitability already decreed by your Lord.
He made inevitable and which He decreed; He will not waive it.

source_text:
Verse: Then We will deliver those who were devout, leaving the wrongdoers there on their knees.

Tafsir: Then We will deliver read nunajjī or nunjī those who were wary of committing idolatry or disbelief We will deliver them from it and leave those who did wrong by way of idolatry and disbelief crouching therein on their knees.

hype_questions: What happens to those who were devout in the afterlife?
How will Allah deliver those who were wary of committing idolatry or disbelief?
What fate awaits those who did wrong by way of idolatry and disbelief?
propositions: We will deliver those who were devout.
Those who were wary of committing idolatry or disbelief will be delivered from it.
Those who did wrong by way of idolatry and disbelief will crouch on their knees.

source_text:
Verse: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, the disbelievers ask the believers ˹mockingly˺, “Which of the two of us is better in status and superior in assembly?”

Tafsir: And when Our manifest evident bayyinātin ‘manifest’ is a circumstantial qualifier signs in the Qur’ān are recited to them namely to the believers and the disbelievers those who disbelieve say to those who believe ‘Which of the two parties — us or you — is better in station in lodging and abode read as maqāman it is derived from the first form qāma ‘he stood’; read as muqāman it is derived from the fourth form aqāma ‘he took up residence’ and more excellent in assembly?’ nadiyyan meaning the place in which a folk assemble and converse. They the disbelievers mean ‘we are the better of the two parties’ and so we will fare better than you. God exalted be He says

hype_questions: Will the believers fare better than the disbelievers in terms of status and assembly?
What is the meaning of 'bayyinātin' in the context of Qur'ān recitation?
How do the disbelievers perceive their relationship with the believers in terms of station and lodging?
propositions: The disbelievers ask the believers which party is better in status and superior in assembly.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whoever is ˹entrenched˺ in misguidance, the Most Compassionate will allow them plenty of time, until—behold!—they face what they are threatened with: either the torment or the Hour. Only then will they realize who is worse in position and inferior in manpower.”

Tafsir: Say ‘As for him who is in error man kāna fī’l-dalālati a conditional clause the response to which is fa’l-yamdud ‘He shall prolong’ and what follows it the Compassionate One shall defer fa’l-yamdud functions in the sense of a predicate him from chastisement by granting him some respite in this world drawing him on to his eventual chastisement gradually until when they catch sight of that which they were promised whether it be chastisement in this world by being killed or taken captive or the Hour the Resurrection that comprises Hell they will enter it. Their hosts will be the devils while the hosts of the believers against them will be the angels.

Verse: He said, “I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful ˹of dust˺ from the hoof-prints of ˹the horse of˺ the messenger-angel ˹Gabriel˺ then cast it ˹on the moulded calf˺. This is what my lower-self tempted me into.”

Tafsir: He said ‘I perceived what they did not perceive read either as third person plural yabsurū or as second person plural tabsurū ‘what you did not perceive’ in other words I realised what they did not realise so I seized a handful of dust from the track of from the hoof of the steed of the messenger Gabriel and threw it in I cast it onto the figure of the calf that had been fashioned. Thus my soul prompted thus it adorned for me’ and it was cast into me the idea that I seize a handful of the dust from that mentioned hoof and cast it onto what possessed no spirit so that it might thus acquire a spirit. I had seen that your people had asked that you make for them a god and so my soul suggested to me the idea that this calf should be their god.

Verse: Moses said, “Go away then! And for ˹the rest of your˺ life you will surely be crying, ‘Do not touch ˹me˺!’ that you cannot escape. Now look at your god to which you have been devoted: we will burn it up, then scatter it in the sea completely.”

Tafsir: Said he Moses to him ‘Begone! It shall be yours as your lot throughout life that is for the duration of your life to say to whomever you may see “Do not touch me!” that is do not come near me — he used to wander about aimlessly throughout the land and whenever he touched a person or a person touched him both would succumb to a fever. And indeed there will be a tryst for you for you to be chastised which you will not fail to keep read lan tukhlifahu meaning ‘a tryst which you shall not miss’; or lan tukhlafahu ‘for which you will not be forgotten’ meaning ‘nay you will be sent forth to keep it’. Now look at your god to whom you remained clinging! zalta is actually zalilta but the first lām has been omitted in order to soften it that is to say you remained by his your god’s side worshipping him. We will surely burn it in fire and then scatter the ashes of it into the waters we will disperse it into the winds of the sea; and after having slaughtered it Moses did exactly that which he has mentioned.

The god to which Moses has been devoted will be burned in fire and scattered into the sea.
Moses will be chastised for his past actions.

source_text:
Verse: So be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say. And glorify the praises of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset, and glorify Him in the hours of the night and at both ends of the day, so that you may be pleased ˹with the reward˺.

Tafsir: So be patient with what they say — this is abrogated by the ‘fighting’ verse cf. Q. 2190ff — and make glorifications pray by praising your Lord bi-hamdi rabbika is a circumstantial qualifier in other words ‘ensconced in such praise’ before the rising of the sun the morning prayer and before its setting — the afternoon prayer — and in the watches of the night during the hours thereof and make glorifications perform the sunset and the evening prayer and at either side of the day wa-atrāfa’l-nahāri a supplement to the syntactical locus of the accusative clause wa-min ānā’i ‘and in the watches’ in other words perform the noon prayer because the time for it begins at the point where the sun starts to go down which is the end side of the first half of the day and the start side of the second half of the day; that perhaps you may be pleased with the reward that you will be given.

hype_questions: What is the ideal time to perform prayers in Islam?
How can one ensure they are pleasing to Allah with their worship?
What is the significance of glorifying one's Lord at different times of the day?
propositions: Be patient with what they say.
Glorify your Lord before sunrise and before sunset, and in the watches of the night and at both ends of the day.
Performing these prayers may lead to being pleased with the reward given by Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Do not let your eyes crave what We have allowed some of the disbelievers to enjoy; the ˹fleeting˺ splendour of this worldly life, which We test them with. But your Lord’s provision ˹in the Hereafter˺ is far better and more lasting.

Tafsir: And do not extend your glance toward what We have given to some pairs certain categories among them to enjoy as the flower of the life of this world its adornment and delight that We may try them thereby to see if they transgress the bounds. And your Lord’s provision in Paradise is better than what they have been given in this world and more enduring longer lasting.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Allah's testing of believers through worldly pleasures?
How does Allah's provision in Paradise compare to what the disbelievers have in this world?
What is the ultimate goal of Allah's testing of believers?
propositions: Allah has allowed some disbelievers to enjoy the fleeting splendor of this worldly life as a test.
The Lord's provision in Paradise is better and more lasting than what the disbelievers have in this world.
Believers are tested through worldly pleasures to see if they transgress the bounds.

source_text:
Verse: Bid your people to pray, and be diligent in ˹observing˺ it. We do not ask you to provide. It is We Who provide for you. And the ultimate outcome is ˹only˺ for ˹the people of˺ righteousness.

Tafsir: And bid your family to prayer and be steadfast in the maintenance of it. We do not ask of you We do not charge you with the procurement of any provision either for yourself or for anyone else. We it is Who provide you and the best sequel Paradise will be in favour of God-fearing for such people.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of prayer?
How does God provide for us?
What happens to those who are righteous?
propositions: Bid your people to pray.
Be diligent in observing it.
We do not ask you to provide.
It is We Who provide for you.
The ultimate outcome is for the people of righteousness.
Bid your family to prayer and be steadfast in its maintenance.
We do not charge you with the procurement of any provision either for yourself or for anyone else.
Paradise will be in favour of God-fearing for such people.

source_text:
Verse: They demand, “If only he could bring us a sign from his Lord!”

Tafsir: And they the idolaters say ‘Why does he Muhammad (s) not bring us a sign from his Lord?’ of the sort which they request. Has there not come to them read ta’tihim or ya’tihim the clear proof the statements of what is in the former scriptures? the tales contained in the Qur’ān relating to past communities and the details of their destruction for denying the messengers?

hype_questions: What is the nature of a sign from God?
How do we know that Muhammad (s) is a prophet?
Can we learn about past communities and their destruction through the Qur'ān?
propositions: They demand a sign from Muhammad (s).
The idolaters ask why Muhammad (s) has not brought them a sign.
The Qur'ān contains clear proof of God's existence and the messages of past prophets.
The stories in the Qur'ān reveal the destruction of communities that denied prophets.
Ta'tihim or ya'tihim are examples of signs mentioned in previous scriptures.

source_text:
Verse: Had We destroyed them with a torment before this ˹Prophet came˺, they would have surely argued, “Our Lord! If only You had sent us a messenger, we would have followed Your revelations before being humiliated and put to shame.”

Tafsir: Had We destroyed them with a chastisement before him before the coming of Muhammad (s) the Messenger they would have said on the Day of Resurrection ‘Our Lord if only You had sent us a messenger so that we might have followed those signs of Yours given to the messengers to convey before we were thus abased at the Resurrection and disgraced?’ in Hell.

hype_questions: Would they have followed the revelations if given the chance?
How would they react to being sent a messenger before their destruction?
What would be their stance on following signs of God's revelation?
propositions: Had We destroyed them with a torment before this Prophet came, they would have surely argued.
They would have said on the Day of Resurrection, 'Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger.'
So that we might have followed those signs of Yours given to the messengers to convey.

source_text:
Verse: Say ˹to them, O  Prophet˺, “Each ˹of us˺ is waiting, so keep waiting! You will soon know who is on the Straight Path and is ˹rightly˺ guided.”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘Each one of us and you is waiting to see what this affair will lead to. So wait! For you shall indeed know at the Resurrection who are the followers of the even path the straight way and who is rightly guided’ away from error us or you.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who are waiting for the Resurrection?
How will we know who is on the Straight Path and is rightly guided?
Will there be a distinction between those who follow the even path and those who stray?
propositions: Each one of us and you is waiting to see what this affair will lead to.
You will soon know who is on the Straight Path and is rightly guided.
At the Resurrection, you shall indeed know who are the followers of the even path and who is rightly guided away from error.

source_text:
Verse: ˹The time of˺ people’s judgment has drawn near, yet they are heedlessly turning away.

Tafsir: Nigh has drawn for mankind the people of Mecca the deniers of the Resurrection their reckoning on the Day of Resurrection yet they are heedless of it disregardful of the preparation required for it by way of embracing faith.

hype_questions: What will be the consequences of ignoring the approaching Judgment Day?
How can one prepare for the Day of Resurrection?
What is the significance of embracing faith in avoiding the reckoning?
propositions: The time of people's judgment has drawn near.
Mankind is being drawn nigh to the people of Mecca, who are deniers of the Resurrection.
Their reckoning on the Day of Resurrection is yet to come.
They are heedless of it and disregardful of the preparation required for it by way of embracing faith.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever new reminder comes to them from their Lord, they only listen to it jokingly,

Tafsir: There does not come to them any new reminder from their Lord revealed gradually in other words new words of the Qur’ān but they listen to it as they play as they engage in mockery

hype_questions: What happens when a person mocks the revelation from their Lord?
How do people respond to new reminders from God?
What is the nature of a person's reaction to the Quran?
propositions: A new reminder comes to them from their Lord.
They only listen to it jokingly.
There does not come to them any new reminder from their Lord revealed gradually in other words new words of the Qur’ān
They listen to it as they play as they engage in mockery

source_text:
Verse: with their hearts ˹totally˺ distracted. The evildoers would converse secretly, ˹saying,˺ “Is this ˹one˺ not human like yourselves? Would you fall for ˹this˺ witchcraft, even though you can ˹clearly˺ see?”

Tafsir: with their hearts preoccupied heedless of its meanings. And they are secret in their conference their speech they the evildoers alladhīna zalamū a substitution for the third person plural indicator wāw of wa-asarrū’l-najwā ‘and they are secret in conference’ ‘Is this namely Muhammad (s) other than a mortal human being like yourselves? and so what he produces is mere sorcery. Will you then take to sorcery will you succumb and follow it even though you are able to see?’ even though you know that it is sorcery?

hype_questions: Will you take to sorcery and succumb to its influence?
Can you see the clear signs of sorcery, yet still follow it?
Are you aware that what they produce is mere sorcery?
propositions: The evildoers converse secretly about Muhammad (s), saying he is not a human being like themselves.
They claim that Muhammad (s) produces witchcraft, which you can clearly see.
You are able to see the signs of sorcery, yet still follow it.

source_text:
Verse: The Prophet responded, “My Lord ˹fully˺ knows every word spoken in the heavens and the earth. For He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”

Tafsir: He said to them ‘My Lord knows the words that are spoken in the heavens and the earth and He is the Hearer of what they keep secret the Knower’ of it.

hype_questions: Does Allah know everything that is spoken in the universe?
Can Allah hear our secrets?
Is Allah all-knowing and all-hearing?
propositions: Allah knows every word spoken in the heavens.
Allah is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
Allah hears what people keep secret.

source_text:
Verse: Yet they say, “This ˹Quran˺ is a set of confused dreams! No, he has fabricated it! No, he must be a poet! So let him bring us a ˹tangible˺ sign like those ˹prophets˺ sent before.”

Tafsir: Nay bal in the three instances below effects a transition from one subject to another but they say regarding those parts of the Qur’ān he the Prophet has brought to them are ‘A muddle of nightmares a confusion of things he has seen in his sleep. Nay he has fabricated it he has invented it; nay he is a poet and what he has brought is merely poetry! So let him bring us a sign such as was sent to the ancients’ like the she-camel Sālih the staff and the glowing hand of Moses. God exalted be He says

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Quran?
How can we trust the Prophet's message?
What kind of sign would be acceptable to the critics?
propositions: The Quran is not a set of confused dreams.
The Prophet has not fabricated or invented the Quran.
The Prophet is not just a poet, but a messenger of God.

source_text:
Verse: Not a ˹single˺ society We destroyed before them ever believed ˹after receiving the signs˺. Will these ˹pagans˺ then believe?

Tafsir: No town before them ever believed — meaning none of its inhabitants — of those that We destroyed for the denial of the signs brought to them. Would they then believe? No.

hype_questions: Will people ever believe after being given clear signs?
Can anyone deny the truth and still be saved?
What is the nature of faith in the face of adversity?
propositions: Not a single society was destroyed before them that believed after receiving the signs.
None of the inhabitants of those destroyed societies believed despite being given clear signs.
They will not believe even if they are given more signs.

source_text:
Verse: We did not send ˹messengers˺ before you ˹O Prophet˺ except mere men inspired by Us. If you ˹polytheists˺ do not know ˹this already˺, then ask those who have knowledge ˹of the Scriptures˺.

Tafsir: And We sent none before you other than men to whom We revealed read nūhī or yūhā ‘to whom it is revealed’ and We sent not any angels. Ask the People of the Remembrance those with knowledge of the Torah and the Gospel if you do not know this; for they will know it. Since you are more likely to believe them than the believers are to believing Muhammad (s).

hype_questions: What is the nature of prophetic revelation?
How do we know about previous prophets and their messages?
Who are the most knowledgeable people to ask about the Torah and Gospel?
propositions: We sent no messengers before you except men inspired by God.
The Torah and Gospel contain knowledge of previous prophets and their messages.
It is more likely that those with knowledge of the Scriptures will believe in Muhammad than believers themselves.

source_text:
Verse: We did not give those messengers ˹supernatural˺ bodies that did not need food, nor were they immortal.

Tafsir: And We did not make them namely the messengers bodies that did not eat food nay they eat it; and they were not immortal in this world.

hype_questions: Can messengers be given supernatural bodies that don't require sustenance?
Are messengers immortal in this world?
Do messengers eat food?
propositions: We did not give those messengers supernatural bodies.
Those messengers have bodies that need food.
Messengers are not immortal in this world.

source_text:
Verse: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, saving them along with whoever We willed and destroying the transgressors.

Tafsir: Then We fulfilled to them the promise to deliver them. So We delivered them and whomever We would of those who believed in them and We destroyed the prodigal those who denied them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who believe in the promise of Allah?
Who are the prodigal ones that Allah destroys?
How does Allah fulfill His promise to deliver believers?
propositions: Allah fulfilled His promise to deliver them.
Believers who were promised salvation were delivered by Allah.
Those who denied the promise of Allah were destroyed.

source_text:
Verse: We have surely revealed to you a Book, in which there is glory for you. Will you not then understand?

Tafsir: Now We have sent down as revelation to you O clan of Quraysh a Book in which there is the remembrance that is yours for it is in your language. Will you not understand? and so believe in it?

hype_questions: Will you not then understand the significance of the Book revealed to you?
Can you comprehend the glory and importance of the message conveyed in this Book?
Do you recognize the relevance of this revelation to your own language and culture?
propositions: We have revealed a Book to you.
The Book contains remembrance that is yours for it is in your language.
You are expected to understand and believe in the Book.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Imagine˺ how many societies of wrongdoers We have destroyed, raising up other people after them!

Tafsir: And how many did We destroy of towns — meaning its inhabitants — that had been wrongdoing disbelieving and brought forth another people after it!

hype_questions: How many societies of wrongdoers have been destroyed by a higher power?
What is the fate of those who engage in wrongdoing and disbelieving behavior?
Can societies be rebuilt after being destroyed?
propositions: We have destroyed many societies of wrongdoers.
We raise up other people after destroying the previous society.
Towns that were inhabited by wrongdoers and disbelievers are destroyed, and another people are raised up in their place.

source_text:
Verse: When the wrongdoers sensed ˹the arrival of˺ Our torment, they started to run away from their cities.

Tafsir: And when they felt Our might when the inhabitants of the town sensed destruction to be near behold they ran away from it they flee hastily therefrom.

hype_questions: What happens when the wrongdoers sense the arrival of Our torment?
Why do the inhabitants of a town flee in haste when they feel destruction is near?
How does the Quran describe the reaction of those who run away from their cities?
propositions: The wrongdoers sensed the arrival of Our torment.
The inhabitants of the town felt destruction was near.
They ran away from it hastily.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They were told,˺ “Do not run away! Return to your luxuries and your homes, so you may be questioned ˹about your fate˺.”

Tafsir: But the angels said to them scornfully ‘Do not run away! Return to the opulence the comforts which you were given to enjoy and your dwelling-places that perhaps you might be asked’ for something of your worldly possessions as usual.

hype_questions: What happens if we don't return to our luxuries and homes?
Will I be punished for not returning to my opulence and comforts?
Can I be asked about something related to my worldly possessions?
propositions: They were told not to run away.
Return to your luxuries and your homes so you may be questioned about your fate.

The angels said do not run away return to the opulence comforts which you were given to enjoy and your dwelling-places that perhaps you might be asked for something of your worldly possessions as usual.

source_text:
Verse: They cried, “Woe to us! We have surely been wrongdoers.”

Tafsir: They said ‘O yā is for calling attention to something woe to us! this is our destruction! We have indeed been doing wrong’ through our disbelief.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of disbelief?
How does one's wrongdoing affect their fate?
What is the nature of destruction in the context of disbelief?
propositions: They cried, 'Woe to us! We have surely been wrongdoers.'
This is our destruction!
We have indeed been doing wrong through our disbelief.

source_text:
Verse: They kept repeating their cry until We mowed them down, ˹leaving them˺ lifeless.

Tafsir: So that saying remained their cry which they would make and repeat until We made them as reaped crops as crops harvested with sickles when they were killed with the sword stilled dead like the stillness of fire when it is extinguished.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are repeatedly crying out for help?
How do people become like reaped crops after being killed?
What is the state of a person who is killed with the sword?
propositions: They kept repeating their cry until they were killed.
We made them as reaped crops after killing them.
A person who is killed with the sword becomes lifeless.

source_text:
Verse: We did not create the heavens and the earth and everything in between for sport.

Tafsir: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and all that is between them playing being frivolous but to indicate Our power and to benefit Our servants.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creating the universe?
Why did Allah create everything?
What does it mean to be a servant of Allah?
propositions: We created the heavens and the earth for Our power.
We created all that is between them for benefit.
Allah's creation is not for sport or frivolity.

source_text:
Verse: Had We intended to take ˹some˺ amusement, We could have found it in Our presence, if that had been Our Will.

Tafsir: Had We desired to find some diversion that which provides diversion in the way of a partner or a child We would have found it with Ourselves from among the beautiful-eyed houris or angels were We to do so. But We did not do so thus We never desired it.

hype_questions: Would Allah have created the houris if not for a purpose?
Can angels be considered as partners in worship?
Is it permissible to seek amusement through relationships with beautiful-eyed houris?
propositions: Had We intended to take amusement, We could have found it in Our presence.
We would have found diversion in the way of a partner or a child among the beautiful-eyed houris or angels if We had done so.
But We did not do so thus We never desired it.

source_text:
Verse: In fact, We hurl the truth against falsehood, leaving it crushed, and it quickly vanishes. And woe be to you for what you claim!

Tafsir: Nay but We hurl We cast the truth faith against falsehood disbelief and it obliterates it and behold it vanishes disappears damaghahu ‘it obliterates it’ actually means ‘it struck the brain with a blow’ a blow which is fatal. And for you O disbelievers of Mecca there shall be woe severe chastisement for what you ascribe to God of mate or child.

hype_questions: What happens when truth is pitted against falsehood?
How will believers be punished for their disbelief?
What will happen to those who attribute human-like qualities to God?
propositions: We hurl the truth against falsehood, leaving it crushed.
It obliterates it and behold it vanishes.
And woe be to you for what you claim!
Nay but We cast the truth faith against disbelief and it strikes the brain with a fatal blow.
For you O disbelievers of Mecca there shall be woe severe chastisement for what you ascribe to God.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belong all those in the heavens and the earth. And those nearest to Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire.

Tafsir: And to Him exalted be He belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth as possessions and those who are near Him namely the angels wa-man ‘indahu the subject the predicate of which is the following clause do not disdain to worship Him nor do they weary.

hype_questions: What is the nature of those who are closest to God?
How do angels and humans relate to God's worship?
What is the significance of humility in worship?
propositions: All beings in heaven and earth belong to God.
Those nearest to God do not disdain His worship.
God's worship does not weary those who are closest to Him.

source_text:
Verse: They glorify ˹Him˺ day and night, never wavering.

Tafsir: They glorify Him night and day and they do not falter in it for it comes to them as naturally as breathing comes to us something which we can never be distracted from.

hype_questions: What is the natural state of glorifying Allah?
How does one maintain consistency in their worship?
Can humans be distracted from their faith?
propositions: They glorify Allah night and day.
Glorification of Allah comes naturally to believers.
Believers do not falter in their worship.

source_text:
Verse: Or have they taken gods from the earth, who can raise the dead?

Tafsir: Or am functions with the meaning of bal ‘nay’ to effect a transition in subject-matter; the hamza is for rhetorical denial have they chosen gods that are from the earth such as stones gold or silver who that is gods who resurrect? who bring the dead back to life? No! Indeed only one who brings the dead back to life can be God.

hype_questions: Can stones or metals bring the dead back to life?
Is gold or silver a god that can resurrect?
Who is the only one capable of bringing the dead back to life?
propositions: They have chosen gods from the earth, such as stones, gold, or silver.
Only God can bring the dead back to life.
God is the only one who can resurrect.

source_text:
Verse: Had there been other gods besides Allah in the heavens or the earth, both ˹realms˺ would have surely been corrupted. So Glorified is Allah, Lord of the Throne, far above what they claim.

Tafsir: Had there been in either of them that is in the heavens and the earth gods other than God that is other than Him the two would have surely deteriorated they the heavens and the earth would have deviated from their observed order because counteractive forces would exist among such gods as is usually the case when there is more than one ruler that there is counteraction and a lack of consensus regarding something. So glory be to God — an exaltation — the Lord the Creator of the Throne al-kursī above what they ascribe the disbelievers to God of His having a partner and otherwise.

hype_questions: If multiple deities existed, would the universe still be governed by a single, all-powerful force?
How might the existence of rival gods impact the stability and order of creation?
Can a unified, supreme deity maintain balance and harmony in the cosmos?
propositions: Had there been other gods besides Allah in the heavens or the earth, both realms would have surely been corrupted.
The two realms (heavens and earth) would have deviated from their observed order if there were multiple gods with counteractive forces.
There is no partner or associate for God, and His sovereignty is above what disbelievers attribute to Him.

source_text:
Verse: He cannot be questioned about what He does, but they will ˹all˺ be questioned.

Tafsir: He shall not be questioned about what He does but they shall be questioned about their actions.

hype_questions: What happens to those who question God's actions?
Will people be held accountable for their deeds?
Can humans truly comprehend God's intentions?
propositions: God cannot be questioned about His actions.
Humans will be questioned about their own actions.
The focus should be on one's own behavior rather than questioning God.

source_text:
Verse: Or have they taken other gods besides Him? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Show ˹me˺ your proof. Here is ˹the Quran,˺ the Reminder for those with me; along with ˹earlier Scriptures,˺ the Reminder for those before me.” But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.

Tafsir: Or have they chosen besides Him exalted be He other than Him gods? herein is an interrogative meant as a rebuke. Say ‘Bring your proof for this — but such a thing is impossible. This is the Remembrance of those with me namely my community and that Remembrance is the Qur’ān and the Remembrance of those before me of communities namely the Torah and the Gospel and other Books of God not a single one of which contains the statement that with God there exists another god in the way that they claim — exalted be He above such a thing. Nay but most of them do not know the truth the affirmation of God’s Oneness and so they are disregardful’ of that discernment that leads to knowledge of it.

hype_questions: Can you provide proof for the existence of other gods besides Allah?
How can we reconcile the concept of multiple gods with the Quran's message of Tawhid?
What is the significance of the Remembrance of those before me, namely the Torah and the Gospel?
propositions: Allah is the only god.
The Quran is a reminder for those with me, namely my community.
None of the earlier Scriptures, such as the Torah and the Gospel, contain the statement that with God there exists another god.

source_text:
Verse: We never sent a messenger before you ˹O Prophet˺ without revealing to him: “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me, so worship Me ˹alone˺.”

Tafsir: And We did not send any Messenger before you but We revealed to him read nūhī or yūhā ‘but it was revealed to him’ that ‘There is no god except Me so worship Me’ that is affirm My Oneness.

hype_questions: What does it mean to worship only one god?
How can we affirm the Oneness of God?
What is the significance of revealing a message to a prophet?
propositions: We never sent a messenger before you without revealing to him that there is no god worthy of worship except Me.
It was revealed to the Messenger that there is no god except Me, so worship Me alone.
The affirmation of My Oneness is the core of the message revealed to the Messenger.

source_text:
Verse: And they say, “The Most Compassionate has offspring!” Glory be to Him! In fact, those ˹angels˺ are only ˹His˺ honoured servants,

Tafsir: And they say ‘The Compassionate One has taken a son’ from the angels. Glory be to Him! Nay but they are merely servants who are honoured in His presence; for the very servitude of all creatures to Him is inconsistent with the attribution of any of them as progeny of His.

hype_questions: Does the concept of divine offspring contradict the nature of God's attributes?
Can angels be considered as progeny of God?
What does it mean for creatures to serve God?
propositions: The Most Compassionate has no offspring.
Angels are honoured servants of God.
The servitude of all creatures to God is inconsistent with the attribution of any of them as progeny of His.

source_text:
Verse: who do not speak until He has spoken, ˹only˺ acting at His command.

Tafsir: They do not venture to speak before Him — they only speak after He has spoken and they act according to His command that is following His issuing of it.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah speaks?
How do people respond to Allah's commands?
Can humans take initiative without Allah's permission?
propositions: They do not speak until He has spoken.
People only act according to His command after it is issued.

source_text:
Verse: He ˹fully˺ knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them. They do not intercede except for whom He approves, and they tremble in awe of Him.

Tafsir: He knows what is before them and what is behind them that is what they have done and what they will do and they do not intercede except for him with whom He is satisfied that he be interceded for and they for awe of Him exalted be He are apprehensive fearful.

hype_questions: What is the nature of divine knowledge?
Can humans intercede with God without His permission?
How does God's power and wisdom manifest in the lives of believers?
propositions: God knows what has occurred before and will occur after.
Humans can only intercede on behalf of someone whom God has deemed worthy.
Believers tremble with awe and fear at the majesty of God.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever of them were to say, “I am a god besides Him,” they would be rewarded with Hell by Us. This is how We reward the wrongdoers.

Tafsir: And should any of them say ‘I am a god besides Him’ that is besides God in other words a god other than Him — and this is Iblīs who summoned others to worship his soul and commanded that it be obeyed — such a one We will requite with Hell. Thus in the same way that We requite him We requite wrong-doers idolaters.

hype_questions: What happens to those who claim to be gods besides the one true God?
How does the Quran respond to those who worship idols?
Who is Iblis and what role did he play in the story of polytheism?
propositions: Those who claim to be gods besides God will be rewarded with Hell.
Iblis was a being who summoned others to worship his soul and commanded that it be obeyed.
The Quran requites those who worship idols with Hell, just as it requited Iblis.

source_text:
Verse: Do the disbelievers not realize that the heavens and earth were ˹once˺ one mass then We split them apart? And We created from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?

Tafsir: Have they not one may read a-wa-lam or a-lam realised have they not come to know those who disbelieve that the heavens and the earth were closed together and then We parted them We made seven heavens and seven earths — or it is meant that the heaven was parted and began to rain when it did not use to do so and that the earth was parted and began to produce plants when it did not use to do so; and We made of water the water that falls from the heaven and that springs from the earth every living thing? in the way of plants and otherwise in other words water is the cause of such things having life. Will they not then believe? by affirming My Oneness?

hype_questions: Can the disbelievers comprehend the majesty of creation?
Will they not be convinced by the wonders of nature?
Can they deny the Oneness of God after witnessing the intricate balance of life?
propositions: The heavens and earth were once a single mass before being split apart.
All living things are created from water.
Belief in the Oneness of God is the key to understanding creation.

source_text:
Verse: And We have placed firm mountains upon the earth so it does not shake with them, and made in it broad pathways so they may find their way.

Tafsir: And We set in the earth firm mountains lest it should shake with them and We set in them in the firm mountains ravines as roads subulan substitutes for fijājan ‘ravines’ which are wide through-routes that perhaps they may be guided to their destinations during travel.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of not having stable mountains on earth?
How do the Quranic description of mountains and ravines relate to human travel?
What is the purpose of creating pathways in the earth?
propositions: We have placed firm mountains upon the earth so it does not shake with them.
We made in it broad pathways so they may find their way.

source_text:
Verse: And We have made the sky a well-protected canopy, still they turn away from its signs.

Tafsir: And We made the heaven a roof for the earth functioning like the roof of a house preserved from collapsing; and yet of the signs thereof namely the signs of this heaven such as the sun the moon and the stars they are disregardful failing to reflect on them and thus realise that the Creator of such things can have no partner.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the sky in Islam?
How does the Quran describe the relationship between heaven and earth?
What can we learn from the signs of nature?
propositions: The sky has been created as a protective canopy.
The heaven serves as a roof for the earth, similar to the roof of a house.
The signs of nature, such as the sun and stars, are reminders of God's creation.
Humans should reflect on the signs of nature to understand God's power and uniqueness.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who created the day and the night, the sun and the moon—each travelling in an orbit.

Tafsir: And He it is Who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon each kullun the nunation of this particle stands in place of the second noun of the genitive construction that would have been al-shams ‘the sun’ or al-qamar ‘the moon’ or their subsidiaries namely al-nujūm ‘the stars’ in an orbit a circular one like a mill in the sky swimming moving with speed like a swimmer in water. In order to effect the analogy with the latter the plural person of the verb employed for rational beings is used.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the celestial bodies created by Allah?
How do the sun and moon move in their orbits?
What is the significance of the stars in the universe?
propositions: Allah created the day and night.
The sun and moon travel in circular orbits.
The stars are part of the celestial bodies created by Allah.

source_text:
Verse: We have not granted immortality to any human before you ˹O Prophet˺: so if you die, will they live forever?

Tafsir: When the disbelievers said that Muhammad (s) would die the following was revealed And We did not assign to any human being before you immortality permanence of life in this world. What if you are fated to die will they be immortal? in it? No! The last sentence constitutes the syntactical locus of the interrogative of denial.

hype_questions: If a person is destined to die, will they live forever?
What if the Prophet dies, will his followers be immortal?
Will those who believe in Muhammad's message live forever?
propositions: We have not granted immortality to any human before you.
No one has been granted immortality before you.
If you die, they will not live forever.

source_text:
Verse: Every soul will taste death. And We test you ˹O humanity˺ with good and evil as a trial, then to Us you will ˹all˺ be returned.

Tafsir: Every soul shall taste death in this world and We will try you We will test you with ill and good such as poverty and wealth sickness and health as an ordeal fitnatan an object denoting reason in other words for the purpose of seeing whether you will be patient and give thanks or not. And then unto Us you shall be brought back that We may requite you.

hype_questions: What happens to a person's soul after death?
How does God test humans?
What is the purpose of trials and tribulations in life?
propositions: Every soul will taste death.
God tests humans with good and evil as a trial.
Humans are brought back to God to be requited.

source_text:
Verse: When the disbelievers see you ˹O Prophet˺, they only make fun of you, ˹saying,˺ “Is this the one who speaks ˹ill˺ of your gods?” while they disbelieve at the mention of the Most Compassionate.

Tafsir: And whenever the disbelievers see you they only take you in derision that is as one to be derided saying ‘Is this the one who mentions your gods?’ that is the one who derides them? And yet when it comes to the mention of the Compassionate One to them they hum repeated for emphasis are disbelieving of it saying ‘We do not know of any such individual’.

hype_questions: Does the Prophet's mention of other people's gods provoke derision?
How do disbelievers respond to the Prophet's mention of the Most Compassionate?
Can anyone claim to be as derisive towards others as the Prophet is?
propositions: The disbelievers make fun of the Prophet.
The Prophet mentions other people's gods, which provokes derision.
When the Prophet mentions the Most Compassionate, some disbelievers hum and repeat for emphasis, indicating their disbelief.

source_text:
Verse: Humankind is made of haste. I will soon show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten them.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding their demand that chastisement be hastened Man was created of haste that is to say because he is so hasty in his affairs it is as if he had been created out of it. Assuredly I shall show you My signs My promises of chastisement so do not demand that I hasten in sending it. And so He God made them suffer death at the battle of Badr.

hype_questions: Will God hasten the chastisement?
Why does God not show His signs faster?
What is the reason for God's delay in sending chastisement?
propositions: Humankind is made of haste.
God will show His signs and promises of chastisement.
Do not demand that God hasten in sending chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: They ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass if what you say is true?”

Tafsir: And they say ‘When will this promise of resurrection be fulfilled if you are truthful?’ about it.

hype_questions: When will the threat come to pass?
When will the promise of resurrection be fulfilled?
Will you be truthful about it?
propositions: This threat will come to pass if what you say is true.
The promise of resurrection will be fulfilled if you are truthful.

source_text:
Verse: If only the disbelievers knew that a time will come when they will not be able to keep the Fire off their faces or backs, nor will they be helped.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says If those who disbelieved only knew of the time when they shall not be able to ward off repel the Fire from their faces nor from their backs nor shall they be helped nor shall they be protected from it at the Resurrection the response to the conditional particle law ‘if only’ is something along the lines of ‘they would not have said that’.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who disbelieve at the Resurrection?

Will they be helped or protected from the Fire?
propositions: God exalted be He says that if those who disbelieved only knew of the time when they shall not be able to ward off repel the Fire from their faces nor from their backs.
They would not have said that.

source_text:
Verse: In fact, the Hour will take them by surprise, leaving them stunned. So they will not be able to avert it, nor will it be delayed from them.

Tafsir: Nay but it the Resurrection shall come upon them suddenly dumbfounding them confusing them and they shall not be able to ward it off nor shall they be granted any respite nor shall they be given any extra time to make a repentance or offer an excuse.

hype_questions: What will happen when the Hour arrives?
Can people avoid or delay their Resurrection?
Is there any chance for repentance or excuse after death?
propositions: The Hour will arrive suddenly.
People will be confused and unable to ward off their Resurrection.
There will be no respite or extra time for repentance or excuses.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Other˺ messengers had already been ridiculed before you ˹O Prophet˺, but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule.

Tafsir: And verily messengers before you were derided — herein is a statement to comfort the Prophet s — but those who mocked them were encircled by it was sent down against them that which they used to deride namely chastisement — likewise it shall befall those who have derided you.

hype_questions: What happens to those who mock the messengers of God?

propositions: Messengers before you were derided.
Those who mocked them were encircled by chastisement.
Likewise, it shall befall those who have derided you.

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet,˺ “Who can defend you by day or by night against the Most Compassionate?” Still they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.

Tafsir: Say to them ‘Who can guard you preserve you by night and day from the Compassionate One?’ from His chastisement if it should befall you? In other words no one can do such a thing. Those being addressed here do not fear God’s chastisement because they deny the truth of it. Nay but of the Remembrance of their Lord that is the Qur’ān they are disregardful failing to reflect on it.

hype_questions: Can anyone protect me from the wrath of God?
Who can save me from the punishment of the Most Compassionate One?
Is there anyone who can shield me from the chastisement of my Lord?
propositions: The Prophet asked his companions if anyone could defend him by day or night against the Most Compassionate.
Those being addressed do not fear God's chastisement because they deny its truth.
They are disregardful of the Remembrance of their Lord, which is the Qur'an.

source_text:
Verse: Or do they have gods—other than Us—that can protect them? They cannot ˹even˺ protect themselves, nor will they be aided against Us.

Tafsir: Or is it that they have am ‘or’ functions with the sense of a hamza used to indicate denial that is read it as a-lahum ‘do they have’ gods to defend them against that which might cause them harm besides Us? In other words do they have anyone other than Us to defend them against such things? No! They namely the gods cannot help themselves and so they will not be able to help them; nor shall they the disbelievers be protected from Us from Our chastisement one may say sahibaka’Llāhu to mean ‘May God preserve and protect you’.

hype_questions: Can other gods protect us from harm?

propositions: They do not have any gods that can protect them.
God is the only one who can protect us from harm.
We will not be protected by anyone else besides God.

source_text:
Verse: In fact, We have allowed enjoyment for these ˹Meccans˺ and their forefathers for such a long time ˹that they took it for granted˺. Do they not see that We gradually reduce ˹their˺ land from its borders? Is it they who will then prevail?

Tafsir: Nay but We provided comforts for these and their fathers in the way of the graces which We bestowed on them until life lasted long for them so that they were deluded by such longevity. Do they not see how We visit the land how We target their land diminishing it at its edges? by granting the Prophet victory through conquest. Are they the ones who will prevail? No it is rather the Prophet and his Companions who will do so.

hype_questions: Will the Meccans prevail?

propositions: We have allowed enjoyment for the Meccans and their forefathers for a long time.

The Prophet and his Companions will prevail.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I warn you only by revelation.” But the deaf cannot hear the call when they are warned!

Tafsir: Say to them ‘I warn you only by the Revelation’ that comes from God and not by my own prompting. But the deaf do not hear the call when idhā read pronouncing both hamzas fully or omitting the second hamza between it and the yā’ they are warned. They are like those who are deaf when they fail to act in accordance with the warnings they hear.

hype_questions: What happens when someone is warned but fails to act?

propositions: I warn you only by the Revelation that comes from God.
The deaf do not hear the call when it is pronounced with both hamzas fully or omitting the second hamza between it and the yā’.
They are like those who are deaf when they fail to act in accordance with the warnings they hear.

source_text:
Verse: If they were touched by even a breath of your Lord’s torment, they would certainly cry, “Woe to us! We have really been wrongdoers.”

Tafsir: And if a whiff a slight instance of your Lord’s chastisement were to touch them they would indeed say ‘O yā used for drawing attention to something woe for us! O this is our destruction! Truly we were doing evil’ in ascribing partners to God and denying the Mission of Muhammad (s).

hype_questions: What would happen if someone were touched by a breath of Allah's torment?
