propositions: If someone were touched by a breath of Allah's torment, they would cry out in distress.
A slight instance of Allah's chastisement would cause people to say 'woe is us!' if it were to touch them.
Ascribing partners to God and denying the Mission of Muhammad (s) is our destruction.

source_text:
Verse: We will set up the scales of justice on the Day of Judgment, so no soul will be wronged in the least. And ˹even˺ if a deed is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as a ˹vigilant˺ Reckoner.

Tafsir: And We shall set up the just balances the equitable ones for the Day of Resurrection that is on it and no soul shall be wronged in any way neither by deducting a good deed from its record nor by adding to it an evil one; and even if it the action be the weight of a single mustard seed We shall produce it with its full weight and We suffice as reckoners to count all things.

hype_questions: Will every soul be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Resurrection?

propositions: Allah will set up scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection.
No soul will be wronged in any way, neither by deducting a good deed from its record nor by adding to it an evil one.
Even if a deed is the weight of a single mustard seed, Allah will produce it with its full weight.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We granted Moses and Aaron the standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺—a light and a reminder for the righteous,

source_text:

source_text:

Abraham was given his rectitude before he came of age.
Abraham was deserving of such guidance.

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: On that Day We will roll up the heavens like a scroll of writings. Just as We produced the first creation, ˹so˺ shall We reproduce it. That is a promise binding on Us. We truly uphold ˹Our promises˺!

Tafsir: The day yawma is in the accusative because of an implied preceding udhkur ‘mention’ when We shall roll up the heaven as the Scribe al-sijill being the name of an angel rolls up the written scroll that is the scroll of the son of Adam when he dies the lām of li’l-kitāb is extra; alternatively one may read the verse so that al-sijill is ‘the scroll’ and al-kitāb means al-maktūb ‘what is written’ in which case the lām of li’l-kitāb has the sense of the particle ‘alā ‘over’; a variant reading for li’l-kitāb has the plural li’l-kutub ‘the books’. As We began the first creation from non-existence We shall repeat it after making it non-existent the kāf of ka-mā ‘as’ is semantically connected to nu‘īdu ‘We shall repeat it’ and its suffixed pronoun -hu ‘it’ refers back to awwala ‘the first’; the mā relates to the verbal noun — a promise binding on Us wa‘dan is in the accusative because it is the direct object of an implied preceding wa‘adnā ‘We promised’ and the clause constitutes a confirmation of the import of the preceding verse 103. Truly We shall do that which We have promised.

hype_questions: What will be the state of the heavens on the Day of Resurrection?
Will God recreate the first creation after destroying it?
Does God keep His promises?
propositions: We will roll up the heavens like a scroll of writings.
We produced the first creation, and We shall reproduce it.
We truly uphold Our promises.

source_text:
Verse: Surely, following the ˹heavenly˺ Record, We decreed in the Scriptures: “My righteous servants shall inherit the land.”

Tafsir: Certainly We wrote in the Scripture al-zabūr means ‘the Book’ that is the revealed Books of God after the Remembrance meaning the Mother of the Book umm al-kitāb which is kept with God ‘Indeed the land the land of Paradise shall be inherited by My righteous servants’ — this promise applies to all righteous ones.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the revealed Books of God?
Who will inherit the land of Paradise?
What does it mean to be a righteous servant?
propositions: We decreed in the Scriptures that My righteous servants shall inherit the land.
The land of Paradise shall be inherited by My righteous servants.
This promise applies to all righteous ones.

source_text:
Verse: Surely this ˹Quran˺ is sufficient ˹as a reminder˺ for those devoted to worship.

Tafsir: Indeed there is in this Qur’ān a proclamation sufficient means for securing entry into Paradise for a people who are devout acting in accordance with what is stipulated in it.

hype_questions: What is the primary purpose of the Quran?
How can one secure entry into Paradise through devotion and obedience to the Quran?
What does it mean to be 'devoted' in the context of worship?
propositions: The Quran serves as a sufficient reminder for those devoted to worship.
There is a proclamation in the Quran that provides means for securing entry into Paradise for a people who are devout and act according to its stipulations.
Devotion and obedience to the Quran's stipulations are essential for entering Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ only as a mercy for the whole world.

Tafsir: We did not send you O Muhammad (s) except as a mercy that is to give mercy to all the worlds the worlds of mankind and jinn through you.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of prophethood?
How does mercy relate to prophetic mission?
Can prophetic mercy extend beyond human and jinn realms?
propositions: We sent O Prophet as a mercy for mankind.
O Muhammad (s) was sent as a mercy to all worlds, including the world of mankind and jinn.
The purpose of prophethood is to give mercy to all beings.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “What has been revealed to me is this: ‘Your God is only One God.’ Will you then submit?”

Tafsir: Say ‘All that is being revealed to me is that your God is One God that is the only thing that is being revealed to me with respect to the Divine is His Oneness. So will you submit?’ will you accede to affirming the Oneness of the Divine that is being revealed to me? the interrogative is meant as an imperative.

hype_questions: What does it mean for God to be One and Unique?
How can I submit to the Oneness of God?
What are the implications of affirming the Oneness of God?
propositions: God is the only one God.
The Oneness of God is being revealed.
Submission to the Oneness of God is required.

source_text:
Verse: If they turn away, then say, “I have warned you all equally. I do not know if what you are threatened with is near or far.

Tafsir: But if they turn away from this say ‘I have proclaimed to you I have notified you of my declaration of war on you all alike ‘alā sawā’ is a circumstantial qualifier referring to both the subject of the verb and the object that is to say you are all equal in having knowledge of this I shall not proceed independently without having first informed you in order for you to make preparations although I do not know whether near or far is that which you have been promised’ with respect to chastisement or to the Day of Resurrection that comprises this chastisement; only God knows it.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's declaration of war on humanity?
How do humans prepare for the consequences of their actions?
What is the significance of the Day of Resurrection in Islamic theology?
propositions: If they turn away, then say, 'I have warned you all equally.'
I shall not proceed independently without having first informed you of my declaration of war on you all alike.
Only God knows whether what you are threatened with is near or far.

source_text:
Verse: Allah surely knows what you say openly and whatever you hide.

Tafsir: Indeed He exalted be He knows whatever is spoken aloud and what you and others do and He knows what you conceal both you and others of secrets.

hype_questions: Does Allah know our innermost thoughts?
Can Allah see into the hearts of humans?
Is Allah aware of all that we do in secret?
propositions: Allah knows what is spoken aloud.
Allah knows what humans do in secret.
Allah is aware of all secrets, whether hidden or revealed.

source_text:
Verse: I do not know if this ˹delay˺ is possibly a test for you and an enjoyment for a while.”

Tafsir: I do not know; perhaps that which I have notified you of but whose time is not known may be a trial a test for you to see how you will act and an enjoyment for a while that is until your terms of life are concluded this second clause wa-matā‘un ‘and an enjoyment’ counters the former which is the object of the optative expressed by the particle la‘alla ‘perhaps’; the second clause cannot be an optative.

hype_questions: Will this delay be a test for me to see how I will act?
Is this delay an enjoyment that will last until my terms of life are concluded?
How will I respond to this trial?
propositions: This delay may be a test for you.
The time for this notification is not known.
You will see how you will act in response to this trial.
This delay is an enjoyment that will last until your terms of life are concluded.

source_text:
Verse: ˹In the end,˺ the Prophet said, “My Lord! Judge ˹between us˺ in truth. And our Lord is the Most Compassionate, Whose help is sought against what you claim.”

Tafsir: Say qul a variant reading has qāla ‘He said’ ‘My Lord! Judge between me and my deniers with truth by assigning chastisement for them or victory for me over them. And so they were chastised at the battles of Badr Uhud Hunayn al-Ahzāb and al-Khandaq and he the Prophet was given victory over them. And our Lord is the Compassionate One Whose help is to be sought against what you allege’ when you invent lies against God saying that ‘God has taken a son’ cf. Q. 2116; and against me when you say ‘he is a sorcerer’ cf. Q. 384 or against the Qur’ān when you say ‘it is poetry’ cf. Q. 5230.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Prophet's prayer for justice in the face of denial?
How did the Prophet and his companions respond to their enemies at the battles of Badr, Udh, Hunayn, Azab, Al-Khandaq?
What is the nature of God according to Islamic teachings?
propositions: The Prophet prayed for truth in judgment between himself and his deniers.
God's help is sought against false claims about Him.
The Prophet was given victory over his enemies at various battles.
Our Lord is the Compassionate One.
God is not a sorcerer or poet.

source_text:
Verse: O humanity! Fear your Lord, for the ˹violent˺ quaking at the Hour is surely a dreadful thing.

Tafsir: O mankind that is the inhabitants of Mecca and others fear your Lord that is of His punishment by being obedient to Him. Surely the earthquake of the Hour of Doom that is the violent quaking of the earth after which the sun will rise from the west something which will be near the time of the Hour is a tremendous thing in the way it will distress people — this itself being a sort of punishment.

hype_questions: What will be the punishment for not obeying God?
How will the world change after the Hour of Doom?
Will the sun still rise if the earth is shaking violently?
propositions: Fear your Lord.
The earthquake of the Hour of Doom is a punishment.
The sun will rise from the west after the violent quaking of the earth.

source_text:
Verse: The Day you see it, every nursing mother will abandon what she is nursing, and every pregnant woman will deliver her burden ˹prematurely˺. And you will see people ˹as if they were˺ drunk, though they will not be drunk; but the torment of Allah is ˹terribly˺ severe.

Tafsir: On the day when you behold it every actually nursing female on account of this tremendous day will neglect her suckling that is she will forget it; and every pregnant female will deliver her burden and you will see mankind as though drunk because of the severity of their fear yet they will not be drunk because of any drink; but God’s chastisement is severe and so they will be terrified of it.

hype_questions: What will cause nursing mothers to abandon their children?
How will people react on the day of judgment?
What is the nature of Allah's chastisement?
propositions: Every nursing mother will abandon what she is nursing on the Day of Judgment.
Every pregnant woman will deliver her burden prematurely on the Day of Judgment.
People will see themselves as drunk, though they will not be drunk, due to their fear and terror.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Still˺ there are some who dispute about Allah without knowledge, and follow every rebellious devil.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding al-Nadr b. al-Hārith and his companions And among mankind are those who dispute about God without any knowledge — they would say ‘The angels are God’s daughters and the Qur’ān a collection of the fables of the ancients’. In addition they would deny resurrection and the bringing back to life of those who had become dust — and those who follow in their manner of disputing every rebellious devil

hype_questions: Does the Qur'ān contain fables of ancient civilizations?
Are angels considered daughters of God in certain interpretations?
Can those who have become dust be brought back to life?
propositions: Some people dispute about Allah without knowledge.
They follow every rebellious devil.
Al-Nadr b. al-Hārith and his companions are mentioned in the Qur'ān.
Some people deny resurrection and the bringing back to life of those who have become dust.
The Qur'ān is not a collection of fables of ancient civilizations.

source_text:
Verse: It has been decreed for such devils that whoever takes them as a guide will be misguided and led by them into the torment of the Blaze.

Tafsir: about whom it has been decreed in other words it has been decreed with regards to a devil that whoever takes him for a friend that is whoever follows him he will make him go astray and will lead him summon him to the chastisement of the Blaze namely to the Fire.

hype_questions: What happens if one takes a devil as a guide?
Will following a devil lead to torment?
What is the chastisement of the Blaze?
propositions: It has been decreed for such devils that whoever takes them as a guide will be misguided and led by them into the torment of the Blaze.
Whoever takes a devil as a friend will make him go astray and will lead him to the chastisement of the Blaze.
The chastisement of the Blaze is the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: O humanity! If you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then ˹know that˺ We did create you—in order to demonstrate ˹Our power˺ to you. ˹Then˺ We settle whatever ˹embryo˺ We will in the womb for an appointed term, then bring you forth as infants, so that you may reach your prime. Some of you ˹may˺ die ˹young˺, while others are left to reach the most feeble stage of life so that they may know nothing after having known much. And you see the earth lifeless, but as soon as We send down rain upon it, it begins to stir ˹to life˺ and swell, producing every type of pleasant plant.

Tafsir: O mankind in other words O people of Mecca if you are in doubt about the Resurrection then lo! consider that We have created you that is We have created your origin — Adam — from dust then We created his progeny from a drop a sperm-drop then from a clot congealed blood then from a little lump of flesh mudgha a piece of flesh the size of what one would be able to chew mā yumdagh partly formed shaped complete in form and partly unformed that is uncomplete in form that We may make clear to you the perfect nature of Our power that you might then infer from this initial act of creation the reality of its future restoration. And We establish nuqirru marks a new grammatically independent sentence in the wombs whatever We will for a specified time that is until the time for it to come out then We bring you forth from the bellies of your mothers as infants and then We extend your life that you may come of age ashuddakum that is to say your prime and strength which is that age between thirty and forty years. And there are some of you who are taken away by death before coming of age and there are some of you who are relegated to the most abject time of life its most despicable state of decrepitude and senility so that after having had some knowledge he no longer knows anything — ‘Ikrima said ‘Whoever recites the Qur’ān such a state will not befall him’. And you see the earth torpid barren yet when We send down water upon it it stirs it moves and swells it rises and grows and grows plants of anbatat min min is extra every delightful fair kind species.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creation?
How does Allah restore life after death?
What happens to those who have knowledge but later forget?
propositions: We created you to demonstrate Our power.
We settle whatever embryo We will in the womb for an appointed term.
Some of you may die young, while others are left to reach the most feeble stage of life.
The earth is lifeless until We send down rain upon it.
We bring you forth from the bellies of your mothers as infants and then extend your life.

source_text:
Verse: That is because Allah ˹alone˺ is the Truth, He ˹alone˺ gives life to the dead, and He ˹alone˺ is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: That which is mentioned from the commencement of man’s creation to the end of the description of the earth being revived is because God He is the Truth the Constant the Permanent and because He revives the dead and has power over all things;

hype_questions: What is the nature of God?
How does God relate to human existence?
What is the significance of resurrection in Islamic theology?
propositions: Allah is the Truth.
Allah gives life to the dead.
Allah is Most Capable of everything.

source_text:
Verse: And certainly the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it. And Allah will surely resurrect those in the graves.

Tafsir: and because the Hour will come whereof there is no doubt uncertainty; and because God will resurrect those who are in the graves.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Hour?
Will everyone be resurrected after death?
How will Allah resurrect those in graves?
propositions: The Hour is coming.
There is no doubt about the coming of the Hour.
Allah will surely resurrect those who are in the graves.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Still˺ there are some who dispute about Allah without knowledge, guidance, or an enlightening scripture,

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding Abū Jahl And among mankind there are some who dispute about God without any knowledge or guidance being with him or an enlightening Scripture one containing light being with him

hype_questions: What is the nature of God that some people dispute without any knowledge or guidance?
How can someone claim to understand God without any enlightening scripture?
What is the significance of an enlightening Scripture in understanding God?
propositions: Some people dispute about Allah without knowledge.
There is no guidance with Allah.
No enlightening Scripture contains light.

source_text:
Verse: turning away ˹in pride˺ to lead ˹others˺ astray from Allah’s Way. They will suffer disgrace in this world, and on the Day of Judgment We will make them taste the torment of burning.

Tafsir: turning aside thāniya ‘itfihi a circumstantial qualifier meaning ‘turning his neck aside in disdain of belief; al-ītf means ‘a side’ and can be either the left or the right to go astray read li-yadilla; or li-yudilla ‘to lead others astray’ from the way of God that is from His religion. For him there will be ignominy chastisement in this world — thus he Abū Jahl was slain on the day of Badr — and on the Day of Resurrection We shall make him taste the chastisement of the burning that is the chastisement of being burnt in the Fire and it shall be said to him

hype_questions: What happens to those who turn away from Allah's way in pride?
How will the Day of Judgment affect those who lead others astray?
What is the chastisement that awaits those who are burnt in the Fire?
propositions: Turning away in pride leads others astray from Allah's Way.
There will be ignominy and chastisement in this world for those who turn away in pride.
On the Day of Resurrection, We shall make them taste the torment of burning.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They will be told,˺ “This is ˹the reward˺ for what your hands have done. And Allah is never unjust to ˹His˺ creation.”

Tafsir: ‘That is the chastisement for what your hands have sent ahead in other words what you have offered in the way of deeds — He refers to him with reference to the two hands as opposed to other parts because most actions are effected through them — and because God is not unjust to His servants’ chastising them without their having committed any sin.

hype_questions: What is the reward for our actions?
Is God unjust to His creation?
How do our deeds affect our fate?
propositions: This is the reward for what your hands have done.
God is never unjust to His creation.
Most actions are effected through the two hands.

source_text:
Verse: And there are some who worship Allah on the verge ˹of faith˺: if they are blessed with something good, they are content with it; but if they are afflicted with a trial, they relapse ˹into disbelief˺, losing this world and the Hereafter. That is ˹truly˺ the clearest loss.

Tafsir: And among mankind there are those who worship God on a knife-edge that is with uncertainty in his worship — such a person has been likened the knife- edge of a mountain in his precariousness — if good fortune befalls him so that he enjoys health and security with respect to his own self and his property he is reassured by it; but if an ordeal befalls him a trial or ill-health with regard to himself or his property he makes a turnabout that is he reverts to disbelief losing both this world when what he had hoped for in it has eluded him and the Hereafter by his disbelief. That is the manifest loss.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who is on the verge of faith but reverts to disbelief?
How does good fortune affect a person's faith?
What is the consequence of losing both this world and the Hereafter due to disbelief?
propositions: Some people worship Allah with uncertainty in their faith.
Good fortune can reassure someone who is on the verge of faith.
A trial or ill-health can cause a person to revert to disbelief, resulting in loss of both this world and the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: They call besides Allah what can neither harm nor benefit them. That is ˹truly˺ the farthest one can stray.

Tafsir: He calls on he worships besides God in the way of idols that which could not hurt him should he refrain from worshipping it and that which could not profit him if were to worship it. Such a call is extreme error from the truth.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of calling upon idols besides Allah?
How does worshiping false deities affect one's well-being?
What is considered extreme error in the context of worship?
propositions: They call upon idols besides Allah.
Such idolatry cannot harm or benefit them.
Worshiping false deities is a grave mistake.

source_text:
Verse: They invoke those whose worship leads to harm, not benefit. What an evil patron and what an evil associate!

Tafsir: He calls on him the lām of la-man is extra whose harm when worshipped is likelier than his benefit even if he were to have any benefit as he imagines him to have. Truly an evil patron is he that is an evil helper and an evil friend an evil companion is he. After the mention of ‘the doubter’ and his being in manifest ‘loss’ above verse 11 there follows the mention of the believers and their reward as follows

hype_questions: What are some examples of patrons who lead to harm when worshipped?
How can one distinguish between a patron who brings benefit and one who leads to harm?
What is the nature of an evil companion in Islamic theology?
propositions: Those who invoke those whose worship leads to harm, not benefit.
The lām of la-man is called upon by some, but its harm outweighs any potential benefit.
A patron who is an evil helper and friend is considered evil in Islamic theology.
Believers will receive a reward for their faith after being warned about the dangers of shirk.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do good into Gardens, under which rivers flow. Surely Allah does what He wills.

Tafsir: Truly God shall admit those who believe and perform righteous deeds in the way of obligatory and supererogatory acts of worship into gardens underneath which rivers flow. Indeed God does whatever He desires in the way of showing beneficence to those who obey Him and degrading those who disobey Him.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe and do good?
How does Allah show beneficence to those who obey Him?
What happens to those who disobey Allah?
propositions: Allah will admit those who believe and do good into Gardens.
God shows beneficence to those who obey Him.
Those who disobey God are degraded.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help His Prophet in this world and the Hereafter, let them stretch out a rope to the ceiling and strangle themselves, then let them see if this plan will do away with ˹the cause of˺ their rage.

Tafsir: Whoever supposes that God will not help him namely Muhammad (s) His Prophet in this world and the Hereafter let him extend a rope to the ceiling to the roof of his house fixing it there and tying it to his neck and let him hang himself that is let him choke to death because of it by severing his soul from any existence on the earth as reported in the various Sahīh compilations. Then let him see whether his strategy against the Prophet being helped dispels that which enrages him about it. In other words let him choke to death with rage because of it for it is inevitable.

hype_questions: Will Allah help His Prophet in this world and the Hereafter?
What happens if one thinks that Allah will not help His Prophet?
How does one's rage change when they consider the help of Allah for His Prophet?
propositions: Allah will help His Prophet in this world and the Hereafter.
If someone thinks that Allah will not help His Prophet, they should hang themselves to death.
The help of Allah for His Prophet is inevitable and will dispel one's rage.

source_text:
Verse: And so We revealed this ˹Quran˺ as clear verses. And Allah certainly guides whoever He wills.

Tafsir: So just as We revealed the previous verse We revealed it that is the remainder of the Qur’ān as clear signs manifest signs bayyināt ‘clear signs’ is a circumstantial qualifier and indeed God guides whomever He desires that he be guided wa-anna’Llāha yahdī man yurīdu a supplement to the suffixed pronoun hā’ ‘it’ of anzalnāhu ‘We revealed it’.

hype_questions: Does Allah guide whoever He wills?
What is the nature of 'clear signs' in the Quran?
Can humans be guided by God's will?
propositions: We revealed the Quran as clear verses.
Allah guides whoever He desires.
The previous verse was a remainder of the Qur'an, manifesting clear signs.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, the believers, Jews, Sabians, and the polytheists—Allah will judge between them ˹all˺ on Judgment Day. Surely Allah is a Witness over all things.

Tafsir: Truly those who believe and those of Jewry namely the Jews and the Sabaeans a sect from among them and the Christians and the Magians and the polytheists — God will indeed judge between them on the Day of Resurrection by admitting the believers into Paradise and all others into the Fire. Assuredly God over all things the things which they do is Witness Knowing them a knowledge of direct vision ‘ilm mushāhada.

hype_questions: What will be the outcome for those who believe and those of other faiths on Judgment Day?
How will Allah judge between believers and polytheists?
Will God admit believers into Paradise and others into the Fire?
propositions: Allah will judge between believers and non-believers on Judgment Day.
God will admit believers into Paradise and all others into the Fire.
God is a Witness over all things.

source_text:
Verse: Do you not see that to Allah bow down ˹in submission˺ all those in the heavens and all those on the earth, as well as the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and ˹all˺ living beings, as well as many humans, while many are deserving of punishment. And whoever Allah disgraces, none can honour. Surely Allah does what He wills.

Tafsir: Have you not seen have you not realised that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth together with the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the animals that is how they are submissive to Him in what He wills of them as well as many of mankind? namely the believers who prostrate to Him in addition to their submissiveness to Him when prostrating in prayer. And for many the chastisement has become due and these are the disbelievers for they refuse to prostrate an action which is contingent on belief. And he whom God abases he whom He makes unprosperous there is none to give him honour none to make him fortunate. Indeed God does whatever He will in the way of abasing or giving honour.

hype_questions: What is the nature of submission to Allah?
Can anyone who is disgraced by Allah be honored?
How does Allah's will manifest in the lives of believers and disbelievers?
propositions: Allah is bowed down by all those in the heavens and on the earth, as well as the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and living beings.
Many humans are deserving of punishment, while others are not.
God does what He wills, and there is none to give honour or make fortunate to him whom God abases.

source_text:
Verse: These are two opposing groups that disagree about their Lord: as for the disbelievers, garments of Fire will be cut out for them and boiling water will be poured over their heads,

Tafsir: These twain are two contenders that is the believers constitute one contending party and the five categories of disbelievers constitute the other contending party the term khasm ‘contender’ may be used to refer to one or many who contend concerning their Lord that is to say concerning His religion. As for those who disbelieve garments of fire will be cut out for them garments which they will wear — meaning that the Fire will encompass them — and boiling water will be poured over their heads hamīm is water that has reached an extreme temperature

hype_questions: What will happen to those who disbelieve in their Lord?
How will the Fire affect those who reject their faith?
What is the nature of the boiling water that will be poured over the heads of disbelievers?
propositions: The believers constitute one contending party.
The five categories of disbelievers constitute the other contending party.
Garments of Fire will be cut out for those who disbelieve, which they will wear — meaning that the Fire will encompass them — and boiling water will be poured over their heads.

source_text:
Verse: melting whatever is in their bellies, along with their skin.

Tafsir: whereby will be melted that which is in their bellies of fats and otherwise and whereby will be grilled their skins.

hype_questions: What will happen to the bodies of those who disbelieve on the Day of Judgment?
How will their sins be punished on the Day of Resurrection?
Will the believers be rewarded or punished on the Day of Judgment?
propositions: The bodies of those who disbelieve will melt.
Their skins will be grilled.

source_text:
Verse: And awaiting them are maces of iron.

Tafsir: And there will be hooked rods of iron for them for their heads to be beaten with.

hype_questions: What will be the instruments used by Allah on the Day of Judgment?
How will Allah punish those who disbelieve?
What will happen to those who reject Allah's message?
propositions: There will be maces of iron awaiting them.
The heads of those who disbelieve will be beaten with hooked rods of iron.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever they try to escape from Hell—out of anguish—they will be forced back into it, ˹and will be told,˺ “Taste the torment of burning!”

Tafsir: Whenever they desire to exit from it that is from the Fire on account of their anguish they are made to return into it they are driven back into it with the hooked rods and it shall be said to them ‘Taste the chastisement of the burning!’ namely the one that has reached ultimate degree of combustion.

hype_questions: What happens to those who try to escape from Hell?
How are people treated when they return to Hell after trying to escape?
What is the ultimate degree of torment in Hell?
propositions: Those who try to escape from Hell will be forced back into it.
The torment of burning is a punishment that will be inflicted upon them.
The Fire is a place where people are driven back with hooked rods.

source_text:
Verse: ˹But˺ Allah will surely admit those who believe and do good into Gardens, under which rivers flow, where they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing will be silk,

Tafsir: And He God says of the believers Indeed God shall admit those who believe and perform righteous deeds into gardens underneath which rivers flow; adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearl read wa-lu’lu’in genitive to mean bracelets made of both elements so that the pearls are set in gold; or read wa-lu’lu’an accusative as a supplement to the syntactical locus of min asāwira ‘bracelets’; and their raiment therein will be silk namely the one forbidden for men to wear in this world.

hype_questions: What is the reward for believers in the afterlife?
How are believers dressed in paradise?
What kind of clothing is forbidden for men to wear in this world?
propositions: Allah will admit those who believe and do good into Gardens.
Gardens have rivers underneath them.
Pearls are set in gold bracelets.
Believers' raiment in paradise will be silk.
Silk is forbidden for men to wear in this world.

source_text:
Verse: for they have been guided to the best of speech, and they have been guided to the Commendable Path.

Tafsir: And they shall be guided in this world to wholesome words namely ‘There is no god except God’ and they shall be guided to the path of the Praised that is to the praiseworthy way of God and His religion.

hype_questions: What is the best way to live a virtuous life?
How can one find guidance in their daily life?
What is the praiseworthy way of God?
propositions: They have been guided to wholesome words.
They shall be guided to the path of the Praised.
There is no god except God.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who persist in disbelief and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque We will cause them to taste a painful punishment.

Tafsir: Truly those who disbelieve and who bar from the way of God from obedience to Him and from the Sacred Mosque which We have assigned as a holy rite and a place of devotion for mankind equally for the dweller the one who resides therein and the visitor the passer-by; and whoever seeks to commit sacrilege therein the bā’ of bi-ilhādin ‘sacrilege’ is extra by doing wrong in other words for such a reason committing what is forbidden even if he should curse the Mosque’s attendant We shall make him taste a painful chastisement that is some such chastisement from this last clause one may derive the predicate of the introductory particle inna ‘truly’ and it is this ‘We shall make them taste a painful chastisement’.

hype_questions: What happens to those who disbelieve and hinder others from the Way of Allah?
Can committing sacrilege in the Sacred Mosque lead to a painful punishment?
How will God punish those who disobey Him and desecrate the Sacred Mosque?
propositions: Those who persist in disbelief and hinder others from the Way of Allah will taste a painful punishment.
The Sacred Mosque is a holy rite and a place of devotion for mankind, equally for the dweller, the visitor, and the passer-by.
Whoever seeks to commit sacrilege in the Sacred Mosque shall be punished with a painful chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ when We assigned to Abraham the site of the House, ˹saying,˺ “Do not associate anything with Me ˹in worship˺ and purify My House for those who circle ˹the Ka’bah˺, stand ˹in prayer˺, and bow and prostrate themselves.

Tafsir: And mention when We settled when We pointed out for Abraham the site of the House that he may build it — for it the House had been raised to heaven at the time of the Flood — and We commanded him saying ‘Do not ascribe any partner to Me and purify My House of graven images for those who circumambulate it and those who are resident staying therein and those who bow and prostrate al-rukka‘ and al-sujūd are the plural forms of rāki‘ and sājid respectively those praying.

hype_questions: What is the significance of purifying the House for those who circle it?
How did Abraham's role in building the House begin?
Why was the House raised to heaven during the time of the Flood?
propositions: We assigned the site of the House to Abraham.
Abraham was commanded not to associate anything with God in worship.
The House must be purified for those who circle it, stand in prayer, and bow and prostrate themselves.

source_text:
Verse: Call ˹all˺ people to the pilgrimage. They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel from every distant path,

Tafsir: And announce call out among the people the season for Pilgrimage. Thus he cried out from the top of the mountain of Abū Qubays ‘O people your Lord has built a House and has made pilgrimage to it an obligation upon you so respond to the call of your Lord’ turning his face to the right and to the left to the east and to the west; and every one of those for whom the performance of the pilgrimage had been preordained by God from among the loins of men and the wombs of women responded to him thus ‘At Your service our Lord we are at Your service’ labbayka’Llāhumma labbayk. The response to the command clause is the following and they shall come to you on foot walking rijāl plural of rājil similar in pattern to qā’im ‘standing’ and its plural qiyām and riding on every lean camel that is on every emaciated camel dāmir this term may be used to refer to both male and female camels. They shall come that is the lean camels by grammatical agreement with the feminine verb form from every deep ravine from every distant route

hype_questions: What is the obligation of pilgrimage in Islam?
How do people respond to the call of their Lord during the Pilgrimage?
Who are the ones for whom the performance of the pilgrimage had been preordained by God?
propositions: Call all people to the pilgrimage.
God has built a House and made pilgrimage an obligation upon you.
The response to the command clause is that they shall come on foot and on every lean camel from every distant path.
Every one of those for whom the performance of the pilgrimage had been preordained by God responded to him thus 'At Your service our Lord we are at Your service'.
They shall come on foot walking, riding on every lean camel that is on every emaciated camel.

source_text:
Verse: so they may obtain the benefits ˹in store˺ for them, and pronounce the Name of Allah on appointed days over the sacrificial animals He has provided for them. So eat from their meat and feed the desperately poor.

Tafsir: that they may witness that they may be present before things that are of benefit to them in this world such as commerce or of benefit in the Hereafter or in both — all of which are valid alternative opinions — and mention God’s Name on appointed days namely the ten days of Dhū’l-Hijja or the Day of ‘Arafa or from the Day of Immolation up to the last days of tashrīq — all of which are valid alternative opinions — over the livestock which He has provided them such as the camels cows and sheep immolated on the Day of the ‘Īd and any subsequent offerings or sacrifices. “So eat thereof if it be recommended and feed the wretched poor” that is the one in dire poverty.

hype_questions: What are the benefits of sacrificing livestock during the ten days of Dhū’l-Hijja?
How can one ensure a good return on investment through commerce and trade?
What is the significance of feeding the desperately poor during the month of Ramadan?
propositions: They should sacrifice livestock provided by Allah on appointed days.
The benefits of sacrificing livestock include commerce, the Hereafter, or both in this world.
One should eat from the meat and feed the wretched poor if it is recommended.

source_text:
Verse: Then let them groom themselves, fulfil their vows, and circle the Ancient House.”

Tafsir: Then let them do away with their self-neglect that is to say let them remove any dirt or unkemptness such as any long fingernails and let them fulfil read wa’l-yūfū or wa’l-yuwaffū their vows in the way of offerings and sacrifices and perform the circumambulation the circumambulation following the egress from ‘Arafa of the Ancient House’ that is the Old one because it was the first House founded for mankind.

hype_questions: What is the significance of fulfilling vows in Islam?
How does circumambulation relate to the Ancient House?
What are some ways to improve one's self-care and spiritual growth?
propositions: Let them remove dirt or unkemptness from their bodies.
They should fulfil their vows in the way of offerings and sacrifices.
Perform the circumambulation following the egress from 'Arafa of the Ancient House'.

source_text:
Verse: That is so. And whoever honours the rituals of Allah, it is best for them in the sight of their Lord. The ˹meat of˺ cattle has been made lawful for you, except what has ˹already˺ been recited to you. So shun the impurity of idolatry, and shun words of falsehood.

Tafsir: That is that dhālika the predicate of an implied subject in other words ‘the matter’ or ‘the affair’ is ‘that which has been mentioned’. And whoever venerates the sacraments of God namely those things whose violation is forbidden that veneration of them shall be better for him with his Lord in the Hereafter. And cattle are lawful for you to consume after their slaughter except for that which has been recited to you as being unlawful in the verse Forbidden to you is carrion … Q. 53. The exceptive clause above is a discontinuous one; but it could also be taken as continuous so that the prohibition is of that which has died and so on. So avoid the abomination of idols mina’l-awthān min here is explicative as opposed to partitive in other words ‘avoid abomination namely idols’ and avoid false speech that is to say ascribing partners to God in your uttering of the talbiya or avoid bearing false witness;

hype_questions: What are the rituals of Allah that are considered sacred?
Can cattle be consumed after slaughter, and if so, what is forbidden?
How can one avoid idolatry and false speech in their daily life?
propositions: The rituals of Allah are sacred.
Cattle are lawful for consumption after slaughter, except for those mentioned in the verse.
Idolatry and false speech are abominations that must be avoided.

source_text:
Verse: Be upright ˹in devotion˺ to Allah, associating none with Him ˹in worship˺. For whoever associates ˹others˺ with Allah is like someone who has fallen from the sky and is either snatched away by birds or swept by the wind to a remote place.

Tafsir: being hanīfs to God being of those who have submitted to God inclining away from every religion except His religion not ascribing partners to Him this clause emphasises the preceding one both clauses being circumstantial qualifiers referring to the third person plural indicator wāw of ijtanibū ‘avoid’. For whoever ascribes partners to God it is as though he had fallen from the heaven and been snatched away by vulture birds that is as though they had seized him swiftly or as though the wind had blown him dropped him into a far-off place so that there is no hope of his being saved.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who ascribes partners to Allah?
How does associating partners with Allah affect a person's fate?
Can someone escape the consequences of associating partners with Allah?
propositions: Be upright in devotion to Allah, associating none with Him.
For whoever associates others with Allah is like someone who has fallen from the sky and is either snatched away by birds or swept by the wind to a remote place.
Associating partners with Allah means being lost forever.

source_text:
Verse: That is so. And whoever honours the symbols of Allah, it is certainly out of the piety of the heart.

Tafsir: That dhālika an implied subject al-amru ‘the matter is’ is taken to precede this predicate. And whoever venerates the sacraments of God then that in other words then that veneration of them — namely of the beasts of sacrifice offered in the Sanctuary after the best of them have been selected and fattened — derives from the piety of the hearts of those individuals. These sacraments are called sha‘ā’ir because they are marked out ish‘ār with something to indicate that they are offerings such as having a hump pierced with a piece of metal.

hype_questions: What are the sacraments of God?
How does veneration of these sacraments relate to piety?
What is the significance of having a hump pierced with metal in animal sacrifices?
propositions: The matter is honoured by those who venerates the sacraments of God.
Veneration of the beasts of sacrifice derives from the piety of the hearts of those individuals.
These sacraments are called sha‘ā’ir because they are marked out with something to indicate that they are offerings.

source_text:
Verse: You may benefit from sacrificial animals for an appointed term, then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.

Tafsir: You may benefit from them such as riding on them and carrying your loads on them in a way that does not harm them until a specified time the time for its immolation. Thereafter its lawful sacrifice that is the site where its immolation becomes due is by the Ancient House meaning the entire Meccan Sanctuary.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of sacrificing animals for a specified term?
At what point does the sacrifice become due?
Where is the site of immolation located?
propositions: You may benefit from sacrificial animals for an appointed term.
The time for its immolation becomes due at the Ancient House, meaning the entire Meccan Sanctuary.

source_text:
Verse: For every community We appointed a rite of sacrifice so that they may pronounce the Name of Allah over the sacrificial animals He has provided for them. For your God is only One God, so submit yourselves to Him ˹alone˺. And give good news ˹O Prophet˺ to the humble:

Tafsir: And for every community that is for every believing group that came before you We have appointed a holy rite read mansakan as the verbal noun ‘ritual’ or mansikan as a noun denoting the site for a rite in other words for every community We have appointed a sacrificial slaughter or the site for such a ritual that they might mention God’s Name over the livestock that He has provided them at the point of slaughtering them. For your God is One God so submit yield to Him. And give good tidings to the humbly obedient

hype_questions: What is the purpose of sacrifice in Islam?
How should Muslims submit to their God?
What is the reward for humility and obedience?
propositions: For every community, a rite of sacrifice was appointed so that they may pronounce the Name of Allah over the sacrificial animals He has provided for them.
Your God is only One God, so submit yourselves to Him alone.
And give good news to the humble: For your God is One God, so submit yield to Him.

source_text:
Verse: those whose hearts tremble at the remembrance of Allah, who patiently endure whatever may befall them, and who establish prayer and donate from what We have provided for them.

Tafsir: who when God is mentioned their hearts tremble fear and who endure patiently whatever may befall them of ordeals and who observe prayer at its appointed times and who from that which We have provided them expend from it give voluntary alms.

hype_questions: What happens when God is mentioned?
How do those who fear Allah behave in difficult times?
What are the rewards for observing prayer and giving charity?
propositions: Those whose hearts tremble at the remembrance of Allah are patient in the face of adversity.
God's mention causes fear to enter the hearts of believers.
Believers who endure patiently whatever may befall them are rewarded with salvation.
Observing prayer at its appointed times is a fundamental aspect of faith.
Giving voluntary alms from one's wealth is a means of expiating sins and seeking forgiveness.

source_text:
Verse: We have made sacrificial camels ˹and cattle˺ among the symbols of Allah, in which there is ˹much˺ good for you. So pronounce the Name of Allah over them when they are lined up ˹for sacrifice˺. Once they have fallen ˹lifeless˺ on their sides, you may eat from their meat, and feed the needy—those who do not beg, and those who do. In this way We have subjected these ˹animals˺ to you so that you may be grateful.

Tafsir: And as for the sacrificial camels al-budn plural of badana which are ‘camels’ — We have appointed them for you as one of God’s sacraments the ritual ceremonies of His religion. There is good for you in them benefit for you in this world as already mentioned and a reward in the Hereafter. So mention God’s Name over them at the point of immolating them when they are lined up standing on three legs with the left foreleg hobbled. Then when their flanks have collapsed fallen to the ground after immolation — which is the time when one may eat of them — eat of them if you wish and feed the self-contained beggar al-qāni‘ a beggar who is content with what he is given neither asking nor approaching people and the suppliant al-mu‘tarr a beggar who asks for charity or approaches people for that purpose. So that is similar to such a disposal We have disposed them for you that it may be immolated or ridden — for otherwise it would not have been possible — that perhaps you might be thankful for My graces to you.

hype_questions: What is the significance of sacrificing camels in Islam?
How can I show gratitude to Allah by performing this act?
Who are the types of beggars that should be fed after sacrificing a camel?
propositions: We have made sacrificial camels among the symbols of Allah.
Pronounce the Name of Allah over them when they are lined up for sacrifice.
Eat from their meat and feed the needy after they have fallen lifeless on their sides.

source_text:
Verse: Neither their meat nor blood reaches Allah. Rather, it is your piety that reaches Him. This is how He has subjected them to you so that you may proclaim the greatness of Allah for what He has guided you to, and give good news to the good-doers.

Tafsir: Neither their flesh nor their blood shall reach God that is neither of these shall be raised up to Him; rather it is your piety that shall reach Him that is it is your righteous action performed purely for Him together with your faith that shall be raised up to Him. Thus has He disposed them for you that you may magnify God for His guiding you for His pointing out to you the ritual ceremonies of His religion and the rites of His pilgrimage. And give good tidings to the virtuous namely those who affirm the Oneness of God.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of animal sacrifice in Islam?
How does piety play a role in determining one's fate after death?
What are the benefits of following Allah's guidance and performing rituals?
propositions: Neither an animal's flesh nor its blood reaches God.
It is one's piety that reaches God, not their flesh or blood.
God has subjected animals to humans so that they may proclaim His greatness.
Piety consists of righteous actions performed purely for God and faith.
God has disposed animals for humans to magnify Him through rituals and pilgrimage.
Good tidings are given to the virtuous, who affirm the Oneness of God.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Allah defends those who believe. Surely Allah does not like whoever is deceitful, ungrateful.

Tafsir: Indeed God protects those who believe against the ruinous misguidance of idolaters. Indeed God does not love the treacherous with regard to what is entrusted to him the ungrateful for His grace — these are the idolaters —in other words He will punish them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who believe in Allah?
How does Allah react towards deceitful and ungrateful individuals?
What is the consequence of idolatry according to Islamic teachings?
propositions: Allah defends those who believe.
Allah does not like whoever is deceitful, ungrateful.
God protects those who believe against the ruinous misguidance of idolaters.
God does not love the treacherous with regard to what is entrusted to him the ungrateful for His grace — these are the idolaters —in other words He will punish them.

source_text:
Verse: Permission ˹to fight back˺ is ˹hereby˺ granted to those being fought, for they have been wronged. And Allah is truly Most Capable of helping them ˹prevail˺.

Tafsir: Permission is granted to those who fight namely to the believers to fight back — this was the first verse to be revealed regarding the struggle in the way of God jihād because they have been wronged as a result of the wrong done to them by the disbelievers. And God is truly able to help them;

hype_questions: What is the purpose of fighting back against those who have wronged us?
How can God help us in our struggle for justice?
What does it mean to fight in the way of God?
propositions: Permission is granted to those being fought, for they have been wronged.
Allah is truly Most Capable of helping them prevail.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who have been expelled from their homes for no reason other than proclaiming: “Our Lord is Allah.” Had Allah not repelled ˹the aggression of˺ some people by means of others, destruction would have surely claimed monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which Allah’s Name is often mentioned. Allah will certainly help those who stand up for Him. Allah is truly All-Powerful, Almighty.

Tafsir: they are those who were expelled from their homes without right for their expulsion; they were expelled only because they said that is because of their saying ‘Our Lord is God’ alone such a saying is ‘right’ and so then to be expelled for saying it is to be expelled without right. Were it not for God’s causing some people ba‘dahum ‘some’ substitutes for al-nāsa ‘people’ to drive back others destruction would have befallen read la-huddimat to emphasise a great number of destructions; or read la-hudimat the monasteries sawāmi‘ is for monks and churches kanā’is are for Christians and synagogues salawāt is the Hebrew term for Jewish houses of worship kanā’is and mosques masājid are for Muslims in which that is in which mentioned places God’s Name is mentioned greatly and with such destruction acts of worship cease. Assuredly God will help those who help Him that is who help His religion. God is truly Strong overpowering His creation Mighty Invincible in terms of His dominion and power;

hype_questions: What happens when people are expelled from their homes for proclaiming 'Our Lord is Allah'?
How would the destruction of places of worship affect the ability to perform acts of worship?
Who will help those who stand up for Allah and His religion?
propositions: Those who were expelled from their homes without right were expelled only because they said 'Our Lord is God'.
If it weren't for God causing some people to drive back others, destruction would have befallen monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques.
God will help those who stand up for Him and His religion.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who, if established in the land by Us, would perform prayer, pay alms-tax, encourage what is good, and forbid what is evil. And with Allah rests the outcome of all affairs.

Tafsir: those who if We empower them in the land by granting them victory over their enemies maintain the prayer and pay the alms and enjoin decency and forbid indecency this last is the response to the conditional clause which together with the response constitute a relative clause of the relative noun ‘those who’; hum ‘they are’ may be taken as the implied subject before this. And with God rests the outcome of all matters in other words to Him these matters return in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What are the qualities of a person who will be established in the land by Allah?
How does Allah empower individuals to maintain good deeds and forbid evil actions?
What is the ultimate outcome of all affairs for those who follow Allah's guidance?
propositions: If established in the land, they would perform prayer.
They would pay alms-tax.
They would encourage what is good and forbid what is evil.
Allah rests the outcome of all affairs.

source_text:
Verse: If they deny you ˹O Prophet˺, so did the people of Noah before them, as well as ˹the tribes of˺ ’Ȃd and Thamûd,

Tafsir: And if they deny you — these words to the end of the statement are meant to comfort the Prophet s — the people of Noah denied before them kadhdhabat in the feminine person on the basis of the overall import and ‘Ād the people of Hūd and Thamūd the people of Sālih

hype_questions: What happened to the people of Noah who denied the Prophet?
How did the tribes of ’Ad and Thamûd respond to the Prophet?
What was the fate of the people of Hūd who rejected the Prophet?
propositions: The people of Noah denied the Prophet.
The people of 'Ād, Hūd, and Thamūd also denied prophets before him.
Prophets are often met with denial and rejection by their communities.

source_text:
Verse: the people of Abraham, the people of Lot,

Tafsir: as well as the people of Abraham and the people of Lot

hype_questions: What are some notable prophets in Islam?
Who is Abraham in the Islamic faith?
What is the significance of Lot in Islamic tradition?
propositions: The people of Abraham and the people of Lot are mentioned together.
Abraham and Lot are two important figures in Islamic history.
Both Abraham and Lot are considered prophets in Islam.

source_text:
Verse: and the residents of Midian. And Moses was denied ˹too˺. But I delayed ˹the fate of˺ the disbelievers ˹until their appointed time˺ then seized them. And how severe was My response!

Tafsir: and the inhabitants of Midian the people of Shu‘ayb and Moses was also denied he was denied by the native Egyptians al-qibt and not by his people the Children of Israel. In other words all of those people denied their messengers so take them these messengers as a good example of constancy. And I granted the disbelievers respite I postponed dealing with them by deferring their requital then I seized them with chastisement and how terrible was My abhorrence! nakīr that is to say My rebuke inkār of them for their denial by My destroying them the interrogative is meant as an affirmative in other words it My chastisement was well-placed.

hype_questions: What is the lesson for believers when messengers are denied?
How did Allah grant respite to disbelievers before dealing with them?
Why was Moses' people punished despite his denial?
propositions: The residents of Midian were denied by their native Egyptians.
Moses was denied by the native Egyptians, not by his people, the Children of Israel.
All those who denied messengers will be taken as an example of constancy.
I granted respite to disbelievers and postponed dealing with them until their appointed time.
My chastisement was well-placed when I seized them with chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Many are the societies We have destroyed for persisting in wrongdoing, leaving them in total ruin. ˹Many are˺ also the abandoned wells and lofty palaces!

Tafsir: How many a town I have destroyed ahlaktuhā a variant reading has ahlaknāhā ‘We have destroyed’ while it was doing wrong that is while its inhabitants were doing wrong by being disbelievers but now it lies fallen down collapsed on its roofs and how many a neglected well abandoned because of the death of its owners and a lofty palace stands empty because of the death of its residents.

hype_questions: What happens to a society that persists in wrongdoing?
How do abandoned wells and palaces reflect the consequences of human actions?
What is the relationship between a community's faith and its fate?
propositions: We have destroyed many societies for persisting in wrongdoing.
Abandoned wells and lofty palaces are remnants of past civilizations that were destroyed due to their inhabitants' wrongdoings.
The destruction of a society is often a consequence of its people's disobedience and lack of faith.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not travelled throughout the land so their hearts may reason, and their ears may listen? Indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but it is the hearts in the chests that grow blind.

Tafsir: Have they namely the disbelievers of Mecca not travelled in the land so that they may have hearts with which to comprehend what befell deniers before them or ears with which to hear? the stories of how they were destroyed and their dwelling-places were ruined and so take heed? Indeed it is not the eyes that turn blind but it is the hearts that turn blind within the breasts allatī fī’l-sudūr for emphasis.

hype_questions: What can help believers comprehend the stories of previous nations that were destroyed?
How can believers take heed and avoid a similar fate?
What is it that truly turns blind, the eyes or the hearts?
propositions: Believers should travel throughout the land to reason and listen.
The disbelievers of Mecca should have had hearts to comprehend the stories of their destruction.
It is not the eyes that turn blind, but rather the hearts within the chests.

source_text:
Verse: They challenge you ˹O Prophet˺ to hasten the torment. And Allah will never fail in His promise. But a day with your Lord is indeed like a thousand years by your counting.

Tafsir: And they ask you to hasten the chastisement even though God would never break His promise of sending down the chastisement upon them — and so He sent it down on the day of Badr. And truly a day with your Lord of the days of the Hereafter on account of the severity of the chastisement is like a thousand years of your counting read ta‘uddūna or ya‘uddūna ‘their counting’ in this world.

hype_questions: What is the significance of hastening the chastisement?
How does Allah's promise relate to the chastisement?
What is the equivalent duration in human years for a day with Allah?
propositions: Allah will never fail in His promise.
God would never break His promise of sending down the chastisement upon them.
A day with your Lord of the days of the Hereafter on account of the severity of the chastisement is like a thousand years of your counting.

source_text:
Verse: Many are the societies whose end We delayed while they did wrong, then seized them. And to Me is the final return.

Tafsir: To how many a town did I give respite while it was doing wrong; but then I seized it meaning I seized its inhabitants and with Me lies the journey’s end the final return.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's delay in punishing wrongdoers?
How does Allah ultimately deal with those who have been given respite but then return to their wrongdoings?
What is the ultimate destination or end that Allah has in store for all people?
propositions: Allah delayed the punishment of many societies while they were doing wrong.
When Allah gives respite to a society, it means He is giving them time to correct their wrongdoings.
The final return refers to the ultimate destination or end that Allah has in store for all people.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O humanity! I am only sent to you with a clear warning.

Tafsir: Say ‘O mankind that is O people of Mecca I am only a manifest warner to you’ one whose warning is plain; but also I am a giver of good tidings to the believers.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the warning given by the Prophet?
How does the Prophet define himself in relation to humanity?
Who are the recipients of the Prophet's message?
propositions: The Prophet was sent with a clear warning.
The Prophet is only a manifest warner to humanity.
The Prophet is also a giver of good tidings to believers.

source_text:
Verse: So those who believe and do good will have forgiveness and an honourable provision.

Tafsir: And so those who believe and perform righteous deeds — for them there shall be forgiveness of their sins and a glorious provision namely Paradise.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe and do good?
How can one attain forgiveness of their sins?
What is the ultimate goal for those who perform righteous deeds?
propositions: Those who believe and do good will have forgiveness.
Believers who perform righteous deeds shall receive forgiveness of their sins.
Paradise is a glorious provision for those who believe and perform righteous deeds.

source_text:
Verse: But those who strive to discredit Our revelations, they will be the residents of the Hellfire.”

Tafsir: But those who strive against Our signs namely the Qur’ān in order to invalidate them seeking to incapacitate mu‘ajjizīna those who follow the Prophet this meaning of mu‘ajjizīna being derived from their assumption that these followers are incapable individuals and impeding them from practising their faith; or mu‘ajjizīna means supposing Us to be incapable against them a variant reading of mu‘ajjizīna has mu‘ājizīna meaning ‘contending with Us’ that is to say they suppose that they will be able to elude Us by denying resurrection and requital — those they shall be the inhabitants of hell-fire.

hype_questions: Can those who reject God's revelations escape punishment?
What happens to those who try to invalidate the message of the Prophet?
Will those who deny resurrection and requital be punished?
propositions: Those who discredit God's revelations will reside in Hellfire.
The Qur'ān is a sign that must not be invalidated.
Following the Prophet is obligatory for believers.
Resurrection and Requital are aspects of God's justice.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever We sent a messenger or a prophet before you ˹O Prophet˺ and he recited ˹Our revelations˺, Satan would influence ˹people’s understanding of˺ his recitation. But ˹eventually˺ Allah would eliminate Satan’s influence. Then Allah would ˹firmly˺ establish His revelations. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And We did not send before you any messenger rasūl — this is a prophet who has been commanded to deliver a Message — or prophet nabī — one who has not been commanded to deliver anything — but that when he recited the scripture Satan cast into his recitation what is not from the Qur’ān but which those to whom he the prophet had been sent would find pleasing. The Prophet s had during an assembly of the men of Quraysh after reciting the following verses from sūrat al-Najm Have you considered Lāt and ‘Uzzā? And Manāt the third one? 5319-20 added as a result of Satan casting them onto his tongue without his the Prophet’s being aware of it the following words ‘those are the high-flying cranes al-gharānīq al-‘ulā and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for’ and so they the men of Quraysh were thereby delighted. Gabriel however later informed him the Prophet of this that Satan had cast onto his tongue and he was grieved by it; but was subsequently comforted with this following verse that he might be reassured of God’s pleasure thereat God abrogates nullifies whatever Satan had cast then God confirms His revelations. And God is Knower of Satan’s casting of that which has been mentioned Wise in His enabling him Satan to do such things for He does whatever He will.

hype_questions: Does Allah abrogate and nullify the actions of Satan?
Can Satan influence people's understanding of a prophet's recitation?
How does Allah confirm His revelations after Satan casts something into a prophet's tongue?
propositions: Whenever We sent a messenger or a prophet before you, Satan would influence people's understanding of his recitation.
Allah would eliminate Satan's influence and establish His revelations.
God abrogates and nullifies whatever Satan had cast onto a prophet's tongue, then confirms His revelations.
Satan casts into a prophet's recitation what is not from the Qur'an but which those to whom he has been sent would find pleasing.
The Prophet was grieved by Satan casting words onto his tongue without his awareness, but was comforted with a subsequent verse from God.

source_text:
Verse: All that so He may make Satan’s influence a trial for those ˹hypocrites˺ whose hearts are sick and those ˹disbelievers˺ whose hearts are hardened. Surely the wrongdoers are totally engrossed in opposition.

Tafsir: That He may make what Satan has cast a trial a test for those in whose hearts is a sickness dissension and hypocrisy and those whose hearts are hardened namely the idolaters hardened against acceptance of the truth. For truly the evildoers the disbelievers are steeped in extreme defiance in a protracted feud with the Prophet s and the believers for his tongue uttered mention of their gods in a way that pleased them and yet this was later nullified.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Satan's influence being made a trial for hypocrites and disbelievers?
How do hypocrites and disbelievers respond to the Prophet's message?
What is the nature of the opposition faced by the Prophet and believers?
propositions: Allah makes Satan's influence a trial for those whose hearts are sick or hardened.
The wrongdoers are engrossed in opposition.
The Prophet's mention of their gods pleased them, but this was later nullified.

source_text:
Verse: ˹This is˺ also so that those gifted with knowledge would know that this ˹revelation˺ is the truth from your Lord, so they have faith in it, and so their hearts would submit humbly to it. And Allah surely guides the believers to the Straight Path.

Tafsir: And that those who have been given knowledge of God’s Oneness and the Qur’ān may know that it the Qur’ān is the truth from your Lord so that they may believe therein and their hearts may find reassurance in it. And assuredly God guides those who believe to a straight path a straight route namely the religion of Islam.

hype_questions: What is the nature of truth in Islam?
How does faith develop through knowledge of God's Oneness and the Qur'ān?
What is the ultimate goal of guidance from Allah?
propositions: This revelation is the truth from your Lord.
God guides believers to the Straight Path, which is the religion of Islam.

source_text:
Verse: Yet the disbelievers will persist in doubt about this ˹revelation˺ until the Hour takes them by surprise, or the torment of a terminating Day comes to them.

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt of it that is the Qur’ān — because of what Satan had cast onto the tongue of the Prophet s and what had thereafter been nullified — until the Hour comes upon them unawares that is the Hour of their death or of resurrection comes upon them suddenly or there come upon them the chastisement of a day of desolation ‘aqīm namely the day of Badr which held nothing of good for disbelievers much like a sterile wind rīh ‘aqīm that bears no good; or it means the Day of Resurrection referred to as ‘desolate’ because thereafter there will be no more night.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Hour that will take the disbelievers by surprise?
How does Satan's influence affect the understanding of the Qur'ān?
What is the significance of the Day of Badr in relation to the afterlife?
propositions: The disbelievers will persist in doubt about this revelation until the Hour takes them by surprise.
Those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt of the Qur'ān due to Satan's influence on the Prophet's tongue.
The Day of Badr is a day of desolation for disbelievers, bringing no good and only a sterile wind.

source_text:
Verse: All authority on that Day is for Allah ˹alone˺. He will judge between them. So those who believe and do good will be in the Gardens of Bliss.

Tafsir: Sovereignty on that day namely on the Day of Resurrection will be God’s alone the sense of God’s ‘consolidation’ of sovereignty on that Day suggested by the clause renders the adverbial qualifier yawma’idhin ‘on that day’ into accusative dependent status. He will judge between them between believers and disbelievers in the way that He explains next Then those who believed and performed righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss as a bounty from God

hype_questions: What will be the ultimate authority on Judgment Day?
How will Allah judge between believers and disbelievers?
What is the reward for those who believe and perform righteous deeds?
propositions: Allah's sovereignty on the Day of Resurrection is alone.
God will judge between believers and disbelievers.
Those who believe and do good will be in the Gardens of Bliss.

source_text:
Verse: But those who disbelieve and deny Our revelations, it is they who will suffer a humiliating punishment.

Tafsir: while those who disbelieved and denied Our signs for them will be a humiliating chastisement a severe one because of their disbelief.

hype_questions: What is the punishment for those who disbelieve in Allah's revelations?
How will those who deny Allah's signs be punished?
What consequences will arise from disbelief?
propositions: Those who disbelieve in Allah's revelations will suffer a humiliating punishment.
Disbelief leads to a severe chastisement.
Denying Allah's signs results in a humiliating punishment.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who emigrate in the cause of Allah and then are martyred or die, Allah will indeed grant them a good provision. Surely Allah is the Best Provider.

Tafsir: And those who emigrated in the way of God that is in obedience to Him from emigrating from Mecca to Medina and then were slain or died God shall provide them with a good provision namely the provision of Paradise. Truly God is the best of providers the most excellent of givers.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who emigrate in the cause of Allah?
How will Allah provide for those who are martyred or die?
What is the ultimate provision granted to those who follow the path of Allah?
propositions: Those who emigrate in the cause of Allah will be granted a good provision.
Allah provides a good provision to those who are martyred or die.
The provision granted to those who emigrate in the cause of Allah is Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: He will certainly admit them into a place they will be pleased with. For Allah is truly All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.

Tafsir: Assuredly He will admit them into a place read mudkhalan or madkhalan respectively signifying the means of entry or the place entered that is pleasing to them and that is Paradise. And truly God is Knowing of their intentions Forbearing in refraining from punishing them.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Paradise?
How does Allah know our intentions?
Why does Allah show mercy to those who enter Paradise?
propositions: He will admit them into a place they will be pleased with.
Allah is truly All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
God is Knowing of their intentions
God is Forbearing in refraining from punishing them.

source_text:
Verse: That is so. And whoever retaliates in equivalence to the injury they have received, and then are wronged ˹again˺, Allah will certainly help them. Surely Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving.

Tafsir: That which We have related to you is so. And whoever retaliates whoever from among the believers requites with the like of what he was made to suffer at the hands of the idolaters wrongfully that is whoever fights against them if they fight against him during the sacred month and then is again made to suffer aggression by them that is to say he is again wronged by being expelled from his house God will surely help him. Indeed God is Pardoning to believers Forgiving them their engaging in combat during the sacred month.

hype_questions: What happens when someone retaliates against an idolater who wronged them?
How does Allah help a believer who is wronged by others?
Can believers be forgiven for engaging in combat during the sacred month?
propositions: Allah will help those who retaliate against an idolater with the like of what they were made to suffer.
God is Pardoning to believers Forgiving them their engaging in combat during the sacred month.
If a believer fights against others during the sacred month and then is wronged, God will surely help him.

source_text:
Verse: That is because Allah causes the night to merge into the day, and the day into the night. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

Tafsir: That help is because God makes the night pass into the day and makes the day pass into the night that is to say He makes each enter into the other by increasing the one and decreasing the other which is a sign of His power exalted be He the same power that produces His help and because God is Hearer of the supplications of believers Seer of them giving them faith and responding to their supplications.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's power?
How does Allah respond to the supplications of believers?
What is the significance of faith in Islam?
propositions: Allah causes the night to merge into the day.
Allah makes the day pass into the night.
God produces His help through increasing one thing and decreasing another.
God is Hearer of the supplications of believers.
God Seer of them giving them faith and responding to their supplications.

source_text:
Verse: That is because Allah ˹alone˺ is the Truth and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and Allah ˹alone˺ is truly the Most High, All-Great.

Tafsir: That help also is because God He is the Truth the Established Truth and what they call on yad‘ūna; also read tad‘ūna ‘you call on’ what they worship besides Him namely idols that is the False the transient and because God He is the High the One supreme above all things in His power the Great besides Whom all things are insignificant.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah?
Is Allah the only one worthy of worship?
What happens to those who worship idols?
propositions: Allah is the Truth and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood.
God is the Established Truth.
Idols are the False, transient things that people worship besides Allah.
Allah is the High, One supreme above all things in His power.
All things are insignificant before Allah's power.

source_text:
Verse: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky, then the earth becomes green? Surely Allah is Most Subtle, All-Aware.

Tafsir: Have you not seen realised that God sends down water rain from the heaven whereupon the earth turns green with plants — and this too is a sign of His power. Indeed God is Subtle in dealing with His servants when He brings forth plants through water Aware of what is in their hearts when the rain is delayed.

hype_questions: Does God bring forth plants through water?
Is God aware of what is in the hearts of His servants when rain is delayed?
Can God's power be seen in the transformation of the earth from barren to green?
propositions: Allah sends down rain from the sky.
The earth becomes green after receiving rain.
God is Most Subtle and All-Aware.
God brings forth plants through water.
God is aware of what is in the hearts of His servants when rain is delayed.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Allah ˹alone˺ is truly the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

Tafsir: To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth in terms of ownership. Surely God He is Independent of His servants Praiseworthy to His friends.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's ownership?
How does Allah's independence relate to His servants?
Can humans be independent like Allah?
