propositions: Allah owns everything in the heavens and on earth.
God is Independent of His servants.
Allah is Praiseworthy to those who acknowledge Him.

source_text:
Verse: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the earth as well as the ships ˹that˺ sail through the sea by His command? He keeps the sky from falling down on the earth except by His permission. Surely Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity.

Tafsir: Have you not seen realised that God has disposed for you all that is in the earth of beasts and that the ships run upon the sea for transport and to carry loads by His command by His leave and He holds back the heaven lest it should fall on the earth save when it may do so by His leave and you are destroyed. Surely God is with mankind Gentle Merciful in disposing things for them and holding others back from them.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Allah's creation?
How does Allah control the forces of nature?
Why is Allah merciful to humanity?
propositions: Allah has subjected all that is in the earth and ships at sea to His command.
The sky is held back from falling on the earth except by Allah's permission.
Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who gave you life, then will cause you to die, and then will bring you back to life. ˹But˺ surely humankind is ever ungrateful.

Tafsir: And He it is Who gave you life by originating you then He will cause you to die upon the conclusion of your terms of life then He will give you life again at the Resurrection. Truly man that is truly the idolater is very ungrateful for God’s graces by neglecting to affirm His Oneness.

hype_questions: What is the nature of human existence in relation to divine life and death?
How does humanity respond to the blessings of Allah?
What is the significance of affirming the Oneness of God?
propositions: Allah gave you life.
You will die upon the conclusion of your terms of life.
Allah will give you life again at the Resurrection.
Man is ungrateful for Allah's graces by neglecting to affirm His Oneness.

source_text:
Verse: For every community We appointed a code So do not let them dispute with you ˹O Prophet˺ in this matter. And invite ˹all˺ to your Lord, for you are truly on the Right Guidance.

Tafsir: For every community We have appointed a holy rite read mansakan or mansikan a Holy Law which they are to observe which they are to implement. So do not let them dispute with you the intended meaning is ‘do not dispute with them’ about the matter namely the matter of the slaughter animal when they said ‘What God has killed is worthier for you to eat than what you killed’; but summon people to your Lord to His religion. Indeed you follow a straight guidance a straight religion.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of following a holy rite in Islam?
How does one summon people to their Lord's religion?
What is the significance of following a straight guidance and straight religion?
propositions: For every community We appointed a holy rite.
Do not let them dispute with you about the matter of slaughter animals.
You are truly on the Right Guidance.

source_text:
Verse: But if they argue with you, then say, “Allah knows best what you do.”

Tafsir: And if they dispute with you in the matter of religion say ‘God knows best what you do and will requite you for it — this was revealed before the command to fight them.

hype_questions: What is the Islamic response when faced with criticism or disagreement about one's faith?
How does Allah respond to those who dispute with believers in matters of religion?
What will Allah requite individuals for their actions, according to Islamic teachings?
propositions: Allah knows best what you do.
God knows best what you do and will requite you for it.
The command to fight those who dispute with believers in matters of religion was revealed after Allah's knowledge of human actions.

source_text:
Verse: Allah will judge between you ˹all˺ on Judgment Day regarding your differences.

Tafsir: God will judge between you O believers and disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ’ when each of the two parties would say the opposite of what the other said.

hype_questions: What will be the outcome when believers and disbelievers face each other on Judgment Day?
How will Allah judge between them regarding their differences?
What is the significance of differing opinions among believers and disbelievers?
propositions: Allah will judge between you on Judgment Day.
God will judge between believers and disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection.
Each party will say the opposite of what the other said.

source_text:
Verse: Do you not know that Allah ˹fully˺ knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Surely it is all ˹written˺ in a Record. That is certainly easy for Allah.

Tafsir: Do you not know the interrogative here is meant as an affirmative that God knows all that is in the heaven and the earth? Truly that which has been mentioned is recorded in a Book namely the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz. Indeed that namely the knowledge of what has been mentioned is easy for God.

hype_questions: Does Allah have complete knowledge of all things?
Is the record of deeds a reliable source of information about human actions?
Can God's knowledge be comprehended by humans?
propositions: Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth.
The Record of Deeds, namely al-lawh al-mahfūz, contains all that has been mentioned.
God's knowledge of what has been mentioned is easy for Him.

source_text:
Verse: Yet they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and of which they have no knowledge. The wrongdoers will have no helper.

Tafsir: And they the idolaters worship besides God that namely idols for which He has never revealed any warrant any definitive proof and that of which they have no knowledge when they claim that these are gods. And those who do evil by way of practising idolatry shall have no helper to protect them against God’s chastisement.

hype_questions: What is the nature of idols worshipped by polytheists?
Can idols be considered as gods?
Will idolaters have any helper or protector against God's chastisement?
propositions: They worship besides Allah idols for which He has never revealed any warrant.
Idolaters claim that these are gods, but they have no knowledge about it.
Those who do evil by way of practising idolatry shall have no helper to protect them against God’s chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever Our clear revelations are recited to them, you ˹O Prophet˺ recognize rage on the faces of the disbelievers, as if they are going to snap at those who recite Our revelations to them. Say, “Shall I inform you of something far more enraging than that? ˹It is˺ the Fire with which Allah has threatened those who disbelieve. What an evil destination!”

Tafsir: And when Our signs in the Qur’ān are recited to them though they are clear manifest signs bayyinātin a circumstantial qualifier you perceive on the faces of those who disbelieve denial that is to say denial of these signs in other words you perceive the effect of such denial in the way of aversion and frowning. They would almost pounce upon those who recite Our signs to them that is they would almost fall upon them in assault. Say ‘Shall I inform you about something worse than that? something more repulsive to you than the Qur’ān that is being recited to you? It is The Fire! God has promised it to the disbelievers in that their journey’s end shall be to it. And it is an evil journey’s end!’

hype_questions: Is the Fire worse than the Qur'ān being recited to them?
What is the destination of those who disbelieve?
Will the journey's end be The Fire for the disbelievers?
propositions: Whenever Our clear revelations are recited to them, you recognize rage on the faces of the disbelievers.
The Fire with which Allah has threatened those who disbelieve is far more enraging than the rage on the faces of the disbelievers.
God has promised The Fire as the destination for those who disbelieve.
The journey's end for those who disbelieve will be to The Fire.
The Qur'ān being recited to them is something worse than the rage on the faces of the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: O humanity! A lesson is set forth, so listen to it ˹carefully˺: those ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Allah can never create ˹so much as˺ a fly, even if they ˹all˺ were to come together for that. And if a fly were to snatch anything away from them, they cannot ˹even˺ retrieve it from the fly. How powerless are those who invoke and those invoked!

Tafsir: O mankind that is to say O people of Mecca a similitude is being struck so listen to it and it is that truly those on whom you call whom you worship besides God that is other than Him and these are the idols will never create a fly dhubāb is a generic noun the singular of which is dhubāba for both the masculine and the feminine even if they rallied together to do so to create it. And if a fly should take away something from them such as a drop of the scents or the saffron in which they drench themselves they would not be able to recover that from it because of their complete incapacity so how can they worship those whom they suppose to be partners of God exalted be He? An odd thing — which He has expressed by striking a similitude. Feeble is the seeker the worshipper and the thing sought the thing worshipped!

hype_questions: Can anything created by humans, even if they work together, create something as complex as a fly?
If a fly were to take away something from an idol, would the worshippers be able to recover it?
Is it possible for humans to worship beings that are powerless and incapable of creating or taking away anything?
propositions: Those who invoke idols besides Allah cannot create even a fly.
If a fly were to take something from an idol, the worshippers would not be able to retrieve it.
Humans are weak and unable to worship beings that are powerless and incapable of creating or taking away anything.

source_text:
Verse: They have not shown Allah the reverence He deserves. Surely Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.

Tafsir: They do not esteem God exalt Him with the esteem He deserves with the exaltedness He deserves for they ascribe to Him partners who can neither protect themselves from a fly nor retaliate against it. Truly God is Strong Mighty Victor.

hype_questions: What does it mean to show reverence to Allah?
How can ascribing partners to Allah affect one's relationship with Him?
What are the consequences of not giving Allah the esteem He deserves?
propositions: They did not show Allah the reverence He deserves.
Allah is All-Powerful and Almighty.
Ascribing partners to Allah is false because they cannot protect themselves from a fly or retaliate against it.
God is Strong Mighty Victor.

source_text:
Verse: Allah selects messengers from both angels and people, for Allah is truly All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

Tafsir: God chooses from the angels messengers and also chooses from mankind messengers — this was revealed after the idolaters said Has the Remembrance been revealed to him out of all of us? Q. 388. Truly God is Hearer of what they say Seer of those whom He chooses as messengers such as Gabriel Michael Abraham Muhammad (s) and others may God bless them and grant them peace.

hype_questions: Who are the messengers chosen by Allah?
How does Allah select messengers?
What is the significance of Allah's hearing and seeing?
propositions: Allah selects messengers from both angels and people.
God chooses from the angels messengers and also chooses from mankind messengers.
Allah is truly All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

source_text:
Verse: He knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them. And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺.

Tafsir: He knows that which is before them and that which is behind them in other words what they have offered in the way of deeds and what they have left behind and what they have done and what they will do next; and to God all matters are returned.

hype_questions: What happens to our deeds after we die?
Is everything predetermined in life?
Will God judge us based on our actions?
propositions: God knows what has been done and will be done.
All matters are returned to God for judgment.
Deeds and their consequences are known by God.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Bow down, prostrate yourselves, worship your Lord, and do ˹what is˺ good so that you may be successful.

Tafsir: O you who believe bow down and prostrate yourselves in other words perform prayer and worship your Lord affirm His Oneness and do good such as showing kindness to kin and the adoption of noble traits that perhaps you may be prosperous that perhaps you may secure everlasting life in Paradise.

hype_questions: What is the reward for performing good deeds?
How can I secure everlasting life in Paradise?
What are some noble traits that I can adopt to be prosperous?
propositions: Believers should bow down and prostrate themselves.
Worshiping one's Lord involves affirming His Oneness.
Doing good deeds is essential for success.
Showing kindness to kin and adopting noble traits are examples of good deeds.
Prosperity in this life may lead to everlasting life in Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: Strive for ˹the cause of˺ Allah in the way He deserves, for ˹it is˺ He ˹Who˺ has chosen you, and laid upon you no hardship in the religion—the way of your forefather Abraham. ˹It is Allah˺ Who named you ‘the ones who submit’ ˹in the˺ earlier ˹Scriptures˺ and in this ˹Quran˺, so that the Messenger may be a witness over you, and that you may be witnesses over humanity. So establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and hold fast to Allah. He ˹alone˺ is your Guardian. What an excellent Guardian, and what an excellent Helper!

Tafsir: And struggle in the way of God in order to establish His religion a struggle worthy of Him by expending all effort therein haqqa is in the accusative because it is a verbal noun. He has elected you He has chosen you for His religion and has not laid upon you in your religion any hardship that is any constraint for He has facilitated adherence to it during times of difficulty such as His permitting you to shorten prayers to seek ritual purification from earth to eat of carrion and to break the fast during illness or travel — the creed of your father millata is in the accusative because the genitive preposition kāf sc. ka-millati ‘like the creed of’ has been omitted Abraham Ibrāhīma an explicative supplement. He that is God named you Muslims before that is before the revelation of this Book and in this that is in the Qur’ān so that the Messenger might be a witness against you on the Day of Resurrection that he delivered the Message to you and that you might be witnesses against mankind that their messengers delivered the Message to them. So maintain prayer observe it regularly and pay the alms and hold fast to God trust in Him. He is your Patron your Helper and the Guardian of your affairs. An excellent Patron is He and an excellent Helper for you.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of submitting to God?
How can I establish a prayer routine that is pleasing to God?
What are some ways to demonstrate my faith and trust in God?
propositions: Strive for the cause of Allah in the way He deserves.
He has chosen you, and laid upon you no hardship in the religion—the way of your forefather Abraham.
So establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Guardian.

source_text:
Verse: Successful indeed are the believers:

Tafsir: Indeed qad is for confirmation prosperous victorious are the believers

hype_questions: What does it mean to be a successful believer?
How do believers achieve prosperity and victory?
What is the nature of belief in Islam?
propositions: The believers are prosperous.
The believers are victorious.
Belief is confirmed.

source_text:

hype_questions: What is the significance of humility in prayer?

What are the benefits of being humble while praying?

Prayer is performed by those who are humble.

They shun vain talk and other nonsense.

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: those who guard their chastity

Tafsir: and who guard their private parts against what is unlawful

hype_questions: What are the consequences of not guarding one's chastity?
How does guarding one's chastity impact one's spiritual growth?
What is the significance of guarding one's private parts in Islam?
propositions: Those who guard their chastity.
And who guard their private parts against what is unlawful.

source_text:
Verse: except with their wives or those ˹bondwomen˺ in their possession, for then they are free from blame,

Tafsir: except from their spouses that is to their spouses and what slaves their right hands possess that is concubines for then they are not blameworthy in having sexual intercourse with them.

hype_questions: What are the conditions for a man to be free from blame in his sexual intercourse?
Can a man have sexual intercourse with his concubine without being blameworthy?
Under what circumstances is a woman considered a 'bondwoman'?
propositions: A man is not blamed for having sexual intercourse with his wife.
A man is not blamed for having sexual intercourse with slaves in his possession, specifically those in his right hand.
Concubines are considered acceptable for sexual intercourse.

source_text:
Verse: but whoever seeks beyond that are the transgressors;

Tafsir: But whoever seeks anything beyond that intercourse with wives and concubines such as masturbation those they are transgressors who have overstepped the bounds into what is not lawful for them.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who seeks something beyond their allowed intimacy?
Can seeking forbidden acts lead to transgression?
How do we define the boundaries of what is lawful for us?

Tafsir: Then We transformed the drop of semen into a clot congealed blood. Then We transformed the clot into a little lump of flesh mudgha a piece of flesh about the size of what one would be able to chew mā yumdagh. Then We transformed the lump of flesh into bones. Then We clothed the bones with flesh a variant reading in both instances instead of the plurals ‘izāman and al-‘izāma ‘the bones’ is singular ‘azman and ‘al-‘azma ‘the bone’; and in all three instances above khalaqnā means ‘We made it become’ as opposed to ‘We created’. Then We produced him as yet another creature by breathing into him Our Spirit. So blessed be God the best of creators! that is the best of determiners the specificier noun for ahsana ‘the best’ has been omitted because it is obvious khalqan ‘in terms of creation’.

Verse: So We inspired him: “Build the Ark under Our ˹watchful˺ Eyes and directions. Then when Our command comes and the oven bursts ˹with water˺, take on board a pair from every species along with your family—except those against whom the decree ˹to drown˺ has already been passed. And do not plead with Me for those who have done wrong, for they will surely be drowned.”

Tafsir: So We revealed to him saying ‘Build the Ark the ship under Our watch under Our observation and protection and by Our revelation Our command. Then when Our command comes that they be destroyed and the oven of the baker gushes with water — and this was Noah’s sign — bring into it admit into the ship of every kind of animal two mates a male and a female that is two of every species thereof ithnayn is an object; min ‘of’ is semantically connected to usluk ‘bring into it’. According to the story God exalted be He gathered all the beasts of prey and the birds and other animals for Noah. As he Noah pushed forth his hands into each species his right hand would fall upon a male and the left upon a female whereafter he would take them on board the ship a variant reading for min kuli ‘of every’ is min kullin ‘of every kind’ in which case zawjayni ‘two mates’ becomes a direct object with ithnayn ‘two’ being repeated for emphasis thereof; together with your family — his wife ? and children — except for those against whom the Word has already gone forth that they be destroyed namely his wife and his son Canaan Kan‘ān unlike Shem Sām Ham Hām and Japheth Yāfith whom together with their three wives he carried on board. In sūrat Hūd the following is mentioned where Noah is told who he should carry in the ship ‘… and those who believe.’ And none believed with him except a few Q. 1140. It is said that these were six men and their wives. Moreover it is said that all those who were on the ship numbered seventy eight half of them were men and half were women. And do not plead with Me concerning those who have done wrong those who have disbelieved that I should refrain from destroying them. They shall indeed be drowned.

Tafsir: So they denied them both and became of those who were destroyed.

hype_questions: What happens when someone rejects an important message?
Who are the people that get destroyed after rejecting a message?
What is the consequence of denying a divine message?
propositions: They rejected both the message and its bearer.
The rejection of the message led to their destruction.
Denying the message resulted in their downfall.

source_text:
Verse: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so perhaps his people would be ˹rightly˺ guided.

Tafsir: And verily We gave Moses the Scripture the Torah that perhaps they his people the Children of Israel might be guided thereby from error — he Moses was given it the Scripture after the destruction of Pharaoh and his folk all at once.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the Torah?
How did Moses receive the Scripture?
Can the Torah guide people from error?
propositions: We gave Moses the Scripture.
The Torah was given to Moses after the destruction of Pharaoh and his folk.
Moses received the Scripture so that his people might be guided thereby.

source_text:
Verse: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and gave them refuge on high ground—a ˹suitable˺ place for rest with flowing water.

Tafsir: And We made the son of Mary Jesus and his mother a sign — He did not say ‘two signs’ because the same sign is in both of them his being born without his mother’s having a male spouse. And We gave them refuge on a height rabwa a highland — in this case either the Holy House of Jerusalem Damascus or Palestine all of which are alternative opinions — level dhāt qarār an flat high- land on which its inhabitants are able to settle yastaqirru and watered by springs running water over ground which the eyes can see.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Jesus' birth without a male spouse?
Where did Allah give refuge to Mary and her son?
What are some alternative locations for the highland where Allah gave refuge?
propositions: Allah made the son of Mary and his mother a sign.
The same sign is in both Jesus and Mary, which is their birth without a male spouse.
Allah gave them refuge on a high land with flowing water.

source_text:
Verse: O messengers! Eat from what is good and lawful, and act righteously. Indeed, I fully know what you do.

Tafsir: ‘O messengers eat of the good things the lawful things and perform righteous acts such as obligatory and supererogatory rituals. Surely I know what you do and will requite you for it.

hype_questions: What are the good things that messengers should eat from?
What kind of acts are considered righteous by Allah?
Will Allah requite the actions of messengers?
propositions: Messengers should eat from good and lawful things.
Messengers should perform righteous acts, including obligatory and supererogatory rituals.
Allah knows what messengers do and will requite them for it.

source_text:
Verse: Surely this religion of yours is ˹only˺ one, and I am your Lord, so fear Me ˹alone˺.

Tafsir: And know that this creed of Islam is your community your religion O you being addressed that is you must adhere to it as one community — a necessary state of affairs a variant reading for anna ‘that’ has the softened form in; a variant has inna ‘truly’ indicating the beginning of an independent new sentence and I am your Lord so fear Me’ so be fearful of Me.

hype_questions: What is the fundamental principle of Islam?
Who is the ultimate authority in Islam?
What is the expected response from a Muslim towards their Lord?
propositions: This religion of yours is one.
I am your Lord, so fear Me alone.

source_text:
Verse: Yet the people have divided it into different sects, each rejoicing in what they have.

Tafsir: But they the followers split into sects regarding their affair their religion zuburan ‘sects’ is a circumstantial qualifier of the subject of the verb taqatta‘ū ‘they split’ in other words they became opposing parties the likes of the Jews and the Christians and others each party rejoicing in exultant with what they had that is with the religion they had.

hype_questions: What are some examples of religious sects that have formed due to disagreements over faith?
How do different groups within a religion often prioritize their own beliefs over the commonalities with others?
Can sectarianism lead to greater division and conflict within communities?
propositions: The people split into different sects.
They became opposing parties regarding their affair and religion.
Each party rejoices in what they have, specifically their own religion.

source_text:
Verse: So leave them ˹O Prophet˺ in their heedlessness for a while.

Tafsir: So leave them the disbelievers of Mecca in their error their misguidance for a while until they die.

hype_questions: What is the recommended course of action for the Prophet when dealing with disbelievers?
How long should the Prophet wait before taking action against the disbelievers?
What will happen to the disbelievers after a certain period of time?
propositions: The Prophet should leave the disbelievers alone for a while.
The disbelievers of Mecca are in a state of error and misguidance.
The disbelievers will die without changing their beliefs.

source_text:
Verse: Do they think, since We provide them with wealth and children,

Tafsir: Do they suppose that in the wealth and children with which We provide them in the life of this world

hype_questions: Do they think that wealth and children are the ultimate goals of human existence?
Can wealth and children bring true happiness in this life?
Is it possible to find fulfillment without considering material possessions and family?
propositions: We provide people with wealth.
We provide people with children.
The wealth and children provided by Allah are for the life of this world.

source_text:
Verse: that We hasten to ˹honour˺ them ˹with˺ all kinds of good? No! They are not aware.

Tafsir: We are hastening to provide them with good things? No. Rather they are not aware that this is a way of gradually drawing them into their punishment.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of hastening to provide good things to people?
How do people become aware of their impending punishment?
Is it possible for people to be drawn into their punishment gradually?
propositions: We are hastening to provide them with good things.
They are not aware that this is a way of gradually drawing them into their punishment.

source_text:
Verse: Surely those who tremble in awe of their Lord,

Tafsir: Surely those who for fear of their Lord are apprehensive are fearful of His chastisement

hype_questions: What is the consequence of fearing one's Lord?
How does fear of one's Lord manifest in their actions?
What is the ultimate goal of those who tremble with awe?
propositions: Those who tremble in awe of their Lord are apprehensive about His chastisement.
Fear of one's Lord leads to apprehension about punishment.
Trembling with awe indicates a deep respect for God's power.

source_text:
Verse: and who believe in the revelations of their Lord,

Tafsir: and who believe in who accept the truth of the signs of their Lord — the Qur’ān;

hype_questions: What are the signs of Allah that believers must accept as true?
Who is the Lord that Muslims believe in and accept as their guide?
What is the Qur'an, and why do Muslims consider it a revelation from their Lord?
propositions: Believers who accept the truth of the signs of their Lord are those who believe in the revelations of their Lord.
The Qur'an is considered a revelation from Allah that believers must accept as true.

source_text:
Verse: and who associate none with their Lord,

Tafsir: and who do not associate others with their Lord

hype_questions: What happens to those who associate partners with Allah?
Who are the ones that Allah forbids from associating with Him?
What is the consequence of shirk in Islam?
propositions: None associates with their Lord.
Associating others with one's Lord is forbidden.
Those who associate partners with Allah are not accepted.

source_text:
Verse: and who do whatever ˹good˺ they do with their hearts fearful, ˹knowing˺ that they will return to their Lord—

Tafsir: and who give what they give of voluntary alms and righteous deeds while their hearts tremble with awe fearful lest it not be accepted from them because the particle lām ‘for’ is taken as implied before annahum ‘that they’ they are going to return to their Lord —

hype_questions: What happens when we perform good deeds with a fearful heart?
How do our actions affect our relationship with Allah?
What is the consequence of not giving voluntary alms and righteous deeds?
propositions: Whoever does good with their hearts will return to their Lord.
Those who give voluntary alms and righteous deeds tremble with awe, fearing it may not be accepted from them.
The particle lām 'for' implies that those who perform good deeds are going to return to their Lord.

source_text:
Verse: it is they who race to do good deeds, always taking the lead.

Tafsir: those are the ones who hasten to perform good works and they are the ones who shall come out ahead in them according to God’s knowledge.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of hastening to perform good works?
How does God's knowledge relate to one's performance in good deeds?
What benefits can be expected from consistently performing good works?
propositions: Those who hasten to perform good works are those who race to do good deeds.
God's knowledge determines the outcome of one's good works.
Performing good works is a means to come out ahead in God's sight.

source_text:
Verse: We never require of any soul more than what it can afford. And with Us is a record which speaks the truth. None will be wronged.

Tafsir: And We do not task any soul beyond its capacity what it can bear — thus he who is not able to pray standing let him pray sitting down and he who is not able to fast let him eat; and with Us is a Record that speaks the truth regarding what it a soul has done — and this Record is the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz wherein deeds are written down; and they namely the souls in their acts will not be wronged in a single thing thereof and so nothing is diminished of the reward for good deeds nor is anything extra added to the evil deeds.

hype_questions: What happens when a soul is unable to perform a certain act of worship?
How does the record of deeds work in Islam?
Can good deeds ever be diminished or evil deeds ever be increased?
propositions: We never require of any soul more than what it can afford.
With Us is a record which speaks the truth. None will be wronged.
He who is not able to pray standing let him pray sitting down and he who is not able to fast let him eat.
This Record is the Preserved Tablet wherein deeds are written down.
Deeds are not diminished in reward nor are evil deeds increased.

source_text:
Verse: But the hearts of those ˹who disbelieve˺ are oblivious to ˹all of˺ this, and they have other ˹evil˺ deeds, opposite to this, in which they are engrossed.

Tafsir: Nay but their hearts that is the hearts of the disbelievers are in ignorance of this Qur’ān and they have other deeds which they will perpetrate besides the ones mentioned against the believers and they will therefore be chastised for them.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of disbelievers' ignorance of the Qur'an?
How do disbelievers' deeds affect their chastisement?
What is the nature of the evil deeds that disbelievers perpetrate?
propositions: The hearts of those who disbelieve are oblivious to this.
They have other evil deeds, opposite to this, in which they are engrossed.
Their ignorance of the Qur'an will lead to their chastisement for their deeds.

source_text:
Verse: But as soon as We seize their elite with torment, they start to cry for help.

Tafsir: Indeed hattā is for inceptiveness when We seize their affluent ones their wealthy and their leaders with chastisement with the sword on the day of Badr behold! they are supplicating loudly clamouring in supplication. It is then said to them

hype_questions: What happens when Allah seizes the elite with torment?
Why do people cry out for help when they are being punished by Allah?
How do people react when they are facing chastisement from Allah?
propositions: When Allah seizes someone with torment, they will start to cry for help.
The affluent and wealthy will be punished with chastisement on the day of Badr.
People will loudly supplicate to Allah when they are being punished.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They will be told,˺ “Do not cry for help today. Surely you will never be saved from Us.

Tafsir: ‘Do not supplicate out loud on this day! Truly you will not receive help you will not be protected against Us.

hype_questions: Will I ever be saved from God's wrath?
Can I expect protection from Allah on this day?
What happens if I don't receive help from God?
propositions: You will not receive help from God.
You will not be protected against God's wrath.
God's help is not available today.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, My revelations were recited to you, but you used to back away ˹in disgust˺,

Tafsir: Verily My signs in the Qur’ān used to be recited to you but you used to take to your heels falling back in retreat

hype_questions: What happens when one disobeys Allah's revelations?
How does Allah react to being disobeyed?
What is the consequence of retreating from Allah's signs?
propositions: My revelations were recited to you.
You used to back away in disgust.
My signs in the Qur'ān are a source of retreat for those who disbelieve.

source_text:
Verse: boasting of the Sacred House, and babbling ˹nonsense about the Quran˺ by night.”

Tafsir: disdainful of embracing faith because of it that is because of the Sacred House or the Meccan Sanctuary and their being inhabitants thereof secure in contrast to the situation with all other peoples in their hometowns while in your night sessions sāmiran is a circumstantial qualifier in other words they come together to converse at night around the Sacred House you talked nonsense’ if read as tahjurūna the third form from hajara means while ‘you disregarded’ the Qur’ān; but if read as the fourth form tuhjirūna from ahjara it means while ‘you speak falsehood’ about the Prophet and the Qur’ān.

hype_questions: Does the Sacred House have a significant influence on people's faith?
How do people's attitudes towards faith change when they are in close proximity to sacred sites?
Can the presence of a sacred site like the Meccan Sanctuary lead to a sense of security and stability?
propositions: The Sacred House has an influence on people's faith.
People who live near the Sacred House tend to be more secure in their faith than those who do not.
Conversing at night around the Sacred House can lead to a lack of understanding and misinterpretation of Islamic teachings.

source_text:
Verse: Is it because they have never contemplated the Word ˹of Allah˺? Or ˹because˺ there has come to them something that did not come to their forefathers?

Tafsir: God exalted be He says Have they not contemplated yaddabbarū should actually be yatadabbarū but the tā’ has been assimilated with the dāl the discourse namely the Qur’ān that is proof of the Prophet’s sincerity or has there come upon them that which has not come upon their forefathers?

hype_questions: Do people not reflect on the Quran?
Has something new been revealed to them that was not present in their ancestors?
Have they considered the sincerity of the Prophet?
propositions: God exalted be He says: Have they not contemplated?
They have not contemplated.
There has come to them something that did not come to their forefathers.

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹because˺ they failed to recognize their Messenger, and so they denied him?

Tafsir: Or is it that they do not recognise their own Messenger and so they reject him?

hype_questions: What happens when we fail to recognize our own Messenger?
Why do people reject their own Messenger?
How can we improve our recognition of our own Messenger?
propositions: They failed to recognize their Messenger.
They do not recognise their own Messenger.
People reject their own Messenger.

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹because˺ they say, “He is insane?” In fact, he has come to them with the truth, but most of them are resentful of the truth.

Tafsir: Or do they say ‘There is a madness in him’? — this interrogative is meant as an affirmation of the truth of the Prophet’s sincerity and of the fact that messengers did come to past communities and of the fact that they do indeed recognise their Messenger to be truthful and trustworthy and of the fact that there is no madness in him. Nay bal is for transition he has brought them the truth namely the Qur’ān that comprises affirmations of the Oneness of God and the Laws of Islam; but most of them are averse to the truth.

hype_questions: Does the Prophet bring madness or truth?
Can messengers be recognized as truthful and trustworthy?
Is there a connection between recognizing the Messenger and embracing the truth?
propositions: The Prophet is sincere.
Messengers come to past communities with the truth.
There is no madness in the Prophet.
The Qur'ān comprises affirmations of the Oneness of God and the Laws of Islam.
Most people are averse to the truth.

source_text:
Verse: Had the truth followed their desires, the heavens, the earth, and all those in them would have certainly been corrupted. In fact, We have brought them ˹the means to˺ their glory, but they turn away from it.

Tafsir: And if the truth namely the Qur’ān had followed their desires and come to them with mention of what they fancied in the way of God having a partner and a child may God be exalted above such associations indeed the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted they the heavens and the earth would have deviated from their observed order because contradictions would ensue as is usually the case when there is more than one ruler. Nay We have brought them their Remembrance namely the Qur’ān in which they are remembered and honoured but they are disregardful of their own Remembrance.

hype_questions: If the truth had followed their desires, what would have been the outcome?
How would the heavens and earth be affected if polytheistic beliefs were to prevail?
What is the significance of the Qur’ān in human remembrance?
propositions: The heavens and the earth would have been corrupted if the truth had followed their desires.
God's oneness is beyond association with a partner or child.
The Qur’ān brings remembrance and honour, but it is often disregarded.

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹is it because˺ you ˹O Prophet˺ are asking them for tribute? But the reward of your Lord is best, for He is the Best Provider.

Tafsir: Or do you ask them for any recompense? any remuneration in return for the faith that you have brought them? Yet the recompense of your Lord is His remuneration His reward and His provision are better one reading has kharjan ‘recompense’ in both instances sc. kharjan fa-kharju; another has kharājan in both sc. kharājan fa-kharāju and He is the best of providers the best of givers and remunerators.

hype_questions: Does asking for tribute affect the reward of one's Lord?
What is the best recompense for faith?
How does one's Lord provide for them?
propositions: You ask them for any recompense in return for the faith that you have brought them.
The recompense of your Lord is His remuneration, His reward, and His provision are better.
He is the best of providers, the best of givers, and remunerators.

source_text:
Verse: And surely you are calling them to the Straight Path,

Tafsir: And truly you summon them to a straight path a straight route that is the religion of Islam.

hype_questions: What is the true nature of the Straight Path?
How does one achieve spiritual guidance on this path?
What are the key principles of the religion of Islam?
propositions: You are calling them to the Straight Path.
The Straight Path is a straight route that is the religion of Islam.

source_text:
Verse: but those who disbelieve in the Hereafter are certainly deviating from that Path.

Tafsir: And truly those who do not believe in the Hereafter in resurrection reward and punishment deviate swerve away from the path that is the route to salvation.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate destination for those who reject the concept of an afterlife?
How does disbelief in the Hereafter affect one's spiritual journey?
What is the nature of the path that leads to salvation?
propositions: Those who disbelieve in the Hereafter are deviating from the correct path.
Belief in the Hereafter is essential for salvation.
Disbelief in the Hereafter leads to spiritual deviation.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Even˺ if We had mercy on them and removed their affliction, they would still persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.

Tafsir: And had We shown them mercy and relieved them of the harm afflicting them — the famine that befell them in Mecca for seven years — they would surely persist in their insolence in their error bewildered hesitating.

hype_questions: Would they still commit sin even if God showed them mercy?
How would the people of Mecca have reacted to an end to their famine?
Can a person change their ways after experiencing hardship?
propositions: If God had shown mercy on them, they would still persist in their transgression.
The famine that befell them in Mecca for seven years was not enough to deter them from their insolence.
They were bewildered and hesitating due to their error.

source_text:
Verse: And We have already seized them with torment, but they never humbled themselves to their Lord, nor did they ˹submissively˺ appeal ˹to Him˺.

Tafsir: And We have already seized them with chastisement with hunger yet they did not humble themselves to their Lord nor did they devote themselves to prayer nor did they seek the pleasure of God through supplication.

hype_questions: What happens when one fails to humble themselves before their Lord?
How does one demonstrate submissiveness to their Lord?
In what ways can prayer and supplication bring a person closer to God?
propositions: We have already seized them with torment.
They did not humble themselves to their Lord.
They did not devote themselves to prayer.
They did not seek the pleasure of God through supplication.

source_text:
Verse: But as soon as We open for them a gate of severe punishment, they will be utterly desperate.

Tafsir: Until hattā is for inceptiveness when We opened on them the gate of a severe chastisement namely the day of Badr slaying them behold! they are aghast thereat despairing of anything good.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah opens a gate of severe punishment for someone?
How do people react when they are faced with the day of Badr?
What is the state of those who are slain on the day of Badr?
propositions: We opened a gate of severe punishment for them.
They were desperate and despairing of anything good when they saw it.
The day of Badr was a severe chastisement for them.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who created for you hearing, sight, and intellect. ˹Yet˺ you hardly give any thanks.

Tafsir: And He it is Who made created for you hearing meaning ears and eyes and hearts. Little thanks do you show qalīlan mā mā emphasises the paucity of the thanks.

hype_questions: What are some ways to show gratitude to Allah?
How does Allah's creation impact our lives?
Why is it important to acknowledge the blessings we receive?
propositions: Allah created hearing, sight, and intellect for humans.
Humans rarely express thanks to Allah despite His numerous blessings.
The lack of gratitude towards Allah is a significant issue.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who has dispersed you ˹all˺ over the earth, and to Him you will ˹all˺ be gathered.

Tafsir: And He it is Who dispersed created you on earth and to Him you shall be gathered resurrected.

hype_questions: What will happen to us after we die?
Who created the world and everything in it?
Will we be brought back to life on the Day of Judgment?
propositions: Allah dispersed created you on earth.
You shall be gathered resurrected by Allah.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who gives life and causes death, and to Him belongs the alternation of the day and night. Will you not then understand?

Tafsir: And He it is Who gives life by breathing the Spirit into the embryo mudgha and brings death and due to Him is the alternation of night and day in darkness and brightness and through increase and diminution. Will you not then comprehend? His handiwork exalted be He and so reflect?

hype_questions: Doesn't the existence of life and death reveal a higher power?
Can we truly comprehend the mysteries of the universe?
Is it possible to understand the workings of Allah?
propositions: Allah gives life by breathing the Spirit into the embryo.
Allah brings death.
The alternation of night and day is due to Allah.
Night and day are characterized by darkness and brightness.
Increase and diminution occur under Allah's will.
Allah's handiwork is exalted.
We should reflect on the workings of Allah.

source_text:
Verse: But they ˹just˺ say what their predecessors said.

Tafsir: Nay but they say the like of what the ancients said.

hype_questions: What motivates people to repeat the same ideas as their predecessors?
How do individuals justify mimicking the thoughts and actions of those who came before them?
In what contexts is it common for people to echo the sentiments of earlier generations?
propositions: They say what their predecessors said.
They say the like of what the ancients said.

source_text:
Verse: They said, “Once we are dead and reduced to dust and bones, will we really be resurrected?

Tafsir: They the ancients said ‘What when we are dead and have become dust and bones shall we then be raised? No! the two hamzas in each of the two instances are either pronounced fully or with the second one not pronounced but with an alif inserted between the two hamzas in both readings.

hype_questions: Will we be resurrected after death?
What happens to our bodies after we die?
Can we be brought back to life?
propositions: We will not be resurrected after death.
Our bodies will return to dust and bones after death.
The two hamzas in each of the two instances are either pronounced fully or with the second one not pronounced but with an alif inserted between the two hamzas in both readings.

source_text:
Verse: We have already been promised this, as well as our forefathers earlier. This is nothing but ancient fables!”

Tafsir: Already We and our fathers have been promised this resurrection after death before these are nothing but the fables the lies of the ancients’ mere jokes and strange tales asātīr the plural of ustūra.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the resurrection promised in the Quran?
How do ancient fables relate to the concept of resurrection?
What are the characteristics of the lies and jokes of the ancients?
propositions: We have already been promised this resurrection after death.
Our forefathers were also promised this resurrection before it.
Ancient fables are nothing but the fables, lies, and jokes of the ancients.

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “To whom belong the earth and all those on it, if you ˹really˺ know?”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘To whom does the earth and whoever is in it of creatures belong if you truly knew?’ their Creator and Owner.

hype_questions: What is the origin of the earth and all living beings if one truly understands their nature?
Who is responsible for the creation and sustenance of the universe?
What is the ultimate authority behind the existence of all creatures?
propositions: The Prophet asked about the ownership of the earth and its inhabitants.
If one truly knew, they would understand that the earth and its creatures belong to their Creator and Owner.
The Creator and Owner are responsible for the creation and sustenance of the universe.

source_text:
Verse: They will reply, “To Allah!” Say, “Why are you not then mindful?”

Tafsir: They will say ‘To God’. Say to them ‘Will you not then remember?’ tadhakkarūna the second tā’ of tatadhakkarūna has been assimilated with the dhāl will you not then be admonished and so realise that the One Who has the power to originate creation also has the power to resurrect after death?

hype_questions: Will you not then remember your Creator?
Can you not be admonished and realize the power of Allah?
Do you not know that Allah is the One Who has the power to originate creation?
propositions: They will reply, 'To God'.
Say to them, 'Will you not then remember?'
The One Who has the power to originate creation also has the power to resurrect after death.

source_text:
Verse: ˹And˺ ask ˹them˺, “Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?”

Tafsir: Say ‘Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne?’ that is the throne kursī.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's throne?
Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Mighty Throne?
What is the significance of the kursī in Islamic theology?
propositions: Allah is the Lord of the seven heavens.
Allah is the Lord of the Great Throne (kursī).
The kursī is a symbol of Allah's power and majesty.

source_text:
Verse: They will reply, “Allah.” Say, “Will you not then fear ˹Him˺?”

Tafsir: They will say ‘God’. Say ‘Will you not then be God-fearing?’ will you then not be wary of worshipping things other than Him?

hype_questions: Can one truly claim to be God if they are not cautious about worshipping other things?
Is it possible for someone to be considered a true believer without showing fear of Allah?
What happens when someone claims to be God but is actually worshipping other deities?
propositions: They will reply, 'Allah'.
Say, 'Will you not then fear Him?'
Will you then not be wary of worshipping things other than Him?

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them also,˺ “In Whose Hands is the authority over all things, protecting ˹all˺ while none can protect against Him, if you ˹really˺ know?”

Tafsir: Say ‘In whose hand is the dominion the possession of all things the final tā’ in malakūt is hyperbolic and who protects while from Him there is no protection if you know?’

hype_questions: What is the ultimate authority behind all things?
Who can protect against an all-powerful being?
Can anyone truly understand the nature of their protector?
propositions: The dominion over all things belongs to a single entity.
This entity protects and safeguards all things.
There is no protection or defense against this entity if one truly understands its power.

source_text:
Verse: They will reply, “Allah.” Say, “How are you then so deluded?”

Tafsir: They will say ‘God.’ a variant reading for Allāh ‘God’ in both instances verses 87 and 89 has li’Llāh ‘to God’ which is in keeping with the sense of ‘to whom belongs what has been mentioned?’. Say ‘How then are you bewitched?’ how then are you duped and turned away from the truth the worship of God alone in other words ‘How do you envisage all this to be invalid?’.

hype_questions: How can one claim to worship a deity other than the one true God?
What is the nature of deception and bewitchment in the context of religious devotion?
Can one truly turn away from the truth and still expect salvation?
propositions: They will reply, 'Allah.'
Say, 'How are you then so deluded?'
They will say 'God.'
a variant reading for Allāh 'God' in both instances verses 87 and 89 has li’Llāh 'to God' which is in keeping with the sense of 'to whom belongs what has been mentioned?'

Verse: As for female and male fornicators, give each of them one hundred lashes, and do not let pity for them make you lenient in ˹enforcing˺ the law of Allah, if you ˹truly˺ believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a number of believers witness their punishment.

Tafsir: As for the fornicatress and the fornicator that is of those not in wedlock — because those in wedlock are stoned according to the Sunna the al in al-zāniya ‘the fornicatress’ and al-zānī ‘the fornicator’ according to some mentioned opinions is a relative particle; the clause al-zāniyatu wa’l-zānī is a subject and because of its similarity to a conditional the fā’ has been inserted into the predicate which is the following fa’jlidū strike each of them a hundred lashes a hundred strikes one says jaladahu to mean daraba jildahu ‘he struck him on the skin’. According to the Sunna in addition to this punishment there is also banishment for a whole year. The slave however receives half of the mentioned punishment. And do not let any pity for them overcome you in God’s religion that is to say in the fulfilment of His rulings by disregarding any part of their prescribed punishment if you believe in God and the Last Day namely the Day of Resurrection in this statement there is an incitement to abide by what was mentioned before the conditional above and it also constitutes the response to the latter or at least is an indication of the response to it. And let their punishment the flogging be witnessed by a group of the believers — some say that this should be a group of three; some say four as in the number of witnesses testifying to an act of fornication.

This was revealed when the poor among the Emigrants resolved to marry the wealthy whores of the idolaters so that they the women would provide for them. Verse: Indeed, those who came up with that ˹outrageous˺ slander are a group of you. Do not think this is bad for you. Rather, it is good for you. he will suffer a tremendous punishment.

Tafsir: Truly those who initiated the slander the worst calumny against ‘Ā’isha — mother of the believers may God be pleased with her — accusing her of fornication are a band from among yourselves a group from among the believers. She said that these were Hassān b. Thābit ‘Abd Allāh b. Ubayy Mistah b. Uthātha and Hamna bt. Jahsh. Do not suppose O you believers other than the mentioned band that it is bad for you; rather it is good for you for God will reward you for it and reveal ‘Ā’isha’s innocence and the innocence of the one who is supposed to have committed it with her namely Safwān b. al-Mu‘attal. She ‘Ā’isha related ‘I accompanied the Prophet s during a raid and this was after the requirement to wear the veil had been revealed. When he was through with it the raid he headed back to the campsite and one night having drawn close to Medina he announced that all should march off home. So I walked a distance away from the campsite and relieved myself. But when I came back to the campsite I realised that my necklace ‘iqd meaning qilāda had snapped. So I went back to look for it. In the meantime they had strapped my litter’ — in which one rides — ‘thinking that I was inside for in those days women were slight and ate very small portions ‘ulqa. Finally I found my necklace but when I went back to where I had been staying overnight they had already departed. I sat in the place where I had camped; I assumed that the group would notice my absence and come back for me. But my eyes were overcome by drowsiness and I fell asleep. Safwān had pitched camp behind the army to rest for some of the night ‘arrasa then set off while it was still night until he reached the site of the camp. He saw what looked like a person sleeping and recognised me when he eventually saw me having seen me on numerous occasions before the requirement of the veil. I woke up to the sound of him saying ‘To God we belong and to Him we shall surely return’ innā li’Llāhi wa-innā ilayhi rāji‘ūn for he had recognised me. So I concealed my face with my gown jilbāb — in other words I covered it up with my wrap mulā’a.

hype_questions: What is the punishment for those who initiate slander against a believer?
How did ‘Ā’isha prove her innocence after being accused of fornication?

propositions: Those who initiated slander against ‘Ā’isha are a group of believers.
Accusing someone of fornication is the worst calumny against them.
God will reward those who defend the innocent and reveal their innocence.
‘Ā’isha accompanied the Prophet during a raid after the requirement to wear the veil had been revealed.
She relieved herself away from the campsite due to her necklace breaking.
Safwān recognized ‘Ā’isha when he saw her sleeping behind the army's campsite.
God belongs to those who say 'To God we belong and to Him we shall surely return'.

Verse: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, and not to reveal their adornments except to their husbands, their fathers, their fathers-in-law, their sons, their stepsons, their brothers, their brothers’ sons or sisters’ sons, their fellow women, those ˹bondwomen˺ in their possession, male attendants with no desire, or children who are still unaware of women’s nakedness. Let them not stomp their feet, drawing attention to their hidden adornments. Turn to Allah in repentance all together, O  believers, so that you may be successful.

Tafsir: And tell believing women to lower their gaze away from what is not lawful for them to look at and to guard their private parts from what is not lawful for them to do with them and not to display their adornment except for what is apparent namely the face and the hands which may be seen by a stranger when there is no danger of either or both falling into temptation — this being one of two opinions. The second of these is that even this is forbidden because there is a presumption that these parts will cause temptation — and this is the preferred opinion if one must settle this topic with a definitive opinion; and let them draw their veils over their bosoms that is let them cover up their heads necks and chests with veils and not reveal their hidden adornment namely all that is other than the face and the hands except to their husbands bu‘ūl is the plural form of ba‘l ‘male spouse’ or their fathers or their husbands’ fathers or their sons or their husbands’ sons or their brothers or their brothers’ sons or their sisters’ sons or their women or what their right hands own all of whom are permitted to look thereat except for the part from the navel down to the knees which is unlawful for any other than their husbands to see; ‘their women’ however excludes disbelieving women for it is not permitted for Muslim women to reveal themselves to these; ‘what their right hands own’ comprises slaves; or such men who are dependant on what food may be left over not ghayri read as an adjective or read ghayra as an exceptive possessing any sexual desire not those men who are in sexual need of women so for example those whose male member cannot become erect; or children who are not yet aware of women’s private parts in the context of sexual intercourse and so to these they may reveal themselves except for that part from the navel to the knees. And do not let them thump with their feet to make known their hidden ornaments as in a rattling anklet and the like. And rally to God in repentance O believers repenting of the occasions on which you may have looked at what is forbidden to look at of such parts and otherwise so that you might be prosperous so that you might be saved from such sinful acts when your repentance thereof is accepted — in this verse the prevalent address is to males over females.

propositions: Believing women should lower their gaze away from what is not lawful for them to look at.

Believing women should not thump with their feet to make known their hidden ornaments.
Believers should repent of looking at what is forbidden to look at and strive to be prosperous and saved from sinful acts.

Verse: And let those who do not have the means to marry keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them out of His bounty. And if any of those ˹bondspeople˺ in your possession desires a deed of emancipation, make it possible for them, if you find goodness in them. And give them some of Allah’s wealth which He has granted you. Do not force your ˹slave˺ girls into prostitution for your own worldly gains while they wish to remain chaste. And if someone coerces them, then after such a coercion Allah is certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful ˹to them˺.

Tafsir: And let those who cannot find the means to marry be continent those who do not have the bridal money or the means for financial support needed for marriage let them restrain themselves from fornication until God enriches them until He improves their means out of His bounty and they marry. And those who seek a written contract of emancipation from among those whom your right hand owns of male slaves and female slaves contract with them accordingly if you know in them any good such as trustworthiness and the ability to earn income in order to fulfil the amount stated in the written contract which might be worded for example thus ‘I contract you for the amount of two thousand to be paid over a period of two months at one thousand a month and if you fulfill this you are a free man’ and the other would say ‘I accept’; and give them — this is a command for the slaves’ owners — out of the wealth of God which He has given you in the measure that will help them to fulfill their commitment to you the action of ītā’ ‘giving’ here suggests that some of the amount to which they have committed themselves should be waived. And do not compel your slave-girls your handmaidens to prostitution fornication when they desire to be chaste to abstain therefrom this ‘desire’ is the cause of the act of ‘compulsion’ so that the statement is not properly a conditional that you may seek through such compulsion the transient things of the life of this world — this was revealed regarding ‘Abd Allāh b. Ubayy who used to force his slave-girls to earn money through fornication. And should anyone compel them then surely God after their compulsion will be Forgiving to these slave-girls Merciful to them.

propositions: Those who cannot afford marriage should remain chaste until Allah provides them with means.
Slaves can be emancipated through a written contract if they demonstrate good behavior.

Verse: Indeed, We have sent down to you clear revelations, along with examples of those who had gone before you, and a lesson to the God-fearing.

Tafsir: And verily We have revealed to you clear verses read mubayyanāt or mubayyināt in this sūra verses in which if read mubayyanāt what is mentioned is already clear or which if read mubayyināt are clarificatory of that which is mentioned and an example a curious tale namely that of ‘Ā’isha of those who passed away before you that is to say of their kind of example that is an example of their curious tales such as the tales of Joseph and Mary and an admonition for those who fear God in what He exalted be He has said And do not let any pity for them overcome you in God’s religion verse 2 above; and Why when you first heard about it did the believing men and women not think good of themselves… to the end of verse 12 above; and And why when you heard it did you not say … to the end of verse 16 above; and God admonishes you lest you should ever repeat the like of it … to the end of verse 17 above. This admonition is specifically for ‘those who fear God’ because they are the ones to benefit from such an admonition.

hype_questions: What is the significance of clear verses in the Quran?
How does the Quran provide examples for believers to follow?
Why is it important for Muslims to fear God and avoid repeating past mistakes?
propositions: The Quran has been sent down with clear revelations.
Examples from before you can be found in this sura.
God-fearing individuals should not let pity overcome them in their religion.
Believers should reflect on their initial reactions to the revelation and avoid repeating past mistakes.
Those who fear God are the ones who benefit from admonition.

source_text:
Verse: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light whose oil would almost glow, even without being touched by fire. Light upon light! Allah guides whoever He wills to His light. And Allah sets forth parables for humanity. For Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

Tafsir: God is the Light of the heavens and the earth in other words He illumines both of them with the sun and the moon. The likeness of His Light that is the description of it as it resides in the heart of a believer is as a niche wherein is a lamp. The lamp is in a glass — this glass is the case for the lantern and the misbāh is the torch that is the wick that is lit; al-mishkāt is a recess that does not penetrate to the other side in other words the tube inside the lantern the glass with the light inside it is as it were a glittering star that is a light-giving star read dirrī’un or durrī’un derived from al-dar‘ ‘to repel’ because it repels darkness; or read durriyyun derived from al-durr ‘pearls’ kindled is this lamp read past tense tawaqqada; a variant reading has the imperfect tense of awqada in the passive voice yūqadu; another reading has tūqadu in which case the reference is to al-zujāja ‘the glass’ from the oil of a Blessed Tree an olive neither of the east nor of the west but in between the two so that no harmful cold or heat affects it; whose oil would almost glow forth of itself though no fire touched it because of the extent of its purity. Light by Him upon light by fire; the light of God is His guidance of the believer light upon the light of faith. God guides to His Light that is to the religion of Islam whom He will. And God strikes He illustrates similitudes for men by approximating such similitudes to their comprehension so that they might take heed and believe; and God is Knower of all things including knowledge of how to strike similitudes.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's Light?
How does Allah guide His believers?
What is the significance of parables in Islam?
propositions: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.
His light shines even without being touched by fire.
God guides whoever He wills to His light.
The likeness of Allah's Light is like a niche wherein is a lamp.
The lamp is in a glass, which is like a glittering star that repels darkness.
Light upon light; God guides to His Light that is to the religion of Islam whom He will.
God strikes similitudes for men by approximating such similitudes to their comprehension so that they might take heed and believe.

source_text:
Verse: ˹That light shines˺ through houses ˹of worship˺ which Allah has ordered to be raised, and where His Name is mentioned. He is glorified there morning and evening

Tafsir: In houses fī buyūtin is semantically connected to yusabbihu ‘glorify’ that will follow whose status God has allowed to be raised houses He has allowed to be venerated and wherein His Name is remembered through the affirmation of His Oneness therein they make glorifications read yusabbahu ‘glorifications are made’ or yusabbihu meaning ‘therein pray’ to Him in the mornings al-ghuduww is a verbal noun meaning al-ghadawāt ‘the early mornings’ and the evenings the darkness after sunset

hype_questions: What are the conditions for a house to be considered a place of worship?
How does Allah's Name being mentioned in a house affect its status?
What is the significance of glorifying Allah in the early mornings and evenings?
propositions: Allah's light shines through houses ordered by Him to be raised.
In such houses, His Name is mentioned and He is glorified morning and evening.
The affirmation of God's Oneness is made therein, leading to glorifications or prayers.

source_text:
Verse: by men who are not distracted—either by buying or selling—from Allah’s remembrance, or performing prayer, or paying alms-tax. They fear a Day when hearts and eyes will tremble,

Tafsir: men rijālun the subject of the verb yusabbihu ‘make glorifications’; if the passive is read yusabbahu ‘glorifications are made’ it rijālun ‘men’ substitutes for the impersonal subject of lahu ‘to Him’ so that rijālun ‘men’ is the subject of an implied verb in response to an implied question as if one had asked who makes glorifications to Him? whom neither trading purchase nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God and the observance of prayer the final hā’ of iqāmat ‘the observance’ has been omitted to facilitate the reading and payment of the alms. They fear a day when hearts and eyes will be tossed about in fear the hearts tossed about between the hope of deliverance and the fear of destruction and the eyes to the right and to the left out of anxiety — this is the Day of Resurrection;

hype_questions: What happens to those who are distracted from remembrance and prayer?
How do people respond to the Day of Resurrection?
What is the state of hearts and eyes on that day?
propositions: Men who are not distracted by buying or selling, or performing prayer, or paying alms-tax fear a Day when hearts and eyes will tremble.
Those who make glorifications to God are not distracted from His remembrance or the observance of prayer.
The hearts of those who fear that Day will be tossed about between hope and fear, while their eyes will be out of anxiety.
That Day is the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: ˹hoping˺ that Allah may reward them according to the best of their deeds, and increase them out of His grace. And Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit.

Tafsir: so that God may reward them for the best of what they did that is reward them the reward for it ahsana means husna and give them more out of His bounty; and God provides whomever He will without any reckoning one says of someone yunfiqu bi-ghayri hisābin to mean that such a person is so generous that it is as though he does not need to reckon what he spends.

hype_questions: What is the best way to earn God's reward?
How can someone be so generous that they don't need to reckon what they spend?
What does it mean to receive more out of God's grace?
propositions: Allah may reward them according to the best of their deeds.
God provides for whoever He wills without limit.
A person is so generous that he does not need to reckon what he spends.

source_text:
Verse: As for the disbelievers, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert, which the thirsty perceive as water, but when they approach it, they find it to be nothing. Instead, they find Allah there ˹in the Hereafter, ready˺ to settle their account. And Allah is swift in reckoning.

Tafsir: And as for those who disbelieve their works are like a mirage in a plain qī‘a is the plural of qā‘ that is to say fulāt ‘an open space’. A mirage is a kind of radiation which one might observe therein at midday during extreme heat resembling running water — which the thirsty man supposes to be water until he comes to it and finds it to be nothing like what he had supposed. Likewise is the case of the disbeliever who supposes that his deeds such as some voluntary alms will benefit him; but when he dies and comes before his Lord he will not find his deed in other words it will be of no benefit to him; and he finds God there namely in the place of his deeds Who pays him his account in full that is He requites him for it in this world; and God is swift at reckoning that is at requiting.

hype_questions: What happens to a person's deeds after they die?
Will good actions in this life guarantee a positive outcome in the afterlife?
How is one's account settled with Allah?
propositions: The deeds of disbelievers are like a mirage in a desert.
Disbelievers will find that their works are of no benefit to them in the afterlife.
Allah pays individuals for their deeds in this world and requites them in the afterlife.
God is swift in reckoning.

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹their deeds are˺ like the darkness in a deep sea, covered by waves upon waves, topped by ˹dark˺ clouds. Darkness upon darkness! If one stretches out their hand, they can hardly see it. And whoever Allah does not bless with light will have no light!

Tafsir: Or it is that those who disbelieve their evil deeds are as the manifold darkness on a deep sea covered by a billow above which that is above which billow there is another billow above which second billow there are clouds these being the manifold layers of darkness one on top of another the darkness of the sea the darkness of the first billow the darkness of the second together with the darkness of the clouds. When he an observer holds out his hand in such layers of darkness he can scarcely see it in other words he would not even come close to seeing it. And he whom God has not granted any light has no light that is to say he whom God does not guide cannot be guided.

hype_questions: What happens to the deeds of those who disbelieve?
How can one see their own hand in a deep sea of darkness?
Who is guided by God?
propositions: Their deeds are like the darkness in a deep sea, covered by waves upon waves, topped by dark clouds.
If one stretches out their hand, they can hardly see it.
And whoever Allah does not bless with light will have no light!

source_text:
Verse: Do you not see that Allah is glorified by all those in the heavens and the earth, even the birds as they soar? Each ˹instinctively˺ knows their manner of prayer and glorification. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all they do.

Tafsir: Have you not seen that God is glorified by all who are in the heavens and the earth prayer being one form of glorification and the birds tayr is the plural of tā’ir between the heaven and the earth spreading their wings? sāffātin is a circumstantial qualifier. Of each one of them He God verily knows its prayer and its glorification; and God knows what they do — the statement is predominantly directed to rational beings.

hype_questions: Does God's glorification extend to all creatures, regardless of their form or function?
Can animals be said to 'pray' in the way that humans do?
Is God's knowledge limited to rational beings, or does it encompass all forms of life?
propositions: Allah is glorified by all those in the heavens and the earth.
Prayer is one form of glorification.
The birds know their manner of prayer and glorification instinctively.
God has perfect knowledge of all they do.
God knows what each creature does, including its prayer and glorification.
Sāffātin is a circumstantial qualifier used to describe the birds' movement between heaven and earth.

source_text:
Verse: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And to Allah is the final return.

Tafsir: And to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth the treasuries of rain provision and vegetation and with God is the journey’s end the final return.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate destination of all creation?
Who holds the power over the heavens and the earth?

propositions: To Allah belongs the kingdom of the heavens.
To Allah belongs the kingdom of the earth.
And to Allah are the treasuries of rain provision.
And to Allah are the treasuries of vegetation.
With Allah is the journey’s end.
The final return is with Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Do you not see that Allah gently drives the clouds, then joins them together, piling them up into masses, from which you see raindrops come forth? And He sends down from the sky mountains ˹of clouds˺ loaded with hail, pouring it on whoever He wills and averting it from whoever He wills. The flash of the clouds’ lightning nearly takes away eyesight.

Tafsir: Have you not seen how God drives the clouds moves them along gently then composes them joining some with others and making scattered pieces as one then piles them up some on top of others whereat you see the rain issuing from the midst of them from specific outlets in them? And He sends down from the heaven out of the mountains min jibālin min is extra that are therein in the heaven fīhā substitutes for mina’l-samā’i ‘from the heaven’ with the repetition of a genitive preposition hail that is He sends down some hail and smites with it whom He will and turns it away from whom He will. The brilliance of its lightning its flashing would almost take away the eyes that look at it in other words it would almost snatching them away.

hype_questions: Does Allah control the weather?
Can God send down hail from the sky?
How does Allah's lightning affect human vision?
propositions: Allah drives the clouds gently.
He joins them together and piles them up into masses.
From these masses, raindrops come forth.
God sends down mountains of clouds loaded with hail from the sky.
He pours hail on whoever He wills and turns it away from whoever He wills.
The flash of the clouds' lightning nearly takes away eyesight.

source_text:
Verse: Allah alternates the day and night. Surely in this is a lesson for people of insight.

Tafsir: God alternates the night and the day that is He brings one in place of the other. Surely in that alternation there is a lesson an indication for those who see those possessing insight an indication of God’s power exalted be He.

hype_questions: What is the lesson in Allah's alternation between day and night?
How does God's alternation between day and night demonstrate His power?
What insight can be gained from observing the cycle of day and night?
propositions: Allah alternates the day and night.
The alternation between day and night is a lesson for people of insight.
God brings one in place of the other, demonstrating His power.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah has created from water every living creature. Some of them crawl on their bellies, some walk on two legs, and some walk on four. Allah creates whatever He wills. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: And God has created every beast that is every animal from fluid from a sperm-drop. Among them are some that creep upon their bellies such as snakes and reptiles and among them are some that walk on two feet such as human beings and birds and among them are some that walk on four such as four-legged beasts and cattle. God creates whatever He will. Truly God has power over all things.

How does Allah create different types of animals?

Some animals crawl on their bellies, some walk on two legs, and some walk on four.
God creates whatever He wills.
God has power over all things.

source_text:
Verse: And the hypocrites say, “We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey.” Then a group of them turns away soon after that. These are not ˹true˺ believers.

Tafsir: And they the hypocrites say ‘We believe in we affirm the truth of God of His Oneness and the Messenger Muhammad (s) and we obey’ them in what rulings they God and Muhammad give. Then after that a party of them turn away they are averse to it and those those who are averse they are not believers as believers should be believers whose hearts agree with the words of their tongues.

How do hypocrites deceive themselves and others?
