True believers have hearts that agree with their words, whereas hypocrites are averse to the truth.
Obedience to Allah's Messenger is not enough; it must be accompanied by a genuine commitment to his teachings.

Rather those they are the wrongdoers for shunning him.

How do believers respond to being summoned by God and His Messenger?

The response of believers is a demonstration of their faith.

source_text:
Verse: For whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, and fears Allah and is mindful of Him, then it is they who will ˹truly˺ triumph.

Tafsir: And he who obeys God and His Messenger and fears God and fears Him read yattaqh or yattaqhi by being obedient to Him those they are the winners of Paradise.

hype_questions: What is the condition for a person to be considered a winner of Paradise?
How does obedience to Allah and His Messenger impact one's spiritual journey?
What role does fear play in achieving success according to Islamic teachings?

source_text:
Verse: They swear by Allah their most solemn oaths that if you ˹O Prophet˺ were to command them, they would certainly march forth ˹in Allah’s cause˺. Say, “˹You˺ do not ˹have to˺ swear; your obedience is well known!” Surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do.”

Tafsir: And they swear by God solemn oaths that if you order them to participate in the struggle they will surely go forth. Say to them ‘Do not swear! Acknowledged obedience to the Prophet is better than the oaths to which you are not true. Surely God is Aware of what you do’ when you say you will obey but act otherwise.

Why does God require acknowledgment of obedience from believers?

Acknowledged obedience to the Prophet is better than the oaths to which you are not true.
God is Aware of what you do when you say you will obey but act otherwise.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then he is only responsible for his duty And if you obey him, you will be ˹rightly˺ guided. The Messenger’s duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Obey God and obey the Messenger.’ But if you turn away from obedience to him tawallaw ‘you turn away’ one of the two tā’ letters in tatawallaw has been omitted; an address to them know that he is only responsible for that with which he has been charged of conveying the Message and you are responsible for that with which you have been charged of obedience to him. And if you obey him you will be rightly guided. And the Messenger’s duty is only to convey the Message clearly’.

hype_questions: What happens when we obey the Messenger?
Who is responsible for conveying the Message?
How will I be guided if I obey the Messenger?

If you turn away from obedience to him, he is only responsible for his duty.
If you obey him, you will be rightly guided.
The Messenger's duty is only to deliver the message clearly.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has promised those of you who believe and do good that He will certainly make them successors in the land, as He did with those before them; and will surely establish for them their faith which He has chosen for them; and will indeed change their fear into security—˹provided that˺ they worship Me, associating nothing with Me. But whoever disbelieves after this ˹promise˺, it is they who will be the rebellious.

Tafsir: God has promised those of you who believe and perform righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the earth in place of the disbelievers just as He made those Children of Israel who were before them successors in place of the ruling tyrants the verb may be read as active istakhlafa ‘He made them successors’ or as passive istukhlifa ‘were made successors’ and He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them namely the religion of Islam by making it prevail over all religions and enrich them throughout the land so that they become masters thereof and that He will give them in exchange read wa-la-yubdilannahum or wa-la-yubaddilannahum after their fear of disbelievers security. And God fulfilled His promise to them in the way mentioned and He praises them with His words ‘They worship Me without associating anything with Me’ ya‘budūnanī lā yushrikūna bī shay’an is an independent new sentence standing as a justification for His promise. And whoever is ungrateful after that bestowal of grace from among them whoever is ungrateful for it those they are the immoral. The first to show ingratitude for that grace of God were the murderers of ‘Uthmān b. ‘Affān may God be pleased with him and they began to kill one another henceforth after having been brothers.

hype_questions: What is the promise of Allah to those who believe and do good?
How will Allah establish their faith for them?
What will happen to those who disbelieve after receiving this promise?
propositions: Allah has promised those of you who believe and do good that He will make them successors in the land.
He will establish for them their faith which He has chosen for them.
He will change their fear into security—provided that they worship Me, associating nothing with Me.

source_text:
Verse: Moreover, establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and obey the Messenger, so you may be shown mercy.

Tafsir: And establish prayer and pay the alms and obey the Messenger that perhaps you may find mercy that is to say do so hoping for mercy.

hype_questions: What are the three essential acts of worship mentioned in this verse?
How can following these commands lead to receiving mercy from Allah?
What is the significance of obedience to the Messenger in achieving spiritual growth?

Pay alms-tax.
Obey the Messenger.

source_text:
Verse: Do not think ˹O Prophet˺ that the disbelievers can escape in the land. The Fire will be their home. Indeed, what an evil destination!

Tafsir: And do not suppose read tahsabanna or yahsabanna the subject of the verb being the Messenger that those who disbelieve can escape Us in the land by eluding us. For their abode will be their return will be to the Fire and it is surely an evil destination it is an evil place of return.

hype_questions: Can believers escape the wrath of Allah?
What is the ultimate destination for those who disbelieve?
How will Allah treat those who reject His message?

The Fire is their abode and an evil destination.
Those who disbelieve will return to the Fire, which is an evil place of return.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Let those ˹bondspeople˺ in your possession and those of you who are still under age ask for your permission ˹to come in˺ at three times: before dawn prayer, when you take off your ˹outer˺ clothes at noon, and after the late evening prayer. ˹These are˺ three times of privacy for you. Other than these times, there is no blame on you or them to move freely, attending to one another. This is how Allah makes the revelations clear to you, for Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: O you who believe let those whom your right hands own of male slaves and female slaves and those of you who have not reached puberty from among the free men and who have not become sexually aware of women ask leave of you three times at three times of the day before the dawn prayer and when you put off your garments at noon and after the night prayer. These are three periods of privacy for you read thalāthu ‘awrātin lakum with nominative inflection as the predicate of an implied subject followed by a genitive annexation with the annexed term standing in place thereof of the predicate in other words the implied predicate followed by the annexation is hiya awqāt ‘these are times of …’; or read thalātha ‘awrātin lakum in the accusative the implication being that awqāta is itself in the accusative as a substitute for the syntactical status of what precedes it in place of which stands the annexed term. It is because clothes are taken off that private parts are revealed during such periods. Neither you nor they namely slaves and young boys would be at fault in entering upon you without asking leave at other times that is after the three times of day specified; they frequent you to provide service as some of you do with others this sentence corroborates the preceding one. So just as He has clarified what has been mentioned God clarifies for you the signs the rulings; and God is Knower of the affairs of His creatures Wise in what He has ordained for them. It is said that the ‘permission’ verse āyat al-isti’idhān was abrogated; but it is also said that it was not abrogated but that people thought little of neglecting to seek permission in such situations.

hype_questions: What are the three times of day when permission is required from believers to interact with slaves or young boys?
Why is it important to seek permission during these specific times?
How does Allah clarify the rules and signs for believers?
propositions: Believers should ask for permission before interacting with slaves or young boys at three specified times.
These times are considered private moments for believers, and seeking permission is necessary to avoid any blame.
Allah has clarified the revelations to make it clear that these rules apply to all believers.

source_text:
Verse: And when your children reach the age of puberty, let them seek permission ˹to come in˺, as their seniors do. This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you, for Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And when the children among you O free men reach puberty let them seek permission at all times just as those now older free men sought permission before them. So God clarifies His signs for you and God is Knower Wise.

hype_questions: What is the significance of seeking permission during puberty?
How does Allah clarify His revelations to humans?
What are the benefits of following the example of older free men?
propositions: When children reach puberty, they should seek permission at all times.
Allah clarifies His signs for those who follow the example of older free men.
God is All-Knowing and All-Wise.

source_text:
Verse: As for elderly women past the age of marriage, there is no blame on them if they take off their ˹outer˺ garments, without revealing their adornments. But it is better for them if they avoid this ˹altogether˺. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Tafsir: And as for menopausal women who have ceased to menstruate or to bear children because of old age who do not expect to marry for that reason they would not be at fault if they put off their clothes such a robe a cloak or the facial mask over a head veil in such a way as not to display adornment that is hidden such as a necklace a bracelet or an anklet; but to refrain from doing so by not putting them off is better for them; and God is Hearer of what you say Knower of what is in your hearts.

hype_questions: Can menopausal women be held accountable for their attire?
Is it acceptable for menopausal women to remove their outer garments without revealing their adornments?
What is the best course of action for menopausal women regarding their clothing?
propositions: Elderly women past the age of marriage can take off their outer garments without revealing their adornments.
It is better for elderly women to avoid removing their outer garments altogether.
Menopausal women who do not expect to marry due to old age should refrain from putting on outer garments that reveal hidden adornments.

source_text:
Verse: There is no restriction on the blind, or the disabled, or the sick. This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you, so perhaps you will understand.

Tafsir: There is no blame upon the blind nor any blame upon the lame nor any blame upon the sick that they be one’s table companions nor any blame upon yourselves if you eat from your own houses that is from the houses of your offspring or your fathers’ houses or your mothers’ houses or your brothers’ houses or your sisters’ houses or the houses of your paternal uncles or the houses of your paternal aunts or the houses of your maternal uncles or the houses of your maternal aunts or from that whereof you hold the keys from that which you safeguard on behalf of others or from those of your faithful friends sadīq is so called because he is ‘faithful’ sadaqa to you in his affection. In other words one is permitted to eat from the houses of those mentioned even if they are not present provided that they consent to it. You would not be at fault whether you eat together in a group or separately individually ashtāt is the plural of shatt. This was revealed concerning those who felt inhibited about eating alone and who when they could not find a table companion they would refrain from eating. But when you enter houses that are yours houses wherein there is no one bid peace to yourselves say ‘Peace be upon us and upon God’s righteous servants’ for the angels will return your greeting; and if there is family therein bid peace to them with a salutation tahiyyatan is the verbal noun from hayyā ‘he saluted’ from God blessed and good and for which one is rewarded. So God clarifies the signs for you that is to say He sets out for you in detail the ritual ceremonies of your religion that perhaps you might comprehend in order for you to understand this.

hype_questions: Can I eat from my own house if I have a guest with a disability?
Is it okay to share food with someone who is blind or sick?
What happens when I enter a house where there are no family members present?
propositions: There is no restriction on the blind, or the disabled, or the sick.
One is permitted to eat from the houses of those mentioned even if they are not present provided that they consent to it.
When entering a house, bid peace to yourselves and the family therein, for the angels will return your greeting.

source_text:
Verse: The ˹true˺ believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a public matter, they do not leave without his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission ˹O Prophet˺ are the ones who ˹truly˺ believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for a private matter, grant permission to whoever you wish and ask Allah’s forgiveness for them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: Only they are believers who believe in God and His Messenger and who when they are with him namely the Messenger in a collective affair such as during the Friday sermon do not leave when they have an excuse until they have asked leave of him. Truly those who ask leave of you — it is they who believe in God and His Messenger. So when they ask leave of you for some affair some matter of theirs give permission to whom you will of them to leave and ask God to forgive them. Truly God is Forgiving Merciful.

hype_questions: What are the conditions for a believer to be considered as such?
How should believers behave when they are with the Prophet in a public matter?
Can believers ask permission to leave during a private matter?
propositions: The true believers are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger.
When believers are with the Prophet in a public matter, they do not leave without his permission.
Believers who ask for permission are those who truly believe in Allah and His Messenger.
Grant permission to whoever you wish when asking for permission for a private matter.
Ask Allah's forgiveness for them when granting permission for a private matter.
God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: Do not treat the Messenger’s summons to you ˹as lightly˺ as your summons to one another. So let those who disobey his orders beware, for an affliction may befall them, or a painful torment may overtake them.

Tafsir: Do not among yourselves consider the calling of the Messenger to be like your calling of one another by saying ‘O Muhammad!’ s but say ‘O Prophet of God’ or ‘O Messenger of God!’ gently respectfully and in a low voice. Verily God knows those of you who slip away surreptitiously that is those who leave the mosque secretly during the sermon without asking leave hiding behind something qad ‘verily’ is for confirmation. So let those who contravene His command that is God’s command or that of His Messenger beware lest an ordeal a trial befall them or there befall them a painful chastisement in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What happens if I disrespect the Prophet's summons?
Can I get in trouble for not showing respect to the Prophet during prayers?
How can I avoid facing punishment from God?
propositions: Do not treat the Messenger’s summons to you as lightly.
Say 'O Prophet of God' or 'O Messenger of God!' gently respectfully and in a low voice.
God knows those who slip away surreptitiously that is those who leave the mosque secretly during the sermon without asking leave.
Let those who contravene His command beware lest an ordeal a trial befall them or there befall them a painful chastisement in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He knows well what you stand for. And ˹on˺ the Day all will be returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. For Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

Tafsir: Lo! surely to God belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth by way of possession creation and servitude. He is ever aware of how you O you who are obligated to the prescriptions of the Law are behaving with regard to faith or hypocrisy and He knows the day when they shall be returned to Him there is a shift here from the second person address to that of the third person in other words He knows when this day will be — He will inform them thereupon of what they did of good and evil and God is Knower of all things which they do and otherwise.

hype_questions: What will Allah do with those who are obedient to Him?
How will Allah judge those who have been hypocrites?
What is the ultimate fate of those who have lived a life of faith?
propositions: Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth.
He knows well what you stand for.
On the Day of Judgment, Allah will inform them of what they did.
God is Knower of all things which they do.

source_text:
Verse: Blessed is the One Who sent down the Standard

Tafsir: Blessed exalted is He Who revealed the Criterion al-furqān the Qur’ān — called thus al-furqān because it has discriminated faraqa between truth and falsehood — to His servant Muhammad (s) that he may be to all the worlds to mankind and the jinn but not the angels a warner a threatening of God’s chastisement.

hype_questions: What is the name of the Qur’ān that has discriminated between truth and falsehood?
Who revealed the Criterion al-furqān to His servant Muhammad (s)?
What role does Muhammad (s) play in relation to God's chastisement?
propositions: God sent down the Standard.
The Qur’ān is called al-furqān because it has discriminated between truth and falsehood.
Muhammad (s) was revealed the Criterion al-furqān by God for warning mankind and jinn but not angels.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Allah is˺ the One to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, Who has never had ˹any˺ offspring, nor does He have a partner in ˹governing˺ the kingdom. He has created everything, ordaining it precisely.

Tafsir: He to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and Who has not taken a son nor has He any partner in sovereignty; and He created everything which was meant to be created and then determined it in a precise measure He fashioned it in a balanced form.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's sovereignty?
How does Allah create and govern the universe?
Is Allah alone in His creation?
propositions: Allah is the One to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth.
Allah has never had offspring.
Allah does not have a partner in governing the kingdom.
Allah created everything precisely.
Allah fashioned everything in a balanced form.

source_text:
Verse: Yet they have taken besides Him gods who cannot create anything but are themselves created. Nor can they protect or benefit themselves. Nor can they control life, death, or resurrection.

Tafsir: Yet they the disbelievers have taken besides Him that is besides God in other words other than Him gods from among the idols who create nothing but have themselves been created and who possess no harm for themselves that is the power to repel it nor any benefit that is the power to attract it nor do they possess any power over death or life that is nor do they have the power to make a person die or to give him life or resurrection that is nor do they have power to raise the dead.

hype_questions: Can idols create anything?
Do idols possess any power over life and death?
Can idols give people life or resurrection?
propositions: There are gods besides God who cannot create anything.
These gods have themselves been created.
They possess no harm for themselves.
They possess no benefit for themselves.
They do not possess any power over death.
They do not possess any power over life.
They do not have the power to make a person die.
They do not have the power to give people life.
They do not have the power to raise the dead.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers say, “This ˹Quran˺ is nothing but a fabrication which he made up with the help of others.” Their claim is totally unjustified and untrue!

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve say ‘This Qur’ān is nothing but a calumny a lie that he Muhammad (s) has invented and other folk have helped him with it’ who according to the disbelievers were from among the People of the Scripture. God exalted be He says Verily thus they have committed wrong and spoken falsehood they have come with disbelief and mendacity.

hype_questions: Does the Quran's authenticity depend on human fabrication?
Can a prophet's message be entirely fabricated by others?
What are the consequences of disbelievers accusing the Prophet Muhammad (s) of lying?
propositions: The disbelievers claim that the Quran is a fabrication made up with the help of others.
Their claim is unjustified and untrue.
God exalted be He says that those who disbelieve have committed wrong and spoken falsehood.

source_text:
Verse: And they say, “˹These revelations are only˺ ancient fables which he has had written down, and they are rehearsed to him morning and evening.”

Tafsir: And they say that it the Qur’ān is also ‘Fables their lies asātir is the plural of ustūra of the ancients which he has had written down that he has had someone from among those people copy it down for him so that they are read to him for him to memorise morning and evening’. God exalted be He responds to them saying

hype_questions: Does the Qur'ān contain ancient fables?
Is the Qur'ān being read to someone for memorization?
Who is copying down the Qur'ān for someone?
propositions: The Qur'ān contains ancient fables.
Someone copies down the Qur'ān for memorization.
God responds to those who deny the Qur'ān.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “This ˹Quran˺ has been revealed by the One Who knows the secrets of the heavens and the earth. Surely He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Tafsir: Say ‘It has been revealed by Him Who knows the secret the Unseen of the heavens and the earth. Truly He is ever Forgiving of believers Merciful’ to them.

hype_questions: What is the nature of divine knowledge?
How does God show mercy to believers?
Who revealed the Quran?
propositions: The Quran has been revealed by Allah.
Allah knows the secrets of the heavens and the earth.
God is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: And they say ˹mockingly˺, “What kind of messenger is this who eats food and goes about in market-places ˹for a living˺? If only an angel had been sent down with him to be his co-warner,

Tafsir: And they also say ‘What is it with this Messenger that he eats food and walks about in the marketplaces? Why has an angel not been sent down to him so as to be a warner along with him? and confirm his truthfulness.

hype_questions: What is the nature of a messenger who engages in worldly activities?
Why has an angel not been sent to accompany this messenger on his mission?
How can one confirm the truthfulness of a messenger?
propositions: The Messenger eats food and goes about in market-places for a living.
An angel has not been sent down to be a co-warner with the Messenger.
The Messenger's truthfulness should be confirmed.

source_text:
Verse: or a treasure had been cast down to him, or he had had a garden from which he may eat!” And the wrongdoers say ˹to the believers˺, “You are only following a bewitched man.”

Tafsir: Or a treasure thrown down to him from the heaven for him to spend from so as not to be in need of walking through the marketplaces in order to earn his livelihood. Or he has a garden an orchard for him to eat from?’ that is to eat from its fruits and satisfy himself therewith a variant reading for ya’kulu ‘for him to eat’ has na’kulu ‘for us to eat’ and thus possess because of that garden an advantage over us. The wrongdoers namely the disbelievers say to the believers ‘You are just following a man bewitched!’ one duped his mind overcome. God exalted be He says

hype_questions: Is following a bewitched man a valid way to earn a living?
Can having a garden provide one with all the necessities of life?
Do disbelievers truly believe that believers are following a bewitched man?
propositions: A treasure was thrown down from heaven for him to spend from, so he would not have to walk through marketplaces to earn his livelihood.
He has a garden and orchard to eat from, which provides him with all the necessities of life.
The wrongdoers say that believers are following a bewitched man, but this is just a misconception.

source_text:
Verse: See ˹O Prophet˺ how they call you names! So they have gone so ˹far˺ astray that they cannot find the ˹Right˺ Way.

Tafsir: See how they strike similitudes for you of the fact that the Prophet is a person bewitched and one in need of something to expend from and of an angel to help him carry out the task of delivering the Message so that they go astray thereby from guidance and are unable to find a way a means thereto to guidance.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Prophet's role in delivering the Message?
How do people's misconceptions about the Prophet affect their understanding of guidance?
What are some common pitfalls that prevent individuals from finding the Right Way?
propositions: The Prophet is a person who delivers the Message.
People strike similitudes for the Prophet, portraying him as bewitched and in need of something to expend.
The Prophet has an angel to help him carry out his task.
The Prophet's role is to deliver the Message.
Guidance is found through understanding the Right Way.
Misconceptions about the Prophet can lead individuals astray from guidance.

source_text:
Verse: Blessed is the One Who—if He wills—can give you far better than ˹all˺ that: gardens under which rivers flow, and palaces as well.

Tafsir: Blessed is He abundant is the good of God Who if He will will give you better than that treasure or orchard which they mentioned — gardens underneath which rivers flow in this world for He has already willed to give him such things in the Hereafter and will give read apocopated form wa-yaj‘al you palaces as well a variant reading of the apocopated yaj‘al is yaj‘alu ‘He will give’ beginning a new sentence.

hype_questions: What are the rewards of Paradise in the Hereafter?
How will God provide for us in the Afterlife?
What kind of palaces and gardens can we expect in Paradise?
propositions: Blessed is He, abundant is the good of God.
God if He wills—can give you far better than that: gardens under which rivers flow, and palaces as well.
He has already willed to give him such things in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: In fact, they deny the Hour. And for the deniers of the Hour, We have prepared a blazing Fire.

Tafsir: Nay but they deny the coming of the Hour the Resurrection and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blaze sa‘īr a fire that has been set ablaze musa‘‘ara in other words an intense fire.

hype_questions: What is the Hour?
Will there be a Resurrection?
What will happen to those who deny the Hour?
propositions: They deny the coming of the Hour.
We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blaze.
The blaze is an intense fire.

source_text:
Verse: Once it sees them from a distance, they will hear it fuming and growling.

Tafsir: When it sees them from a distant place they will hear it raging boiling like an enraged person when his heart boils with anger and roaring producing a powerful noise. Alternatively what is meant by their ‘hearing it raging’ is their vision of it and awareness of it.

hype_questions: What happens when a person sees something from a distance?
How does an enraged person behave?
What is the sound of a raging boiling entity?
propositions: When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear it.
It rages and boils like an enraged person when his heart boils with anger.
The entity produces a powerful noise.

source_text:
Verse: And when they are tossed into a narrow place inside ˹Hell˺, chained together, then and there they will cry out for ˹instant˺ destruction.

Tafsir: And when they are flung into a narrow place thereof read dayyiqan or dayqan ‘narrow’ such that it constricts them; minhā ‘thereof’ is a circumstantial qualifier referring to makānan ‘place’ because it is actually an adjectival qualification of it bound together shackled with their hands bound to their necks in chains the use of the intensive form muqarranīna as opposed to muqranīna is meant to indicate a large number they will at that point pray for their own annihilation and it will be said to them

hype_questions: What happens when people are thrown into a narrow place in Hell?
How do people react when they are chained together in Hell?
Will those who are thrown into Hell pray for their own destruction?
propositions: When people are flung into a narrow place in Hell, they will cry out for destruction.
The narrow place in Hell constricts them and binds them with chains.
They will pray for their own annihilation at that point.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They will be told,˺ “Do not cry only once for destruction, but cry many times over!”

Tafsir: ‘Do not pray for a single annihilation on this day but pray for many annihilations!’ which will be the nature of your chastisement.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's chastisement?
How many times should one cry over destruction?
What is the correct approach to prayer on the day of reckoning?
propositions: Do not pray for a single annihilation on this day.
Pray for many annihilations!
This will be the nature of your chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Is this better or the Garden of Eternity which the righteous have been promised, as a reward and ˹an ultimate˺ destination?

Tafsir: Say ‘Is that which is mentioned of the threat of chastisement and the description of the Fire better or the Garden of Immortality which has been promised to the God-fearing which will be in God’s knowledge exalted be He their requital their reward and journey’s end?’ their place of return.

hype_questions: Is the Garden of Eternity better than the threat of chastisement and the Fire?
What is the ultimate destination for the righteous?
How will God's knowledge be revealed in the afterlife?
propositions: The Prophet asked if the Garden of Eternity was a better reward.
The Garden of Immortality has been promised to those who fear God.
God's knowledge is exalted and will reveal their requital and reward.

source_text:
Verse: There they will have whatever they wish for, forever. That is a promise ˹to be sought after˺, binding on your Lord.”

Tafsir: In it they shall have what they wish abiding therein — an irrevocable state — it the promise to them of what is mentioned is a promise binding on your Lord a promise much besought requested by those who have been promised it as is clear from the following Our Lord grant us what You have promised us through Your messengers Q. 3194 or requested on their behalf by the angels who say Our Lord and admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them Q. 408.

hype_questions: What will I have in the afterlife?
Is God's promise binding?
How can we get what is promised to us?
propositions: They will have whatever they wish for, forever.
The promise of an irrevocable state abiding therein is a promise binding on your Lord.
Our Lord grant us what You have promised us through Your messengers.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Watch for˺ the Day He will gather them along with what they used to worship besides Allah, and ask ˹the objects of worship˺, “Was it you who misled these servants of Mine, or did they stray from the Way ˹on their own˺?”

Tafsir: And on the day when He will assemble them yahshuruhum; a variant reading has nahshuruhum ‘We assemble them’ and that which they worship besides God that is other than Him such as the angels Jesus Ezra and the jinn and will say exalted be He fa-yaqūlu; a variant has fa-naqūlu and We shall say’ to those who were worshipped as a way of establishing the argument against the worshippers of the former ‘Was it you read a-antum pronouncing both hamzas or by substituting the second one with an alif or not pronouncing this last and inserting an alif between the one not pronounced and the former or without such an insertion who misled these servants of Mine causing them to fall into error by commanding them to worship you or did they go astray from the way? the path of truth by themselves?

hype_questions: Will the objects of worship be held accountable for misleading humans?
Did humans choose to stray from the path of truth on their own, or was it forced upon them?
What is the nature of free will in relation to one's relationship with Allah?
propositions: Allah will gather humans along with what they used to worship besides Him.
The objects of worship will be asked if they misled humans.
Humans strayed from the path of truth on their own, or were they misled by others?
Free will plays a role in human's relationship with Allah.

source_text:
Verse: They will say, “Glory be to You! It was not right for ˹others like˺ us to take any lords besides You, but You allowed enjoyment for them and their forefathers ˹for so long˺ that they forgot ˹Your˺ remembrance and became a doomed people.”

Tafsir: They will say ‘Glory be to You — exalted be You above what does not befit You! It was not it would not have been right for us to take any guardians besides You that is other than You min awliyā’a the first direct object the min being extra added to emphasise the negation; the preceding min dūnika ‘besides You’ is the second direct object. So how can we command that we be worshipped? But You gave them and their fathers before them ease of living by granting them long life and abundant provision until they forgot the Remembrance until they became remiss about admonitions and belief in the Qur’ān and became a lost folk’ a folk destroyed. God exalted be He says

hype_questions: Can humans ever truly worship a deity besides the one true God?
How can we reconcile our desire for ease and comfort with our duty to remember and obey God?
What happens when people forget about their faith and become remiss in their duties?
propositions: It was not right for humans to take any lords besides God.
God gave humans and their fathers ease of living by granting them long life and abundant provision.
Humans forgot the Remembrance until they became a doomed people.

source_text:
Verse: ˹The doomed will be told˺, “Your gods have clearly denied your claims. So now you can neither ward off ˹the punishment˺ nor get any help.” And whoever of you does wrong, We will make them taste a horrible punishment.

Tafsir: Thus they will deny you that is the ones who were worshipped denied those who worshipped them in what you allege namely that they are gods and they will neither be able to read yastatī‘ūna or second person plural tastatī‘ūna in other words neither they nor you will be able to circumvent ward off the chastisement from you nor help nor protect you from it. And whoever of you does evil whoever ascribes partners to God We shall make him taste an awful a severe chastisement in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What happens to those who worship false gods?
Can humans ward off punishment from God?
What is the consequence for those who ascribe partners to God?
propositions: Your gods have clearly denied your claims.
Neither you nor they will be able to circumvent the chastisement from you nor help nor protect you from it.
We shall make him taste an awful a severe chastisement in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: We never sent any messenger before you ˹O Prophet˺, who did not eat food and go about in market-places. We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you ˹not then˺ be patient? And your Lord is All-Seeing.

Tafsir: And We did not send before you any messengers but that they ate food and walked in the marketplaces and so you are like them in this respect and truly what was said to them is being said to you. And We have made some of you a trial for others a test trying the rich with the poor the healthy with the sick the honourable with the vulgar in each case the latter would say ‘Why can I not be like the other person?’ Will you be steadfast? and endure what you hear from those with whom you are tried? the interrogative is meant as an imperative in other words ‘Be steadfast!’. And your Lord is ever Watchful of those who remain steadfast and those who become miserable.

hype_questions: Will you be patient in the face of trials?
Can you endure what you hear from those with whom you are tried?
What is the reward for remaining steadfast?
propositions: We never sent any messenger before you who did not eat food and go about in market-places.
You are like them in this respect.
We have made some of you a trial for others.
A test trying the rich with the poor, the healthy with the sick, the honourable with the vulgar.
The latter would say ‘Why can I not be like the other person?’
Will you be steadfast?
Endure what you hear from those with whom you are tried.
Your Lord is ever Watchful of those who remain steadfast and those who become miserable.

source_text:
Verse: Those who do not expect to meet Us say, “If only the angels were sent down to us, or we could see our Lord!” They have certainly been carried away by their arrogance and have entirely exceeded all limits.

Tafsir: And those who do not expect to encounter Us those who have no fear of the Resurrection say ‘Why have the angels not been sent down to us to act as messengers to us or why do we not see our Lord?’ so that we might be informed by Him that Muhammad (s) is truly His Messenger? God exalted be He says Assuredly they are full of arrogance within their souls and have become terribly insolent in demanding to see God exalted be He in this world read ‘utuwwan ‘insolence’ with the wāw according to the original root form as opposed to ‘itiyyan with the yā’ substitution as in sūrat Maryam Q. 198.

hype_questions: Would seeing the angels and our Lord be enough to convince them of Muhammad's (s) prophethood?
Can we trust that God will reveal Himself to us if only we could see Him?
Is it arrogant to demand a personal encounter with God?
propositions: Those who do not expect to meet Us are arrogant and insolent.
They say, 'If only the angels were sent down to us or we could see our Lord!'
God exalted be He says: Assuredly they are full of arrogance within their souls.

source_text:
Verse: ˹But˺ on the Day they will see the angels, there will be no good news for the wicked, who will cry, “Keep away! Away ˹from us˺!”

Tafsir: The day when they see the angels while they stand together with the rest of creation namely on the Day of Resurrection yawma is in the accusative because of an implied preceding udhkur ‘mention’ there will be no good tidings on that day for the guilty that is the disbelievers in contrast to the believers for whom there shall be the good tidings of Paradise and they will say ‘A forbidding ban!’ as was their the pagan custom in this world whenever a misfortune befell them; in other words they mean ‘awdhan ma‘ādhan seeking refuge from the angels who will chastise them. God exalted be He says

hype_questions: What happens when we see the angels on Judgment Day?
Will there be good news for believers on that day?
How do disbelievers react to seeing the angels?
propositions: On the Day of Resurrection, those who are wicked will see the angels.
There will be no good tidings for the guilty on that day.
Believers will receive good tidings of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.
God exalted be He says

source_text:
Verse: Then We will turn to whatever ˹good˺ deeds they did, reducing them to scattered dust.

Tafsir: And We shall attend to We shall turn to the works they did that were good such as voluntary alms or kindness to kin a hospitable reception of a guest or the succour of a troubled person in this world and turn them into scattered dust habā’an manthūran namely as those individual particles of dust which one might observe near a window when the sun is shining through. In other words We shall make their good works like those particles of dust in their uselessness there being no reward for such works for lack of any binding obligation to reward them therefor; but they are rewarded for it in the life of this world.

hype_questions: What happens to good deeds after death?
Are there any rewards for good works without a binding obligation?
How are good works in this life related to their value after death?
propositions: We will turn to the good deeds they did.
Their good works were voluntary alms, kindness to kin, hospitable reception of a guest, or succour of a troubled person.
Good works are like scattered dust in their uselessness.
There is no reward for such works due to lack of binding obligation.
However, they are rewarded in the life of this world.

source_text:
Verse: ˹But˺ on that Day the residents of Paradise will have the best settlement and the finest place to rest.

Tafsir: Those who will be the inhabitants of Paradise on that day the Day of Resurrection will be in a far better abode than are the disbelievers in this world and a far better resting place than theirs the latter’s; in other words a better place for qā’ila which is a rest taken during midday during hot days. From this last interpretation of maqīlan it has been inferred that the Reckoning will be concluded in half a day as is stated in one hadīth.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Paradise in the afterlife?
How does the concept of qā’ila relate to the Day of Resurrection?
Can the Reckoning be concluded in a specific timeframe?
propositions: The residents of Paradise will have the best settlement and the finest place to rest.
Those who inhabit Paradise on the Day of Resurrection will have a better abode than disbelievers in this world.
The Reckoning will be concluded in half a day.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Watch for˺ the Day the heavens will burst with clouds, and the angels will be sent down in successive ranks.

Tafsir: And on the day when the heaven each of the seven heavens will be split asunder with the clouds in other words split asunder together with them the clouds al-ghamām is white cloud and the angels will be sent down from every heaven in a majestic descent and this is the Day of Resurrection it yawma ‘on the day’ is in the accusative because of an implied preceding udhkur ‘mention’; a variant reading for tashaqqaqu is tashshaqqaqu ‘will be split asunder’ where the second tā’ of the original form tatashaqqaqu has been assimilated with it the the shīn; another variant reading instead of nuzzila al-malā’ikatu ‘the angels will be sent down’ has nunzilu al-malā’ikata ‘We will send down the angels’;

hype_questions: What will happen to the heavens on the Day of Resurrection?
How will the angels be sent down during the Day of Judgment?
Will the clouds be present during the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: The heavens will burst with clouds on the Day of Resurrection.
Each of the seven heavens will be split asunder with the clouds on that day.
The angels will be sent down from every heaven in a majestic descent on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: True authority on that Day will belong ˹only˺ to the Most Compassionate. And it will be a hard day for the disbelievers.

Tafsir: true Sovereignty on that day will belong to the Compassionate One with no one else sharing it with Him and it that day will be a hard day for the disbelievers in contrast to the believers.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate authority on the Day of Judgment?
Who will share sovereignty with God on that day?
How will believers and disbelievers be affected on the Day of Judgment?
propositions: True authority on the Day of Judgment belongs to the Most Compassionate.
Sovereignty on the Day of Judgment is exclusive to the Compassionate One.
The Day of Judgment will be a hard day for disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹beware of˺ the Day the wrongdoer will bite his nails ˹in regret˺ and say, “Oh! I wish I had followed the Way along with the Messenger!

Tafsir: And it will be a day when the wrongdoer the idolater ‘Uqba b. Abī Mu‘ayt — who had uttered the two-part profession ‘there is no god but God Muhammad (s) is His Messenger’ but retracted it in order to please Ubayy b. Khalaf — will bite his hands in regret and anguish on the Day of Resurrection saying ‘O yā is for drawing attention would that I had followed a way with the Messenger! Muhammad (s) a route to guidance.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the message of guidance?
Can one ever truly repent and seek forgiveness after straying from the right path?
How does one find guidance in a world filled with distractions?
propositions: There will be a Day of Resurrection when wrongdoers will regret their actions.
Idolatry is a grave sin that can lead to eternal regret.
Repentance is possible, but it must be genuine and sincere.
Following the Messenger (s) is a route to guidance and salvation.
The path of righteousness is often obscured by worldly distractions.

source_text:
Verse: Woe to me! I wish I had never taken so-and-so as a close friend.

Tafsir: O woe to me! yā waylatā the final alif stands in place of the first person singular possessive yā’ yā waylatī meaning ‘alas for my destruction!’ Would that I had not taken so and so in other words that Ubayy as friend!

hype_questions: What happens when we form close friendships with people who may not have our best interests at heart?
How can we avoid regret in our relationships with others?
Can we ever truly know if someone is a true friend or just using us for their own gain?
propositions: I took Ubayy as my close friend.
This friendship has led to my destruction.
If I had not taken Ubayy as my friend, I would be in a better state.

source_text:
Verse: It was he who truly made me stray from the Reminder after it had reached me.” And Satan has always betrayed humanity.

Tafsir: Verily he has led me astray from the Remembrance namely the Qur’ān after it had come to me by causing me to recant my belief in it. God exalted be He says And Satan is ever a deserter of the disbelieving man’ abandoning him and dissociating from him in times of tribulation.

hype_questions: What causes a person to stray from their faith?
How does Satan affect a person's belief in God?
What is the nature of Satan's relationship with humans?
propositions: God made the narrator stray from the Remembrance (Qur'ān) after it reached them.
Satan betrayed humanity by causing the narrator to recant their belief in the Qur'ān.
Satan is a deserter of the disbelieving man, abandoning and dissociating from them in times of tribulation.

source_text:
Verse: The Messenger has cried, “O my Lord! My people have indeed received this Quran with neglect.”

Tafsir: And the Messenger Muhammad (s) says ‘O my Lord lo! my people the tribe of Quraysh consider this Qur’ān as something to be shunned’ to be disregarded.

hype_questions: What is the reaction of the tribe of Quraysh to the arrival of the Quran?
How do the people of Quraysh perceive the Quran?
Why does the Messenger Muhammad consider his people's response to be negative?
propositions: The Messenger Muhammad cried out to Allah, saying that his people had neglected the Quran.
The tribe of Quraysh considered the Quran to be something to be shunned or disregarded.
Muhammad's people viewed the Quran with disdain.

source_text:
Verse: Similarly, We made enemies for every prophet from among the wicked, but sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and Helper.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says So just as We have appointed for you enemies from among the idolaters of your people We have appointed to every prophet before you an enemy from among the guilty the idolaters — so be steadfast as they were; but your Lord suffices as a Guide for you and a Helper to bring you victory over your enemies.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the enemies appointed by God for every prophet?
How should a prophet respond to their challenges?
What role does God play in guiding and helping prophets?
propositions: God has appointed enemies for every prophet from among the wicked.
Your Lord suffices as a Guide for you and a Helper to bring you victory over your enemies.
Be steadfast as they were, but your Lord is sufficient as a Guide for you.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers say, “If only the Quran had been sent down to him all at once!” ˹We have sent it˺ as such ˹in stages˺ so We may reassure your heart with it. And We have revealed it at a deliberate pace.

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve say ‘Why has the Qur’ān not been revealed to him all at once?’ as the Torah the Gospel and the Book of Psalms were. God exalted be He says We have revealed it thus in parts it is that We may strengthen your inner-heart with it and We have arranged it in a specific order that is to say We produce it in stages one part after another gradually and deliberately in order to facilitate its comprehension and its memorisation.

hype_questions: Why did God not reveal the Quran all at once?
How does the Quran's revelation help strengthen one's heart?
What is the purpose of the Quran being revealed in stages?
propositions: The Quran was sent down to the Prophet in stages.
God revealed the Quran to reassure the Prophet's heart with it.
The Quran was arranged in a specific order to facilitate its comprehension and memorization.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever they bring you an argument, We come to you with the right refutation and the best explanation.

Tafsir: And they do not bring you any similitude to invalidate your mission but that We bring you the truth that refutes it and what is better as exposition explanation.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the refutation provided by Allah?
How does Allah explain complex concepts to His messengers?
What is the ultimate goal of the prophet's explanation?
propositions: Whenever they bring you an argument, We come to you with the right refutation.
We bring you the truth that refutes any invalidating similitude.
We bring you what is better as exposition and explanation.

source_text:
Verse: Those who will be dragged into Hell on their faces will be in the worst place, and are ˹now˺ farthest from the ˹Right˺ Way.

Tafsir: They are those who will be gathered on their faces that is those who will be driven as cattle toward Hell they will be in the worst place namely Hell and furthest astray from the way they will be on a path of error worse than that of others; and this path is their disbelief.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are dragged into Hell on their faces?
How far astray are those who will be driven as cattle toward Hell?
What is the path of error that leads to disbelief?
propositions: Those who will be dragged into Hell on their faces will be in the worst place.
They will be gathered on their faces, namely those who will be driven as cattle toward Hell.
This path is their disbelief.

source_text:
Verse: We certainly gave Moses the Book and appointed his brother Aaron as his helper.

Tafsir: And verily We gave Moses the Scripture the Torah and made Aaron his brother go with him as a minister an assistant.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Moses receiving the Scripture?
Who was appointed as Aaron's helper by God?
What is the name of the book given to Moses?
propositions: We gave Moses the Book.
Aaron was appointed as Moses' helper.
Moses received the Torah.

source_text:
Verse: We had ordered ˹them˺, “Go to the people who would deny Our signs.” Then We annihilated the deniers entirely.

Tafsir: Then We said ‘Go both of you to the people who have denied Our signs’ that is to the Egyptians — Pharaoh and his folk. So they went to them with the Message but they the Egyptians denied both of them. Then We destroyed them utterly.

hype_questions: What happens when people deny the signs of Allah?
How did Pharaoh and his folk respond to the message from Allah?
What was the ultimate fate of those who denied the signs of Allah?
propositions: We ordered the two prophets to go to the people who would deny Our signs.
The Egyptians, including Pharaoh and his folk, denied the message from Allah.
We annihilated the deniers entirely.

source_text:
Verse: And when the people of Noah rejected the messengers, We drowned them, making them an example to humanity. And We have prepared a painful punishment for the wrongdoers.

Tafsir: And mention the people of Noah when they denied the messengers in denying Noah — it is as though he were many messengers given the length of time he remained among them; or it is thus expressed in the plural because to deny him is equivalent to denying all the other messengers for they all came with the same Message concerning affirmation of God’s Oneness — We drowned them this is the response to lammā ‘when’ and made them a sign a lesson for mankind thereafter and We have prepared in the Hereafter for the evildoers the disbelievers a painful chastisement in addition to what chastisement may befall them in this world.

hype_questions: What is the punishment for those who reject God's messengers?
How did the people of Noah respond to their prophet?
What lesson can we learn from the story of Noah?
propositions: The people of Noah rejected their prophet.
God sent prophets to affirm His Oneness.
Those who reject God's messengers will face a painful punishment in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: Also ˹We destroyed˺ ’Ȃd, Thamûd, and the people of the Water-pit, as well as many peoples in between.

Tafsir: And mention ‘Ād the people of Hūd and Thamūd the people of Sālih and the dwellers at al-Rass al-rass — the name of a ‘well’; their prophet is said to have been Shu‘ayb; although some say it was someone else. The story is that they had been sitting around it on one occasion when it collapsed beneath them burying them together with their dwellings. And many generations peoples in between that is between the people of ‘Ād and the dwellers at al-Rass.

hype_questions: What happened to the people of 'Ād and Thamûd?
Who was the prophet of al-Rass?
Why did the well collapse beneath the dwellers at al-Rass?
propositions: We destroyed 'Ad, Thamûd, and the people of the Water-pit, as well as many peoples in between.
'Ād had a prophet named Shu‘ayb who was said to have been buried alive with his dwellings when the well collapsed.
The people of al-Rass were dwelling at a 'well' whose name is mentioned as al-Rass.

source_text:
Verse: For each We set forth ˹various˺ lessons, and We ultimately destroyed each.

Tafsir: For each of them We struck similitudes when establishing arguments against them and We destroyed them only after warning them and each of them We ruined utterly We destroyed utterly because of their denial of the prophets sent to them.

hype_questions: What happens when we reject the messages of the prophets?
How do we respond to arguments against us?
What is the ultimate fate of those who deny the truth?
propositions: We set forth various lessons.
We struck similitudes when establishing arguments against them.
We destroyed them only after warning them.
Each of them We ruined utterly.
We destroyed utterly because of their denial of the prophets sent to them.

source_text:
Verse: They have certainly passed by the city ˹of Sodom˺, which had been showered with a dreadful rain ˹of stones˺. Have they not seen its ruins? But they do not expect to be resurrected.

Tafsir: And verily they namely the disbelievers of Mecca will have passed by the town on which an evil shower was rained al-saw’ ‘evil’ is the verbal noun from sā’a ‘was evil’ that is it was showered with stones. This was the principal town of the towns inhabited by the people of Lot; God destroyed its inhabitants for their committing acts of lewdness. Can it be that they have not seen it? on their journeys to Syria and so take heed thereof? the interrogative is affirmative. Nay but it is that they do not expect they have no fear of any resurrection and so they do not believe.

hype_questions: Will the people of Mecca be resurrected after their death?
Can they see the ruins of Sodom on their journeys to Syria?
Do they have any fear of being resurrected?
propositions: They have passed by the city of Sodom.
The city was showered with stones.
God destroyed its inhabitants for their committing acts of lewdness.
They do not expect to be resurrected.
Can they see it on their journeys to Syria?
They do not believe in resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: When they see you ˹O Prophet˺, they only make fun of you, ˹saying,˺ “Is this the one that Allah has sent as a messenger?

Tafsir: And when they see you they take you in mockery only as an object of derision saying ‘Is this the one whom God has sent as a messenger? as he is wont to claim? — contemptuously of him as one not worthy of being a messenger.

hype_questions: Does the Prophet receive mockery from people?
Is the Prophet considered worthy of being a messenger by God?
How do people react to the Prophet's claim of being a messenger?
propositions: The Prophet is mocked by people when they see him.
God has sent the Prophet as a messenger.
People consider the Prophet unworthy of being a messenger.

source_text:
Verse: He would have almost tricked us away from our gods, had we not been so devoted to them.” ˹But˺ soon they will know, when they face the punishment, who is far astray from the ˹Right˺ Way.

Tafsir: Indeed in softened in place of the hardened form with its subject omitted namely innahu he was about to lead us astray turn us away from our gods had we not stood by them’ he would have turned us away from them. God exalted be He says And soon they will know when they behold the chastisement with their own eyes in the Hereafter who is further astray from the way who is further upon the path of error they or the believers?

hype_questions: What happens to those who are astray from the right path?
Can believers be astray from the right path?
How will people know who is further astray from the way?
propositions: He would have led us astray if we had not stood by our gods.
God exalted be He says that soon they will know when they behold the chastisement with their own eyes in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: Have you seen ˹O Prophet˺ the one who has taken their own desires as their god? Will you then be a keeper over them?

Tafsir: Have you seen — inform Me about — him who has taken as his god his own desire? that is as something that will be bring about his ruin the indirect object ilāhahu ‘as his god’ precedes the direct object because it is more important; the clause beginning man ittakhadha ‘him who has taken’ constitutes the first direct object of a-ra’ayta ‘have you seen’ the second being the following a-fa-anta … Will you be a guardian over him? a protector to preserve him from following his desires? No.

hype_questions: Can we protect someone who is destroying themselves with their own desires?
Is it our duty to watch over those who are succumbing to their own ego?
What happens when we fail to intervene in the self-destruction of another person?
propositions: The Prophet saw a person who has taken his desire as his god.
This will lead to ruin for him.
We should not be a guardian or protector over someone who is destroying themselves with their desires.

source_text:
Verse: Or do you think that most of them listen or understand?

Tafsir: Or do you suppose that most of them listen listening so as to understand or comprehend? what you say to them? They are but as the cattle — nay but they are further astray from the way further from these cattle upon the path of misguidance for at least they cattle yield to the person who looks after them whereas these disbelievers do not obey their Master Who is gracious to them.

hype_questions: Do most people truly listen and understand the message?
What do you say to those who are misled by their own desires?
How can one guide someone who is lost on the path of misguidance?
propositions: Most people do not truly listen or understand.
They are further astray from the way than cattle, and they do not obey their Master.
Cattle yield to those who care for them, whereas disbelievers do not obey their Master.

source_text:
Verse: Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade—He could have simply made it ˹remain˺ still if He so willed—then We make the sun its guide,

Tafsir: Have you not seen contemplated the work of your Lord how He extends the twilight shadow? from the point of daybreak to the point of sunrise. For had He your Lord willed He would have made it still ever-present so that it does not disappear with the rising of the sun. Then We made the sun an indicator of it of the shadow; were it not for the sun the shadow would not have been known.

hype_questions: Does your Lord have the power to make the shade remain still at any time?
Why does your Lord allow the shade to disappear with the rising of the sun?
What is the purpose of making the sun an indicator of the shadow?
propositions: Your Lord extends the twilight shadow from daybreak to sunrise.
If your Lord willed, He would have made the shade still present.
The sun was made an indicator of the shadow so that it could be known.

source_text:
Verse: causing the shade to retreat gradually?

Tafsir: Then We retract it the extended shadow to Us by gentle retraction subtle retraction through the rising of the sun.

hype_questions: What happens when the sun rises?
How does the shade react to the sunrise?
Why does God retract the extended shadow?
propositions: The shade retreats gradually.
God retracts the extended shadow through subtle retraction as the sun rises.
The sun's rise causes the shade to withdraw.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who has made the night for you as a cover, and ˹made˺ sleep for resting, and the day for rising.

Tafsir: And He it is Who made for you the night as a garment veiling you like a garment and sleep for repose rest for bodies through the temporary cessation of labour and He made the day for rising a time in which all rise to seek their livelihood and so on.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the night?
How does sleep benefit the human body?
Why do people rise during the day?
propositions: The One Who has made the night for you as a cover.
He made sleep for resting and repose rest for bodies through the temporary cessation of labour.
He made the day for rising a time in which all rise to seek their livelihood.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who sends the winds ushering in His mercy, and We send down pure rain from the sky,

Tafsir: And He it is Who sends forth the winds al-riyāha; a variant has al-rīha ‘the wind’ dispersing before His mercy nushuran ‘dispersing’ scattered before the coming of the rain a variant reading has nushran the singular of which is nashūr similar in pattern to rasūl ‘messenger’ plural rusul; another reading has nashran as a verbal noun; and a third variant has bushran in other words the winds function as mubashshirāt ‘bearers of good tidings’ the singular of which is bashīr; and We send down from the heaven purifying water

hype_questions: What is the role of mercy in the Quran?
How does God send down rain from the sky?
What do the winds represent in Islamic theology?
propositions: God sends forth the winds as a means of His mercy.
We send down pure rain from the sky.
The winds function as bearers of good tidings.

source_text:
Verse: giving life to a lifeless land, and providing water for countless animals and humans of Our Own creation.

Tafsir: with which We revive a dead land read maytan in the softened form equally valid for the masculine and the feminine but in the masculine here because of the masculine noun indicating ‘place’ implicit therein and We give it the water as drink to the many cattle camels cows and sheep and humans We have created anāsiyy is the plural of insān properly it the plural should be anāsīn but the final nūn has been replaced with a yā’ with which the other yā’ has been assimilated; or it anāsiyy is simply the plural of insiyy.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Allah's creation?
How does Allah provide for His creations?
What is the significance of water in Allah's sustenance?
propositions: Allah gives life to a dead land.
Allah provides water as drink to many cattle, camels, cows, and humans.
Allah has created all living beings.

source_text:
Verse: We certainly disperse it among them so they may be mindful, but most people persist in ungratefulness.

Tafsir: And verily We have distributed it the water among them so that they may remember li-yadhdhakkarū should actually be li-yatadhakkarū but the tā’ has been assimilated with the dhāl; a variant reading has li-yadhkurū that is to say so that they may remember therewith the grace of God. But most people are only intent on ingratitude on denial of the grace saying ‘We have received this rain because of such-and-such a storm’.

hype_questions: What happens when people are ungrateful for the blessings they receive?
How does God's grace manifest in our lives?
Can we truly attribute our successes to anything other than divine intervention?
propositions: We disperse blessings among people so that they may be mindful.
God distributes water among people to remind them of His grace.
Most people persist in ungratefulness and deny God's grace.

source_text:
Verse: Had We willed, We could have easily sent a warner to every society.

Tafsir: And had We willed We could have sent forth in every town a warner to threaten its inhabitants with God’s chastisement; instead We have sent you to the inhabitants of all towns as a warner for your reward to be a great one.

hype_questions: Would God have sent a warner to every society if He had willed?
What is the purpose of sending a warner to every town?
How will the inhabitants of all towns be rewarded for following the warner?
propositions: Had We willed, We could have easily sent a warner to every society.

And had We willed, We could have sent forth in every town a warner to threaten its inhabitants with God’s chastisement; instead We have sent you to the inhabitants of all towns as a warner for your reward to be a great one.

source_text:
Verse: So do not yield to the disbelievers, but strive diligently against them with this ˹Quran˺.

Tafsir: So do not obey the disbelievers in their desires but struggle against them therewith that is through adherence to the Qur’ān with a great endeavour.

hype_questions: What is the recommended approach when faced with disbelievers?
How can one demonstrate their commitment to the Qur'ān in the face of adversity?
What does it mean to 'struggle against' disbelievers in a spiritual context?
propositions: Do not obey the disbelievers in their desires.
Struggle against them with the Qur'ān.
This is through adherence to the Qur'ān with great endeavour.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who merges the two bodies of water: one fresh and palatable and the other salty and bitter, placing between them a barrier they cannot cross.

Tafsir: And He it is Who merged the two seas letting them flow one adjacent to the other this one palatable sweet and the other saltish bitter; and He set between the two an isthmus so that the one does not mix with the other and a forbidding ban a shield that prevents the two from becoming mixed.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of separating the two seas?
How does Allah create a barrier between the two seas?
Why does Allah prevent the two seas from mixing?
propositions: Allah merges the two bodies of water.
The Two Seas are adjacent to each other.
One Sea is palatable and sweet, while the other is salty and bitter.
Allah sets an isthmus between the two Seas.
The isthmus prevents the two Seas from mixing.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who creates human beings from a ˹humble˺ liquid, then establishes for them bonds of kinship and marriage. For your Lord is Most Capable.

Tafsir: And He it is Who created man from water He created from a sperm-drop a human being and made for him ties of blood and ties of marriage whether it be a male or a female they marry for the purposes of procreation. For your Lord is ever Powerful with the power to do whatever He will.

hype_questions: What is the origin of human life?
How do humans form relationships through marriage and blood ties?
What are the purposes of procreation?
propositions: Human beings were created from a liquid.
Ties of blood and marriage are established for humans.
Humans marry for the purpose of procreation.

source_text:
Verse: Yet they worship besides Allah what can neither benefit nor harm them. And the disbeliever always collaborates against their Lord.

Tafsir: And they the disbelievers worship besides God that which neither benefits them when they worship it nor harms them should they refrain therefrom — and these are idols; and the disbeliever is ever a partisan against his Lord an assistant to Satan through his obedience to him.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of worshiping idols?
How does a disbeliever's obedience to Satan affect their relationship with Allah?
Can worshiping idols bring any benefits or harm?
propositions: They worship besides Allah that which neither benefits them when they worship it nor harms them.
The disbeliever is ever a partisan against his Lord an assistant to Satan through his obedience to him.

source_text:
Verse: And We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ only as a deliverer of good news and a warner.

Tafsir: And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good tidings of Paradise and as a warner a threatener of people with the chastisement of the Fire.

hype_questions: What is Paradise?
What is the chastisement of the Fire?
What does it mean to be a warner and a threatener?
propositions: We sent the Prophet as a bearer of good tidings of Paradise.
The Prophet was sent as a warner and a threatener of people with the chastisement of the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺, but whoever wishes, let them pursue the Way to their Lord.”

Tafsir: Say ‘I do not ask of you in return for this that is for delivering that Message with which I have been sent any reward except that whoever wishes to follow a way to his Lord should do so’ by expending his wealth for the sake of attaining God’s pleasure exalted be He; then whoever wishes to do so I will not prevent him from doing so.

hype_questions: What is the reward for following the way to one's Lord?
How can one attain God's pleasure?
Is it permissible to pursue a path to one's Lord?
propositions: I do not ask you for any reward for this message.
Whoever wishes to follow a way to their Lord should do so by expending his wealth for the sake of attaining God's pleasure.

source_text:
Verse: Put your trust in the Ever-Living, Who never dies, and glorify His praises. Sufficient is He as All-Aware of the sins of His servants.

Tafsir: And put your trust in the Living One Who does not die and make glorifications ensconced in His praise in other words say subhāna’Llāhi wa’l-hamdu li’Llāh ‘Glory be to God and praise be to God’. And He suffices as One Aware as Knower of the sins of His servants khabīran ‘One Aware’ is semantically connected to bi-dhunūbi ‘of the sins’.

hype_questions: What happens when we put our trust in the Ever-Living?
How does glorifying God's praises impact our relationship with Him?
What is the significance of acknowledging God's awareness of our sins?
propositions: Put your trust in the Ever-Living, Who never dies.
Glorify His praise.
God suffices as One Aware of the sins of His servants.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is˺ the One Who created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne. ˹He is˺ the Most Compassionate! Ask ˹none other than˺ the All-Knowledgeable about Himself.

Tafsir: He it is Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days of the length of the days of this world since there was no sun at that point — had He willed He could have created them in an instant but His not having done so is because He will to teach His creatures to be circumspect — then presided upon the Throne al-‘arsh in the classical language is the seat on which a king sits the Compassionate One al-rahmānu substitutes for the subject of the verb istawā ‘presided’ a presiding befitting of Him; so ask O man about Him about the Compassionate One anyone who is well aware to inform you about His attributes!

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's creation?
How does Allah's power manifest in His creation?
What are some attributes of Allah that can be understood through contemplation?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six days.
Allah established Himself on the Throne after creating the universe.
Allah is compassionate towards His creatures.
It is not necessary for Allah to create something instantly, but rather He chooses to teach His creatures about the importance of being circumspect.
The Throne represents a seat of power and authority, befitting of Allah's majesty.

source_text:
Verse: When it is said to them, “Prostrate to the Most Compassionate,” they ask ˹in disgust˺, “What is ‘the Most Compassionate’? Will we prostrate to whatever you order us to?” And it only drives them farther away.

Tafsir: And when it is said to them to the disbelievers of Mecca ‘Prostrate yourselves before the Compassionate One’ they say ‘And what is the Compassionate One? Should we prostrate ourselves to whatever you bid us’ ta’murunā; or read ya’murunā ‘whatever he bids us’ — in both cases the one bidding is Muhammad (s) — when we do not know who He is? No! And it this that is said to them increases their aversion to faith.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's compassion?
Can humans be certain about their faith in a compassionate deity?
How does the concept of prostration relate to one's understanding of Allah?
propositions: When it is said to them, 'Prostrate to the Most Compassionate,' they ask what 'the Most Compassionate' means.
The disbelievers of Mecca are asked to prostrate themselves before the Compassionate One, but they question who this deity is.
The concept of prostration increases their aversion to faith when they do not know who Allah is.

source_text:
Verse: Blessed is the One Who has placed constellations in the sky, as well as a ˹radiant˺ lamp and a luminous moon.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says Blessed magnified is He Who has placed in the heaven constellations twelve of them Aries Taurus Gemini Cancer Leo Virgo al-sunbula Libra Scorpio Sagittarius Capricorn Aquarius and Pisces. They are the mansions for the seven orbiting planets Mars rules Aries and Scorpio Venus Taurus and Libra Mercury Gemini and Virgo the Moon Cancer the Sun Leo Jupiter Sagittarius and Pisces and Saturn Capricorn and Aquarius; and has also placed in it a lamp namely the sun and a shining moon a variant reading for sirājan ‘sun’ has the plural surujan which would mean ‘luminous stars’. The moon is singled out for mention because of its particular merit.

hype_questions: What are the twelve constellations in the sky?
Which planet rules Aries and Scorpio?
Why is the Moon singled out for mention?
propositions: God has placed constellations in the heaven.
The sun is a lamp.
The moon is shining.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who causes the day and the night to alternate, ˹as a sign˺ for whoever desires to be mindful or to be grateful.

Tafsir: And He it is Who made the night and day to appear in succession that is one succeeding the other for him who desires to remember read yadhdhakkara or yadhkura as before Q. 2550 — so that if he misses the opportunity to do some good during the one he can do it during the other; or desires to be thankful for the graces of his Lord to him during both of these periods.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of alternating day and night?
How can one make the most of both day and night for good deeds?
What is the significance of being thankful during both day and night?
propositions: He causes the day and night to alternate.
The night and day appear in succession for him who desires to remember.
If he misses the opportunity to do some good during the day, he can do it during the night, or vice versa.

source_text:
Verse: The ˹true˺ servants of the Most Compassionate are those who walk on the earth humbly, and when the foolish address them ˹improperly˺, they only respond with peace.

Tafsir: And the true servants of the Compassionate One ‘ibādu’l-rahmāni is the subject and what comes after it all the way up to ūlā’ika yujzawna ‘they will be rewarded’ of verse 75 below are adjectival qualifiers of this subject with the exception of the parenthetical statements are those who walk upon the earth modestly that is peacefully and humbly and who when the ignorant address them with what they are averse to say words of peace salām in other words words by which they are safe yaslamūna from committing any sin;

hype_questions: What is the key characteristic of a true servant of Allah?
How do they respond to those who address them improperly?
What benefit do they gain from walking on the earth humbly?
propositions: The servants of the Most Compassionate walk on the earth humbly.
Those who are addressed improperly by the ignorant will only respond with peace.
Walking on the earth humbly brings safety and protection from sin.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who spend ˹a good portion of˺ the night, prostrating themselves and standing before their Lord.

Tafsir: and who spend the night before their Lord prostrating sujjad is the plural of sājid and standing in worship in other words they spend the night performing prayers;

hype_questions: What does it mean to prostrate oneself before one's Lord?
How does spending the night in prayer affect a person's relationship with God?
What is the significance of standing in worship during the night?
propositions: Those who spend the night prostrating themselves are spending time in prayer.
Prostrating oneself before one's Lord means performing prayers.
Spending the night in prayer is a form of worship.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who pray, “Our Lord! Keep the punishment of Hell away from us, for its punishment is indeed unrelenting.

Tafsir: and who say ‘Our Lord avert from us from the chastisement of Hell. Truly its chastisement is abiding that is irrevocable.

hype_questions: What happens if one does not pray to Allah?
Can the punishment of Hell be avoided?
What is the nature of the chastisement of Hell?
propositions: Those who pray to Allah seek to avoid the punishment of Hell.
The punishment of Hell is unrelenting and abiding.
