Allah can avert the chastisement of Hell from those who seek refuge with Him.

source_text:
Verse: It is certainly an evil place to settle and reside.”

Tafsir: It is truly a wretched abode and residence!’ in other words it is truly wretched as a place in which to abide and reside.

hype_questions: What kind of place is described as an evil settlement?
Is the abode mentioned in the verse truly wretched?
Why is residing in this place considered undesirable?
propositions: It is a place to settle that is certainly evil.
This place is truly a wretched abode and residence.
Residing in this place is undesirable.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who spend neither wastefully nor stingily, but moderately in between.

Tafsir: And who when they expend upon their dependants are neither prodigal nor parsimonious read yaqturū or yuqtirū; but between such prodigality and parsimony lies — between the two their expenditure is in — moderation;

hype_questions: What is the ideal level of spending on dependents?
How can one avoid excessive generosity or stinginess when giving to others?
What is the middle ground between extravagance and miserliness?
propositions: Those who spend moderately are neither wasteful nor stingy.
Expenditure on dependants should be moderate, avoiding both excessiveness and parsimony.
Moderation lies between prodigality and parsimony in expenditure.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who do not invoke any other god besides Allah, nor take a ˹human˺ life—made sacred by Allah—except with ˹legal˺ right, nor commit fornication. And whoever does ˹any of˺ this will face the penalty.

Tafsir: and those who do not call on another god along with God nor slay the soul which God has forbidden that it be slain except with due cause and who do not commit fornication — for whoever does that namely whoever does one of these three things shall meet with retribution;

hype_questions: What are the conditions for a person to be considered innocent in the eyes of Allah?
How does Allah define the taking of a human life, and what is the consequence of violating this prohibition?
What is the nature of fornication in Islam, and how can it be avoided?
propositions: Those who do not invoke any other god besides Allah are innocent.
The soul which God has forbidden to be slain must be slain with due cause.
Fornication is a grave sin that must be avoided.

source_text:
Verse: Their punishment will be multiplied on the Day of Judgment, and they will remain in it forever, in disgrace.

Tafsir: doubled yudā‘af a variant reading has yuda‘‘af will be the chastisement for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will abide therein both verbs may be read in the imperfect apocopated form yudā‘af ‘it will be doubled’ and yakhlud ‘he will abide’ as substitutions or with the indicative damma inflection yudā‘afu and yakhludu to indicate the beginning of a new sentence abased muhānan is a circumstantial qualifier;

hype_questions: What happens to those who are punished on the Day of Judgment?
How long will they remain in their punishment?
Will they be treated with any respect or dignity?
propositions: Their punishment will be multiplied on the Day of Judgment.
They will remain in it forever, in disgrace.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who repent, believe, and do good deeds, they are the ones whose evil deeds Allah will change into good deeds. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: except for him who repents and believes and acts righteously from among them for such God will replace their mentioned evil deeds with good deeds in the Hereafter for God is ever Forgiving Merciful that is He is ever possessed of such attributes;

hype_questions: What happens to those who repent and believe?
How does Allah respond to good deeds?
Can evil deeds be changed in the Hereafter?
propositions: Those who repent, believe, and do good deeds will have their evil deeds replaced with good deeds.
Allah is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.
God replaces mentioned evil deeds with good deeds in the Hereafter for those who repent and believe.

source_text:
Verse: And whoever repents and does good has truly turned to Allah properly.

Tafsir: and whoever repents of his sins from among other than those mentioned and acts righteously indeed turns to God with due repentance that is he returns to God a sincere return and God will requite him with good;

hype_questions: What happens when someone repents from their sins?
How does one turn to God with due repentance?
What is the reward for returning to God with a sincere return?
propositions: Whoever repents and does good has truly turned to Allah properly.
Repentance of sins, not just any sin, but from among those mentioned, leads to turning to God with due repentance.
Turning to God with due repentance results in a sincere return.
God requites the one who returns with a sincere return with good.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who do not bear false witness, and when they come across falsehood, they pass ˹it˺ by with dignity.

Tafsir: and those who do not give false testimony that is testimony containing mendacity and falsehood and when they come across senseless talk in the way of vile speech and otherwise they pass by with dignity shunning such vanity;

hype_questions: What is the importance of bearing false witness?
How do individuals with integrity handle senseless talk and vile speech?
What does it mean to pass by falsehood with dignity?
propositions: Those who do not bear false witness are truthful.
When encountering falsehood, they pass it by with dignity.
Individuals with integrity shun senseless talk and vile speech.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who, when reminded of the revelation of their Lord, do not turn a blind eye or a deaf ear to it.

Tafsir: and those who when they are reminded when they are admonished of the revelations of their Lord that is reminded of the Qur’ān do not fall on them deaf and blind but fall on them listening contemplating benefiting and obedient;

hype_questions: What happens when someone is reminded of their Lord's revelation?
How do people respond to being admonished about their Lord's revelations?
What is the desired state for those who are reminded of their Lord's revelations?
propositions: Those who are reminded of their Lord's revelation do not turn a blind eye or a deaf ear to it.
When reminded, they listen, contemplate, benefit, and obey.
The Qur'ān is a reminder that prompts people to be listening, contemplating, benefiting, and obedient.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ those who pray, “Our Lord! Bless us with ˹pious˺ spouses and offspring who will be the joy of our hearts, and make us models for the righteous.”

Tafsir: and those who say ‘Our Lord! Grant us in our spouses and our offspring read plural dhurriyyātinā or singular dhurriyyatinā a joyful sight for us so that we see them obedient to You and make us paragons of virtue for the God-fearing’.

hype_questions: What is the ideal spouse in Islam?
How can I raise obedient children?
What are the characteristics of a righteous person?
propositions: The speaker's Lord should bless them with pious spouses.
The speaker's offspring should bring joy to their hearts.
The speaker's offspring should be obedient to God.

source_text:
Verse: It is they who will be rewarded with ˹elevated˺ mansions ˹in Paradise˺ for their perseverance, and will be received with salutations and ˹greetings of˺ peace,

Tafsir: Those they will be rewarded with the sublime abode the highest degree in Paradise forasmuch as they were steadfast in obedience to God and they will be met read yulaqqawna or yalqawna therein in this sublime abode with a greeting and words of peace from the angels;

hype_questions: What is the reward for perseverance in Islam?
How do angels greet believers in Paradise?
What is the highest degree of obedience to God?
propositions: They will be rewarded with elevated mansions in Paradise for their perseverance.
God rewards those who are steadfast in obedience to Him.
Believers will be met with a greeting and words of peace from the angels in Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: staying there forever. What an excellent place to settle and reside!

Tafsir: abiding therein. Excellent is it as an abode and station as a place of residence for them ūlā’ika ‘those they …’ and what comes after it constitute the predicate to the subject ‘ibādu’l-rahmāni ‘the servants of the Compassionate One’.

hype_questions: What is the ideal place to settle and reside?
How does Allah describe a suitable abode for His servants?
What are the characteristics of a place that is considered excellent as an abode?
propositions: Staying in a place forever is excellent.
Abiding in a place constitutes its excellence as an abode and station.
The servants of the Compassionate One reside in a suitable place.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “You ˹all˺ would not ˹even˺ matter to my Lord were it not for your faith ˹in Him˺. But now you ˹disbelievers˺ have denied ˹the truth˺, so the torment is bound to come.”

Tafsir: Say O Muhammad (s) to the people of Mecca ‘My Lord would not be concerned with you mā is for negation were it not for your supplications to Him when you are in adversity which He then removes. But why should He be concerned with you when you have denied the Messenger and the Qur’ān and so that the chastisement will remain binding’ permanently bound to you in the Hereafter in addition to what will befall you in this world; and so on the day of Badr seventy of them were slain the response to the conditional lawlā ‘were it not for …’ is indicated the preceding words.

hype_questions: What happens if one denies the Messenger and the Qur'an?
Why would Allah be concerned with someone who has denied Him?
What is the consequence of denying faith in the face of adversity?
propositions: My Lord would not be concerned with you were it not for your supplications to Him when you are in adversity.
You have denied the Messenger and the Qur'an, so the chastisement will remain binding.
Seventy of them were slain on the day of Badr.

source_text:
Verse: Ṭa-Sĩn-Mĩm.

Tafsir: Tā sīn mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

hype_questions: What does God mean by the letter Ṭa-Sĩn-Mĩm?
Can humans truly understand God's intentions?
How do we interpret divine revelations?
propositions: God knows best what He means by these letters.
The meaning of the letter Ṭa-Sĩn-Mĩm is unknown to humans.
Interpretation of divine revelations requires humility and trust in God's knowledge.

source_text:
Verse: These are the verses of the clear Book.

Tafsir: Those namely these signs are the signs of the Manifest Book the Qur’ān the genitive annexation āyātu’l-kitābi conveys the partitive meaning of min the Manifest meaning the one that manifests what is truth from what is falsehood.

hype_questions: What is the clear Book?
How does the Manifest Book manifest truth from falsehood?
What are the signs of the Manifest Book?
propositions: The clear Book is a book.
The Manifest Book manifests what is truth from what is falsehood.
The signs of the Manifest Book are the signs of the Qur'an.

source_text:
Verse: Perhaps you ˹O Prophet˺ will grieve yourself to death over their disbelief.

Tafsir: Perhaps O Muhammad (s) you might kill yourself out of distress for the reason that they namely the people of Mecca will not become believers la‘alla here expresses sympathy in other words what is meant is ‘have pity on it your self by alleviating the burden of this distress’.

hype_questions: Will Prophet grieve himself to death over disbelief?
Can Prophet alleviate the burden of distress for people who won't believe?
What is meant by 'have pity on it yourself' in this context?
propositions: The Prophet may grieve himself to death due to their disbelief.
The people of Mecca will not become believers.
One should alleviate the burden of distress for others.

source_text:
Verse: If We willed, We could send down upon them a ˹compelling˺ sign from the heavens, leaving their necks bent in ˹utter˺ submission to it.

Tafsir: If We will We will send down to them a sign from the heaven before which their necks will remain fa-zallat although grammatically in the past tense is being used in the sense of the imperfect tense bowed in humility and they will believe since ‘necks’ are described as ‘bowed in humility’ a status which in fact refers to those who possess them the adjectival form khādi‘ūn ‘bowed in humility’ used therein is the one normally used for rational beings.

hype_questions: What would happen if Allah sent a sign from heaven?
How would humans respond to a heavenly sign?
What is the nature of submission and humility in Islam?
propositions: If We will, We can send down a sign from the heavens.
Their necks will remain bowed in humility before such a sign.
They will believe when they see the sign.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever new reminder comes to them from the Most Compassionate, they always turn away from it.

Tafsir: And there would never come to them from the Compassionate One any remembrance any revelation from the Qur’ān that is new muhdathin is an explicative adjective but that they used to disregard it.

hype_questions: What happens when we turn away from divine reminders?
How do we respond to new revelations from the Qur'ān?
Why do people often disregard new reminders from Allah?
propositions: New reminders from Allah are always turned away.
The Compassionate One never sends new remembrance or revelation that is disregarded by humans.
Humans have a tendency to disregard new revelations from the Qur'ān.

source_text:
Verse: They have certainly denied ˹the truth˺, so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule.

Tafsir: Verily then they have denied it; but soon there will come to them the news the consequences of that which they used to deride.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of ridiculing something?
How will those who deny the truth be punished?
What happens when people mock something they later realize was true?
propositions: They have denied the truth.
The consequences of their ridicule will soon come to them.
Those who deride something may face punishment for it.

source_text:
Verse: Have they failed to look at the earth, ˹to see˺ how many types of fine plants We have caused to grow in it?

Tafsir: Have they not contemplated observed the earth how many We have caused to grow therein in other words We have caused to grow therein many of every splendid kind of vegetation of every fair species.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of observing the earth?
How does Allah create different types of plants?
Why did Allah grow various kinds of vegetation?
propositions: The earth has many types of fine plants that Allah has caused to grow.
Allah has created different types of plants in the world.
The earth is full of splendid and fair species of vegetation.

source_text:
Verse: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

Tafsir: Surely in that there is a sign an indication of the perfection of His power exalted be He; but most of them in God’s knowledge are not believers kāna here according to Sībawayhi is extra.

hype_questions: What is the sign that God has revealed?
Why do most people refuse to believe in God's power?
How does God's perfection manifest itself?
propositions: There is a sign.
Most of them are not believers according to God’s knowledge.
God’s power is exalted and His perfection is evident.

source_text:
Verse: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: And surely your Lord He is the Mighty One Who will exact vengeance from the disbelievers the Merciful Who shows mercy to believers.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's mercy?
How does Allah show mercy to believers?
What will happen to those who disbelieve in Allah?
propositions: Your Lord is the Almighty.
Your Lord is the Merciful One.
Allah will exact vengeance from the disbelievers.
Allah shows mercy to believers.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember˺ when your Lord called out to Moses, “Go to the wrongdoing people—

Tafsir: And mention O Muhammad (s) to your people when your Lord called to Moses on the night he saw the fire and the bush saying ‘Go to the wrongdoing folk as a messenger

hype_questions: What is the significance of Moses' encounter with the fire and the bush?
How did Muhammad (s) become a messenger to the people?
What is the nature of the 'wrongdoing folk' that Moses was called to address?
propositions: Your Lord called out to Moses.
Moses saw the fire and the bush on the night he was summoned by God.
You should mention Muhammad (s) to your people when your Lord calls you to do so.
Go to the wrongdoing folk as a messenger.

source_text:
Verse: the people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear ˹Allah˺?”

Tafsir: Pharaoh’s folk to them as well as him — they wronged their souls by disbelieving in God and wronged the Children of Israel by enslaving them — Will they not a-lā the hamza indicates a negation meant as a rebuke show fear?’ of God by being obedient to Him and affirm His Oneness?

hype_questions: Will the people of Pharaoh fear God?
Why should the people of Pharaoh be obedient to God?
What is the consequence of disbelieving in God for the people of Pharaoh?
propositions: The people of Pharaoh will not fear Allah.
Pharaoh's folk wronged their souls by disbelieving in God and wronging the Children of Israel by enslaving them.
They should show fear of God by being obedient to Him and affirming His Oneness.

source_text:
Verse: He replied, “My Lord! I fear that they will reject me.

Tafsir: He Moses said ‘My Lord I fear they will deny me

hype_questions: Will the people reject him?
What is Moses' concern about?
How does Moses feel about being rejected?
propositions: He feared that they would deny him.
Moses said, 'My Lord, I fear they will deny me'.
The people might reject Moses.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹so˺ my heart will be broken and my tongue will be tied. So send Aaron along ˹as a messenger˺.

Tafsir: and that anguish will constrain my breast because of their denial of me and that my tongue will not utter clearly to deliver the Message because of the knot in it. So give the Mission to my brother Aaron alongside me.

hype_questions: What will cause my heart to be broken?
How will I deliver the Message if my tongue is tied?
Who should accompany me on this Mission?
propositions: My heart will be broken due to their denial of me.
The anguish caused by their denial will constrain my breast.
I will not utter clearly to deliver the Message because of a knot in my tongue.
Give the Mission to my brother Aaron alongside me.

source_text:
Verse: Also, they have a charge against me, so I fear they may kill me.”

Tafsir: And I have sinned against them by my slaying of the Egyptian man and I fear they will slay me’ for this.

hype_questions: Will they kill me?
What will be my punishment?
Can I escape retribution?
propositions: I have sinned against them by slaying the Egyptian man.
They may kill me for this.

source_text:
Verse: Allah responded, “Certainly not! So go, both of you, with Our signs. We will be with you, listening.

Tafsir: Said He exalted be He ‘Certainly not! they shall not slay you. Go both of you you and your brother — this address although in the dual form is predominantly for the person present as opposed to the absent one — with Our signs. We will indeed be with you hearing what you say and what is said to you ma‘akum the two Moses and Aaron are referred to here with the plural pronoun.

hype_questions: What does Allah mean by 'Our signs'?
How will Allah be with the Prophet and his companion?
What is the significance of using the plural pronoun for Moses and Aaron?
propositions: Allah responded, saying 'Certainly not!'
They shall not slay you.
Go both of you with Our signs.
We will be with you, listening.
The address is predominantly for the person present.
Moses and Aaron are referred to here with the plural pronoun.

source_text:
Verse: Go to Pharaoh and say, ‘We are messengers from the Lord of all worlds,

Tafsir: So the two of you approach Pharaoh and say “Indeed We are — indeed each of the two of us is the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds to you

hype_questions: What does it mean to be a messenger from God?
How do I approach someone with important news?
What is the significance of being a messenger in Islamic context?
propositions: Go to Pharaoh and say, 'We are messengers from the Lord of all worlds'.
Each of the two of you is the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds.
The two messengers approach Pharaoh with this message.

source_text:
Verse: ˹commanded to say:˺ ‘Let the Children of Israel go with us.’’”

Tafsir: that you should let go forth with us to Syria the Children of Israel” ’. So they approached him and said to him that which has been mentioned.

hype_questions: What is the significance of letting the Children of Israel go with the Prophet Muhammad?
Why did the Prophet Muhammad command the Children of Israel to accompany him to Syria?
How did the Children of Israel respond to the Prophet Muhammad's request?
propositions: The Prophet Muhammad commanded the Children of Israel to go with him.
The destination of the Prophet Muhammad's journey was Syria.
The Children of Israel agreed to accompany the Prophet Muhammad.

source_text:
Verse: Pharaoh protested, “Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed several years of your life in our care?

Tafsir: He Pharaoh said to Moses ‘Did we not rear you among us in our homes as a child? as an infant only recently born but weaned and did you not stay with us for years of your life? for thirty years — he would dress from Pharaoh’s clothes and ride chariots of his and was referred to as Pharaoh’s son.

hype_questions: Did we not raise you among us as a child?
How long did Moses stay with Pharaoh's family?
What was Moses referred to as by Pharaoh?
propositions: Pharaoh raised Moses among his people as a child.
Moses stayed in Pharaoh's care for thirty years.
Moses was referred to as Pharaoh's son.

source_text:
Verse: Then you did what you did, being ˹utterly˺ ungrateful!”

Tafsir: And you committed that deed of yours — namely his slaying of the Egyptian — being an ingrate’ a denier of my favours to you in having reared you among us and not enslaved you.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be ungrateful?
How can someone be considered an ingrate?
Why was the Egyptian person treated unfairly?
propositions: You were raised among us and not enslaved.
He committed the act of slaying the Egyptian.
You are being described as ungrateful for not showing appreciation.

source_text:
Verse: Moses replied, “I did it then, lacking guidance.

Tafsir: He Moses said ‘I did that then when I was astray from the knowledge and the Message which God would later give me.

hype_questions: Does Moses acknowledge his lack of guidance when performing the action?
How does Moses explain his actions in light of receiving later guidance from God?
What is Moses' state of mind when he performs the action?
propositions: Moses performed an action.
Moses was astray from knowledge and the Message of God at the time of performing the action.
God would later give Moses guidance.

source_text:
Verse: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me wisdom and made me one of the messengers.

Tafsir: So I fled from you as I was afraid of you. Then my Lord gave me judgement knowledge and made me one of the messengers.

hype_questions: What is the significance of fearing Allah in Islam?
How does Allah grant wisdom to His messengers?
What are the qualities required to become a messenger of Allah?
propositions: The speaker fled from Allah due to fear.
Allah granted the speaker wisdom.
Allah made the speaker one of His messengers.

source_text:
Verse: How can that be a ‘favour,’ of which you remind me, when ˹it was only because˺ you ˹have˺ enslaved the Children of Israel?”

Tafsir: That is a favour with which you now reproach me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel’ an ‘abbadta banī Isrā’īl is explicative of tilka ‘that’ in other words you have enslaved them but not me there is no favour in that for your enslavement of them is wrong some scholars have reckoned there to be an interrogative hamza of denial at the beginning of this verse a-tilka ni‘matun ‘is that a favour?’.

hype_questions: Is enslaving a people ever considered a favour?
Can the actions of one's ancestors be used to justify their own wrongdoings?
What is the nature of the 'favour' that is being referenced in this verse?
propositions: You enslaved the Children of Israel.
There is no favour in your enslavement of them.
Your actions are wrong, regardless of whether they were done to you or not.

source_text:
Verse: Pharaoh asked, “And what is ‘the Lord of all worlds’?”

Tafsir: Pharaoh said to Moses ‘And what is “the Lord of the Worlds” ’ the One Whose Messenger you say you indeed are? In other words what exactly is He? And since there is no way for creation to know the true nature of God but only to know Him through an articulation of His attributes Moses blessings and peace be upon him responds to him with mention of some of these attributes

hype_questions: What is the true nature of God?

Verse: But the one who had knowledge of the Scripture said, “I can bring it to you in the blink of an eye.” So when Solomon saw it placed before him, he exclaimed, “This is by the grace of my Lord to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, it is only for their own good. But whoever is ungrateful, surely my Lord is Self-Sufficient, Most Generous.”

Tafsir: The one who had knowledge of the revealed Scripture — and this was one Āsif b. Barkhiyā a righteous individual with knowledge of God’s Greatest Name which when invoked in supplication for something it is immediately granted — said ‘I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you after you look at something. So he the afreet said to him ‘Look up towards the heaven’ which he did and when his glance returned in front of him he found it Bilqīs’ throne placed before him — for in the instance in which Solomon looked up to the heaven Āsif supplicated by invoking the Greatest Name that God bring it thereto; and this was done by having it travel under the earth until it sprung up below Solomon’s seat kursī. Then when he saw it standing still before him he said ‘This bringing it to me is of my Lord’s bounty that He may try me test me whether I give thanks read a-ashkur pronouncing both hamzas; or by replacing the second one with an alif; or by not pronouncing the second one but inserting an alif between the one not pronounced and the other one or without the insertion or am ungrateful for the favour. And whoever gives thanks gives thanks only for his own sake because the reward for his thanks shall be his and whoever is ungrateful for the favour should know then my Lord is surely Independent with no need of his thanks Generous’ by being bounteous to those who are ungrateful for it.

Verse: Then she was told, “Enter the palace.” But when she saw the hall, she thought it was a body of water, so she bared her legs. Solomon said. “It is just a palace paved with crystal.” ˹At last˺ she declared, “My Lord! I have certainly wronged my soul. Now I ˹fully˺ submit myself along with Solomon to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.”

Tafsir: It was also said to her ‘Enter the palace hallway’ — this was a transparent white glass floor underneath which flowed sweet water that contained fish. Solomon had it made when he was told that her legs and feet resembled the shanks of a mule. And when she saw it she supposed it to be a pool of water and so she bared her legs to wade through it. Meanwhile Solomon was seated on his throne at the front part of the palace hallway and he saw that her legs and feet were in fact fair. He said to her ‘It is a hallway paved smooth with crystal’ and thereafter he called her to submit to God. She said ‘My Lord indeed I have wronged myself by worshipping other than You and I submit with Solomon to God the Lord of the Worlds’. He wanted to marry her but disliked the hair on her legs. So the devils made a depilatory lime mixture nūra and she removed it therewith. He married her and had great love for her. And he let her remain as ruler of her kingdom and would visit her once a month staying for three days every time. Her reign came to an end at the same time as that of Solomon. It is reported that he became king at the age of 13 and died at the age of 53 — Glory be to the One whose enduring sovereignty will never end!

hype_questions: What is the story of the woman who was told to enter a palace, but thought it was a pool of water?
How did Solomon marry a queen and let her remain as ruler of her kingdom?
What happened to the devils when they tried to stop Solomon from marrying the queen?
propositions: She was told to enter a palace.
The palace had a transparent white glass floor underneath which flowed sweet water that contained fish.
Solomon saw that her legs and feet were fair, not like those of a mule.
He said it was a hallway paved smooth with crystal.
She submitted herself along with Solomon to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.
The devils made a depilatory lime mixture nūra.
She removed the hair on her legs using the nūra mixture.
Solomon married her and had great love for her.
He let her remain as ruler of her kingdom.
Her reign came to an end at the same time as that of Solomon.

source_text:
Verse: And We certainly sent to the people of Thamûd their brother salih, proclaiming, “Worship Allah,” but they suddenly split into two opposing groups.

Tafsir: And verily We sent to Thamūd their brother in terms of his belonging to the same tribe Sālih with the following decree ‘Worship God!’ affirm His Oneness. And lo! they then became two parties quarrelling with one another over religion one party having become believers upon his arrival as messenger to them and the other party disbelievers.

hype_questions: Did Allah's message of oneness and worship bring people together or drive them apart?
How did the people of Thamud respond to their brother Salih's call to worship God?
What was the outcome for those who believed in Salih's message versus those who rejected it?
propositions: We sent Salih to the people of Thamud with a decree to worship God.
The people of Thamud split into two opposing groups over religion after Salih's arrival.
One party became believers upon his arrival, while the other remained disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: He urged ˹the disbelieving group˺, “O my people! Why do you ˹seek to˺ hasten the torment If only you sought Allah’s forgiveness so you may be shown mercy!”

Tafsir: He said to the deniers ‘O my people why do you seek to hasten on evil before seeking good? in other words why do you seek to hasten on chastisement instead of mercy when you say ‘If what you bring us is true then bring us the chastisement!’ Why do you not ask God to forgive you your idolatry so that you might be shown mercy?’ and not be chastised.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of seeking evil before good?
Why do people ask for punishment instead of mercy?
How can one seek forgiveness from God and avoid chastisement?
propositions: He urged the disbelieving group to hasten the torment.
If only you sought Allah’s forgiveness so you may be shown mercy!
Why do you not ask God to forgive you your idolatry so that you might be shown mercy?
You seek to hasten on chastisement instead of mercy when you say ‘If what you bring us is true then bring us the chastisement!’
People ask for punishment instead of mercy

source_text:
Verse: They replied, “You and your followers are a bad omen for us.” He responded, “Your omens are destined by Allah. In fact, you are ˹only˺ a people being tested.”

Tafsir: They said ‘We augur evil ittayyarnā is actually tatayyarnā but the tā’ has been assimilated with the tā’ and a conjunctive hamza added of you and of those who are with you’ namely the believers — when they the tribe of Thamūd were deprived of rain and suffered hunger. He said ‘Your evil augury is with God — He has given it to you; nay but you are a people being tried’ being tested with good and evil turns of fortune.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be a people being tested?
How do we interpret the concept of evil augury in Islam?
Can we find good fortune amidst trials and tribulations?
propositions: They said they augur evil.
Their evil augury is with God, He has given it to them.
You are a people being tested.

source_text:
Verse: And there were in the city nine ˹elite˺ men who spread corruption in the land, never doing what is right.

Tafsir: And there were in the city the city of Thamūd a band of nine men that is nine men who were causing corruption in the land with acts of disobedience which included their corroding of dinar and dirham coins rendering them worthless and did not reform their ways through obedience to God.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of corruption in a society?
How can individuals reform their ways and follow obedience to God?
What is the impact of disobedience on economic systems?
propositions: There were nine men causing corruption in the land through acts of disobedience.
The corruption was due to the corroding of coins, rendering them worthless.
They did not reform their ways despite being disobedient to God.

source_text:
Verse: They vowed, “Let us swear by Allah that we will take him and his family down by night. Then we will certainly say to his ˹closest˺ heirs, ‘We did not witness the murder of his family. We are definitely telling the truth.’”

Tafsir: They said that is some said to others ‘Swear to one another by God that we will attack him by night la-nubayyitannahu; or read la-tubayyitunnahu ‘that you will attack him by night’ together with his folk that is those who believed in him in other words swear that we will kill them at night; then we will surely say la-naqūlanna; or read la-taqūlunna ‘you surely will say’ to his heir the avenger of his blood that we did not witness we were not present at the destruction of his folk read muhlika or mahlika meaning ‘the destroying of them’ or ‘their death’ respectively and so we do not know who killed them and that indeed we are being truthful’.

hype_questions: What would happen to the avenger of his blood if they were to claim innocence?
How would the believers respond to accusations of killing his family?
What would be the consequence of swearing by God to attack someone by night?
propositions: They vowed to take him and his family down by night.
They swore that they will attack his folk at night.
They said they did not witness the destruction of his folk.
They claimed they were telling the truth about not witnessing the murder.
The avenger of his blood would surely say they were not present.

Allah also made a plan.

source_text:
Verse: So their homes are there, ˹but completely˺ ruined because of their wrongdoing. Surely in this is a lesson for people of knowledge.

Tafsir: So those then are their houses lying deserted khāwiyatan is in the accusative because it is a circumstantial qualifier the operator of which is the import of the demonstrative pronoun tilka ‘those’ because of the evil which they did that is their disbelief. Surely in that there is a sign a lesson for a people who have knowledge of Our power and are thus admonished.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of a person's disbelief?
How do people who have knowledge of Allah's power benefit from this verse?

The evil they did is their disbelief.
There is a sign in that destruction, a lesson for people with knowledge of Allah's power.

Tafsir: And We delivered those who believed in Sālih — and they numbered 4000 — and were fearful of idolatry.

How many people were delivered by Allah according to the Quran?

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ Lot, when he rebuked ˹the men of˺ his people, “Do you commit that shameful deed while you can see ˹one another˺?

Tafsir: And Lot Lūtan is in the accusative because of an implied udhkur ‘mention’ before it and it Lūtan is substituted by the following idh qāla … when he said to his people ‘What! Do you commit such abomination namely homosexual intercourse while you watch? that is to say while you watch one another so engrossed are you in the sinful act?

The men of Lot's people committed shameful deeds while they could see each other.
Homosexual intercourse is considered an abomination in the context of Lot's people.

Tafsir: What! Do you read a-innakum pronouncing both hamzas or by not pronouncing the second and inserting an alif between the two in both cases come unto men in lust instead of women? Nay but you are truly a people in ignorance’ of the consequence of your action.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon the servants He has chosen.” ˹Ask the disbelievers,˺ “Which is better: Allah or whatever ˹gods˺ they associate ˹with Him˺?”

Tafsir: Say O Muhammad (s) ‘Praise be to God for the destruction of the disbelievers of past communities and peace be on His servants whom He has chosen’. Is God read a-Allāhu pronouncing both hamzas; or by substituting an alif for the second one; or by not pronouncing the second one but inserting an alif between the one not pronounced and the other one or without such an insertion better for those who worship Him or the partners which they ascribe? read either tushrikūna ‘you ascribe’ or yushrikūna ‘they ascribe’ they being the people of Mecca the partners they ascribe to Him in other words are such gods better for those who worship them?

hype_questions: Is it better to worship one God or multiple gods?
Do the partners ascribed by humans bring any benefits?
Can reading Allah's name with hamzas improve one's spiritual state?

Reading Allah's name with hamzas does not improve one's spiritual state.

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who created the heavens and the earth, and sends down rain for you from the sky, by which We cause delightful gardens to grow? You could never cause their trees to grow. Was it another god besides Allah?” Absolutely not! But they are a people who set up equals ˹to Allah˺!

Tafsir: Or He Who created the heavens and the earth and sends down for you water from the heaven whereby We cause to grow there is a shift here from third person to that of the first person plural splendid gardens hadā’iq is the plural of hadīqa which is an enclosed garden whose trees you could never cause to grow? because of you do not have the ability for it. Is there a god a-ilāhun here and in the seven instances in which it occurs read by pronouncing both hamzas or by not pronouncing the second inserting an alif between the two in both cases with God? who has helped Him in all of this? In other words there is no god with Him. Nay but they are a people who ascribe equals to Him who associate with God others.

hype_questions: Is there a god besides Allah?
Who has helped Allah in creating the heavens and earth?
What is the nature of the divine power that creates delightful gardens?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and the earth.
Allah sends down rain for us from the sky.
We cause delightful gardens to grow with this rain.
Humans cannot cause trees to grow without Allah's help.
There is no god besides Allah.
Humans ascribe equals to Allah who associate with Him others.

Verse: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who made the earth a place of settlement, caused rivers to flow through it, placed firm mountains upon it, and set a barrier between ˹fresh and salt˺ bodies of water? Was it another god besides Allah?” Absolutely not! But most of them do not know.

Tafsir: Or He Who made the earth an abode of stability that does not constantly shake beneath the feet of its inhabitants and made rivers to flow throughout it and set firm mountains for it with which He fixed the earth in place and set an isthmus between the two seas between the sweet one and the salty one the one not mixing with the other. Is there a god with God? Nay but most of them have no knowledge of His Oneness.

Rivers flow throughout the earth.

An isthmus was set between the two seas, separating sweet and salty waters.
There is no god besides Allah.
Most people do not know about the Oneness of Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who responds to the distressed when they cry to Him, relieving ˹their˺ affliction, and ˹Who˺ makes you successors in the earth? Is it another god besides Allah? Yet you are hardly mindful!”

Tafsir: Or He Who answers the desperate one the anguished person suffering harm when he calls to Him and Who removes his distress from him and from others and makes you successors in the earth the annexation khulafā’a l-ardi ‘successors of the earth’ has the same meaning as fī ‘in’ khulafā’a fī’l-ardi ‘successors in the earth’ in other words each generation succeeding the one before it. Is there a god with God? Little do you remember little are you admonished read mā tadhakkarūna ‘do you remember’; or read yadhdhakkarūna ‘do they remember’ where in both cases the tā’ has been assimilated with the dhāl; the mā is extra used to make less what is already ‘little’.

Is there a god with God?

He Who answers the desperate one the anguished person suffering harm when he calls to Him
Is it another god besides Allah?
Yet you are hardly mindful!
The annexation khulafā’a l-ardi 'successors of the earth' has the same meaning as fī ‘in’ khulafā’a fī’l-ardi 'successors in the earth'
Each generation succeeding the one before it
Do you remember?
Do they remember?

Verse: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who guides you in the darkness of the land and sea, Is it another god besides Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate ˹with Him˺!

Tafsir: Or He Who guides you shows you the way to your destinations in the darkness of the land and the sea by the stars at night and by the various landmarks during the day and Who sends forth the winds as harbingers of His mercy ahead of the rain. Is there a god with God? Exalted be God high above what others they associate with Him!

Who sends forth the winds as harbingers of His mercy ahead of the rain.
Is there a god with God?

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who originates the creation then resurrects it, and gives you provisions from the heavens and the earth? Is it another god besides Allah?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Show ˹me˺ your proof, if what you say is true.”

Tafsir: Or He Who originates creation in the wombs from a sperm-drop then brings it back again after death as established by the proofs for this resurrection even if you do not acknowledge it; and Who provides for you from the heaven rain and from the earth vegetation. Is there a god with God? In other words none of the things mentioned is done by anyone other than God and there is no god with Him. Say O Muhammad (s) ‘Produce your proof your definitive argument if you are truthful’ about their being a god with Me who has done any of the things mentioned.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “None in the heavens and the earth has knowledge of the unseen except Allah. Nor do they know when they will be resurrected.

Tafsir: They the disbelievers also asked him when the Hour will come to pass and the following was revealed Say ‘No one in the heavens or the earth knows be it angels or human beings the Unseen namely what is hidden from them except God He knows it and they are not aware the disbelievers of Mecca like others when is the time in which they will be resurrected.

Nor do they know when they will be resurrected.

source_text:
Verse: No! Their knowledge of the Hereafter amounts to ignorance. In fact, they are in doubt about it. In truth, they are ˹totally˺ blind to it.

Tafsir: Nay has their knowledge come to comprise read adraka similar to the 4th verbal form akrama ‘he was kind to’; a variant reading has iddāraka which is actually tadāraka with the tā’ changed into a dāl and assimilated with the other dāl and a conjunctive hamza added meaning ‘attained’ or ‘caught up with’ the Hereafter? such that they have reason to ask about the time of its coming — not so Nay for they are in doubt of it. Rather they are blind to it ‘amūna ‘blind’ as in blindness of the heart; this statement is rhetorically more powerful than the preceding one; the origin of the term is ‘amiyūn but the damma vowel is deemed too heavy for the yā’ and has been moved to the mīm after dropping its kasra vowel.

hype_questions: What is the nature of knowledge about the Hereafter?
How do people reason about the time of the Hereafter's arrival?
Can one attain or catch up with the Hereafter?
propositions: Their knowledge of the Hereafter amounts to ignorance.
They are in doubt about it.
They are blind to it.

source_text:
Verse: For there is nothing hidden in the heavens or the earth without being ˹written˺ in a perfect Record.

Tafsir: And there is not a thing hidden in the heaven and the earth the hā’ tā’ marbūta of ghā’ibatun is hyperbole in other words anything that is completely hidden from people but it is in a manifest Book namely in the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz and in God’s concealed knowledge an example of which is the time of the chastising of the disbelievers.

Can God's knowledge be hidden from humans?

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: And when the decree ˹of the Hour˺ comes to pass against them, We will bring forth for them a beast from the earth, telling them that the people had no sure faith in Our revelations.

Tafsir: And when the word of judgement falls upon them when they deserve that chastisement befalls them as well as all other disbelievers We shall bring forth for them a beast from the earth which shall speak to them saying that is which shall speak in Arabic to those who are alive at the time when it appears among its other statements it will say to them on Our behalf ‘Indeed mankind read tukallimuhum inna’l-nāsa; a variant has tukallimuhum bi-anna’l-nāsa ‘to tell them that mankind’ had no faith in Our signs’ in other words they did not believe in the Qur’ān and what it comprises of the mention of resurrection reckoning and requital. With its the beast’s appearance the enjoining of decency and forbidding of indecency will cease and thereafter no disbeliever will believe — just as God revealed to Noah when He said to him None of your people will believe except he who has already believed Q. 1136.

hype_questions: Will anyone believe after witnessing the beast?
What is the consequence of disbelieving in the Quran's signs?
Can anyone change their belief after witnessing the beast?
propositions: When the decree of the Hour comes to pass, We will bring forth a beast from the earth.
The people had no sure faith in Our revelations.
Mankind did not believe in Our signs.
With its appearance, the enjoining of decency and forbidding of indecency will cease.
No disbeliever will believe thereafter.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Watch for˺ the Day We will gather from every faith-community a group of those who denied Our revelations, and they will be driven in ranks.

Tafsir: And mention the day when We shall gather from every community a group of those who denied Our signs namely their leaders the ones whom they followed and they will be set in array assembled with the last of them brought together with the first and then led away

hype_questions: What happens to those who denied God's revelations?

source_text:
Verse: When they ˹finally˺ come before their Lord, He will ask ˹them˺, “Did you deny My revelations without ˹even˺ comprehending them? Or what ˹exactly˺ did you do?”

Tafsir: until when they arrive at the site of the Reckoning He exalted be He shall say to them ‘Did you deny My prophets by denying My signs without comprehending them from the perspective of your denial in knowledge or what ammā the interrogative mā has been assimilated with am ‘or’ was it dhā is a relative pronoun in other words it is in fact mā alladhī that you did? with the commands given to you.

hype_questions: Did they deny My prophets without comprehending My signs?
What exactly did they do with the commands given to them?
Will they be held accountable for their denial?
propositions: They will be asked if they denied My revelations without understanding them.
Their denial of My prophets is equivalent to denying My signs without comprehension.
They were given commands, but did they follow them?

source_text:
Verse: And the decree ˹of torment˺ will be justified against them for their wrongdoing, leaving them speechless.

Tafsir: And the word of judgement shall fall the chastisement will be due upon them because of the evil they committed that is because of what they associated with God and they will not speak since they will have no valid argument.

hype_questions: What happens to those who associate other deities with God?
Can they find a valid argument when faced with the consequences of their actions?
How will they be held accountable for their wrongdoing?

They associated themselves with God, which led to their downfall.
They will not speak since they will have no valid argument.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not see that We made the night for them to rest in and the day bright? Surely in this are signs for those who believe.

Tafsir: Do they not see that We made We created the night that they like others may rest in it and the day for sight? meaning for people to see in it so that they may go about their business therein. Surely in that there are signs indications of His power exalted be He for a people who believe — they the believers are singled out for mention because they benefit from such signs in their faith in contrast to the disbelievers.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creating night and day?
How do people benefit from signs in their faith?
What distinguishes believers from disbelievers?
propositions: We created the night for them to rest.
The day was made for sight so that they may go about their business therein.
In the signs of His power, there are indications for a people who believe.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹beware of˺ the Day the Trumpet will be blown, and all those in the heavens and all those on the earth will be horrified ˹to the point of death˺, except those Allah wills ˹to spare˺. And all will come before Him, fully humbled.

Tafsir: And the day when the Trumpet will be blown the Horn will be blown the First Blast by the archangel Isrāfīl and whoever is in the heavens and the earth will be terrified that is a fright that brings about death — as is stated in another verse and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon Q. 3968 the past tense fazi‘a is used to express the fact that such events will have occurred; except whom God will namely Gabriel Michael Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death. According to Ibn ‘Abbās however these excepted individuals are the martyrs who are described as living with their Lord provided for by Him’ Q. 3169. And all kullun the nunation compensates for the missing genitive annexation in other words and every one of them after being brought back to life on the Day of Resurrection will come to Him read in the form of the verb atawhu or the active participle ātūhu in utter humility humbled the past tense atawhu is used to express the fact that this will have happened.

hype_questions: What will happen when the Trumpet is blown?
Who will be spared from death on the Day of Resurrection?
How will people behave on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: The Trumpet will be blown.
Allah wills to spare some individuals from death.
Everyone who is in the heavens and earth will be terrified when the Trumpet is blown.
God will bring back to life those who have died.
Every person will come before Allah on the Day of Resurrection, fully humbled.

source_text:
Verse: Now you see the mountains, thinking they are firmly fixed, but they are travelling ˹just˺ like clouds. ˹That is˺ the design of Allah, Who has perfected everything. Surely He is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: And you see the mountains you notice them at the moment of the Blast supposing them to be still stationary in their place because of their tremendous size while they drift like passing clouds like the drifting of the rain when it is blown around by the wind in other words they the mountains will be drifting in like manner until they eventually fall to the ground whereby they are flattened before becoming like tufts of ‘wool’ cf. Q. 1015 and then ‘scattered dust’ cf. Q. 566. God’s handiwork sun‘a a verbal noun emphasising the import of the preceding sentence and which has been annexed in a genitive construction to its agent Allāhi ‘God’ after the omission of its operator Who has perfected everything that He has made. Truly He is aware of what you do taf‘alūna; or read yaf‘alūna ‘what they do’ namely His enemies what they do in the way of disobedience and His friends in the way of obedience.

hype_questions: Will the mountains eventually fall to the ground?
How does Allah's power manifest in the natural world?
What is the nature of Allah's awareness of human actions?
propositions: The mountains appear stationary but are actually moving like clouds.
Allah has perfected everything He creates.
God's handiwork emphasizes the importance of His actions.
Allah is aware of what His enemies and friends do in terms of obedience or disobedience.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever comes with a good deed will be rewarded with what is better, and they will be secure from the horror on that Day.

Tafsir: Whoever brings a good deed namely the profession of ‘there is no god but God’ on the Day of Resurrection shall have good shall have a reward for it because of it this khayrun is not the comparative ‘better’ since there is no deed better than a good deed. In another verse it is stated that he shall have tenfold the like of it Q. 6160; and they namely those who bring such good deeds shall be secure from the terror of that day min faza‘i yawmi’idhin if read as a genitive annexation; or min faza‘in yawma’idhin ‘from terror on that day’.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who brings a good deed on the Day of Resurrection?

Will someone who brings a good deed be secure from terror on that day?
propositions: Whoever comes with a good deed will be rewarded with what is better.
The profession of ‘there is no god but God’ is a good deed that shall have tenfold the like of it.
Those who bring such good deeds shall be secure from terror on that day.

source_text:
Verse: And whoever comes with an evil deed will be hurled face-first into the Fire. Are you rewarded except for what you used to do?

Tafsir: And whoever brings an evil deed namely the ascribing of partners to God their faces shall be thrust into the Fire having been oriented towards it — ‘faces’ are specifically mentioned here because of all the sensory organs it is where a person’s dignity resides and so other parts of the body are more deserving of punishment. It shall be said to them in reproach ‘Are you requited except the requital for what you used to do?’ in the way of idolatry and acts of disobedience.

hype_questions: Will I be rewarded for my good deeds, or will I face punishment for my past wrongdoings?

propositions: Whoever brings an evil deed will be hurled face-first into the Fire.
Are you rewarded except for what you used to do?

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city ˹of Mecca˺, Who has made it sacred, and to Him belongs everything. And I am commanded to be one of those who ˹fully˺ submit ˹to Him˺,

Tafsir: Say to them I have been commanded only to worship the Lord of this land namely Mecca which He has made inviolable which He has made a secure Sanctuary one in which no human blood may be shed no person may be wronged none of its prey may be hunted and a sanctuary which is never deserted. Such were the graces bestowed by God upon its inhabitants the tribe of Quraysh graces whereby God has spared their land the suffering and civil strife common to all the other lands of the Arabs; and to Whom exalted be He all things belong for He is their Lord Creator and Possessor. And I have been commanded to be of those who submit to God by affirming His Oneness;

hype_questions: What is the significance of Mecca as a sacred city in Islam?
How does God's protection and provision impact the lives of its inhabitants?

propositions: The Lord of this city (Mecca) has made it sacred.
God has spared the land of Mecca from suffering and civil strife.
All things belong to God, Who is their Creator and Possessor.

source_text:
Verse: and to recite the Quran.” Then whoever chooses to be guided, it is only for their own good. But whoever chooses to stray, say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I am only a warner.”

Tafsir: and to recite the Qur’ān to you as a call to faith. So whoever is guided to it is guided only for his own sake since the reward for his being guided will be his; and whoever goes astray from faith and errs from the path of guidance say to him ‘I am just one of the warners’ the threateners and therefore my duty is only to deliver the Message — this was revealed before the command to fight against the disbelievers.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of reciting the Quran?

Guidance is only for an individual's own good.
A warner's duty is to deliver the Message, regardless of the outcome.

source_text:
Verse: And say, “All praise is for Allah! He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them. And your Lord is never unaware of what you do.”

Tafsir: And say ‘Praise be to God. He will show you His signs and you will recognise them. Thus on the day of Badr God showed them how it was to be killed to be taken prisoner and to be beaten by the angels on their faces and backs; and God hastened on for them the punishment of the Fire. And your Lord is not oblivious of what they do’ ya‘malūna; or read ta‘malūna ‘what you do’ but grants them respite until their appointed time of requital.

hype_questions: What are the signs that Allah will show to His servants?

propositions: Allah is worthy of praise.

Allah grants respite to those who disobey Him until their appointed time of requital.

source_text:

Tafsir: Tā sīn mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

source_text:

hype_questions: What is the nature of the clear Book?

source_text:
Verse: We narrate to you ˹O Prophet˺ part of the story of Moses and Pharaoh in truth for people who believe.

Tafsir: We will recount narrate to you something of the tale of Moses and Pharaoh truthfully for a people who believe for their sake since they are the ones to benefit from such an account.

hype_questions: What is the story of Moses and Pharaoh?

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Pharaoh ˹arrogantly˺ elevated himself in the land and divided its people into ˹subservient˺ groups, one of which he persecuted, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women. He was truly one of the corruptors.

Tafsir: Truly Pharaoh had exalted himself in the land the land of Egypt and reduced its people into sects groups to serve him oppressing a group of them namely the Children of Israel slaughtering their sons the new-born and sparing their women keeping them alive — for some of the Egyptian priests had told him ‘A new-born of the Children of Israel shall bring about the end of your kingdom’. Indeed he was of those who cause corruption through the use of slaughter and otherwise.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of oppressing a group of people?
How did Pharaoh's actions affect his kingdom?
What was the reason behind Pharaoh's slaughter of newborns?
propositions: Pharaoh elevated himself in Egypt.
He divided its people into groups to serve him, oppressing one group, specifically the Children of Israel.
The Egyptian priests warned Pharaoh that a new-born of the Children of Israel would bring about the end of his kingdom.
Pharaoh was truly one of the corruptors.

source_text:
Verse: But it was Our Will to favour those who were oppressed in the land, making them models ˹of faith˺ as well as successors;

Tafsir: And We desired to show favour to those who were oppressed in the land and to make them exemplars read a’immatan pronouncing both hamzas or by replacing the second one with a yā’ whose good example would be followed and to make them the inheritors of Pharaoh’s kingdom;

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Allah's favour towards those oppressed in the land?

These individuals became models of faith and successors.

source_text:
Verse: and to establish them in the land; and through them show Pharaoh, Haman,

Tafsir: and to establish them in the land the land of Egypt and Syria and to show Pharaoh and Hāmān and their hosts a variant reading has wa-yarā Fir‘awnu wa-Hāmānu wa-junūduhumā ‘so that Pharaoh and Hāmān and their hosts might see’ with all three nouns in the nominative from them that of which they were apprehensive that which they feared of the new-born Israelite who would bring about the end of their kingdom.

hype_questions: What was the purpose of establishing the Israelites in Egypt and Syria?

propositions: The Prophet was sent to establish the Israelites in the land.
Pharaoh, Haman, and their hosts were apprehensive of the new-born Israelite who would bring about the end of their kingdom.
The Prophet's mission was to show Pharaoh and Haman a variant reading that would make them see the reality.

source_text:
Verse: We inspired the mother of Moses: “Nurse him, but when you fear for him, put him then into the river, and do not fear or grieve. We will certainly return him to you, and make him one of the messengers.”

Tafsir: And We revealed by inspiration or in a dream to the mother of Moses — who was the said new-born; his sister was the only other person aware of his birth — ‘Suckle him then when you fear for him cast him into the waters namely the Nile and do not fear that he should drown or grieve for being separated from him for We will restore him to you and make him one of the messengers’. She suckled him for three months during which he never cried. She then began to fear for him and so she placed him in a basket coated with pitch and made as a cradle for him on the inside. She then closed it and cast it into the waters of the Nile at night.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Moses' birth in Islamic tradition?
How did the mother of Moses care for her newborn son before sending him to the Nile?
What role does patience play in the story of Moses' upbringing?
propositions: The mother of Moses was instructed by God to nurse her son but to put him into the river if she feared for his safety.
God promised to return Moses to his mother and make him one of His messengers.
Moses was suckled by his mother for three months without crying, after which she placed him in a basket and sent him to the Nile.
The Nile is mentioned as the location where Moses was cast into the water.
God will restore those who are sent away from them to their families.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹it so happened that˺ Pharaoh’s people picked him up, only to become their enemy and source of grief. Surely Pharaoh, Haman, and their soldiers were sinful.

Tafsir: Then Pharaoh’s folk aids picked him up with him still in the basket the morning following that night — it was placed him in front of him Pharaoh and then opened and Moses was brought out of it sucking milk from his thumb — to be at the end of the affair an enemy slaying their menfolk and a cause of grief to them enslaving their womenfolk a variant reading for hazanan is huznan both of which are alternative forms of the verbal noun and it functions as an active participle derived from hazanahu which is like ahzanahu ‘he caused him grief’. Truly Pharaoh and his minister Hāmān and their hosts were sinners that is disobedient and so they were punished at his Moses’s hands.

hype_questions: What was the consequence of Pharaoh's actions?
How did Moses ultimately punish Pharaoh and his followers?
What role did Moses play in resolving the conflict with Pharaoh?
propositions: Pharaoh’s people picked him up, only to become their enemy and source of grief.
Moses was brought out of the basket sucking milk from his thumb.
Pharaoh and his minister Hāmān and their hosts were sinners that is disobedient and so they were punished at Moses's hands.

source_text:
Verse: Pharaoh’s wife said ˹to him˺, “˹This baby is˺ a source of joy for me and you. Do not kill him. Perhaps he may be useful to us or we may adopt him as a son.” They were unaware ˹of what was to come˺.

Tafsir: And Pharaoh’s wife said after he and his aids had resolved to slay him he is ‘A joyous sight for me and you. Do not slay him. Perhaps he will be of benefit to us or we will adopt him as a son’ and so they obeyed her wish. And they were not aware of the sequel to their affair with him.

hype_questions: Will Pharaoh's life be saved?
Can Pharaoh's wife influence her husband's decision?
What will happen to the baby after his birth?
propositions: Pharaoh's wife said that the baby was a source of joy for her and Pharaoh.
Pharaoh and his aids had decided to kill the baby, but Pharaoh's wife intervened and asked them not to.
Pharaoh's wife suggested adopting the baby as their own son.
Pharaoh and his aids obeyed Pharaoh's wife's wish.
Pharaoh's wife was unaware of the consequences of her actions.

source_text:
Verse: And the heart of Moses’ mother ached so much that she almost gave away his identity, had We not reassured her heart in order for her to have faith ˹in Allah’s promise˺.

Tafsir: And the heart of Moses’s mother when she found out that they had picked him up became empty of everything other than him. Indeed in softened from the hardened form its subject omitted in other words understand it as innaha she was about to expose him that is as being her son had We not fortified her heart with patience that is We made it at peace that she might be of the believers of those who have faith in God’s promise the response to the conditional lawlā ‘had … not’ is given by the preceding statement.

hype_questions: What would have happened if Moses' mother had exposed him?
How did Allah reassure her heart for her to have faith in His promise?
What is the significance of patience and faith in understanding God's promise?
propositions: Moses' mother almost gave away his identity.
Her heart became empty of everything other than him after finding out they had picked him up.
Allah fortified her heart with patience to make it at peace so she might be a believer in God's promise.

source_text:
Verse: And she said to his sister, “Keep track of him!” So she watched him from a distance, while they were unaware.

Tafsir: And she said to his sister Mary ‘Follow him’ in other words follow where he goes in order to find out his news. So she watched him from afar from a distance secretly while they were not aware that she was his sister or that she was even watching him.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Mary's surveillance on Jesus?
How did Mary's actions demonstrate her devotion to Jesus?
What can we learn from Mary's secret observation of Jesus?
propositions: She watched him from a distance.
She was his sister but they were unaware she was watching him.
She followed where he went in order to find out his news.

source_text:
Verse: And We had caused him to refuse all wet-nurses at first, so his sister suggested, “Shall I direct you to a family who will bring him up for you and take good care of him?”

Tafsir: And We had forbidden him to take to the breasts of fostermothers from before that is to say we prevented him from taking to the breasts of any suckling mother other than his own mother. Therefore he would not accept the breasts of any of the foster-mothers brought for him. So she his sister said ‘Shall I show you a household — having seen their affection for him — who will take care of him for you by having him suckled and so on and who will act in good faith towards him?’ the suffixed pronoun in lahu has been interpreted as referring to the king as a response to them when they asked Mary how she could be sure. Her suggestion was accepted. So she brought his mother and he took to her breast. She explained to them that he had taken to her breast because of her pleasant scent and the wholesome taste of her milk. Permission was given to her to breast-feed him in her own house and so she returned with him just as God exalted be He says

hype_questions: How did Mary's sister find a suitable foster family for her baby?
Why was the baby refused by other wet-nurses?
What made the baby accept his mother's breast?
propositions: We had forbidden him to take to the breasts of any suckling mother other than his own mother.
She suggested showing a household who would take care of him and act in good faith towards him.
He took to her breast because of her pleasant scent and wholesome taste of her milk.

source_text:
Verse: This is how We returned him to his mother so that her heart would be put at ease, and not grieve, and that she would know that Allah’s promise is ˹always˺ true. But most people do not know.

Tafsir: Thus We restored him to his mother so that her eyes might delight in seeing him again and not grieve thereat and that she might know that God’s promise to restore him to her is true; but most of them that is the people do not know about this promise or of the fact that this was his sister and the other was his mother. He Moses remained with her until he was weaned during which time she was paid wages at one dinar per day. She took this because it was money from enemy territory harbī. She then brought him back to Pharaoh in whose household he was raised as God recounts of him in sūrat al-Shu‘arā’ Q. 2618 Did we not rear you among us as a child and did you not stay with us for years of your life?

hype_questions: Did Allah's promise of restoration to his mother ever come true?
How did Moses' sister care for him after their separation?
Why does Pharaoh question Moses' identity and upbringing?
propositions: Allah returned Moses to his mother so that her heart would be put at ease.
Moses was raised in Pharaoh's household as a child.
Pharaoh questioned Moses about his identity and upbringing.
The people do not know about Allah's promise to restore Moses to his mother.
Moses' sister received wages for caring for him during their separation.

source_text:
Verse: And when he reached full strength and maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. This is how We reward the good-doers.

Tafsir: And when he came of age namely at 30 or 33 and then was fully mature that is when he reached the age of 40 We gave him judgement wisdom and knowledge comprehension of religious matters before he was sent as a prophet. And so just as We rewarded him do We reward those are virtuous to their own souls.

hype_questions: What is the age at which a person reaches full strength and maturity?

propositions: When he reached full strength and maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge.
We rewarded him with judgement, wisdom, and knowledge comprehension of religious matters before he was sent as a prophet.
Just as We rewarded him do We reward those are virtuous to their own souls.

source_text:
Verse: ˹One day˺ he entered the city unnoticed by its people. There he found two men fighting: one of his own people, and the other of his enemies. The man from his people called to him for help against his foe. So Moses punched him, causing his death. Moses cried, “This is from Satan’s handiwork. He is certainly a sworn, misleading enemy.”

Tafsir: And he Moses entered the city Pharaoh’s city Memphis having been absent from it for a while at a time when its people were oblivious the time of the afternoon nap and found therein two men fighting one of his own faction namely an Israelite and the other of his enemies in other words an Egyptian who was exploiting an Israelite to carry firewood to Pharaoh’s kitchen. So the one who was of his faction called to him for help against the one who was of his enemies and so Moses said to him ‘Leave him be!’ and it is said that he replied to Moses thus ‘I am truly considering making you carry this firewood!’. So Moses punched him that is he hit him with his fist clenched — he Moses was a strong man with a powerful strike and did away with him that is he killed him but he had not intended to kill him. He buried him in the sand. He said ‘This killing of him is of Satan’s doing inciting my anger. Indeed he is an enemy to the son of Adam a manifest misleader’ of him.

hype_questions: What is the story of Moses and Pharaoh?
How did Moses handle a difficult situation in his journey?
What role does Satan play in the life of Moses?
propositions: Moses entered the city of Pharaoh, Memphis, without being noticed by its people.
Two men were fighting in the city, one of whom was an Israelite and the other an Egyptian.
The Israelite called to Moses for help against his enemy, but Moses told him to leave him alone.
Moses punched the Egyptian, killing him, although he did not intend to do so.
Moses buried the Egyptian in the sand and attributed the killing to Satan's influence.
Satan is considered an enemy to humanity, leading people astray.

Moses said to him ‘Clearly you are a trouble-maker!’ whose trouble-making is evident judging by what you did yesterday and today.

Verse: Then when Moses was about to lay his hands on their foe, the enemy said, “O Moses! Do you intend to kill me as you killed a man yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land. You do not intend to make peace!”

Tafsir: But when fa-lammā an an is extra he was about to strike the man who was an enemy to both of them to Moses and the one seeking his help he the one seeking help supposing that Moses was about to strike him because of what he Moses had said to him said ‘O Moses do you want to slay me just as you slew a soul yesterday? You merely want to be a tyrant in the land and you do not want to be of the reformers’. The Egyptian heard this and realised that the slayer had been Moses. Thus he hurried off to Pharaoh to inform him of this. Pharaoh then ordered slaughterers to slay Moses and they set off in his direction.

source_text:
Verse: When he arrived at the well of Midian, he found a group of people watering ˹their herds˺. Apart from them, he noticed two women holding back ˹their herd˺. He asked ˹them˺, “What is the problem?” They replied, “We cannot water ˹our animals˺ until the ˹other˺ shepherds are done, for our father is a very old man.”

Tafsir: And when he arrived at the Water of Midian the name of a well therein he found a group of people there watering their flocks and he found besides them two women holding back their flock from the water. He Moses said to the two ‘What is your business?’ that is ‘What is the matter with you that you are not watering?’ They said ‘We do not water our flock until the shepherds have moved on ri‘ā’u ‘shepherds’ the plural of rā‘in that is to say until they have returned from the watering for fear of being crushed by the throng after which we go to water a variant reading for yasdiru ‘move on’ is the 4th form subjunctive yusdira ‘to drive away’ meaning until they the shepherds have driven their flocks away from the water’ and our father is a very old man’ unable to come and water.

Two women were holding back their herd from the water until the other shepherds finished.

source_text:
Verse: So he watered ˹their herd˺ for them, then withdrew to the shade and prayed, “My Lord! I am truly in ˹desperate˺ need of whatever provision You may have in store for me.”

Tafsir: So he watered their flock for them from another well nearby by lifting a rock from on top of it which only ten men could have lifted; then he retreated to the shade of an acacia tree samura because of the extreme heat of the sun and he was hungry and said ‘My Lord indeed I am in utter need of whatever good whatever food You send down to me’. The two women returned to their father quicker than usual and so he asked them why it was so. They told him about the man who had watered their flock for them. So he said to one of them ‘Summon him to come to me’.

source_text:
Verse: Then one of the two women came to him, walking bashfully. She said, “My father is inviting you so he may reward you for watering ˹our animals˺ for us.” When Moses came to him and told him his whole story, the old man said, “Have no fear! You are ˹now˺ safe from the wrongdoing people.”

Tafsir: God exalted be He says Then one of the two women came to him walking bashfully — in other words covering her face with the sleeve of her shirt being shy of him — and said ‘My father invites you that he may pay you a wage for watering our flock for us’. He accepted her invitation while inwardly he disapproved of accepting any wage for it was as though she sought to remunerate him and as though he were of those who would want it which he was not. She walked in front of him but when the wind began to blow off her dress and reveal her legs he said to her ‘Walk behind me and show me the way’ which she did. Finally he came to her father Shu‘ayb peace be upon him who was sitting with some supper in front of him. He said to him ‘Sit and have some supper’. He Moses said ‘I hope that this is not some sort of compensation for having watered their flock for them? For we are People of a House and do not demand compensation for good deeds’. He Shu‘ayb said ‘No. It is simply a custom of mine and of my forefathers to be hospitable to guests and to offer them food’. Thus he Moses ate and informed him of his predicament. God exalted be He says So when he came to him and recounted to him the story al-qasas is a verbal noun with the sense of al-maqsūs ‘that which is recounted’ of his slaying of the Egyptian and their intention to slay him and his fear of Pharaoh he their father said ‘Do not be afraid. You have escaped from the evildoing people’ as Pharaoh had no authority over Midian.

Shu‘ayb offered Moses food and hospitality despite initial reservations.

Verse: One of the two daughters suggested, “O my dear father! Hire him. The best man for employment is definitely the strong and trustworthy ˹one˺.”

Tafsir: One of the two women the one that had been sent by her father either the elder or the younger said ‘O my father hire him employ him in return for a wage that he may tend our flock instead of us. Surely the best man you can hire is the strong the trustworthy man’ in other words hire him on account of his strength and trustworthiness. He Shu‘ayb asked her about him and she told him as mentioned above how he had lifted the rock off the well and that he had said to her ‘Walk behind me’ in addition to his lowering his head when he realised that she was coming towards him refusing to lift it until she left. He Shu‘ayb therefore was keen to have him marry one of his daughters.

Verse: The old man proposed, “I wish to marry one of these two daughters of mine to you, provided that you stay in my service for eight years. If you complete ten, it will be ˹a favour˺ from you, but I do not wish to make it difficult for you. Allah willing, you will find me an agreeable man.”

Tafsir: He said ‘I desire to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine either the elder or the younger one on condition that you hire yourself to me that you are employed by me to tend my flock for eight years. And if you complete ten that is the tending of ten years that completion shall be of your own accord. I do not want to be hard on you by making it the marriage conditional on ten years service. God willing — expressed to seek God’s blessing — you shall find me to be one of the righteous’ of those who fulfil their covenants.

If the servant completes ten years of service, it will be considered a favor from the servant.
