Verse: Moses responded, “˹Then˺ it is ˹settled˺ between you and I. Whichever term I fulfill, there will be no ˹further˺ obligation on me. And Allah is a Witness to what we say.”

Tafsir: He Moses said ‘That which you have said is settled then between me and you. Whichever of the two terms the eight or the ten the mā in ayyamā ‘whichever of the two’ is extra in other words the tending thereof I complete there shall be no injustice done to me by demanding of me to do more tending. And God is Guardian Keeper or Witness over what we you and I say’. The contract was agreed in this way. Shu‘ayb bid his daughter to give Moses a staff with which to beat off predatory beasts from his sheep — the staffs of the prophets were in his keeping. It was Adam’s staff made from the myrtle of Paradise that fell into her hands and so Moses took it with Shu‘ayb’s knowledge.

source_text:
Verse: When Moses had completed the term and was travelling with his family, he spotted a fire on the side of Mount Ṭûr. He said to his family, “Stay here, ˹for˺ I have spotted a fire. Perhaps from there I can bring you some directions or a torch from the fire so you may warm yourselves.”

Tafsir: So when Moses had completed the term of his tending — of eight years or of ten years which is what is generally assumed — and was travelling with his family his wife with the permission of her father in the direction of Egypt he saw in the distance on the side of the Mount Tūr a fire al-Tūr is the name of a mountain. He said to his family ‘Wait here; I see a fire in the distance. Maybe I will bring you from it news about how to rejoin the route to Egypt — for he had strayed from it along the way — or a brand read with any of the three vowels jadhwa jidhwa or judhwa which either means ‘a bundle’ or ‘a flame’ from the fire that you may warm yourselves’ tastalūna the tā’ replaces the tā’ of the 8th verbal paradigm ifta‘ala of the verb saliya or salaya.

He told his family to stay behind while he investigated the fire.
He hoped to find directions or a torch from the fire to warm himself and his family.

Verse: Now put your hand through ˹the opening of˺ your collar, it will come out ˹shining˺ white, unblemished. These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. They have truly been a rebellious people.”

Tafsir: Insert your right hand meaning the palm into your bosom jayb is the neck area of the shirt and then take it out and it will emerge not in its usual skin colour but white without any blemish any vestige of leprosy. So he inserted it and took it out and it shone as bright as the sun blinding the eyes; and draw your arm back to your side as a precaution against fear read rahab rahb or ruhb in other words against the fear produced by the glow of the hand so that you insert it back into your bosom and it is restored to its former state; it the arm is referred to as jināh ‘wing’ because they are for humans what wings are for birds. These then read fa-dhānika or fa-dhānnika namely the staff and the hand both of which ‘asā and yad are feminine nouns but the demonstrative pronoun dhānika used for them being the subject is in the masculine because its predicate is masculine shall be two proofs to be sent from your Lord to Pharaoh and his council; for surely they are an immoral people’.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We gave Moses the Scripture—after destroying earlier nations—as an insight for the people, a guide, and mercy so perhaps they would be mindful.

Tafsir: And verily We gave Moses the Scripture the Torah after We had destroyed the former generations the people of Noah ‘Ād Thamūd and others containing eye-openers for mankind basā’ira is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-kitāb ‘the Scripture’ the plural of basīra which is the perceptive light of the heart in other words illumination for the hearts of mankind and as guidance from error for those who implement it and mercy for those who believe therein that perhaps they might remember that they might be admonished by the admonitions it the Scripture contains.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the Torah in Islam?
How does the Quran view the role of guidance in human life?
What is the significance of mercy in Islamic theology?
propositions: We gave Moses the Scripture as an insight for the people.
The Scripture contains eye-openers for mankind, basā’ira being a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-kitāb.
The Scripture was given as guidance from error for those who implement it and mercy for those who believe therein.

source_text:
Verse: You were not there ˹O Prophet˺ on the western side of the mountain when We entrusted the Commandments to Moses, nor were you present ˹in his time˺.

Tafsir: And you were not O Muhammad (s) on the western side of the mountain the valley or the spot to the west of Moses at the time of the communion when We decreed revealed to Moses the commandment to deliver the Message to Pharaoh and his people nor were you among the witnesses to this to know it and inform of it;

entities: the western side of the mountain
the spot to the west of Moses
hype_questions: Did you witness the revelation of the Commandments to Moses?
Were you present when We entrusted the Commandments to Moses?
Did you receive any revelations from Allah at the western side of the mountain?
propositions: You were not present on the western side of the mountain when We entrusted the Commandments to Moses.
You were not among the witnesses to the revelation of the Commandments to Moses.
Allah did not entrust the Commandments to you, but to Moses.

source_text:
Verse: But We ˹later˺ raised ˹several˺ generations, and the ages took their toll on them. Nor were you living among the people of Midian, rehearsing Our revelations with them. But it is We Who have sent ˹this revelation to you˺.

Tafsir: but We brought forth generations communities after Moses and life was prolonged in their case in other words they lived long lives and so they forgot the covenants made with God knowledge disappeared and revelation ceased. Then We brought you as Messenger and revealed to you the story of Moses and others. And you were not a dweller a resident among the people of Midian reciting to them Our revelations tatlū ‘alayhim āyātinā a second predicate after thāwiyan ‘dweller’ to know their story and inform of it; but truly We are the senders of you as Messenger and the senders to you of the stories of former generations.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the prolonged lifespan of generations after Moses?
How did the knowledge and revelation cease among those communities?
Why was the Messenger sent to reveal the story of Moses and others?
propositions: We brought forth generations communities after Moses.
Life was prolonged in their case, but they forgot the covenants made with God.
Then We brought you as Messenger and revealed to you the story of Moses and others.
You were not a dweller among the people of Midian reciting Our revelations to them.
But truly We are the senders of you as Messenger and the senders to you of the stories of former generations.

source_text:
Verse: And you were not at the side of Mount Ṭûr when We called out ˹to Moses˺. But ˹you have been sent˺ as a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, so perhaps they may be mindful.

Tafsir: And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called out to Moses to take the Scripture earnestly; but We have sent you as a mercy from your Lord that you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you — these are the people of Mecca — and that perhaps they may remember they may be admonished.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of sending a prophet to warn a people?
How can one be considered a mercy from God?
What does it mean to be admonished by a prophet?
propositions: You were not at the side of Mount Ṭûr when We called out to Moses.
We have sent you as a mercy from your Lord to warn a people.
These are the people of Mecca who have not been warned before.

source_text:
Verse: Also so they would not say, if struck by an affliction for what their hands have done: “Our Lord! If only You had sent us a messenger, we would have followed Your revelations and become believers.”

Tafsir: Otherwise if an affliction a punishment should befall them because of what their own hands have sent before them in the way of disbelief and otherwise they might say ‘Our Lord why did You not send a messenger to us that we might have followed Your signs the ones sent with the messengers and been of the believers?’ the response to the conditional particle lawlā ‘if’ has been omitted and what follows it is a new subject; the meaning is ‘were it not for the affliction that is the cause of their saying’ or ‘were it not for their saying that is the cause of their affliction We would have hastened on for them their punishment and We would not have sent you as a messenger to them’.

hype_questions: Would following the revelations of God lead to belief?
propositions: If struck by an affliction, they would say their Lord did not send a messenger.
They would have followed the signs and become believers if a messenger had been sent.
God hastens on their punishment unless they repent.

source_text:
Verse: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, “If only he was given the like of what Moses had been given.” Adding, “We truly deny both.”

Tafsir: But when the truth namely Muhammad (s) came to them from Us they said ‘Why has he not been given the like of what Moses was given?’ in the way of signs such as the glowing hand the staff and others or by having the Book revealed all at once. God exalted be He says And did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?; before when they said regarding him and Muhammad (s) ‘Two sorcerers sāhirān; a variant reading has sihrān ‘two sorceries’ namely what they said regarding the Qur’ān and the Torah abetting each other.’ And they said ‘We indeed disbelieve in both’ the two prophets and the two Scriptures of Moses and Muhammad.

hype_questions: Why was Muhammad not given the like of what Moses had been given?
Did they disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?
Do we indeed disbelieve in both prophets and Scriptures?
propositions: The truth came to Muhammad from Us.
They said, 'Why has he not been given the like of what Moses was given?'
God exalted be He says And did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?
They indeed disbelieved in both prophets and Scriptures.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Bring then a scripture from Allah which is a better guide than these two so I may follow it, if your claim is true.”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘Then bring some Scripture from God that is better in guidance than these two Scriptures that I may follow it if you are truthful’ in what you say.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate guide for a prophet to follow?
How can one determine the authenticity of a claim?
What is the significance of guidance in religious context?
propositions: The Prophet asks for a scripture from Allah that is better than two existing scriptures.
The Prophet emphasizes the importance of truthfulness in one's words and actions.
Guidance is essential for a prophet to follow, and it should be based on divine revelation.

source_text:
Verse: So if they fail to respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires. And who could be more astray than those who follow their desires with no guidance from Allah? Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

Tafsir: Then if they do not respond to you regarding your invitation to them to bring a Scripture know that they are only following their desires in persisting in their disbelief. And who is more astray than he who follows his desire without any guidance from God? in other words there is no one more astray than such a person. Truly God does not guide the evildoing the disbelieving folk.

hype_questions: What happens when someone follows their desires without guidance from Allah?
Can anyone be more astray than those who follow their desires without guidance?
Does God guide the people who are evildoing and disbelieving?
propositions: If they fail to respond, they only follow their desires.
Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
Who is more astray than he who follows his desire without any guidance from God?
There is no one more astray than such a person.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We have steadily delivered the Word ˹of Allah˺ to the people so they may be mindful.

Tafsir: And now verily We have brought We have explained to them the Word the Qur’ān that perhaps they might remember they might be admonished and believe.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of delivering the Word of Allah to people?
How can people be admonished and believe through the Qur'ān?
What is the significance of remembering the Qur'ān?
propositions: We have delivered the Word of Allah to people.
The Qur'ān has been explained to them.
They might remember the Qur'ān.
They might be admonished through the Qur'ān.
They might believe through the Qur'ān.

source_text:
Verse: ˹As for˺ those ˹faithful˺ to whom We had given the Scripture before this ˹Quran˺, they do believe in it.

Tafsir: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before this that is before the Qur’ān they believe in it too. This was revealed regarding certain Jews who became Muslims such as ‘Abd Allāh b. Salām and others and certain Christians who had come from Abyssinia and Syria who also became Muslims.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Quran for those who already have a scripture?
How did certain Jews and Christians become Muslims after receiving the previous scriptures?
Who are some notable individuals mentioned in the Quranic verse?
propositions: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before this Quran believe in it.
Certain Jews who became Muslims were among those to whom the previous scripture was given.
Some Christians from Abyssinia and Syria also converted to Islam after receiving the previous scriptures.

source_text:
Verse: When it is recited to them, they declare, “We believe in it. This is definitely the truth from our Lord. We had already submitted ˹even˺ before this.”

Tafsir: And when it is recited to them the Qur’ān they say ‘We believe in it. It is indeed the Truth from our Lord. Lo! even before it we had submitted’ we affirmed God’s Oneness.

hype_questions: What is the nature of submission to one's Lord?
How does belief in the Qur'ān relate to previous beliefs?
What is the significance of affirming God's Oneness?
propositions: When the Qur'ān is recited, people believe in it.
The Qur'ān is the truth from one's Lord.
Submission to one's Lord implies belief in the Qur'ān.

source_text:
Verse: These ˹believers˺ will be given a double reward for their perseverance, responding to evil with good, and for donating from what We have provided for them.

Tafsir: Those will be given their reward twice over for believing in both Scriptures for the patience they showed for having been steadfast in implementing the prescriptions in them; and they ward off from themselves evil with good and expend give as voluntary alms of that which We have provided them.

hype_questions: What is the reward for believers who persevere and respond to evil with good?
How do believers show patience and steadfastness in implementing religious prescriptions?
What is the significance of warding off evil with good and donating alms?
propositions: Believers will be given a double reward for their perseverance.
Believers will receive their reward twice over for believing in both Scriptures.
Believers show patience by being steadfast in implementing religious prescriptions.
Believers ward off evil with good.
Believers expend voluntary alms from what has been provided to them.

source_text:
Verse: When they hear slanderous talk, they turn away from it, saying, “We are accountable for our deeds and you for yours. Peace ˹is our only response˺ to you! We want nothing to do with those who act ignorantly.”

Tafsir: And when they hear vanity vile words and hurtful intent from the disbelievers they disregard it and say ‘To us belong our deeds and to you belong your deeds. Peace to you — a parting truce salām mutāraka in other words you are secure from any abuse or the like on our part. We do not desire friendship with the ignorant’ we do not seek companionship with them.

hype_questions: What happens when believers respond to slanderous talk with peace?
How do believers prioritize their own actions over the actions of others?
What is the significance of a 'parting truce' in Islam?
propositions: When they hear slanderous talk, they turn away from it.
They say, “We are accountable for our deeds and you for yours.”
Peace is their only response to others.
To them belongs their deeds and to the disbelievers belong their deeds.
Believers do not desire friendship with the ignorant.

source_text:
Verse: You surely cannot guide whoever you like ˹O Prophet˺, but it is Allah Who guides whoever He wills, and He knows best who are ˹fit to be˺ guided.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding the Prophet’s longing for his uncle Abū Tālib to embrace faith You cannot guide whom you like to be guided but it is God Who guides whomever He will and He knows best those who will be guided.

hype_questions: Can God guide anyone to faith?
What is the nature of God's guidance?
How does God determine who will be guided?
propositions: You cannot guide whom you like to be guided.
It is Allah Who guides whoever He wills.
He knows best those who are fit to be guided.

source_text:
Verse: They say ˹to the Prophet˺, “If we were to follow ˹true˺ guidance with you, we would certainly be snatched away from our land.” Have We not established for them a safe haven ˹in Mecca˺ to which fruits of all kinds are brought as a provision from Us? But most of them do not know ˹this favour˺.

Tafsir: And they his people say ‘If we were to follow the Guidance with you we will be deprived from our land’ torn out of it swiftly. God exalted be He says Have We not established for them a secure Sanctuary one in which they are secure from the raids and killings that occur among the Arab tribes to which are brought read tujbā or yujbā fruits of all kinds fruits from every direction as a provision for them from Us? But most of them do not know that what We say is the truth.

hype_questions: If following guidance with the Prophet would lead to being torn out of one's land, what is the nature of this 'land'?
What kind of provision does God provide for those who follow His guidance?
Why do most people not recognize the truth about God's provision?
propositions: If we were to follow true guidance with the Prophet, we would be snatched away from our land.
God has established a safe haven in Mecca as a provision for those who follow His guidance.
Most people do not know that God provides fruits of all kinds as a provision for them.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Imagine˺ how many societies We have destroyed that had been spoiled by their ˹comfortable˺ living! Those are their residences, never inhabited after them except passingly. And We ˹alone˺ were the Successor.

Tafsir: And how many a town We have destroyed whose lifestyle was one of arrogant ungratefulness — by ‘town’ is meant the inhabitants thereof. Those are their dwellings which have not been dwelt in after them except a little by passers-by for a day or part of it. And it was We Who were the sole inheritors after them.

hype_questions: What happens to societies that become too comfortable?
How do people respond when their way of life is destroyed?
Who inherits the world after a society is destroyed?
propositions: We have destroyed many societies that were spoiled by their comfortable living.
The lifestyle of those who are arrogant and ungrateful will be destroyed.
We were the sole inheritors of the world after it was destroyed.

source_text:
Verse: Your Lord would never destroy a society until He had sent to its capital a messenger, reciting Our revelations to them. Nor would We ever destroy a society unless its people persisted in wrongdoing.

Tafsir: And your Lord never destroyed the towns because of evildoing on their part until He had raised up in their mother-town that is the major town among them a messenger to recite Our signs to them. And We never destroyed the towns unless their inhabitants were committing evil by denying the messengers.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of sending a messenger to a society before destroying it?
How does one's society determine its fate in the eyes of Allah?
Can a society be destroyed without its people committing wrongdoing?
propositions: Your Lord would never destroy a society until He had sent to its capital a messenger, reciting Our revelations to them.
And your Lord never destroyed the towns because of evildoing on their part until He had raised up in their mother-town that is the major town among them a messenger to recite Our signs to them.
Nor would We ever destroy a society unless its people persisted in wrongdoing.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever ˹pleasure˺ you have been given is no more than ˹a fleeting˺ enjoyment and adornment of this worldly life. But what is with Allah is far better and more lasting. Will you not then understand?

Tafsir: And whatever things you have been given are only the short-lived enjoyment of the life of this world and an ornament thereof in other words things which you enjoy and adorn yourselves with for the days of your lives after which they perish; and what is with God in other words His reward is better and more lasting. Will you not understand? ta‘qilūna; or read ya‘qilūna ‘will they not understand’ that what lasts is better than what perishes.

hype_questions: Will the fleeting joys of this world be more satisfying than eternal bliss with God?
Can temporary earthly adornments compare to the lasting beauty of God's reward?
Do humans truly appreciate the impermanence of worldly pleasures and the enduring value of Allah's favor?
propositions: Whatever pleasure you have been given is only a fleeting enjoyment.
The things you have been given are only the short-lived enjoyment of this world's life.
God's reward is better and more lasting than the temporary joys of this world.
What lasts is better than what perishes.
You will not understand unless you recognize the impermanence of worldly pleasures and the enduring value of Allah's favor.

source_text:
Verse: Can those to whom We have made a fine promise—which they will see fulfilled—be like those who We have allowed to enjoy the pleasures of this worldly life, but on the Day of Judgment will be brought ˹for punishment˺?

Tafsir: Is he to whom We have given a fair promise which he will receive which he will attain and that promise is Paradise like him to whom We have given the enjoyment of the life of this world enjoyment which will disappear soon then on the Day of Resurrection he will be of those arraigned? before the Fire. The former is the believer the latter the disbeliever in other words the two are not equal.

hype_questions: What happens to those who fulfill their promises to Allah?
How does the enjoyment of worldly life compare to Paradise?
What is the difference between a believer and a disbeliever on the Day of Judgment?
propositions: Those who are given a fair promise by Allah will receive it and attain Paradise.
The enjoyment of the life of this world is temporary and will disappear soon.
Believers will be brought before the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, while disbelievers will be arraigned in front of them.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Watch for˺ the Day He will call to them, “Where are those you claimed were My associate-gods?”

Tafsir: And mention the day when He God will call to them and say ‘Where then are My partners those whom you used to claim?’ were partners of Mine.

hype_questions: What happens to those who claimed gods other than Allah?
Will Allah hold accountable those who worshipped false deities?
propositions: Allah will call on the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment and ask where their claimed associates are.
The claimed associates were partners of Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Those ˹misleaders˺ against whom the decree ˹of torment˺ is justified will cry, “Our Lord! These ˹followers˺ are the ones we caused to deviate. We led them into deviance, for we ourselves were deviant. We disassociate ourselves ˹from them˺ before You. It was not us that they used to worship.”

Tafsir: Those against whom the Word of punishment will have become due the justified Word that they be admitted into the Fire — and these are the leaders of misguidance — they shall say ‘Our Lord! These are the ones whom we led astray hā’ūlā’i’lladhīna aghwaynā is both a subject and an adjectival qualification. We led them astray aghwaynāhum the predicate thereof and they went astray even as we went astray — we did not compel them to follow error. We declare our innocence of them before You; it was not us that they worshipped’ mā ‘not’ is for negation; the direct object iyyānā ‘us’ precedes the verb ya‘budūna ‘they worshipped’ in order to concord with the end-rhyme of the verses.

hype_questions: What happens to those who lead others astray?
Can one be held accountable for leading someone astray?
How does Allah respond to those who mislead others?
propositions: Those against whom the Word of punishment will have become due will be admitted into the Fire.
The leaders of misguidance will say, 'Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray.'
We did not compel them to follow error.

source_text:
Verse: It will be said ˹to the disbelievers˺, “Call upon your associate-gods ˹for help˺.” So they will call them, but will receive no response. And they will face the punishment, wishing they had been ˹rightly˺ guided!

Tafsir: And it shall be said ‘Call now to your associates!’ namely the idols you alleged to be partners of God. So they will call to them but they will not answer them their call and they the former will see they will sight the chastisement they will wish if only they had been guided! in this world they would not have seen it in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What happens to those who call upon false gods for help?
Will they receive any response from their alleged partners of God?
Can they see the punishment in this world or only in the Hereafter?
propositions: It will be said to the disbelievers, 'Call upon your associate-gods for help.'
They will call them, but will receive no response.
And they will face the punishment, wishing they had been rightly guided.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹watch for˺ the Day He will call to them, asking, “What response did you give to the messengers?”

Tafsir: And mention the day when He will call to them and say ‘What response did you give to those messengers who were sent?’ to you.

hype_questions: Will I be held accountable for my actions?
Did I respond correctly to the messengers sent by God?
What is the consequence of not responding to the messengers?
propositions: God will call to them on the Day of Judgment.
He will ask about their response to the messengers.
The messengers were sent to convey a message from God.

source_text:
Verse: They will be too dumbstruck on that Day to ask one another ˹for answers˺.

Tafsir: The tidings the news of deliverance contained in the response will be obscured to them on that day in other words they will not find any statement that might contain hope of deliverance for them; so they will not question one other about this and will fall silent.

hype_questions: Will they be able to comprehend the news of deliverance on that Day?
How will they react when faced with the tidings of their deliverance?
What will happen to them when they are unable to find any hope of deliverance?
propositions: The tidings of deliverance will be obscured to them on that Day.
They will not find any statement that might contain hope of deliverance for them.
They will fall silent when faced with the news of their deliverance.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who repent, believe, and do good ˹in this world˺, it is right to hope that they will be among the successful.

Tafsir: But as for him who repents of idolatry and believes in the affirmation of God’s Oneness and acts righteously he observes the duties of religion maybe he will be among the successful those delivered according to God’s promise.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who repents of idolatry and believes in the affirmation of God's Oneness?
How does one demonstrate righteousness in their faith?
Can someone be considered successful if they follow the duties of religion?
propositions: Those who repent, believe, and do good will be among the successful.
He who repents of idolatry and believes in the affirmation of God's Oneness acts righteously and observes the duties of religion.
God's promise is fulfilled for those delivered according to His promise.

source_text:
Verse: Your Lord creates and chooses whatever He wills—the choice is not theirs. Glorified and Exalted is Allah above what they associate ˹with Him˺!

Tafsir: And your Lord creates whatever He will and chooses whatever He will. They the idolaters do not have the choice the right to choose anything. Glory be to God and exalted be He above what they associate above their idolatry.

hype_questions: Does Allah have the power to choose whatever He wills?
Can humans truly make choices that are not influenced by Allah?
What is the nature of Allah's sovereignty over creation?
propositions: Your Lord creates and chooses whatever He wills—the choice is not theirs.
They the idolaters do not have the right to choose anything.
Glory be to God and exalted be He above what they associate above their idolatry.

source_text:
Verse: And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they reveal.

Tafsir: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal what their hearts keep secret of disbelief and otherwise and what they proclaim by their tongues of such things.

hype_questions: Does Allah know our innermost thoughts?
Can Allah see through our deception?
How does Allah distinguish between truth and falsehood?
propositions: Your Lord knows what is in your heart.
Your Lord knows what is in your breast.
Your Lord knows the secrets of disbelief and the things you proclaim.

source_text:
Verse: He is Allah. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. All praise belongs to Him in this life and the next. All authority is His. And to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.

Tafsir: And He is God; there is no god except Him. To Him belongs all praise in the former namely the life of this world and in the latter Paradise. And to Him belongs the judgement the decree effective in the case of all things and to Him you will be returned through resurrection.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah?
How does Allah reward His believers?
What happens to humans after death?
propositions: He is Allah.
There is no god except Him.
All praise belongs to Him in this life and the next.
All authority is His.
To Him you will be returned.

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Imagine if Allah were to make the night perpetual for you until the Day of Judgment, which god other than Allah could bring you sunlight? Will you not then listen?”

Tafsir: Say to the people of Mecca ‘Have you considered in other words inform Me if God were to make the night everlasting over you until the Day of Resurrection what god other than God as you are wont to claim could bring you light? daylight hours during which you could earn a living. Will you not then listen?’ to this in a way so as to understand it and so repent of your idolatry.

hype_questions: Can any god other than Allah bring light to humanity?
Will the absence of sunlight affect human productivity and livelihood?
How can humans repent from idolatry when faced with the reality of their beliefs?
propositions: Allah could make the night perpetual for humans until the Day of Judgment.
No god other than Allah can bring light to humanity.
Humans should listen and repent from idolatry upon understanding the reality of their beliefs.

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them also˺, “Imagine if Allah were to make the day perpetual for you until the Day of Judgment, which god other than Allah could bring you night to rest in? Will you not then see?”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘Have you considered if God were to make the day everlasting over you until the Day of Resurrection what god other than God as you are wont to claim could bring you night wherein you rest? from any weariness. Will you not then see? the error you are upon when you ascribe partners to God and so repent of it.

hype_questions: Would you prefer eternal life with no rest, or a temporary life with night to rest in?
Can any god besides Allah bring you relief from weariness?
Will you not see the error of ascribing partners to God?
propositions: If Allah were to make the day perpetual for you until the Day of Judgment, what god other than Allah could bring you night to rest in?
You are wont to claim that there is a god besides Allah, but can this god bring you relief from weariness?
You will not see the error of ascribing partners to God and repenting of it

source_text:
Verse: It is out of His mercy that He has made for you the day and night so that you may rest ˹in the latter˺ and seek His bounty ˹in the former˺, and perhaps you will be grateful.

Tafsir: And of His mercy exalted be He He has made for you night and day that you may rest therein in the night and that you may seek in the day of His bounty to earn your livelihood that perhaps you might give thanks’ for the grace of God during both of these times.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of day and night?
How can I show gratitude to God?
Why is rest important?
propositions: God has made day and night for you to rest in the night and seek His bounty in the day.
You should be grateful for God's mercy during both day and night.
Resting at night and seeking God's bounty during the day is a way to earn your livelihood.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹watch for˺ the Day He will call to them, “Where are those you claimed were My associate-gods?”

Tafsir: And mention the day when He will call to them and say ‘Where now are My associates those whom you used to claim?’ — this is mentioned again in order to expound upon it

hype_questions: What happens when Allah calls us to account for our actions?
Will we be held accountable for claiming false gods?
How will Allah judge those who claimed associates besides Him?
propositions: Allah will call humans to account on the Day of Judgment.
Humans claimed false gods as associates of Allah, but He is unique.
The claimants of false gods will be questioned about their actions.

source_text:
Verse: And We will bring forth a witness from every faith-community and ask ˹the polytheists˺, “Show ˹Us˺ your proof.” Then they will ˹come to˺ know that the truth is with Allah ˹alone˺. And whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them.

Tafsir: And We shall draw bring forth from every community a witness and this will be their prophet who will bear witness against what they say and We shall say to them ‘Produce your evidence’ for the justification of the idolatry which you asserted. Then they will know that the right to divineness is God’s — none share it with Him. And that which they used to invent in this world of His having an associate exalted be He high above such associations will fail them.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's divineness?
How do polytheists justify their idolatrous beliefs?
What happens to those who invent false gods?
propositions: We will bring forth a witness from every faith-community.
Polytheists are asked to produce evidence for their idolatry.
The right to divineness belongs to God alone, and none share it with Him.
Idolatrous beliefs will fail those who invent them.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Korah was from the people of Moses, but he behaved arrogantly towards them. We had granted him such treasures that even their keys would burden a group of strong men. ˹Some of˺ his people advised him, “Do not be prideful! Surely Allah does not like the prideful.

Tafsir: Indeed Korah belonged to the people of Moses — being his paternal and maternal cousin and he had believed in him in Moses — but he became insolent towards them through his disdain haughtiness and great wealth. For We had given him so many treasures that the number of their keys would verily have burdened a group of strong men in other words they would have been too heavy for such men the bā’ of bi’l-‘usbati ‘a group’ is to render transitive the intransitive verb; the number of such men required is estimated to be 70 40 or 10; other estimates are also given. Mention when his people the believers among the Children of Israel said to him ‘Do not be exultant in your great wealth an exultation of insolence; truly God does not love the exultant in such things;

hype_questions: What happens when one becomes too proud and arrogant?
How does wealth affect a person's behavior?
Can excessive pride lead to divine displeasure?
propositions: Korah was the cousin and believer of Moses.
He became insolent towards his people due to disdain, haughtiness, and great wealth.
God does not like the proud or exultant in material possessions.
The believers among the Children of Israel advised Korah not to be exultant in his wealth.
Excessive pride can lead to divine displeasure.

source_text:
Verse: Rather, seek the ˹reward˺ of the Hereafter by means of what Allah has granted you, without forgetting your share of this world. And be good ˹to others˺ as Allah has been good to you. Do not seek to spread corruption in the land, for Allah certainly does not like the corruptors.”

Tafsir: but seek in that which God has given you of wealth the Abode of the Hereafter by expending it in obedience to God and do not forget your share of this world that is do not forget to strive in it for the sake of the Hereafter; and be good to people by giving voluntary alms just as God has been good to you. And do not seek to cause corruption in the earth by committing acts of disobedience. Surely God does not love the agents of corruption’ meaning that He will punish them.

hype_questions: What is the reward for living a virtuous life?
How can I make the most of my wealth to achieve a better hereafter?
What are the consequences of causing corruption in society?
propositions: Seek the reward of the Hereafter by expending your wealth in obedience to God.
Do not forget to strive in this world for the sake of the Hereafter.
Be good to people by giving voluntary alms just as God has been good to you.
God does not like the corruptors and will punish them.

source_text:
Verse: He replied, “I have been granted all this because of some knowledge I have.”

Tafsir: He said ‘In fact I have been given it that is this wealth because of knowledge I possess’ in other words in return for it — he was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel in the Torah after Moses and Aaron. God exalted be He says Does he not know that God had already destroyed before him generations communities of men stronger than him in might and greater in the amassing? of wealth; in other words he does know this. And God destroys them and the guilty will not be questioned about their sins because of God’s knowledge of these sins and so they will be admitted into the Fire without a reckoning.

hype_questions: Does he not know that God had already destroyed before him generations of men stronger than him in might and greater in the amassing of wealth?
And God destroys them and the guilty will not be questioned about their sins because of God’s knowledge of these sins
so they will be admitted into the Fire without a reckoning
propositions: He replied, “I have been granted all this because of some knowledge I have.”
In fact I have been given it that is this wealth because of knowledge I possess”.
God exalted be He says Does he not know that God had already destroyed before him generations communities of men stronger than him in might and greater in the amassing? of wealth.
he does know this. And God destroys them and the guilty will not be questioned about their sins because of God’s knowledge of these sins
so they will be admitted into the Fire without a reckoning.

source_text:
Verse: Then he came out before his people in all his glamour. Those who desired the life of this world wished, “If only we could have something like what Korah has been given. He is truly a man of great fortune!”

Tafsir: So he Korah emerged before his people in his finery with his large retinue all of them in procession dressed in gold and silk garments and mounted on adorned horses and mules. Those who desired the life of this world said ‘O yā is for drawing attention would that we had the like of what Korah has been given this world. Truly he enjoys great fortune’ abundant fortune in it.

hype_questions: What is the secret to Korah's great fortune?
How does Korah's wealth compare to that of others?
Can we achieve true prosperity like Korah?
propositions: Korah emerged before his people in his finery.
Those who desired the life of this world wished they had something like Korah's fortune.
Korah enjoys great fortune in this world.

source_text:
Verse: But those gifted with knowledge said, “Shame on you! Allah’s reward is far better for those who believe and do good. But none will attain this except the steadfast.”

Tafsir: But those to whom knowledge had been given knowledge of what God had promised in the Hereafter said to them ‘Woe to you! waylakum is an expression of reprimand God’s reward of Paradise in the Hereafter is better for him who believes and acts righteously than what Korah has been given in this world; and none will obtain it namely the Paradise that is given as a reward except those who are steadfast’ in their adherence to obedience and refrain from disobedience.

hype_questions: What is the reward of Paradise in the Hereafter?
How can one attain Paradise?
What is the significance of steadfastness in obedience?
propositions: Allah's reward for believers is better than what Korah has been given in this world.
God's promise of Paradise in the Hereafter is far better for those who believe and do good.
None will attain Paradise except those who are steadfast in their adherence to obedience.

source_text:
Verse: Then We caused the earth to swallow him up, along with his home. There was no one to help him against Allah, nor could he even help himself.

Tafsir: So We caused the earth to swallow him Korah and his dwelling and he had no host to help him besides God that is other than Him to protect him from destruction nor was he of those who can rescue themselves from it.

hype_questions: Can one's own actions lead to destruction?
What is the nature of reliance on God?
How does faith impact one's ability to cope with adversity?
propositions: The earth swallowed Korah and his dwelling.
Korah had no host to help him besides God.
God protects from destruction.

source_text:
Verse: And those who had craved his position the previous day began to say, “Ah! It is certainly Allah Who gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills of His servants. Had it not been for the grace of Allah, He could have surely caused the earth to swallow us up! Oh, indeed! The disbelievers will never succeed.”

Tafsir: And those who had longed to be in his place the day before that is only recently were saying ‘Alas! God expands provision for whomever He will of His servants and straitens it He restricts it for whomever He will way-ka’anna way is a noun of action with the sense of ‘How astonished I am’ while the kāf functions as a causative lām ‘because’. Had God not been gracious to us He would have made us to be swallowed too’ read active la-khasafa or passive la-khusifa. Lo! indeed those who are ungrateful for God’s grace such as Korah never prosper.

hype_questions: What would have happened if Allah had not been gracious to us?
How does Allah determine the amount of provision for His servants?
What is the consequence of being ungrateful for Allah's grace?
propositions: Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills.
Had it not been for the grace of Allah, He could have caused the earth to swallow us up.
Those who are ungrateful for God’s grace such as Korah never prosper.

source_text:
Verse: That ˹eternal˺ Home in the Hereafter We reserve ˹only˺ for those who seek neither tyranny nor corruption on the earth. The ultimate outcome belongs ˹only˺ to the righteous.

Tafsir: That is the Abode of the Hereafter namely Paradise which We shall grant to those who do not desire to be haughty in the earth through insolence nor to cause corruption by committing acts of disobedience. And the praiseworthy sequel will be for those who fear God’s punishment by performing deeds of obedience.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate destination for those who seek a virtuous life?
How can one ensure a place in Paradise?
What is the reward for those who fear God's punishment?
propositions: We reserve a home in the Hereafter for those who seek neither tyranny nor corruption on earth.
The ultimate outcome belongs only to the righteous.
Paradise will be granted to those who do not desire to be haughty in the earth through insolence nor to cause corruption by committing acts of disobedience.
The praiseworthy sequel will be for those who fear God's punishment by performing deeds of obedience.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever comes with a good deed will be rewarded with what is better. And whoever comes with an evil deed, then the evildoers will only be rewarded for what they used to do.

Tafsir: Whoever brings a good deed shall have better than it as a reward because of it and this will be the like of it tenfold; while whoever brings an evil deed those who commit evil deeds shall only be requited the requital for what they used to do in other words only the like of it.

hype_questions: What happens when someone brings a good deed?
How is an evil deed rewarded?
Can someone change their fate through good deeds?
propositions: Whoever comes with a good deed will be rewarded with what is better.
Whoever comes with an evil deed, then the evildoers will only be rewarded for what they used to do.

source_text:
Verse: Most certainly, the One Who has ordained the Quran for you will ˹ultimately˺ bring you back home ˹to Mecca˺. Say, “My Lord knows best who has come with ˹true˺ guidance and who is clearly astray.”

Tafsir: Indeed He Who has prescribed for you the Qur’ān He Who has revealed it will surely restore you to a place of return to Mecca — he had yearned for it. Say ‘My Lord knows best him who brings guidance and him who is in manifest error’ — this was revealed in order to refute what the Meccan disbelievers had said to him ‘Indeed you are error’. In other words God is saying that he the Prophet is the one who has brought guidance while they are the ones in error.

hype_questions: Will I be guided to the right path?
What is the nature of guidance and error?
How will my return be determined?
propositions: The One Who has ordained the Qur'ān will bring me back home.
My Lord knows best who brings true guidance and who is clearly astray.
God is saying that I, the Prophet, have brought guidance while the Meccan disbelievers are in error.

source_text:
Verse: You never expected this Book to be revealed to you, but ˹it came˺ only ˹as˺ a mercy from your Lord. So never side with the disbelievers ˹in their disbelief˺.

Tafsir: And you never expected that the Scripture the Qur’ān would be conferred on you; but it was conferred on you as a mercy from your Lord. So never be a supporter of the disbelievers in that religion of theirs to which they summon you.

hype_questions: What is the nature of mercy from Allah?
How should a Muslim respond to disbelievers?
What is the relationship between faith and support for one's religion?
propositions: The Qur’ān was revealed as a mercy from your Lord.
Never side with the disbelievers in their disbelief.
Be a supporter of the believers in that religion to which they summon you.

source_text:
Verse: Do not let them turn you away from the revelations of Allah after they have been sent down to you. Rather, invite ˹all˺ to ˹the Way of˺ your Lord, and never be one of the polytheists.

Tafsir: And never let them bar you yasuddunnaka is actually yasuddūnannaka but the nūn of the indicative ending has been omitted because of the apocopating particle lā as has the wāw of the third person plural subject of the verb because of its coming together with an unvocalised nūn from God’s signs after they have been revealed to you in other words do not consult with them in such matters and summon people to your Lord by affirming His Oneness and worshipping Him and never be of the idolaters by supporting them lā takūnanna the apocopating particle does not affect the ending of the verb here because of its invariability.

hype_questions: What is the correct approach when faced with conflicting opinions from others about religious matters?
How can one ensure they are worshipping the one true God?
What does it mean to be a polytheist and how can one avoid this?
propositions: Do not let others turn you away from Allah's revelations after they have been sent down to you.
Invite people to the Way of your Lord and never be one of the polytheists.
Do not consult with others in matters related to religion, but rather summon them to your Lord by affirming His Oneness and worshipping Him.

source_text:
Verse: And do not invoke any other god with Allah. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. Everything is bound to perish except He Himself. All authority belongs to Him. And to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.

Tafsir: And do not call on do not worship another god with God; there is no god except Him. Everything will perish except His Countenance except Him. His is the judgement the effective decree and to Him you will be brought back by being raised from the grave.

hype_questions: What happens to those who worship other gods besides Allah?
Will everything perish in the end, or is there something that will endure?
What is the nature of Allah's judgment and decree?
propositions: There is no god worthy of worship except Allah.
Everything will perish except Allah's countenance.
All authority belongs to Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm.

Tafsir: Alif lām mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

hype_questions: Does God have a specific meaning in mind when using the alphabet?
Can humans truly understand God's intentions?
What does it mean for God to 'know best'?
propositions: God knows what He means by these letters.
These letters are part of God's language.
God has a specific meaning in mind when using the alphabet.

source_text:
Verse: Do people think once they say, “We believe,” that they will be left without being put to the test?

Tafsir: Do people suppose that they will be left to say that is that they will be left alone because of their saying ‘We believe’ and they will not be tried? tested with that which will reveal the sincerity of their belief. This verse was revealed regarding a group of individuals who when they became believers endured suffering at the hands of the idolaters.

hype_questions: Will I be tested on my faith after declaring my belief?
Can I avoid being tried if I say 'I believe'?
How will my sincerity as a believer be revealed?
propositions: People who say they believe will be put to the test.
The declaration of belief is not a guarantee of immunity from trial.
Belief is tested by the sincerity of one's actions and intentions.

source_text:
Verse: We certainly tested those before them. And ˹in this way˺ Allah will clearly distinguish between those who are truthful and those who are liars.

Tafsir: And certainly We tried those who were before them. So God shall surely know those who are sincere in their faith — a knowledge of direct vision — and He shall surely know those who are liars regarding it.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's knowledge?
How does Allah distinguish between truthful and liars?
What is the significance of sincerity in faith?
propositions: Allah tested those before them.
God shall surely know those who are sincere in their faith through direct vision.
He shall surely know those who are liars regarding it.

source_text:
Verse: Or do the evildoers ˹simply˺ think that they will escape Us? How wrong is their judgment!

Tafsir: Or do those who commit evil deeds idolatry and acts of disobedience suppose that they can elude Us? so that We will not be able to requite them. Evil is that judgement of theirs which they judge!

hype_questions: Will those who commit evil deeds escape God's punishment?
Can people avoid being held accountable for their actions?
What is the nature of the judgment that those who do wrong will face?
propositions: Those who commit evil deeds think they can elude God.
God will not be able to requite those who commit evil deeds.
The judgment of those who do wrong is that they will be held accountable for their actions.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, ˹let them know that˺ Allah’s appointed time is sure to come. He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Tafsir: Whoever expects to encounter God should know that God’s appointed term for this encounter will indeed come; so let him prepare for it. And He is the Hearer of the sayings of His servants the Knower of their actions.

hype_questions: What should I do to prepare for my meeting with God?
How can I ensure that I am ready for the encounter with God?
What is God's appointed term for this encounter?
propositions: Whoever expects to encounter God should know that God’s appointed term for this encounter will indeed come.
God is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
He is the Hearer of the sayings of His servants and the Knower of their actions.

source_text:
Verse: And whoever strives ˹in Allah’s cause˺, only does so for their own good. Surely Allah is not in need of ˹any of˺ His creation.

Tafsir: And whoever struggles in war or against the temptations of his own soul struggles only for his own sake because the benefits to be reaped from his struggle will be for his sake and not for God’s. For truly God is Independent of the creatures of all the Worlds mankind jinn and angels and He is also without need of their worship.

hype_questions: What motivates someone to engage in spiritual struggle?
Can human actions be driven by self-interest without contradicting divine purpose?
Is Allah truly independent of the needs and worship of creation?
propositions: Whoever strives in Allah's cause does so for their own good.
The benefits of one's struggle are ultimately for their own sake, not God's.
God is Independent of the creatures of all worlds, including mankind, jinn, and angels.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who believe and do good, We will certainly absolve them of their sins, and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.

Tafsir: And those who believe and perform righteous deeds We will surely absolve them of their misdeeds by their performance of righteous deeds and We will indeed requite them with the best of what they used to do namely their righteous deeds it ahsana is in the accusative because the operator of the oblique bi has been omitted.

hype_questions: What happens to those who believe and do good?
How will Allah reward believers who perform righteous deeds?
Can believers be absolved of their sins through their own actions?
propositions: Allah will absolve believers of their sins.
Believers who perform righteous deeds will be rewarded with the best of what they used to do.
The performance of righteous deeds is a means of absolving misdeeds.

source_text:
Verse: We have commanded people to honour their parents. But if they urge you to associate with Me what you have no knowledge of, then do not obey them. To Me you will ˹all˺ return, and then I will inform you of what you used to do.

Tafsir: And We have enjoined on man kindness to his parents that he should be dutiful towards them; but if they urge you to ascribe to Me as partner that of which you do not have any knowledge any knowledge that accords with reality and so is meaningless then do not obey them in such incitements to idolatry. To Me will be your return whereat I will inform you of what you used to do and I will requite you for it.

hype_questions: What happens when we disobey our parents?
Can we be forgiven for our past mistakes?
How will Allah judge us on the Day of Reckoning?
propositions: We have commanded people to honour their parents.
If they urge you to associate with Me what you have no knowledge of, then do not obey them.
To Me you will return, and then I will inform you of what you used to do.

source_text:
Verse: Those who believe and do good will surely be admitted by Us into ˹the company of˺ the righteous.

Tafsir: And those who believe and perform righteous deeds assuredly We shall admit them among the righteous among the prophets and the saints by gathering in the company of one another at the Resurrection.

hype_questions: What happens to those who believe and do good deeds after death?
How will believers be treated on the Day of Resurrection?
Can righteous people be reunited with one another at the end times?
propositions: Those who believe and do good deeds will be admitted into the company of the righteous.
Believers who perform righteous deeds will be gathered among the prophets and saints at the Resurrection.
The righteous will be reunited with one another at the Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: There are some who say, “We believe in Allah,” but when they suffer in the cause of Allah, they mistake ˹this˺ persecution at the hands of people for the punishment of Allah. But when victory comes from your Lord, they surely say ˹to the believers˺, “We have always been with you.” Does Allah not know best what is in the hearts of all beings?

Tafsir: And among people there are those who say ‘We believe in God’ but if such a person suffers hurt in God’s cause he takes people’s persecution that is their harming of him to be the same as God’s chastisement in terms of his fear of it and so he obeys them and behaves hypocritically. Yet if la-in the lām is for oaths there comes help to believers from your Lord and they take spoils they will assuredly say la-yaqūlunna the final nūn of the indicative has been omitted because of the other nūn coming after it and likewise the wāw indicating the plural person has been replaced by a damma because of two unvocalised consonants coming together ‘We were indeed with you’ in faith so give us a share of the booty. God exalted be He says Does God not know best what is in the breasts of all creatures? what is in their hearts of faith or hypocrisy? Indeed He does.

hype_questions: What is the difference between true faith and hypocrisy?
How do people react when they face persecution in the name of God?
Does God reward those who claim to be with believers but are actually hypocrites?
propositions: Some people believe in Allah but behave hypocritically when faced with persecution.
God does not punish believers for their fear of persecution.
True faith is evident through one's actions, not just words.
Believers who claim to be with them but are actually hypocrites will not receive a share of the booty.

source_text:
Verse: Allah will certainly distinguish between those who have ˹sure˺ faith and the hypocrites.

Tafsir: And God shall surely ascertain those who believe in their hearts and He shall surely ascertain the hypocrites and He will requite each group accordingly the lām in both verbs la-ya‘lamanna ‘He shall ascertain’ is for oaths.

hype_questions: What are the characteristics of those who have true faith?
How does God distinguish between believers and hypocrites?
What is the fate of those who practice hypocrisy?
propositions: Allah will distinguish between those who have sure faith and the hypocrites.
God shall surely ascertain those who believe in their hearts.
He shall surely ascertain the hypocrites.
He will requite each group accordingly.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers say to the believers, “˹Just˺ follow our way, and we will bear ˹the burden of˺ your sins.” But they would never ˹want to˺ bear any of the believers’ sins. They are simply lying.

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe ‘Follow our path our religion and we will bear responsibility for your sins’ when you follow us should there be any such sins the imperative here functions as a predicate. God exalted be He says But they will not be able to bear anything of their sins. Truly they are liars in saying this.

hype_questions: Can those who disbelieve truly bear the burden of others' sins?
What is the nature of the imperatives used by those who disbelieve in their messages?
How do believers respond to the claims made by those who disbelieve?
propositions: The disbelievers claim that following their way will bear the burden of the believers' sins.
God says that those who disbelieve cannot bear anything of the believers' sins.
Those who disbelieve are liars when they make such claims.

source_text:
Verse: Yet they will certainly ˹be made to˺ carry their own burdens, as well as other burdens along with their own. And they will surely be questioned on Judgment Day about what they used to fabricate.

Tafsir: And they shall certainly bear their own burdens their sins and other burdens along with their own burdens as punishment for saying to believers Follow our path previous verse and for their leading astray those who follow them blindly; and on the Day of Resurrection they shall surely be questioned concerning what they used to invent what they used to fabricate of lies against God a questioning of rebuke the lām in both verbs la-yahmilunna and la-yus’alunna is for oaths; in both verbs the plural indicators of the subject wāw and nūn -ūna have been omitted.

hype_questions: What happens to those who lead others astray?
How will people be held accountable for their actions?
What is the consequence of fabricating lies against God?
propositions: They will carry their own burdens, including their sins.
Those who follow false leaders will be questioned on Judgment Day about their actions.
People will be held accountable for inventing lies against God.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them for a thousand years, less fifty. Then the Flood overtook them, while they persisted in wrongdoing.

Tafsir: And verily We sent Noah to his people when he was forty years of age or older and he remained among them a thousand-less-fifty years calling them to affirm God’s Oneness but they denied him; so the Flood engulfed them a deluge of water drifted against them rising above them and drowning them for they were wrongdoers idolaters.

hype_questions: What is the significance of patience in Islam?
How did Noah's message of Tawheed affect his people?
What is the consequences of denying God's Oneness?
propositions: We sent Noah to his people when he was forty years of age or older.
Noah remained among them a thousand-less-fifty years calling them to affirm God’s Oneness.
The Flood engulfed them a deluge of water drifted against them rising above them and drowning them.

source_text:
Verse: But We delivered him and those in the Ark, making it a sign for all people.

Tafsir: Then We delivered him namely Noah and the occupants of the ship those who were with him in it and We made this a sign a lesson for all peoples for all peoples that would come after them should they disobey the messengers sent to them. Noah lived for a further sixty years or more after the Flood until mankind multiplied again.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Ark in Islamic tradition?
How did Noah's patience and obedience to Allah ultimately lead to his salvation?
What lesson can be learned from the story of Noah and the Flood for future generations?
propositions: Allah delivered Noah and those with him on the Ark.
The Ark was a sign for all people, serving as a lesson for future generations.
Noah lived sixty years or more after the Flood, allowing humanity to repopulate.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ when Abraham said to his people, “Worship Allah, and fear Him. This is better for you, if only you knew.

Tafsir: And mention Abraham when he said to his people ‘Worship God and fear Him fear His punishment; that is better for you than the worship of idols which you practice if you only knew what is good from what is otherwise.

hype_questions: What is the best way to worship God?
Why should we fear God's punishment?
Is worshipping idols better than worshipping one true God?
propositions: Worship Allah and fear Him.
The worship of idols is not better than worshipping one true God.
Fearing God's punishment is better for you than not fearing it.

source_text:
Verse: You worship besides Allah nothing but idols, simply creating lies ˹about them˺. Those you worship besides Allah certainly cannot give you any provision. So seek provision from Allah ˹alone˺, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.

Tafsir: What you worship besides God that is other than Him are only graven images and you fabricate a calumny you speak lies such as ‘These graven images are God’s partners’. Truly those whom you worship besides God have no power to provide for you. So seek your provision from God request it from Him and worship Him and be thankful to Him; to Him you shall be returned.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of worshiping idols besides Allah?
How can one seek provision from Allah alone?
What happens to those who worship idols besides Allah?
propositions: You worship besides Allah nothing but idols, simply creating lies about them.
Those you worship besides Allah certainly cannot give you any provision.
Seek provision from Allah alone and worship Him, and be grateful to Him.

source_text:
Verse: If you ˹Meccans˺ persist in denial, so did ˹many˺ communities before you. The Messenger’s duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.”

Tafsir: But if you deny that is if you deny me O people of Mecca then many communities have denied before you that is before my time; and the messenger’s duty is only to communicate the Message clearly’. Both stories are meant to comfort the Prophet s. And regarding his people God exalted be He says

hype_questions: What happens to communities that deny the message?
How does the Prophet's duty relate to his people's denial?
Why is God exalted?
propositions: If you persist in denial, so did many communities before you.
The Messenger's duty is only to deliver the message clearly.
Many communities have denied before you that is before my time;
God exalted be He says

source_text:
Verse: Have they not seen how Allah originates the creation then resurrects it? That is certainly easy for Allah.

Tafsir: Have they not seen yaraw or taraw ‘have you not seen?’ observed how God originates creation yubdi’u from 4th form abda’a; a variant reading has yabda‘u from 1st form bada’a both with the same meaning ‘He creates them originally’ then He restores it namely creation just as He originated them? Surely that which is mentioned of the first and the second acts of creation is easy for God so how can they deny the second one?

hype_questions: Does Allah's power of creation and resurrection make it impossible for humans to deny the second act?
Can humans truly deny the ease of Allah's actions in creating and then restoring the world?
Is it reasonable for humans to reject the idea that Allah's first and second acts of creation are both easy for Him?
propositions: Allah originates creation.
Allah resurrects creation.
The ease of Allah's actions in creating and then restoring the world is undeniable.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Travel throughout the land and see how He originated the creation, then Allah will bring it into being one more time. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: Say ‘Travel in the land and observe how He originated creation of those before you and how He made them die. Then God shall bring about the other genesis al-nashā’a or al-nash’a. Truly God has power over all things among them the origination of creation and the restoration thereof.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's power over creation?

source_text:
Verse: And you cannot escape Him on earth or in heaven. Nor have you any protector or helper besides Allah.”

Tafsir: And you will never be able to thwart Him your Lord and prevent Him from catching up with you on earth or in the heaven were you to be in it in other words you cannot elude Him; and you do not have besides God that is other than Him any guardian to defend you against Him or any helper to help you escape from His chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who disbelieve in Allah’s signs and the meeting with Him, it is they who will have no hope in His mercy. And it is they who will suffer a painful punishment.

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve in God’s signs and the encounter with Him namely the Qur’ān and the Resurrection respectively they have despaired of My mercy that is of attaining My Paradise and for those there shall be a painful chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject Allah's signs and the Day of Judgment?

source_text:
Verse: But the only response of Abraham’s people was to say: “Kill him or burn him!” But Allah saved him from the fire. Surely in this are signs for people who believe.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says with regard to the tale of Abraham peace be upon him But the only answer of his people was that they said ‘Slay him or burn him!’ Then God delivered him from the fire into which they threw him by making it cool and harmless for him. Surely in that namely in that deliverance of him from it there are signs — namely the fact that it did not have any affect on him despite its greatness and the fact that it was extinguished and that within a brief period meadows sprung up in its place — for a people who believe a people who affirm the truth of God’s Oneness and His power for they are the ones to benefit from these signs.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Abraham's deliverance from the fire?
How did God make the fire 'cool and harmless' for Abraham?
What are the signs that people who believe can learn from Abraham's story?
propositions: Abraham's people asked him to be killed or burned.
God saved Abraham from the fire.
The fire did not affect Abraham despite its greatness.
Meadows sprouted up in the place of the fire after a brief period.

source_text:
Verse: He said ˹to his people˺, “You have taken idols ˹for worship˺ instead of Allah, only to keep ˹the bond of˺ harmony among yourselves in this worldly life. But on the Day of Judgment you will disown and curse one another. Your home will be the Fire, and you will have no helper!”

Tafsir: And he Abraham said ‘You have adopted mere idols besides God which you worship mā of innamā relates to the verbal noun for the sake of mutual affection between you mawaddatu baynikum this is the predicate of inna of innamā; the accusative reading mawaddata baynikum would denote a direct object denoting reason so that the mā would denote ‘entirety’ — in other words you are friends of one another in your worship of them in the life of this world. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will disown one another the leaders will dissociate from those who followed them; and you will curse one another those who followed will curse their leaders; and your abode your destination all together will be the Fire and you will have no helpers’ to protect you against it.

hype_questions: What happens to those who worship idols besides God?
Will the leaders be held accountable for their followers on the Day of Judgment?
What is the ultimate destination of those who adopt idols as a form of mutual affection?
propositions: You have taken idols for worship instead of Allah.
The bond of harmony among yourselves in this worldly life is maintained through idolatry.
On the Day of Judgment, you will disown and curse one another.
Your home will be the Fire.
You will have no helper to protect you against it.

source_text:
Verse: So Lot believed in him. And Abraham said, “I am emigrating ˹in obedience˺ to my Lord. He ˹alone˺ is indeed the Almighty, All-Wise.”

Tafsir: And Lot believed in him he affirmed the sincerity of Abraham and he was his paternal nephew from his brother Hārān and he Abraham said ‘Indeed I am migrating away from my people toward my Lord to where my Lord commands. So he shunned his people and emigrated from the rural lands of Iraq to Syria. Indeed He is the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise’ in what He does.

hype_questions: What does it mean to emigrate in obedience to one's Lord?
How did Abraham demonstrate sincerity towards his faith?
What are the consequences of shunning one's people for the sake of faith?
propositions: Abraham emigrated from Iraq to Syria in obedience to his Lord.
Lot believed in Abraham and affirmed his sincerity.
Abraham was the paternal nephew of Hārān, Abraham's brother.

source_text:
Verse: We blessed him with Isaac and ˹later˺ Jacob, and reserved prophethood and revelation for his descendants. We gave him his reward in this life, and in the Hereafter he will certainly be among the righteous.

Tafsir: And We gave him after Ishmael Isaac and Jacob after Isaac; and We ordained among his descendants prophethood thus all prophets after Abraham are descended from him and the Scripture meaning the Holy Books the Torah the Gospels the Psalms and the Criterion al-furqān. And We gave him his reward in this world which is fair praise of him by members of all the Abrahamic religions. And in the Hereafter he shall truly be among the righteous for whom there shall be the highest degrees of reward.

hype_questions: What is the significance of prophethood in Islam?
How are Abraham's descendants related to all prophets?
What rewards can be expected for those who are righteous?
propositions: Abraham was blessed with Isaac and Jacob.
Prophethood and revelation were reserved for Abraham's descendants.
Abraham received his reward in this life, and will be among the righteous in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ when Lot rebuked ˹the men of˺ his people: “You certainly commit a shameful deed that no man has ever done before you.

Tafsir: And mention Lot when he said to his people ‘Truly you read a-innakum pronouncing both hamzas or not pronouncing the second and inserting an alif between the two in either case and in both instances commit lewdness namely coming in unto the rears of men such as none in all the worlds of jinn or men has committed before you.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Lot's rebuke to his people?
How did Lot describe the shameful deed committed by his people?
What makes this deed unique and unprecedented?
propositions: Lot rebuked his people for committing a shameful deed.
The shameful deed involves lewdness, specifically coming in unto men's rears.
This deed is unique and unprecedented, as no one else has committed it before.

source_text:
Verse: Do you really lust after ˹other˺ men, abuse the travellers, and practice immorality ˹openly˺ in your gatherings?” His people’s only response was to say ˹mockingly˺: “Bring Allah’s punishment upon us, if what you say is true.”

Tafsir: What! Do you come unto men and cut off the way the travel roads of passers-by committing lewd acts with whoever passes your way such that people ceased to pass by where you live and you discuss in your gatherings in your conversations indecency?’ you discuss committing lewd acts with one another. But the only answer of his people was that they said ‘Bring us the chastisement of God if you are truthful’ in your deeming such acts vile and that chastisement will befall those who do such things.

hype_questions: Do you really lust after other men?

The chastisement of God will befall those who do such things.

source_text:
Verse: Lot prayed, “My Lord! Help me against the people of corruption.”

source_text:

Tafsir: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings of Isaac and Jacob after him they said ‘We shall assuredly destroy the people of this town namely the town of Lot for truly its people are evildoers’ disbelievers.

Assuredly We shall deliver him read la-nunjiyannahu or la-nunajjiyannahu and his family except his wife she is of those who will stay behind’ of those who will remain behind in the chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: And when Our messenger-angels came to Lot, he was distressed and worried by their arrival. They reassured ˹him˺, “Do not fear, nor grieve. We will surely deliver you and your family—except your wife, who is one of the doomed.

Tafsir: And when Our messengers came to Lot he was distressed on their account he was grieved because of them and he was constrained unable to help them because they had handsome faces dressed as guests and thus he feared for them from his people. So they informed him that they were the messengers of his Lord. But they said ‘Do not be afraid nor grieve. We shall surely deliver you read munajjūka or munjūka and your family except your wife she is of those who will remain behind ahlaka ‘your family’ is in the accusative as a supplement to the suffixed direct object pronoun kāf of munajjūka ‘We shall surely deliver you’.

hype_questions: Will the messengers of God save me and my family?

Lot was distressed on their account.
They reassured him, 'Do not fear, nor grieve.'
We will surely deliver you and your family—except your wife, who is one of the doomed.
They had handsome faces dressed as guests.
He feared for them from his people.
So they informed him that they were the messengers of his Lord.
But they said 'Do not be afraid nor grieve.'
We shall surely deliver you and your family.

source_text:
Verse: We are certainly bringing down a punishment from heaven upon the people of this city for their rebelliousness.”

Tafsir: We are indeed going to bring down read munzilūna or munazzilūna upon the people of this town a scourge a chastisement from the heaven because of on account of the acts of their immorality’.

source_text:

hype_questions: What is the significance of leaving ruins as a lesson for people?

source_text:
Verse: And to the people of Midian ˹We sent˺ their brother Shu’aib. He said, “O my people! Worship Allah, and hope for ˹the reward of˺ the Last Day. And do not go about spreading corruption in the land.”

Tafsir: And We sent to Midian their brother Shu‘ayb. He said ‘O my people! Worship God and anticipate the Last Day fear it namely the Day of Resurrection; and do not be degenerate in the earth working corruption’ mufsidīna is a circumstantial qualifier emphasising its operator wa-lā ta‘thaw ‘do not be degenerate’; it the verb derives from ‘athiya meaning afsada ‘he corrupted’.

hype_questions: What is the importance of worshiping God in Islam?

Do not go about spreading corruption in the land.
Fear the Day of Resurrection, which is a time of reckoning.

source_text:
Verse: But they rejected him, so an ˹overwhelming˺ earthquake struck them and they fell lifeless in their homes.

Tafsir: But they denied him and so the earthquake the violent tremor seized them and they ended up lying lifeless prostrate in their habitations keeled over their knees dead.

hype_questions: What happens when someone is rejected by God?
