An overwhelming earthquake struck them.
They fell lifeless in their homes.

source_text:
Verse: And the people of ’Ȃd and Thamûd ˹met a similar fate˺, which must be clear to you ˹Meccans˺ from their ruins. Satan made their ˹evil˺ deeds appealing to them, hindering them from the ˹Right˺ Way, although they were capable of reasoning.

Tafsir: And We destroyed ‘Ād and Thamūd may be fully declined or not as diptotes denoting both the district or the tribe respectively— it is indeed evident to you their destruction from their former dwellings in al-Hijr and in Yemen. For Satan adorned for them their deeds of disbelief and disobedience and thus barred them from the Way the way of truth though they had been discerning perceptive people.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Satan's influence on humanity?

Satan made their evil deeds appealing to them, hindering them from the Right Way.
Although they had been discerning perceptive people, Satan barred them from the Way of truth.

source_text:
Verse: ˹We˺ also ˹destroyed˺ Korah, Pharaoh, and Haman. Indeed, Moses had come to them with clear proofs, but they behaved arrogantly in the land. Yet they could not escape ˹Us˺.

Tafsir: And We destroyed Korah and Pharaoh and Hāmān! And verily Moses brought them beforehand clear signs manifest proofs but they acted arrogantly in the land; and they could not thwart Us they could not elude Our chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens when a group of people refuse to acknowledge the signs of God?

propositions: We destroyed Korah, Pharaoh, and Haman.

source_text:
Verse: So We seized each ˹people˺ for their sin: against some of them We sent a storm of stones, some were overtaken by a ˹mighty˺ blast, some We caused the earth to swallow, and some We drowned. Allah would not have wronged them, but it was they who wronged themselves.

Tafsir: So each of those mentioned We seized for his sin; and among them were some upon whom We unleashed a squall of stones as in the case of the people of Lot and among them were some who were seized by the Cry such as Thamūd and among them were some whom We made the earth swallow such as Korah and among them were some whom We drowned like the people of Noah Pharaoh and his people. And God never wronged them by chastising them for having committed no sin but they wronged themselves by committing sins.

hype_questions: What happens to those who commit sin?
Why do people get punished for their sins?
How does Allah hold individuals accountable for their actions?
propositions: Allah seized each person for their sin.
Some were struck by a storm of stones, others by a mighty blast, others by the earth swallowing them, and others by drowning.
God chastises those who commit sin, but it was they who wronged themselves.

source_text:
Verse: The parable of those who take protectors other than Allah is that of a spider spinning a shelter. And the flimsiest of all shelters is certainly that of a spider, if only they knew.

Tafsir: The likeness of those who choose besides God other patrons namely idols from whom they hope to profit is as the likeness of the spider that makes a home for itself in which to shelter. And truly the frailest the weakest of homes is the home of the spider for it neither protects it from heat nor cold — likewise idols cannot benefit those who worship them — if they only knew this they would not worship them.

hype_questions: What happens when one seeks shelter from idols instead of Allah?

propositions: Those who choose besides God other patrons are like a spider spinning a shelter.
The frailest and weakest of homes is the home of the spider, which neither protects from heat nor cold.
Idols cannot benefit those who worship them.

source_text:
Verse: Allah surely knows that whatever ˹gods˺ they invoke besides Him are ˹simply˺ nothing. For He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: Truly God knows whatever thing mā functions like alladhī they call on what they worship read yad‘ūna ‘they call on’ or tad‘ūna ‘you call on’ besides Him other than Him. And He is the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in what He does.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of worshiping idols besides Allah?

propositions: Allah knows that whatever gods people invoke besides Him are nothing.
God knows what people call on when they worship, other than Himself.
Allah is the Mighty in His kingdom and the Wise in what He does.

source_text:
Verse: These are the parables We set forth for humanity, but none will understand them except the people of knowledge.

Tafsir: And such similitudes in the Qur’ān We strike them We coin them for the sake of mankind; but none understands them none grasp them except those who know those who reflect.

hype_questions: What are the parables set forth by God in the Qur'ān?
How can humans understand the similitudes in the Qur'ān?

propositions: God sets forth parables for humanity.
The Qur'ān contains similitudes that are struck and coined for mankind.
None will understand the parables except those who know.

source_text:
Verse: Allah created the heavens and the earth for a purpose. Surely in this is a sign for the people of faith.

Tafsir: God created the heavens and the earth with truth that is rightly. Surely in that there is a sign indicating His power exalted be He for believers — they are specifically mentioned because they are the ones to benefit thereby in their faith in contrast to disbelievers.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creation?
How do believers benefit from the signs of faith?
What distinguishes believers from disbelievers?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and the earth.
The creation of the heavens and the earth is a sign of God's power.
Believers are specifically mentioned because they will benefit from their faith.
Disbelievers do not benefit from their lack of faith.

source_text:
Verse: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, ˹genuine˺ prayer should deter ˹one˺ from indecency and wickedness. The remembrance of Allah is ˹an˺ even greater ˹deterrent˺. And Allah ˹fully˺ knows what you ˹all˺ do.

Tafsir: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book the Qur’ān and maintain prayer; truly prayer prohibits lewd acts and indecency defined as such according to the Law. In other words that is its purpose provided that the person adheres to observance of it. And the remembrance of God is surely greater than other acts of obedience and God knows what you do and He will requite you for them.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of prayer in Islam?
How does prayer relate to obedience and accountability in Islam?
What is the significance of remembrance of Allah in Islamic teachings?
propositions: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book.
Establish prayer.
Indeed, genuine prayer should deter one from indecency and wickedness.
The remembrance of Allah is an even greater deterrent than prayer.
Allah fully knows what you all do.

source_text:
Verse: Do not argue with the People of the Book unless gracefully, except with those of them who act wrongfully. And say, “We believe in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to you. Our God and your God is ˹only˺ One. And to Him we ˹fully˺ submit.”

Tafsir: And do not dispute with the People of the Scripture unless it be with that — in that manner of disputation bettering the most virtuous way such as calling them to God by reference to His signs and pointing out His arguments; except in the case of those of them who have done wrong by waging war and refusing to accept to pay the jizya-tax dispute with these using the sword until such time as they submit or pay the jizya-tax; and say to those who have accepted the imposition upon them of the jizya-tax should they inform you of something stated in their Scriptures ‘We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you — and neither believe nor disbelieve them in that which they tell you — our God and your God is one and the same and to Him we submit’ to Him we are obedient.

hype_questions: Can interfaith dialogue be effective in promoting mutual understanding?
What is the historical context of the jizya tax, and how has it been received by different communities?
How can individuals demonstrate their submission to one God while respecting the beliefs of others?
propositions: It is permissible to engage in respectful dialogue with people of other faiths.
The jizya tax was imposed on non-Muslim communities as a form of protection and tribute.
Submission to one God is a fundamental aspect of Islamic faith, but it does not require the rejection of other faiths.

source_text:
Verse: Similarly ˹to earlier messengers˺, We have revealed to you a Book ˹O Prophet˺. ˹The faithful of˺ those to whom We gave the Scriptures believe in it, as do some of these ˹pagan Arabs˺. And none denies Our revelations except the ˹stubborn˺ disbelievers.

Tafsir: Thus have We revealed to you the Book the Qur’ān in the same way that We have revealed to them the Torah and other scripture. And so those to whom We have given the Scripture the Torah such as ‘Abd Allāh b. Salām and others believe in it in the Qur’ān and of these people of Mecca there are some who believe in it; and none denies Our signs after they have been manifested except disbelievers namely the Jews and those for whom it was apparent that the Qur’ān was the truth and that the one who brought it was truthful but still denied it.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Quran's revelation?
How do people respond to the Quran after receiving the Torah?
Who are the disbelievers that deny the truth of the Quran?
propositions: We have revealed to you a Book, O Prophet.
Those to whom We gave the Scriptures believe in it.
None denies Our revelations except the stubborn disbelievers.
We have revealed to them the Torah and other scripture in the same way as we revealed to you the Quran.
Those who were given the Scripture, such as 'Abd Allāh b. Salām, believe in the Quran.
Of those people of Mecca, there are some who believe in the Quran.
The Jews and others for whom it was apparent that the Quran was the truth and that the one who brought it was truthful but still denied it.

source_text:
Verse: You ˹O Prophet˺ could not read any writing ˹even˺ before this ˹revelation˺, nor could you write at all. Otherwise, the people of falsehood would have been suspicious.

Tafsir: And you did not use to recite before this namely before the Qur’ān any other Book nor did you write it with your right hand for had you been reciting something and writing then those who follow falsehood the Jews would have had doubts about you and would have said ‘What the Torah states is that he will be unlettered ummī unable to read or write’.

hype_questions: Would the people of falsehood have believed in the Prophet's prophethood if he could read and write?
How would the Jews react if the Prophet could recite and write with ease?
What would be the consequences if the Prophet were unlettered and unable to read or write?
propositions: The Prophet was unable to read any writing before receiving the revelation.
He did not use to recite any other Book before this, namely the Qur’ān.
If the Prophet could recite and write with ease, the Jews would have doubted his prophethood.

source_text:
Verse: But this ˹Quran˺ is ˹a set of˺ clear revelations ˹preserved˺ in the hearts of those gifted with knowledge. And none denies Our revelations except the ˹stubborn˺ wrongdoers.

Tafsir: Nay but it that is the Qur’ān which you have brought is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge namely the believers who preserve it in their hearts and none denies Our signs except wrongdoers namely the Jews — they denied them after they were manifested to them.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Quran?
How do believers preserve knowledge in their hearts?
Who are the wrongdoers that deny Our signs?
propositions: This is a set of clear revelations preserved in the hearts of those gifted with knowledge.
The believers who have been given knowledge preserve it in their hearts.
None denies Our signs except the wrongdoers.

source_text:
Verse: They say, “If only ˹some˺ signs had been sent down to him from his Lord!” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Signs are only with Allah. And I am only sent with a clear warning.”

Tafsir: And they namely the disbelievers of Mecca say ‘Why has not some sign been sent down to him to Muhammad (s) from his Lord?’ āyatun ‘sign’ a variant reading has āyātun ‘signs’ such as the she-camel of Sālih or the staff of Moses or the Table of Jesus. Say to them ‘Signs are only with God and He sends them down as He will and I am only a plain warner’ making manifest my warning of the punishment of the Fire for disobedient people.

hype_questions: What is the significance of signs in Islam?
How does Muhammad (s) respond to criticism about not receiving signs from Allah?
What is the nature of Muhammad's warning and its purpose?
propositions: Signs are only with Allah.
I am only sent with a clear warning.
My warning makes manifest the punishment of the Fire for disobedient people.

source_text:
Verse: Is it not enough for them that We have sent down to you the Book, ˹which is˺ recited to them. Surely in this ˹Quran˺ is a mercy and reminder for people who believe.

Tafsir: Is it not sufficient for them regarding what they have demanded that We have revealed to you the Book the Qur’ān which is recited to them? — as it constitutes a ongoing sign that will never terminate in contrast to the signs mentioned. Surely in that Book is mercy and a reminder an admonition for a people who believe.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Quran in Islam?
How does the Quran serve as a reminder for believers?
What role does mercy play in the Quran?
propositions: The Quran has been revealed to humanity.
The Quran serves as an ongoing sign that will never terminate.
The Quran contains mercy and a reminder for those who believe.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Sufficient is Allah as a Witness between me and you. He ˹fully˺ knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah, it is they who are the ˹true˺ losers.”

Tafsir: Say ‘God suffices as a witness between me and you’ of my sincerity. He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth including my circumstances and yours. And those who believe in falsehood namely all that is worshipped besides God and who disbelieve in God from among you — those they are the losers in their bargain for they have purchased disbelief in return for faith.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Allah as a witness in our lives?
How does Allah's knowledge impact our faith and actions?
What are the consequences of believing in falsehood and disbelieving in Allah?
propositions: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you.
Allah knows everything that exists in the heavens and the earth, including human circumstances.
Those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah are the losers in their bargain.
Disbelieving in Allah means purchasing disbelief for faith.

source_text:
Verse: They challenge you ˹O Prophet˺ to hasten the punishment. Had it not been for a time already set, the punishment would have certainly come to them ˹at once˺. But it will definitely take them by surprise when they least expect it.

Tafsir: And they ask you to hasten the chastisement. Yet were it not for an appointed term for this chastisement the chastisement would have come upon them before long but it shall assuredly come upon them suddenly while they are unaware of the time of its coming.

hype_questions: Will the punishment come sooner or later?
Can humans hasten the punishment?
What is the appointed term for the chastisement?
propositions: The punishment will come upon them suddenly while they are unaware of the time of its coming.
Had it not been for a time already set, the punishment would have certainly come to them at once.
Yet were it not for an appointed term for this chastisement the chastisement would have come upon them before long

source_text:
Verse: They urge you to hasten the punishment. And Hell will certainly encompass the disbelievers

Tafsir: And they ask you to hasten the chastisement in this world. And lo! Hell shall encompass the disbelievers

hype_questions: Will hastening punishment bring about a faster end to suffering?
What is the ultimate fate of those who disbelieve in Allah's message?
Can patience and faith lead to salvation from Hell's torment?
propositions: They urge you to hasten the punishment.
Hell will certainly encompass the disbelievers.
They ask you to hasten the chastisement in this world.

source_text:
Verse: on the Day the punishment will overwhelm them from above them and from below their feet. And it will be said, “Reap what you sowed.”

Tafsir: on the Day when the chastisement shall envelop them from above them and from under their feet and We shall say thereat read the verb as naqūlu in other words ‘We shall command that it be said; or if read yaqūlu ‘he shall say’ namely the one in charge of meting out chastisement ‘Taste now what you used to do!’ that is taste the requital for it as you will not be able to elude Us.

hype_questions: What happens on the Day of Reckoning?
Will I be held accountable for my actions?
How will I face punishment?
propositions: The punishment will overwhelm them from above and from below their feet.
We shall command that it be said, 'Taste now what you used to do!'
You will not be able to elude Us.

source_text:
Verse: O My believing servants! My earth is truly spacious, so worship Me ˹alone˺.

Tafsir: O My servants who believe! My earth is indeed vast. So worship only Me in whichever land worship is possible by emigrating to it from a land in which worship is not possible — this verse was revealed regarding the oppressed Muslims living in Mecca who were constrained to manifest their Islam in it.

hype_questions: What is the significance of worshiping only one God?
How can Muslims manifest their Islam in a land where it's not possible?
What does it mean to emigrate to a new land for the sake of worship?
propositions: My earth is truly spacious.
Worship Me alone in whichever land worship is possible by emigrating to it from a land in which worship is not possible.

source_text:
Verse: Every soul will taste death, then to Us you will ˹all˺ be returned.

Tafsir: Every soul shall taste death. Then to Us you shall be returned turja‘ūna; or yurja‘ūna ‘they shall be returned’ after resurrection.

hype_questions: What happens to a person's soul after death?
Will I be resurrected and returned to Allah?
What is the ultimate fate of every soul?
propositions: Every soul will taste death.
Then you shall be returned to Us.

source_text:
Verse: ˹As for˺ those who believe and do good, We will certainly house them in ˹elevated˺ mansions in Paradise, under which rivers flow, to stay there forever. How excellent is the reward for those who work ˹righteousness!˺—

Tafsir: And those who believe and perform righteous deeds We shall surely lodge them We shall give them residence a variant reading has nuthwiyannahum derived from thawā’ ‘residence’; the transitive link to the indirect object ghurafan is made without the preposition fī ‘in’ in lofty abodes of Paradise underneath which rivers flow to abide decreed for them to live forever in them — excellent is this reward as the reward of the toilers;

hype_questions: What is the ultimate destination for those who believe and perform righteous deeds?
How will Allah reward those who work righteousness?
What is the nature of the abode prepared for believers in Paradise?
propositions: Those who believe and do good will be housed in elevated mansions in Paradise.
Rivers flow underneath these mansions in Paradise.
Believers will reside in Paradise forever.
The reward for those who work righteousness is excellent.

source_text:
Verse: those who patiently endure, and put their trust in their Lord!

Tafsir: they are those who are steadfast in enduring the harm inflicted upon them by the idolaters and in enduring the Emigration in order to make manifest the religion of Islam and who put their trust in their Lord so that He provides for them whence they do not expect.

hype_questions: What is the significance of patience in Islam?
How does trusting in Allah provide for one's needs?
What is the ultimate goal of emigration in Islam?
propositions: Those who patiently endure and put their trust in their Lord are steadfast in enduring harm inflicted by idolaters.
The Emigration is a means to manifest the religion of Islam.
Trusting in Allah provides for one's needs without expectation.

source_text:
Verse: How many are the creatures that cannot secure their provisions! ˹It is˺ Allah ˹Who˺ provides for them and you ˹as well˺. He is indeed the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Tafsir: And how many ka-ayyin means kam an animal there is that does not bear its own provision on account of its inability to do so. Yet God provides for it and for you O Emigrants al-muhājirūn even when you carry with you neither supplies nor substance. And He is the Hearer of your sayings the Knower of your consciences.

hype_questions: Does Allah not provide for all creatures, including those that cannot secure their provisions?
Can humans truly rely on themselves to provide for their needs, or is it Allah's responsibility?
How does Allah's provision extend to those who are unable to care for themselves?
propositions: Allah provides for the creatures that cannot secure their provisions.
There is no animal that can bear its own provision due to its inability to do so.
God provides for both humans and animals, regardless of their ability to provide for themselves.

source_text:
Verse: If you ask them ˹O Prophet˺ who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon ˹for your benefit˺, they will certainly say, “Allah!” How can they then be deluded ˹from the truth˺?

Tafsir: And if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths you were to ask them namely the disbelievers ‘Who created the heavens and the earth and disposed the sun and the moon?’ They would assuredly say ‘God.’ So how then are they turned away? from affirming His Oneness after affirming that God created them.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's creation?
How can disbelievers affirm God's existence while denying His Oneness?
Why do people reject the truth after acknowledging Allah's power?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and the earth.
The sun and moon were subjected to Allah's will.
Disbelievers acknowledge Allah's existence but deny His Oneness.

source_text:
Verse: Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills of His servants. Surely Allah has ˹full˺ knowledge of everything.

Tafsir: God extends provision He makes it abundant for whomever He will of His servants by way of a test and He straitens He restricts it for him after having extended it that is for whomever He will to try. Truly God has knowledge of all things among them the occasion in which it is appropriate for Him to extend or to straiten.

hype_questions: Does Allah decide who gets abundant provisions?
Why does Allah sometimes restrict provision for His servants?
What is the purpose of Allah's tests through provision?
propositions: Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills.
God extends provision, making it abundant for whomever He will of His servants by way of a test.
He straitens and restricts provision for him after having extended it.
This is for whomever Allah wills to try.
Truly God has knowledge of all things among them the occasion in which it is appropriate for Him to extend or to straiten.

source_text:
Verse: And if you ask them who sends down rain from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death, they will surely say, “Allah!” Say, “Praise be to Allah!” In fact, most of them do not understand.

Tafsir: And if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths you were to ask them ‘Who sends down water from the heaven and therewith revives the earth after its death?’ They would assuredly say ‘God’ so how can they ascribe partners to Him?! Say to them ‘Praise be to God!’ that the proof has been established against you. Nay but most of them do not realise their contradictiousness in this respect.

hype_questions: What is the source of rain and water that revives the earth?
How can humans ascribe partners to Allah when they acknowledge His power in creating life?
What is the proof that establishes against those who attribute partners to Allah?
propositions: Allah sends down rain from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death.
Most of people do not understand the true nature of Allah's power.
Ascribing partners to Allah is contradictious and has been proven false.

source_text:
Verse: This worldly life is no more than play and amusement. But the Hereafter is indeed the real life, if only they knew.

Tafsir: And the life of this world is nothing but diversion and play whereas closeness to God pertains to concern for the Hereafter since the fruits thereof will be revealed in it. But surely the Abode of the Hereafter is indeed the true Life if they only knew this then they would not prefer this world to it.

hype_questions: What is the true nature of life?
How does one prioritize between this worldly life and the Hereafter?
What are the consequences of preferring the worldly life over the Hereafter?
propositions: The life of this world is nothing but diversion and play.
Closeness to God pertains to concern for the Hereafter.
The Abode of the Hereafter is indeed the true Life if they only knew this.

source_text:
Verse: If they happen to be aboard a ship ˹caught in a storm˺, they cry out to Allah ˹alone˺ in sincere devotion. But as soon as He delivers them ˹safely˺ to shore, they associate ˹others with Him once again˺.

Tafsir: And when they board the ship they call on God making their supplications purely to Him in other words they do not call on any other besides Him suffering distress which only He is able to remove; but when He delivers them to land behold! they ascribe partners to Him

hype_questions: What happens when a person is in distress and calls out to God?
How does God respond to a person's supplication?
Can a person truly be sincere in their devotion to God?
propositions: If someone boards a ship during a storm, they call out to Allah alone with sincere devotion.
Allah is the only one who can remove distress.
When Allah delivers someone safely to shore, they often associate others with Him.

source_text:
Verse: So let them be ungrateful for all We have given them, and ˹let them˺ enjoy themselves ˹for now˺! For they will soon know.

Tafsir: that they may be ungrateful for what We have bestowed on them of graces and that they may seek enjoyment in consenting to worship idols together a variant reading for the purposive wa-li-yatamatta‘ū has wa’l-yatamatta‘ū ‘and let them seek their enjoyment’ as an imperative denoting a threat for they will soon know! the consequences of this.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of seeking enjoyment in idol worship?
How will people react when they realize the error of their ways?
What is the ultimate outcome for those who reject Allah's blessings?
propositions: Allah has bestowed upon them many graces.
They may seek enjoyment in consenting to worship idols.
For they will soon know the consequences of this.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not seen how We have made ˹Mecca˺ a safe haven, whereas people ˹all˺ around them are snatched away? and deny Allah’s favours?

Tafsir: Or is it that they have not seen have not realised that We have appointed their town of Mecca to be a secure Sanctuary while people are snatched away all around them? by being killed or taken captive except for them? Is it that they believe in falsehood in the idol and are wont to be ungrateful for God’s grace? when they ascribe partners to Him?

hype_questions: What is the significance of Mecca being a safe haven?
Why do people around them get snatched away?
How does believing in falsehood and ascribing partners to Allah affect one's gratitude?
propositions: We have made Mecca a safe haven.
People are snatched away all around them by being killed or taken captive except for those in Mecca.
Believing in falsehood and ascribing partners to Allah makes one ungrateful for God’s grace.

source_text:
Verse: And who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah or reject the truth after it has reached them? Is Hell not a ˹fitting˺ home for the disbelievers?

Tafsir: And who — in other words there is none who — does greater wrong than he who invents a lie against God by ascribing partners to Him or denies truth be it the Prophet or the Book when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell a lodging an abode for the disbelievers? in other words there is such an abode therein and such a person belongs with them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who fabricate lies against Allah?
Is there a place where disbelievers will reside in the afterlife?
Who belongs with the disbelievers in Hell?
propositions: Those who invent a lie against God are doing greater wrong.
Denying truth, whether it be about the Prophet or the Book, is also a grave sin.
Hell has a lodging for the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who struggle in Our cause, We will surely guide them along Our Way. And Allah is certainly with the good-doers.

Tafsir: But as for those who struggle for Our sake for Our truth We shall assuredly guide them in Our ways that is the means to come to Us and truly God is with the virtuous the believers assisting and helping.

hype_questions: What happens to those who struggle for a higher purpose?
How can one find guidance on their spiritual journey?
What role does Allah play in the lives of believers?
propositions: Those who struggle in Our cause will be guided along Our Way.
God is with the good-doers and virtuous believers.
The means to come to God is through following His ways.

source_text:
Verse: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm.

Tafsir: Alif lām mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

hype_questions: Does God have a specific meaning in mind when using the alphabet?
Can humans truly understand God's intentions?
What does it mean for God to 'know best'?
propositions: God knows what He means by these letters.
These letters are part of God's language.
God has a specific meaning in mind when using the alphabet.

source_text:
Verse: The Romans have been defeated

Tafsir: The Byzantines — who are among the People of the Scripture — have been vanquished; the Persians vanquished them and they are not people of a scripture but worship graven images. The Meccan disbelievers rejoiced in this defeat of the Byzantines and said to the Muslims ‘We shall vanquish you as the Persians vanquished the Byzantines’;

hype_questions: Will the Muslims be able to withstand the pressure of their enemies?
How will the Muslims respond to the taunts of their foes?
Can the Muslims overcome their challenges and emerge victorious?
propositions: The Byzantines were defeated by the Persians.
The Meccan disbelievers rejoiced at the defeat of the Byzantines.
The Persians vanquished the Byzantines because they are not people of a scripture but worship graven images.

source_text:
Verse: in a nearby land. Yet following their defeat, they will triumph

Tafsir: in the nearer part of the land that is in the Byzantine land that lies nearest to Persia in Mesopotamia al-Jazīra. There the two armies met and the Persians were the ones who had begun the invasion. But they that is the Byzantines after their vanquishing ghalabihim the verbal noun ghalab has been annexed to the direct object hum in other words ghalabatu fāris iyyāhum ‘the Persians’ vanquishing of them’ shall be the victors over the Persians

hype_questions: What is the outcome of a defeat for a group?
How do the victors relate to their defeated enemies?
Can a group that has been defeated still triumph?
propositions: There is a land nearby.
The Persians will be the victors over the Byzantines after their defeat.
The Byzantine land lies nearest to Persia in Mesopotamia al-Jazīra.

source_text:
Verse: within three to nine years. The ˹whole˺ matter rests with Allah before and after ˹victory˺. And on that day the believers will rejoice

Tafsir: in a few years bid‘ usually means between three and nine or ten years. So the two armies met again seven years after this former encounter and the Byzantines defeated the Persians. To God belongs the command before and after that is before the defeat of the Byzantines and thereafter that is to say the Persian victory at first and the Byzantine victory later were the result of God’s command in other words His will and on that day the day when the Byzantines will be victorious the believers shall rejoice

hype_questions: What is the significance of Allah's command in determining the outcome of battles?
How do believers relate to God's will in times of victory and defeat?
What can be inferred about the nature of God's justice from this verse?
propositions: The matter rests with Allah before and after victory.
The Byzantines defeated the Persians seven years after their previous encounter.
God's command determines the outcome of battles, leading to either victory or defeat.

source_text:
Verse: at the victory willed by Allah. He gives victory to whoever He wills. For He is the Almighty, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: in God’s help to them against the Persians. They the believers indeed rejoiced in this as they came to know of it on the day that it took place on the day of the battle of Badr when Gabriel came down with this news thereon in addition to their rejoicing in their victory over the idolaters on that same day. He helps whomever He will; and He is the Mighty the Victor the Merciful to believers.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Allah's victory in Islamic history?
How do believers react to receiving news of their victory from Gabriel?
What does it mean for Allah to help whomever He will?
propositions: Allah gives victory to whoever He wills.
God helps whomever He will; and He is the Mighty the Victor the Merciful to believers.

source_text:
Verse: ˹This is˺ the promise of Allah. ˹And˺ Allah never fails in His promise. But most people do not know.

Tafsir: The promise of God wa‘da’Llāhi is the verbal noun substituting for the full verbal construction; it is actually wa‘adahumu’Llāhu al-nasr ‘God promised them victory’. God does not fail His promise of such help but most people namely the disbelievers of Mecca are not aware of His promise to help them to victory.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's promise?
How does Allah ensure His promises are kept?
Can anyone truly rely on Allah's help?
propositions: Allah promised victory to his people.
Most people, including disbelievers in Mecca, do not know about Allah's promise of help.
God does not fail His promise of assistance.

source_text:
Verse: They ˹only˺ know the worldly affairs of this life, but are ˹totally˺ oblivious to the Hereafter.

Tafsir: They know merely an outward aspect of the life of this world that is to say its various means of securing livelihood such as commerce agriculture construction and cultivation and so on; but they of the Hereafter they are oblivious this repetition of hum ‘they’ is for emphasis.

hype_questions: What are the worldly affairs of this life?
How do people secure their livelihood in this world?
What is the nature of the Hereafter?
propositions: They know merely an outward aspect of the life of this world.
The various means of securing livelihood include commerce, agriculture, construction, and cultivation.
They are oblivious to the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not reflected upon their own being? Allah only created the heavens and the earth and everything in between for a purpose and an appointed term. Yet most people are truly in denial of the meeting with their Lord!

Tafsir: Have they not contemplated themselves? so that they might emerge from their oblivion. God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with the truth and an appointed term for that creation at the conclusion of which this creation will perish and after which will be the Resurrection. But indeed many people that is to say such as the Meccan disbelievers disbelieve in the encounter with their Lord that is they do not believe in resurrection after death.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creation?
Will there be a resurrection after death?
How can people overcome their denial and contemplate themselves?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and earth for a purpose.
God created everything with truth.
The appointed term for creation will end in perishing.
Many people disbelieve in resurrection after death.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not travelled throughout the land to see what was the end of those ˹destroyed˺ before them? They were far superior in might; they cultivated the land and developed it more than these ˹Meccans˺ ever have. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. Allah would have never wronged them, but it was they who wronged themselves.

Tafsir: Have they not travelled in the land and beheld how was the consequence for those before them? of past communities which was that they were destroyed for denying their messengers. They were more powerful than them — such were ‘Ād and Thamūd — and they effected the land they tilled it and churned it up to sow crops and cultivate trees and developed it more than these the Meccan disbelievers have developed it; and their messengers brought them clear signs manifest proofs for God would never wrong them by destroying them without being guilty but they used to wrong themselves by denying their messengers.

hype_questions: What happened to the communities that denied their messengers?
How did the power and development of past communities compare to the current state?
Why were some communities destroyed while others were not?
propositions: Those who came before them were destroyed for denying their messengers.
The 'Ād and Thamūd were more powerful than the Meccans and developed the land more.
God would never wrong a community by destroying it without being guilty, but they used to wrong themselves by denying their messengers.

source_text:
Verse: Then most evil was the end of the evildoers for denying and mocking the signs of Allah.

Tafsir: Then the consequence for those who committed evil was evil al-sū’ā is the feminine form of al-aswa’ ‘the worst’; it may be read as the predicate of kāna if one reads ‘āqibatu in the nominative; or it is the subject of kāna if read as ‘āqibata in the accusative; and so what is meant is Hell in the former reading or according to the latter reading simply their evil actions because they denied the signs of God the Qur’ān and made a mock of them.

hype_questions: What is the consequence for those who deny the signs of Allah?
How do evil actions manifest when one mocks the signs of God?
What happens to those who make a mockery of the Qur'ān?
propositions: The end of evildoers was evil due to their denial and mockery of Allah's signs.
Hell is the consequence for those who deny the signs of God.
Their evil actions are a result of denying the signs of God and mocking them.

source_text:
Verse: It is Allah Who originates the creation, and will resurrect it. And then to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.

Tafsir: God originates creation in other words He produces the creation of mankind then He will reproduce it that is the creation of them after their death then to Him you shall be returned read turja‘ūna; or yurja‘ūna ‘they shall be returned’.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate fate of human existence?
How does Allah relate to creation and its eventual end?
What happens to individuals after death?
propositions: Allah originates creation.
Allah will resurrect creation.
Individuals will be returned to Allah after death.

source_text:
Verse: On the Day the Hour will arrive, the wicked will be dumbstruck.

Tafsir: And on the Day when the Hour comes the sinners will be dumbfounded the idolaters will be fall into silence as their line of argument can no longer be continued.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the truth on the Day of Judgment?
How will the wicked be treated when their time comes?
Will the idolaters find a way to justify themselves in front of Allah?
propositions: The Hour will arrive on the Day of Judgment.
Sinners will be dumbfounded on the Day of Judgment.
Idolaters will fall into silence as their argument can no longer be continued.

source_text:
Verse: There will be no intercessors for them from among their associate-gods, and they will ˹totally˺ deny their associate-gods.

Tafsir: And none from among those partners of theirs those whom they ascribed as partners of God namely the idols to intercede for them shall be intercessors for them and they shall disavow these partners of theirs in other words they shall dissociate from them.

hype_questions: Can idols intercede for humans?
Will humans disavow their associate-gods?
What happens to those who ascribe partners to God?
propositions: There will be no intercessors from among the associate-gods.
Humans shall dissociate from their associate-gods.
Idols are not capable of interceding for humans.

source_text:
Verse: And on the Day the Hour will arrive, the people will then be split ˹into two groups˺.

Tafsir: And on the Day when the Hour comes that day yawma’idhin is repeated for emphasis they believers and disbelievers shall be separated.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who disbelieve on the Day of Judgment?
How will believers be distinguished from disbelievers on that day?
What is the nature of the separation between believers and disbelievers?
propositions: The Hour will arrive on a specific day.
Believers and disbelievers will be separated on that day.
Yawma'idhin is repeated for emphasis.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who believed and did good, they will be rejoicing in a Garden.

Tafsir: As for those who believed and performed righteous deeds they shall be made happy in a garden of Paradise.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe and perform righteous deeds?
How will believers be treated in the afterlife?
What can one expect to find in a garden of Paradise?
propositions: Those who believed and performed righteous deeds shall be made happy.
Believers will rejoice in a Garden of Paradise.
Righteous deeds are rewarded with happiness in the afterlife.

source_text:
Verse: And as for those who disbelieved, and denied Our signs and the meeting ˹with Allah˺ in the Hereafter, they will be confined in punishment.

Tafsir: But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs namely the Qur’ān and the encounter of the Hereafter the Resurrection and other matters those they shall be arraigned into the chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the Quran and deny the afterlife?
Will those who disbelieve be punished for their denial of Allah's signs?
How will Allah deal with individuals who refuse to acknowledge the Resurrection?
propositions: Those who disbelieved and denied Our signs shall be confined in punishment.
The Qur'ān is one of the signs that were denied by those who disbelieve.
The Resurrection is a matter that will be arraigned against those who disbelieve.

source_text:
Verse: So glorify Allah in the evening and in the morning—

Tafsir: So glory be to God — in other words so glorify God meaning perform prayer — when you enter the time of the night in which there are two prayers the sunset one maghrib and the later night one ‘ishā’ and when you rise in the morning in which there is the morning prayer subh.

hype_questions: What is the significance of performing prayer during the evening and morning?
How many prayers are performed in a day during the night time?
What is the name of the prayer performed at sunset?
propositions: Glorify Allah in the evening.
Glorify God by performing prayer when entering the time of the night with two prayers: maghrib and ‘ishā’.
Rise in the morning to perform the morning prayer, subh.

source_text:
Verse: all praise is for Him in the heavens and the earth—as well as in the afternoon, and at noon.

Tafsir: And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth — a parenthetical statement in other words the inhabitants in both of these realms praise Him — and as the sun declines wa-‘ashiyyan is a supplement to hīna ‘when’ of the previous verse in which comes the afternoon prayer ‘asr and when you enter noontime in which comes the midday prayer zuhr.

hype_questions: What is the time of day when the afternoon prayer 'asr is performed?
At what time does the midday prayer zuhr take place?
When does the sun decline?
propositions: All praise belongs to Him in the heavens and the earth.
The inhabitants of both realms praise Him.
The afternoon prayer 'asr is performed when the sun declines.
Noontime, or midday, is when the zuhr prayer takes place.

source_text:
Verse: He brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. And He gives life to the earth after its death. And so will you be brought forth ˹from the grave˺.

Tafsir: He brings forth the living from the dead as in the case of the human being who is produced from a sperm-drop and a bird from an egg and He brings forth the dead a sperm-drop or an egg from the living and He revives the earth with vegetation after it has died dried out. And in such a manner of being brought forth you shall be brought forth from the graves read either as the active takhrujūna ‘you shall come forth’ or the passive tukhrajūna ‘you shall be brought forth’.

hype_questions: What is the nature of human creation?
How does God revive lifeless matter?
Will we be revived after death like the earth?
propositions: God brings forth living beings from dead matter.
God gives life to the earth after its death.
You will be brought forth from your graves.

source_text:
Verse: One of His signs is that He created you from dust, then—behold!—you are human beings spreading over ˹the earth˺.

Tafsir: And of His signs exalted be He indicating His power is that He created you in other words your origin Adam of dust then lo! you are human beings of flesh and blood spreading across the earth.

hype_questions: What is the origin of humanity?
How did humans come to be on Earth?
What is a sign of God's power?
propositions: God created Adam from dust.
Humans are made of flesh and blood.
God's power is evident in creation.

source_text:
Verse: And one of His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves so that you may find comfort in them. And He has placed between you compassion and mercy. Surely in this are signs for people who reflect.

Tafsir: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates — Eve was created from Adam’s rib and the remainder of mankind from the reproductive fluids of men and women — that you might find peace by their side and become intimate with them and He ordained between you all affection and mercy. Surely in that mentioned there are signs for a people who reflect upon God’s handiwork exalted be He.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of marriage in Islam?
How does God create mates for humans?
What are some signs of God's compassion and mercy?
propositions: God created spouses from among themselves to find comfort.
Eve was created from Adam's rib.
The remainder of mankind was created from reproductive fluids of men and women.
God ordained affection and mercy between humans.
Humans can find peace by the side of their mates.

source_text:
Verse: And one of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and colours. Surely in this are signs for those of ˹sound˺ knowledge.

Tafsir: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the differences of your tongues that is your languages such as Arabic non-Arabic and so on and your colours such as white or black or otherwise even though all of you are originally the offspring of the same man and woman. Surely in that there are signs indications of His power exalted be He for all peoples this may be vocalised either as li’l-‘ālamīna or li’l-‘ālimīna so it means either rational creatures or people of knowledge respectively.

hype_questions: What is the significance of human diversity in the Quran?
How does the Quran explain the origin of different languages?
What does it mean to be a 'rational creature' according to Islamic theology?
propositions: The creation of the heavens and the earth is one of God's signs.
Human diversity in language and colour is a sign of God's power.
All humans are originally from the same man and woman, yet they have different languages and colours.

source_text:
Verse: And one of His signs is your sleep by night and by day ˹for rest˺ as well as your seeking His bounty ˹in both˺. Surely in this are signs for people who listen.

Tafsir: And of His signs is your sleep by night and day by His will as a repose for you and your seeking during the day of His bounty in other words your going about freely in order to seek a living is by His will. Surely in that there are signs for people who listen listening in a way so as to be prompted to reflect and take heed.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of sleep according to Islamic teachings?
How does seeking blessings from Allah relate to one's daily activities?
What is the significance of listening to and reflecting on divine signs?
propositions: Your sleep by night and day is a sign from Allah.
You seek rest in order to be refreshed for the next day.
Your seeking during the day is for His bounty, which includes finding a living.
Allah's will guides you in your daily activities.
Listening to divine signs prompts reflection and heedfulness.

source_text:
Verse: And one of His signs is that He shows you lightning, inspiring ˹you with˺ hope and fear. And He sends down rain from the sky, reviving the earth after its death. Surely in this are signs for people who understand.

Tafsir: And of His signs is His showing you lightning to arouse fear in the traveller of storms and hope in the one not travelling of the coming of the rain; and He sends down water from the heaven and with it He revives the earth after it has died that is after it has dried out so that it produces vegetation once again. Surely in that mentioned there are signs for people who understand a people who reflect.

hype_questions: What is the significance of lightning in inspiring fear and hope?
How does rain revive the earth after it has died?
What are some signs that people who understand can recognize in nature?
propositions: God shows you lightning to inspire fear in travelers of storms and hope in those not traveling.
God sends down water from heaven, reviving the earth after it has dried out so that it produces vegetation once again.
There are signs for people who understand in nature.

source_text:
Verse: And one of His signs is that the heavens and the earth persist by His command. Then when He calls you out of the earth just once, you will instantly come forth.

Tafsir: And of His signs is that the heaven and the earth remain standing by His command by His will without any supports; then when He calls you to come out of the earth when Isrāfīl blows the Horn for the raising from the graves to commence lo! you shall come forth from it alive. Thus your coming forth out of it by a call constitutes one of His many signs exalted be He.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the heavens and earth persisting by God's command?
How will we be resurrected when God calls us out of the earth?
What does it mean to come forth from the earth alive upon hearing the Horn?
propositions: The heavens and the earth remain standing by God's command.
When God calls you out of the earth, you will instantly come forth.
Isrāfīl blows the Horn for the raising from the graves to commence.
You shall come forth from it alive upon hearing the Horn.
Your coming forth out of it by a call constitutes one of God's many signs.

source_text:
Verse: And to Him belong all those in the heavens and the earth—all are subject to His Will.

Tafsir: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth as possessions creatures and servants. All are obedient to Him.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate authority in the universe?
Who or what has control over all existence?
What is the relationship between humans and their creator?
propositions: All beings in heaven and earth are possessions of God.
All creatures and servants are obedient to God.
God's will is supreme over all existence.

source_text:
Verse: And He is the One Who originates the creation then will resurrect it—which is even easier for Him. To Him belong the finest attributes in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And He it is Who initiates the creation of mankind then brings it back after their destruction and that is even easier for Him than the initiation — from the perspective of those addressed for whom to repeat something is easier than doing it for the first time — otherwise in God’s case exalted be He both are just as easy. His is the loftiest description in the heavens and the earth the most sublime attribute namely that ‘there is no god except God’. And He is the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His creation.

hype_questions: What is easier for God to do: creating something from nothing or bringing it back to life after destruction?
Why does God have the most sublime attribute, 'there is no god except God'?
How does God's wisdom manifest in His creation?
propositions: Allah originates and resurrects creation.
The repetition of something is easier for some than doing it for the first time.
God has the finest attributes in the heavens and the earth.
There is no god except God.
God is the Mighty in His kingdom.
God is the Wise in His creation.

source_text:
Verse: He sets forth for you an example ˹drawn˺ from your own lives: would you allow some of those ˹bondspeople˺ in your possession to be your equal partners in whatever ˹wealth˺ We have provided you, keeping them in mind as you are mindful of your peers? This is how We make the signs clear for people who understand.

Tafsir: He has struck He has coined for you O idolaters a similitude that is actually drawn from yourselves and it is as follows do you have among those whom your right hands own that is to say among your servants any partners of yourselves who may share in what We have provided for you of property and so on so that you and they are equal therein fearing them as you fear your own folk just as you fear those free men like you? the interrogative is meant as a negation in other words ‘your servants are not partners of yours in what you own so how can you make some of God’s servants partners of His. So We detail the signs so We explain them in such detail for people who understand a people who reflect.

hype_questions: Can humans be equal partners with their servants in wealth and property?
Do humans fear their own people as much as they fear God's servants?
Why do humans make some of God's servants partners of His when it is not allowed?
propositions: Some people among your possessions are like equals to you in terms of wealth.
You should be mindful of your peers and treat them with fairness.
God does not allow humans to share their wealth with their servants as partners.

source_text:
Verse: In fact, the wrongdoers merely follow their desires with no knowledge. Who then can guide those Allah has left to stray? They will have no helpers.

Tafsir: Nay but those who do evil through idolatry follow their own desires without any knowledge. So who will guide he whom God has led astray? that is to say he will have none to guide him. And they have no helpers no protectors against God’s chastisement.

hype_questions: Can anyone guide someone who Allah has left to stray?
What happens to those who follow their desires without knowledge?
Who will help someone in need of guidance?
propositions: Those who do evil through idolatry follow their own desires without any knowledge.
God has led astray he whom God has left astray, and he will have none to guide him.
They have no helpers or protectors against God's chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: So be steadfast in faith in all uprightness ˹O Prophet˺—the natural Way of Allah which He has instilled in ˹all˺ people. Let there be no change in this creation of Allah. That is the Straight Way, but most people do not know.

Tafsir: So set your purpose O Muhammad (s) for religion as a hanīf as one inclining to it — in other words devote your religion you and whoever follows you purely to God — a nature given by God upon which He originated mankind and this nature is His religion in other words adhere to it. There is no changing God’s creation His religion that is to say do not change it by becoming idolaters. That is the upright religion the belief in God’s Oneness but most people namely the Meccan disbelievers do not know anything of God’s Oneness —

hype_questions: What is the natural way of Allah that He has instilled in all people?
How should one devote their religion to God?
What is the upright religion that believes in God's Oneness?
propositions: Be steadfast in faith in all uprightness.
Set your purpose O Muhammad (s) for religion as a hanīf, devoted to God and His nature.
There is no changing God’s creation His religion.
The belief in God’s Oneness is the upright religion.
Most people do not know anything of God’s Oneness.

source_text:
Verse: ˹O believers!˺ Always turn to Him ˹in repentance˺, be mindful of Him, and establish prayers. And do not be polytheists—

Tafsir: turning referring to Him exalted be He concerning what He has commanded and what He has forbidden munībīna ‘turning’ is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb aqim ‘set up’ in other words addressing the third plural person aqīmū ‘set up’ and fear Him and establish prayer and do not be among the idolaters

hype_questions: What is the significance of turning to Allah in repentance?
How does establishing prayers demonstrate one's fear of Allah?
What are the consequences of being among the idolaters?
propositions: Believers should always turn to Allah in repentance.
Establishing prayers demonstrates a person's fear of Allah.
Being an idolater is a grave consequence.

source_text:
Verse: ˹like˺ those who have divided their faith and split into sects, each rejoicing in what they have.

Tafsir: of those mina’lladhīna is a substitution for al-mushrikīna ‘idolaters’ using the same operator of the oblique min who have divided up their religion by being at variance over what they worship and have become dissenting factions sects divided over this matter each party among them rejoicing delighting in what they have a variant reading for farraqū is fāraqū in other words ‘of those who have parted with the religion to which they have been commanded’.

hype_questions: What happens when Muslims divide into sects?
How do idolaters react to being called out for their disbelief?
Can a person truly be happy with a faith they have abandoned?
propositions: Those who divided their faith and split into sects rejoice in what they have.
The term 'idolater' refers to those who worship other than Allah.
When Muslims disagree over their faith, they become dissenting factions.

source_text:
Verse: When people are touched with hardship, they cry out to their Lord, turning to Him ˹alone˺. But as soon as He gives them a taste of His mercy, a group of them associates ˹others˺ with their Lord ˹in worship˺,

Tafsir: And when some distress some hardship befalls people that is people such as the Meccan disbelievers they call on their Lord turning returning in penitence to Him alone. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him by way of rain lo! a party of them ascribe partners to their Lord.

hype_questions: What happens when people are touched with hardship?
How do people respond to Allah's mercy?
Why do some people associate partners with their Lord?
propositions: When people are touched with hardship, they cry out to their Lord.
Allah gives His servants a taste of His mercy after they turn to Him alone.
Some people ascribe partners to their Lord when Allah lets them taste mercy from Him.

source_text:
Verse: becoming ungrateful for whatever ˹favours˺ We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for soon you will know.

Tafsir: Let them be ungrateful for what We have given them this is an imperative meant as a threat. ‘So take your enjoyment. Soon you will know’ the consequences of your enjoyment there is a shift away from the third person address to the second.

hype_questions: What happens when we become ungrateful for the blessings we receive?
How will our actions affect us in the end?
What consequences can we expect if we indulge in worldly pleasures?
propositions: We have given them favours.
They should be ungrateful for what We have given them.
Enjoy yourselves, for soon you will know.

source_text:
Verse: Or have We sent down to them an authority which attests to what they associate ˹with Him˺?

Tafsir: Or am the hamza here is meant for denial have We revealed any warrant any argument or scripture to them which might speak a token speech of what they associate with Him? in other words commanding them to associate others with God? No!

hype_questions: Does the Quran confirm or deny the idea that humans can associate partners with Allah?
Can the Quran provide evidence for or against the concept of shirk (associating partners with Allah)?
Is the Quran's authority sufficient to refute the notion of polytheism?
propositions: The Quran sent down an authority that attests to what they associate with God.
No warrant, argument, or scripture was revealed to them which might speak a token speech of what they associate with Him.
They should not associate others with God.

source_text:
Verse: If We give people a taste of mercy, they become prideful ˹because˺ of it. But if they are afflicted with an evil for what their hands have done, they instantly fall into despair.

Tafsir: And when We let people that is people such as the disbelievers of Mecca and others taste some mercy some grace they exult in it an exultation of arrogance. But if some evil some hardship befalls them for what their own hands have sent ahead behold! they despair of mercy. It is in the nature of a believer to give thanks in times of grace and to hope for mercy from his Lord in times of hardship.

hype_questions: What happens when people are given mercy?
How do people react to hardship after experiencing mercy?
Can believers find hope in times of hardship?
propositions: If people are given mercy, they become prideful.
When people experience hardship for their own actions, they despair of mercy.
Believers give thanks in times of grace and hope for mercy from their Lord in times of hardship.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not seen that Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills? Surely in this are signs for people who believe.

Tafsir: Have they not seen have they not realised that God extends He makes abundant His provision to whomever He will as a test and straitens? and He restricts it for whomever He will as a trial? Surely in that there are signs for people who believe in them.

hype_questions: Does God provide abundance or scarcity to His creation?
What is the purpose of God's provision in the lives of believers?
How does God's providence serve as a test for those who believe?
propositions: Allah gives abundant provisions to whoever He wills.
God extends His provision to whomever He wills as a test and straitens it for whomever He wills as a trial.
There are signs for people who believe in the abundance of God's provision.

source_text:
Verse: So give your close relatives their due, as well as the poor and the ˹needy˺ traveller. That is best for those who seek the pleasure of Allah, and it is they who will be successful.

Tafsir: And give the relative what is his due in the way of dutifulness and kindness and the needy and the wayfarer the traveller give voluntary alms — the Prophet’s community must emulate him in this respect. That is better for those who desire God’s Countenance who desire His reward in exchange for what they do; those they are the successful the winners.

hype_questions: What is the best way to show kindness and dutifulness to those in need?
How can I emulate the Prophet's community in giving voluntary alms?
What is the reward for showing kindness and generosity to others?
propositions: Give your close relatives their due, as well as the poor and the traveller.
The Prophet’s community must emulate him in this respect.
Those who desire God’s Countenance are the successful ones.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever loans you give, ˹only˺ seeking interest at the expense of people’s wealth will not increase with Allah. But whatever charity you give, ˹only˺ seeking the pleasure of Allah—it is they whose reward will be multiplied.

Tafsir: And what you give in usury — such as when something is given as a gift or a present for the purpose of demanding more in return; it the practice of usury ribā is referred to by the same noun denoting that illicit ‘extra’ ziyāda requested in the financial transaction — that it may increase the wealth of the people giving it does not increase with God — there is no reward in it for those who give it. But what you give as alms zakāt as voluntary alms sadaqa seeking thereby God’s Countenance such of you who do so — they are the receivers of manifold increase in their reward for what they sought there is here a shift of address away from the second person.

hype_questions: What happens to wealth when it's given in usury?
How does giving charity as zakat affect one's reward?
Can seeking Allah's pleasure increase one's reward?
propositions: Whatever loans you give, only seeking interest at the expense of people’s wealth will not increase with Allah.
Whatever charity you give, only seeking the pleasure of Allah—it is they whose reward will be multiplied.
There is no reward in giving something as usury that may increase the wealth of the people giving it.

source_text:
Verse: It is Allah Who created you, then gives you provisions, then will cause you to die, and then will bring you back to life. Can any of your associate-gods do any of this? Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate with Him ˹in worship˺!

Tafsir: God is the One Who created you then provided for you then makes you die then gives you life is there anyone among your associates of those whom you have associated with God who does anything of the kind? No! Glory be to Him and exalted be He above what they associate with Him.

hype_questions: Can any of your associate-gods bring you back to life after death?
Do any of your associate-gods provide for you?
Can any of your associate-gods cause you to die?
propositions: Allah created you.
Allah provides for you.
Allah causes you to die.
Allah gives you life after death.
No one among your associates can do anything of the kind.

source_text:
Verse: Corruption has spread on land and sea as a result of what people’s hands have done, so that Allah may cause them to taste ˹the consequences of˺ some of their deeds and perhaps they might return ˹to the Right Path˺.

Tafsir: Corruption has appeared on land in the wastelands because of the rain being withheld and the vegetation diminishing and on sea in lands near rivers because of their waters diminishing because of what people’s hands have perpetrated of acts of disobedience that He may make them taste li-yudhīqahum; or may be read li-nudhīqahum ‘that We may make them taste’ something of what they have done that is the punishment for it that perhaps they may repent.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of human actions?
How can people return to the Right Path?
What punishment will Allah inflict on those who disobey Him?
propositions: Corruption has spread on land and sea as a result of what people's hands have done.
Allah may cause them to taste some of their deeds.
Perhaps they might return to the Right Path.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Travel throughout the land and see what was the end of those ˹destroyed˺ before ˹you˺—most of them were polytheists.”

Tafsir: Say to the Meccan disbelievers ‘Travel in the land and behold how was the consequence for those who were before; most of them were idolaters’ and so they were destroyed because of their idolatry and their dwellings and habitations lie desolate in ruin.

hype_questions: What was the end of those destroyed cities?
How did idolatry affect the people of old?
Why do abandoned dwellings remain desolate?
propositions: Most of those who were destroyed before you were polytheists.
Their dwellings and habitations lie in ruin due to their idolatry.

source_text:
Verse: So be steadfast in the Upright Faith ˹O Prophet˺, before the coming of a Day from Allah that cannot be averted. On that Day the people will be divided:

Tafsir: So set your purpose for the upright religion the religion of Islam before there comes the inevitable day from God namely the Day of Resurrection. On that day they shall be sundered yassadda‘ūna the original tā’ yatasadda‘ūna has been assimilated with the sād that is they will be split into separate groups after the Reckoning destined for Paradise or the Fire.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of humanity?
How will people be divided on the Day of Resurrection?
What are the consequences of not following the Upright Faith?
propositions: The Prophet was commanded to uphold the Upright Faith.
The Day of Resurrection is inevitable and will bring about a division among people.
Those who follow the Upright Faith will be destined for Paradise, while those who do not will face the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: those who disbelieved will bear ˹the burden of˺ their own disbelief; and those who did good will have prepared for themselves ˹eternal homes˺,

Tafsir: Whoever disbelieves the consequence of his disbelief shall upon him that is the evil consequences of his disbelief which will be his being punished in the Fire and those who act righteously they will be paving the way for the salvation of their own souls preparing their places in Paradise

hype_questions: What happens to those who disbelieve?
How do righteous individuals prepare for their afterlife?
What is the consequence of disbelief?
propositions: Those who disbelieve will bear the burden of their own disbelief.
Those who act righteously are paving the way for the salvation of their souls.
The consequence of disbelief is punishment in the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: so that He may ˹generously˺ reward those who believe and do good, out of His grace. He truly does not like the disbelievers.

Tafsir: that He may requite li-yajziya is semantically connected to yassadda‘ūna ‘they shall be sundered’ those who believe and perform righteous deeds out of His bounty that He may reward them. Indeed He does not like the disbelievers in other words He will punish them.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe and do good?
How does Allah punish disbelievers?
What is the connection between believing in Allah and performing righteous deeds?
propositions: Allah rewards those who believe and do good out of His grace.
Believing in Allah and performing righteous deeds are connected to receiving a reward from Him.
Disbelievers will be punished by Allah.

source_text:
Verse: And one of His signs is that He sends the winds, ushering in good news ˹of rain˺ so that He may give you a taste of His mercy, and that ships may sail by His command, and that you may seek His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.

Tafsir: And of His signs exalted be He is that He unleashes the winds as bearers of good tidings meaning so that they may bring you good tidings of rain and that He may let you taste thereby of His mercy namely in the way of rain and fertile soil and that the ships may run thereby by His command by His will and that you may seek that you may request of His bounty provision by way of commerce at sea and that perhaps you might then give thanks for these graces O people of Mecca and so affirm His Oneness.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the winds in Islam?
How does the Quran describe the mercy of Allah?
Why is gratitude important according to Islamic teachings?
propositions: Allah sends the winds as bearers of good tidings.
The winds bring good news of rain.
Allah lets you taste His mercy through rain and fertile soil.
Ships sail by Allah's command.
You should seek Allah's bounty in commerce at sea.
Perhaps you will give thanks for these graces.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We sent before you ˹O Prophet˺ messengers, each to their own people, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We inflicted punishment upon those who persisted in wickedness. For it is Our duty to help the believers.

Tafsir: And verily We sent before you messengers to their people and they brought them clear signs plain proofs of their sincerity concerning their Message to them but they denied them. Then We took vengeance upon those who were guilty We destroyed those who denied them and it was ever incumbent upon Us to give victory to the believers over the disbelievers by destroying these and delivering the believers.

hype_questions: What is the role of messengers in Islam?
How do believers receive divine guidance?
What happens to those who deny the message of God?
propositions: We sent messengers before you to their people with clear proofs.
Those who persisted in wickedness were punished by Us.
It is Our duty to help the believers.
We destroyed those who denied the messengers and gave victory to the believers.

source_text:
Verse: It is Allah Who sends the winds, which then stir up ˹vapour, forming˺ clouds, which He then spreads out in the sky or piles up into masses as He wills, from which you see rain come forth. Then as soon as He causes it to fall on whoever He wills of His servants, they rejoice,

Tafsir: God is the One Who unleashes the winds which then raise stir up clouds and He then spreads them across the heaven as He will in small or large quantities and He forms them into fragments read kisafan or kisfan ‘scattered pieces’ then you see the rain issuing out of them that is out of the midst of them. Then when He drops it the rain upon whomever of His servants He will lo! they rejoice they are happy because of the rain.

hype_questions: What is the role of Allah in creating weather patterns?
How does Allah control the amount of rain that falls on His servants?
Why do Allah's servants rejoice when they receive rain?
propositions: Allah sends the winds.
The winds stir up clouds which Allah spreads out in the sky or piles up into masses as He wills.
Rain comes forth from the clouds that Allah forms.
Allah causes rain to fall on whomever He wills of His servants.
His servants rejoice when they receive rain.

source_text:
Verse: although they had utterly lost hope just before it was sent down to them.

Tafsir: Though indeed before it was sent down upon them before that min qablihi is repeated for emphasis they had been despondent despairing of its sending down.

hype_questions: What would happen to those who lost hope before the revelation was sent down?
How did people feel when they heard that the verse was being sent down?
What does it mean for someone to be 'despondent' and 'despairing'?
propositions: They had utterly lost hope just before it was sent down to them.
Before the revelation was sent down, people were despondent and despairing of its sending down.

source_text:
Verse: See then the impact of Allah’s mercy: how He gives life to the earth after its death! Surely That ˹same God˺ can raise the dead. For He is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: So behold the effects a variant reading has singular athar ‘the effect’ of God's mercy that is His grace in giving them rain how He revives the earth after it has died after it has dried out so that it produces vegetation again. Surely He is the Reviver of the dead and He has power over all things.

hype_questions: Can Allah revive the earth after it has died?
Does Allah have power over all things?
What is the effect of Allah's mercy on the earth?
propositions: Allah gives life to the earth after its death.
Allah can raise the dead.
Allah revives the earth after it has died and produces vegetation again.

source_text:
Verse: Then if We send a ˹harsh˺ wind which they see withering ˹their˺ crops, they will definitely deny ˹old favours˺ right after.

Tafsir: But if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths We unleash a different wind that damages vegetation and they see it turn yellow they would begin la-zallū is the response to the conditional oath after that that is after its turning yellow to disbelieve to deny the grace of having been given rain.

hype_questions: What happens when a harsh wind damages crops?
How do people respond to being denied blessings?
Can conditional oaths be trusted?
propositions: If a harsh wind damages crops, they will deny old favours.
We unleash a different wind that damages vegetation and it turns yellow.
The response to the conditional oath is to disbelieve after the turning yellow.

source_text:
Verse: So you ˹O Prophet˺ certainly cannot make the dead hear ˹the truth˺. Nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs and walk away.

Tafsir: And so you cannot make the dead hear nor can you make the deaf hear the call when read al-du‘ā’a idhā pronouncing both hamzas or by not pronouncing the second one that comes between it and the yā’ they go away with their backs turned.

hype_questions: Can a prophet make the dead hear?
Can a prophet make the deaf hear?
propositions: You cannot make the dead hear.
You cannot make the deaf hear.

source_text:
Verse: Nor can you lead the blind out of their misguidance. You can make none hear ˹the truth˺ except those who believe in Our revelations, ˹fully˺ submitting ˹to Allah˺.

Tafsir: Nor can you guide the blind out of their error. You can only make hear in a way so as to understand and accept those who believe in Our signs in the Qur’ān and have thus submitted sincere in their affirmation of God’s Oneness.

hype_questions: Can anyone be guided to the truth if they don't believe in God's revelations?
What is the condition for someone to truly understand and accept the message of God?
How can one ensure their affirmation of God's Oneness is sincere?

source_text:

He creates what He will of weakness and strength youth and grey hairs and He is the Knower of how to manage His creatures the Omnipotent.

Allah developed human weakness into strength during youth.

Allah creates whatever He wills, including the cycles of life and death.

God exalted be He says That is how they use to be deceived how they used to be turned away from the truth — the Resurrection — similar to the way in which they have now been turned away from the real truth about how long they had remained.

source_text:
Verse: But those gifted with knowledge and faith will say ˹to them˺, “You did actually stay—as destined by Allah—until the Day of Resurrection. So here is the Day of Resurrection ˹which you denied˺! But you did not know ˹it was true˺.”
