source_text:
Verse: We have certainly set forth every ˹kind of˺ lesson for people in this Quran. And no matter what sign you bring to them ˹O Prophet˺, the disbelievers will definitely say ˹to the believers˺, “You are only a people of falsehood.”

Tafsir: And verily We have struck We have coined for mankind in this Qur’ān every kind of similitude as a way of cautioning them. And if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths you O Muhammad (s) were to bring them a miraculous sign such as the staff or the hand in the case of Moses those who disbelieve from among them will certainly say la-yaqūlanna the indicative nūn has been omitted because of the other nūn coming after it and likewise the wāw replaced by the damma in lu because of two unvocalised consonants coming together and it indicates the plural person ‘You — in other words Muhammad (s) and his Companions — are nothing but followers of falsehood’.

If Muhammad (s) were to bring a miraculous sign, those who disbelieve will say he is only a people of falsehood.
The staff or the hand of Moses are examples of miraculous signs that can be used to caution mankind.

Verse: But there are some who employ theatrics, only to lead others away from Allah’s Way—without any knowledge—and to make a mockery of it. They will suffer a humiliating punishment.

Tafsir: And among people there is he who purchases idle talk in other words that part of it which diverts people from its true significance that he may lead people astray read li-yadilla; or li-yudilla from the way of God the religion of Islam without knowledge and take it read subjunctive wa-yattakhidhahā as a supplement to yudilla ‘that he may lead astray’; or indicative wa-yattakhidhuhā as a supplement to yashtarī ‘who buys’ in mockery as something to be mocked. For such there will be a humiliating chastisement one of abasement.

topics: Leading people astray from Allah's Way

source_text:
Verse: Whenever Our revelations are recited to them, they turn away in arrogance as if they did not hear them, as if there is deafness in their ears. So give them good news ˹O Prophet˺ of a painful punishment.

Tafsir: And when Our signs in other words in the Qur’ān are recited to such a one he turns away disdainfully as though he never heard them as though there were a deafness in his ears both comparisons constitute two circumstantial qualifiers referring to the subject of the verb wallā ‘turns away’; or it is that the second comparison is an explication of the first. So give him tidings of inform him of a painful chastisement. The use of the expression ‘good tidings’ meant derisively against such a person — this was al-Nadr b. al-Hārith. He used to visit al-Hīra for commerce and purchase books containing the stories of the non-Arab peoples and then recount these to the people of Mecca. He would say ‘Muhammad recounts to you the stories of ‘Ād and Thamūd whereas I relate to you the stories of the Persians and the Byzantines!’ They would thus go to enjoy his stories and neglect to listen to the Qur’ān.

source_text:
Verse: This is Allah’s creation. Now show Me what those ˹gods˺ other than Him have created. In fact, the wrongdoers are clearly astray.

Tafsir: This is God’s creation in other words what is created by Him. Now show me inform me O people of Mecca what those you worship besides Him those other than Him have created namely your gods so that you have associated them with Him exalted be He mā is an interrogative of denial and a subject; dhā has the significance of alladhī and what follows it of the relative clause is the predicate of the subject mā; arūnī glosses ‘the action’ and what follows it stands in place of two direct objects. Nay bal is for transition but the evildoers are in manifest error error that is evident because of their ascribing partners to God and you are like them.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We blessed Luqman with wisdom, ˹saying˺, “Be grateful to Allah, for whoever is grateful, it is only for their own good. And whoever is ungrateful, then surely Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.”

Tafsir: And verily We gave Luqmān wisdom comprising knowledge religiousness and right-mindedness in speech; his many wisdoms are well-known. He used to give legal opinions in matters of religion before David was summoned to prophethood but lived on into the latter’s summoning. He then took to acquiring knowledge from him David and refrained from giving any more legal opinions explaining this thus ‘Should I not be content if someone like the prophet David has spared me the trouble?’ He was once asked ‘What is the worst kind of person?’ He said ‘The one who does not care that people should see him doing evil’. In other words We gave him wisdom and We said to him ‘Give thanks to God for the wisdom that He has given you. Whoever gives thanks only for his own sake because the reward for his gratitude shall be his and whoever is ungrateful for a grace then surely God is Independent without need of His creation Praised’ in what He does.

God is Independent without need of His creation.

source_text:
Verse: But if they pressure you to associate with Me what you have no knowledge of, do not obey them. Still keep their company in this world courteously, and follow the way of those who turn to Me ˹in devotion˺. Then to Me you will ˹all˺ return, and then I will inform you of what you used to do.

And keep them company in this world honourably in other words with decency dutifulness and kindness — and follow the way of him who returns to Me in penitence with acts of obedience. then We will drive them in the Hereafter to a harsh chastisement namely the chastisement of the Fire from which they will find no escape.

Who is the creator of the universe?
Is there one God?
propositions: The heavens and the earth were created by Allah.
Most people do not know who created the heavens and the earth.
Praise be to Allah for affirming His Oneness.

source_text:
Verse: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Allah is truly the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

Tafsir: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth as possessions creatures and servants and so none other than Him deserves to be worshipped in them. Indeed God He is the Independent without need of His creatures the Praised in His actions.

hype_questions: What belongs to God?
Who deserves worship?
Is God independent?
propositions: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.
None other than Allah deserves to be worshipped in them.
God is the Independent without need of His creatures.

source_text:
Verse: If all the trees on earth were pens and the ocean ˹were ink˺, refilled by seven other oceans, the Words of Allah would not be exhausted. Surely Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And if all the trees on earth were pens and the sea wa’l-bahru is a supplement to mā the subject of anna replenished with seven more seas were ink the Words of God would not be spent those words expressing all the things He knows written in those pens with that amount of ink or with even more ink than that would not be spent for His knowledge exalted be He is infinite. Truly God is Mighty nothing being beyond Him Wise from Whose knowledge and wisdom nothing escapes.

hype_questions: Can the words of God ever be exhausted?
Is God's knowledge infinite?
Does nothing escape from God's wisdom?
propositions: If all the trees on earth were pens and the ocean were ink, the Words of Allah would not be exhausted.
The Words of God would not be spent even if replenished with seven more seas.
God's knowledge is infinite and nothing escapes from His wisdom.

source_text:
Verse: The creation and resurrection of you ˹all˺ is as simple ˹for Him˺ as that of a single soul. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

Tafsir: Your creation and your resurrection are only as that of a single soul in terms of creation and resurrection because it is the result of the words kun fa-yakūn ‘“Be!” and it is!’ Truly God is Hearer hearing everything that may be heard Seer seeing everything that may be seen nothing able to distract Him from anything else.

hype_questions: Does Allah's creation and resurrection follow a similar pattern to human creation and resurrection?
Can Allah hear and see everything that is happening in the world?
Is Allah able to be distracted from anything else?
propositions: Allah created and resurrected humanity through the words 'kun fa-yakūn' (Be!) and 'itī' (is!).
Allah is All-Hearing, meaning He hears everything that may be heard.
Allah is All-Seeing, meaning He sees everything that may be seen.
Nothing can distract Allah from His creation and resurrection.
Allah's power and ability are not limited to human comprehension.

source_text:
Verse: Do you not see that Allah causes the night to merge into the day and the day into the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each orbiting for an appointed term, and that Allah is All-Aware of what you do?

Tafsir: Have you not seen have you not realised O you being addressed that God makes the night pass into the day and makes the day pass into the night such that the increase of the one is relative to the decrease of the other and He has disposed the sun and the moon each of the two running in its course to an appointed term namely to the Day of Resurrection and that God is Aware of what you do?

hype_questions: Does Allah control the passage of time?
Is the sun's orbit predetermined?
Can God see our actions?
propositions: Allah causes the night to merge into the day.
The day merges into the night.
The increase of one is relative to the decrease of the other.
Allah has subjected the sun and the moon, each orbiting for an appointed term.
This appointed term is until the Day of Resurrection.
God is Aware of what you do.

source_text:
Verse: That is because Allah ˹alone˺ is the Truth and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and ˹because˺ Allah ˹alone˺ is the Most High, All-Great.

Tafsir: That which is mentioned is so because God He is the Truth the established truth and whatever they call on read yad‘ūna; or tad‘ūna ‘you call on’ whatever they worship besides Him is evanescent falsehood and because God is the High Exalted above His creation by virtue of His subjugation of them the Great the Mighty.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah?
Is Allah the only one worthy of worship?
How does Allah's greatness relate to His creation?
propositions: Allah is the Truth.
Whatever they call on besides Allah is falsehood.
God is the High Exalted above His creation by virtue of His subjugation of them.

source_text:
Verse: Do you not see that the ships sail ˹smoothly˺ through the sea by the grace of Allah so that He may show you some of His signs? Surely in this are signs for whoever is steadfast, grateful.

Tafsir: Have you not seen that the ships run upon the sea by the grace of God that He may show you O you who are being addressed in this statement some of His signs? Surely in that there are signs lessons for every servant who is steadfast in abstaining from acts of disobedience to God grateful for His grace.

hype_questions: Does Allah show us signs through the movement of ships on the sea?
What are the lessons for a servant who is steadfast and grateful to God?
How does God's grace manifest in our lives?
propositions: The ships sail smoothly through the sea by the grace of Allah.
Allah shows us signs through the movement of ships on the sea.
A servant who is steadfast and grateful to God receives lessons from Allah.

source_text:
Verse: And as soon as they are overwhelmed by waves like mountains, they cry out to Allah ˹alone˺ in sincere devotion. But when He delivers them ˹safely˺ to shore, only some become relatively grateful. And none rejects Our signs except whoever is deceitful, ungrateful.

Tafsir: And if waves cover them that is if these rise above the disbelievers like awnings like mountains that act as awnings over those below them they call on God sincere before Him in their faith that is in their supplication that He may deliver them in other words they do not call on any other god with Him; but when He delivers them to land some of them compromise middling between belief and disbelief while others persist in their disbelief. And none denies Our signs an example of which is Our delivering them from such treacherous waves except every perfidious ingrate ungrateful for God’s graces exalted be He.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah delivers believers from difficult situations?
How do some people respond to Allah's blessings?
Why do some individuals reject Allah's signs?
propositions: Believers cry out to Allah in sincere devotion when overwhelmed by waves.
Some believers become relatively grateful after being delivered safely to shore.
None rejects Allah's signs except those who are deceitful and ungrateful.

source_text:
Verse: O humanity! Be mindful of your Lord, and beware of a Day when no parent will be of any benefit to their child, nor will a child be of any benefit to their parent. Surely Allah’s promise is true. So do not let the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Chief Deceiver deceive you about Allah.

Tafsir: O people namely such as the people of Mecca fear your Lord and fear a day when no parent shall avail a child thereon in any way; and no child thereon shall avail its parent in any way. Surely God’s promise of resurrection is true. So do not let the life of this world deceive you and divert you from Islam and do not let the Deceiver Satan deceive you concerning God because of His forbearance and granting people respite.

hype_questions: What happens to a child after their parent passes away?
Can a person's faith be swayed by the temptations of Satan?
Is it possible for humans to achieve spiritual enlightenment through following Islam?
propositions: Allah’s promise of resurrection is true.
The life of this world cannot deceive you into abandoning your faith in Allah.
Satan will not deceive you about Allah due to His forbearance and granting people respite.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ has the knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain, No soul knows what it will earn for tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.

Tafsir: Lo! God with Him lies knowledge of the Hour when it will come to pass; and He sends down read yunzilu or yunazzilu the rain at times which only He knows; and He knows what is in the wombs whether it is a male or a female; and not one of the three things is known by anyone other than God exalted be He. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow of good or evil but God exalted be He knows this; and no soul knows in what land it will die but God exalted be He knows this. Truly God is Knower of all things Aware of the inward and outward aspects thereof. Al-Bukhārī reported by way of an isnād from ‘Abd Allāh Ibn ‘Umar the following hadīth ‘The Keys of the Unseen are five Lo! God with Him lies knowledge of the Hour … to the end of the sūra’ above.

hype_questions: What is the knowledge of the Hour?
How does Allah send down rain?
Can humans know what they will earn tomorrow?
propositions: Allah has knowledge of the Hour.
God sends down rain at times which only He knows.
No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, but God knows this.
No soul knows in what land it will die, but God knows this.
God is Knower of all things Aware of the inward and outward aspects thereof.

source_text:
Verse: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm.

Tafsir: Alif lām mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

hype_questions: Does God have a specific meaning in mind when using the alphabet?
Can humans truly understand God's intentions?
What does it mean for God to 'know best'?
propositions: God knows what He means by these letters.
These letters are part of God's language.
God has a specific meaning in mind when using the alphabet.

source_text:
Verse: The revelation of this Book is—beyond doubt—from the Lord of all worlds.

Tafsir: The revelation of the Book the Qur’ān tanzīlu’l-kitābi the subject whereof there is no doubt lā rayba fīh the first predicate from the Lord of the Worlds min rabbi’l-‘ālamīna the second predicate.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Qur'ān?
Who is the Lord of all worlds?
What is the first predicate in the tanzīlu of the Book?
propositions: The revelation of the Qur'ān is beyond doubt.
The subject of the Qur'ān has no doubt.
The first predicate from the Lord of all worlds is the second predicate.

source_text:
Verse: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it!”? No! It is the truth from your Lord in order for you to warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, so they may be ˹rightly˺ guided.

Tafsir: Or do they say ‘He Muhammad (s) has invented it’? Nay but it is the truth from your Lord that you may warn thereby a people to whom no warner came before you mā is for negation that perhaps they may find right guidance by your warning.

hype_questions: Does the Quran claim to be from God?
Is the Quran a reliable source of guidance for humanity?
Can human beings truly benefit from the warnings and teachings in the Quran?
propositions: The Quran is not fabricated.
God is the source of truth.
Warning people with the Quran can guide them to righteousness.

source_text:
Verse: It is Allah Who has created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him. Will you not then be mindful?

Tafsir: God is He Who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days the first of which was Sunday and the last of which was Friday then He presided upon the Throne al-‘arsh in the classical Arabic idiom denotes the seat of a king a presiding worthy of Him. You do not have O disbelievers of Mecca besides Him in other words other than Him any protector min waliyyin is the subject of the particle mā with the min added extra in other words any helper or intercessor to ward off His chastisement from you. Will you not then remember? this and become believers.

hype_questions: Will you not then be mindful of Allah's sovereignty?
Can anyone protect you from Allah's chastisement besides Him?
Will you not then remember and become believers?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days.
The first day was Sunday, and the last day was Friday.
You do not have a protector or intercessor besides Allah.
Al-‘arsh denotes the seat of a king worthy of Allah's presence.
You should be mindful of Allah's sovereignty.
Remembering Allah is essential to becoming believers.

source_text:
Verse: He conducts every affair from the heavens to the earth, then it all ascends to Him on a Day whose length is a thousand years by your counting.

Tafsir: He directs the command from the heaven to the earth for the duration of this world then it ascends then the command and the direction thereof returns to Him in a day whose measure is a thousand years by your reckoning in this world. In sūrat sa’ala An asker asked the measure is said to be ‘fifty thousand years’ Q. 704 — and this day is the Day of Resurrection reckoned so because of the severity of its terrors for the disbeliever. As for the believer however for him it will be easier than performing any one of his obligatory prayers in this world — as is stated in hadīth.

hype_questions: What is the duration of a thousand years in this world?
How does the Day of Resurrection differ for believers and disbelievers?
What is the measure of the Day of Resurrection according to Q. 704?
propositions: He conducts every affair from the heavens to the earth.
The command from the heaven to the earth lasts for this world's duration.
The command and direction return to Him in a day whose measure is a thousand years by your reckoning.
This day is the Day of Resurrection, reckoned due to its severity.
For believers, it will be easier than performing any one of their obligatory prayers in this world.

source_text:
Verse: That is the Knower of the seen and unseen—the Almighty, Most Merciful,

Tafsir: That Creator and Director is the Knower of the Unseen and the visible that is what is hidden from creatures and what is present before them the Mighty the Invincible in His kingdom the Merciful to those who are obedient to Him

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's knowledge?
How does Allah relate to His creation?
What are the characteristics of Allah's mercy?
propositions: Allah is the Knower of the seen and unseen.
Allah is the Creator and Director of the universe.
The unseen refers to that which is hidden from creatures, while the visible refers to what is present before them.
Allah is Mighty and Invincible in His kingdom.
Allah is Merciful to those who are obedient to Him.

source_text:
Verse: Who has perfected everything He created. And He originated the creation of humankind from clay.

Tafsir: Who perfected everything that He created read khalaqahu as a past tense functioning as an adjectival qualification of what He perfected; or khalqahu ‘its creation’ as an inclusive substitution for kulla shay’in ‘everything’. And He began the creation of man Adam from clay

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's perfection?
How did God create humanity?
What is the significance of Adam in Islamic theology?
propositions: God perfected everything He created.
God originated the creation of humankind from clay.
Adam was created from clay.

source_text:
Verse: Then He made his descendants from an extract of a humble fluid,

Tafsir: then He made his progeny his offspring from an extract a blood clot of a base delicate fluid namely the sperm-drop;

hype_questions: Does Allah create life from a humble fluid?
What is the origin of human offspring?
How does Allah create life?
propositions: Allah created his descendants from an extract of a humble fluid.
His progeny are his offspring from an extract of a blood clot of a base delicate fluid, namely the sperm-drop.

source_text:
Verse: then He fashioned them and had a spirit of His Own ˹creation˺ breathed into them. And He gave you hearing, sight, and intellect. ˹Yet˺ you hardly give any thanks.

Tafsir: then He proportioned him that is to say He created Adam and breathed into him of His spirit in other words He made him a living sensory being after having been an inanimate thing. And He made for you in other words for you his descendants hearing meaning ears and sight and hearts. Little thanks do you give mā here is extra emphasising the ‘littleness’ of the thanks.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Adam's creation in Islamic theology?
How does the Quran describe the proportioning of humans?
Why is gratitude emphasized in the context of human creation?
propositions: God created Adam and breathed His spirit into him.
He gave humans hearing, sight, and intellect.
Humans give little thanks for their blessings.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Still˺ they ask ˹mockingly˺, “When we are disintegrated into the earth, will we really be raised as a new creation?” In fact, they are in denial of the meeting with their Lord.

Tafsir: And they namely the deniers of resurrection say ‘When we are lost beneath the earth when we have gone thereunder having become dust mixed with its dust shall we be indeed created anew?’ an interrogative of denial; read a-innā by pronouncing both hamzas or by not pronouncing the second one and inserting an alif between them either way in both places. God exalted be He says Nay but they disbelieve in the encounter with their Lord through resurrection.

hype_questions: Will we be raised as a new creation after being disintegrated into the earth?
propositions: They ask when they will be created anew.
God says Nay, but they disbelieve in the encounter with their Lord through resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Your soul will be taken by the Angel of Death, who is in charge of you. Then to your Lord you will ˹all˺ be returned.”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘The Angel of death who has been charged with you shall receive you in death in other words he shall seize your spirits then to your Lord you shall be returned’ alive whereat He will requite you for your deeds.

hype_questions: What happens to a person after they die?
Will I be held accountable for my actions in the afterlife?
How will God reward or punish me for my deeds?
propositions: Your soul will be taken by the Angel of Death.
You will be returned to your Lord alive.
God will requite you for your deeds.

source_text:
Verse: If only you could see the wicked hanging their heads ˹in shame˺ before their Lord, ˹crying:˺ “Our Lord! We have now seen and heard, so send us back and we will do good. We truly have sure faith ˹now˺!”

Tafsir: And if could you but see the guilty the disbelievers hanging their heads low before their Lord lowering them in shame saying ‘Our Lord! We have seen the resurrection that we denied and heard from You the confirmation of the truth of the messengers concerning that in which we used to call them liars. So send us back to the world so that we may act righteously therein for indeed we are convinced’ now. But none of this is of any use to them and they will not be sent back the response to the conditional clause beginning with law ‘if’ is an implicit ‘you would see a terrible thing’.

hype_questions: What would happen if the wicked saw their Lord's judgment?
Can people change their ways after denying the truth?
How will those who reject faith face their Lord?
propositions: The wicked hang their heads in shame before their Lord.
They cry out to their Lord, seeking forgiveness and a chance to act righteously.
Their denial of the resurrection is confirmed by the messengers' truth.
None of this can save them from their fate.
If they could see their Lord's judgment, they would be filled with terror.

source_text:
Verse: Had We willed, We could have easily imposed guidance on every soul. But My Word will come to pass: I will surely fill up Hell with jinn and humans all together.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says ‘And had We so willed We could have given every soul its means to guidance so that it may be guided through faith and obedience through its own choice but My Word became due and it is that “Verily I shall fill Hell with jinn and mankind together”.

hype_questions: Can humans be guided without free will?
What is the nature of Hell in Islamic theology?
Does God's Word have a direct impact on human choices?
propositions: Had We willed, We could have easily imposed guidance on every soul.
My Word became due and it is that 'Verily I shall fill Hell with jinn and mankind together'.
I will surely fill up Hell with jinn and humans all together.

source_text:
Verse: So taste ˹the punishment˺ for neglecting the meeting of this Day of yours. We ˹too˺ will certainly neglect you. And taste the torment of eternity for what you used to do!

Tafsir: When they enter Hell its Keepers shall say to them So taste now the chastisement for your having forgotten the encounter of this day of yours in other words for your having neglected to believe in it. We too shall forget you we shall abandon you in the chastisement. And taste now the everlasting chastisement for what you used to practise’ of disbelief and denial.

hype_questions: What happens when one neglects the meeting of this Day of yours?
Will those who forget their faith be abandoned in the chastisement?
What is the everlasting chastisement for those who practise disbelief and denial?
propositions: We will certainly neglect you.
When they enter Hell, its Keepers shall say to them: So taste now the chastisement for your having forgotten the encounter of this day of yours.
And taste now the everlasting chastisement for what you used to practise' of disbelief and denial.

source_text:
Verse: The only ˹true˺ believers in Our revelation are those who—when it is recited to them—fall into prostration and glorify the praises of their Lord and are not too proud.

Tafsir: Only those believe in Our signs such as the Qur’ān who when they are reminded of them admonished with them fall down in prostration and make glorifications ensconced in praise of their Lord in other words they say ‘Glory be to God through His praise’ subhāna’Llāh wa-bi-hāmdihi and they do not disdain to believe and to obey.

hype_questions: What is the condition for a person to be considered a true believer in Islam?
How do believers respond when reminded of Allah's signs?
What is the attitude that believers should have towards their Lord?
propositions: Only those who believe in Our revelation fall into prostration and glorify the praises of their Lord.
Believers are admonished with Our signs and then fall down in prostration.
They say 'Glory be to God through His praise' when reminded of Allah's signs.

source_text:
Verse: They abandon their beds, invoking their Lord with hope and fear, and donate from what We have provided for them.

Tafsir: Their sides withdraw they rise from their lying places the places for lying down to sleep together with the bedding in order to spend the night in prayer tahajjud to supplicate to their Lord in fear of His punishment and in hope of His mercy and they expend of what We have provided them they give voluntary alms.

hype_questions: What is the significance of tahajjud in Islam?
How does one demonstrate fear and hope when supplicating to Allah?
What are the benefits of giving voluntary alms?
propositions: They abandon their beds to spend the night in prayer.
They invoke their Lord with hope and fear.
They donate from what has been provided for them as voluntary alms.

source_text:
Verse: No soul can imagine what delights are kept in store for them as a reward for what they used to do.

Tafsir: For no soul knows what has been kept hidden for them in the way of joyous sights a variant reading for ukhfiya has the imperfect tense ukhfī as a reward for what they used to do.

hype_questions: What delights are kept in store for us as a reward?
What has been kept hidden for us in the way of joyous sights?
What is the nature of the ukhfiya?
propositions: No soul can imagine what delights are kept in store for them as a reward for what they used to do.
For no soul knows what has been kept hidden for them in the way of joyous sights.
A variant reading for ukhfiya has the imperfect tense ukhfī as a reward for what they used to do.

source_text:
Verse: Is the one who is a believer equal ˹before Allah˺ to the one who is rebellious? They are not equal!

Tafsir: Is he who is a believer like him who is a transgressor? They are not equal namely the believers and the transgressors.

hype_questions: Does being a believer make someone equal to a rebellious person in God's eyes?
Are believers and transgressors treated equally by Allah?
Can one's faith justify their actions?
propositions: A believer is not equal to a rebellious person before Allah.
Believers are not equal to transgressors.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who believe and do good, they will have the Gardens of ˹Eternal˺ Residence—as an accommodation for what they used to do.

Tafsir: As for those who believe and perform righteous deeds for them shall be the Gardens of the Abode — a hospitality nuzul is what is prepared for a guest for what they used to do.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe and perform righteous deeds?
How will Allah accommodate those who do good?
What is prepared for a guest in the Gardens of Residence?
propositions: Those who believe and do good will have the Gardens of Eternal Residence.
Performing righteous deeds is a condition for receiving the Gardens of Abode.
Allah prepares hospitality for those who do good.

source_text:
Verse: But as for those who are rebellious, the Fire will be their home. Whenever they try to escape from it, they will be forced back into it, and will be told, “Taste the Fire’s torment, which you used to deny.”

Tafsir: But as for those who transgressed by disbelieving and denying their abode shall be the Fire. Whenever they seek to exit from it they shall be brought back into it and it shall be said to them ‘Taste the chastisement of the Fire which you used to deny’.

hype_questions: What happens to those who rebel against Allah?
Will those who deny the existence of Fire be punished for it?
Can those who transgress against their abode escape the consequences?
propositions: Those who are rebellious will be forced into the Fire.
The Fire is their home.
They will be told to taste the torment of the Fire which they denied.
Transgressing by disbelieving and denying one's abode leads to being in the Fire.
Seeking to exit the Fire will result in being brought back into it.

source_text:
Verse: We will certainly make them taste some of the minor torment ˹in this life˺ before the major torment ˹of the Hereafter˺, so perhaps they will return ˹to the Right Path˺.

Tafsir: And We shall surely make them taste the nearer chastisement that is the chastisement of this world — in their being killed or taken captive or through years of drought and disease — before the greater chastisement the chastisement of the Hereafter that perhaps they namely those remaining of them may return to belief.

hype_questions: Will those who have been tested in this life be given another chance to return to the Right Path?
What is the nature of the chastisement that will be inflicted upon those who reject faith?
Can those who have been taken captive or killed ever truly return to their previous state?
propositions: We will certainly make them taste some of the minor torment in this life before the major torment of the Hereafter.
The chastisement of this world includes being killed, taken captive, years of drought, and disease.
Those who remain after being tested may return to belief.

source_text:
Verse: And who does more wrong than the one who is reminded of Allah’s revelations then turns away from them? We will surely inflict punishment upon the wicked.

Tafsir: And who does greater wrong than he who is reminded of the signs of his Lord such as the Qur’ān but then turns away from them? in other words none does greater wrong than such a person. Assuredly We shall take vengeance upon the criminals the idolaters.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who is reminded of Allah's revelations but turns away from them?
Who does greater wrong than someone who ignores Allah's signs and warnings?
Will the wicked be punished for their disobedience?
propositions: The one who is reminded of Allah’s revelations then turns away from them does more wrong.
The Qur’ān contains the signs of Allah that must be followed.
Allah will take vengeance upon those who disobey and turn away from His signs.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We gave the Scripture to Moses—so let there be no doubt ˹O Prophet˺ that you ˹too˺ are receiving revelations—and We made it a guide for the Children of Israel.

Tafsir: And verily We gave Moses the Scripture the Torah; so do not be in doubt concerning the encounter with Him and indeed he and He met on the Night of the Journey; and We appointed him namely Moses — or read ‘We appointed it’ the Scripture a guidance for the Children of Israel.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Torah in Islamic theology?
How did Moses receive revelations from God?
What was the encounter between Moses and God like?
propositions: We gave the Scripture to Moses.
The Scripture is a guide for the Children of Israel.
Moses met with God on the Night of the Journey.

source_text:
Verse: We raised from among them leaders, guiding by Our command, when they patiently endured and firmly believed in Our signs.

Tafsir: And We appointed among them leaders read a-immatan by pronouncing both hamzas or by substituting the second one with a yā who guided people by Our command when they had endured patiently in observing their religion and against the hardships they suffered because of their enemies lammā ‘when’ a variant reading has limā ‘because’ and had conviction in Our signs the ones indicating Our power and Our Oneness.

hype_questions: What is the role of patience in leadership?
How do leaders guide people according to God's command?
What are the signs that indicate God's power and Oneness?
propositions: We raised leaders from among them.
They were guided by Our command.
They endured patiently in observing their religion.
They suffered hardships because of their enemies.
They had conviction in Our signs indicating Our power and Our Oneness.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, your Lord will decide between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their differences.

Tafsir: Surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ in matters of religion.

hype_questions: What will be the outcome of the differences between individuals on the Day of Judgment?
How will Allah judge the disputes between people regarding religious matters?
Will there be any consequences for the disagreements that occurred in matters of religion?
propositions: Your Lord will decide between them on the Day of Judgment.
Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection.
They used to differ in matters of religion.

source_text:
Verse: Is it not yet clear to them how many peoples We destroyed before them, whose ruins they still pass by? Surely in this are signs. Will they not then listen?

Tafsir: Or is it not an indication for them how many generations communities on account of their disbelief We destroyed before them that is to say has not Our destruction of many generations become clear to the disbelievers of Mecca amid whose dwellings they walk yamshūna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person of the pronoun lahum ‘for them’ during their travels to Syria and other places so that they might take heed? Surely in that there are signs indications of Our power. Are they not able to hear? in a way so as to reflect and be admonished.

hype_questions: Will they not take heed of the signs around them?
Are they not able to hear the message being conveyed?
Can they not reflect on their own actions and be admonished?
propositions: We destroyed many generations before them due to their disbelief.
Their dwellings are a sign of Our power.
They should take heed of the signs around them during their travels.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not see how We drive rain to parched land, producing ˹various˺ crops from which they and their cattle eat? Will they not then see?

Tafsir: Or have they not seen how We drive the water to barren land juruz this is arid land that contains no vegetation and therewith bring forth crops whereof their cattle and they themselves eat? Can they not see? this and so realise that We have the power to bring them back to life after death.

hype_questions: Can they not see how Allah brings life to barren land?
Will they not then see the power of Allah in producing crops from rain?
Can they not realise that Allah has the power to bring them back to life after death?
propositions: Allah drives rain to parched land.
This produces various crops from which humans and their cattle eat.
Allah brings forth crops whereof their cattle and they themselves eat.
Can they not see that this is a sign of Allah's power?
Will they not then realise that Allah has the power to bring them back to life after death?

source_text:
Verse: They ask ˹mockingly˺, “When is this ˹Day of final˺ Decision, if what you say is true?”

Tafsir: And they say to the believers ‘When will this decisive Judgement between us and yourselves be if you are truthful?’

hype_questions: What is the date of the Day of final Decision?
How will we be judged on the Day of final Decision?
Will there be a decisive Judgement between us and ourselves?
propositions: The Day of final Decision will come.
Believers will be judged on the Day of final Decision.
There will be a decisive Judgement between believers and non-believers.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “On the Day of Decision it will not benefit the disbelievers to believe then, nor will they be delayed ˹from punishment˺.”

Tafsir: Say ‘On the day of this Judgement which will be effected by sending the chastisement on them their newly found faith then shall not benefit those who had been disbelievers nor shall they be given respite to make repentance or offer excuses.

hype_questions: What happens when a person believes in God after they have been disbelievers?
Can someone be forgiven for their past sins if they repent after becoming a believer?
Is it possible to escape punishment on the Day of Judgement?
propositions: The Day of Judgement will not benefit those who become believers after being disbelievers.
Disbelievers will not be given respite to make repentance or offer excuses.
Faith gained by disbelievers after the Day of Judgement will not save them from punishment.

source_text:
Verse: So turn away from them, and wait! They too are waiting.

Tafsir: So turn away from them and wait for the chastisement to be sent down on them. They too are waiting for your death to take place or for you to be killed and so be rid of you — this was revealed before the command to fight them.

hype_questions: What happens when we wait for Allah's chastisement?
How do we deal with those who are waiting for our death?
What is the significance of waiting in Islam?
propositions: Turn away from them.
Wait for the chastisement to be sent down on them.
They too are waiting for your death to take place or for you to be killed and so be rid of you.

source_text:
Verse: O Prophet! ˹Always˺ be mindful of Allah, and do not yield to the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: O Prophet! Fear God remain in fear of Him and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites and so follow them in what contravenes your Law. Truly God is Knower of what will happens before it happens Wise in what He creates.

hype_questions: What is the importance of fearing Allah in Islam?
How should Muslims respond to disbelievers and hypocrites?
What does it mean for God to be All-Knowing and All-Wise?
propositions: O Prophet, always be mindful of Allah.
Fear God and remain in fear of Him.
Do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.
God is All-Knowing of what will happen before it happens.
God is Wise in what He creates.

source_text:
Verse: Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Surely Allah is All-Aware of what you ˹all˺ do.

Tafsir: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord namely the Qur’ān. Truly God is Aware of what you do ta‘malūna; a variant reading has ya‘malūna ‘what they do’.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate source of guidance for Muslims?
How does Allah know about human actions?
What is the correct approach to following divine instructions?
propositions: Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord.
God is Aware of what you do.
The Qur'ān is a source of guidance from Allah.

source_text:
Verse: And put your trust in Allah, for Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs.

Tafsir: And put your trust in God regarding this affair of yours; and God suffices as Guardian to preserve you. And the members of his the Prophet’s community are subject to the same admonitions in all of the above.

hype_questions: What is Tawakkul in Islam?
How does Allah provide for His believers?
Can humans rely solely on God for their well-being?
propositions: Put your trust in Allah.
Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs.
God suffices as Guardian to preserve you.
The Prophet's community is subject to the same admonitions regarding Tawakkul.

source_text:
Verse: Allah does not place two hearts in any person’s chest. Nor does He regard your wives as ˹unlawful for you like˺ your real mothers, ˹even˺ if you say they are. These are only your baseless assertions. But Allah declares the truth, and He ˹alone˺ guides to the ˹Right˺ Way.

Tafsir: God has not placed two hearts inside any man this was revealed in order to refute those disbelievers who said that they each had two hearts with which they could reason better than Muhammad’s single mind; nor has He made your wives whom read as allā’ī or allā’ you repudiate by zihār read tazzahharūna or tuzāhirūna; the original tā’ of tatazāharūna has been assimilated with the zā’ — a man would say to his wife for example ‘You are for me as untouchable as my mother’s back’ — your mothers in other words He has not made you wives like your mothers so that they are illicit for conjugality in that respect a practice which in pre-Islamic times was considered a valid form of divorce. An atonement with necessary conditions is necessary in such a case as mentioned in sūrat al-Mujādila Q. 582-3. Nor has He made those whom you claim as adopted sons ad‘iyā’ the plural of da‘iyy which is one claimed as the son of one who is not his biological father your sons in reality. That is a mere utterance of your mouths namely of the Jews and the hypocrites. When the Prophet s married Zaynab bt. Jahsh who had been Zayd b. Hāritha’s wife the adopted son of the Prophet s they said ‘Muhammad married his son’s wife!’ and so God proved them liars in this. But God speaks the truth in this matter and He guides to the way the way of truth.

hype_questions: Does God place two hearts in any person's chest?
Are your wives considered as unlawful for you like your real mothers?
Do those whom you claim as adopted sons are actually your biological sons?
propositions: Allah does not place two hearts in any person’s chest.
Your wives are not regarded as unlawful for you like your real mothers, even if you say they are.
God declares the truth and guides to the Right Way.

source_text:
Verse: Let your adopted children keep their family names. That is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are ˹simply˺ your fellow believers and close associates. There is no blame on you for what you do by mistake, but ˹only˺ for what you do intentionally. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: Instead attribute them to their true fathers. That is more equitable that is more just in the sight of God. If you do not know their true fathers then they are your brethren in religion and as your associates. And you would not be at fault for any mistake you make in this respect except in what your hearts may premeditate after the prohibition has been issued. And God is Forgiving of whatever you said before the prohibition was issued Merciful to you in this respect.

hype_questions: What happens if I don't know the true father of my adopted child?
Can I still be at fault for not knowing the true father of my adopted child?
How does Allah feel about me when I make mistakes with adoption?
propositions: You should attribute your adopted children to their true fathers.
Not knowing the true fathers of your adopted children makes them your fellow believers and close associates.
You will not be at fault for any mistake you make in this respect except for what your hearts may premeditate after the prohibition has been issued.
God is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: The Prophet has a stronger affinity to the believers than they do themselves. And his wives are their mothers. As ordained by Allah, blood relatives are more entitled ˹to inheritance˺ than ˹other˺ believers and immigrants, unless you ˹want to˺ show kindness to your ˹close˺ associates ˹through bequest˺.

Tafsir: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own souls in terms of what he calls them to and what their own souls have called them to contravene and his wives are their mothers insofar as they the believers are forbidden to marry them. And those related by blood kinsmen are more entitled to inherit from one another in the Book of God than the other believers and the Emigrants in other words than inheriting on account of their sharing faith and the Emigration which had been the case at the beginning of Islam but was then abrogated; barring any favour you may do your friends by making a bequest which is permissible. This namely the abrogation of inheritance on account of shared faith and Emigration by the inheritance on account of kinship is written in the Book — in both instances al-kitāb ‘the Book’ denotes the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz.

hype_questions: What is the status of inheritance among believers and immigrants?
Can a believer's kindness to their associates be considered in inheritance decisions?
How does the Prophet's relationship with his wives affect their status as mothers?
propositions: The Prophet has a stronger affinity to the believers than they do themselves.
Blood relatives are more entitled to inheritance than other believers and immigrants, unless kindness is shown through bequest.
The Book of God states that inheritance on account of shared faith and Emigration was abrogated.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ when We took a covenant from the prophets, as well as from you ˹O Prophet˺, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. We did take a solemn covenant from ˹all of˺ them

Tafsir: And mention when We took a pledge from the prophets at the point when they were brought forth from the loins of Adam the size of atoms and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus son of Mary that they worship only God and call others to worship Him the mention of the five names is an instance of supplementing the specific to the general. And We took from them a solemn pledge a solid one that they fulfil what they have been charged with and this was effected by swearing an oath to God after which the pledge was consummated;

hype_questions: What is the significance of the covenant between God and prophets?
How did the prophets fulfill their obligations after swearing an oath to God?
What does it mean for humans to worship only one God?
propositions: We took a solemn covenant from the prophets, as well as from you, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
They were brought forth from the loins of Adam, the size of atoms.
They worshiped only God and called others to worship Him.
We took from them a solemn pledge that they fulfill what they have been charged with.
This was achieved by swearing an oath to God after which the pledge was consummated.

source_text:
Verse: so that He may question these men of truth about their ˹delivery of the˺ truth. And He has prepared a painful punishment for the disbelievers.

Tafsir: that He God may question the truthful about their truthfulness in delivering the Message as a way thereby to justifiably reproach the disbelievers; and He exalted be He has prepared for those who disbelieve in them a painful chastisement ‘adhāban alīman is a supplement to akhadhnā ‘We took’.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of God questioning those who deliver truth?
How does God justify reproaching disbelievers?
What punishment has God prepared for those who disbelieve?
propositions: God will question men of truth about their delivery of truth.
God has prepared a painful punishment for the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Remember Allah’s favour upon you when ˹enemy˺ forces came to ˹besiege˺ you ˹in Medina˺, And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.

Tafsir: O you who believe! Remember God’s favour to you when hosts of disbelievers came against you as confederates at the time the Ditch al-khandaq was being dug and We unleashed against them a great wind and hosts of angels you did not see. And God is ever Seer of what you do read ta‘malūna to imply ‘in the way of your digging of the ditch’; or read ya‘malūna ‘of what they do’ to imply ‘the idolaters’ forming of a confederation’.

hype_questions: What happened to the believers when their enemies besieged them in Medina?
How did Allah respond to the enemies of the believers?
What was the significance of the Ditch al-khandaq in Islamic history?
propositions: Believers were besieged by enemy forces in Medina.
Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
God unleashed a great wind and hosts of angels against the enemies of the believers.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember˺ when they came at you from east and west,

Tafsir: When they came at you from above you and from below you in other words from the higher side of the valley and from its lower side from the east and from the west and when the eyes turned away in fear from everything to gaze at their enemies approaching from every side and the hearts lept to the throats hanājir the plural of hunjura which lies at the bottom of the gullet out of intense fear while you entertained all sorts of different thoughts concerning God some of assistance some of despair;

hype_questions: What happens when enemies approach from all sides?
How do people react to intense fear?
What are the different thoughts that come up in one's mind during times of persecution?
propositions: Enemies approached from east and west.
The eyes turned away in fear from everything to gaze at their enemies approaching from every side.
The hearts leapt to the throats due to intense fear.
People entertained all sorts of different thoughts concerning God, some of assistance, some of despair.

source_text:
Verse: Then and there the believers were put to the test, and were violently shaken.

Tafsir: it was there that the believers were sorely tried there they were tested to distinguish the sincere individual from the one otherwise and were shaken with a mighty shock because of the severity of the terror.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the test faced by believers?
How do believers distinguish between sincerity and insincerity?
What is the cause of the mighty shock experienced by believers?
propositions: The believers were put to the test.
They were tested to distinguish the sincere individual from the one otherwise.
They were shaken with a mighty shock because of the severity of the terror.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ when the hypocrites and those with sickness in their hearts said, “Allah and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion!”

Tafsir: And mention when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is sickness namely weakness of conviction were saying ‘What God and His Messenger promised us of assistance to victory was nothing but delusion’ falsehood.

hype_questions: Did Allah and His Messenger promise the hypocrites anything real?
What did God and His Messenger promise to those with sickness in their hearts?
Is the assistance promised by God and His Messenger for victory just an illusion?
propositions: The hypocrites and those with weakness of conviction believe that Allah and His Messenger promised them nothing but delusion.
God and His Messenger did not promise any real assistance to victory to those who are hypocritical or have sickness in their hearts.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ when a group of them said, “O people of Yathrib! There is no point in you staying ˹here˺, so retreat!” Another group of them asked the Prophet’s permission ˹to leave˺, saying, “Our homes are vulnerable,” while ˹in fact˺ they were not vulnerable. They only wished to flee.

Tafsir: And when a party of them namely the hypocrites said ‘O people of Yathrib! namely the region of Medina it Yathriba is a diptote because of its being a proper noun and because of the morphological similarity it bears to a verbal form there is not a stand possible read muqām or maqām for you here in other words no place to stay and no strategic position so turn back to your dwellings in Medina — they had set out with the Prophet s towards the foot of a mountain outside Medina for battle. And a group of them even sought the permission of the Prophet to turn back saying ‘Our homes are exposed unprotected and we fear for them’. God exalted be He says although they were not exposed. They only sought to flee from battle.

hype_questions: What is the reason behind the hypocrites' desire to leave Medina?
How did the Prophet respond to their request to turn back?
What was the true intention of the hypocrites in seeking permission to leave?
propositions: The people of Yathrib were advised to retreat from Medina.
Their homes were vulnerable, but they only wished to flee from battle.
God exalted be He says that although their homes were not exposed, they sought to flee.

source_text:
Verse: Had their city been sacked from all sides and they had been asked to abandon faith, they would have done so with little hesitation.

Tafsir: And had they been invaded in it namely Medina from all sides and had they been exhorted in other words had the invaders exhorted them to treachery a return to idolatrous ways they would have committed it read la-ātawhā or la-atawhā meaning ‘they would have offered it’ or ‘they would have committed it’ respectively and would have hesitated thereupon but a little.

hype_questions: Would they have abandoned their faith if their city was invaded?
How would the people of Medina react to being exhorted to treachery?
What would be the outcome if the invaders asked them to return to idolatrous ways?
propositions: If their city was invaded, they would abandon their faith.
The people of Medina would commit treachery and idolatry if exhorted by the invaders.
They would hesitate but a little before committing treachery.

source_text:
Verse: They had already pledged to Allah earlier never to turn their backs ˹in retreat˺. And a pledge to Allah must be answered for.

Tafsir: Though they had assuredly pledged to God before that that they would not turn their backs to flee; and a pledge given to God must be answered for regarding whether it was fulfilled or not.

hype_questions: What happens when someone breaks their pledge to Allah?
Can a pledge given to God be ignored?
How is a pledge fulfilled or broken?
propositions: They had already pledged to Allah earlier never to turn their backs.
A pledge to Allah must be answered for.
A pledge given to God must be answered for regarding whether it was fulfilled or not.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Fleeing will not benefit you if you ˹try to˺ escape a natural or violent death. ˹If it is not your time,˺ you will only be allowed enjoyment for a little while.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Flight will not avail you should you flee from death or from being slain and then if you were to flee you would not be extended comfort in this world after you have fled except a little’ except for the remainder of your terms of life.

hype_questions: What happens when one tries to escape death?
Can fleeing from death bring comfort in this world?
How long can one expect comfort after fleeing?
propositions: Fleeing will not benefit you if you try to escape a natural or violent death.
If it is not your time, you will only be allowed enjoyment for a little while.
You would not be extended comfort in this world after you have fled except a little

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Who can put you out of Allah’s reach if He intends to harm you or show you mercy?” They can never find any protector or helper besides Allah.

Tafsir: Say ‘Who is it that can protect you grant you sanctuary from God should He desire to cause you ill whether it be destruction or defeat or who is it that can cause you ill should He God desire for you mercy?’ good. And they shall not find for themselves besides God in other words other than God any protector to avail them or helper to ward off harm from them.

hype_questions: Can anyone protect me from Allah's wrath?
Who can grant me sanctuary from God's mercy?
Is there anyone who can cause harm to me if God desires to show me mercy?
propositions: Allah is the only protector and helper.
God's power is beyond human comprehension.
No one can protect or help you except Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Allah knows well those among you who discourage ˹others from fighting˺, saying ˹secretly˺ to their brothers, “Stay with us,” and who themselves hardly take part in fighting.

Tafsir: Indeed God already knows the hinderers among you and those who say to their brethren ‘Come to us’ and they do not engage in the battle except a little for show and for the sake of their reputation

hype_questions: What are some common excuses people use to avoid participating in battles?
How do some individuals discourage others from engaging in combat?
What motivates people to pretend to participate in battles for personal gain?
propositions: Allah knows those who discourage others from fighting.
Those who say 'Come to us' and don't engage in battle are hindrances among you.
People may pretend to participate in battles for their reputation.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ totally unwilling to assist you. When danger comes, you see them staring at you with their eyes rolling like someone in the throes of death. But once the danger is over, they slash you with razor-sharp tongues, ravenous for ˹worldly˺ gains. Such people have not ˹truly˺ believed, so Allah has rendered their deeds void. And that is easy for Allah.

Tafsir: grudging to you in their help ashihha ‘grudging’ is the plural of shahīh and is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb ya’tūna ‘they engage’. And when there is a panic you see them looking at you their eyes rolling like one that is like the look of one or the rolling of one fainting at death in other words one in the throes thereof; but when the panic subsides and the spoils have been secured they scald you they hurt you or they smite you with their sharp tongues in their greed for the riches in other words for the spoils which they demand greedily. Those they never believed really. Therefore God has invalidated their works and that invalidation is easy for God by His will.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are unwilling to help others in times of need?
How do people behave when they are faced with danger and then later seek to exploit others for personal gain?
Can a person's actions be invalidated if they have not truly believed?
propositions: They are unwilling to assist you.
When danger comes, they stare at you with their eyes rolling like someone in the throes of death.
But once the danger is over, they slash you with razor-sharp tongues, ravenous for worldly gains.
Such people have not truly believed, so Allah has rendered their deeds void.
And that is easy for Allah.

source_text:
Verse: They ˹still˺ think that the enemy alliance has not ˹yet˺ withdrawn. And if the allies were to come ˹again˺, the hypocrites would wish to be away in the desert among nomadic Arabs, ˹only˺ asking for news about you ˹believers˺. And if the hypocrites were in your midst, they would hardly take part in the fight.

Tafsir: They suppose that the confederates of disbelievers have not yet departed to Mecca because of their fear of them and were the confederates to come a second time they would wish that they were in the desert with the Bedouins asking about your news your encounters with the disbelievers. And if they were among you this second time they would fight but a little for show and for fear of being reviled.

hype_questions: Would the hypocrites wish to be in the desert with the Bedouins if they knew about the believers' encounters with disbelievers?
How would the hypocrites behave if they were among the believers during a second alliance of disbelievers?
What would motivate the hypocrites to fight alongside the believers, even if it's just for show?
propositions: The confederates of disbelievers have not yet departed from Mecca due to their fear of them.
If the confederates were to come a second time, they would wish to be in the desert with the Bedouins asking about the believers' news and encounters with disbelievers.
If the hypocrites were among the believers during a second alliance of disbelievers, they would fight but little for show and for fear of being reviled.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever has hope in Allah and the Last Day, and remembers Allah often.

Tafsir: Verily there is for you a good example read iswa or uswa in the Messenger of God to emulate in combat and in holding one’s ground therein for whoever li-man substitutes for lakum ‘for you’ hopes for the encounter with God fears Him and the Last Day and remembers God often in contrast to those who do not.

topics: Jihad (struggle in the way of Allah)
hype_questions: What is the significance of emulating the Messenger of Allah in times of combat and holding one's ground?
How does hope for an encounter with God impact a person's behavior?
What is the difference between those who fear God and remember Him often, and those who do not?
propositions: The Messenger of Allah is an excellent example to emulate in times of combat and holding one's ground.
Hope for an encounter with God and remembering Him often are essential qualities for a person.
Fearing God and remembering Him often distinguishes those who will be rewarded from those who will not.

source_text:
Verse: When the believers saw the enemy alliance, they said, “This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us. The promise of Allah and His Messenger has come true.” And this only increased them in faith and submission.

Tafsir: And when the believers saw the confederates of disbelievers they said ‘This is what God and His Messenger promised us in the way of trial and assistance to victory and God and His Messenger were truthful’ about the promise. And that only increased them in faith in belief in God’s promise and submission to His command.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the promise made by Allah and His Messenger to the believers?
How did the believers' faith increase after witnessing the enemy alliance?
What role does trial play in the context of Allah's promise?
propositions: The believers saw the enemy alliance.
This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us.
The promise of Allah and His Messenger has come true.
God and His Messenger were truthful about the promise.
Their faith increased after witnessing the enemy alliance.
Submission to God's command increased their faith.

source_text:
Verse: Among the believers are men who have proven true to what they pledged to Allah. Some of them have fulfilled their pledge ˹with their lives˺, others are waiting ˹their turn˺. They have never changed ˹their commitment˺ in the least.

Tafsir: Among the believers are men who are true to the covenant they made with God in steadfastly remaining alongside the Prophet s. Some of them have fulfilled their vow having died or been killed fighting for God’s cause and some are still awaiting for this fate and they have not changed their commitment to the covenant in the least and they stand in contrast to the situation with the hypocrites;

hype_questions: What is the significance of faithfulness among believers?
How do believers fulfill their covenant with God?
What distinguishes believers from hypocrites?
propositions: Among the believers are men who have proven true to what they pledged to Allah.
Some of them have fulfilled their pledge with their lives, others are waiting their turn.
They have never changed their commitment in the least.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It all happened˺ so Allah may reward the faithful for their faithfulness, and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them ˹in mercy˺. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: that God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and chastise the hypocrites if He will by causing them to die in a state of hypocrisy or relent to them. Surely God is Forgiving to he who repents Merciful to him.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are faithful to God?
How does God punish the hypocrites?
Can people change their ways and receive mercy from God?
propositions: Allah may reward the faithful for their faithfulness.
Allah punishes the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in mercy.
Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah drove back the disbelievers in their rage, totally empty-handed. And Allah spared the believers from fighting. For Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.

Tafsir: And God repulsed those who were disbelievers namely the confederates in their rage without their attaining any good without achieving their desire in any way to triumph over the believers. And God spared the believers from fighting by unleashing the wind and the angels. And truly God is Strong in bringing about what He wants Mighty prevailing with His way.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah drives back the disbelievers in their rage?
How does Allah spare the believers from fighting?
What is the nature of God's power and might?
propositions: Allah drove back the disbelievers in their rage, totally empty-handed.
God repulsed those who were disbelievers namely the confederates in their rage without their attaining any good without achieving their desire in any way to triumph over the believers.
God spared the believers from fighting by unleashing the wind and the angels.
Truly God is Strong in bringing about what He wants Mighty prevailing with His way.

source_text:
Verse: And He brought down those from the People of the Book who supported the enemy alliance from their own strongholds, and cast horror into their hearts. You ˹believers˺ killed some, and took others captive.

Tafsir: And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture namely the Banū Qurayza who had supported them from their strongholds sayāsī is the plural of sīsa and is that in which one fortifies himself against an enemy and He cast terror into their hearts so that some of them you slew and these were the combatants and some of them you took captive namely their children.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of supporting an enemy alliance?
How does Allah cast terror into the hearts of those who oppose Him?
What happens to those who take part in combat during a war?
propositions: Allah brought down those from the People of the Book who supported the enemy alliance from their own strongholds.
He cast horror into their hearts.
Some were killed, and others taken captive.

source_text:
Verse: He has also caused you to take over their lands, homes, and wealth, as well as lands you have not yet set foot on. And Allah is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: And He made you inherit their land and their homes and their possessions and a land you had not trodden thitherto and this was the territory of Khaybar which was captured after that of Qurayza. And God has power over all things.

hype_questions: What is the significance of inheriting lands and possessions from others in Islam?
How does Allah's power manifest in conquests and inheritances?
What can be learned from the historical context of Khaybar and Qurayza?
propositions: Allah has caused you to take over their lands, homes, and wealth.

Verse: It is not for a believing man or woman—when Allah and His Messenger decree a matter—to have any other choice in that matter. Indeed, whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has clearly gone ˹far˺ astray.

Tafsir: And it is not fitting for any believing man or believing woman when God and His Messenger have decided on a matter to have read takūna or yakūna a choice in their matter in contravention of the decision of God and His Messenger. This verse was revealed regarding ‘Abd Allāh b. Jahsh and his sister Zaynab whose hand the Prophet had asked for in marriage but meaning on behalf of Zayd b. Hāritha. They were loathe to this proposal when they found out that it was on the latter’s behalf for they had thought that the Prophet s wanted to marry her himself. But afterwards they consented because of the following part of the verse And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into manifest error. Thus the Prophet s gave her in marriage to Zayd. Then on one occasion he the Prophet caught sight of her and felt love for her whereafter when he realised that Zayd lost his affection for her and so said to the Prophet s ‘I want to part with her’. But the Prophet said to him ‘Retain your wife for yourself’ as God exalted be He says

topics: Decision of Allah and His Messenger

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember, O  Prophet,˺ when you said to the one “Keep your wife and fear Allah,” while concealing within yourself what Allah was going to reveal. And ˹so˺ you were considering the people, whereas Allah was more worthy of your consideration. So when Zaid totally lost interest in ˹keeping˺ his wife, We gave her to you in marriage, so that there would be no blame on the believers for marrying the ex-wives of their adopted sons after their divorce. And Allah’s command is totally binding.

Tafsir: And when idh is dependent because of an implied preceding udhkur ‘mention when’ you said to him to whom God had shown favour by guiding him to Islam and to whom you too had shown favour by manumitting him — this was Zayd b. Hāritha who had been a prisoner of war before the coming of Islam in the period of al-jāhiliyya. The Messenger of God s purchased him before his call to prophethood and then manumitted him and adopted him as his son — ‘Retain your wife for yourself and fear God’ before divorcing her. But you had hidden in your heart what God was to disclose what He was to manifest of your love for her and of the fact that should Zayd part with her you would marry her and you feared people would say ‘He has married his son’s wife!’ though God is worthier that you should fear Him in all things so take her in marriage and do not be concerned with what people say. Zayd subsequently divorced her and her obligatory waiting period was completed. God exalted be He says So when Zayd had fulfilled whatever need he had of her We joined her in marriage to you — the Prophet consummated his marriage with her without the customary permission from her legal guardian and gratified the Muslims with a feast of bread and meat — so that there may not be any restriction for the believers in respect of the wives of their adopted sons when the latter have fulfilled whatever wish they have of them. And God’s commandment that which He has decreed is bound to be realised.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Prophet's marriage to Zaid's wife?

propositions: The Prophet was advised to 'retain your wife for yourself and fear God' before divorcing her.
The Prophet had hidden his true intentions regarding his love for Zaid's wife, fearing what people would say.
God exalted be He says that when Zaid divorced his wife, she was joined in marriage to the Prophet without the customary permission from her legal guardian.
The Prophet consummated his marriage with Zaid's wife and gratified the Muslims with a feast of bread and meat.

Verse: O believers! If you marry believing women and then divorce them before you touch them, so give them a ˹suitable˺ compensation, and let them go graciously.

Tafsir: O you who believe if you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them read tamassūhunna or tumāsūhunna that is before you have copulated with them there shall be no waiting period for you to reckon against them no waiting period needed to preclude pregnancy or otherwise. But provide for them give them what they can use for securing comforts in cases where no dowry has been fixed for them; otherwise theirs is to retain half of what was fixed but no more — this is what Ibn ‘Abbās said and it is the opinion followed by al-Shāfi‘ī’; and release them in a gracious manner leave them be without the intention to cause them any harm.
