propositions: Believers who divorce their wives before consummation must provide suitable compensation and release them graciously.
There is no waiting period to reckon against divorced women before physical intimacy, but provision must be made for their comfort.
If no dowry has been fixed, the woman's share is half of what was agreed upon; otherwise, it remains as agreed upon.
Ibn 'Abbās and al-Shāfi‘ī' followed this opinion regarding divorce compensation.

source_text:
Verse: O Prophet! We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have paid their ˹full˺ dowries as well as those ˹bondwomen˺ in your possession, whom Allah has granted you. We know well what ˹rulings˺ We have ordained for the believers in relation to their wives and those ˹bondwomen˺ in their possession. As such, there would be no blame on you. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: O Prophet! Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their dowries and what your right hand owns of those whom God has given you as spoils of war from the disbelievers whom you have taken captive such as Safiyya and Juwayriyya and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you as opposed to those who did not emigrate and any believing woman if she gift herself in marriage to the Prophet and if the Prophet desire to take her in marriage and ask for her hand in marriage without paying her a dowry — a privilege for you exclusively not for the rest of the believers nikāh ‘marriage’ when expressed by the term hiba ‘gift’ denotes marriage without dowry. Indeed We know what We have imposed upon them namely the believers with respect to their wives in the way of rulings to the effect that they should not take more than four wives and should only marry with the consent of a legal guardian the presence of witnesses and the payment of a dowry and with respect to what their right hands own of slavegirls in the way of purchase or otherwise so that the handmaiden be one lawful for her master such as a slavegirl belonging to the People of the Scripture kitābiyya and not a Magian or an idolater and that she should be ascertained as not carrying child with the necessary waiting period istibrā’ before copulation; so that li-kaylā is semantically connected to what came before this last statement there may be no unnecessary restriction for you no constraint in marriage for you. And God is Forgiving of what is difficult to guard against Merciful in giving dispensations allowing for latitude in this respect.

hype_questions: What are the conditions for a woman to be considered lawful in marriage?
Can a man marry multiple wives without restrictions?
What is the significance of the waiting period (istibrā') before copulation?
propositions: The Prophet is allowed to marry his wives whom he has given their dowries and what his right hand owns.
Believers are not allowed to take more than four wives without the consent of a legal guardian, witnesses, and payment of a dowry.
A slavegirl belonging to the People of the Scripture (kitābiyya) is considered lawful for her master if she is ascertained not to be carrying child with the necessary waiting period (istibrā').

source_text:
Verse: It is up to you ˹O Prophet˺ to delay or receive whoever you please of your wives. There is no blame on you if you call back any of those you have set aside. That is more likely that they will be content, not grieved, and satisfied with what you offer them all. Allah ˹fully˺ knows what is in your hearts. And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.

Tafsir: You may put off read turji’ or turjī you may postpone consorting with whomever of them you wish namely of your wives from their turn for intimacy and consort embrace in conjugality whomever you wish of them and come unto her and as for whomever you may desire of those whom you have set aside from their share you would not be at fault to desire her and consort with her again. He was given the choice in this respect after it had been obligatory for him to give each wife her equal share of conjugality. That freedom of choice makes it likelier that they will be comforted and not grieve and that they will be satisfied with what you give them of what has been mentioned of your freedom to choose whom to consort with every one of them kulluhunna emphasises the subject of the verb yardayna ‘they will be satisfied’ will be well-pleased with what you give her. And God knows what is in your hearts with respect to your women and your preferring some to others. We have given you the freedom to choose from among them in order to make it easier for you to have what you desire. And God is Knower of His creatures Forbearing in refraining from punishing them.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Do not enter the homes of the Prophet without permission ˹and if invited˺ for a meal, do not ˹come too early and˺ linger until the meal is ready. But if you are invited, then enter ˹on time˺. Once you have eaten, then go on your way, and do not stay for casual talk. Such behaviour is truly annoying to the Prophet, yet he is too shy to ask you to leave. But Allah is never shy of the truth. And when you ˹believers˺ ask his wives for something, ask them from behind a barrier. This is purer for your hearts and theirs. And it is not right for you to annoy the Messenger of Allah, nor ever marry his wives after him. This would certainly be a major offence in the sight of Allah.

Tafsir: O you who believe do not enter the Prophet’s houses unless permission is granted you to enter by invitation to share a meal and so you enter without waiting for the right moment for when it is ready ināhu a verbal noun from anā ya’nī. But when you are invited enter and when you have had your meal disperse without lingering for any leisurely conversation amongst yourselves. Indeed that lingering is upsetting for the Prophet and he is too shy of you to make you leave but God is not shy of the truth that you should leave — in other words He would never refrain from declaring it a variant reading for yastahyī has yastahī. And when you ask anything of his womenfolk in other words the wives of the Prophet s ask them from behind a screen a curtain. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts than entertaining sinful thoughts. And you should never cause the Messenger of God hurt in any way; nor ever marry his wives after him. Assuredly that in God’s sight would be very grave as a sin.

hype_questions: What is the proper etiquette for entering the homes of the Prophet?
Why should believers not linger over meals with the Prophet's household?
What is the significance of asking the Prophet's wives for something behind a barrier?
propositions: Believers should not enter the homes of the Prophet without permission.
When invited, believers should enter on time and not linger over leisurely conversation.
Believers should ask the Prophet's wives for something from behind a barrier to purify their hearts and hers.
It is not right for believers to annoy the Messenger of Allah or marry his wives after him.

source_text:
Verse: Whether you reveal something or conceal it, surely Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

Tafsir: Whether you disclose anything or keep it hidden regarding marrying them after him truly God has knowledge of all things and will requite you for it.

hype_questions: Does Allah have complete knowledge of everything?
Will Allah hold me accountable for my actions?
Can I trust in Allah's wisdom?
propositions: Allah has perfect knowledge of all things.
God has knowledge of all things and will requite you for it.

source_text:
Verse: There is no blame on the Prophet’s wives ˹if they appear unveiled˺ before their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers’ sons, their sisters’ sons, their fellow ˹Muslim˺ women, and those ˹bondspeople˺ in their possession. And be mindful of Allah ˹O wives of the Prophet!˺ Surely Allah is a Witness over all things.

Tafsir: They the Prophet’s wives would not be at fault with regard to socialising with their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their brothers’ sons or their sisters’ sons or their own believing women or what their right hands own of slavegirls or male servants in seeing them or conversing with them without a screen. And fear O women God in what you have been commanded. Surely God is Witness to all things with nothing being hidden from Him.

hype_questions: Can a woman be at fault for socializing with her family members without a screen?
What are the consequences of not following God's commands regarding women's behavior?
Is God truly all-knowing and watching over everything?
propositions: The Prophet’s wives will not be blamed for socializing with their fathers, sons, brothers, or other relatives without a screen.
God has commanded women to fear Him and be mindful of their behavior.
God is a Witness to all things and nothing is hidden from Him.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Allah showers His blessings upon the Prophet, and His angels pray for him. O  believers! Invoke Allah’s blessings upon him, and salute him with worthy greetings of peace.

Tafsir: Indeed God and His angels bless the Prophet Muhammad (s). O you who believe invoke blessings on him and invoke peace upon him in a worthy manner in other words say ‘O God bless our master Muhammad and grant him peace’ Allāhumma sallī ‘alā sayyidinā Muhammad wa-sallim.

hype_questions: What is the correct way to invoke blessings on the Prophet Muhammad?
How can we show respect and peace towards our master Muhammad?
What does it mean to say 'O God bless our master Muhammad and grant him peace'?
propositions: Allah showers His blessings upon the Prophet.
His angels pray for him.
Believers should invoke Allah’s blessings upon him.
They should salute him with worthy greetings of peace.
God and His angels bless the Prophet Muhammad (s).
O you who believe, invoke blessings on him and invoke peace upon him in a worthy manner.

source_text:
Verse: Surely those who offend Allah are condemned by Allah in this world and the Hereafter. And He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.

Tafsir: Indeed those who are injurious to God and His Messenger — and they are the disbelievers who attribute to God what He is exalted above of such things as His having a son or a partner and they deny His Messenger — God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter He has banished them from His mercy and has prepared for them a humiliating chastisement and that is the Fire.

hype_questions: What happens to those who attribute false attributes to God?
How does God punish those who disbelieve in Him and His Messenger?
What is the consequence of denying God's Messenger?
propositions: Those who offend Allah are condemned by Allah.
God has prepared a humiliating punishment for those who offend Allah.
God has cursed those who attribute false attributes to Him and His Messenger.
God has banished those who disbelieve in Him and His Messenger from His mercy.
The Fire is the humiliation chastisement prepared for those who offend Allah.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who abuse believing men and women unjustifiably, they will definitely bear the guilt of slander and blatant sin.

Tafsir: And those who cause hurt to believing men and believing women without the latter’s having done anything those who accuse them of what they have not done have verily borne the guilt of calumny they have borne lies and the burden of manifest sin.

hype_questions: What are the consequences for those who falsely accuse believing men or women?
How do those who cause harm to believers without justification affect their reputation?
What is the nature of the sin committed by those who spread false accusations?
propositions: Those who abuse believing men and women unjustifiably will bear the guilt of slander and blatant sin.
Accusing believing men or women without evidence is a form of calumny that carries a heavy burden.
The sin committed by those who falsely accuse others is manifest and cannot be ignored.

source_text:
Verse: O Prophet! Ask your wives, daughters, and believing women to draw their cloaks over their bodies. In this way it is more likely that they will be recognized ˹as virtuous˺ and not be harassed. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: O Prophet! Tell your wives and daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks closely over themselves jalābīb is the plural of jilbāb which is a wrap that covers a woman totally — in other words let them pull part of it also over their faces leaving one eye visible when they need to leave the house for something. That makes it likelier that they will be known to be free women and not be molested by being approached. In contrast slavegirls did not use to cover their faces and so the disbelievers used to pester them. And God is Forgiving of any occasion in the past when they may have neglected to cover themselves Merciful to them in His veiling them.

hype_questions: What is the dress code for women in Islam?
How can women protect themselves from harassment?
What is the significance of covering one's face in Islam?
propositions: Women should draw their cloaks over their bodies.
The purpose of drawing a cloak over one's body is to be recognized as virtuous and not harassed.
God is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: If the hypocrites, and those with sickness in their hearts, and rumour-mongers in Medina do not desist, We will certainly incite you ˹O Prophet˺ against them, and then they will not be your neighbours there any longer.

Tafsir: If la-in the lām is for oaths the hypocrites do not desist from their hypocrisy and likewise those in whose hearts is a sickness in their urge to fornicate as well as the scaremongers in the city who alarm the believers by saying to them things like ‘Your enemy is here and your raiding parties have been massacred!’ or they say to them ‘They have been defeated!’. Assuredly We will urge you to take action against them We will give you sway over them then they will not be your neighbours they will not dwell near you in it except for a little while after which they will depart.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who continue to spread false information and alarm the believers?
How will the Prophet be treated by those who refuse to desist from their hypocrisy?
What is the ultimate fate of those who are given sway over the hypocrites?
propositions: If the hypocrites do not desist, We will incite the Prophet against them.
Those with sickness in their hearts and rumour-mongers will be alarmed by the believers.
We will give the Prophet sway over the hypocrites, after which they will depart.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They deserve to be˺ condemned. ˹If they were to persist,˺ they would get themselves seized and killed relentlessly wherever they are found!

Tafsir: Accursed banished from mercy shall they be wherever they are found they shall be seized and slain violently that is to say that is the ruling concerning them — meant as a command for the Prophet.

hype_questions: What happens if someone persists in their wrongdoings?
Can people be punished severely for their actions?
Is there a specific ruling for those who are condemned?
propositions: They deserve to be condemned.
If they were to persist, they would get themselves seized and killed relentlessly wherever they are found.
Accursed banished from mercy shall they be wherever they are found.

source_text:
Verse: That was Allah’s way with those ˹hypocrites˺ who have gone before. And you will find no change in Allah’s way.

Tafsir: God’s precedent in other words God has made this His precedent in dealing with those who passed away before with regard to the hypocrites of past communities who used to alarm believers with their scaremongery and you will find that there is no changing God’s precedent no changing of it from Him.

hype_questions: What is Allah's way with those who are hypocrites?
Can Allah's way change over time?
How does Allah deal with past communities of hypocrites?
propositions: Allah dealt with hypocrites in a certain way before.
This way will not change for Allah.
Hypocrites used to alarm believers with their scaremongery.

source_text:
Verse: People ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the Hour. Say, “That knowledge is only with Allah. You never know, perhaps the Hour is near.”

Tafsir: People such as the people of Mecca question you concerning the Hour when will it be? Say ‘Knowledge thereof lies only with God — and what do you know what would provide you with knowledge thereof? In other words you do not know it perhaps the Hour is near’.

hype_questions: What will happen when the Hour arrives?
How can we gain knowledge about the Hour?
Is the Hour near or far?
propositions: The knowledge of the Hour is only with Allah.
You do not know when the Hour will be.
Perhaps the Hour is near.

source_text:
Verse: Surely Allah condemns the disbelievers, and has prepared for them a blazing Fire,

Tafsir: God has indeed cursed the disbelievers He has banished them from His mercy and prepared for them a blaze a violent fire into which they shall be admitted

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject Allah?
Will the disbelievers be punished for their actions?
Can anyone escape the wrath of Allah?
propositions: God condemns the disbelievers.
The disbelievers have been banished from God's mercy.
A blazing fire has been prepared for the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: to stay there for ever and ever—never will they find any protector or helper.

Tafsir: to abide their abiding having been foreordained therein forever. They shall not find any protector to preserve them from it or helper to ward it off from them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject Allah's signs?
Can they find any protector or helper in this world?
Will they be saved from the punishment of their actions?
propositions: They will not find any protector.
They will not find any helper.
Their abiding has been foreordained forever.

source_text:
Verse: On the Day their faces are ˹constantly˺ flipped in the Fire, they will cry, “Oh! If only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!”

Tafsir: On the day when their faces are turned about in the Fire they shall say ‘O yā is for alerting would that we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger!’

hype_questions: If only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!
What would have happened if they had obeyed God and followed the Prophet?
How would their lives change if they had submitted to God's will?
propositions: On the Day their faces are constantly flipped in the Fire, they will cry.
They shall say 'O yā is for alerting',
that we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger!

source_text:
Verse: And they will say, “Our Lord! We obeyed our leaders and elite, but they led us astray from the ˹Right˺ Way.

Tafsir: And they namely those who had been the followers of the leaders of error shall say ‘Our Lord we obeyed our leaders read plural sādatanā or sādātanā which is the plural of the plural and elders and they led us astray from the way the path of guidance.

hype_questions: What happens when we follow wrong leaders?
How do we distinguish between right and wrong guidance?
Can obedience to leaders lead us astray?
propositions: They obeyed their leaders.
Their leaders led them astray from the Right Way.
The path of guidance is distinct from the way of error.

source_text:
Verse: Our Lord! Give them double ˹our˺ punishment, and condemn them tremendously.”

Tafsir: Our Lord give them a double chastisement in other words twice the like of our chastisement and curse them chastise them with numerous curses!’ with the equivalent number of chastisements la‘nan kathīran ‘numerous curses’ is also read la‘nan kabīran which means ‘with a mighty curse’.

hype_questions: What does the Quran say about punishment for those who disbelieve?
How many chastisements will Allah give to those who reject His message?
What is the equivalent of Allah's curse on those who disobey Him?
propositions: Our Lord gives them double chastisement.
Their chastisement is twice that of ours.
They are cursed with numerous curses.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Do not be like those who slandered Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they said. And he was honourable in the sight of Allah.

Tafsir: O you who believe do not behave towards your Prophet as did those who harmed Moses — when they would say for example ‘The only reason he does not wash with us is that he has an inflammation in his testicles’ — whereat God absolved him of what they alleged when Moses placed his robe on a rock to go to wash the rock hurtled away with it until it came to a halt amid a group of men from the Children of Israel. As Moses chased it and took his robe to cover himself they saw that he had no such inflammation udra is an inflammation of the testicle. And he was distinguished in God’s sight. An instance of our Prophet s being subjected to hurt was when on one occasion while dividing up the spoils a man said to him ‘This is a division that I do not want to please God!’ whereat the Prophet s became angered and said ‘May God have mercy upon Moses for truly he was hurt with worse than this but endured’ — reported by al-Bukhārī.

hype_questions: Does Allah clear individuals of false accusations?
How did Moses handle a situation where he was slandered by others?
What is an example of the Prophet's patience in the face of adversity?
propositions: Believers should not behave towards their Prophet as those who harmed Moses.
Allah cleared Moses of what they said about him.
Moses was distinguished in God's sight despite being slandered by others.
The Prophet became angered when someone questioned the fairness of a division, but remained patient like Moses.
God has mercy on individuals who endure hardships with patience.

source_text:
Verse: O  believers! Be mindful of Allah, and say what is right.

Tafsir: O you who believe fear God and speak words of integrity what is proper.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be mindful of Allah?
How can speaking words of integrity benefit a Muslim's relationship with God?
What are the consequences of not being obedient to God?
propositions: Believers should be mindful of Allah.
Saying what is right is proper.
Fear of God and speaking truthfully are essential for believers.

source_text:
Verse: He will bless your deeds for you, and forgive your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, has truly achieved a great triumph.

Tafsir: He will rectify your deeds for you He will accept them and will forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has verily achieved a great success he has attained his ultimate goal.

hype_questions: What happens to my deeds when I obey Allah and His Messenger?
How will Allah forgive my sins?
What is the ultimate goal of obeying God and His Messenger?
propositions: He will bless your deeds for you.
He will rectify your deeds for you.
Allah will accept them and will forgive you your sins.
Whoever obeys God has verily achieved a great success he has attained his ultimate goal.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they ˹all˺ declined to bear it, being fearful of it. But humanity assumed it, ˹for˺ they are truly wrongful ˹to themselves˺ and ignorant ˹of the consequences˺,

Tafsir: Indeed We offered the Trust — the obligation to prayer and other matters which when performed result in reward and when neglected result in punishment — to the heavens and the earth and the mountains and created in them the power of comprehension and speech at the time of that offer but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it; but man Adam undertook it when it was offered to him. Truly he is a wrongdoer to his own soul because of what he undertook ignorant of the responsibility that comes with it —

hype_questions: What is the nature of the trust offered to humanity?
Why did humans decline to bear the responsibility of prayer and other matters?
How does humanity's assumption of the trust impact their relationship with Allah?
propositions: Allah offered the trust to the heavens, earth, and mountains.
Humans declined to bear the responsibility of prayer and other matters due to fear.
Man (Adam) assumed the trust when it was offered to him.
Assuming the trust without understanding its consequences is a wrongdoer's act towards oneself.
The power of comprehension and speech was created in humans at the time of the offer.

source_text:
Verse: so that Allah will punish hypocrite men and women and polytheistic men and women, and Allah will turn in mercy to believing men and women. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: so that God may chastise li-yu‘adhdhiba the lām therein is semantically connected to ‘aradnā ‘We offered’ which resulted in ‘Adam’s undertaking’ the hypocrites men and women and the idolaters men and women those who forsake the Trust and that God may relent to the believing men and believing women who fulfil the Trust. And God is Forgiving to believers Merciful to them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are hypocrites and polytheists?
How do believers fulfill the Trust?
Why is God merciful to believers?
propositions: Allah will punish hypocrite men and women, and polytheistic men and women.
God may relent to the believing men and women who fulfil the Trust.
God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: All praise is for Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And praise be to Him in the Hereafter. He is the All-Wise, All-Aware.

Tafsir: Praise be to God — God exalted be He praises Himself with these words; the import constitutes the eulogy that ‘praise’ is ever-established for God and it entails the attribution to Him of all that is beautiful exalted be He — to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth as possessions and creation. And to Him belongs all praise in the Hereafter as in this world for His friends praise Him as they enter Paradise. And He is the Wise in what He does the Aware of His creatures.

hype_questions: What are the attributes that God praises Himself with?
Why does God exalt His praise in both this world and the Hereafter?
How does God's wisdom manifest in His actions?
propositions: Allah is to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
God praises Himself with these words, which constitute an eulogy for Him.
Praise be to God — God exalted be He praises Himself with these words.
To Whom belongs all praise in this world and the Hereafter.
He is the All-Wise, All-Aware.

source_text:
Verse: He knows whatever goes into the earth and whatever comes out of it, and whatever descends from the sky and whatever ascends into it. And He is the Most Merciful, All-Forgiving.

Tafsir: He knows what penetrates the earth of water and so forth and what issues out of it of vegetation and so on and what comes down from the heaven of provision and so on and what ascends into it of deeds and so on and He is the Merciful to His friends the Forgiving to them.

hype_questions: What does Allah know about the earth?
How does Allah provide for us?
What happens to our deeds after we die?
propositions: Allah knows what penetrates the earth.
Allah issues out vegetation from the earth.
Allah provides for us from heaven.
Allah ascends deeds into heaven.
Allah is Merciful to His friends.
Allah is Forgiving to His friends.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers say, “The Hour will never come to us.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Yes—by my Lord, the Knower of the unseen—it will certainly come to you!” Not ˹even˺ an atom’s weight is hidden from Him in the heavens or the earth; nor anything smaller or larger than that, but is ˹written˺ in a perfect Record.

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve say ‘The Hour the Resurrection will never come to us’. Say to them ‘Yes indeed by my Lord it shall come to you — by the Knower of the Unseen read ‘ālimi’l-ghaybi as an adjectival qualification of wa-rabbī ‘by my Lord’ or read ‘ālimu’l-ghaybi as the predicate of a missing subject such as huwa ‘He is’; or read ‘allāmi’l-ghaybi. Not even the weight of an atom escapes is hidden from Him in the heavens or in the earth nor is there anything smaller than that or greater but it is in a Manifest Book namely the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz

hype_questions: Will the Resurrection come to us?
Is anything hidden from Allah?
What is the nature of Allah's knowledge?
propositions: The Hour will certainly come to you.
Not even an atom's weight is hidden from Allah in the heavens or on earth.
Allah has a Manifest Book that contains everything.

source_text:
Verse: So He may reward those who believe and do good. It is they who will have forgiveness and an honourable provision.

Tafsir: that He may requite thereat those who believe and perform righteous deeds — for such there will be forgiveness and a fair provision in Paradise.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe and do good?
How does Allah requite those who perform righteous deeds?
What can be expected from those who are forgiven in Paradise?
propositions: Allah rewards those who believe and do good.
Those who believe and perform righteous deeds will receive forgiveness.
There will be a fair provision in Paradise for such individuals.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who strive to discredit Our revelations, it is they who will suffer the ˹worst˺ torment of agonizing pain.

Tafsir: And those who strive against who strive to invalidate Our signs namely the Qur’ān deeming Us inomnipotent mu‘ajjizīna a variant reading of this here and later on in verse 38 below is mu‘ājizīna so that respectively these mean ‘deeming that We are incapable’ mu‘ajjizīna or if read mu‘ājizīna ‘vying with Us in order to elude Us’ for they suppose that there is no such thing as resurrection or punishment — for such there will be a chastisement of an awful punishment’ read either alīmin or alīmun respectively as an adjectival qualification of rijzin ‘punishment’ or ‘adhābun ‘chastisement’.

hype_questions: What happens to those who try to discredit the Quran?
Will there be a punishment for those who deny resurrection and punishment?
How will those who try to invalidate the signs of Allah be treated?
propositions: Those who strive to discredit Our revelations will suffer agonizing pain.
Those who invalidate Our signs, namely the Qur'ān, are deemed incapable by them.
For such, there will be a chastisement of an awful punishment.

source_text:
Verse: Those gifted with knowledge ˹clearly˺ see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ is the truth, and that it guides to the Path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.

Tafsir: And those who have been given knowledge — the believers from among the People of the Scripture such as ‘Abd Allāh b. Salām and his companions — see they know that what has been revealed to you from your Lord that is the Qur’ān is the decisive truth and that it guides to the path the way of the Mighty the Praised in other words of God the Lord of Might Who is ever-praised.

hype_questions: Does the Qur'ān guide to the path of the Almighty?
What is the decisive truth revealed by God in the Qur'ān?
How does the Qur'ān lead to the way of the Mighty and Praised?
propositions: The Qur'ān has been revealed from your Lord, O Prophet.
The believers see that what has been revealed is the decisive truth.
The Qur'ān guides to the path of the Almighty.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers say ˹mockingly to one another˺, “Shall we show you a man who claims that when you have been utterly disintegrated you will be raised as a new creation?

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve say that is some of them say to others in order to provoke disbelief in them ‘Shall we show you a man — namely Muhammad (s) — who will inform you that when you have been utterly torn to pieces you shall indeed be created anew?’

hype_questions: Will I be resurrected after death?
Can I be recreated from nothing?
What happens to those who disbelieve?
propositions: Some people claim that when they are utterly disintegrated, they will be raised as a new creation.
Muhammad (s) informs us that we shall indeed be created anew after death.
Those who disbelieve say that this is not true.

source_text:
Verse: Has he fabricated a lie against Allah or is he insane?” In fact, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are bound for torment and have strayed farthest ˹from the truth˺.

Tafsir: Has he invented read a’ftarā; the hamza read with a fatha vowelling is for the interrogative and suffices in place of the conjunctive hamza a lie against God in this respect or is there a madness in him does he suffer a dementia on account of which he has imagined that? God exalted be He says Nay but those who do not believe in the Hereafter that comprises resurrection and chastisement will be in the chastisement thereat and in error that is far from the truth in this world.

hype_questions: Can a person fabricate a lie against Allah?
Is it possible for someone to be insane or suffer from dementia?
propositions: Has he invented a lie against God?
Or is there madness in him?
Those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in torment and error.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not then seen all that surrounds them of the heavens and the earth? If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them up, or cause ˹deadly˺ pieces of the sky to fall upon them. Surely in this is a sign for every servant who turns ˹to Allah˺.

Tafsir: Have they not observed what is before them and what is behind them in other words what is above them and what is beneath them of heaven and earth? If We will it We can make the earth swallow them or let fall on them fragments read kisfan or kisafan ‘large pieces’ from the heaven a variant reading has the third person singular for all three verbs sc. yashā’ ‘He will’ yakhsif ‘He makes to swallow’ yusqit ‘He lets fall’. Surely in that which is observed there is a sign for every penitent servant turning back to his Lord signs indicating God’s power to resurrect and to do what He will.

hype_questions: Can Allah create the universe and control its forces?
What is the purpose of human existence in relation to Allah?
How does Allah's power manifest in the natural world?
propositions: The earth can swallow people if Allah wills.
Allah can cause large pieces of the sky to fall upon people if He wills.
There is a sign for every servant who turns to Allah in observing the wonders of creation.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We granted David a ˹great˺ privilege from Us, ˹commanding:˺ “O mountains! Echo his hymns! And the birds as well.” We made iron mouldable for him,

Tafsir: And verily We bestowed on David a great favour from Us — prophethood and scripture — and We said ‘O mountains repeat with him in praise by making glorifications and the birds too!’ read wa’l-tayra in the accusative as a supplement to the syntactical locus of jibāl ‘mountains’ in other words and We also called on them to glorify God with him. And We made iron malleable for him so that it was as dough in his hands.

hype_questions: What is the significance of prophethood in Islam?
How does glorification relate to the concept of worship in Islam?
What is the role of scripture in Islamic faith?
propositions: We granted David a great privilege from Us.
O mountains, echo his hymns and the birds as well.
We bestowed on David prophethood and scripture.
We made iron malleable for him so that it was as dough in his hands.

source_text:
Verse: instructing: “Make full-length armour, ˹perfectly˺ balancing the links. And work righteousness ˹O family of David!˺. Indeed, I am All-Seeing of what you do.”

Tafsir: And We said ‘Fashion from it long coats of mail — complete suits of armour which the person wearing it drags behind him along the ground — and measure well the links’ that is in the weaving of the coats the maker of these is called sarrād. In other words make them so that the rings thereof are arranged properly. And act O family of David together with him righteously. Indeed I am Seer of what you do and will requite you for it accordingly.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of making full-length armour?
How should one make long coats of mail?
What will be the consequence of acting righteously?
propositions: Make full-length armour, balancing the links.
Work righteousness O family of David.
I am All-Seeing of what you do.

source_text:
Verse: And to Solomon ˹We subjected˺ the wind: its morning stride was a month’s journey and so was its evening stride. And We caused a stream of molten copper to flow for him, and ˹We subjected˺ some of the jinn to work under him by his Lord’s Will. And whoever of them deviated from Our command, We made them taste the torment of the blaze.

Tafsir: And We disposed for Solomon the wind the nominative reading of al-rīhu would be based on an implicit missing verb sakhkharnā ‘We disposed’ its morning course meaning its journey from the morning to the noon was a month’s journey and its evening course that is its journey from the noon to sunset was a month’s journey. And We caused a fount of molten copper to flow for him in other words We caused the copper to melt for him and so the fount flowed for three days and nights like water and to this day people have been using of that copper which was given to Solomon at that time. And of the jinn there were those who worked before him by the leave by the command of his Lord. And such of them as deviated from Our command to him to obey him Solomon We would make them taste the chastisement of the Blaze the Fire in the Hereafter — but it is also said that their chastisement was in this world in which case an angel would smite one of them with a lash thereof that would scorch him.

hype_questions: What was the duration of Solomon's morning and evening strides?
How long did the stream of molten copper flow for Solomon?
What happened to those jinn who deviated from Solomon's command?
propositions: We disposed the wind for Solomon.
The morning stride of the wind was a month’s journey.
The evening stride of the wind was a month’s journey.
We caused a fount of molten copper to flow for Solomon.
People have been using the copper given to Solomon since that time.
Some jinn worked under Solomon by his Lord's command.
Those who deviated from Our command were made to taste the torment of the blaze.

source_text:
Verse: They made for him whatever he desired of sanctuaries, statues, basins as large as reservoirs, and cooking pots fixed ˹into the ground˺. ˹We ordered:˺ “Work gratefully, O  family of David!” ˹Only˺ a few of My servants are ˹truly˺ grateful.

Tafsir: They fashioned for him whatever he wished lofty shrines mahārīb are high edifices which are ascended by stairs and statues tamāthīl is the plural of timthāl which is any thing which you fashion as a likeness of another in other words brass crystal or marble figures — the use of figures was not prohibited according to his Law; and basins jifān is the plural of jafna like cisterns jawābin is the plural of jābiya which is a large basin — around each ‘basin’ a thousand men would gather to eat — and cauldrons built into the ground fixed with foundations and cannot be moved from their places these were made from the rocks of the mountains of Yemen and to which one ascended by climbing up a ladder. And We said ‘Work O House of David in obedience to God in thankfulness to Him for what He has given you. And few indeed of My servants are thankful’ labouring in obedience to Me in thanks for My favours.

hype_questions: What is the significance of gratitude in Islam?
How does obedience to God bring about thankfulness?
What are some ways to cultivate a sense of thankfulness in daily life?
propositions: God fashioned for David whatever he desired, including lofty shrines, statues, basins, and cooking pots.
God ordered the House of David to work gratefully and in obedience to Him.
Few of God's servants are truly grateful and labor in obedience to Him.

source_text:
Verse: When We decreed Solomon’s death, nothing indicated to the ˹subjected˺ jinn that he was dead except the termites eating away his staff. So when he collapsed, the jinn realized that if they had ˹really˺ known the unseen, they would not have remained in ˹such˺ humiliating servitude.

Tafsir: And when We decreed for him for Solomon death in other words when he died — he remained supported against his staff an entire year while the jinn continued to toil in hard labour as was customary unaware of his death until finally when a termite ate through his staff he fell to the ground and was seen to be dead — nothing indicated to them that he had died except a termite al-ard is the verbal noun from uridat al-khashaba passive verbal form in other words ‘it the piece of wood was eaten away by a termite al-arada’ that gnawed away at his staff read minsa’atahu or minsātahu replacing the hamza with an alif meaning a ‘staff’ so called because when describing it one would say yunsa’u bihā to mean it is used to repel or drive away creatures’. And when he fell down dead the jinn realised it became apparent to them that an is softened in other words annahum had they known the Unseen — comprising what was hidden from them in the way of Solomon being dead — they would not have continued in the humiliating chastisement in that hard labour of theirs in which they continued as they supposed him to be alive which is in contrast to what they would have supposed had they known the Unseen and the fact that he had been there an entire year judging by how much of the staff the termite had eaten through after his death; in other words they would not have continued in the humiliating chastisement for a single day or even a single night longer.

hype_questions: Would the jinn have continued in their humiliating servitude if they had known Solomon was dead?
How would the jinn's perception of Solomon change if they knew about the Unseen?
What would happen to the jinn if they were aware of Solomon's death?
propositions: When Solomon died, nothing indicated to the jinn that he was dead except for a termite eating away his staff.
The jinn continued in their hard labour unaware of Solomon's death until a termite ate through his staff.
If the jinn had known the Unseen, they would not have continued in their humiliating servitude.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, there was a sign for ˹the tribe of˺ Sheba in their homeland: two orchards—one to the right and the other to the left. ˹They were told:˺ “Eat from the provision of your Lord, and be grateful to Him. ˹Yours is˺ a good land and a forgiving Lord.”

Tafsir: Verily there was for Sheba Saba’ declined as li-Saba’in or left as indeclinable li-Saba’a is the name of a tribe that took its name from one of their Arab ancestors in their dwelling-place in Yemen a sign indicating God’s power exalted be He two gardens jannatān a substitution for āyatun ‘a sign’ to the right and to the left in other words on the right side of their valley and on its left side. And it was said to them ‘Eat of your Lord’s provision and give thanks to Him for the graces He has bestowed on you in the land of Sheba. A good land — in which there was no dung gnats flies fleas scorpions or snakes and in which when a stranger passed through with his clothes lice-infected these lice would be killed off because of the purity of its air — and God is a forgiving Lord.’

hype_questions: What is the name of the tribe that took its name from one of their Arab ancestors in Yemen?
What was the condition of the land of Sheba, where there were no pests or diseases?
What is the nature of God's forgiveness?
propositions: There was a sign for the tribe of Sheba in their homeland: two orchards—one to the right and the other to the left.
God told them to eat from His provision and be grateful to Him.
Sheba had a good land with no pests or diseases, where God's air would kill off lice on any stranger who passed through.
God is a forgiving Lord.

source_text:
Verse: But they turned away. So We sent against them a devastating flood, and replaced their orchards with two others producing bitter fruit, fruitless bushes,

Tafsir: But they were disregardful of giving thanks to Him and became disbelievers so We unleashed upon them the flood of the Dam al-‘arim is the plural of ‘arima which is a structure or something similar that holds water back to be stored for when it is needed in other words We unleashed upon them the flood-waters of their valley which had been held back by the mentioned structure so that they engulfed their two gardens together with all their property. And We gave them in place of their two gardens two gardens bearing dhawātay a dual form of feminine plural dhawāt; usually the form dhātay from the singular would have been used bitter fruit bitter and vile ukul may be read as a genitive annexation ukulin khamtin in the sense of ‘that which is eaten thereof being bitter; or it may be read without as ukuli khamtin; and this phrase is supplemented by the following wa-athlin wa-shay’in min sidrin qalīl and tamarisk and sparse lote trees.

hype_questions: What happens when people disobey Allah?
How did the flood affect the gardens of the disbelievers?
What kind of fruit did the two new gardens produce?
propositions: They turned away from giving thanks to Allah.
We sent a devastating flood against them.
Their orchards were replaced with two others producing bitter fruit and fruitless bushes.
The flood-waters engulfed their two gardens and all their property.
We gave them in place of their two gardens two gardens bearing bitter fruit and vile ukul.

source_text:
Verse: This is how We rewarded them for their ingratitude. Would We ever punish ˹anyone in such a way˺ except the ungrateful?

Tafsir: That replacement of what they had is what We requited them with for their ingratitude and is anyone but the ingrate ever so requited? read hal yujāzā illā’l-kafūru; or read as hal nujāzī illā’l-kafūra ‘Would We requite anyone but the ingrate?’ in other words it is only the like of such who is called to account.

hype_questions: Will We ever punish anyone for their ingratitude?
Is it only the ungrateful who will be requited?
Who is called to account for their actions?
propositions: We rewarded them for their ingratitude.
Anyone but the ingrate would not be punished in such a way.
It is only the like of such who is called to account.

source_text:
Verse: We had also placed between them and the cities We showered with blessings ˹many small˺ towns within sight of one another. And We set moderate travel distances in between, ˹saying,˺ “Travel between them by day and night safely.”

Tafsir: And We set between them between Sheba who were in Yemen and the towns which We had blessed with abundance of water and trees — these being the towns of Syria to which they used to travel for commerce — prominent towns continuous along the route from Yemen to Syria and We facilitated for travellers the journeying through them such that they would rest for the afternoon in one and spend the night in the next and so on until the end of their travel having no need of any supplies or water along the way; and We said ‘Travel through them night and day safely’ having no fear by night or by day.

hype_questions: What are the benefits of traveling through these blessed towns?
How did Allah facilitate travel for traders between Yemen and Syria?
What is the significance of resting in one town and continuing on to the next?
propositions: We placed small towns between Sheba and the cities, showering them with blessings.
We set moderate travel distances between these towns, allowing safe passage by day and night.
These blessed towns provided abundant water and trees, making them ideal for commerce.
Allah facilitated travel through these towns, enabling traders to rest in one town and continue on to the next without needing supplies or water.
Traveling through these towns is safe at all times, day and night.

source_text:
Verse: But they said, “Our Lord! Make ˹the distances of˺ our journeys longer,” wronging themselves. So We reduced them to ˹cautionary˺ tales, and scattered them utterly. Surely in this are lessons for whoever is steadfast, grateful.

Tafsir: But they said ‘Our Lord make far apart ba‘‘id a variant reading has bā‘id the stages of our travel’ to Syria make these stages through deserts so that they could glory before the poor in riding their camels and bearing their supplies and water and so they behaved wantonly with the graces bestowed on them by God and they wronged their souls through disbelief and so We made them bywords of wrongdoing in this respect for those who came after them and We caused them to disintegrate totally We scattered them all over the lands. Surely in that which is mentioned there are signs lessons for every servant who is steadfast in refraining from acts of disobedience grateful for God’s graces.

hype_questions: What happens when one disobeys God's will?
How does gratitude impact a person's spiritual growth?
What is the importance of steadfastness in avoiding disobedience?
propositions: The Prophet Muhammad and his companions were sent to guide the people of Syria.
God tests His servants by sending them on journeys through deserts.
Those who disobey God's will are punished in this life and the next.
Gratitude is a key aspect of spiritual growth.
Steadfastness in refraining from acts of disobedience is essential for a person's spiritual well-being.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Iblis’ assumption about them has come true, so they ˹all˺ follow him, except a group of ˹true˺ believers.

Tafsir: And verily Iblīs proved true read sadaqa or saddaqa his opinion of them that is of the disbelievers among them — the folk of Sheba — which was that by his tempting them to go astray they would follow him. So they followed him if the verb above is read sadaqa this would mean that ‘he was right in his opinion’ and if read saddaqa it would mean that ‘he found this opinion of his to be true’ — all except a group of the believers mina’l-mu’minīna the min ‘of’ is explicative not partitive in other words all except that group who were the believers they did not follow him.

hype_questions: Does Iblis' opinion about the people of Sheba being disbelievers hold true?
Can tempting someone to go astray guarantee they will follow Iblis?
Are there any believers among the people of Sheba?
propositions: Iblis assumed that the people of Sheba were disbelievers.
The people of Sheba followed Iblis because he tempted them to go astray.
There is a group of believers among the people of Sheba who did not follow Iblis.

source_text:
Verse: He does not have any authority over them, but ˹Our Will is˺ only to distinguish those who believe in the Hereafter from those who are in doubt about it. And your Lord is a ˹vigilant˺ Keeper over all things.”

Tafsir: And he did not have any warrant over them any power to sway them from Us but that We might know by this knowledge being made manifest him who believed in the Hereafter from him who was in doubt thereof and so requite each of the two accordingly. And your Lord is Preserver Watcher of all things.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are certain about the Hereafter?
How does one's belief in the Hereafter affect their fate?
Who is rewarded for their faith in the Hereafter?
propositions: He does not have any authority over them.
Our Will is only to distinguish those who believe in the Hereafter from those who are in doubt about it.
Your Lord is a vigilant Keeper over all things.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Call upon those you claim ˹to be divine˺ besides Allah. They do not possess ˹even˺ an atom’s weight either in the heavens or the earth, nor do they have any share in ˹governing˺ them. Nor is any of them a helper to Him.”

Tafsir: Say O Muhammad (s) to the disbelievers of Mecca ‘Call on those whom you have asserted those whom you have asserted to be gods besides God in other words other than Him so that they might benefit you as you are wont to assert. God exalted be He says of them They do not possess even so much as the weight of an atom of good or evil in the heavens or in the earth and they do not have any share in either of them nor has He exalted be He among them the gods any auxiliary’ anyone required as His helper.

hype_questions: What happens to those who claim to be gods besides Allah?
Do they have any share in governing the universe?
Can they provide any benefit to humans?
propositions: Those who claim to be gods besides Allah do not possess even an atom's weight.
They do not have any share in governing the heavens or the earth.
No one of them is a helper to Allah.

source_text:
Verse: No intercession will be of any benefit with Him, except by those granted permission by Him. ˹At last,˺ when the dread ˹of Judgment Day˺ is relieved from their hearts ˹because they are permitted to intercede˺, they will ˹excitedly˺ ask ˹the angels˺, “What has your Lord ˹just˺ said?” The angels will reply, “The truth! And He is the Most High, All-Great.”

Tafsir: And intercession will not avail with Him exalted be He — this was in response to their saying that their gods would intercede for them with Him — except for him to whom leave is given in this respect read adhina ‘to whom He gives leave’; or udhina ‘to whom leave is given’. Yet when fear is banished from their hearts read active fazza‘a or passive fuzzi‘a when fear is removed from them upon leave being given for this intercession they will say — some will say to others in anticipation of a favourable outcome — ‘What has your Lord said?’ concerning this. They will say He has said the saying that is ‘The truth’ in other words leave has been given for it. And He is the Exalted above His creation by His subjugation of them the Great the Tremendous.

hype_questions: What has your Lord just said?
Will intercession be of any benefit with Him?
What is the truth that He has revealed?
propositions: No intercession will be of any benefit with Him, except by those granted permission by Him.
Intercession will not avail with Him exalted be He — this was in response to their saying that their gods would intercede for them with Him —
He has said the saying that is ‘The truth’ in other words leave has been given for it.

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?” Say, “Allah! Now, certainly one of our two groups is ˹rightly˺ guided; the other is clearly astray.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Who provides for you from the heavens rain and from the earth?’ vegetation. Say ‘God!’ — even if they do not say it there is no other valid answer. And indeed either we or you are — in other words either one of the two parties is — rightly guided or in manifest error. The ambiguity here concerning which of the two is rightly guided is intended as a gentle invitation for them to embrace faith if their way to it is facilitated by God.

hype_questions: What is the source of our sustenance from heaven and earth?
How do we receive blessings from God?
Is one group more guided than another?
propositions: Allah provides for us from the heavens and the earth.
One party is rightly guided, while the other is clearly astray.
Either we or our companion are guided by God.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “You will not be accountable for our misdeeds, nor will we be accountable for your deeds.”

Tafsir: Say ‘You will not be questioned about the sins we committed nor shall we be questioned about what you do’ for we are quit of you.

hype_questions: Will I be held accountable for my past mistakes?
Can I be blamed for someone else's wrongdoings?
What happens to me after I die?
propositions: You will not be held accountable for the sins committed by others.
You will not be questioned about your actions if you are no longer accountable for them.
You are quit of someone else's wrongdoings.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us with the truth. For He is the All-Knowing Judge.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Our Lord will bring us together on the Day of Resurrection then He will judge between us with truth and He will admit the truthful into Paradise and the liars into the Fire. And He is the Judge the Knowing’ in what He judges.

hype_questions: What will be the outcome for those who tell the truth on Judgment Day?
How will Allah judge between us on the Day of Resurrection?
Will liars be admitted to Paradise or Hell?
propositions: Our Lord will gather us together.
He will judge between us with the truth.
The truthful will be admitted into Paradise, and the liars into the Fire.
Allah is the All-Knowing Judge.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “Show me those ˹idols˺ you have joined with Him as partners. No! In fact, He ˹alone˺ is Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Show me apprise me of those whom you have joined to Him as associates in worship. No indeed! — this is meant to deter them from even supposing that He has an associate. Rather He is God the Mighty Whose way will prevail the Wise’ in the way in which He manages the affairs of His creation and so He could not have any associate in His kingdom.

hype_questions: Does Allah have an associate?
What is the nature of Allah's kingdom?
How does Allah manage the affairs of His creation?
propositions: Allah has no associates.
The way of Allah will prevail.
Allah manages the affairs of His creation.

source_text:
Verse: We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ only as a deliverer of good news and a warner to all of humanity, but most people do not know.

Tafsir: And We did not send you except to all kāffatan is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-nās ‘mankind’ and is made to precede li’l-nās because of the importance attached to it of mankind both as a bearer of good tidings to believers of Paradise and a warner to the disbelievers of chastisement but most people such as the disbelievers of Mecca do not know this.

hype_questions: What is the role of a prophet in delivering good news and warning humanity?
How do most people respond to the message of a prophet?
What is the significance of mankind as a bearer of good tidings and a warner?
propositions: We sent you as a deliverer of good news and a warner to all of humanity.
The importance of mankind is emphasized due to its role in receiving good tidings and facing chastisement.
Most people, including disbelievers, do not know the significance of mankind.

source_text:
Verse: And they ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”

Tafsir: And they say ‘When shall this promise of chastisement be fulfilled if you are being truthful?’ concerning it.

hype_questions: When will the threat come to pass?
When shall this promise of chastisement be fulfilled?
If what you say is true?
propositions: This threat will come to pass.
The promise of chastisement will be fulfilled if you are being truthful.
You say that this threat will come to pass.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “A Day has ˹already˺ been appointed for you, which you can neither delay nor advance by a ˹single˺ moment.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Yours is the tryst of a Day which you can neither defer nor advance by a single hour’ and this is the Day of Resurrection.

hype_questions: What happens when we die?
Can we change our fate?
What is the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: A Day has been appointed for you.
You can neither delay nor advance this Day by a single moment.
This is the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers vow, “We will never believe in this Quran, nor in those ˹Scriptures˺ before it.” If only you could see when the wrongdoers will be detained before their Lord, throwing blame at each other! The lowly ˹followers˺ will say to the arrogant ˹leaders˺, “Had it not been for you, we would certainly have been believers.”

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve from among the people of Mecca say ‘We will not believe in this Qur’ān nor in that which was revealed before it’ — in other words what preceded it such as the Torah and the Gospel both of which contain proofs of the Resurrection — because they reject the truth of this last. God exalted be He says of them But if you were to see O Muhammad (s) when the evildoers the disbelievers are brought to stand before their Lord bandying arguments against one another. Those who were oppressed — the followers — will say to those who were arrogant — the leaders ‘Had it not been for you barring us from faith we would have been believers’ in the Prophet.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the truth of the Resurrection?
How do the oppressed respond to the arrogant leaders when brought before their Lord?
Would the followers have been believers if not for the actions of the arrogant leaders?
propositions: The disbelievers vow that they will never believe in the Qur'ān or previous scriptures.
God exalted be He says that if you could see, the evildoers and disbelievers would be brought to stand before their Lord, throwing blame at each other.
Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, 'Had it not been for you, barring us from faith, we would have been believers.'

source_text:
Verse: The arrogant will respond to the lowly, “Did we ever hinder you from guidance after it came to you? In fact, you were wicked ˹on your own˺.”

Tafsir: Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed ‘Was it us who barred you from guidance after it had come to you? Nay! Rather you were guilty’ of your own accord.

hype_questions: Can arrogance lead to missed opportunities for guidance?
How does personal guilt affect one's relationship with guidance?
What is the role of individual responsibility in seeking guidance?
propositions: The arrogant will respond to the lowly, “Did we ever hinder you from guidance after it came to you?”
Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed ‘Was it us who barred you from guidance after it had come to you?’
Nay! Rather you were guilty’ of your own accord.

source_text:
Verse: The lowly will say to the arrogant, “No! It was your plotting by day and night—when you ordered us to disbelieve in Allah and to set up equals with Him.” They will ˹all˺ hide ˹their˺ remorse when they see the torment. And We will put shackles around the necks of the disbelievers. Will they be rewarded except for what they used to do?

Tafsir: And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant ‘Nay but it was your scheming night and day in other words such were your schemes against us during both of these times when you used to command us to disbelieve in God and set up partners with Him’. And they that is the two parties will conceal their remorse for not having believed in Him when they see the chastisement in other words each person will hide it his remorse from the next for fear of being reviled; and We will place fetters around the necks of the disbelievers while they are in the Fire. Shall they be requited except the requital for what they used to do? in the world.

hype_questions: Will those who disbelieve be rewarded except for what they used to do?
What is the consequence of plotting against Allah and setting up equals with Him?
How will those who were oppressed react when they see the torment?
propositions: The lowly will say to the arrogant, 'No! It was your plotting by day and night—when you ordered us to disbelieve in Allah and to set up equals with Him.'
And We will put shackles around the necks of the disbelievers.
Will they be rewarded except for what they used to do?

Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant 'Nay but it was your scheming night and day in other words such were your schemes against us during both of these times when you used to command us to disbelieve in God and set up partners with Him'.

And they that is the two parties will conceal their remorse for not having believed in Him when they see the chastisement in other words each person will hide it his remorse from the next for fear of being reviled;
Shall they be requited except the requital for what they used to do?

source_text:
Verse: Whenever We sent a warner to a society, its elite would say, “We truly reject what you have been sent with.”

Tafsir: And We did not send a warner to any town without its affluent ones its leaders those enjoying life’s comforts saying ‘Indeed we disbelieve in that Message with which you have been sent’.

hype_questions: What happens when a society rejects the message sent by God?
Why do elite leaders often disbelieve in divine messages?
How does God respond to societies that reject His warnings?
propositions: Whenever We sent a warner to a society, its elite would say, 'We truly reject what you have been sent with.'
We did not send a warner to any town without its affluent ones, its leaders, those enjoying life's comforts saying 'Indeed we disbelieve in that Message with which you have been sent'.

source_text:
Verse: Adding, “We are far superior ˹to the believers˺ in wealth and children, and we will never be punished.”

Tafsir: And they say ‘We possess more wealth and children than those who are believers and we shall not be chastised’.

hype_questions: Can having more wealth and children guarantee salvation?
Is it possible to be punished for one's actions in this life?
What is the nature of the relationship between material possessions and spiritual reward?
propositions: We possess more wealth and children than those who are believers.
They say we shall not be chastised for our actions.
We are far superior to the believers in wealth and children.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely ˹it is˺ my Lord ˹Who˺ gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills. But most people do not know.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Truly my Lord extends provision He makes it abundant for whomever He will as a test and restricts it for whomever He will to try them but most people such as the disbelievers of Mecca do not know’ this truth.

hype_questions: Does Allah provide for whoever He wills?
What is the purpose of Allah's provision?
Can humans truly understand Allah's plans?
propositions: Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills.
Most people do not know that Allah provides provisions as a test and restricts them for whomever He wills.

source_text:
Verse: It is not your wealth or children that bring you closer to Us. But those who believe and do good—it is they who will have a multiplied reward for what they did, and they will be secure in ˹elevated˺ mansions.

Tafsir: Nor is it your wealth or your children that will bring you near to Us in closeness except for but it is those who believe and act righteously those they shall have a twofold reward for what they did in other words they shall have it as the reward of their action — as a good deed for example is rewarded tenfold or more — and they shall be in the lofty abodes of Paradise secure from death and otherwise a variant reading for al-ghurufāt is al-ghurfa the generic noun implying a plural.

hype_questions: What is the true source of closeness to Allah?
How does one achieve a multiplied reward for their actions?
What are the characteristics of those who will be secure in the lofty abodes of Paradise?
propositions: It is not wealth or children that bring you closer to Us.
Belief and righteous action lead to a twofold reward for one's deeds.
Those who believe and act righteously shall have a multiplied reward, and be secure in the lofty abodes of Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who strive to discredit Our revelations, it is they who will be confined in punishment.

Tafsir: And those who strive against Our signs namely the Qur’ān seeking to invalidate it supposing Us to be inomnipotent — or supposing that they can elude Us — those they will be arraigned into the chastisement.

hype_questions: Can anyone truly discredit the Qur'ān?
What happens to those who try to invalidate the message of God?
Is it possible to elude God's punishment?
propositions: Those who strive to discredit Our revelations will be confined in punishment.
Those who seek to invalidate the Qur'ān, assuming Us to be inomnipotent or that they can elude Us, will be arraigned into chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely ˹it is˺ my Lord ˹Who˺ gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills of His servants. And whatever you spend in charity, He will compensate ˹you˺ for it. For He is the Best Provider.”

Tafsir: Say ‘My Lord extends provision He makes it abundant for whomever He will of His servants as a test and restricts it for him after having extended it — or He restricts it for him whom He will to try and whatever thing you may expend for the cause of good He will replace it. And He is the best of providers’. It is said that every man ‘provides for’ his dependants yarzuqu ‘ā’ilatahu meaning that he does so from the provision given to him by God.

hype_questions: Does Allah provide for His servants?
Can Allah compensate us for our charitable spending?
What is the purpose of Allah's provision?
propositions: Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills of His servants.
Whatever you spend in charity, Allah will compensate you for it.
Allah extends provision and restricts it as a test.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹consider˺ the Day He will gather them all together, and then ask the angels, “Was it you that these ˹polytheists˺ used to worship?”

Tafsir: And mention on the Day when He will gather them all together namely all the idolaters He will say to the angels ‘Was it these who used to worship you?’ read a-hā’ūlā’i iyyākum pronouncing both hamzas or by replacing the first with a yā’ or dropping it altogether.

hype_questions: Will the angels be held accountable for the worship of polytheists?
What will the angels say when asked about the worship of polytheists?
Who will be responsible for the worship of polytheists?
propositions: He will gather them all together.
The idolaters used to worship you.
Was it these who used to worship you?

source_text:
Verse: They will say, “Glory be to You! Our loyalty is to You, not them. In fact, they ˹only˺ followed the ˹temptations of evil˺ jinn, in whom most of them had faith.”

Tafsir: They will say ‘Glory be to You exalted above that You should have an associate! You are our Supporter not they in other words as far as we are concerned there are no bonds of association between us and them. Nay bal is to indicate transition rather they used to worship the jinn the devils in other words they used to obey them and agree to worship us; most of them were believers in them’ accepting as truth what these jinn used to say to them.

Our loyalty is to You, not them.

source_text:
Verse: So Today neither of you can benefit or protect each other. And We will say to the wrongdoers, “Taste the torment of the Fire, which you used to deny.”

Tafsir: God exalted be He says ‘So today none among you has any power over another in other words none of those worshipped have any power over any of those who worshipped either to benefit through intercession or to hurt’ through chastisement. And We shall say to those who did wrong who disbelieved ‘Taste the chastisement of the Fire which you used to deny!’

hype_questions: What happens when one person tries to benefit another through intercession?
Can those who worshiped God hurt or benefit each other?

source_text:
Verse: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, they say, “This is only a man who wishes to hinder you from what your forefathers used to worship.” They also say, “This ˹Quran˺ is no more than a fabricated lie.” And the disbelievers say of the truth when it has come to them, “This is nothing but pure magic.”

Tafsir: And when Our signs from the Qur’ān are recited to them being clear signs evident ones by the tongue of our Prophet Muhammad (s) they say ‘This is just a man who desires to bar you from worshipping what your fathers used to worship’ of idols. And they say ‘This Qur’ān is nothing but a calumny a lie that has been invented against God. And those who disbelieve say to the truth the Qur’ān when it comes to them ‘This is nothing but plain sorcery’. God exalted be He says

hype_questions: Does the Quran contain fabricated lies about God?

Is the Quran a calumny against God?

They say, 'This is only a man who wishes to hinder you from what your forefathers used to worship.'
The disbelievers say of the truth when it has come to them, 'This is nothing but pure magic.'

source_text:
Verse: ˹They say so even though˺ We had never given them any scriptures to study, nor did We ever send them a warner before you ˹O Prophet˺.

propositions: We had never given them any scriptures to study.

source_text:
Verse: Those ˹destroyed˺ before them denied as well—and these ˹Meccans˺ have not attained even one-tenth of what We had given their predecessors. Yet ˹when˺ they denied My messengers, how severe was My response!

Tafsir: And those who were before them also denied and they these ones the Meccans have not received even a tenth of what We gave those others in the way of might long life and abundance of wealth. Yet they denied My messengers who were sent to them so how was My abhorrence! so how was My rebuttal against them through punishment and destruction in other words it was appropriate.

hype_questions: What happens when people deny the messengers of God?

The Meccans have not received even a tenth of what was given to their predecessors.
My messengers were sent to them, and they denied them.
My abhorrence is towards those who deny My messengers.
My rebuttal against them was through punishment and destruction.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I advise you to do ˹only˺ one thing: stand up for ˹the sake of˺ Allah—individually or in pairs—then reflect. Your fellow man is not insane. He is only a warner to you before ˹the coming of˺ a severe punishment.”

Tafsir: Say ‘I will give you just one piece of admonition namely that you rise up for God in other words for His sake in twos and individually and then reflect and realise that there is no madness in your companion Muhammad (s). He is just a warner to you before the befalling of a severe chastisement’ in the Hereafter if you disobey him.

hype_questions: What is the one thing that Allah advises us to do?

What happens if we disobey our companion Muhammad (s)?
propositions: Stand up for Allah individually or in pairs.

Your fellow man is not insane, but a warner before a severe punishment.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “If I had ever asked you for a reward, you could keep it. My reward is only from Allah. And He is a Witness over all things.”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘I have not asked you in return for my warning and delivering the Message to you any reward since it is for the benefit of you in other words I do not ask you for any reward in return for this. Indeed my reward lies only with God and He is Witness over all things’ observing them all knowing my truthfulness.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the reward mentioned in this verse?

propositions: If I had ever asked you for a reward, you could keep it.
My reward is only from Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “Surely my Lord hurls the truth ˹against falsehood˺. ˹He is˺ the Knower of all unseen.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Indeed my Lord hurls the truth He casts it onto His prophets — He is the Knower of the Unseen’ of all that is hidden from His creatures throughout the heavens and the earth.

hype_questions: Does God cast truth onto His prophets?

How does God relate to the hidden aspects of creation?

The truth is cast onto His prophets.
God is the Knower of all unseen.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “The truth has come, and falsehood will vanish, never to return.”

Tafsir: Say ‘The truth Islam has come. And falsehood disbelief neither originates nor restores anything’ in other words it leaves no trace of itself behind.

hype_questions: What happens to falsehood after the truth has come?

source_text:
Verse: Say, “If I am astray, the loss is only mine. And if I am guided, it is ˹only˺ because of what my Lord reveals to me. He is indeed All-Hearing, Ever Near.”

Tafsir: Say ‘If I go astray from the truth I will be going astray only to my own loss that is to say the sin of my going astray shall be held against me; and if I am rightly guided it will have been by what my Lord reveals to me of the Qur’ān and wisdom. Truly He is Hearer of supplications Nigh’.

source_text:
Verse: If only you could see when they will be horrified with no escape ˹on Judgment Day˺! And they will be seized from a nearby place.

Tafsir: If you could but see O Muhammad (s) when they are stricken with terror at the Resurrection you would see a dreadful thing and so there is no escape for them from Us that is to say they will not be able to elude Us and they are seized from a close quarter namely from the graves.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who are horrified on Judgment Day?

source_text:
Verse: They will ˹then˺ cry, “We do ˹now˺ believe in it ˹all˺.” But how could they ˹possibly˺ attain faith from a place so far-off ˹from the world˺,

Tafsir: And they will say ‘We believe in him now’ in other words in Muhammad (s) — or if read ‘We believe in it’ then in the Qur’ān. But how can they attain it read tanāwush or tanā’ush that is attain faith from a place that is far away from the place for attaining it — as they are now in the Hereafter and the proper place for attaining it was in this world —

hype_questions: Can one attain faith from a place far away from the world?

They will say 'We believe in him now' meaning Muhammad (s) or Qur'ān.
They cannot attain faith from a place far away from the world.

source_text:
Verse: while they had already rejected it before, guessing blindly from a place ˹equally˺ far-away ˹from the Hereafter˺?

Tafsir: when they disbelieved in it before? in this world. And they throw guesses at the Unseen from a far-off place in other words they make guesses about something the knowledge of which was hidden far away from them as when they would say that the Prophet was a sorcerer or a poet or a soothsayer or that the Qur’ān was sorcery poetry or soothsaying.

source_text:
Verse: They will be sealed off from whatever they desire, as was done to their counterparts before. Indeed, they were ˹all˺ in alarming doubt.

Tafsir: And a barrier is set between them and what they crave in the way of faith — in other words their craving to embrace it — just as was done with their counterparts in respect to disbelief formerly in other words before them. A barrier is set between them and what they crave in the way of faith.
Indeed, they were in alarming doubt.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever mercy Allah opens up for people, none can withhold it. And whatever He withholds, none but Him can release it. For He is the Almighty, All-Wise.
