source_text:
Verse: O humanity! Remember Allah’s favours upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. How can you then be deluded ˹from the truth˺?

Tafsir: O people that is the people of Mecca remember God’s grace to you in His making you dwell within the Meccan Sanctuary and preventing raids against you. Is there any creator min khāliqin min is extra; khāliq is the subject other than God read ghayru’Llāhi or gharyri’Llāhi as an adjectival qualification of khāliq ‘creator’ either concording with the oblique form of min khāliqin or concording with the syntactical status thereof; the predicate of the subject is the following who provides for you from the heaven rain and from the earth? vegetation the interrogative is actually an affirmative that is to say ‘there is no creator or provider other than Him. There is no god except Him. So how then do you deviate? how are you turned away from affirming His Oneness when you already affirm that He is the Creator and the Provider?

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's creation?
How does Allah provide for humanity?
Why do humans deviate from affirming Allah's Oneness?
propositions: Allah is the creator and provider of humanity.
There is no god worthy of worship except Allah.

source_text:
Verse: If you are rejected by them, so too were messengers before you. And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺.

Tafsir: And if they deny you O Muhammad (s) with regard to your coming with the message of God’s Oneness resurrection reckoning and punishment verily other messengers before you were denied in this respect so be steadfast as they were steadfast; and to God all matters are returned in the Hereafter when He will requite the deniers and grant victory to the messengers.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the messengers of God?
How will Allah judge those who deny His message?

And to Allah matters will be returned for judgment.
Other messengers before you were denied in this respect.
So be steadfast as they were steadfast;
Verily other messengers before you were denied in this respect
so be steadfast as they were steadfast;
and to God all matters are returned in the Hereafter when He will requite the deniers and grant victory to the messengers.

source_text:
Verse: O humanity! Indeed, Allah’s promise is true. So do not let the life of this world deceive you, nor let the Chief Deceiver deceive you about Allah.

Tafsir: O mankind! Indeed God’s promise of resurrection and of other issues is true. So do not let the life of this world deceive you from believing in all of that and do not let the Deceiver Satan deceive you concerning God on account of His forbearance and respiting of sinners in this life.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's promise?

The life of this world cannot deceive you from believing in Allah's resurrection and other issues.
Satan deceives people concerning God due to His forbearance and respiting of sinners in this life.

source_text:
Verse: Surely Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his followers to become inmates of the Blaze.

Tafsir: Truly Satan is an enemy to you. So treat him as an enemy by being obedient to God and do not obey him; he only summons his faction his followers in disbelief so that they may be among the inhabitants of the Blaze the fierce Fire.

hype_questions: What happens if you obey Satan?

source_text:
Verse: Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment. But those who believe and do good will have forgiveness and a great reward.

Tafsir: Those who disbelieve theirs will be a severe chastisement; but those who believe and perform righteous deeds theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward — this is a declaration of what fate will be for the adherents of Satan and what will be for his opponents respectively.

hype_questions: What happens to those who disbelieve?
How do believers receive forgiveness and a great reward?
What is the fate of Satan's followers compared to his opponents?
propositions: Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment.
Those who believe and do good will have forgiveness and a great reward.
Believers perform righteous deeds for forgiveness and a great reward.

source_text:
Verse: Are those whose evil-doing is made so appealing to them that they deem it good ˹like those who are rightly guided˺? ˹It is˺ certainly Allah ˹Who˺ leaves to stray whoever He wills, and guides whoever He wills. So do not grieve yourself to death over them ˹O Prophet˺. Surely Allah is All-Knowing of what they do.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding Abū Jahl and others Is he the evil of whose deeds is made to seem fair to him by distortion so that he deems it good …? a-fa-man ‘is he whose’ constitutes the subject the predicate of which is an omitted ‘like one whom God has guided?’ No! And this predicate is indicated by what follows. Indeed God leads astray whomever He will and guides whomever He will. So do not let your soul expire for their sake for those to whom it has made to seem fair out of sighings by becoming anguished lest they do not believe. Indeed God is Knower of what they do and He will requite them for it.

hype_questions: Does Allah guide those who are misled by their own desires?
Can humans truly believe if they are being swayed by false appearances?
Will Allah hold individuals accountable for the choices they make?
propositions: Allah leaves to stray whoever He wills.
Allah guides whoever He wills.
God is Knower of what they do and He will requite them for it.

source_text:
Verse: And it is Allah Who sends the winds, which then stir up ˹vapour, forming˺ clouds, and then We drive them to a lifeless land, giving life to the earth after its death. Similar is the Resurrection.

Tafsir: And it is God Who unleashes the winds al-riyāha a variant reading has al-rīha and they raise clouds fa-tuthīru’l-sahāba the imperfect tense here is used to narrate the past that is they stir them up then We drive them there is a shift here from the third person to the first person address to a dead land read mayyitin or maytin wherein is no plant life and therewith revive the earth of that land after it has been dead after its having been dried-out. In other words We made seeds and grass grow in it Such will be the Raising that is the Resurrection and the bringing of the dead back to life.

hype_questions: What is the process of creation in Islam?
How does Allah bring life to a dead land?
What will happen to the earth after death?
propositions: Allah sends the winds which stir up vapour forming clouds.
We drive the winds to a lifeless land giving life to the earth after its death.
The Resurrection is similar to this process of bringing life to a dead land.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever seeks honour and power, then ˹let them know that˺ all honour and power belongs to Allah. To Him ˹alone˺ good words ascend, and righteous deeds are raised up by Him. As for those who plot evil, they will suffer a severe punishment. And the plotting of such ˹people˺ is doomed ˹to fail˺.

Tafsir: Whoever desires glory should know that all glory belongs to God in this world and in the Hereafter and it cannot be obtained from Him except through obedience to Him so let such a one be obedient to Him. To Him ascends good words that is to say He is aware of such good words and these are statements such as ‘there is no god except God’ and the like; and as for righteous action He exalts it He accepts it; but those who plot evil schemes against the Prophet — as was the case at the council assembly in the way of imprisoning him killing him or expelling him as mentioned in sūrat al-Anfāl Q. 830 — theirs shall be a severe chastisement and their plotting shall come to nothing it shall be ruined.

hype_questions: What is the source of true glory?
How can one attain righteousness and avoid evil plotting?
What consequences will those who plot against the Prophet face?
propositions: All honour and power belongs to Allah.
Good words ascend to Allah, and righteous deeds are raised up by Him.
Those who plot evil schemes against the Prophet shall suffer a severe punishment.
Obedience to Allah is the means of obtaining glory in this world and the Hereafter.
Good words that ascend to Allah include statements such as 'there is no god except God'.
Allah exalts righteous action and accepts it.
Those who plot evil schemes against the Prophet will have their plotting ruined.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹it is˺ Allah ˹Who˺ created you from dust, That is certainly easy for Allah.

Tafsir: And God created you from dust by having created your father Adam from it then from a drop of seminal fluid in other words from sperm by creating his seed from it; then He made you pairs males and females. And no female bears or brings forth except with His knowledge illā bi-‘ilmihi is a circumstantial qualifier in other words ‘except that it is known by Him’ and no long-living person is given long life in other words the life of none is increased for one who has a long life nor is anything diminished of his life in other words of the life of that same long-living person or some other long-living person but it is recorded in a Book namely the Preserved Tablet. Surely that is easy for God.

hype_questions: Does Allah have the power to create life from dust?
Is the creation of humans a straightforward process for God?
Can humans influence their lifespan?
propositions: Allah created you from dust.
Adam was created from dust by Allah.
The life of a long-living person is not increased or diminished except as recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

source_text:
Verse: The two bodies of water are not alike: one is fresh, palatable, and pleasant to drink and the other is salty and bitter. Yet from them both you eat tender seafood and extract ornaments to wear. And you see the ships ploughing their way through both, so you may seek His bounty and give thanks ˹to Him˺.

Tafsir: Nor are the two kinds of seas alike this one is extremely sweet pleasant to drink and that one is salty extremely bitter. Yet from each of the two you eat fresh meat namely fish and obtain from the salt — and it is also said from both of them — ornaments which you wear namely pearls and coral. And you see you sight the ships therein in each of the two seas ploughing through mawākhira in other words tamkhuru’l-mā’a meaning ‘it cleaves it as it makes its way through it coming and going by the same wind that you may seek of His bounty exalted be He through commerce and that perhaps you may give thanks to God for this bounty.

hype_questions: What are the two kinds of seas mentioned in the verse?
Why do we see ships ploughing through both seas?
How can we seek God's bounty and give thanks to Him?
propositions: The two bodies of water are not alike.
One sea is fresh and pleasant to drink, while the other is salty and bitter.
We eat tender seafood from both seas.
We extract ornaments such as pearls and coral from both seas.
Ships plough through both seas.
We seek God's bounty through commerce.
We give thanks to God for His bounty.

source_text:
Verse: He merges the night into the day and the day into the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each orbiting for an appointed term. That is Allah—your Lord! All authority belongs to Him. But those ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Him do not possess even the skin of a date stone.

Tafsir: He God makes the night pass enter into the day so that it becomes longer and He makes the day pass into the night so that it becomes longer and He has disposed the sun and the moon each of them moving in its course to an appointed term — to the Day of Resurrection. That is God your Lord; to Him belongs all sovereignty. As for those on whom you call whom you worship besides Him in other words other than Him — and they are the idols — they do not possess even so much as the husk of a date-stone.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's power over time?
How does Allah govern the movements of celestial bodies?
What happens to those who are worshipped besides Allah?
propositions: Allah makes the night pass into the day.
Allah makes the day pass into the night.
The sun and moon orbit on appointed terms.
All authority belongs to Allah.
Those worshipped besides Allah do not possess even the skin of a date stone.

source_text:
Verse: If you call upon them, they cannot hear your calls. And if they were to hear, they could not respond to you. On the Day of Judgment they will disown your worship ˹of them˺. And no one can inform you ˹O Prophet˺ like the All-Knowledgeable.

None can inform you about the state in the two abodes like One Who is Aware Knower and this is God exalted be He.

source_text:
Verse: No soul burdened with sin will bear the burden of another. And if a sin-burdened soul cries for help with its burden, none of it will be carried—even by a close relative. You ˹O Prophet˺ can only warn those who stand in awe of their Lord without seeing Him and establish prayer. Whoever purifies themselves, they only do so for their own good. And to Allah is the final return.

Tafsir: And no burdened soul shall bear the burden of another sinful soul. And should one soul burdened heavily with sin call for some of its burden to be borne by another nothing of it will be borne even if the one called be a relative kin such as a father or a son — the impossibility of ‘having something borne by another’ in both instances is something ordained by God. You can only warn those who fear their Lord in secret in other words those who fear Him despite not having seen Him for they are the ones to benefit from the warning and observe the prayer maintain performance of it. For whoever purifies himself cleansing himself of idolatry and other similar abominations is purifying himself only for the sake of his own soul because the reforming of his self pertains to him. And to God is the end of the journeying the return in the Hereafter when He will requite according to deeds.

God is the final return.

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Have you considered your associate-gods which you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created on earth! Or do they have a share in ˹the creation of˺ the heavens? Or have We given the polytheists a Book, which serves as a clear proof for them? In fact, the wrongdoers promise each other nothing but delusion.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Have you considered your associates on whom you call those whom you worship besides God? in other words other than God — and they are the idols whom you asserted to be partners of God exalted be He. Show me apprise me of what part of the earth they have created. Or do they have some partnership some share alongside God in the creation of the heavens?’ Or have We given them a scripture so that they are acting upon a clear proof a definitive argument therefrom? to the effect that they have some partnership with Me? Nothing of the sort! Nay but the evildoers the disbelievers promise one another nothing but delusion falsehood when they say that the idols will intercede for them.

source_text:
Verse: behaving arrogantly in the land and plotting evil. But evil plotting only backfires on those who plot. Are they awaiting anything but the fate of those ˹destroyed˺ before? You will find no change in the way of Allah, nor will you find it diverted ˹to someone else˺.

Tafsir: acting with disdain in the land against faith istikbāran fī’l-ardi an object denoting reason and devising acts of evil in the way of idolatry and otherwise; and evil schemes will beset surround only their authors namely the one who devises such evil the qualifying of makr ‘scheme’ with the noun al-sayyi’ ‘evil’ is intrinsic to the fact that it is a scheme and so the annexation of the former to the latter is said to be alternative usage in which the annexed term is implied as a precaution against annexing a noun to an adjective. So do they expect do they await anything but the precedent of the ancients? God’s way of dealing with them such as chastising them for their denial of the messengers? Yet you will never find any change in God’s precedent and you will never find any revision in God’s precedent that is to say chastisement is never replaced by anything else nor is it ever meted out other than to the one who deserves it.

propositions: Those who behave arrogantly in the land will face the consequences of their actions.
Evil plotting only backfires on those who plot against others.
God's way of dealing with those who deny the messengers is to chastise them for their denial.
There is no change in God's precedent, and chastisement is never replaced by anything else.

But He reprieves them to an appointed term namely to the Day of Resurrection. And when their term comes — then truly they will know that God is ever Seer of His servants and so He will requite them according to the nature of their deeds rewarding the believers and punishing the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: And they ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”

Tafsir: And they say ‘When will this promise of resurrection be fulfilled if you are being truthful?’ therein.

hype_questions: When will the promise of resurrection be fulfilled?
Will the threat come to pass?
Are you being truthful?
propositions: This promise of resurrection will be fulfilled if you are being truthful.
The threat will come to pass if what you say is true.

source_text:
Verse: They must be awaiting a single Blast, which will seize them while they are ˹entrenched˺ in ˹worldly˺ disputes.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says They await but a single Cry namely the cry of Isrāfīl’s First Blast that will seize them while they are disputing read yakhassimūna which is actually yakhtasimūna where the vowel of the tā’ has been moved to the khā’ and it the tā’ has been assimilated with the sād in other words while they are oblivious to it busily engaged in disputes concluding bargains eating and drinking and so on; a variant reading has yakhsimūna similar in pattern to yadribūna in which case the meaning is while they dispute with one another.

hype_questions: What happens when we are too busy with worldly disputes?
How do our actions in this life affect our fate?
What is the significance of Isrāfīl's First Blast?
propositions: They await but a single Cry.
The cry is namely the cry of Isrāfīl’s First Blast.
While they are disputing, read yakhassimūna (or yakhtasimūna) which means while they are oblivious to it busily engaged in disputes concluding bargains eating and drinking and so on.

source_text:
Verse: Then they will not be able to make a ˹last˺ will, nor can they return to their own people.

Tafsir: Then they will not be able to make any testament that is to make a bequest nor will they return to their folk from their markets and their businesses rather they will die then and there.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are not prepared for the afterlife?
Can those who have lived a worldly life return to their families after death?
How do people in the afterlife spend their time?
propositions: They will not be able to make any testament.
They will not return to their folk from their markets and businesses.
They will die then and there.

source_text:
Verse: The Trumpet will be blown ˹a second time˺, then—behold!—they will rush from the graves to their Lord.

Tafsir: And the Trumpet is blown — this is the Horn — at the second Blast for the Resurrection to take place; between the two Blasts is an interval of forty years; and lo! they those interred will be scrambling out of their graves towards their Lord emerging therefrom hurriedly.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who are buried when the Trumpet is blown for the second time?
How long will there be an interval between the two Blasts of the Trumpet?
Will those who are interred in their graves rush towards their Lord after the Resurrection takes place?
propositions: The Trumpet will be blown a second time.
Those who are buried will scramble out of their graves to their Lord after the Resurrection takes place.
There is an interval of forty years between the two Blasts of the Trumpet.

source_text:
Verse: They will cry, “Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our place of rest? This must be what the Most Compassionate warned us of; the messengers told the truth!”

Tafsir: They the disbelievers among them will say ‘O yā is for calling attention to something woe to us! waylanā means halākanā ‘O our destruction!’ and it is a verbal noun which has no regular verbal conjugation Who has raised us from our place of sleep? they say this because they will have been asleep in the interval between the two blasts and will not have been punished yet. This that is this raising is that which the Compassionate One had promised and regarding which the messengers had spoken the truth’ they affirm this truth when such affirmation is no longer of any benefit to them — but it is also said that this is said to them.

hype_questions: What event will cause destruction for those who have been asleep?
Who is the one responsible for raising people from their place of rest?
What promise did the Compassionate One make that the messengers spoke the truth about?
propositions: They will cry, 'Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our place of rest?'
This must be what the Most Compassionate warned us of;
the messengers told the truth!
Who has raised us from our place of sleep?
This that is this raising is that which the Compassionate One had promised and regarding which the messengers had spoken the truth

source_text:
Verse: It will only take one Blast, then at once they will all be brought before Us.

Tafsir: It is but a single Cry and behold they will all be arraigned before Us!

hype_questions: What will happen to those who cry out for help?
How will people be held accountable for their actions?
Will everyone face the consequences of their deeds?
propositions: It will only take one Blast.
They will all be brought before Us.
It is but a single Cry.
Behold they will all be arraigned before Us!

source_text:
Verse: On that Day no soul will be wronged in the least, nor will you be rewarded except for what you used to do.

Tafsir: So today no soul shall be wronged in any way and you shall not be requited except the requital of what you used to do.

hype_questions: What will happen to a person on the Day of Judgment?
Will I be rewarded for my good deeds?
How will I be held accountable for my actions?
propositions: No soul will be wronged in the least.
You shall not be rewarded except for what you used to do.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, on that Day the residents of Paradise will be busy enjoying themselves.

Tafsir: Indeed today the inhabitants of Paradise are busy read fī shughlin or fī shughulin oblivious to what the inhabitants of the Fire are suffering busy delighting in pleasures such as deflowering virgins — not busy with anything wearisome as there is no toil in Paradise — rejoicing blissful fākihūna is a second predicate of inna the first being fī shugulin ‘busy’;

hype_questions: What is the state of the inhabitants of Paradise?
How do the inhabitants of Paradise spend their time?
Is there any toil in Paradise?
propositions: The residents of Paradise are busy enjoying themselves.
Today, the inhabitants of Paradise are busy delighting in pleasures such as deflowering virgins.
There is no toil in Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: They and their spouses will be in ˹cool˺ shade, reclining on ˹canopied˺ couches.

Tafsir: they hum the subject and their spouses beneath the shade zilāl is the plural of zulla or zill and is the predicate in other words no blinding sunlight affects them reclining upon muttaki’ūna is a second predicate connected to ‘alā ‘upon’ couches arā’ik is the plural of arīka which is a bed inside a curtained canopy or the bedding therein.

hype_questions: What is the shade that protects them in paradise?
How do they recline upon couches in paradise?
What are the couches made of in paradise?
propositions: They will be in cool shade.
Their spouses will be beneath the shade.
No blinding sunlight affects them.
They recline upon muttaki’ūna.
Muttaki’ūna are couches.
Arā'ik is a plural of arīka, which refers to a bed inside a curtained canopy or the bedding therein.

source_text:
Verse: There they will have fruits and whatever they desire.

Tafsir: They have fruits therein and therein they have whatever they call for whatever they wish for.

hype_questions: What will be the state of those who enter paradise?
What will they find in paradise?
What will they have in paradise?
propositions: They will have fruits.
Whatever they desire, they will have it.
Whatever they wish for, they will have it.

source_text:
Verse: And “Peace!” will be ˹their˺ greeting from the Merciful Lord.

Tafsir: “Peace!” salāmun is a subject — the word qawlan is its predicate that is peace by way of a word from a Lord Who is Merciful to them in other words He says to them ‘Peace be on you!’

hype_questions: What is the greeting that believers will have from Allah?
How does Allah describe Himself to His servants?
What is the meaning of 'salāmun' in Arabic?
propositions: The word qawlan means peace.
Allah says to His servants 'Peace be on you!'
Believers will have a greeting of 'peace' from Allah

source_text:
Verse: ˹Then the disbelievers will be told,˺ “Step away ˹from the believers˺ this Day, O  wicked ones!

Tafsir: And He says ‘Stand apart O you sinners on this day! in other words separate yourselves from the believers — said to them upon their mingling with the latter.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who disbelieve on the day of judgment?
How should believers separate themselves from disbelievers?
What is the purpose of separating from believers?
propositions: The disbelievers will be told to step away from the believers on the day of judgment.
He says 'Stand apart O you sinners' and separates them from the believers.
Separation from believers means separating oneself from their community.

source_text:
Verse: Did I not command you, O  Children of Adam, not to follow Satan, for he is truly your sworn enemy,

Tafsir: Did I not charge you command you O children of Adam by the tongues of My messengers that you should not worship Satan that you should not obey him; truly he is a manifest enemy to you one whose enmity is evident

hype_questions: What is the nature of Satan's relationship with humanity?
How should humans respond to Satan's influence?
What are the consequences of obeying Satan?
propositions: I commanded you not to follow Satan.
You should not worship Satan or obey him.
Satan is your sworn enemy and his enmity towards you is evident.

source_text:
Verse: but to worship Me ˹alone˺? This is the Straight Path.

Tafsir: and that you should worship Me and that you should affirm My Oneness and obey Me — that is the straight path?

hype_questions: What does it mean to worship only one God?
How can affirming the Oneness of God lead to a straight path in life?
What are the consequences of obeying one true God?
propositions: Worshiping only one God is required.
Affirming the Oneness of God and obeying it leads to the Straight Path.
The Straight Path is achieved by submitting to one true God.

source_text:
Verse: Yet he already misled great multitudes of you. Did you not have any sense?

Tafsir: For verily he has led astray from among you many a creature jibillan is the plural of jabīl similar in pattern to qadīm ‘old’; a variant reading has jubulan. Did you not use to comprehend? his enmity and his misguidance or the chastisements that befell them and so believe? And it will be said to them in the Hereafter

hype_questions: Did you not have any sense of the dangers of following a misguided leader?
Why did you not comprehend the enmity and misguidance of such individuals?
Will those who were misled find solace in believing despite the chastisements they faced?
propositions: He has led astray many creatures from among you.
You should have comprehended his enmity and misguidance.
The chastisements that befell them will be a lesson to those who were misled.

source_text:
Verse: This is the Hell you were warned of.

Tafsir: This is Hell which you were promised!

propositions.text: This is Hell.
you were warned of.
this is Hell which you were promised.

source_text:
Verse: Burn in it Today for your disbelief.”

Tafsir: Burn therein today as chastisement for that which you used to reject!’

propositions.text: Burn in it
propositions: Today

propositions.text: for your disbelief
that which you used to reject

source_text:
Verse: On this Day We will seal their mouths, their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify to what they used to commit.

Tafsir: Today We shall seal up their mouths namely the mouths of the disbelievers for their saying By God our Lord we were never idolaters!’ Q. 623; and their hands shall speak to Us and their feet shall bear witness as will other parts of their bodies concerning what they used to earn and so each limb will speak of that sinful action which issued from it.

hype_questions: What happens to the hands of disbelievers on the Day of Judgment?
How do the feet of disbelievers testify to their past actions?
Will all parts of a person's body speak about their sinful actions?
propositions: We will seal up the mouths of disbelievers.
Their hands will speak to Us.
Their feet will bear witness to what they used to commit.

source_text:
Verse: Had We willed, We could have easily blinded their eyes, so they would struggle to find their way. How then could they see?

Tafsir: And had We willed We would have obliterated their eyesight We would have rendered them blind by obliterating them then they would have tried to advance towards the path to be on their way as usual but how would they have seen? then. In other words they would not have been to see.

hype_questions: If God had willed, could humans still find their way without sight?
What happens if God were to blind humanity?
Can humans progress towards righteousness even in darkness?
propositions: God can blind or grant sight at will.
Humans have the ability to choose their path regardless of physical sight.
Blindness does not necessarily hinder spiritual progress.

source_text:
Verse: And had We willed, We could have transfigured them on the spot, so they could neither progress forward nor turn back.

Tafsir: And had We willed We would have transformed them into apes or swine or stones in their place makānatihim variant reading has makānātihim the plural of makāna meaning makān in other words ‘in their dwellings’; then they would have neither been able to go ahead nor to return in other words they would not then be able to come and go.

hype_questions: Would Allah have transformed them into apes or swine if He willed?
What would be the consequence of being transformed into stones?
Can humans progress forward and return if they are transformed?
propositions: Allah could have transfigured them on the spot.
If Allah willed, they would have been transformed into apes or swine or stones in their dwellings.
They would not be able to come and go if they were transformed.

source_text:
Verse: And whoever We grant a long life, We reverse them in development. Will they not then understand?

Tafsir: And whomever We give long life by prolonging his term of life We cause him to regress nankushu; a variant reading has 2nd verbal form nunakkishu derived from al-tankīs in creation that is in terms of his physical form so that after having enjoyed strength and youth he becomes feeble and decrepit. Will they then not understand? that One Who is able to effect such a state — with which they are familiar — is also able to resurrect that they might then become believers? a variant reading for ya‘qilūna ‘they understand’ has the second person plural ta‘qilūna ‘you understand’.

hype_questions: Can a being who experiences physical decline due to divine intervention still comprehend the nature of their fate?
Will those who are familiar with the effects of divine intervention on human life come to understand its purpose?
Is it possible for one who has experienced the consequences of divine intervention to become a believer in the afterlife?
propositions: God grants long life by prolonging one's term of life.
As a result, they regress and become feeble and decrepit.
One Who is able to effect such a state is also able to resurrect them so that they might become believers.

source_text:
Verse: We have not taught him poetry, nor is it fitting for him. This ˹Book˺ is only a Reminder and a clear Quran

Tafsir: And We did not teach him that is the Prophet poetry — this was revealed to refute their saying ‘This Qur’ān that he has brought is but poetry!’ — nor is it poetry seemly nor is it facilitated for him. It — that which he has brought — is just Remembrance an admonition and a Qur’ān that clarifies that manifests God’s rulings and other matters;

hype_questions: Does the Quran only serve as a reminder and not as poetry?
Is the Prophet's message solely based on remembrance and admonition, rather than poetry?
Can the Quran be understood to clarify God's rulings and other matters?
propositions: The Quran is only a Reminder.
The Quran clarifies God's rulings and other matters.
It is not fitting for him that this Qur'an is but poetry!
This Qur'an is just Remembrance an admonition.

source_text:
Verse: to warn whoever is ˹truly˺ alive and fulfil the decree ˹of torment˺ against the disbelievers.

Tafsir: that he may warn li-yundhira; or read li-tundhira ‘that you may warn’ therewith whoever is alive able to comprehend what is being said to him — and such are the believers — and that the Word of chastisement from God may be fulfilled against the disbelievers who are like the dead unable to comprehend what is said to them.

hype_questions: What happens when a person disobeys God's command?
How can believers warn others about the consequences of disbelief?
What is the ultimate fate of those who reject God's message?
propositions: There exists a person alive who will be warned by God.
The warning given to this person is that he may warn others who are alive and able to comprehend the message.
God's word of chastisement will be fulfilled against those who disbelieve and are like the dead, unable to understand what is being said to them.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not see that We singlehandedly created for them, among other things, cattle which are under their control?

Tafsir: Or have they not seen have they not realised the interrogative is meant as an affirmative and the wāw inserted therein in a-wa-lam is for supplementation that We have created for them and for all human beings of what Our hands worked of what We have made without any partner or helper cattle namely camels cows and sheep so that they are their owners? masters controlling them.

hype_questions: Do humans have control over the creatures they've created?
Can humans be considered the owners of the animals they've created?
Is there a partner or helper involved in the creation of cattle?
propositions: We single-handedly created cattle for them.
Humans are the owners and masters of cattle.
Cattle were created by Our hands without any partner or helper.

source_text:
Verse: And We have subjected these ˹animals˺ to them, so they may ride some and eat others.

Tafsir: And We have subdued We have disposed these cattle for them so that some of them provide rides for them and some of them they eat.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of subjugating animals?
How do some animals provide rides for humans?
Why do other animals get eaten?
propositions: We have subjected these cattle to them.
Some cattle are disposed to provide rides for humans.
Other cattle are disposed to be eaten.

source_text:
Verse: And they derive from them other benefits and drinks. Will they not then give thanks?

Tafsir: And there are other benefits for them therein such as their wool fur and hairs and drinks made from their milk mashārib is the plural of mashrab meaning shurb ‘a drink’; or what is meant is the place from which the drink issues. Will they not then give thanks? to the One Who has bestowed these graces upon them and so become believers? In other words they do not do any of this.

hype_questions: What are the benefits that come from drinking milk?
How do people show gratitude to Allah for the blessings they receive?
Can someone become a believer by receiving divine graces?
propositions: They derive other benefits and drinks from them.
There are other benefits in mashrab such as wool fur, hairs, and drinks made from milk.
The One Who has bestowed these graces upon them becomes their Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Still they have taken other gods besides Allah, hoping to be helped ˹by them˺.

Tafsir: And they have taken besides God in other words other than Him other gods idols which they worship that perhaps they might be helped protected against God’s chastisement by their gods’ interceding for them as they are wont to claim.

hype_questions: Can worshiping other gods besides Allah protect us from God's chastisement?
Do idols have the power to intervene on our behalf with God?
Is it possible to be helped by other gods in addition to Allah?
propositions: They have taken other gods besides Allah.
These other gods are idols that they worship.
Their hope is that these idols might help them or protect them from God's chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: They cannot help the pagans, even though they serve the idols as dedicated guards.

Tafsir: They their gods cannot help them — they are being treated as though they were rational beings — and they their idol gods are their host as they claim their supporters ever-present but in the Fire together with them.

hype_questions: Can idols truly provide protection or assistance?
What happens to those who claim their gods are always present but end up in the Fire?
How do rational beings treat those who worship idols?
propositions: Those who serve idols are treated as if they were rational beings.
Idols cannot help pagans.
Pagans will be with their idol gods in the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: So do not let their words grieve you ˹O Prophet˺. Indeed, We ˹fully˺ know what they conceal and what they reveal.

Tafsir: So do not be grieved by their remarks to you that you have not been sent by God and otherwise. Assuredly We know what they conceal and what they proclaim in this respect and otherwise and We will requite them accordingly.

hype_questions: What does God want from me?
How can I be patient in the face of criticism?
Will God requite those who criticize me?
propositions: The Prophet is not sent by God.
God knows what people conceal and reveal about the Prophet's mission.
God will requite those who criticize the Prophet accordingly.

source_text:
Verse: Do people not see that We have created them from a sperm-drop, then—behold!—they openly challenge ˹Us˺?

Tafsir: Or has man — namely the like of al-‘Āsī b. Wā’il — not seen has he not realised that We created him from a drop of sperm and so on in stages until We made him powerful and strong. Then lo! he is an open adversary severely antagonistic towards Us openly making this manifest by his denial of resurrection.

hype_questions: Does humanity not recognize its own creation?
Why do people openly defy God's power and authority?
Can anyone truly deny the reality of resurrection?
propositions: We created humans from a sperm-drop.
Humans have free will but often use it to challenge God's power.
The denial of resurrection is a manifestation of humanity's antagonism towards God.

source_text:
Verse: And they argue with Us—forgetting they were created—saying, “Who will give life to decayed bones?”

Tafsir: And he strikes for Us a similitude in this respect and forgets the manner of his creation from a sperm-drop a thing more curious than his similitude; he says ‘Who will revive the bones when they are rot?’ in other words when they have become withered He does not say ramīmatun ‘decayed’ because it ramīmun ‘rot’ is a noun and not an adjective. It is reported that he al-‘Āsī took some withered bones and crushed them into pieces and said to the Prophet s ‘Do you think that God can revive these bones after they have decayed and become rot?’ And so the Prophet s said ‘Yes indeed! And He will also throw you into the Fire’.

hype_questions: Can God revive decayed bones?
Will God throw someone into the Fire after they have decayed and become rot?
What is the nature of 'ramīmun' in Arabic?
propositions: God created humans from a sperm-drop.
God can revive decayed bones.
God will throw someone into the Fire if they disbelieve.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “They will be revived by the One Who produced them the first time, for He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of every created being.

Tafsir: Say ‘He will revive them Who originated them the first time and He is Knower of all creation of every single creature generally and in detail before and after it has been created —

entities: One Who produced them the first time
hype_questions: Will all beings be revived?
Who is responsible for creating and reviving beings?
Does God have complete knowledge of every created being?
propositions: God will revive those who were created the first time.
God is the originator of all creation.
God has perfect knowledge of every created being.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is the One˺ Who gives you fire from green trees, and—behold!—you kindle ˹fire˺ from them.

Tafsir: He Who has made for you and for all human beings fire from the green tree namely from the markh and ‘afār variety or from all trees except for the jujube ‘unnāb and behold from it you kindle’ from it you strike fire this is proof of the power of God to resurrect for in this example of the green tree He has combined the elements of water fire and wood; but neither the water extinguishes the fire nor does the fire ignite the wood.

hype_questions: Can God create fire from any tree?
What is the significance of green trees in Islamic theology?
How does God's power manifest through natural phenomena?
propositions: God can give humans fire from green trees.
Green trees contain water, fire, and wood, but neither extinguishes nor ignites the other.
God's power is demonstrated through the resurrection of life from inanimate matter.

source_text:
Verse: Can the One Who created the heavens and the earth not ˹easily˺ resurrect these ˹deniers˺?” Yes ˹He can˺! For He is the Master Creator, All-Knowing.

Tafsir: Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth in all their immensity able to create the like of them? namely human beings in all their minuteness? Yes indeed He is able to do this — God Himself replies here. And He is the Creator khallāq means Creator of many things the Knower of all things.

hype_questions: Can God resurrect humans?
Is God capable of creating human beings?
Does God have the power to create and destroy?
propositions: The One Who created the heavens and the earth can easily resurrect deniers.
God is able to create human beings in all their minuteness.
He is the Master Creator, All-Knowing.

source_text:
Verse: All it takes, when He wills something ˹to be˺, is simply to say to it: “Be!” And it is!

Tafsir: His command His affair when He wills a thing that is when He will to create something is just to say to it ‘Be’ and it is a variant reading for fa-yakūnu has fa-yakūna as a supplement to yaqūla ‘to say’.

hype_questions: What is the power of Allah in creation?
How does Allah create something?
What happens when Allah wills something to be?
propositions: When Allah wills something, He simply says 'Be!' and it is.
Allah's command is His affair.
To say 'Be' to something means for Allah to create it.

source_text:
Verse: So glory be to the One in Whose Hands is the authority over all things, and to Whom ˹alone˺ you will ˹all˺ be returned.

Tafsir: So glory be to Him in Whose hand is the dominion of all things malakūt means mulk the wāw and tā’ have been added for hyperbole and to Whom you will be returned restored in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's dominion?
How will I be judged in the Hereafter?
What is the significance of malakūt?
propositions: Glory be to the One in Whose Hands is the authority over all things.
You will be returned restored in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: By those ˹angels˺ lined up in ranks,

Tafsir: By those who are ranged in ranks — by the angels who range their souls in worship or their wings in the air awaiting their orders;

hype_questions: What is the role of angels in worship?
How do angels prepare for their orders?
What happens to an angel's soul when they are ordered?
propositions: Angels range their souls in worship.
Angels range their wings in the air awaiting their orders.
The angels who range their souls in worship or their wings in the air await their orders.

source_text:
Verse: and those who diligently drive ˹the clouds˺,

Tafsir: and the drivers who drive away the angels who drive the clouds;

hype_questions: What is the role of driving in Islam?
How do we demonstrate patience in our daily lives?
Can we be like the angels who drive the clouds?
propositions: Those who diligently drive the clouds are angels.
Driving away angels means demonstrating patience and obedience to Allah.
The act of driving is a metaphor for taking control of one's life and actions.

source_text:
Verse: and those who recite the Reminder!

Tafsir: and those who recite that is to say the readers of the Qur’ān they recite it by way remembrance dhikran is a verbal noun referring to the action of al-tāliyāt ‘those who recite’.

hype_questions: What is the action referred to by 'al-tāliyāt'?
Who are the readers of the Qur’ān?
What does it mean to recite the Qur’ān?
propositions: Those who recite the Reminder are those who recite the Qur’ān by way of remembrance.
The action referred to by 'al-tāliyāt' is the act of reciting.
The readers of the Qur’ān are those who recite it.

source_text:
Verse: Surely your God is One!

Tafsir: Indeed your God O people of Mecca is certainly One

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah?
Is there only one God?
Who is the one true God?
propositions: Your God is One.
Allah is the one and only God.
There is no god but Allah.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is˺ the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, and the Lord of all points of sunrise.

Tafsir: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them and Lord of the sun’s risings that is as well as the sun’s settings — each day it the sun has a rising and a setting.

entities: Lord of the heavens and the earth
hype_questions: What is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?
How does the sun's movement relate to its rising and setting?
What is the significance of the sun's daily cycle?
propositions: The Lord of the heavens and the earth is one entity.
The sun has a fixed point of rising and setting each day.
The sun's daily cycle is a recurring phenomenon.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the stars for decoration

Tafsir: We have indeed adorned the lowest heaven with an adornment the stars that is to say adorned with their light or with them the stars the genitive annexation bi-zīnati’l-kawākib is for explication; similarly explicative is the reading of bi-zīnatin ‘with an adornment’ with nunation the adornment explained as being ‘the stars’;

hype_questions: What is the purpose of adorning the lowest heaven?
How are the stars related to the adornment of the lowest heaven?
What does it mean for something to be adorned with light?
propositions: We have adorned the lowest heaven with the stars.
The stars are an adornment on the lowest heaven.
The lowest heaven is decorated with its own light.

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We destroyed before them, and they cried out when it was too late to escape.

Tafsir: How many — in other words many — a generation a community of past communities We have destroyed before them and they cried out when the chastisement was sent down on them when it was no longer the time for escape that is to say the time was not one for fleeing the suffixed tā’ of wa-lāta is extra; the sentence is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb nādaw ‘they cried out’ in other words they called for help but the situation was such that there could be no escape or deliverance; but still the Meccan disbelievers have not taken heed from their example.

hype_questions: What is the significance of past communities being destroyed in Islamic theology?
How does the Quran address the concept of chastisement and its impact on individuals?

propositions: We have destroyed many generations before them.
They cried out when the chastisement was sent down on them.
The time for escape had passed.

Tafsir: And they marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves a messenger from among their number to warn them and to threaten them with the punishment of the Fire after resurrection — and this warner is the Prophet s. And those who disbelieve the overt noun al-kāfirūnā has replaced the third person pronominalisation say ‘This is a sorcerer a liar.

Those who disbelieve say, 'This is a sorcerer, a liar.'
The pagans are astonished that a warner has come to them from among themselves.

source_text:
Verse: Has he reduced ˹all˺ the gods to One God? Indeed, this is something totally astonishing.”

Tafsir: Has he made the gods One God? — for he had said to them ‘Say there is no god except God’ — in other words they objected how could one god suffice for all of creation? Lo! that is indeed a curious thing’.

hype_questions: Can one God be sufficient for the entire universe?

The oneness of God is a curious thing.

Tafsir: And the council from among them go about from the place of their assembly at the house of Abū Tālib and the place where they heard the Prophet s say ‘Say there is no god except God’ saying ‘Go! they say to one another go and stand by your gods adhere firmly to worship of them; lo! this that has been mentioned concerning the Oneness of God is indeed a thing sought from us.

hype_questions: What does it mean to stand firm in devotion to one's gods?

This scheme for power is indeed a thing sought from us.

source_text:

Tafsir: We never heard of this in the latter-day creed namely the creed of Jesus. This is surely nothing but an invention mere lies.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the 'creed' mentioned in the verse?

This concept is considered a fabrication and an invention.
The speaker believes that this concept is a lie.

source_text:
Verse: Has the Reminder been revealed ˹only˺ to him out of ˹all of˺ us?” In fact, they are ˹only˺ in doubt of My ˹revealed˺ Reminder. In fact, ˹they do so because˺ they have not yet tasted My punishment.

Tafsir: Has the Remembrance the Qur’ān been revealed to him Muhammad (s) out of all of us’ when he is neither the elder nor the noblest among us? In other words it could not have been revealed to him read a-unzila pronouncing both hamzas or not pronouncing the second one but in both cases inserting an intervening alif or without this insertion. God exalted be He says Nay but they are in doubt concerning My Remembrance My revelation that is the Qur’ān for they deny the one who has brought it. Nay but they have not yet tasted My chastisement and if they were to taste it they would certainly believe the Prophet s in what he has brought — but then in such a case their belief in the Prophet would be of no benefit to them.

hype_questions: Would they have believed in the Prophet if they had tasted My chastisement?
Can anyone bring forth the Qur'ān and claim it is from God?
Is the Prophet's message of no benefit to those who deny him?
propositions: The Qur’ān was not revealed to Muhammad (s) out of all of us.
They are in doubt concerning My Remembrance, My revelation that is the Qur’ān.
If they were to taste My chastisement, they would certainly believe the Prophet s in what he has brought.

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹is it because˺ they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord—the Almighty, the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.

Tafsir: Or do they possess the treasuries of your Lord’s mercy the Mighty the Victor the Bestower? treasuries such as prophethood and otherwise so that they might give it to whomever they want?

hype_questions: Do they possess the power to bestow blessings on others?
Can they grant prophethood to whoever they desire?

propositions: Your Lord possesses the treasuries of mercy.
The treasuries of your Lord's mercy are mighty, victorious, and bestowing.
Prophethood is one of the treasuries of your Lord's mercy.

source_text:

Tafsir: Or do they possess the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them? If this is what they claim Then let them ascend by the means of ascension that lead to the heaven and bring down some revelation wahy and then assign it exclusively to whomever they wish am in both verses represents the rhetorical hamza of denial.

hype_questions: Do they possess the kingdom of the heavens and the earth?

They claim to possess the kingdom, but it is not true.

Revelation will be brought down from heaven exclusively for whoever they wish.

source_text:

We shall destroy these people.

source_text:

Pharaoh punished those who incurred his wrath by tying their hands and feet to four stakes.

source_text:

My punishment was justified.

There will be no revoking read fawāq or fuwāq after chastisement.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says Bear patiently what they say and remember Our servant David the one of fortitude that is to say the one of fortitude in worship he used to fast every other day and keep vigil for half the night sleep for a third and then keep vigil for the last sixth. Indeed he was a penitent soul always returning to what pleases God.

hype_questions: What is the significance of patience in Islam?

propositions: God exalted be He says Bear patiently what they say.
David used to fast every other day and keep vigil for half the night, sleep for a third, and then keep vigil for the last sixth.

source_text:

David’s sanctuary that is his place of prayer for they had been prohibited from entering by the front gates because of his being engaged in worship in other words has it come to you their tale and their account?

source_text:
Verse: When they came into David’s presence, he was startled by them. They said, “Have no fear. ˹We are merely˺ two in a dispute: one of us has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth—do not go beyond ˹it˺—and guide us to the right way.

Tafsir: When they entered upon David and he was frightened by them. And they said ‘Do not fear; we are two disputants some say that this means ‘two groups’ in order to agree with the plural person of the verb dakhalū ‘they entered’; others say ‘two individuals’ with the plural person actually denoting these two; al-khasm may refer to a one or more individuals. These two were angels who had come in the form of two disputants between whom there was supposed to have occurred the situation mentioned — but only hypothetically — in order to alert David peace be upon him to what he had done he had ninety nine women but desired the woman of a man who had only her and no other. He David had married her and consummated the marriage. One of us has infringed upon the rights of the other so judge justly between us and do not transgress do not be unjust and guide us direct us to the right path’ the correct way.

David should judge between the two with truth and not go beyond it.
The correct way is to guide us towards righteousness.

source_text:
Verse: This is my brother. He has ninety-nine sheep while I have ˹only˺ one. ˹Still˺ he asked me to give it up to him, overwhelming me with ˹his˺ argument.”

Tafsir: ‘Behold this brother of mine in other words my fellow co-religionist has ninety-nine ewes — here used to represent the women — while I have a single ewe; yet he said “Entrust it to me” in other words make me in charge of it and he overcame me in speech’ in other words in the argument; so the latter conceded charge of it to him.

He overcame me with his argument.

source_text:
Verse: David ˹eventually˺ ruled, “He has definitely wronged you in demanding ˹to add˺ your sheep to his. And certainly many partners wrong each other, except those who believe and do good—but how few are they!” Then David realized that We had tested him so he asked for his Lord’s forgiveness, fell down in prostration, and turned ˹to Him in repentance˺.

Tafsir: He said ‘He has certainly wronged you by asking for your ewe that he may add it to his sheep. And indeed many associates infringe upon the rights of one another except such as believe and perform righteous deeds but few are they!’ mā emphasises the ‘fewness’. As the two angels were ascending to the heaven one said to the other ‘He has certainly passed judgement on himself!’ David was thus alerted to his deed. God exalted be He says And David thought in other words he became certain that We had indeed tried him that We had caused him to fall into a trial that is a test through his love for that woman. So he sought forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing in other words prostrate and repented.

hype_questions: What happens when we wrong someone and then seek forgiveness?

What is the importance of repenting to God?

Many partners infringe upon each other's rights except those who believe and do good deeds.
God exalted be He says David realized We had tested him through his love for the woman.

source_text:
Verse: So We forgave that for him. And he will indeed have ˹a status of˺ closeness to Us and an honourable destination!

source_text:
Verse: ˹We instructed him:˺ “O David! We have surely made you an authority in the land, so judge between people with truth. And do not follow ˹your˺ desires or they will lead you astray from Allah’s Way. Surely those who go astray from Allah’s Way will suffer a severe punishment for neglecting the Day of Reckoning.”

Tafsir: ‘O David! We have indeed made you a vicegerent on the earth managing the affairs of people; so judge justly between people and do not follow desire that is the desires of the soul that it then lead you astray from the way of God that is to say from the proofs that indicate the truth of His Oneness. Truly those who go astray from the way of God in other words from belief in God — for them there will be a severe chastisement because of their forgetting the Day of Reckoning’ as a result of their having neglected faith. For had they been certain of the truth of the Day of Reckoning they would have first been believers in this world.

hype_questions: What is the role of a vicegerent in society?

David was made an authority in the land, but he must not follow his desires.
Those who go astray from Allah's Way will suffer a severe punishment for neglecting the Day of Reckoning.

source_text:
Verse: We have not created the heavens and earth and everything in between without purpose—as the disbelievers think. So woe to the disbelievers because of the Fire!

Tafsir: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in vain frivolously. That namely the creation of what has been mentioned as being for no particular purpose is the supposition of those who disbelieve from among the people of Mecca. So woe — a valley in hell-fire — to the disbelievers from the Fire!

source_text:
Verse: Or should We treat those who believe and do good like those who make mischief throughout the land? Or should We treat the righteous like the wicked?

Tafsir: Or shall We treat those who believe and perform righteous deeds like those who cause corruption in the earth; or shall We treat the God-fearing like the profligate? This was revealed when the Meccan disbelievers said to the believers ‘In the Hereafter we will receive the same reward as that which you will receive’ am ‘or’ contains the rhetorical hamza of denial.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember˺ when the well-trained, swift horses were paraded before him in the evening.

Tafsir: When one evening — which is the period after midday — there were displayed before him the prancing steeds al-sāfināt ‘horses’ is the plural of sāfina which denotes a horse standing on three legs with the fourth supported on the edge of the hoof and derives from the verb safana yasfinu sufūnan; al-jiyād is the plural of jawād which is a ‘racer’; the meaning is that these horses are such that when they are halted they stand still and when they run they surpass others in speed. One thousand horses were displayed before him after he had performed the midday prayer for he had wanted to use them in a holy struggle jihād against an enemy. But when the display reached the nine-hundredth horse the sun set and he had not performed the afternoon prayer. So he was greatly distressed.

The horses were prancing steeds that stood still when halted and surpassed others in speed when running.

The display reached the nine-hundredth horse when the sun set, but the leader had not performed afternoon prayer.

Verse: ˹He ordered,˺ “Bring them back to me!” Then he began to rub down their legs and necks.

Then he set about slashing with his sword their legs al-sūq is the plural of sāq and necks in other words he slaughtered them and cut off their legs as an offering of atonement to God exalted be He for having been distracted by them from the prayer. He gave all the meat thereof as voluntary alms and so God compensated him what was better and faster that these horses and this was the wind which blew at his command as he wished.

Then he began to rub down their legs and necks.

source_text:
Verse: And indeed, We tested Solomon, placing a ˹deformed˺ body on his throne, then he turned ˹to Allah in repentance˺.

Tafsir: And We certainly tried Solomon We tested him by wresting his kingdom from him because he had married a woman solely out of his desire for her. She used to worship idols in his own home without his knowledge. Now control of his kingdom lay in his ring. On one occasion needing to withdraw to relieve himself he took it off and left it with this woman of his whose name was al-Amīna as was his custom; but a jinn disguised in the form of Solomon came to her and seized it from her. And We cast upon his throne a lifeless body which was that very jinn and he was the one known as Sakhr — or it was some other jinn; he sat upon Solomon’s throne and so as was the case with Solomon the birds and other creatures devoted themselves to him in service. When Solomon came out of his palace having seen him the jinn upon his throne he said to the people ‘I am Solomon not him!’ But they did not recognise him. Then he repented — Solomon returned to his kingdom many days later after he had managed to acquire the ring. He wore it and sat upon his throne again.

hype_questions: What happened to Solomon's kingdom?
Why did Solomon marry a woman solely out of his desire for her?
How did Solomon regain control of his throne?
propositions: Solomon was tested by being placed on a lifeless body on his throne.
The jinn disguised as Sakhr seized the ring from al-Amīna and sat on Solomon's throne.
Solomon repented after not recognizing the jinn upon his throne.
Solomon regained control of his throne after acquiring the ring.

Verse: ˹And We said to him,˺ “Take in your hand a bundle of grass, and strike ˹your wife˺ with it, and do not break your oath.” We truly found him patient. What an excellent servant ˹he was˺! Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.

Verse: Surely We have revealed to you the Book ˹O Prophet˺ with the truth for humanity. So whoever chooses to be guided, it is for their own good. And whoever chooses to stray, it is only to their own loss. You are not a keeper over them.

Tafsir: Truly We have revealed the Book to you for the sake of mankind with the truth bi’l-haqqi is semantically connected to anzalnā ‘We have revealed’. So whoever is guided then it his being guided is for the sake of his own soul and whoever goes astray goes astray only to the detriment thereof. And you are not meant to be a guardian over them and so compel them to embrace guidance.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of the Quran?
How should a prophet handle his followers?
Can humans truly choose their own path?
propositions: The Quran was revealed to the Prophet for the sake of humanity with truth.
Guidance is for one's own soul.
Straying is only detrimental to oneself.
A prophet is not meant to be a guardian over his followers.
It is not the prophet's duty to compel others to follow guidance.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It is˺ Allah ˹Who˺ calls back the souls ˹of people˺ upon their death as well as ˹the souls˺ of the living during their sleep. Then He keeps those for whom He has ordained death, and releases the others until ˹their˺ appointed time. Surely in this are signs for people who reflect.

Tafsir: God takes the souls at the time of their death and He takes those that have not died in their sleep in other words He takes them during sleep. Then He retains those for whom He has ordained death and releases the others until an appointed term that is until the time of their death. The one that is released is the soul that possesses the faculty of discernment without which the soul containing the force of life is able to remain temporarily — but this cannot be the other way round. Truly in that mentioned there are signs indications for a people who reflect and then realise that the One with the power to do this also has the power to resurrect — Quraysh however never reflected on this fact.

hype_questions: Does Allah have the power to resurrect?
What is the faculty of discernment in the soul?
Can a soul containing life force remain temporarily without it?
propositions: Allah calls back the souls of people upon their death and during their sleep.
He retains those for whom He has ordained death and releases others until an appointed term.
The faculty of discernment is necessary for a soul to remain temporarily.
Allah has the power to resurrect.
Quraysh never reflected on the fact that Allah can resurrect.

source_text:
Verse: Or have they taken others besides Allah as intercessors? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹Would they do so,˺ even though those ˹idols˺ have neither authority nor intelligence?”

Tafsir: Or have they — nay but they have — taken besides God idols as gods to act as intercessors? with God as they are wont to allege. Say to them ‘What! will they intercede even though they have no power whatever of intercession or otherwise and are unable to comprehend?’ that you worship them or to comprehend anything else for that matter? Nay.

hype_questions: Can idols act as intercessors?
Do idols have any power of intercession?
What is the purpose of worshiping idols?
propositions: They took idols as gods to act as intercessors.
Idols have no power of intercession or comprehension.
One should not worship idols or seek their comprehension.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “All intercession belongs to Allah ˹alone˺. To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.”

Tafsir: Say ‘All intercession belongs solely to God that is to say He has exclusive control over it and so none can intercede except with His permission. To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be brought back’.

hype_questions: Can anyone intercede with God without His permission?
What happens to humans after death?
Is Allah's kingdom limited to the heavens and earth?
propositions: Allah has exclusive control over intercession.
Only with Allah's permission can someone intercede.
Humans will be brought back to Allah after death.

source_text:
Verse: Yet when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter are filled with disgust. But as soon as those ˹gods˺ other than Him are mentioned, they are filled with joy.

Tafsir: And when God is mentioned alone that is without the mention of their gods thereat shrink they are repelled and they become constricted the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter; but when those others besides Him namely the idols are mentioned behold they rejoice!

hype_questions: What happens when Allah is mentioned alone?
How do people react when other gods are mentioned?
What is the difference between believing in Allah and not believing in Him?
propositions: When Allah is mentioned alone, those who disbelieve in the Hereafter feel disgust.
Mentioning other gods besides Allah fills the hearts of unbelievers with joy.
Believing in a god other than Allah leads to happiness for those who do not believe in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O Allah—Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the seen and unseen! You will judge between Your servants regarding their differences.”

Tafsir: Say ‘O God! Allāhumma means yā Allāh Originator of the heavens and the earth! the Creator of them without precedent Knower of the Unseen and the visible Knower of what is hidden and what is witnessed You will judge between Your servants concerning that wherein they used to differ’ in the matter of religion guide me to the truth over which they are at variance.

hype_questions: What is the role of Allah in judging His servants?
How will Allah guide us to the truth?
What are the differences between Allah's knowledge of the seen and unseen?
propositions: Allah is the Originator of the heavens and the earth.
Allah is the Knower of both the seen and unseen.
Allah will judge His servants regarding their differences.

source_text:
Verse: Even if the wrongdoers were to possess everything in the world twice over, they would certainly offer it to ransom themselves from the horrible punishment on Judgment Day, for they will see from Allah what they had never expected.

Tafsir: And even if the evildoers possessed all that is in the earth and as much of it besides they would surely offer it to ransom themselves from the terrible chastisement on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear there will become manifest to them from God that which they had never reckoned what they never supposed they would see.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who try to buy their way out of punishment on Judgment Day?
Can anyone ransom themselves from the terrible chastisement they will face on the Day of Resurrection?
How will people react when they see God's punishment manifest before them?
propositions: Even if someone possesses everything in the world, they would still try to ransom themselves from punishment.
The punishment on Judgment Day is terrible and cannot be bought.
People will be surprised by what they see on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: And the evil ˹consequences˺ of their deeds will unfold before them, and they will be overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.

Tafsir: And there will appear to them the evils of what they had earned and they will be besieged by there will descend on them that which they used to deride in other words the chastisement.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of one's actions?
How will individuals be held accountable for their deeds?
What happens when people ridicule something, but ultimately face its consequences?
propositions: The evil consequences of their deeds will unfold before them.
They will be overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.
There will appear to them the evils of what they had earned.

source_text:
Verse: When one is touched with hardship, they cry out to Us ˹alone˺. Then when We shower Our blessings upon them, they say, “I have been granted all this only because of ˹my˺ knowledge.” Not at all! It is ˹no more than˺ a test. But most of them do not know.

Tafsir: So when some distress befalls man al-insān here a generic he supplicates Us. Then when We bestow on him a grace from Us he says ‘I was given it merely by force of knowledge’ from God that I was deserving of it. Nay but it this saying is a trial a test by which servants are tested. But most of them do not know that such bestowal of grace is a way of drawing them on and a test of their faith.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of hardship in a person's life?
How does one demonstrate faith when faced with blessings?
Can knowledge alone be credited for success?
propositions: When one faces hardship, they cry out to God.
God showers blessings upon those who are tested.
Knowledge is not the sole reason for receiving blessings from God.

source_text:
Verse: The same had already been said by those ˹destroyed˺ before them, but their ˹worldly˺ gains were of no benefit to them.

Tafsir: Already the same was said by those who were before them of communities such as Korah and those of his people who were content with such a saying. But what they used to earn did not avail them.

hype_questions: What happens when one is content with a simple saying?
Can worldly gains bring salvation?
How do people like Korah fare in the afterlife?
propositions: Those who were before them had already been told the same message.
Their worldly gains did not provide any benefit to them.
Contentment with a simple saying does not guarantee salvation.
Worldly earnings are not sufficient for salvation.
Korah and his people's fate serves as an example of the consequences of being content with a simple message.

source_text:
Verse: So the evil ˹consequences˺ of their deeds overtook them. And the wrongdoers among these ˹pagans˺ will be overtaken by the evil ˹consequences˺ of their deeds. And they will have no escape.

Tafsir: So the evils of what they earned smote them that is the requital thereof smote them. And the evildoers among these namely among Quraysh shall also be smitten by the evils of what they earned and they will not be able to thwart it they will not elude Our chastisement — thus they were made to suffer seven years of drought and only afterwards were they enriched with provision from God.

hype_questions: What happens to those who earn evil deeds?
Can the evildoers of Quraysh escape their fate?
How did Allah respond to the drought in Quraysh?
propositions: The evils of what they earned smote them.
The evildoers among these namely among Quraysh shall also be smitten by the evils of what they earned.
They will have no escape from Our chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not know that Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills? Surely in this are signs for people who believe.

Tafsir: Do they not know that God extends His provision that He makes it abundant for whomever He will as a test and restricts it? for whomever He will as a trial? Truly in that there are signs for a people who believe in Him.

hype_questions: Does God provide abundance or scarcity to His creation?
What is the purpose of God's provision?
How do people who believe in God interpret the signs of His providence?
propositions: Allah gives abundant provisions to whoever He wills.
God extends His provision, making it abundant for some and restricting it for others as a test or trial.
There are signs for people who believe in Allah's providence.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet, that Allah says,˺ “O My servants who have exceeded the limits against their souls! Do not lose hope in Allah’s mercy, for Allah certainly forgives all sins. He is indeed the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: Say that God declares ‘O My servants who have been prodigal against their own souls do not despair read taqnitū taqnatū or taqnutū do not give up hope of God’s mercy. Truly God forgives all sins for those who repent from idolatry. Truly He is the Forgiving the Merciful.

hype_questions: What happens when we repent from idolatry?
Can Allah forgive all sins?
How can I not lose hope in Allah's mercy?
propositions: Allah forgives all sins.
God is the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
Repentance leads to forgiveness from idolatry.

source_text:
Verse: Turn to your Lord ˹in repentance˺, and ˹fully˺ submit to Him before the punishment reaches you, ˹for˺ then you will not be helped.

Tafsir: And turn return penitently to your Lord and submit perform deeds sincerely to Him before the chastisement comes on you whereupon you will not be helped to ward it off if you have not repented.

hype_questions: What happens when one turns to Allah in repentance?
How can one avoid punishment by submitting sincerely to Allah?
What is the consequence of not repenting before facing punishment?
propositions: Turn to your Lord in repentance.
Submit fully to Him before the punishment reaches you.
Perform deeds sincerely to Him before the chastisement comes on you.

source_text:
Verse: Follow ˹the Quran,˺ the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord, before the punishment takes you by surprise while you are unaware,

Tafsir: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord — namely the Qur’ān — before the chastisement comes on you suddenly while you are unaware’ of the time of its arrival until it has actually come;

hype_questions: What is the best course of action to take before facing punishment?
How can one prepare for the unexpected chastisement?
What does it mean to be unaware of the time of arrival?
propositions: Follow the Quran from your Lord.
The Qur'an is the best guidance to follow.
Punishment can come suddenly without warning.

source_text:
Verse: so that no ˹sinful˺ soul will say ˹on Judgment Day˺, ‘Woe to me for neglecting ˹my duties towards˺ Allah, while ridiculing ˹the truth˺.’

Tafsir: so apply yourselves to this before any soul should say ‘Alas for me yā hasratā is actually yā hasratī meaning ‘O regret of mine’ for what I have neglected of my duty to God in other words of obedience to Him. Indeed wa-in in is softened in place of the hardened form in other words understand it as wa-innī I was among those who ridiculed’ His religion and His Book;

hype_questions: What happens to a person who neglects their duties towards Allah on the Day of Judgment?

What is the consequence of ridiculing Allah's religion and His Book?
propositions: No soul will say on Judgment Day, 'Woe to me for neglecting my duties towards Allah.'
Applying this verse means understanding that one should not ridicule the truth.
Ridiculing Allah's religion and His Book is equivalent to being among those who ridiculed it.

source_text:
Verse: Or ˹a soul will˺ say, ‘If only Allah had guided me, I would have certainly been one of the righteous.’

Tafsir: or before that it should say ‘If only God had guided me to obedience and I had become guided I would have been among those who have feared’ His chastisement;

hype_questions: If only a person could be certain they would be righteous?

propositions: A soul will say if Allah had guided me I would have been one of the righteous.
God guides individuals to obedience if they seek it.
Obedience to God leads to fearing His chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Or say, upon seeing the torment, ‘If only I had a second chance, I would have been one of the good-doers.’

Tafsir: or before that it should say when it sees the chastisement ‘If only there had been a second chance a return to this world I would be among the virtuous’ the believers. It is then said to him by God

hype_questions: Would being virtuous in a second chance be enough to redeem one's past actions?

propositions: If one sees torment, they should reflect on their past actions.
