God's mercy and forgiveness are available to those who repent and seek virtue.

source_text:
Verse: Not at all! My revelations had already come to you, but you rejected them, acted arrogantly, and were one of the disbelievers.”

Tafsir: ‘Yes indeed! My signs came to you the Qur’ān — which is the means to guidance — but you denied them and were arrogant you disdained to believe in them and you were among the disbelievers’.

hype_questions: Did the Prophet reject your revelations?

propositions: My revelations had already come to you.

source_text:
Verse: On the Day of Judgment you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces gloomy. Is Hell not a ˹fitting˺ home for the arrogant?

Tafsir: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who imputed lies to God by ascribing partner and child to Him with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a fitting abode for those who are too arrogant? to believe? Indeed there is.

hype_questions: What happens to those who lie about Allah on the Day of Judgment?
Is Hell a suitable place for the arrogant?
Can anyone truly believe in Allah?
propositions: You will see those who lied about Allah with their faces gloomy.
Hell is a fitting home for the arrogant.
There is indeed a fitting abode for those who are too arrogant to believe.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah will deliver those who were mindful ˹of Him˺ to their place of ˹ultimate˺ triumph. No evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.

Tafsir: And God will deliver from Hell those who fear idolatry because of their triumph that is on account of the place they have won in Paradise by placing them in it. No evil will touch them nor will they grieve.

hype_questions: What happens to those who fear idolatry?
How do people triumph in Paradise?
Will evil touch those who have won their place of ultimate triumph?
propositions: Allah will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of ultimate triumph.
No evil will touch those who are delivered by Allah.
Those who fear idolatry will not grieve in Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Maintainer of everything.

Tafsir: God is the Creator of all things and He is Guardian over all things disposing of them as He will.

hype_questions: What is Allah's role in creation?
How does Allah maintain the universe?
What are Allah's powers over creation?
propositions: Allah is the Creator of all things.
Allah is the Maintainer of everything.
Allah disposes of everything as He wills.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belong the keys ˹of the treasuries˺ of the heavens and the earth. As for those who rejected the signs of Allah, it is they who will be the ˹true˺ losers.

Tafsir: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth in other words the keys to their storehouses of rain and vegetation and other things. And those who disbelieve in the signs of God such as the Qur’ān — those they are the losers ūlā’ika humu’l-khāsirūna is semantically connected to His words wa-yunajjī’Llāhu’lladhīna ittaqaw ‘and God will deliver those who guarded themselves …’ to the end of that statement; the intervening statements are parentheticals.

hype_questions: What are the keys to the storehouses of rain and vegetation?
Who will be delivered by God if they guard themselves?
What is the meaning of 'ūlā’ika humu’l-khāsirūna' in the context of the Qur'ān?
propositions: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth.
Those who disbelieve in the signs of God are the losers.
God will deliver those who guarded themselves.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Are you urging me to worship ˹anyone˺ other than Allah, O  ignorant ones?”

Tafsir: Say ‘Is it something other than God that you bid me to worship O you who are ignorant?’ ghayra is in the accusative because of the verb a‘budu ‘I worship’ which itself is operated by ta’murūnī ‘you bid me’ read with one nūn on the basis of an implicit an; it ta’murūnī may also be read with two nūns assimilated ta’murūnnī or separated ta’murūnanī.

hype_questions: Does the Prophet urge anyone to worship besides Allah?
What does it mean to bid someone to worship something other than God?
Can someone be ignorant of the one true God?
propositions: You are urging me to worship someone other than Allah.
It is something other than God that you bid me to worship.
O you who are ignorant, is it something other than God that you bid me to worship?

source_text:
Verse: It has already been revealed to you—and to those ˹prophets˺ before you—that if you associate others ˹with Allah˺, your deeds will certainly be void and you will truly be one of the losers.

Tafsir: And certainly it has been revealed to you and to those before you that by God! if you associate others with God O Muhammad (s) — hypothetically — your work shall surely fail and you shall surely be among the losers’.

topics: Consequences of associating partners with Allah
hype_questions: What happens if you associate others with God?
Will your work fail if you associate partners with God?
How will associating partners with God affect your fate?
propositions: If you associate others with Allah, your deeds are void.
Associating others with Allah will surely fail.
You shall be among the losers if you associate others with Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Rather, worship Allah ˹alone˺ and be one of the grateful.

Tafsir: Rather worship God alone and be among the thankful of His bestowal of graces on you.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of worshiping a single deity?
How can one cultivate gratitude towards their creator?
What are the benefits of being thankful for God's blessings?
propositions: Worship Allah alone.
Be among the thankful of His bestowal of graces on you.

source_text:
Verse: They have not shown Allah His proper reverence—when on the Day of Judgment the ˹whole˺ earth will be in His Grip, and the heavens will be rolled up in His Right Hand. Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate ˹with Him˺!

Tafsir: And they do not esteem God as He should be esteemed they do not understand His true nature or it means that they do not exalt Him with the exaltation truly worthy of Him when they associate others with Him. And the entire earth jamī‘an is a circumstantial qualifier in other words the seven earths will be in His grasp in other words it shall be grasped by Him meaning that it will be in His possession and at His disposal on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be rolled up brought together in His Right Hand by His power. Glory be to Him! And exalted be He above what they associate! with Him of partners.

hype_questions: What is the proper reverence due to Allah?
How will the earth be in Allah's Grip on the Day of Judgment?
What will happen to the heavens on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: They have not shown Allah His proper reverence.
The entire earth will be in Allah's Grip on the Day of Judgment.
The heavens will be rolled up in Allah's Right Hand.

source_text:
Verse: The Trumpet will be blown and all those in the heavens and all those on the earth will fall dead, except those Allah wills ˹to spare˺. Then it will be blown again and they will rise up at once, looking on ˹in anticipation˺.

Tafsir: And the Trumpet will be blown for the First Blast and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon will die except whomever God wills such as the houris the beautiful youths of Paradise and others. Then it will be blown again and behold they that is all creatures who are dead will rise up looking on waiting to see what will be done with them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are not spared by Allah on the Day of Judgment?
Who will be resurrected and what is their state upon resurrection?

propositions: The Trumpet will be blown, and all those in the heavens and all those on the earth will fall dead, except those Allah wills.
Then it will be blown again, and they will rise up at once, looking on in anticipation.
Whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon and die except whomever God wills.
The houris, the beautiful youths of Paradise, and others will be spared.
Then it will be blown again, and behold, they that are all creatures who are dead will rise up looking on waiting to see what will be done with them.

source_text:
Verse: The earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the record ˹of deeds˺ will be laid ˹open˺, the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward—and judgment will be passed on all with fairness. None will be wronged.

Tafsir: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord when God reveals Himself for the passing of judgement and the Book of deeds shall be set in place for the Reckoning and the prophets and witnesses namely Muhammad (s) and his community will be brought to bear witness that the messengers delivered the Message to their respective communities. And judgement will be made between them with truth in other words justly and they will not be wronged in a single thing.

hype_questions: What will be the state of the earth on Judgment Day?
How will the Book of Deeds be revealed?
Will the prophets and witnesses be held accountable for their actions?
propositions: The earth will shine with the light of its Lord.
The record of deeds will be laid open.
Judgment will be passed on all with fairness.
None will be wronged.

source_text:
Verse: Every soul will be paid in full for its deeds, for Allah knows best what they have done.

Tafsir: And every soul will be paid in full for what it did that is it will be paid the requital thereof and He is best aware of what they do and has no need for any witnesses.

hype_questions: What happens to our deeds after we die?
Will we be held accountable for our actions?
How will Allah judge us?
propositions: Every soul will be paid in full for its deeds.
Allah knows best what they have done.
He is best aware of what they do and has no need for any witnesses.

source_text:
Verse: Those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in ˹successive˺ groups. When they arrive there, its gates will be opened and its keepers will ask them: “Did messengers not come to you from among yourselves, reciting to you the revelations of your Lord and warning you of the coming of this Day of yours?” The disbelievers will cry, “Yes ˹indeed˺! But the decree of torment has come to pass against the disbelievers.”

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve will be driven violently to Hell in troops in separate groups until when they reach it its gates are opened futihat abwābuhā is the response to idhā ‘when’ and its keepers will say to them ‘Did there not come to you any messengers from among yourselves reciting to you the signs of your Lord the Qur’ān and otherwise and warning you of the encounter of this day of yours?’ They will say ‘Yes indeed; but the word of chastisement — namely the verse Assuredly I will fill Hell … Q. 11119 — against the disbelievers has been fulfilled’.

hype_questions: What is the fate of those who disbelieve?
Why do messengers come to humans from among themselves?
How does God punish the disbelievers?
propositions: Those who disbelieve will be driven violently to Hell in troops in separate groups.
Messengers came to humans from among themselves, reciting to them the revelations of their Lord and warning them of the coming of this Day of theirs.
The word of chastisement against the disbelievers has been fulfilled.

source_text:
Verse: It will be said to them, “Enter the gates of Hell, to stay there forever.” What an evil home for the arrogant!

Tafsir: It will be said ‘Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein’ — decreed for you to abide therein. For evil indeed is the abode of the arrogant!’

hype_questions: What happens to those who are arrogant?
Will they be punished for their arrogance?
How will the arrogant be treated in the afterlife?
propositions: It will be said 'Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein'.
You have been decreed to abide therein.
The abode of the arrogant is evil.

source_text:
Verse: And those who were mindful of their Lord will be led to Paradise in ˹successive˺ groups. When they arrive at its ˹already˺ open gates, its keepers will say, “Peace be upon you! You have done well, so come in, to stay forever.”

Tafsir: And those who feared their Lord will be driven gently to Paradise in troops until when they reach it and its gates are opened wa-futihat the wāw here indicates a circumstantial qualifier implying qad ‘already’ and its keepers will say to them ‘Peace be to you! You are good! tibtum a circumstantial qualifier So enter it to abide therein’ — enter it with the decree that you are to abide in it forever the response to idhā ‘when’ is implicit and is in other words dakhalūhā ‘they enter it’. The manner of their being driven as well as the opening of the gates before their arrival is a way of honouring them; the driving of the disbelievers however and the opening of the gates only upon their arrival so that all of its heat is retained for them is a means of humiliating them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are mindful of their Lord?
How do the keepers of Paradise greet its visitors?
What is the ultimate fate of those who enter Paradise?
propositions: Those who were mindful of their Lord will be led to Paradise in successive groups.
The keepers of Paradise say, 'Peace be upon you! You have done well, so come in, to stay forever.'
Paradise is driven gently to those who fear their Lord.
Its gates are opened for them when they reach it.
All of its heat is retained for the disbelievers as a means of humiliating them.

source_text:
Verse: The righteous will say, “Praise be to Allah Who has fulfilled His promise to us, and made us inherit the ˹everlasting˺ land to settle in Paradise wherever we please.” How excellent is the reward of those who work ˹righteousness˺!

Tafsir: And they will say this is a supplement to the implicit response dakhalūhā ‘they enter it’ ‘Praise be to God Who has fulfilled His promise to us of Paradise and has made us inherit the land the land of Paradise that we may settle in Paradise wherever we wish’ for it is all Paradise and there is no spot that can be preferred to another. So how excellent is Paradise as the reward of those who worked hard!

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reward for those who work righteousness?
Can we choose our destination in Paradise?
Is there a better place to settle in Paradise?
propositions: The righteous will inherit the land of Paradise.
Paradise has no spot that can be preferred to another.
Allah has fulfilled His promise to those who work righteousness.

source_text:
Verse: You will see the angels all around the Throne, glorifying the praises of their Lord, for judgment will have been passed on all with fairness. And it will be said, “Praise be to Allah—Lord of all worlds!”

Tafsir: And you will see the angels encircling hāffīna a circumstantial qualifier all round the Throne from its every side glorifying yusabbihūn is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person of the participle hāffīn with praise of their Lord continuously proclaiming His praise — in other words saying subhāna’Llāhi wa-bi-hamdih ‘Glory and praise be to God!’ — and judgement will be made between them that is between all creatures with truth in other words with justice so that believers enter Paradise while the disbelievers enter the Fire and it will be said ‘Praise be to God the Lord of the Worlds!’ — the final establishing of both groups in their respective abodes is concluded with this angelic praise.

hype_questions: What is the nature of judgment in Islam?
How do believers and disbelievers differ in their fate?
What is the significance of angelic praise in Islamic eschatology?
propositions: You will see the angels all around the Throne glorifying the praises of their Lord.
Judgment will have been passed on all with fairness.
Praise be to Allah—Lord of all worlds!—and judgement will be made between them that is between all creatures with truth in other words with justice.

source_text:
Verse: ha-Mĩm.

Tafsir: Hā mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

hype_questions: Does God have a specific meaning in mind when using the letter mīm?
Can humans truly understand the intentions of God?
What does it mean for God to 'know best'?
propositions: Hā mīm means that God knows best what He means by these letters.
God has a specific meaning in mind when using the letter mīm.
Humans cannot truly understand the intentions of God.

source_text:
Verse: The revelation of this Book is from Allah—the Almighty, All-Knowing,

Tafsir: The revelation of the Book the Qur’ān tanzīlu’l-kitābi is the subject is from God mina’Llāhi is its predicate the Mighty in His kingdom the Knower of His creatures.

hype_questions: What is the source of the Qur'ān?
Who is the Mighty in His kingdom?
What does it mean to be the Knower of His creatures?
propositions: The revelation of the Book is from Allah.
Allah is the Mighty in His kingdom.
God is the Knower of His creatures.

source_text:
Verse: the Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance, the Severe in punishment, and Infinite in bounty. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. To Him ˹alone˺  is the final return.

Tafsir: Forgiver of sins for believers and Accepter of repentance from them al-tawb is the verbal noun Severe in punishment of disbelievers — in other words One Who makes it severe for them — One of abundant bounty bestower of abundant grace — God is eternally possessed of all of these attributes and so the annexation construction using the derivatives of these attributes is for the purposes of characterisation as in the case of the last. There is no god except Him; to Him is the journeying the ultimate return.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's punishment for disbelievers?
How does God respond to the repentance of believers?
What are some of the attributes that describe God's character?
propositions: God is the Forgiver of sins for believers.
God is the Accepter of repentance from believers.
God is Severe in punishment for disbelievers.
God is Infinite in bounty and bestows abundant grace.

source_text:
Verse: None disputes the signs of Allah except the disbelievers, so do not be deceived by their prosperity throughout the land.

Tafsir: None dispute the signs of God — the Qur’ān — except those who disbelieve from among the people of Mecca so do not be deceived by their bustle in the towns going about seeking their livelihood in security for the sequel for them will be the Fire.

hype_questions: What happens to those who disbelieve in the signs of God?
Why should we not be deceived by the prosperity of those who reject faith?
What is the ultimate fate of those who seek security through worldly means?
propositions: None disputes the signs of Allah except the disbelievers.
The Qur’ān is a sign from God.
Those who disbelieve in Mecca will be deceived by their prosperity.
Seeking security through worldly means is not secure.
Their ultimate fate is the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: Before them, the people of Noah denied ˹the truth˺, as did ˹other˺ enemy forces afterwards. Every community plotted against its prophet to seize him, and argued in falsehood, ˹hoping˺ to discredit the truth with it. So I seized them. And how ˹horrible˺ was My punishment!

Tafsir: The people of Noah denied before them and also the factions such as ‘Ād Thamūd and others who came after them. And every community sought to seize their messenger to slay him and they argued falsely thinking to rebut to eliminate thereby the truth. Then I seized them with punishment; so how fitting was My punishment! of them — in other words it was appropriate.

hype_questions: What happens when a community denies the truth?
How do people react when their prophet is threatened?
Can punishment ever be fitting for those who deny the truth?
propositions: The people of Noah denied the truth.
Every community plotted against its prophet to seize him.
I seized them with punishment.

source_text:
Verse: And so your Lord’s decree has been proven true against the disbelievers—that they will be the inmates of the Fire.

Tafsir: And thus was the word of your Lord — namely the verse Assuredly I will fill Hell … Q. 11119 — fulfilled against those who disbelieve that they shall be the inhabitants of the Fire annahum ashābu’l-nāri substitutes for kalimatu ‘the word’.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who disbelieve?
Will the disbelievers be punished?
Who will inhabit the Fire?
propositions: Your Lord's decree has been proven true against the disbelievers.
Those who disbelieve shall be the inmates of the Fire.
The word of your Lord fulfilled against those who disbelieve that they shall be the inhabitants of the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: Those ˹angels˺ who carry the Throne and those around it glorify the praises of their Lord, have faith in Him, and seek forgiveness for the believers, ˹praying:˺ “Our Lord! You encompass everything in ˹Your˺ mercy and knowledge. So forgive those who repent and follow Your Way, and protect them from the torment of the Hellfire.

Tafsir: Those who bear the Throne alladhīna yahmilūna’l-‘arsha is the subject and those around it wa-man hawlahu is a supplement to that subject glorify yusabbihūna is the predicate thereof with praise of their Lord continuously proclaiming praise in other words continuously saying subhāna’Llāhi wa-bi-hamdihi ‘Glory and praise be to God’; and they believe in Him exalted be He through their power of discernment in other words they affirm the truth of His Oneness and they ask forgiveness for those who believe saying ‘Our Lord You embrace all things in Your mercy and knowledge that is to say Your mercy embraces all things and Your knowledge also embraces all things. So forgive those who repent of idolatry and follow Your way — the religion of Islam — and shield them from the chastisement of Hell-fire that is the Fire.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's mercy and knowledge?
How can humans seek forgiveness from God?
What is the ultimate punishment for those who reject Islam?
propositions: God encompasses everything in His mercy.
God's knowledge also embraces all things.
Those who repent and follow God's way will be forgiven.

source_text:
Verse: Our Lord! Admit them into the Gardens of Eternity which You have promised them, along with the righteous among their parents, spouses, and descendants. You ˹alone˺ are truly the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: Our Lord and admit them into the Gardens of Eden as a place of residence for them that which You have promised them along with whoever were righteous wa-man salaha is a supplement either to the pronominal third person plural suffix hum ‘them’ in wa-adkhilhum ‘and admit them’ or in wa‘adttahum ‘You have promised them’ among their fathers and their wives and their descendants. Surely You are the One Who is the Mighty the Wise in what He does.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate destination for those who are righteous in their faith?
How does Allah reward the righteous among their parents, spouses, and descendants?
What qualities make someone righteous in the eyes of Allah?
propositions: Our Lord admits them into the Gardens of Eternity which You have promised them.
You admit them into the Gardens of Eden as a place of residence for them that which You have promised them.
Allah rewards the righteous among their parents, spouses, and descendants.

source_text:
Verse: And protect them from ˹the consequences of their˺ evil deeds. For whoever You protect from the evil of their deeds on that Day will have been shown Your mercy. That is ˹truly˺ the ultimate triumph.”

Tafsir: And shield them from evil deeds that is from the chastisement thereof; for whomever You shield from evil deeds that day the Day of Resurrection verily him You will have had been merciful to; and that is indeed the supreme triumph’.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah protects us from our evil deeds on the Day of Resurrection?
How does Allah's protection from evil deeds relate to His mercy?
What is considered ultimate triumph in Islam?
propositions: Allah protects individuals from the consequences of their evil deeds.
Whomever Allah shields from the evil of their deeds on that Day will have been shown His mercy.
The ultimate triumph is indeed Allah's mercy.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, it will be announced to the disbelievers, “Allah’s contempt for you—as you disbelieved when invited to belief—was far worse than your contempt for one another ˹Today˺.”

Tafsir: Indeed to those who disbelieve it will be proclaimed to them from the part of the angels as they disbelievers enter the Fire in utter loathing of themselves ‘Surely God’s loathing of you is greater than your loathing of yourselves as you were called during life in this world to faith but you used to disbelieve’.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's contempt for those who reject Him?
How does one's contempt for themselves compare to Allah's contempt for them?
What was the purpose of inviting people to faith in this life?
propositions: Allah's contempt for disbelievers is greater than their contempt for each other.
God loathes those who reject Him more than they loathe themselves.
People were called to faith during their lifetime, but rejected it.

source_text:
Verse: They will plead, “Our Lord! You made us lifeless twice, and gave us life twice. Now we confess our sins. So is there any way out?”

Tafsir: They will say ‘Our Lord You have caused us to die twice two deaths and You have given us life twice — for they were lifeless drops of semen then they were given life then made to die then brought back to life for the Resurrection. We now confess our sins in having disbelieved in the Resurrection. Is there then any way to go out?’ out of the Fire and return to the world to be obedient to our Lord? The answer given to them will be No!

hype_questions: Is there any way out of the Fire?
Can we return to the world and be obedient to our Lord after disbelieving in Resurrection?
What is the outcome for those who confess their sins after being given life twice?
propositions: They were lifeless drops of semen before being given life.
They were made to die before being brought back to life for the Resurrection.
The answer given to them will be No! for those who confess their sins after being given life twice.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They will be told,˺ “˹No!˺ This is because when Allah alone was invoked, you ˹staunchly˺ disbelieved. But when others were associated with Him ˹in worship˺, you ˹readily˺ believed. So ˹Today˺ judgment belongs to Allah ˹alone˺—the Most High, All-Great.”

Tafsir: That namely the chastisement which you find yourselves in is because during the life of this world when God was invoked alone you would disbelieve in His Oneness; but if partners were ascribed to Him you would believe you would accept such idolatry. So the judgement to chastise you belongs to God the Exalted above His creation the Great the Tremendous.

hype_questions: What happens when you disbelieve in the Oneness of Allah?
How do you respond to idolatry when partners are ascribed to Allah?
Who is responsible for judging us on the Day of Reckoning?
propositions: When Allah alone was invoked, they disbelieved in His Oneness.
When others were associated with Him in worship, they believed.
Judgment belongs to Allah alone—the Most High, All-Great.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who shows you His signs and sends down ˹rain as˺ a provision for you from the sky. ˹But˺ none will be mindful except those who turn ˹to Him˺.

Tafsir: He it is Who shows you His signs the proofs of His Oneness and sends down from the heaven for you provision by way of rain. Yet no one remembers no one is admonished except him who returns penitently who recants idolatry.

hype_questions: What are the signs of Allah?
Why does Allah send down rain as a provision?
How can one return to Allah and be admonished?
propositions: Allah shows you His signs.
Allah sends down from the heaven for you provision by way of rain.
No one remembers or is admonished except him who returns penitently who recants idolatry.

source_text:
Verse: So call upon Allah with sincere devotion, even to the dismay of the disbelievers.

Tafsir: So supplicate God worship Him devoting your religion purely to Him free from any idolatry however much the disbelievers be averse to its being free of such idolatry.

hype_questions: What is the correct way to worship Allah?
How can one ensure their religion is free from idolatry?
What happens when disbelievers are averse to the idea of pure monotheism?
propositions: Call upon Allah with sincere devotion.
Supplicate God worship Him devoting your religion purely to Him.
Your religion should be free from any idolatry.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is˺ Highly Exalted in rank, Lord of the Throne. He sends down the revelation by His command to whoever He wills of His servants to warn ˹all˺ of the Day of Meeting—

Tafsir: Exalter of ranks either means that God is One Whose attributes are majestic — or it means the raiser of the ranks of believers in Paradise — Lord of the Throne in other words the Creator thereof He casts the Spirit the Revelation of His command that is of His words upon whomever He will of His servants that he the one upon whom it is cast may warn them of that he may make people fear the Day of Encounter read yawma’l-talāqi omitting the final long yā’ or yawma’l-talāqī that is to say the Day of Resurrection so called because thereat the inhabitants of the heavens will encounter those of the earth and the worshipper will encounter the one whom he worshipped and the wrongdoer will encounter the person whom he wronged;

hype_questions: What is the Day of Resurrection?
How does God send down revelation to His servants?
What is the purpose of warning people of the Day of Meeting?
propositions: God is Highly Exalted in rank.
God is the Lord of the Throne and casts the Spirit upon whomever He wills.
God sends down the revelation by His command to whoever He wills of His servants.
The purpose of warning people is to make them fear the Day of Resurrection.
The inhabitants of heaven will encounter those of earth on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: the Day all will appear ˹before Allah˺. Nothing about them will be hidden from Him. ˹He will ask,˺ “Who does all authority belong to this Day? To Allah—the One, the Supreme!

Tafsir: the day when they will emerge the day they will exit from their graves; nothing about them will be hidden from God. ‘To whom does Sovereignty belong today?’ — God exalted be He asks this and Himself responds — ‘To God the One the All-compelling!’ over His creatures.

hype_questions: What will happen to humanity on the Day of Resurrection?
Who has ultimate authority over all creation?
Will anyone be able to escape accountability on that day?
propositions: The Day of Resurrection is a time when all individuals will emerge from their graves.
Nothing about an individual's actions or circumstances will be hidden from God on the Day of Resurrection.
Sovereignty belongs to Allah, the One and Supreme, over all His creatures.

source_text:
Verse: Today every soul will be rewarded for what it has done. No injustice Today! Surely Allah is swift in reckoning.”

Tafsir: Today every soul shall be requited for what it has earned; there will be no injustice today. Indeed God is swift at reckoning’ reckoning with all of creation in the space of half a day of the days of this world — a hadīth states this.

hype_questions: Will every soul be rewarded for its actions?
Is there to be no injustice today?
How does God's reckoning work?
propositions: Every soul will be rewarded for what it has done.
There will be no injustice today.
God is swift at reckoning with all of creation in the space of half a day.

source_text:
Verse: Warn them ˹O Prophet˺ of the approaching Day when the hearts will jump into the throats, suppressing distress. The wrongdoers will have neither a close friend nor intercessor to be heard.

Tafsir: And warn them of the Impending Day namely the Day of Resurrection al-azifa as in azifa al-rahīlu ‘departure is very near’ when the hearts will rising up in fear reach the throats choking with anguish filled with suppressed anxiety kāzimīna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-qulūbu ‘the hearts’ which is qualified by the active animate participle plural kāzimīna and referred to as though they were the very individuals themselves. The evildoers will not have any intimate friend any sympathiser nor any intercessor who might be heeded — the adjectival qualification ‘who might be heeded’ has no literal significance for they do not have intercessors in the first place So now we have no intercessors … Q. 26100. The first part however may be said to have significance if understand on the basis of their claim to have intercessors and so in other words even if — hypothetically speaking — they their intercessors did intercede for them they would not be heeded.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are wrongdoers on the Day of Resurrection?
Can anyone intercede for a wrongdoer on the Day of Resurrection?
Will a wrongdoer be heard even if they have an intercessor?
propositions: The approaching Day will bring great distress.
Wrongdoers will not have any intimate friend or sympathiser.
Even if their intercessors did intercede for them, they would still not be heeded.

source_text:
Verse: Allah ˹even˺ knows the sly glances of the eyes and whatever the hearts conceal.

Tafsir: He namely God knows the treachery of the eyes when it steals a glance at what is prohibited for it to look at and what the breasts hide — what the hearts hide.

hype_questions: Does God know our true intentions?
Can God see into the hearts of humans?
What is forbidden for us to look at?
propositions: Allah knows the treachery of the eyes when it steals a glance at what is prohibited for it to look at.
The breasts hide what the hearts hide.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah judges with the truth, while those ˹idols˺ they invoke besides Him cannot judge at all. Indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

Tafsir: And God decrees with truth while those on whom they call whom they worship that is the disbelievers of Mecca read yad‘ūna ‘they call’ or tad‘ūna ‘you call’ besides Him — and these are the idols — do not decree by any means at all so how can they be God’s associates? Truly God is the Hearer of their sayings the Seer of their actions.

hype_questions: Can idols judge at all?
How can those who worship idols be considered God's associates?
Does God not decree with truth?
propositions: Allah judges with the truth.
Those who invoke idols besides Allah cannot judge at all.
God is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not travelled throughout the land to see what was the end of those ˹destroyed˺ before them? They were far superior in might and ˹richer in˺ monuments throughout the land. But Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah.

Tafsir: Have they not travelled in the land and beheld the nature of the consequence for those who were before them? They were more powerful than them a variant reading has minkum ‘than yourselves’ in strength and in their vestiges on earth in the way of large structures and palaces. Yet God seized them He destroyed them for their sins and they had none to shield them from God from His chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are destroyed by God?
How do we measure the power and wealth of a nation?
Can anyone shield us from God's chastisement?
propositions: Those who were before them were destroyed for their sins.
They were more powerful than themselves in strength and had larger structures on earth.
God seized them and had no protector to shield them from His chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: That was because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they persisted in disbelief. So Allah seized them. Surely He is All-Powerful, severe in punishment.

Tafsir: That was because their messengers used to bring them clear signs manifest miracles but they disbelieved. So God seized them. Indeed He is Strong Severe in punishment.

hype_questions: What happens when people reject clear signs from their messengers?
How does Allah respond to those who disbelieve in His miracles?
What is the nature of Allah's power and severity?
propositions: Their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs.
They persisted in disbelief despite receiving clear signs and manifest miracles from their messengers.
Allah seized those who disbelieved.
Allah is All-Powerful.
Allah is Severe in punishment.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs and compelling proof

Tafsir: And verily We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear warrant an evident and manifest proof

hype_questions: What are the signs that God sent to Moses?
How did God prove His existence to Moses?
What is the nature of the proof that God gave to Moses?
propositions: God sent Moses with signs.
Moses received a clear warrant from God.
The signs sent by God are evident and manifest.

source_text:
Verse: to Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah. But they responded: “Magician! Total liar!”

Tafsir: to Pharaoh and Hāmān and Korah but they said — that he was — ‘A sorcerer a mere liar!’

hype_questions: Does Pharaoh and Haman believe in the magician's powers?
What do Korah and Pharaoh think about the magician's claims?
Do Hāmān and Korah consider the magician a sorcerer or a liar?
propositions: Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah rejected the magician's claim.
They considered the magician a mere sorcerer.
The magician was labeled as a total liar by Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah.

source_text:
Verse: Then, when he came to them with the truth from Us, they said, “Kill the sons of those who believe with him and keep their women.” But the plotting of the disbelievers was only in vain.

Tafsir: So when he brought them the truth from Us they said ‘Slay the sons of those who believe with him and spare keep alive their women’. But the guile of the disbelievers is ever in error in perdition.

hype_questions: What would happen if someone brought the truth to a group of people?
How did the disbelievers react when faced with the truth?
What is the nature of the plotting of the disbelievers?
propositions: When he came to them with the truth from Us, they said, 'Kill the sons of those who believe with him and keep their women.'
The plotting of the disbelievers was only in vain.
The guile of the disbelievers is ever in error in perdition.

source_text:
Verse: And Pharaoh said, “Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord! I truly fear that he may change your traditions or cause mischief in the land.”

Tafsir: And Pharaoh said ‘Let me slay Moses — for they used to restrain him from slaying him — and let him call to his Lord to defend him against me. Indeed I fear that he may change your religion involving your worship of me so that you will then follow him in his religion or that he may cause corruption to appear in the land’ by initiating killing and otherwise a variant reading for wa-an ‘and that’ is aw-an ‘or that’; a variant reading for an yuzhira fī’l-ardi’l-fasāda is the impersonal construction an yazhara fī’l-ardi’l-fasādu ‘that corruption may appear in the land’.

hype_questions: What would happen if Pharaoh were to kill Moses?
How might Moses' actions affect the worship of Pharaoh in Egypt?
Could Moses' religion potentially lead to corruption in the land?
propositions: Pharaoh said, 'Let me slay Moses.'
They used to restrain him from slaying him.
Moses called upon his Lord to defend himself against Pharaoh.
Pharaoh feared that Moses might change their religion involving worship of him.
Pharaoh feared that Moses might cause corruption to appear in the land.

source_text:
Verse: Moses replied, “I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.”

Tafsir: And Moses said to his people after he had heard that saying of Pharaoh ‘Indeed I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning’.

hype_questions: What is the Day of Reckoning?
How can one seek refuge from arrogance?
Who is considered arrogant in Islamic context?
propositions: Moses sought refuge in his Lord and Pharaoh's Lord from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.
The concept of seeking refuge from arrogance is emphasized in this verse.
Pharaoh's statement was misinterpreted by Moses' people.

source_text:
Verse: A believing man from Pharaoh’s people, who was hiding his faith, argued, “Will you kill a man ˹only˺ for saying: ‘My Lord is Allah,’ while he has in fact come to you with clear proofs from your Lord? If he is a liar, it will be to his own loss. But if he is truthful, then you will be afflicted with some of what he is threatening you with. Surely Allah does not guide whoever is a transgressor, a total liar.

Tafsir: Then said a believing man from among Pharaoh’s folk — this is said to have been his paternal cousin — who had concealed his faith ‘Will you slay a man for saying “My Lord is God” even though he has also brought you clear signs manifest miracles from your Lord? If he is lying then his mendacity will be to his own detriment that is the harm resulting from his mendacity will be to his own detriment; but if he is truthful then there will befall you some of that with which he is threatening you in the way of chastisement soon. Truly God does not guide one who is a prodigal an idolater a liar.

hype_questions: What happens if someone claims to be a believer but is actually a liar?
Can someone threaten you with punishment and still be truthful about their faith?
How does God respond to those who are deceitful or idolatrous?
propositions: A believing man from Pharaoh's people argued that killing someone for saying 'My Lord is Allah' would be unjust.
If someone claims to have come with clear proofs from their Lord, they should not be killed for their faith.
God does not guide those who are transgressors or liars.
Deception will ultimately harm the deceiver.
Miracles can serve as evidence of a person's faith.
Chastisement may befall those who threaten others with punishment if they are not truthful about their intentions.

source_text:
Verse: O  my people! Authority belongs to you today, reigning supreme in the land. But who would help us against the torment of Allah, if it were to befall us?” Pharaoh assured ˹his people˺, “I am telling you only what I believe, and I am leading you only to the way of guidance.”

Tafsir: O my people! Today the kingdom is yours you are dominant prevailing zāhirīna a circumstantial qualifier in the land the land of Egypt. But who will help us against the might of God against His chastisement if you resolve to slay His friends should it reach us?’ In other words we would have no helper. Pharaoh said ‘I only point out to you what I see to be best that is to say I only suggest to you what I suggest to myself and that is to kill Moses would be best; and I am only guiding you to the path of rectitude’ to the correct way.

hype_questions: What would happen if Pharaoh's people were to resolve to slay God's friends?
Who would help Pharaoh's people against the torment of God?
What is the correct way that Pharaoh suggests?
propositions: The kingdom belongs to Pharaoh's people today.
Pharaoh believes he is leading his people to guidance.
Killing Moses would be best for Pharaoh's people.
Pharaoh is only guiding his people to the path of rectitude.

source_text:
Verse: And the man who believed cautioned, “O my people! I truly fear for you the doom of ˹earlier˺ enemy forces—

Tafsir: Then said he who believed ‘O my people! Truly I fear for you a day like the day of the factions in other words the day of one faction being destroyed after another;

hype_questions: What is the consequence of not believing in a warning?
How does the destruction of one faction relate to another?
What is the nature of the doom mentioned in the verse?
propositions: The man who believed fears for his people.
He believes that a day will come when factions are destroyed after another.
This day will be similar to the day of the factions.

source_text:
Verse: like the fate of the people of Noah, ’Ȃd, Thamûd, and those after them. For Allah would never will to wrong ˹His˺ servants.

Tafsir: like the case of the people of Noah and ‘Ād and Thamūd and those who came after them mithla ‘like’ substitutes for the previous mithla ‘like’ in other words the same requital as was customarily dealt to those who disbelieved before you of their being chastised in this world and God does not desire to wrong any of His servants.

hype_questions: Does Allah desire to wrong any of His servants?
What is the requital dealt to those who disbelieved before you?
How does Allah deal with those who disbelieve?
propositions: Allah would never will to wrong His servants.
Those who disbelieved before you were chastised in this world.
God does not desire to wrong any of His servants.

source_text:
Verse: O  my people! I truly fear for you the Day all will be crying out ˹to each other˺—

Tafsir: And O my people! Truly I fear for you a day of mutual calling read yawma’l-tanādi omitting the final long yā’ or retaining it thus yawma’l-tanādī that is to say the Day of Resurrection in which repeated calls are made by those meriting Paradise to those meriting the Fire and vice versa as well as calls proclaiming good fortune for those who merit the former and misery for those who merit the latter and many other such calls

hype_questions: What is the Day of Resurrection?
Who will be called to Paradise and the Fire?
How will good fortune and misery be determined?
propositions: There will be a Day of Resurrection.
Those who merit Paradise will be called by those who merit it, while those who merit the Fire will be called by those who merit it.

Verse: So He formed the heaven into seven heavens in two Days, assigning to each its mandate. And We adorned the lowest heaven with ˹stars like˺ lamps ˹for beauty˺ and for protection. That is the design of the Almighty, All-Knowing.”

Tafsir: Then He ordained them the suffixed pronoun refers back to al-samā’ ‘the heaven’ because it al-samā’ actually denotes that plural sense to which it will lead in the following clause in other words He made them to be seven heavens in two days — Thursday and Friday. He completed them in the last hour thereof in which He created Adam — which is why He does not say sawā’an ‘evenly’ here as He did earlier; what is said here concords with those verse in which it is stated that the heavens and the earth were created in six days; and in each heaven He revealed its commandment’ that to which He commanded those in it to follow in the way of obedience and worship. And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps with stars and this was also to guard them hifzan is in the accusative because of its implicit verbal sense in other words ‘We guarded it against the devils lest they try to listen therein to the angels by stealth with meteors’. That is the ordaining of the Mighty in His kingdom the Knower of His creatures.

hype_questions: What happens to the enemies of God on Judgment Day?
Will God's enemies be punished in the Fire?
How are God's enemies gathered for the Fire?
propositions: The enemies of Allah will be gathered for the Fire.
God’s enemies are gathered read either yuhsharu a‘dā’u’Llāhi or nahshuru a‘dā’a’Llāhi ‘when We gather God’s enemies’.
They will be driven thereto

source_text:
Verse: When they reach it, their ears, eyes, and skin will testify against what they used to do.

Tafsir: until when they reach it idhā mā the mā is extra their hearing and their eyes and their skins will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do.

hype_questions: What happens when someone reaches a certain point in their life?
How will people be held accountable for their actions?
What consequences can one expect after reaching a specific milestone?
propositions: When they reach it, their ears, eyes, and skin will testify against what they used to do.
Their hearing and eyes and skins will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do.

source_text:
Verse: They will ask their skin ˹furiously˺, “Why have you testified against us?” It will say, “We have been made to speak by Allah, Who causes all things to speak. He ˹is the One Who˺ created you the first time, and to Him you were bound to return.

Tafsir: And they will say to their skins ‘Why did you bear witness against us?’ They will say ‘God made us speak Who gave speech to all things in other words all things which He wanted to be able to speak. And He created you the first time and to Him you will be returned it is said that this statement is made by their skins; but it is also said to be God’s words as is the case with what follows for it is similar in context to what preceded namely that the One with the power to originate you without any precedent and restore you to life after death also has the power to make your skins and your limbs speak.

hype_questions: What is the nature of prophetic speech?
Can inanimate objects be said to 'speak'?
Is there a universal power that can animate all things?
propositions: God made us speak.
Allah gave speech to all things.
You were created by Allah the first time and will return to Him.

source_text:
Verse: You did not ˹bother to˺ hide yourselves from your ears, eyes, and skin to prevent them from testifying against you. Rather, you assumed that Allah did not know much of what you used to do.

Tafsir: And you did not use to conceal yourselves when you used to commit lewd acts lest your hearing or your eyes or your skins should bear witness against you because you were never certain about the truth of resurrection; but you thought when you used to conceal yourselves that God did not know most of what you did.

hype_questions: What happens if my actions are revealed after death?
Can God know everything about human behavior?
How will I be held accountable for my deeds?
propositions: You did not hide yourselves from Allah's creation to prevent it from testifying against you.
You used to commit lewd acts without concealing yourselves, fearing your hearing or eyes would bear witness against you.
You were uncertain about the truth of resurrection and thought God was unaware of your actions.

source_text:
Verse: It was that ˹false˺ assumption you entertained about your Lord that has brought about your doom, so you have become losers.”

Tafsir: And that wa-dhālikum the subject supposition of yours zannukum substitutes for it which you supposed of your Lord alladhī zanantum bi-rabbikum a descriptive clause; the predicate is the following ardākum has ruined you that is it has brought about your destruction. So you have become among the losers’.

hype_questions: What assumption can lead to one's downfall?
How does a false belief about one's Lord affect their fate?
What is the consequence of entertaining a mistaken idea about God?
propositions: You entertained a false assumption about your Lord.
This assumption has brought about your destruction.
As a result, you have become among the losers.

source_text:
Verse: Even if they endure patiently, the Fire will ˹always˺ be their home. And if they ˹beg to˺ appease ˹their Lord˺, they will never be allowed to.

Tafsir: So if they endure the chastisement the Fire will still be their abode; and if they seek reconciliation if they seek the satisfaction of God then they will not be among the reconciled those deemed satisfactory by God.

hype_questions: What happens to those who endure patiently in the face of adversity?
Can seeking reconciliation with God change their fate?
What is the ultimate destination for those who are deemed satisfactory by God?
propositions: The Fire will always be the home of those who endure patiently.
If they seek reconciliation, they will not be among the reconciled.
God's satisfaction is not attainable through human means.

source_text:
Verse: We placed at their disposal ˹evil˺ associates who made their past and future ˹misdeeds˺ appealing to them. ˹So˺ the fate of earlier communities of jinn and humans has been justified against them ˹as well˺, ˹for˺ they were truly losers.

Tafsir: And We have assigned We have occasioned for them companions from among the devils who have adorned for them that which is before them of what concerns this world and the following after lusts and that which is behind them of what concerns the Hereafter when they make them say that there will be neither resurrection nor reckoning. And the word of chastisement — namely the verse Assuredly I will fill Hell … Q. 11119 — became due against them being among all those communities that passed away that were destroyed before them of jinn and mankind. Truly they were losers.

hype_questions: Will there be a resurrection after death?
What is the punishment for those who deny the Hereafter?
Are those who have been destroyed before us doomed to eternal suffering?
propositions: We placed evil associates at their disposal.
Their past and future misdeeds are appealing to them.
The fate of earlier communities has been justified against them.
They were truly losers.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers advised ˹one another˺, “Do not listen to this Quran but drown it out so that you may prevail.”

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve say during the Prophet’s s recitation of the Qur’ān ‘Do not listen to this Qur’ān and hoot it down make a din and so forth and clamour whenever he is reciting that perhaps you might prevail’ so that he will then desist from recitation.

hype_questions: Can listening to the Quran lead to success?
How can one counter the negative effects of disbelievers on a prophet's recitation?
What is the purpose behind the Prophet's recitation of the Quran?
propositions: The disbelievers advised each other not to listen to the Quran.
Those who disbelieve say that one should not listen to the Quran and instead make a din when the Prophet is reciting it.
The Prophet's recitation of the Quran may lead to success if one listens to it.

source_text:
Verse: So We will certainly make the disbelievers taste a severe punishment, and We will surely repay them according to the worst of their deeds.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says regarding them But verily We will make those who disbelieve taste a severe chastisement and We will verily requite them the worst of what they used to do in other words with the worst requital for their deeds.

hype_questions: What is the punishment that God will make the disbelievers taste?
How will God repay the disbelievers according to their deeds?
What is the worst requital for the deeds of those who disbelieve?
propositions: God will make the disbelievers taste a severe chastisement.
God will repay the disbelievers according to the worst of their deeds.
The disbelievers will receive the worst requital for their deeds.

source_text:
Verse: That is the reward of Allah’s enemies: the Fire, which will be their eternal home—a ˹fitting˺ reward for their denial of Our revelations.

Tafsir: That severe chastisement and worst requital is the requital of God’s enemies jazā’u a‘dā’i the second hamza may be pronounced fully or replaced with a wāw — the Fire! al-nāru an explicative supplement to jazā’u ‘the requital’ alluded to by the demonstrative dhālika ‘that’. Therein will be their everlasting abode that is as a place of permanent residence from which there will be no removal as a requital jazā’an is in the accusative as a verbal noun from the implicit verbal action for their denial of Our signs for their denial of the Qur’ān.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who deny Allah's revelations?
Will the Fire be their eternal home?
How will Allah requite His enemies?
propositions: The reward of Allah’s enemies is the Fire.
That severe chastisement and worst requital is the requital of God’s enemies.
Therein will be their everlasting abode that is as a place of permanent residence from which there will be no removal.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers will ˹then˺ cry, “Our Lord! Show us those jinn and humans who led us astray: we will put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest ˹in Hell˺.”

Tafsir: And those who disbelieve will say while in the Fire ‘Our Lord show us those who led us astray from among the jinn and mankind — namely Iblīs and Cain respectively both of whom established disbelief and slaying as something to be emulated — so that we may have them underneath our feet to trample them in the Fire that they may be among the lowermost’ in other words in a chastisement more severe than ours.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of disbelief in Islam?
How do humans and jinn end up in Hell?
What is the significance of Iblīs and Cain in Islamic theology?
propositions: The disbelievers will be shown those who led them astray.
Iblīs and Cain established disbelief and slaying as something to be emulated.
Those who disbelieve will be punished more severely than others.

source_text:
Verse: Surely those who say, “Our Lord is Allah,” and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, ˹saying,˺ “Do not fear, nor grieve. Rather, rejoice in the good news of Paradise, which you have been promised.

Tafsir: Truly those who say ‘Our Lord is God!’ and then remain upright adhering to the affirmation of God’s Oneness and to whatever else has been enjoined on them the angels descend upon them at the point of death saying to them ‘Do not fear death and what will come after it nor grieve for any family or children that you have left behind for we will look after them after you and rejoice in the good tidings of the paradise which you were promised.

hype_questions: What happens to those who say 'Our Lord is Allah' and remain steadfast?
How do angels interact with believers at the point of death?
What promises does God make to believers about their families and children left behind?
propositions: Those who say 'Our Lord is Allah' and remain steadfast will be visited by angels at the point of death.
The angels tell believers not to fear or grieve, but rather rejoice in the good news of Paradise.
God promises to look after the families and children left behind after believers pass away.

source_text:
Verse: We are your supporters in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. There you will have whatever your souls desire, and there you will have whatever you ask for:

Tafsir: We are your friends in the life of this world that is we will look after you in it and in the Hereafter in other words we will be alongside you thereat until you enter Paradise; and therein you will have whatever your souls desire and therein you will have whatever you request

hype_questions: What will I have in the Hereafter?
Will I be looked after in this worldly life and the Hereafter?
What will I desire in Paradise?
propositions: We are your supporters in this worldly life and in the Hereafter.
You will have whatever your souls desire in the Hereafter.
You will have whatever you ask for in the HereAfter.

source_text:
Verse: an accommodation from the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful ˹Lord˺.”

Tafsir: as a hospitality a pre-prepared provision nuzulan is in the accusative because of an implied preceding verb ‘appointed for you’ from One Forgiving Merciful’ namely God.

hype_questions: What is the nature of nuzulan in Islam?
How does God provide for His servants?
What is meant by 'hospitality' in Islamic context?
propositions: The All-Forgiving, Most Merciful Lord has provided a pre-prepared provision.
This provision is an accommodation from God.
Nuzulan is a hospitality provided by God.

source_text:
Verse: And whose words are better than someone who calls ˹others˺ to Allah, does good, and says, “I am truly one of those who submit.”?

Tafsir: And who speaks better words — in other words no one speaks better words — than him who summons others to God by affirming His Oneness and acts righteously and says ‘Indeed I am one of those who submit to God’?

hype_questions: What are the qualities of a person who summons others to Allah?
How does one demonstrate their submission to Allah?
What is the significance of affirming Tawhid?
propositions: Someone who calls others to Allah and acts righteously is considered one of those who submit to God.
Summoning others to Allah by affirming His Oneness is a superior form of speech.
Righteous action and affirmation of Tawhid are essential characteristics of a person who submits to God.

source_text:
Verse: Good and evil cannot be equal. Respond ˹to evil˺ with what is best, then the one you are in a feud with will be like a close friend.

Tafsir: And they are not equal the good deed and the evil deed even with respect to their subdivisions because any number of such good deeds are always above any number of the latter. Repel the evil deed with that in other words with that trait which is better such as repelling anger with endurance ignorance with forbearance and the intention to inflict harm with pardon then behold he between whom and you there was enmity will be as though he were a dear friend in other words then your enemy will become like a close friend in terms of his affection for you if you act in such a way alladhī ‘he … whom’ is the subject; ka-annahu ‘as though’ is the predicate; idhā is an adverbial particle for expressing the comparative import.

hype_questions: What happens when you respond to evil with good?
How does responding to evil affect your relationship with someone you were once enemies with?
Can responding to evil lead to a deeper connection with someone?
propositions: Good deeds are always superior to evil deeds, regardless of their quantity.
Responding to evil with good is more effective than repelling it with something lesser.
Pardoning and showing forbearance can turn an enemy into a close friend.

source_text:
Verse: But this cannot be attained except by those who are patient and who are truly fortunate.

Tafsir: But none is granted it in other words none is given that better trait except those who are steadfast; and none is granted it except one deserving of a great reward.

hype_questions: What is the key to attaining something in Islam?
Who is eligible for a great reward in Islam?
What trait is highly valued in Islam?
propositions: None is granted a better trait than patience.
None is given a great reward except one who is steadfast.
Patience is the key to attaining something in Islam.

source_text:
Verse: And if you are tempted by Satan, then seek refuge with Allah. Indeed, He ˹alone˺ is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Tafsir: And if wa-immā here the nūn of the conditional particle in has been assimilated with the mā which is extra some temptation from Satan should provoke you in other words if some diversion should turn you away from that better trait and other good acts then seek refuge in God this is the response to the conditional ‘and if’; the response to the command clause is omitted being ‘and He will ward it off from you’. Truly He is the Hearer of what is said the Knower of what is done.

hype_questions: What happens when Satan tempts me?
How can I protect myself from Satan's temptations?
What is the best way to seek refuge from Satan?
propositions: If you are tempted by Satan, then seek refuge with Allah.
Allah is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing.
He will ward off the temptation from you.

source_text:
Verse: Among His signs are the day and the night, the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon, but prostrate to Allah, Who created them ˹all˺, if you ˹truly˺ worship Him ˹alone˺.

Tafsir: And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun and moon but prostrate to God Who created them namely these fours signs if it is Him Whom you worship.

hype_questions: What are the signs of Allah that we should worship Him alone?
Why is it wrong to prostrate to the sun or moon, but not to Allah?
Who created the sun and the moon?
propositions: The day and night are among the signs of Allah.
Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon, but rather to Allah.
Allah is the one who created the sun and the moon.

source_text:
Verse: But if the pagans are too proud, then ˹let them know that˺ those ˹angels˺ nearest to your Lord glorify Him day and night, and never grow weary.

Tafsir: But if they disdain to prostrate to God alone still those who are with your Lord that is to say still the angels glorify perform prayers to Him night and day and they tire not they never weary thereof.

hype_questions: What happens when pagans refuse to prostrate to God alone?
How do angels respond to those who reject God's oneness?
What is the nature of the angels' worship towards God?
propositions: Those nearest to your Lord glorify Him day and night.
The angels perform prayers to God night and day.
They tire not, they never weary thereof.

source_text:
Verse: And among His signs is that you see the earth devoid of life, but as soon as We send down rain upon it, it begins to stir ˹to life˺ and swell. Indeed, the One Who revives it can easily revive the dead. He is certainly Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: And among His signs is that you see the earth desolate dried out without any vegetation but when We send down water upon it it stirs it moves and swells swells and rises. Truly He Who revives it is indeed the Reviver of the dead. Surely He has power over all things.

hype_questions: What can revive the earth after it's been desolate for so long?
How does the power of revival work in nature?
Can anyone else revive the dead like Allah?
propositions: The earth is devoid of life until rain is sent down upon it.
Rain brings life to the earth and causes it to swell.
Allah has the power to revive the dead.
Allah's power is over all things.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who abuse Our revelations are not hidden from Us. Who is better: the one who will be cast into the Fire or the one who will be secure on Judgment Day? Do whatever you want. He is certainly All-Seeing of what you do.

Tafsir: Indeed those who blaspheme yulhidūna derives from the verb alhada or lahada ‘he blasphemed’ Our signs — the Qur’ān by denying its truth — are not hidden from Us and We will requite them. Is one who is cast into the Fire better off or one who arrives secure on the Day of Resurrection? Act as you wish; indeed He is Seer of what you do — this is meant as a threat for them.

hype_questions: Is it better to be cast into the Fire or secure on Judgment Day?
What happens to those who blaspheme against Allah's signs?
Will Allah requite those who deny His signs?
propositions: Those who abuse Our revelations are not hidden from Us.
One who is cast into the Fire is not better off than one who arrives secure on the Day of Resurrection.
He is certainly All-Seeing of what you do.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who deny the Reminder after it has come to them ˹are doomed˺, for it is truly a mighty Book.

Tafsir: Truly those who disbelieve in the Remembrance — the Qur’ān — when it comes to them … We will requite them — and truly it is an unassailable Book

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the Quran after it has been revealed?
Can anyone change or alter the message of the Quran?
How will people be held accountable for their actions if they deny the truth of the Quran?
propositions: Those who deny the Reminder after it has come to them are doomed.
The Qur'ān is a mighty Book.

source_text:
Verse: It cannot be proven false from any angle. ˹It is˺ a revelation from the ˹One Who is˺ All-Wise, Praiseworthy.

Tafsir: falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it in other words there is no scripture before it or after it that contradicts it; it is a revelation from One Wise Praised that is to say from God the One Who is praised in His affair.

hype_questions: What is the nature of a revelation that cannot be proven false?
How does this revelation differ from other scriptures?
What is the significance of this revelation in Islamic theology?
propositions: It cannot be proven false from any angle.
A falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it.
There is no scripture before it or after it that contradicts it.
This revelation is a message from God, the One Who is praised in His affair.

source_text:
Verse: ˹O Prophet!˺ Nothing is said to you ˹by the deniers˺ except what was already said to the messengers before you. Surely your Lord is ˹the Lord˺ of forgiveness and painful punishment.

Tafsir: Nothing is said to you in terms of denial of you except the like of what has already been said to the messengers before you. Surely your Lord is One of forgiveness to believers and also One of painful punishment for disbelievers.

hype_questions: Does God forgive those who reject Him?
What is the nature of God's punishment for those who deny Him?
Can a prophet like Muhammad be denied by others?
propositions: Nothing is said to you in terms of denial except what was already said to the messengers before you.
Your Lord is One of forgiveness to believers and also One of painful punishment for disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: Had We revealed it as a non-Arabic Quran, they would have certainly argued, “If only its verses were made clear ˹in our language˺. What! A non-Arabic revelation for an Arab audience!” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “It is a guide and a healing to the believers. As for those who disbelieve, there is deafness in their ears and blindness to it ˹in their hearts˺. It is as if they are being called from a faraway place.”

Tafsir: And had We made it namely the Remembrance a non-Arabic Qur’ān they would have said ‘Why have its signs not been explained clearly? so that we might understand them? What! a Qur’ān that is non-Arabic and an Arab prophet?’ this is an interrogative of denial spoken by them; read a-a‘jamiyyun pronouncing both the first and the second hamza or by changing it into an alif and either writing it out in full or not. Say ‘For those who believe it is guidance from error and a healing from the disease of ignorance; but as for those who do not believe there is a deafness in their ears a heaviness and so they are unable to hear it and they are blind to it so they are unable to comprehend it. Those they are as if they were being called from a distant place’ that is to say they are like one who is called from far away unable to hear or comprehend what is being called out to him.

hype_questions: Can a non-Arabic revelation be effective for an Arab audience?
What is the purpose of the Quran's verses being made clear in Arabic?
How do those who disbelieve respond to the idea of a non-Arabic prophet?
propositions: The Quran was revealed in Arabic for an Arab audience.
The Quran serves as guidance and healing for believers.
Those who disbelieve are deaf to the truth and blind to its meaning.
The Quran is like a call from a distant place, which those who disbelieve cannot hear or comprehend.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We had given Moses the Scripture, but differences arose regarding it. Had it not been for a prior decree from your Lord, their differences would have been settled ˹at once˺. They are truly in alarming doubt about it.

Tafsir: And verily We gave Moses the Scripture the Torah but differences arose concerning it in terms of some affirming the truth of it and others denying it as with the Qur’ān; and were it not for a Word that had already preceded from your Lord to defer the reckoning and requital of creatures until the Day of Resurrection judgement would have been made between them in this world concerning that over which they differed; for indeed they the deniers of it are in grave doubt concerning it doubt which leads to utter uncertainty.

hype_questions: What would have happened if the Quran had not been revealed?
How did Moses and his followers resolve their differences about the Torah?
What is the significance of the Day of Resurrection in Islam?
propositions: We gave Moses the Scripture (Torah).
Differences arose regarding the Scripture among Moses' followers.
If not for a prior decree from God, their differences would have been settled immediately.
The deniers of the Scripture are in grave doubt about it.
This doubt leads to utter uncertainty.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever does good, it is to their own benefit. And whoever does evil, it is to their own loss. Your Lord is never unjust to ˹His˺ creation.

Tafsir: Whoever acts righteously it is for the good of his own soul that he acts thus and whoever does evil it is to the detriment thereof in other words the harm consequent from his evildoing will only be to him. And your Lord is not at all a tyrant to His servants that is He is not One of injustice as He exalted be He says Surely God shall not wrong so much as the weight of an atom Q. 440.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of one's actions in this life?
How does God relate to His creation?
Can God be unjust?
propositions: Doing good is beneficial for an individual.
Doing evil results in harm to oneself.
God is not a tyrant and cannot wrong His servants.

source_text:
Verse: With Him ˹alone˺ is the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit comes out of its husk, nor does a female conceive or deliver without His knowledge. And ˹consider˺ the Day He will call to them, “Where are My ˹so-called˺ associate-gods?” They will cry, “We declare before you that none of us testifies to that ˹any longer˺.”

Tafsir: To Him devolves all knowledge of the Hour — when it shall come to pass none other than Him knows this. And no fruit thamaratin a variant reading has the plural thamarātin ‘fruits’ emerges from its sheath its receptacle akmām the plural of kimm except with His knowledge and no female bears child or delivers except with His knowledge. And on the day when He will call out to them ‘Where then are My associates?’ they will say ‘We proclaim to You we now apprise You that there is no witness amongst us’ that is a witness who can testify to the allegation that You have an associate.

hype_questions: What is the nature of divine knowledge?
Can humans conceive or deliver without God's will?
How do humans respond to being called to account for their beliefs?
propositions: The knowledge of the Hour belongs solely to God.
No fruit ripens or a female gives birth without God's knowledge and permission.
Humans will deny having any associates when questioned by God on the Day of Judgment.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever ˹idols˺ they used to invoke besides Allah will fail them. And they will realize that they will have no escape.

Tafsir: And what they used to call on what they used to worship before in this world of idols has forsaken them and they suppose they will be certain that there is no refuge for them no escape from the chastisement the negation in both instances comments on the operation implied in the nouns of actions; also the negation stands in place of the direct objects in both instances.

hype_questions: What happens to those who worship idols besides Allah?
Will they find any refuge from the chastisement?
Can they escape their fate?
propositions: Whatever idols they used to invoke besides Allah will fail them.
They will realize that there is no refuge for them.
There is no escape from the chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: One never tires of praying for good. And if touched with evil, they become desperate and hopeless.

Tafsir: Man never wearies of supplicating for good in other words he never ceases to ask his Lord for wealth and good health and other good things but should any ill befall him such as impoverishment or hardship then he becomes despondent despairing of God’s mercy — this and what follows relates to the attitude of disbelievers.

hype_questions: What happens when a person's supplication for good is answered with evil?
How do people respond when they face hardship or poverty?
Can a person ever lose hope in God's mercy?
propositions: One never tires of praying for good.
If touched with evil, they become desperate and hopeless.
A person becomes despondent despairing of God’s mercy when faced with hardship or poverty.

source_text:
Verse: And if We let them taste a mercy from Us after being touched with adversity, they will certainly say, “This is what I deserve. I do not think the Hour will ˹ever˺ come. And if in fact I am returned to my Lord, the finest reward with Him will definitely be mine.” But We will surely inform the disbelievers of what they used to do. And We will certainly make them taste a harsh torment.

Tafsir: And if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths We let him taste if We bestow on him mercy such as riches or good health from Us after the harm the hardship or tribulation that had befallen him he will surely say ‘This is my due! in other words it is on account of what I do. I do not think that the Hour will ever set in and even if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths I am returned to my Lord I will indeed have the best reward with Him’ namely Paradise. But We will assuredly inform those who disbelieve of what they did and assuredly We will make them taste a harsh chastisement the lām prefixed in both verbs is that for oaths.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who are returned to their Lord after experiencing hardship?
Will the Hour of Judgment ever come for those who disbelieve?
What will happen to those who are informed of their past deeds?
propositions: If We bestow on him mercy, he will say, 'This is my due.'
He does not think that the Hour will set in.
If he is returned to his Lord, he will have the best reward with Him.

source_text:
Verse: When We show favour to someone, they turn away, acting arrogantly. And when touched with evil, they make endless prayers ˹for good˺.

Tafsir: And when We bestow graces upon man insān the generic noun is meant he shows disregard of giving thanks and turns aside turns his head in arrogance a variant reading for nā’a has na’ā; but when ill befalls him he makes prolonged supplications.

hype_questions: What happens when someone is favored by God?
How do people respond to divine blessings?
When faced with adversity, what do people typically do?
propositions: When God shows favor to someone, they become arrogant.
When someone is touched with evil, they make prolonged prayers for good.
God bestows graces upon man, but he often disregards giving thanks.

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Imagine if this ˹Quran˺ is ˹truly˺ from Allah and you deny it: who can be more astray than those who have gone too far in opposition ˹to the truth˺?”

Tafsir: Say ‘Consider this if it the Qur’ān is from God as the Prophet says and you disbelieve in it who — in other words none — will be further astray than one who is in extreme defiance?’ of the truth this third person singular address is used instead of ‘who will be further astray than you’ in order to point out their status as disbelievers.

hype_questions: If the Qur'ān is truly from Allah, who can be more astray than those who have gone too far in opposition to the truth?
What happens if someone denies the truth of the Qur'ān?
Who will be further astray than one who is in extreme defiance of the truth?
propositions: The Prophet asked his followers to consider the possibility that the Qur'ān is from Allah.
If the Qur'ān is truly from Allah, then denying it would make someone more astray than those who have gone too far in opposition to the truth.
Extreme defiance of the truth would lead someone further away from it.

source_text:
Verse: We will show them Our signs in the universe and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that this ˹Quran˺ is the truth. Is it not enough that your Lord is a Witness over all things?
