Tafsir: We shall show them Our signs in the horizons in all the regions of the heavens and the earth in the way of the luminous celestial bodies the varieties of vegetation and trees and in their own souls in the way of the exquisite craftsmanship and unique wisdom inherent in their creation until it becomes clear to them that it namely the Qur’ān is the truth revealed by God informing of the Resurrection the Reckoning and the Punishment so that they realise that they will be punished for their disbelief in it and in the one who has come with it. Is it not sufficient that your Lord bi-rabbika governs the verb yakfi ‘sufficient’ is witness to all things? annahu ‘alā kulli shay’in shahīd substitutes for bi-rabbika. In other words is not sufficient proof of your truthfulness that nothing whatsoever can be hidden from God?

hype_questions: Will the revelation of the Qur'ān be enough to guide humanity?
Can anything be hidden from God's all-seeing eye?
What is the ultimate punishment for those who reject the truth?
propositions: We will show them Our signs in the universe and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that this Qur'ān is the truth.
Is it not enough that your Lord is a Witness over all things?
Nothing whatsoever can be hidden from God's sight.
The Qur'ān is the truth revealed by God informing of the Resurrection, the Reckoning, and the Punishment.

source_text:
Verse: They are truly in doubt of the meeting with their Lord! ˹But˺ He is indeed Fully Aware of everything.

Tafsir: Nay verily they are in doubt about the encounter with their Lord because they deny the Resurrection. Nay verily He exalted be He encompasses all things in knowledge and in power and so He will requite them for their disbelief.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the meeting with one's Lord?
How does one's belief in the Resurrection affect their relationship with God?
Will those who deny the Resurrection be requited for their disbelief?
propositions: They are in doubt about the encounter with their Lord.
God is Fully Aware of everything.
He exalted be He encompasses all things in knowledge and in power.
He will requite them for their disbelief.

source_text:
Verse: ha-Mĩm.

Tafsir: Hā mīm

hype_questions: What does 'Hā mīm' refer to in the Quran?
Can you explain the significance of 'Hā mīm' in Islamic theology?
How is 'Hā mīm' related to the concept of revelation in Islam?
propositions: Hā mīm refers to a symbol used in the Quran.
The symbol Hā mīm represents God's revelation in Islamic theology.
Hā mīm is a sign of the Quran's divine origin.

source_text:
Verse: ’Aĩn-Sĩn-Qãf.

Tafsir: ‘ayn sīn qāf God knows best what He means by these letters.

hype_questions: Does God have a hidden meaning behind the letter Qaf?
Can humans truly understand God's intentions?
What does it mean for God to know best?
propositions: God knows what He means by the letters.
The letter Qaf has a specific meaning assigned to it by God.
God's knowledge is beyond human comprehension.

source_text:
Verse: And so you ˹O Prophet˺ are sent revelation, just like those before you, by Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: Thus — in other words in the same manner of revelation — does He reveal to you and did He reveal to those who were before you God Allāhu is the agent of the action of revelation the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His actions.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's revelation?
How does Allah reveal Himself to prophets?
Who is responsible for the action of revelation?
propositions: The Prophet is sent revelation by Allah.
Allah reveals Himself to prophets in the same manner as before.
God is the agent of the action of revelation.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And He is the Most High, the Greatest.

Tafsir: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth as possession creation and servants and He is the Exalted above His creatures the Tremendous the Great.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be the 'Most High'?
How does Allah's greatness relate to His creation?
What is the significance of being 'Exalted above His creatures'?
propositions: Allah owns everything in the heavens and on earth.
Allah created everything in the heavens and on earth.
Allah is the Exalted above His creations.

source_text:
Verse: The heavens nearly burst, one above the other, ˹in awe of Him˺. And the angels glorify the praises of their Lord, and seek forgiveness for those on earth. Surely Allah alone is the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: The heavens are well-nigh read yakādu or takādu rent asunder yanfatirna a variant reading has yatafattarna from above one another in other words well-nigh is each one torn away from above the one below it because of the magnitude of God exalted be He and the angels glorify with praise of their Lord in other words they are continuously engaged in praise of Him and ask forgiveness for those believers on earth. Verily God is the Forgiving to His friends the Merciful to them.

hype_questions: What is the magnitude of God that causes the heavens to nearly burst?
How do angels glorify their Lord and seek forgiveness for believers on earth?
What does it mean to be 'Forgiving' and 'Merciful' in the context of Allah's nature?
propositions: The heavens are well-nigh torn away from above one another due to the magnitude of God.
Angels glorify their Lord with praise and ask forgiveness for believers on earth.
God is the All-Forgiving and Most Merciful to His friends.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who take other protectors besides Him, Allah is Watchful over them. And you ˹O Prophet˺ are not a keeper over them.

Tafsir: And those who have taken besides Him namely idols as guardians God is watchful over them He keeps count of their deeds that He may requite them; and you are not a guardian over them in order to secure what is demanded of them your duty is only to deliver the Message.

hype_questions: What happens to those who take idols as guardians besides Allah?
How does Allah keep count of the deeds of those who have taken other protectors besides Him?
What is the role of the Prophet in delivering the Message?
propositions: Allah is watchful over those who take other protectors besides Him.
God keeps count of the deeds of those who have taken other protectors besides Him to requite them.
You are not a guardian over those who have taken other protectors besides Allah to secure what is demanded of them.
Your duty is only to deliver the Message.

source_text:
Verse: And so We have revealed to you a Quran in Arabic, so you may warn the Mother of Cities and everyone around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering—about which there is no doubt—˹when˺ a group will be in Paradise and another in the Blaze.

Tafsir: And thus — in the same manner of revelation — have We revealed to you an Arabic Qur’ān that you may warn that you may threaten the mother-town and those around it namely the inhabitants of Mecca and all other people and that you may warn all people of the Day of Gathering the Day of Resurrection whereat all creatures will be gathered of which there is no doubt. A part of them will be in Paradise and a part will be in the Blaze the Fire.

hype_questions: What is the Day of Resurrection?
Will I be in Paradise or the Blaze after death?
How can I warn others about the consequences of my actions?
propositions: We revealed a Quran in Arabic to you.
You are warned to threaten the mother-town and those around it, namely the inhabitants of Mecca.
All creatures will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection.
A part of them will be in Paradise and a part will be in the Blaze.

source_text:
Verse: Had Allah willed, He could have easily made all ˹humanity˺ into a single community ˹of believers˺. But He admits into His mercy whoever He wills. And the wrongdoers will have no protector or helper.

Tafsir: And had God willed He would have made them one community in other words following one religion and that is Islam; but He admits whomever He will into His mercy and the evildoers the disbelievers have neither guardian nor helper to ward off the chastisement from them.

hype_questions: Can God create a single community of believers?
What happens to those who reject God's mercy?
How does God protect His people from harm?
propositions: Had Allah willed, He could have easily made all humanity into a single community of believers.
But He admits into His mercy whoever He wills.
The wrongdoers will have no protector or helper.

source_text:
Verse: How can they take protectors besides Him? Allah alone is the Protector. He ˹alone˺ gives life to the dead. And He ˹alone˺ is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: Or have they taken idols as guardians besides Him? am ‘or’ is disjunctive functioning with the sense of bal ‘nay but’ the one used to denote a shift in the subject matter; the hamza is for denial in other words ‘those who are taken’ as guardians are not in fact guardians of anything. But God He alone is the Guardian in other words then One who helps believers the fā’ of fa’Llāhu is merely for coordination and He revives the dead and He has power over all things.

hype_questions: Can anyone else protect us besides Allah?
What are the consequences of taking idols as guardians?
How does Allah help believers?
propositions: Allah is the only protector.
Idols cannot be taken as guardians besides Allah.
God revives the dead and has power over all things.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Say to the believers, O  Prophet,˺ “Whatever you may differ about, its judgment rests with Allah. That is Allah—my Lord. In Him I put my trust, and to Him I ˹always˺ turn.”

Tafsir: And whatever you may differ with disbelievers in of religion or otherwise the verdict therein belongs it will return to God on the Day of Resurrection; He will judge between you. Say to them That then is God my Lord; in Him I have put my trust and to Him I turn penitently.

hype_questions: What happens when believers disagree about a matter of faith?
Who will ultimately judge the verdicts in religious disputes?
How do Muslims express their trust and devotion to God?
propositions: The Prophet says that Allah is the one who judges all matters, including those where believers may differ.
Believers should turn to Allah for judgment on matters of faith, rather than relying on human opinions.
In times of disagreement with disbelievers, Muslims are encouraged to express their trust and devotion to God.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is˺ the Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you spouses from among yourselves, and ˹made˺ mates for cattle ˹as well˺—multiplying you ˹both˺. There is nothing like Him, for He ˹alone˺ is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

Tafsir: The Originator of the heavens and the earth the One Who created them without precedent. He has made for you from your own selves pairs when He created Eve from Adam’s rib and also pairs males and females of the cattle He multiplies you read yadhra’ukum by such means by the mentioned ‘making’ that is to say He multiplies you through this means by way of propagation the suffixed pronoun -kum in yadhra’ukum ‘He multiplies you’ refers to both human beings and cattle but predominantly to humans. There is nothing like Him ka-mithlihi the kāf is extra as there is no likeness of Him exalted be He. He is the Hearer of what is said the Seer of what is done.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creation?
How does Allah create pairs for humans and cattle?
What are the characteristics of Allah's hearing and seeing?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and earth without precedent.
He created Eve from Adam's rib and formed pairs for humans and cattle.
Allah multiplies humans through propagation.
There is nothing like Him, for He is the All-Hearing and All-Seeing.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belong the keys ˹of the treasuries˺ of the heavens and the earth. He gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills. Indeed, He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

Tafsir: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth the keys to their storehouses of rain and vegetation and other things. He extends provision He makes it abundant for whomever He will as a test of their gratitude and He restricts it He straitens it for whomever He will as a trial. Truly He has knowledge of all things.

hype_questions: Does Allah have control over the distribution of resources?
How does Allah test the gratitude of His servants?
Can Allah's knowledge be limited?
propositions: Allah has control over the keys of the heavens and the earth.
Allah extends provision to whomever He wills, making it abundant or limited as a test of their gratitude.
Allah restricts provision for whomever He wills, straitening it as a trial.
Allah has perfect knowledge of all things.

source_text:
Verse: He has ordained for you ˹believers˺ the Way which He decreed for Noah, and what We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ and what We decreed for Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, ˹commanding:˺ “Uphold the faith, and make no divisions in it.” What you call the polytheists to is unbearable for them. Allah chooses for Himself whoever He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns ˹to Him˺.

Tafsir: He has prescribed for you as a religion that which He enjoined upon Noah — for he was the first of the prophets sent with a Divine Law — and that which We have revealed to you and that which We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus declaring ‘Establish religion and do not be divided in it’ this is what has been prescribed and enjoined upon those mentioned above and what has been revealed to Muhammad (s) and it is the affirmation of God’s Oneness. Dreadful is for the idolaters that to which you summon them in the way of affirming the Oneness of God. God chooses for it for the task of affirming His Oneness whomever He will and He guides to it whomever turns penitently whomever applies himself to obedience of Him.

hype_questions: What is the fundamental principle of Islam?
How does Allah choose and guide believers?
What is the ultimate goal of summoning polytheists to monotheism?
propositions: Allah has ordained for believers the Way which He decreed for Noah.
God chooses for Himself whoever He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns (to Him).
The affirmation of God's Oneness is a fundamental principle of Islam.

source_text:
Verse: They did not split ˹into sects˺ out of mutual envy until knowledge came to them. after them are truly in alarming doubt about this ˹Quran˺.

Tafsir: And they did not become divided that is the adherents of the monotheistic religions did not become divided in religion — so that some affirmed the Oneness of God while others rejected it — except after the knowledge of His Oneness had come to them out of jealous rivalry on the part of the disbelievers among themselves. And were it not for a Word that preceded from your Lord to defer requital of them until an appointed term until the Day of Resurrection it would have already been judged between them to chastise the disbelievers in this world. And indeed those who were made heirs to the Scripture after them namely the Jews and the Christians are truly in grave doubt concerning him Muhammad (s).

hype_questions: What is the reason behind the sectarian divisions among monotheistic religions?
How did the knowledge of God's Oneness affect the adherents of these religions?
Why are the Jews and Christians in grave doubt about Muhammad (s)?
propositions: The adherents of monotheistic religions became divided due to jealous rivalry among disbelievers after they gained knowledge of God's Oneness.
If not for a Word from God, the disbelievers would have been judged and chastised in this world before the appointed term.
The Jews and Christians are in grave doubt about Muhammad (s) because of their lack of understanding or faith.

source_text:
Verse: Because of that, you ˹O Prophet˺ will invite ˹all˺. Be steadfast as you are commanded, and do not follow their desires. And say, “I believe in every Scripture Allah has revealed. And I am commanded to judge fairly among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. We will be accountable for our deeds and you for yours. There is no ˹need for˺ contention between us. Allah will gather us together ˹for judgment˺. And to Him is the final return.”

Tafsir: So to that then to that affirmation of God’s Oneness summon O Muhammad (s) people and be upright in summoning them to this just as you have been commanded and do not follow them in their desires to abandon it. And say ‘I believe in whatever Book God has revealed. And I have been commanded to be just between you in passing judgement. God is our Lord and your Lord. Our deeds concern us and your deeds concern you and so each one of us will be requited according to his own deeds. There is no argument no dispute between us and you — this was revealed before the command to struggle against them. God will bring us together at the time of the Return to decide definitively between us and to Him is the final destination’ the ultimate return.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of humanity?
How will we be held accountable for our actions?
What is the nature of God's justice?
propositions: You are commanded to invite people to Allah.
Be steadfast in your faith and do not follow their desires.
I believe in every Scripture revealed by Allah.
I am commanded to judge fairly among you.
God is our Lord and your Lord.
Our deeds concern us, and your deeds concern you.
Each one of us will be requited according to his own deeds.
There is no argument or dispute between us and you.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who dispute about Allah after He is ˹already˺ acknowledged ˹by many˺, their argument is futile in the sight of their Lord. Upon them is wrath, and they will suffer a severe punishment.

Tafsir: And those who argue with the Prophet concerning the religion of God after His call has been answered through faith on account of His miracle having been manifested — and they are the Jews — their argument stands refuted is invalid with their Lord and His wrath shall be upon them and there will be a severe chastisement for them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who dispute about Allah after faith has been established?
How does the Lord respond to those who argue with the Prophet about religion?
What punishment will befall those who reject God's miracle?
propositions: Those who dispute about Allah after He is acknowledged by many will face wrath.
The argument of those who dispute with the Prophet about religion is futile in the sight of their Lord.
Their Lord's wrath shall be upon them, and they will suffer a severe punishment.

source_text:
Verse: It is Allah Who has revealed the Book with the truth and the balance ˹of justice˺. You never know, perhaps the Hour is near.

Tafsir: God it is Who has revealed the Book the Qur’ān with the truth bi’l-haqqi is semantically connected to anzala ‘revealed’ as well as the Balance Justice. And what do you know — perhaps the Hour that is its arrival is near! la‘alla ‘perhaps’ comments on the verb describing the action with what follows it functioning as two direct objects.

hype_questions: Will the Hour arrive soon?
What is the nature of justice according to Allah?
How can we prepare for the arrival of the Hour?
propositions: Allah has revealed the Qur'ān with truth and balance.
The Hour may be near.
Justice is a fundamental aspect of Allah's revelation.

source_text:
Verse: Those who disbelieve in it ˹ask to˺ hasten it ˹mockingly˺. But the believers are fearful of it, knowing that it is the truth. Surely those who dispute about the Hour have gone far astray.

Tafsir: Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it they say ‘When will it come?’ as a presumption on their part that it will never come; but those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth. Nay but verily those who are in doubt those who argue concerning the Hour are indeed in extreme error!

hype_questions: When will the Hour come?
Will the Hour ever arrive?
What is the nature of the Hour?
propositions: Those who disbelieve in it seek to hasten it.
The believers are fearful of it, knowing that it is the truth.
Those who dispute about the Hour have gone far astray.

source_text:
Verse: Allah is Ever Kind to His servants. He provides ˹abundantly˺ to whoever He wills. And He is the All-Powerful, Almighty.

Tafsir: God is Gracious to His servants both the pious and the profligate for He does not destroy them through hunger despite their acts of disobedience. He provides for whomever He will from among each of the two classes of individuals whatever He will. And He is the Strong in effecting what He wants the Mighty Whose way always prevails.

hype_questions: Does Allah provide for all His servants equally?
Can Allah destroy His servants through hunger despite their disobedience?
Is Allah's power absolute?
propositions: Allah is Ever Kind to His servants.
Allah provides abundantly to whoever He wills.
Allah is the All-Powerful, Almighty.

source_text:
Verse: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase their harvest. And whoever desires ˹only˺ the harvest of this world, We will give them some of it, but they will have no share in the Hereafter.

Tafsir: And whoever desires in return for his actions the harvest of the Hereafter in other words its gains and that is reward We will enhance for him his harvest by multiplying in it the good deed up tenfold or more; and whoever desires the harvest of this world We will give him of it without multiplying any of it giving him only what is his preordained share; but in the Hereafter he will have no share.

hype_questions: What happens when we desire the harvest of the Hereafter?
How will our actions be rewarded in the Hereafter?
What is the difference between the harvest of this world and the harvest of the Hereafter?
propositions: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase their harvest.
Whoever desires only the harvest of this world, We will give them some of it, but they will have no share in the Hereafter.
We will enhance for him his harvest by multiplying in it the good deed up tenfold or more.
We will give him of it without multiplying any of it giving him only what is his preordained share.
but in the Hereafter he will have no share.

source_text:
Verse: Or do they have associate-gods who have ordained for them some ˹polytheistic˺ beliefs, which Allah has not authorized? Had it not been for ˹prior˺ decree on Judgment, the matter would have certainly been settled between them ˹at once˺. And surely the wrongdoers will suffer a painful punishment.

Tafsir: Or have they the Meccan disbelievers associates — these being their devils — who have prescribed for them for the disbelievers a religion a corrupt religion which God has not given permission for? such as idolatry and denial of resurrection? And were it not for a prior decisive word in other words a prior decree to the effect that requital will take place on the Day of Resurrection it would have been judged between them and the believers by chastising the former in this world. Truly the wrongdoers the disbelievers will have a painful chastisement.

hype_questions: Will Allah permit polytheistic beliefs?
What is the nature of the corrupt religion prescribed for disbelievers?
How will wrongdoers be punished on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: Allah has not authorized any polytheistic beliefs.
The Meccan disbelievers' devils have prescribed a corrupt religion for them.
God has given permission for chastisement to take place in this world and on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: You will see the wrongdoers fearful ˹of the punishment˺ for what they committed but it will be inevitable for them, whereas those who believe and do good will be in the lush Gardens of Paradise. They will have whatever they desire from their Lord. That is ˹truly˺ the greatest bounty.

Tafsir: You will see the wrongdoers on the Day of Resurrection apprehensive because of what they had earned in this world in the way of evil deeds lest they be requited for these; and it that is the requital for these deeds will surely befall them on the Day of Resurrection inevitably; but those who believe and perform righteous deeds will be in the lushest Gardens in other words in the best of these Gardens in comparison with the other ones. They will have whatever they wish near their Lord; that is the great favour.

hype_questions: What will be the fate of those who commit evil deeds?
How will believers be rewarded in the afterlife?
What is the greatest blessing that Allah has in store for His believers?
propositions: Those who do wrong will see the wrongdoers fearful on the Day of Resurrection because of what they had earned in this world.
Believers will be in the lushest Gardens in comparison with the other ones.
Allah will give His believers whatever they wish near Him.

source_text:
Verse: That ˹reward˺ is the good news which Allah gives to His servants who believe and do good. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I do not ask you for a reward for this ˹message˺—only honour for ˹our˺ kinship.” Whoever earns a good deed, We will increase it in goodness for them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.

Tafsir: That is the good tidings read yubshiru or yubashshiru from bishāra ‘good news’ which God gives to His servants who believe and perform righteous deeds. Say ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it for delivering the Message except the affection for my kinsfolk illā ‘except’ this represents a discontinuous exception in other words ‘but I do ask of you that you show affection for my kinship with you which at the same time is your kinship’; for he the Prophet had kinship ties with all the subdivisions of the tribe of Quraysh. And whoever acquires a good deed an act of obedience We shall enhance for him its goodness by multiplying the reward for it. Surely God is Forgiving of sins Appreciative even of little good and so He multiplies it manifold.

hype_questions: What is the reward for delivering a message of good news?
How does Allah show appreciation to His servants?
What happens when someone performs a good deed?
propositions: Allah gives good news to His servants who believe and do good.
The Prophet delivers a message without asking for reward, except for affection towards his kinship.
God multiplies the goodness of a good deed by enhancing its reward.

source_text:
Verse: Or do they say, “He has fabricated a lie about Allah!”? ˹If you had,˺ Allah would have sealed your heart, if He willed. And Allah wipes out falsehood and establishes the truth by His Words. He certainly knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.

Tafsir: Or am here is like bal do they say ‘He has invented a lie against God?’ in ascribing the Qur’ān to God exalted be He. For if God will He can seal He can fortify your heart with patience to endure the hurt they cause you by such sayings and otherwise — and God did this. And God will efface the falsehood which they speak and vindicate confirm the truth with His words the ones revealed to His Prophet. Truly He is Knower of what is in the breasts of what is in the hearts of people.

hype_questions: Can God protect us from false accusations?
How can we develop patience in the face of hurtful words?
What is the role of truth and falsehood in our lives?
propositions: Allah wipes out falsehood and establishes the truth by His Words.
God will fortify your heart with patience to endure the hurt they cause you.
God effaces the falsehood which they speak and vindicates confirm the truth with His words.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons ˹their˺ sins. And He knows whatever you do.

Tafsir: And He it is Who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons evil deeds those from which repentance has been made and knows what they do yaf‘alūna may also be read taf‘alūna ‘you do’.

hype_questions: What happens when someone repents to Allah?
Can Allah forgive any sin?
How does Allah know what we do?
propositions: Allah accepts repentance from His servants.
Allah pardons sins after repentance.
Allah knows the actions of His servants.

source_text:
Verse: He responds to those who believe and do good, and increases their reward out of His grace. As for the disbelievers, they will suffer a severe punishment.

Tafsir: And He answers those who believe and perform righteous deeds He grants them what they ask for and He enhances them of His bounty. And as for the disbelievers for them there will be a severe chastisement.

hype_questions: What is the reward given to believers who perform good deeds?
How does Allah respond to those who believe and do righteous actions?
What punishment will befall disbelievers?
propositions: Allah responds to those who believe and do good.
The reward for believers increases out of Allah's grace.
Disbelievers will suffer a severe punishment.

source_text:
Verse: Had Allah given abundant provisions to ˹all˺ His servants, they would have certainly transgressed throughout the land. But He sends down whatever He wills in perfect measure. He is truly All-Aware, All-Seeing of His servants.

Tafsir: For were God to extend His provision to His servants to all of them they would all of them surely become covetous in other words they would become tyrants in the earth; but He sends down read yunzilu or yunazzilu of provisions in the measure that He will thus extending it for some of His servants to the exclusion of others — and from such extending of provision to some emerges tyranny. Surely He is Aware Seer of His servants.

hype_questions: If God were to provide for all people equally, would humanity become a utopia?
How does God's provision affect human behavior?
Can God's providence be seen as a form of justice?
propositions: God gives His servants abundant provisions.
If God gave all people equal provision, they would become tyrants.
God sends down provisions in perfect measure to some of His servants while excluding others.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who sends down rain after people have given up hope, spreading out His mercy. He is the Guardian, the Praiseworthy.

Tafsir: And He it is Who sends down the saving rain after they have despaired after they have given up hope of its being sent down and unfolds His mercy He extends His rain and He is the true Patron the Benevolent towards believers the Praised by them.

hype_questions: What happens when people lose hope?
How does Allah show mercy to His believers?
Who is the true Patron of believers?
propositions: Allah sends down rain after people have given up hope.
Allah spreads out His mercy.
Allah is the Guardian, the Praiseworthy.

source_text:
Verse: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and all living beings He dispersed throughout both. And He is Most Capable of bringing all together whenever He wills.

Tafsir: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the creation of whatever He has scattered whatever He has divided and spread in them in the way of creatures dābba this denotes all those creatures which tread yadubbu upon the earth whether human beings or otherwise. And He is able to bring them together for the Gathering whenever He will rational beings as opposed to others predominate in the suffixed pronoun -him of jam‘ihim ‘to bring them together’.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of God's creation?
How does God bring all living beings together?
What is the significance of the Gathering in Islam?
propositions: God created the heavens and the earth.
God scattered and divided various creatures throughout both.
God can bring all living beings together for the Gathering.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your own hands have committed. And He pardons much.

Tafsir: And whatever affliction whatever misfortune or hardship may befall you — this is an address to the believers — is on account of what your own hands have earned that is to say for the sins that you have committed — the use of ‘hands’ to express this is because most actions are effected by them. And He pardons much of these sins and does not requite them for God’s kindness is greater than that He should for example double the requital in the Hereafter; as for those who do not commit grave sins then what befalls them in this world of hardship raises their degree in the reward of the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of our own actions?
How does God's mercy relate to punishment?
Can good deeds in this life increase one's reward in the Hereafter?
propositions: Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your own hands have committed.
God pardons much of these sins and does not requite them.
For those who do not commit grave sins, hardship in this world can raise their degree in the reward of the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: You can never escape ˹Him˺ on earth, nor do you have any protector or helper besides Allah.

Tafsir: And you O idolaters cannot escape from God by fleeing on earth and thus elude Him and besides God that is to say other than Him you have neither protector nor helper to ward off His chastisement from you.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate source of protection and help?
Can humans escape God's chastisement?
Who can provide assistance in times of need?
propositions: You cannot escape Allah on earth.
Allah is the only protector and helper.
Fleeing from Allah will not elude Him.

source_text:
Verse: And among His signs are the ships like mountains ˹sailing˺ in the sea.

Tafsir: And of His signs are the ships that run on the sea appearing like landmarks like mountains in terms of their magnitude.

hype_questions: What are some natural wonders that can be compared to mountains?
How do ships navigate the vastness of the ocean?
Can we find any other signs of Allah's power in the natural world?
propositions: Ships appear like mountains on the sea due to their magnitude.
The sea is a vast and powerful force that can be compared to mountains.
Allah has created many natural wonders that demonstrate His power.

source_text:
Verse: If He wills, He can calm the wind, leaving the ships motionless on the water. Surely in this are signs for whoever is steadfast, grateful.

Tafsir: If He will He stills the wind whereat they remain they become motionless fixed not moving on its surface. Surely in that there are signs for every steadfast grateful servant — this is the believer who is steadfast during hardship and grateful in times of comfort.

hype_questions: Can God calm the wind and leave the ships motionless on the water?
What are signs of God's power in calming the wind and stilling the waves?
How does a steadfast and grateful servant respond to times of hardship and comfort?
propositions: If He wills, He can calm the wind.
The ships remain motionless on the water when the wind is stilled.
In this there are signs for whoever is steadfast and grateful.

source_text:
Verse: Or He can wreck the ships for what the people have committed—though He forgives much—

Tafsir: Or He wrecks them yūbiqhunna a supplement to yuskin ‘He stills’ that is to say or He sinks them including their passengers by sending violent winds upon them because of what they that is the passengers of these ships have earned of sins. And He pardons much of such sin and does not cause those who have sinned to drown.

hype_questions: What happens when a person sins?
Can God forgive someone's sins?
How does God deal with those who have committed wrongdoings?
propositions: God can wreck ships as punishment for people's sins.
God stills or sinks ships and their passengers due to sin.
God pardons much of such sin and does not cause those who have sinned to drown.

source_text:
Verse: so those who dispute about Our signs may know that they have no refuge.

Tafsir: And that those who dispute concerning Our signs may know read indicative wa-ya‘lamu ‘and they know’ beginning a new sentence; or subjunctive wa-ya‘lama ‘and that they may know’ as a supplement to an implicit reason in other words ‘He drowns them in order to exact vengeance against them and so that they may know that …’ they have no refuge no escape from the chastisement the negation represents two direct objects of the verb ya‘lamu or ya‘lama ‘they know’; the negation is also a comment on the implied action of ‘escaping’.

hype_questions: What happens to those who dispute about God's signs?
Can they find refuge from God's chastisement?
How does God respond to those who question His signs?
propositions: Those who dispute about God's signs have no refuge.
God drowns them in order to exact vengeance against them.
The negation represents two direct objects of the verb 'they know'.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever ˹pleasure˺ you have been given is ˹no more than a fleeting˺ enjoyment of this worldly life. But what is with Allah is far better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord;

Tafsir: So whatever you — this is an address is to believers and others — have been given of the luxuries of this world is but the enjoyment of the life of this world enjoyed for the duration of it but then perishes. But what is with God of reward is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord li’lladhīna āmanū wa-‘alā rabbihim yatawakkalūna is supplemented by the following clause

hype_questions: What happens to worldly pleasures after death?
How does Allah reward believers?
What is the lasting reward for those who trust in their Lord?
propositions: Whatever pleasure you have been given is a fleeting enjoyment of this worldly life.
The reward with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord.

source_text:
Verse: who avoid major sins and shameful deeds, and forgive when angered;

Tafsir: and those who avoid grave sins and indecencies those acts that require the implementing of the prescribed legal punishments hudūd the supplement above is an example of supplementing the part to the whole and who when they are angry forgive they let it pass;

hype_questions: What are some ways to avoid major sins?
How can one show forgiveness when angered?
What is the concept of hudūd in Islamic law?
propositions: Those who avoid grave sins and indecencies are rewarded.
Forgiveness is a virtue in Islam.
Hudūd refers to the prescribed legal punishments for certain acts.

source_text:
Verse: who respond to their Lord, establish prayer, conduct their affairs by mutual consultation, and donate from what We have provided for them;

Tafsir: and those who answer their Lord those who respond to what He has summoned them in the way of affirming His Oneness and worship of Him and observe prayer maintaining it regularly and whose courses of action those courses of action that seem good to them are a matter of counsel between them in which they consult one another and do not act hastily and who of what We have bestowed on them expend in obedience to God — such mentioned individuals constitute one category;

hype_questions: What is the importance of responding to one's Lord?
How does mutual consultation impact decision-making in Islam?
What is the significance of expending from one's wealth in obedience to God?
propositions: Who respond to their Lord establish prayer.
Those who answer their Lord maintain regular prayer.
They conduct their affairs by mutual consultation.
They donate from what We have provided for them in obedience to God.

source_text:
Verse: and who enforce justice when wronged.

Tafsir: and those who when they suffer aggression injustice defend themselves — these are another category — that is to say they retaliate against those who wrong them in the same manner in which the latter wronged them as God exalted be He says

hype_questions: What is the role of individuals when they are wronged?
How do those who suffer aggression and injustice respond?
What does God say about retaliation?
propositions: Those who are wronged defend themselves.
God exalted be He says that those who retaliate against their aggressors do so in the same manner as they were wronged.

source_text:
Verse: The reward of an evil deed is its equivalent. But whoever pardons and seeks reconciliation, then their reward is with Allah. He certainly does not like the wrongdoers.

Tafsir: For the requital of an evil deed is an evil deed like it the latter is also referred to as ‘an evil deed’ because in outward form it resembles the former; this is evident in what concerns retaliation for wounds. Some scholars say that even if another were to say ‘May God disgrace you!’ then one should respond equally with ‘May God disgrace you!’. But whoever pardons his wrongdoer and reconciles the amity between himself and the one pardoned his reward will be with God that is to say God will give him his reward without doubt. Truly He does not like wrongdoers that is those who initiate acts of wrongdoing and so merit His punishment.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who forgives their wrongdoer?
Can retaliation for a wound be equivalent to the original injury?
How does God reward someone who pardons and reconciles with their wrongdoer?
propositions: The reward of an evil deed is its equivalent.
Whoever pardons and seeks reconciliation will receive a reward from Allah.
God does not like the wrongdoers, but rewards those who pardon and reconcile.

source_text:
Verse: There is no blame on those who enforce justice after being wronged.

Tafsir: And whoever defends himself after he has been wronged that is to say after the wrongdoer has wronged him — for such there will be no course of action against them no blame on them.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who defends themselves after being wronged?
Can someone be blamed for defending themselves against a wrongdoer?
What is the consequence of defending oneself after being wronged?
propositions: There is no blame on those who enforce justice after being wronged.
Defending oneself after being wronged means that the wrongdoer has already been wronged.
There will be no course of action against someone who defends themselves after being wronged.

source_text:
Verse: Blame is only on those who wrong people and transgress in the land unjustly. It is they who will suffer a painful punishment.

Tafsir: A course of action is only open against those who wrong people and seek to commit who commit in the earth what is not right what are acts of disobedience. For such there will be a painful chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens to those who commit injustices on earth?
Who is held accountable for wrongdoings?
What punishment awaits those who disobey God's laws?
propositions: Blame lies with those who unjustly wrong people and transgress in the land.
Only those who commit acts of disobedience will face a painful punishment.
It is not right to act unjustly on earth.

source_text:
Verse: And whoever endures patiently and forgives—surely this is a resolve to aspire to.

Tafsir: But verily he who is patient and defend himself by retaliating and forgives excuses the wrong done to him — surely that patience and excusing is true constancy in such affairs that is to say it is one of those courses of action for which one must have firm resolve meaning those which are required of the believer by God’s Law.

hype_questions: What is the true nature of patience and forgiveness in Islam?
How does one demonstrate constancy in forgiving others?
What are some courses of action that require firm resolve from a believer?
propositions: Whoever endures patiently and forgives is on a path to aspire to.
Patience and forgiving oneself by retaliating excuses the wrong done to one.
True constancy in such affairs requires firm resolve, as mandated by God's Law.

source_text:
Verse: And whoever Allah leaves to stray will have no guide after Him. You will see the wrongdoers, when they face the torment, pleading, “Is there any way back ˹to the world˺?”

Tafsir: And whomever God leads astray has no protector after Him that is to say none to take charge of guiding him after God has led him astray. And you will see the wrongdoers when they sight the chastisement saying ‘Is there any way any route by which to return?’ to this world.

hype_questions: Can one ever find redemption after being led astray by God?
Is there a way back to the world for those who have been punished?
What happens to those who plead for forgiveness after facing torment?
propositions: Allah leaves no one to stray without consequence.
Those who are led astray by Allah have no protector or guide.
The wrongdoers will plead for a way back to the world when they face punishment.

source_text:
Verse: And you will see them exposed to the Fire, fully humbled out of disgrace, stealing glances ˹at it˺. And the believers will say, “The ˹true˺ losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on Judgment Day.” The wrongdoers will certainly be in everlasting torment.

Tafsir: And you will see them being exposed to it namely the Fire submissive fearful and humbled by abasement looking at it with a furtive glance a slight look stealthily min of min tarfin khafiyyin ‘with a furtive glance’ is to indicate inceptiveness or it functions with the sense of a bā’ ‘with’ sc. bi-tarfin khafiyyin. And those who believe will say ‘Verily the true losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection for being condemned to abide forever in the Fire and for not being able to attain the blissful company of the houris prepared for them in Paradise had they been believers the relative clause alladhīna khasirū... ‘those who have lost …’ constitutes the predicate of the particle inna ‘verily’. Truly the wrongdoers the disbelievers will be in lasting everlasting chastisement — these words constitute God’s speech exalted be He.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject faith on the Day of Resurrection?
Can believers attain the blissful company of houris in Paradise if they were not believers?
What is the nature of God's chastisement for wrongdoers?
propositions: Those who are exposed to the Fire will be humbled and fearful.
The true losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on Judgment Day.
God's chastisement for wrongdoers is everlasting torment.

source_text:
Verse: They will have no protectors to help them against Allah. And whoever Allah leaves to stray, for them there is no way.

Tafsir: And they have no guardians to help them besides God that is to say other than Him to ward off His chastisement from them and whomever God leads astray has no course of action’ no route to the truth in this world or to Paradise in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah leaves someone to stray?
Is there any way out of Allah's chastisement for those who are led astray?
Can someone find the truth in this world or in Paradise after being led astray?
propositions: Allah is the only protector against His chastisement.
There is no guardian besides God to help those in need.
Those who are led astray have no course of action and no route to the truth.

source_text:
Verse: Respond to your Lord before the coming of a Day from Allah that cannot be averted. There will be no refuge for you then, nor ˹grounds for˺ denial ˹of sins˺.

Tafsir: Answer your Lord respond to Him by affirming His Oneness and worshipping Him before there comes a day namely the Day of Resurrection for which there is no revoking from God in other words one which when He brings about He will not revoke. On that day you will have no refuge in which to seek refuge in and for you there will be no way of denying your sins.

hype_questions: What happens to a person on the Day of Resurrection?
Can a person seek refuge from Allah on the Day of Resurrection?
How will a person be held accountable for their sins on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: You must respond to your Lord by affirming His Oneness.
Worship Allah before the coming of the Day of Resurrection.
There is no refuge from Allah on the Day of Resurrection.
There will be no way to deny one's sins on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: But if they turn away, We have not sent you ˹O Prophet˺ as a keeper over them. Your duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺. And indeed, when We let someone taste a mercy from Us, they become prideful ˹because˺ of it. But when afflicted with evil because of what their hands have done, then one becomes totally ungrateful.

Tafsir: But if they are disregardful of answering God We have not sent you as a keeper over them to keep track of their deeds by securing what is demanded of them. Your duty is only to deliver the Message — this was revealed before the command to struggle against them. And indeed when We let man taste from Us some mercy some grace such as wealth and good health he exults in it; but if some ill some calamity befalls them the pronoun here refers to ‘man’ on the basis of the plural import of the generic noun because of what their own hands have sent ahead because of what they have offered of deeds — the expression refers to ‘the hands’ because most actions are effected by them then lo! man is ungrateful for the grace.

hype_questions: What happens when people turn away from God's message?
How do humans react to receiving mercy and blessings from Allah?
Why are people often ungrateful for the good things they receive?
propositions: If people ignore God's message, it is not the Prophet's duty to keep track of their deeds.
The Prophet's only responsibility is to deliver the Message.
When humans experience mercy and blessings from Allah, they often become proud and ungrateful.

source_text:
Verse: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He wills. He blesses whoever He wills with daughters, and blesses whoever He wills with sons,

Tafsir: To God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He will; He gives to whomever He will in the way of children females and He gives to whomever He will males.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's creation?
How does Allah determine the gender of children?
What is the significance of Allah's will in shaping human life?
propositions: To Allah belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth.
Allah creates whatever He wills.
Allah gives to whomever He will in the way of children females.
Allah gives to whomever He will males.

source_text:
Verse: or grants both, sons and daughters, ˹to whoever He wills˺, and leaves whoever He wills infertile. He is indeed All-Knowing, Most Capable.

Tafsir: Or He combines them that is to say or He makes them males and females; and He makes whomever He will infertile such that she is unable to conceive or he cannot have a child. Surely He is Knower of what He creates Powerful in bringing about whatever He will.

hype_questions: Does Allah have the power to create life and determine fertility?
Can Allah's will be done in all aspects of creation?
Is Allah's knowledge and power absolute?
propositions: Allah grants both sons and daughters to whoever He wills.
He leaves whoever He will infertile, making them unable to conceive or have a child.
Allah is All-Knowing and Most Capable.

source_text:
Verse: It is not ˹possible˺ for a human being to have Allah communicate with them, except through inspiration, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger-angel to reveal whatever He wills by His permission. He is surely Most High, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And it is not possible for any human that God should speak to him except that He should reveal to him by revelation in sleep or by inspiration or except from behind a veil where He makes the person able to hear His speech but without seeing Him — as was the case with Moses peace be upon him; or except that He should send a messenger an angel such as Gabriel and he the messenger then reveals to the person to whom he has been sent that is to say and then he speaks to him with His permission that is God’s whatever He God will. Truly He is Exalted above the attributes of created beings Wise in His actions.

hype_questions: Can humans communicate directly with Allah?
How does Allah reveal Himself to humans?
What is the role of prophets and angels in conveying Allah's message?
propositions: Allah communicates with humans only through inspiration, revelation, or by sending a messenger-angel.
God reveals His speech to humans without seeing Him, as seen in the case of Moses.
Prophets and angels convey Allah's message with permission from God.

source_text:
Verse: And so We have sent to you ˹O Prophet˺ a revelation by Our command. You did not know of ˹this˺ Book and faith ˹before˺. But We have made it a light, by which We guide whoever We will of Our servants. And you are truly leading ˹all˺ to the Straight Path—

Tafsir: And thus in the same way that We have revealed to messengers other than you have We revealed to you O Muhammad (s) a Spirit namely the Qur’ān by which hearts are revived from Our command that command which We reveal to you. You did not know before revelation came to you what the Book was what the Qur’ān was nor faith that is its ordinances and ritual ceremonies the negation comments in place of the verb on the action and what has come after it constitutes two direct objects; but We have made it namely the Spirit — or the Qur’ān — a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants. And verily you guide you are summoning people by means of what is revealed to you to a straight path a straight way the religion of Islam

hype_questions: What is the Qur'an?
How does Islam guide its followers?
What is the straight path in Islam?
propositions: We have sent a revelation to you by Our command.
The Qur'an is a light that guides whoever We will of Our servants.
You are summoning people to a straight path with what is revealed to you.

source_text:
Verse: the Path of Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Surely to Allah all matters will return ˹for judgment˺.

All matters come to an end with God, and then return to Him.

source_text:
Verse: ha-Mĩm.

God has a specific meaning in mind when using the letter mīm.

source_text:
Verse: By the clear Book!

hype_questions: What is the Qur'ān?

propositions: The Qur'ān clarifies a path of guidance.

source_text:
Verse: Certainly, We have made it a Quran in Arabic so perhaps you will understand.

source_text:
Verse: And indeed, it is—in the Master Record with Us—highly esteemed, rich in wisdom.

Tafsir: And it is indeed fixed in the Mother Book the source of all the scriptures namely the Preserved Tablet which is with Us ladaynā substitutes for fī ummi’l-kitābi ‘in the Mother Book’ and it is indeed exalted above all the scriptures that came before it wise containing excellent wisdoms.

hype_questions: What is the Preserved Tablet?

propositions: The Master Record is highly esteemed.
The Preserved Tablet is the source of all scriptures.
The Mother Book contains excellent wisdoms.

source_text:
Verse: Should We then turn the ˹Quranic˺ Reminder away from you ˹simply˺ because you have been a transgressing people?

Tafsir: Shall We turn away shall We withhold from you the Remembrance the Qur’ān utterly an utter withholding so that you are then neither commanded nor forbidden because you are a profligate an idolatrous folk? No!

hype_questions: Will we turn away from you the Remembrance of the Qur'an?

Will you be commanded or forbidden if we withhold the Qur'an?
propositions: You have been a transgressing people.

We will not turn away from you the Remembrance of the Qur'an.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Imagine˺ how many prophets We sent to those ˹destroyed˺ before!

hype_questions: How many prophets were sent before?

propositions: We sent prophets to those who were destroyed.

The destruction of a nation does not necessarily mean the failure of its prophets.

source_text:

hype_questions: Do people always mock prophets?

propositions: No prophet came without being mocked.

source_text:
Verse: So We destroyed those who were far mightier than these ˹Meccans˺. The examples of ˹their˺ predecessors have ˹already˺ been related.

hype_questions: What is the fate of those who are stronger than us?

propositions: We destroyed those who were mightier than them in prowess and strength.

source_text:
Verse: If you ask them ˹O Prophet˺ who created the heavens and the earth, they will certainly say, “The Almighty, All-Knowing did.”

Tafsir: And if wa-la-in the lām is for oaths you ask them ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say the indicative nūn has been omitted because of the other nūn coming after it and likewise the wāw replaced by the damma in -lunna because of two unvowelled consonants coming together ‘The Mighty the Knower created them’ — this would have to be their eventual response that is to say God created them Lord of Might and Knowledge. God exalted be He adds

propositions: The Almighty, All-Knowing created the heavens and the earth.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is the One˺ Who has laid out the earth for you, and set in it pathways for you so that you may find your way.

hype_questions: Does Allah guide us on our journey?
What is the purpose of the earth according to Islamic teachings?
How does Allah help us find our way?
propositions: Allah laid out the earth for humans.
The earth serves as a resting place for humans like a child's cradle.
Allah placed pathways in the earth for guidance.

source_text:

Tafsir: and Who sent down water from the heaven in measure that is to say in the measure that you require thereof and did not send it down in a deluge and We revived with it a dead land. Thus — like this revivification — will you be brought forth from your graves alive;

hype_questions: Will I be revived after death?

propositions: Allah sends down rain from the sky in perfect measure.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹He is the One˺ Who created all ˹things in˺ pairs, and made for you ships and animals to ride

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creating pairs in all things?

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: Still the pagans have made some of His creation out to be a part of Him. Indeed, humankind is clearly ungrateful.

Tafsir: And they assign to Him from among His own servants a part when they say that the angels are God’s daughters — for a child is a part of its parent — even though the angels are like them servants of His exalted be He. source_text:
Verse: Has He taken ˹angels as His˺ daughters from what He created, and favoured you ˹O pagans˺ with sons?

Tafsir: Or am has the significance of the hamza of denial; the ‘saying’ is implied in other words a-taqūlūna ‘or do you say that …’ He has adopted from all that He has created daughters for Himself and preferred you privileged you with sons? — that which is the necessary inference from what you claim and which by itself is an abomination.

source_text:
Verse: Whenever one of them is given the good news of what they attribute to the Most Compassionate, his face grows gloomy, as he suppresses his rage.

Tafsir: And when one of them is given the good tidings of that which he has attributed to the Compassionate One of that which he has likened to Him by the ascription to Him of daughters — for a child is likened to its parent; in other words when one of them is informed that a daughter has been born to him his face becomes darkened transformed into one laden with anguish and he chokes inwardly filled with anguish so how can such a person then attribute daughters to Him? Exalted be He high above such claims.

hype_questions: How can someone attribute daughters to Allah?
What is the significance of a child being likened to its parent in this context?
How does one's reaction to good news about a child affect their faith?
propositions: When someone receives good news that they have attributed to Allah, their face becomes gloomy as they suppress their rage.
A person's reaction to receiving news of a child being born is one of anguish and darkness, rather than joy or celebration.
It is not possible for someone who experiences such strong emotions upon hearing good news about a child to attribute daughters to Allah.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Do they attribute to Him˺ those who are brought up in fineries and are not commanding in disputes?

Despite being brought up in fineries and ornaments, someone can still be said to have the ability to understand and attribute to God.

source_text:
Verse: Still they have labelled the angels, who are servants of the Most Compassionate, as female. Did they witness their creation? Their statement will be recorded, and they will be questioned!

Tafsir: And they have made the angels who are themselves servants of the Compassionate One females. Did they witness were they present at their creation? Their testimony to the effect that they are females will be written down and they will be questioned about it in the Hereafter wherefore punishment will ensue for them.

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: Is it they who distribute your Lord’s mercy? We ˹alone˺ have distributed their ˹very˺ livelihood among them in this worldly life and raised some of them in rank above others so that some may employ others in service. ˹But˺ your Lord’s mercy is far better than whatever ˹wealth˺ they amass.

We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world making some of them wealthy and others poor and raised some of them in wealth above others by degrees so that some of them who are wealthy may take others who are poor in service disposed to work for them in return for a wage the final yā’ in sukhriyyā is attributive; a variant reading has sikhriyyan; and the mercy of your Lord that is Paradise is better than what they amass in this world.

Paradise is a reward that surpasses all worldly riches.

source_text:
Verse: and ornaments ˹of gold˺. Yet all this is no more than a ˹fleeting˺ enjoyment in this worldly life. ˹But˺ the Hereafter with your Lord is ˹only˺ for those mindful ˹of Him˺.

Yet surely wa-in in is softened from the hardened form inna all that would be nothing read lamā with the mā as extra; or read lammā to mean ‘but’ making the particle in for negation but the transient enjoyment of the life of this world enjoyed during it but then perishes and the Hereafter Paradise with your Lord is for the God-fearing.

Verse: Or do those who commit evil deeds ˹simply˺ think that We will make them equal—in their life and after their death—to those who believe and do good? How wrong is their judgment!

Tafsir: Or am has the significance of the rhetorical hamza of denial do those who have perpetrated evil acts such as disbelief and disobedience suppose that We shall treat them as those who believe and perform righteous deeds equally sawā’an is the predicate in their life and in their death? mahyāhum wa-mamātuhum this clause constitutes the subject and a supplement; the sentence itself is a substitution for the kāf of ka’lladhīna ‘as those’ and both suffixed pronouns -hum refer to the disbelievers. The meaning is do they suppose that in the Hereafter We will assign them a good fate like believers that they will enjoy a life of plenty one equal to their life in this world as when they said to the believers ‘Surely if we were to be resurrected we will be given the same good things that you will be given!’ God exalted be He says in accordance with His denial implicit in the rhetorical interrogative hamza How evil is that judgement which they make! In other words it will not be so for in the Hereafter they will be suffering in the chastisement in contrast to their lives in this world; the believers on the other hand will be delighting in the Reward in the Hereafter because of their righteous deeds in this world such as their observance of prayers their alms-giving fasting and otherwise the mā ‘that … which’ relates to the verbal action that is to say ba’isa hukman hukmuhum hādhā ‘awful as a judgement is this judgement of theirs’.

Tafsir: This is Our book the register of deeds recorded by the guardian angels which pronounces against you with truth. Indeed We used to write down record and preserve what you used to do’.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the record of our deeds?
How are our deeds recorded?
Who records our deeds?
propositions: This record of ours speaks the truth about you.
We always had your deeds recorded by the angels.
Indeed, We used to write down record and preserve what you used to do.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who believed and did good, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is ˹truly˺ the absolute triumph.

Tafsir: So as for those who believed and performed righteous deeds their Lord will admit them into His mercy His Paradise. That is the manifest triumph the clear and evident triumph.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reward for those who believe and do good?
How does Allah's mercy manifest in the afterlife?
What is the nature of triumph in Islam?
propositions: Those who believed and did good will be admitted into their Lord's mercy.
The ultimate triumph is entering one's Lord's mercy and Paradise.
Performing righteous deeds is a means to attain Allah's mercy and Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: And as for those who disbelieved, ˹they will be told,˺ “Were My revelations not recited to you, yet you acted arrogantly and were a wicked people?

Tafsir: But as for those who disbelieved it will be said to them ‘Were not My signs was not the Qur’ān recited to you but you were disdainful you were arrogant and were a guilty a disbelieving lot?

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the Quran?
Why do people act arrogantly despite receiving divine revelations?
How will those who disbelieve be held accountable?
propositions: My revelations were recited to them.
They acted arrogantly and were a wicked people.
They were disdainful of the Quran's signs.

source_text:
Verse: And whenever it was said ˹to you˺, ‘Surely Allah’s promise ˹of judgment˺ is true and there is no doubt about the Hour,’ you said ˹mockingly˺, ‘We do not know what the Hour is! We think it is no more than speculation, and we are not convinced ˹that it will ever come˺.’”

Tafsir: And when it was said to you O disbelievers “God’s promise of resurrection is indeed true and there is no doubt about the Hour” read al-sā‘atu or al-sā‘ata you said “We do not know what the Hour is. We only make conjectures al-Mubarrad said that this actually means in nahnu illā nazunnu zannan and we are by no means certain” ’ that it will come to pass.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's promise of resurrection?
Can we be certain about the Hour (of Judgment)?
Is the Hour (of Judgment) a matter of speculation or reality?
propositions: Allah's promise of resurrection is indeed true.
There is no doubt about the Hour.
We do not know what the Hour is, but we make conjectures.

source_text:
Verse: And the evil ˹consequences˺ of their deeds will unfold before them, and they will be overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.

Tafsir: And there will appear before them in the Hereafter the evils of what they did in this world that is to say the requital thereof and they will be besieged by there shall befall them what they used to deride namely the chastisement of the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What will be the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter?
How will they be punished for ridiculing others?
What will happen to those who deride others in this life?
propositions: The evil consequences of their deeds will unfold before them.
There will appear before them in the Hereafter the evils of what they did in this world that is to say the requital thereof.
They will be besieged by there shall befall them what they used to deride namely the chastisement of the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: It will be said, “This Day We will neglect you as you neglected the meeting of this Day of yours! Your home will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.

Tafsir: And it will be said ‘Today We will forget you We will abandon you in the Fire just as you forgot the encounter of this day of yours that is to say just as you neglected to perform those good deeds in preparation for the encounter with it and your abode will be the Fire and you will not have any helpers any protectors therefrom.

hype_questions: What happens when we neglect our preparations for the Day of Judgment?
Will I have any protectors in the Fire?

propositions: This Day We will neglect you as you neglected the meeting of this Day of yours.
Your home will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.
We will forget you We will abandon you in the Fire just as you forgot the encounter of this day of yours.
just as you neglected to perform those good deeds in preparation for the encounter with it
your abode will be the Fire and you will not have any helpers any protectors therefrom.

source_text:
Verse: This is because you made a mockery of Allah’s revelations, and were deluded by ˹your˺ worldly life.” So ˹from˺ that Day ˹on˺ they will not be taken out of the Fire, nor will they be allowed to appease ˹their Lord˺.

Tafsir: That is because you took God’s signs the Qur’ān in mockery and the life of this world deceived you’ to the extent that you said ‘There is neither Resurrection nor Reckoning’. So today they will not be brought out read either active yakhrujūna ‘they will not come out’ or passive yukhrajūna ‘they will not be brought out’ of it of the Fire nor will they asked to make amends they will not be asked to try to attain the pleasure of their Lord by repenting or being obedient for such action will be of no use then.

hype_questions: Will those who deny the Day of Judgment be brought out of the Fire?
Can repentance or obedience change their fate?
Is it possible for them to attain the pleasure of Allah?
propositions: You took God's signs in mockery.
The life of this world deceived you.
There is neither Resurrection nor Reckoning.

source_text:
Verse: So all praise is for Allah—Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of all worlds.

Tafsir: So to God belongs all praise the attribution to Him of what is beautiful in words for fulfilling His promise regarding the deniers; Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth the Lord of the Worlds the Creator of all that has been mentioned ‘ālam ‘world’ denotes everything other than God; it is in the plural ‘ālamīn because of the different types of beings in them; rabbi ‘Lord’ in the last clause is a substitution for the previous ones.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's lordship?
How does Allah fulfill His promises to those who deny Him?
What does it mean for something to be 'other than God'?
propositions: All praise belongs to Allah.
The attribution of beauty in words is attributed to Allah for fulfilling His promise regarding the deniers.
Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and the Creator of all that has been mentioned.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belongs ˹all˺ Majesty in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And to Him belongs all grandeur all majesty in the heavens and the earth fī’l-samāwāti wa’l-ardi is a circumstantial qualifier and He is the Mighty the Wise — as explained in a similar statement above.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's majesty?
How does Allah's wisdom manifest in creation?
What are the characteristics of Allah's power?
propositions: Allah possesses grandeur and majesty in both heaven and earth.
Allah is the Mighty, All-Wise

source_text:
Verse: ha-Mĩm.

Tafsir: Hā mīm God knows best what He means by these letters.

hype_questions: Does God have a specific meaning in mind when using the letter mīm?
Can humans truly understand the intentions of God?

source_text:
Verse: The revelation of this Book is from Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: The revelation of the Book the Qur’ān tanzīlu’l-kitābi the subject is from God mina’Llāhi the predicate thereof the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His actions.

hype_questions: What is the source of the Qur'ān?
Who is the Almighty God in Islam?
What does it mean to be All-Wise?
propositions: The revelation of the Book is from Allah.
Allah is the Mighty in His kingdom.
Allah is the Wise in His actions.

source_text:
Verse: We only created the heavens and the earth and everything in between for a purpose and an appointed term. Yet the disbelievers are turning away from what they have been warned about.

Tafsir: We have not created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except as a creation in truth so that it may be an indication of Our power and Our Oneness and for an appointed term until the point of their annihilation on the Day of Resurrection. Yet those who disbelieve are disregardful of what they are warned of what they are threatened with in the way of impending chastisement.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creation?
How does the Quran describe God's power and Oneness?
What happens to those who disbelieve on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: We created the heavens and the earth for a purpose and an appointed term.
The Quran is an indication of God's power and Oneness.
Those who disbelieve will be disregarded by God on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Have you considered whatever ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created on earth! Or do they have a share in ˹the creation of˺ the heavens? Bring me a scripture ˹revealed˺ before this ˹Quran˺ or a shred of knowledge, if what you say is true.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Have you considered say Inform me about what you invoke what you worship besides God? namely the idols min dūni’Llāhi constitutes the first object of the verb. Show me — inform me — arūnī repeated for emphasis what they have created mādhā khalaqū the second object of the earth mina’l-ardi the explication of mā ‘what part’. Or do they have any share any partnership in the creation of the heavens? with God? am ‘or’ has the significance of the rhetorical interrogative hamza of denial. Bring me a scripture that has been revealed before this Qur’ān or some vestige some remnant of knowledge transmitted from the ancients confirming the soundness of your claim that your worship of the idols brings you closer to God if you are truthful’ in your claim.

hype_questions: Do idols have a share in the creation of the heavens?
Can idols create on earth?
Does worshiping idols bring you closer to God?
propositions: The Prophet asked his followers to inform him about what they invoke besides Allah.
Allah created the earth and the heavens, but idols did not.
There is no scripture revealed before the Qur'an that confirms the soundness of worshiping idols.

source_text:
Verse: And who could be more astray than those who call upon others besides Allah—˹others˺ that cannot respond to them until the Day of Judgment, and are ˹even˺ unaware of their calls?

Tafsir: And who is man here is interrogative but meant rhetorically as a negation in other words ‘no one is’ further astray than him who invokes him who worships besides God that is to say other than Him such as would not respond to him even until the Day of Resurrection — these are the idols who never answer those who worship them in anything that they ask for — and who are heedless of their supplication? their worship because they are inanimates that possess no faculty of comprehension.

hype_questions: What happens to those who worship idols besides Allah?
Can idols respond to the supplications of their worshippers?
Who is more astray than one who invokes other deities besides Allah?
propositions: No one is further astray than he who invokes other deities besides Allah.
Idols do not respond to the supplications of their worshippers until the Day of Resurrection.
Those who worship idols are unaware of their calls and possess no faculty of comprehension.

source_text:
Verse: And when ˹such˺ people will be gathered together, those ˹gods˺ will be their enemies and will disown their worship.

Tafsir: And when mankind are gathered they the idols will be enemies to them to those who had worshipped them and they will deny they will disavow their worship the worship of those who had worshipped them.

hype_questions: What happens when people gather to worship idols?
Will the idols turn against those who worshipped them?
How will the idols respond to those who had worshipped them?

Those who worshipped idols will be denied their worship.
