Paradise is a place where inhabitants will abide.
They will be rewarded for what they used to do.

source_text:
Verse: We have commanded people to honour their parents. Their mothers bore them in hardship and delivered them in hardship. Their ˹period of˺ bearing and weaning is thirty months. In time, when the child reaches their prime at the age of forty, they pray, “My Lord! Inspire me to ˹always˺ be thankful for Your favours which You blessed me and my parents with, and to do good deeds that please You. And instil righteousness in my offspring. I truly repent to You, and I truly submit ˹to Your Will˺.”

Tafsir: And We have enjoined man to be kind husnan a variant reading has ihsānan that is to say We have commanded him to act kindly towards both of them thus ihsānan is in the accusative as a verbal noun because of the implied verbal action; the same applies to husnan to his parents. His mother carries him in travail and gives birth to him in travail that is to say with suffering; and his gestation and his weaning from suckling take thirty months six months being the minimum period for gestation the remainder being the maximum period of suckling; it is also said that regardless of whether she bore him for six or nine months she should suckle him for the remainder. So that hattā is a particle of purpose for an implied sentence that is to say wa-‘āsha hattā ‘and he lived on so that …’ when he is mature namely at his prime in terms of his strength intellect and reasoning the minimum age for which is thirty or thirty three years and reaches forty years that is exactly forty years which is the maximum for attaining maturity he says ‘My Lord! this to the end of this verse was revealed regarding Abū Bakr al-Siddīq when he had reached forty years of age two years after the beginning of the Prophet’s Mission s. He Abū Bakr believed in him whereafter his parents believed in the Prophet followed by his son ‘Abd al-Rahmān then ‘Abd al-Rahmān’s son Abū ‘Atīq Muhammad b. ‘Abd al-Rahmān. Inspire me to give thanks for Your favour with which You have favoured me and my parents namely the grace of affirming God’s Oneness and that I may act righteously in a way that will please You thus he Abū Bakr emancipated nine believers who had been enduring torture at the hands of the idolaters for their belief in God and invest my seed with righteousness all of them were believers. Indeed I repent to You and I am truly of those who submit to You’.

hype_questions: What is the significance of honoring one's parents in Islam?
How does a Muslim express gratitude to Allah for His blessings?
What is the importance of acting righteously and investing in righteousness?
propositions: We have commanded people to honour their parents.
Their mothers bore them in hardship and delivered them in hardship.
In time, when the child reaches their prime at the age of forty, they pray for inspiration to be thankful for Allah's favours.
He truly repent[s] to You, and he truly submit[s] to Your Will.

source_text:
Verse: It is from these ˹people˺ that We will accept the good they did, and overlook their misdeeds—along with the residents of Paradise, ˹in fulfilment of˺ the true promise they have been given.

Tafsir: Those that is those who say such words Abū Bakr and others are they from whom We accept the best of what they do and overlook their misdeeds as they stand among the inhabitants of Paradise fī ashābi’ll-jannati a circumstantial qualifier in other words ‘being among them’ — this is the true promise which they were promised by His words God has promised the believers both men and women Gardens … Q. 972.

hype_questions: What is the promise that believers were given?
How do we get accepted by God?
What happens to those who are among the inhabitants of Paradise?
propositions: We will accept the good they did.
We overlook their misdeeds.
God has promised the believers Gardens.

source_text:
Verse: But some scold their parents, “Enough with you! Are you warning me that I will be brought forth ˹from the grave˺, while many generations had already perished before me ˹for good˺?” The parents cry to Allah for help, ˹and warn their child,˺ “Pity you. Have faith! Surely Allah’s promise is true.” But the deniers insist, “This is nothing but ancient fables.”

Tafsir: As for him who says to his parents li-wālidayhi a variant reading has li-wālidihi ‘his parent’ denoting the generic noun ‘Fie read uffin or uffan as a verbal noun meaning ‘something putrid and disgusting’ on you both I am exasperated at both of you. Do you threaten me a-ta‘idāninī a variant reading has a-ta‘idānnī that I shall be raised from the grave when already generations communities have passed away before me?’ and they have not been raised from their graves. And they call on God for succour that he their child repent saying to him if you do not repent ‘Woe to you waylaka that is to say halākaka ‘you are ruined!’. Believe! in resurrection. Surely God’s promise is true’. But he says ‘This belief in resurrection is nothing but the fables of the ancients’ lies of theirs.

hype_questions: Will I be brought forth from the grave?
Have my parents been raised from their graves before me?
What happens to those who do not repent?
propositions: Some scold their parents, saying 'Enough with you!'
Parents cry to Allah for help and warn their child to have faith.
The deniers insist that the belief in resurrection is nothing but ancient fables.

source_text:
Verse: These are the ones against whom the fate of earlier communities of jinn and humans has been justified, ˹for˺ they were truly losers.

Tafsir: Such are the ones against whom the Word of chastisement is due is necessary concerning communities of jinn and humans that have passed away before them. Truly they are losers.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the message of their Lord?
Can those who have passed away be held accountable for their actions?
How do communities of jinn and humans ultimately fare in the afterlife?
propositions: The fate of earlier communities of jinn and humans has been justified against those who reject the message of their Lord.
Those who reject the message of their Lord are truly losers.
Communities of jinn and humans that have passed away before others are accountable for their actions.

source_text:
Verse: Each ˹of the two groups˺ will be ranked according to what they have done so He may fully reward all. And none will be wronged.

Tafsir: And for each one of both categories believer and disbeliever there will be degrees of status thus the degrees of the believers in Paradise are high while the degrees of disbelievers in the Fire are despicable according to what they have done that is to say according to what believers have done in the way of acts of obedience and disbelievers in the way of acts of disobedience and that He may recompense them fully namely God li-yuwaffiyahum a variant reading has li-nuwaffiyahum ‘that We may recompense them fully’ for their deeds that is pay them their deserts and they will not be wronged not even in a single thing that may be diminished for believers or increased for disbelievers.

hype_questions: Will the righteous be rewarded in full?
How will individuals be judged based on their actions?
What is the ultimate fate of those who have lived virtuous lives?
propositions: Each group will be ranked according to their deeds so that God may fully reward all.
Believers will receive high degrees in Paradise, while disbelievers will receive low degrees in the Fire based on their actions.
God will recompense individuals fully for their deeds, ensuring they are not wronged in any aspect.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Watch for˺ the Day ˹when˺ the disbelievers will be exposed to the Fire. ˹They will be told,˺ “You ˹already˺ exhausted your ˹share of˺ pleasures during your worldly life, and ˹fully˺ enjoyed them. So Today you will be rewarded with the torment of disgrace for your arrogance throughout the land with no right, and for your rebelliousness.”

Tafsir: And on the day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire by its being revealed for them it will be said to them ‘You squandered read with one hamza adhhabtum or with two hamzas as an interrogative a-adhhabtum ‘have you sqaundered …?’; or with one hamza adhhabtum or with an initial long ‘a’ ādhhabtum with both of these pronounced fully or without pronouncing the second hamza your good things during your life of the world by preoccupying yourselves with sensual delights and enjoyed them. So today you will be requited with the chastisement of humiliation in return for acting arrogantly in the earth without right and in return for that regarding which you used to act immorally’ and for the torture you used to inflict upon others therein.

hype_questions: Will those who disbelieve be punished for their past actions?
What will happen to individuals who have squandered their life's pleasures?
Can one ever escape the consequences of their arrogance?
propositions: The Day of Judgment is approaching.
Those who disbelieve will be exposed to the Fire.
They squandered their worldly pleasures without any right or justification.
Their arrogance and rebelliousness will lead to humiliation in return.
They inflicted torture on others, which will now be requited upon them.

source_text:
Verse: And remember the brother of ’Ȃd, when he warned his people, who inhabited the sand-hills—there were certainly warners before and after him—˹saying,˺ “Worship none but Allah. I truly fear for you the torment of a tremendous day.”

Tafsir: And mention the brother of ‘Ād namely Hūd peace be upon him when idh … from here to the end of the verse constitutes an inclusive substitution he warned his people he threatened them at Ahqāf ‘the Sand dunes’ is the name of a valley in Yemen where their dwellings were located — and already warners messengers had passed away before him and after him that is to say before Hūd came to them and after him to their peoples — saying ‘Do not worship anyone but God the statement beginning with wa-qad khalat ‘and already warners had passed away’ is a parenthetical one. Truly I fear for you — should you worship other than God — the chastisement of a dreadful day’.

hype_questions: What is the message of Prophet Hūd to his people?
Why did Prophet Hūd warn his people about the torment of a tremendous day?
What is the consequence of worshiping other than God, according to Prophet Hūd?
propositions: Prophet Hūd warned his people not to worship anyone but Allah.
There were already warners and messengers before and after Prophet Hūd.
Worshiping other than God will lead to the chastisement of a dreadful day.

source_text:
Verse: They argued, “Have you come to turn us away from our gods? Bring us then whatever you threaten us with, if what you say is true.”

Tafsir: They said ‘Have you come to divert us from our gods? to turn us away from worship of them. Then bring us what you threaten us with of chastisement for worshipping them if you are of the truthful’ in saying that it will befall us.

hype_questions: Will this Quran bring about a change in our worship?
What consequences will we face if we continue to worship other than Allah?
Is the Quran's message of truth and guidance?
propositions: They argued that the prophet should not turn them away from their gods.
The prophet was asked to bring chastisement for worshipping other than Allah.
If the prophet is truthful, then he will bring about a change in their worship.

source_text:
Verse: He responded, “The knowledge ˹of its time˺ is only with Allah. I only convey to you what I have been sent with. But I can see that you are a people acting ignorantly.”

Tafsir: He Hūd said ‘The knowledge is with God only He is the One Who knows when chastisement will befall you and I am merely conveying to you what I have been sent with to you. But I see that you are an ignorant lot’ given your hastening on of the chastisement.

hype_questions: What is the nature of knowledge in relation to Allah?
How does one convey divine messages to humanity?
What is the consequence of ignoring divine warnings?
propositions: The knowledge of a particular time is only with Allah.
I convey only what I have been sent with.
You are acting ignorantly due to your hastening towards chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Then when they saw the torment as a ˹dense˺ cloud approaching their valleys, they said ˹happily˺, “This is a cloud bringing us rain.” ˹But Hûd replied,˺ “No, it is what you sought to hasten: a ˹fierce˺ wind carrying a painful punishment!”

Tafsir: Then when they saw it that is when they saw what chastisement really was as a sudden cloud a cloud that appeared out of nowhere on the horizon heading towards their valleys they said ‘This is a cloud that will bring us rain!’. God exalted be He says Nay but it is what you sought to hasten of the chastisement — a hurricane rīhun substitutes for mā ‘what’ containing a painful chastisement

hype_questions: What is the true nature of chastisement?
How does God respond to those who seek hastened punishment?
What is the difference between a cloud bringing rain and a hurricane?
propositions: A dense cloud was approaching their valleys.
They said it was a cloud that would bring them rain.
It was actually a fierce wind carrying a painful punishment.

source_text:
Verse: It destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, leaving nothing visible except their ruins. This is how We reward the wicked people.

Tafsir: destroying ruining everything it passes through by the command of its Lord by His will that is to say destroying everything that He wants to destroy with it. And so it destroyed their men women children and properties by flinging them up into the air high above the ground and tearing them to pieces. Only Hūd and those who believed with him remained unscathed. So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thus in the way that We requited them do We requite guilty folk besides them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are destroyed by the Qiyamah?
How does Allah requite guilty folk besides Hūd and his believers?
What is the nature of the destruction caused by the Qiyamah?
propositions: The Qiyamah destroys everything in its path by command of its Lord.
Allah destroys everything He wants to destroy with it, including men, women, children, and properties.
Only Hūd and those who believed with him remained unscathed from the destruction caused by the Qiyamah.
The dwellings of Hūd and his believers are the only things left visible after the destruction.
Allah requites guilty folk besides Hūd and his believers in a manner similar to how He requited them.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We had established them in a way We have not established you ˹Meccans˺. And We gave them hearing, sight, and intellect. But neither their hearing, sight, nor intellect were of any benefit to them whatsoever, since they persisted in denying Allah’s signs. And ˹so˺ they were overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.

Tafsir: And verily We had empowered them in ways in which We have not in is either for negation or extra empowered you O people of Mecca in the way of strength and means and We had vested them with ears and eyes and hearts. But their ears and their eyes and their hearts did not avail them in any way min shay’in min is extra since idh is operated by aghnā ‘avail’ and imbued with the sense of a particle introducing a reason they used to deny the signs of God His clear proofs and they were besieged by there befell them what they used to deride of chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens when one ridicules the signs of God?
How does denial of Allah's signs affect an individual?
Can ridicule lead to chastisement?
propositions: We established them in a way We have not established you.
We gave them hearing, sight, and intellect.
Their hearing, sight, nor intellect were of any benefit to them whatsoever.
They persisted in denying Allah’s signs.
They were overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.
We empowered them in ways in which We have not empowered you O people of Mecca.
We vested them with ears and eyes and hearts.
Their ears and their eyes and their hearts did not avail them in any way.
They used to deny the signs of God His clear proofs.
They were besieged by there befell them what they used to deride of chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: We certainly destroyed the societies around you after having varied the signs so perhaps they would return ˹to the Right Path˺.

Tafsir: And We certainly destroyed the towns that were around you that is We destroyed their inhabitants the likes of Thamūd ‘Ād and the people of Lot and We dispensed the signs We repeated the clear proofs so that perhaps they might return.

hype_questions: Can destruction lead to a return to righteousness?
What are the consequences of ignoring divine signs?
How can humanity learn from past civilizations?
propositions: We destroyed the societies around you after varying the signs.
The destruction of Thamūd, Ād, and Lot serves as a warning for future generations.
Repeating clear proofs may prompt individuals to return to the Right Path.

source_text:
Verse: Why then did those ˹idols˺ they took as gods—hoping to get closer ˹to Him˺—not come to their aid? Instead, they failed them. That is ˹the result of˺ their lies and their fabrications.

Tafsir: So why did they not help them by averting from them the chastisement those whom they had chosen besides God that is to say other than Him as a means of nearness through whom they may secure nearness to God to be gods? alongside Him and these are the idols the first object of ittakhadhū ‘they had chosen’ is the omitted pronoun referred to by the relative clause alladhīna ‘those who …’ and it is hum ‘they’; qurbānan ‘nearness’ is the second object with ālihatan ‘gods’ as its substitution. Nay but they forsook them when the chastisement came down on them and that that is to say that choosing of theirs of idols as gods as a means of nearness to God was their lie and what they used to invent — the lies they used to speak mā ‘what’ either relates to the verbal action ‘their lying’ or it indicates a relative clause with the referential pronoun omitted this being fīhi ‘about’.

hype_questions: What happens when people choose false gods instead of God?
Why did the idols not help those who took them as gods?
Can choosing false gods bring people closer to God?
propositions: Those who took idols as gods failed to receive aid from them.
The chastisement that came down on them was a result of their lies and fabrications.
Choosing idols as gods is a means of nearness to God, but it is false.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember, O  Prophet,˺ when We sent a group of jinn your way to listen to the Quran. Then, upon hearing it, they said ˹to one another˺, “Listen quietly!” Then when it was over, they returned to their fellow jinn as warners.

Tafsir: And mention when We sent a company of jinn your way — the jinn of Nasībīn in Yemen or the jinn of Nineveh who were seven or nine and this was while the Prophet s was leading the dawn prayer with some of his Companions at Batn Nakhla as reported by the two Shaykhs al-Bukhārī and Muslim — to listen to the Qur’ān and when they were in its presence they said that is they said to one another ‘Listen carefully!’ concentrate in order to hear it carefully. Then when it was finished when he was finished reciting it they went back to their people to warn them to threaten their people with the chastisement from God if they do not believe — they had been Jews but then become Muslims.

hype_questions: Can jinn be swayed by the recitation of the Qur'an?
How do jinn respond to hearing the Qur'an?
What is the role of jinn as warners in the context of prophethood?
propositions: The Prophet was sent a group of jinn to listen to the Qur'an.
Upon hearing the Qur'an, the jinn said 'Listen quietly!'
After finishing reciting the Qur'an, the jinn went back to their people to warn them.
The jinn had been Jews but then became Muslims.
God threatens chastisement upon those who do not believe.

source_text:
Verse: They declared, “O our fellow jinn! We have truly heard a scripture revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it. It guides to the truth and the Straight Way.

Tafsir: They said ‘O our people! Indeed we have heard a Book namely the Qur’ān which has been revealed after Moses confirming what was before it what preceded it such as the Torah. It guides to the truth submission to God islām and to a straight way that is the way thereto to Islam.

hype_questions: What is the main guide of the Qur'ān?
How does the Qur'ān confirm what came before it?
What is the straight way guided by the Qur'ān?
propositions: A scripture has been revealed after Moses confirming what came before it.
The Qur'ān guides to the truth and the Straight Way.
Submission to God is a part of the guidance provided by the Qur'ān.

source_text:
Verse: O  our fellow jinn! Respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him, He will forgive your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.

Tafsir: O our people! Respond to God’s summoner Muhammad (s) by embracing faith and believe in him and He God will forgive you some of your sins because some of these sins are wrongs done to others and which therefore can only be forgiven after those wronged are reconciled — and shelter you from a painful chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens if I respond to God's summoner?
Can I get forgiveness for my sins?
How can I avoid a painful punishment?
propositions: Respond to the caller of Allah.
Believe in Muhammad (s).
God will forgive some of your sins.
Some sins are wrongs done to others, which must be reconciled before forgiveness is granted.
Shelter you from a painful chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will have no escape on earth, nor will they have any protectors against Him. It is they who are clearly astray.”

Tafsir: And whoever does not respond to God’s summoner cannot thwart God on earth that is to say he will not be able to thwart God by escaping from Him and eluding Him and he the one who does not respond will not have besides Him that is besides God any protectors any helpers to ward off the chastisement from him — those who do not respond are in manifest error’ plain and evident error.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who refuses to acknowledge God's summons?
Can escaping from God's wrath ever be successful?
Who can protect someone from God's chastisement?
propositions: Anyone who does not respond to Allah's caller will have no escape on earth.
Those who do not respond to Allah's summoner cannot thwart Allah on earth.
There is no one besides Allah that can protect someone from His chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not realize that Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth and did not tire in creating them, is able to give life to the dead? Yes ˹indeed˺! He is certainly Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: Have they not seen have they not realised that is the deniers of resurrection that God Who created the heavens and the earth and Who was not wearied by their creation Who did not fail therein is able to give life to the dead? bi-qādirin is the predicate of anna ‘that’ the bi- having been added to it because the statement has the same force as the construction a-laysa’Llāhu bi-qādirin ‘Is God not able …?’. Yes indeed He is able to give life to the dead. Indeed He has is able to do all things.

hype_questions: Is God not able to give life to the dead?
Can God create and sustain the universe without getting tired?
Does God have the power to do all things?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and the earth.
Allah is able to give life to the dead.
Allah has the ability to do all things.

source_text:
Verse: And on the Day the disbelievers will be exposed to the Fire, ˹they will be asked,˺ “Is this ˹Hereafter˺ not the truth?” They will cry, “Absolutely, by our Lord!” It will be said, “Then taste the punishment for your disbelief.”

Tafsir: And on the day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire when they are being chastised in it it will be said to them ‘Is not this chastisement the truth?’ They will say ‘Yes by our Lord!’ He will say ‘Then taste the chastisement for what you used to disbelieve in’.

hype_questions: Will those who disbelieve be punished for their disbelief?
Is the chastisement of the Fire a sign of truth?
What will happen to those who are exposed to the Fire?
propositions: The Day of Judgment is real.
Disbelievers will be punished for their disbelief.
The Fire is a chastisement from Allah.

source_text:
Verse: So endure patiently, as did the Messengers of Firm Resolve. ˹This is˺ a ˹sufficient˺ warning! Then, will anyone be destroyed except the rebellious people?

Tafsir: So endure with patience the harm done to you by your people just as the resolute those of constancy and power of endurance during hardships from among the messengers endured with patience before you so that you may be one of resolve like them min of mina’l-rusuli is explicative as all of them were men of resolve; but some say that this particle min is actually meant to be partitive since excluded from their number are Adam on the basis of God’s saying exalted be He And We did not find in him any constancy Q. 20115; and Jonah on the basis of His words And do not be like the One of the fish Q. 6848. And do not seek to hasten it for them for your people the sending down of the chastisement on them. Some say that he the Prophet seemed by this stage to have become exasperated because of them and desired that chastisement be sent down on them which is why he was enjoined to exercise patience and to refrain from hastening the chastisement for them — for it would befall them eventually without doubt. It shall seem for them on the day when they see what they are promised of chastisement in the Hereafter given its long duration as though they had tarried in this world by their reckoning only an hour of a day. This Qur’ān is a communication a proclamation from God to you. So shall any be destroyed that is to say none shall be destroyed upon seeing the chastisement but the immoral folk? that is to say the disbelieving folk.

hype_questions: Will anyone be destroyed except the rebellious people?
What is the nature of constancy and power of endurance during hardships?
How will the people perceive their punishment in the Hereafter?
propositions: Endure patiently with harm done by your people.
The resolute messengers endured with patience before you.
Some say that min is partitive, excluding Adam and Jonah from the number of messengers.
Do not seek to hasten the chastisement for your people.
It shall seem for them on the day when they see what they are promised of chastisement in the Hereafter as though they had tarried in this world by their reckoning only an hour of a day.
This Qur’ān is a communication a proclamation from God to you.

source_text:
Verse: Those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, He will render their deeds void.

Tafsir: Those who disbelieve from among the people of Mecca and bar others from the way of God that is to say from faith He will leave their works to waste such as giving food to the poor or being kind to kin and so they will find no reward for these works of theirs in the Hereafter; but they are requited for them in this world purely out of His bounty exalted be He.

hype_questions: What happens to those who disbelieve and hinder others from the Way of Allah?
How will those who disbelieve be requited for their good deeds in this world?
Can one find reward for good works like giving food to the poor or being kind to kin if they disbelieve?
propositions: Those who disbelieve and hinder others from the Way of Allah will have their deeds rendered void.
The people of Mecca who disbelieve will be left with no reward for their good works in the Hereafter.
God's bounty is what rewards those who disbelieve for their good deeds in this world.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who believe, do good, and have faith in what has been revealed to Muhammad—which is the truth from their Lord—He will absolve them of their sins and improve their condition.

Tafsir: But those who believe namely the Helpers al-Ansār and others like them and perform righteous deeds and believe in what has been revealed to Muhammad namely the Qur’ān — and it is the truth from their Lord — He will absolve them of He will forgive them their misdeeds and rightly dispose their mind their state so that they do not disobey Him.

hype_questions: What happens to those who believe and perform good deeds?
How will Allah treat those who have faith in Muhammad's revelation?
Can believers expect forgiveness from Allah for their past misdeeds?
propositions: Those who believe and perform good deeds will be absolved of their sins.
Believers who have faith in Muhammad's revelation will be forgiven for their misdeeds.
Allah will improve the condition of believers and prevent them from disobeying Him.

source_text:
Verse: This is because the disbelievers follow falsehood, while the believers follow the truth from their Lord. This is how Allah shows people their true state ˹of faith˺.

Tafsir: That rendering void of their works and the absolution of evil deeds is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood Satan and because those who believe follow the truth the Qur’ān from their Lord. Thus in the same manner of clarification does God strike for mankind similitudes of themselves that is how He clarifies for them their states in other words the disbeliever has his work rendered void while the believer is forgiven.

hype_questions: Does Allah show people their true state of faith?
What happens to the works of those who disbelieve?
Can believers be forgiven for their evil deeds?
propositions: The disbelievers follow falsehood, while the believers follow the truth from their Lord.
Those who disbelieve are absolved of their evil deeds and have their works rendered void.
Allah clarifies the states of mankind through similitudes that reflect their true nature.

source_text:
Verse: So when you meet the disbelievers ˹in battle˺, strike ˹their˺ necks until you have thoroughly subdued them, then bind them firmly. Later ˹free them either as˺ an act of grace or by ransom until the war comes to an end. So will it be. Had Allah willed, He ˹Himself˺ could have inflicted punishment on them. But He does ˹this only to˺ test some of you by means of others. And those who are martyred in the cause of Allah, He will never render their deeds void.

Tafsir: So when you encounter in battle those who disbelieve then attack them with a striking of the necks fa-darba’l-riqābi is a verbal noun in place of the full verbal construction that is to say fa’dribū riqābahum ‘then strike their necks’ in other words slay them — reference is made to the ‘striking of the necks’ because the predominant cause of being slayed is to be struck in the neck. Then when you have made thoroughly decimated them bind spare them take them captive and bind firmly the bonds al-wathāq is what is used to bind yūthaqu a captive. Thereafter either set them free by grace mannan is a verbal noun in place of the full verbal construction that is to say either show them grace by setting them free unconditionally; or by ransom ransoming them with payment or with Muslim captives until the war that is to say its participants lay down its burdens its heavy loads of weaponry and other things so that either the disbelievers surrender or enter into a treaty. This last clause constitutes the ‘purpose’ of enjoining the Muslims to slaying and taking captive. So shall it be dhālika is the predicate of an implied subject such as al-amr ‘the ordinance’ in other words ‘the ordinance of God regarding them is as mentioned’. And had God willed He could have Himself taken vengeance on them without any fighting but He has commanded you to do it that He may test some of you by means of others from among them by way of battle so that the slain among you will end up in Paradise while those slain among them will end up in the Fire. And those who are slain qutilū a variant reading has qātalū ‘those who fight’ — this verse was revealed on the day of the battle of Uhud after the dead and the wounded had become numerous among the Muslims — in the way of God He will not let their works go to waste He will not render them void.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of fighting in battle?
How will Allah test some of us through others?
What happens to those who are martyred in the cause of Allah?
propositions: When you meet disbelievers in battle, strike their necks until they are thoroughly subdued.
You should bind them firmly and either set them free by grace or ransom them until the war comes to an end.
Allah will test some of us through others by means of battle.
Those who are martyred in the cause of Allah will not have their deeds rendered void.

source_text:
Verse: He will guide them ˹to their reward˺, improve their condition,

Tafsir: He will guide them in this world and in the Hereafter to what benefits them and rightly dispose their minds their condition in both with that guidance and disposal in this world being for those who were not slain but who have been included in the statement ‘and those who were slain’ qutilū because of the predominance therein of those who were slain.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of guidance in Islam?
How does guidance affect a person's condition in this world and the Hereafter?
Who are included in the statement 'and those who were slain'?
propositions: He will guide them to their reward.
Guidance improves their condition in both this world and the HereAfter.
Their condition in both worlds is disposed of with guidance.

source_text:
Verse: and admit them into Paradise, having made it known to them.

Tafsir: And He will admit them into Paradise which He has made known which He has pointed out to them so that they are guided to their dwellings in it and to their spouses and servants without asking to be shown the way.

hype_questions: What is Paradise?
How does Allah guide us to our dwellings in Paradise?
Can we ask for guidance on how to reach Paradise?
propositions: Allah will admit those who have been guided to Paradise into it.
Paradise has been made known to them.
Those who are guided to Paradise will be shown their dwellings in it.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! If you stand up for Allah, He will help you and make your steps firm.

Tafsir: O you who believe! If you help God that is to say His religion and His Messenger He will help you against your enemy and make your foothold firm He will make you stand firm while you fight on the battleground.

hype_questions: What happens when I stand up for Allah?
How will Allah help me in my struggle against an enemy?
What does it mean to have a firm foothold in the battlefield?
propositions: If you stand up for Allah, He will help you.
Helping God means His religion and His Messenger.
Allah will help you against your enemy and make your foothold firm.
He will make you stand firm while you fight on the battleground.

source_text:
Verse: As for the disbelievers, may they be doomed and may He render their deeds void.

Tafsir: And as for those who disbelieve from among the people of Mecca wa’lladhīna kafarū is the subject the predicate of which is an implicit ta‘isū ‘they shall be wretched’ as indicated by what follows wretchedness shall be their lot that is destruction and defeat from God. And He will make their works go to waste wa-adalla a‘mālahum is a supplement to the implied ta‘isū ‘they shall be wretched’.

hype_questions: What happens to those who disbelieve in the afterlife?
How will God judge those who reject Him?
What is the ultimate fate of those who refuse to believe?
propositions: The disbelievers will be wretched.
Wretchedness shall be their lot, which is destruction and defeat from God.
God will make their works go to waste.

source_text:
Verse: That is because they detest what Allah has revealed, so He has rendered their deeds void.

Tafsir: That wretchedness and wasting of their works is because they are averse to what God has revealed of the Qur’ān with all that it includes of religious obligations takālīf so He has made their works fail.

hype_questions: Does rejecting divine revelation lead to the nullification of one's actions?
How does the concept of religious obligations affect an individual's productivity?
Can aversion to God's revelations result in the failure of one's endeavors?
propositions: They detest what Allah has revealed.
Their works are void due to their rejection of divine revelation.
Takālīf refers to religious obligations that must be fulfilled.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not travelled throughout the land to see what was the end of those before them? Allah annihilated them, and a similar fate awaits the disbelievers.

Tafsir: Have they not travelled in the land to see the nature of the consequence for those who were before them? God destroyed them — He destroyed them their children and their possessions; and a fate the like thereof will be for the disbelievers that is to say the like of the fate of those before them.

hype_questions: What happens to those who disbelieve after being destroyed?
Will the fate of the disbelievers be similar to that of previous generations?
How does God's destruction affect the lives of believers and non-believers alike?
propositions: Allah annihilated those before them.
God destroyed their children and possessions.
A similar fate awaits the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: This is because Allah is the Patron of the believers while the disbelievers have no patron.

Tafsir: That granting of victory to the believers and the vanquishing of the disbelievers is because God is Patron Ally and Helper of those who believe and because the disbelievers have no patron.

hype_questions: What is the role of Allah in granting victory to believers?
Why do disbelievers have no patron?
How does God assist those who believe?
propositions: Allah is the Patron of the believers.
The disbelievers have no patron.
God is Patron Ally and Helper of those who believe.

source_text:
Verse: Surely Allah will admit those who believe and do good into Gardens under which rivers flow. As for the disbelievers, they enjoy themselves and feed like cattle. But the Fire will be their home.

Tafsir: God will surely admit those who believe and perform righteous deeds into gardens underneath which rivers flow. As for those who disbelieve they take their enjoyment in this world and eat as the cattle eat that is to say they are only concerned with filling their bellies and satisfying their private parts without giving any thought to the Hereafter; and the Fire will be their habitation their home their station and their final destination.

hype_questions: What happens to those who believe and do good?
How do disbelievers spend their lives?
What awaits those who reject Allah?
propositions: Allah admits believers into Gardens under which rivers flow.
Disbelievers enjoy themselves in this world but neglect the Hereafter.
The Fire is the final destination of disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Imagine, O  Prophet,˺ how many societies We destroyed that were far superior in might than your society—which drove you out—and there was none to help them!

Tafsir: And how many ka-ayyin means kam a town by which is meant the inhabitants thereof mightier in power than your town Mecca that is to say its inhabitants which expelled you akhrajatka is feminine despite the plural sense of inhabitants meant is because it takes into account the feminine form of qarya ‘town’ have We destroyed ahlaknāhum takes into account the former plural import of qarya ‘town’ and they had none to help them against Our destruction of them.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Prophet's society being driven out?
How do the destroyed societies compare to the Prophet's society in terms of power?
Why did the destroyed societies lack help against their destruction?
propositions: The Prophet's society was driven out.
Destroyed societies were far superior in might than the Prophet's society.
There was none to help the destroyed societies against their destruction.

source_text:
Verse: Can those ˹believers˺ who stand on clear proof from their Lord be like those whose evil deeds are made appealing to them and ˹only˺ follow their desires?

Tafsir: Is he who follows a clear sign a definitive argument and proof from his Lord and these are the believers like those whose evil deeds have been adorned for them so that they see them as fair deeds and these are the disbelievers of Mecca and who follow their desires? by worshipping graven images. In other words there is no similarity between the two.

hype_questions: Can a person who follows their desires be considered a believer?
What is the difference between those who follow their desires and believers?
How does worshiping graven images affect one's faith?
propositions: Those who stand on clear proof from their Lord cannot be like those whose evil deeds are made appealing to them.
Believers follow a clear sign as a definitive argument and proof from their Lord.
The disbelievers of Mecca follow their desires by worshipping graven images.

source_text:
Verse: The description of the Paradise promised to the righteous is that in it are rivers of fresh water, rivers of milk that never changes in taste, rivers of wine delicious to drink, and rivers of pure honey. There they will ˹also˺ have all kinds of fruit, and forgiveness from their Lord. ˹Can they be˺ like those who will stay in the Fire forever, left to drink boiling water that will tear apart their insides?

Tafsir: A similitude a description of the Garden promised to the God-fearing the Garden that is shared equally by all those who enter it this first clause is the subject of which the predicate follows therein are rivers of unstaling water read āsin or asin similar in form to dārib ‘striker’ and hadhir ‘cautious’ that is to say one that does not change in contrast to the water of this world which may change due to some factor; and rivers of milk unchanging in flavour in contrast to the milk of this world on account of its issuing from udders and rivers of wine delicious to the drinkers in contrast to the wine of this world which is distasteful to drink; and also rivers of purified honey in contrast to the honey of this world which when it issues out of the bellies of bees becomes mixed with wax and other elements; and there will be for them therein varieties of every fruit and forgiveness from their Lord for He is pleased with them in addition to His beneficence towards them in the way mentioned in contrast to one who is a master of servants in this world who while being kind to them may at the same time be wrathful with them. Is such a one like him who abides in the Fire? ka-man huwa khālidun fī’l-nāri the predicate of an implied subject which is a-man huwa fī hādha’l-na‘īm ‘Is one who is amidst such bliss as him who abides in the Fire?’. And they will be given to drink boiling water which rips apart their bowels that is their entrails so that these will be excreted from their rears. Am‘ā’ ‘bowels’ is the plural of mi‘an its alif being derived from the yā’ of their saying mi‘yān as an alternative singular to mi‘an.

hype_questions: Can the righteous be like those who will stay in the Fire forever?
Is one who is amidst such bliss as him who abides in the Fire?
What happens to those who are given boiling water that rips apart their bowels?
propositions: The Paradise promised to the righteous has rivers of fresh water, milk, wine, and honey.
All kinds of fruit will be available in the Paradise.
Forgiveness from their Lord will be granted to those who enter the Paradise.
One who is a master of servants in this world may at the same time be wrathful with them.
The Fire is like a place where one abides forever, left to drink boiling water that will tear apart their insides.

source_text:
Verse: There are some of them who listen to you ˹O Prophet˺, but when they depart from you, they say ˹mockingly˺ to those ˹believers˺ gifted with knowledge, “What did he just say?” These are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed and who ˹only˺ follow their desires.

Tafsir: And there are some among them namely the disbelievers who listen to you during the Friday sermon — and these are the hypocrites; until when they go forth from you they say to those who have been given knowledge that is to say to the knowledgeable ones among the Companions of the Prophet such as ‘Abd Allāh Ibn Mas‘ūd and ‘Abd Allāh Ibn ‘Abbās in derision and mockery ‘What was he saying just now?’ read ānifan or anifan meaning al-sā‘a ‘just now’. In other words they mean to say ‘we will not go back to listen to him again’. Those are the ones on whose hearts God has set a seal of disbelief and who follow their own desires in acting with hypocrisy.

hype_questions: What is the significance of hypocrisy in Islam?
How does Allah seal the hearts of disbelievers?
What are the consequences of following one's desires and acting with hypocrisy?
propositions: Some individuals listen to the Prophet but depart and mock believers gifted with knowledge.
The hypocrites among the disbelievers listen to the Friday sermon but depart and deride knowledgeable Companions of the Prophet.
God has sealed the hearts of those who follow their desires and act with hypocrisy, preventing them from returning to listen to the Prophet.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who are ˹rightly˺ guided, He increases them in guidance and blesses them with righteousness.

Tafsir: But those who are rightly guided namely the believers He God enhances their guidance and invests them with fear of Him He inspires them to do that by which they can be wary of ending up in the Fire.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal for those who are guided by Allah?
How does Allah bless believers with righteousness?
What motivates believers to avoid the Fire?
propositions: Allah increases guidance in those who are rightly guided.
Believers are blessed with righteousness by Allah.
The fear of Allah inspires believers to avoid the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: Are they only waiting for the Hour to take them by surprise? Yet ˹some of˺ its signs have already come. Once it actually befalls them, will it not be too late to be mindful?

Tafsir: Do they then await they do not await namely the disbelievers of Mecca anything except that the Hour should come upon them an ta’tiyahum is an inclusive substitution for al-sā‘ata ‘the Hour’; in other words it cannot be other than that it will come upon them … suddenly? For already its portents the signs thereof have come among which are the sending of the Prophet s the splitting of the Moon Q. 541 and the Smoke Q. 4410. So when it the Hour has come upon them for what benefit will their reminder be? their remembering; in other words it will be of no benefit to them.

hype_questions: Will the reminder be of any benefit to them when the Hour comes?
Can they truly say that they were not warned about the Hour?
What will happen to those who are left behind after the Hour is revealed?
propositions: The Hour will come upon them suddenly.
Its portents and signs have already come among which are the sending of the Prophet s, the splitting of the Moon, and the Smoke.

source_text:
Verse: So, know ˹well, O  Prophet,˺ that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah. And seek forgiveness for your shortcomings and for ˹the sins of˺ the believing men and women. For Allah ˹fully˺ knows your movements and places of rest ˹O people˺.

Tafsir: Know then that there is no god except God that is to say adhere O Muhammad (s) to knowledge of this fact that will benefit you at the Resurrection and ask forgiveness for your sin — this was said to him despite his infallibility ‘isma so that his community might emulate him in this respect. Indeed he did do this. The Prophet s said ‘Verily I do ask God for forgiveness a hundred times every day’ — and for the believing men and believing women — herein is an honouring for them by having their Prophet enjoined to ask forgiveness for them. And God knows your going to and fro your bustle during the day in pursuit of your business and your place of rest when you retire to where you sleep at night. In other words He has knowledge of all your states nothing of which can be hidden from Him so be mindful of Him — the address in this verse is meant for believers as well as others.

hype_questions: Does Allah know our movements and places of rest?
Can we ask forgiveness for the sins of believers and non-believers alike?
Is it beneficial to ask God for forgiveness every day?
propositions: There is no god worthy of worship except Allah.
Allah knows your movements and places of rest.
You should seek forgiveness for your shortcomings and the sins of believers and non-believers alike.
The Prophet Muhammad (s) asks God for forgiveness a hundred times every day.
God has knowledge of all your states, nothing of which can be hidden from Him.

source_text:
Verse: And the believers say, “If only a sûrah was revealed ˹allowing self-defence˺!” Yet when a precise sûrah is revealed, in which fighting is ˹explicitly˺ mentioned, you see those with sickness in their hearts staring at you like someone in the throes of death. It would have been better for them

Tafsir: And those who believe say seeking to take part in the struggle ‘Why has a sūra not been revealed?’ one in which there is mention of the command to participate in the struggle. But when a definitive sūra is revealed one in which nothing is abrogated naskh and fighting that is to say requirement for it is mentioned in it you see those in whose hearts is a sickness that is doubt — and they are the hypocrites — looking at you with the look of someone fainting at the point of death because of their fear of it and their aversion to it; in other words they fear fighting and are averse to it. Yet more fitting for them fa-awlā lahum is a subject the predicate of which is the following tā‘atun wa-qawlun ma‘rūfun

hype_questions: What are the consequences of a person's fear and aversion to struggle in Islam?
How do hypocrites react when they see others participating in struggle?
What is the nature of those who are afflicted with sickness in their hearts?
propositions: Believers seek a sûrah that allows self-defence.
When a precise sûrah is revealed with explicit mention of fighting, hypocrites appear to be on the brink of death due to fear and aversion.
Fa-awlā lahum is a subject whose predicate is tā‘atun wa-qawlun ma‘rūfun.

source_text:
Verse: to obey and speak rightly. Then when fighting was ordained, it surely would have been better for them if they were true to Allah.

Tafsir: would be to offer obedience and honourable words that is words that are kind to you. Then when the matter has been resolved upon that is to say when fighting has been prescribed if they are loyal to God in faith and obedience it will be better for them the sentence beginning with law ‘if’ constitutes the response to idhā ‘when’.

hype_questions: What is the importance of obeying and speaking rightly?
How does loyalty to God impact one's situation when fighting is prescribed?
What constitutes a kind word that honors oneself?
propositions: To obey and speak rightly.
When fighting is ordained, it is better for them if they are true to Allah in faith and obedience.
Offering obedience and honourable words (i.e., kind words) is what constitutes a response when the matter has been resolved upon.

source_text:
Verse: Now if you ˹hypocrites˺ turn away, perhaps you would then spread corruption throughout the land and sever your ˹ties of˺ kinship!

Tafsir: May it not be the case with you read ‘asītum or ‘asaytum; there is a shift here from the third person to the second person address that if you were to turn away if you were to shun faith you would then cause corruption in the land and sever your kinship ties? in other words that you would then return to the ways of pagandom such as belligerence and fighting.

hype_questions: If I were to abandon my faith, would I cause corruption in the land?
Would shunning faith lead me back to pagandom and violence?
How would abandoning faith affect my relationships with my kin?
propositions: If you turn away from faith, you will spread corruption throughout the land.
You will sever your ties of kinship if you turn away from faith.
Abandoning faith may lead to a return to pagandom and violence.

source_text:
Verse: These are the ones who Allah has condemned, deafening them and blinding their eyes.

Tafsir: Those that is the agents of corruption are the ones whom God has cursed so made them deaf to hearing the truth and blinded their eyes to the path of guidance.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah curses someone?
How does God's curse affect a person's perception of truth?
Can someone be 'deafened' and 'blinded' by God's curse?
propositions: Allah has condemned those who are agents of corruption.
God has cursed those who are agents of corruption, making them deaf to the truth.
The path of guidance is obscured from those who are agents of corruption due to God's curse.

source_text:
Verse: Do they not then reflect on the Quran? Or are there locks upon their hearts?

Tafsir: Do they not contemplate the Qur’ān? and so recognise the truth. Or am here is like bal ‘nay but’ is it that there are locks on their hearts? so they are unable to comprehend it.

hype_questions: Can they understand the Quran?
Is there a barrier preventing them from comprehending it?
Do they recognize the truth?
propositions: They do not contemplate the Qur'an.
There are locks on their hearts.
They are unable to comprehend it.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who relapse ˹into disbelief˺ after ˹true˺ guidance has become clear to them, ˹it is˺ Satan ˹that˺ has tempted them, luring them with false hopes.

Tafsir: Truly those who have turned by way of hypocrisy their backs after the guidance has become clear to them Satan has seduced he has adorned disbelief for them and has given them false hopes read wa-umliya lahum ‘false hopes have been given to them’ or wa-amlā lahum where the one who gives the false hopes is Satan but only by God’s will exalted be He for he Satan is the one who leads them astray.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject guidance after it has become clear to them?
Who leads people astray and tempts them with false hopes?
Can anyone be saved from Satan's temptation?
propositions: Those who relapse into disbelief after true guidance has become clear to them are tempted by Satan.
Satan seduces people and gives them false hopes, leading them astray.
God's will is the only factor that determines whether someone is led astray or saved.

source_text:
Verse: That is because they said ˹privately˺ to those who ˹also˺ detest what Allah has revealed, “We will obey you in some matters.” But Allah ˹fully˺ knows what they are hiding.

Tafsir: That leading of them astray is because they said to those who were averse to what God revealed namely to the idolaters ‘We will obey you in some matters’ that is to say by cooperating to maintain enmity against the Prophet s and preventing people from participating in the struggle alongside him they had said as much secretly but God exalted be He exposed it; and God knows their secrets read asrārahum as the plural of sirr ‘a secret’ or isrārahum ‘their keeping of things secret’ as the verbal noun.

hype_questions: What happens when people disobey Allah's revelation?
How do idolaters respond to the Prophet's message?
What is the consequence of cooperating with those who oppose the Prophet?
propositions: They said they would obey in some matters, but Allah knows their secrets.
The leading of them astray is because they opposed what God revealed.
God exposed their secret cooperation against the Prophet and his struggle.

source_text:
Verse: Then how ˹horrible˺ will it be when the angels take their souls, beating their faces and backs!

Tafsir: Then how will it be their predicament when the angels take them away beating yadribūna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the angels their faces and their backs? with hooked iron rods.

hype_questions: What will be the state of those who are taken away by angels?
How will the angels treat the souls of the deceased?
What is the nature of the punishment in the hereafter?
propositions: The angels will take the souls of the deceased.
The angels will beat the faces and backs of the deceased with hooked iron rods.

source_text:
Verse: This is because they follow whatever displeases Allah and hate whatever pleases Him, so He has rendered their deeds void.

Tafsir: That taking of them away in the state mentioned is because they followed what angers God and because they were averse to what pleases Him that is to say they were averse to doing what pleases Him. Therefore He has made their works fail.

hype_questions: What happens when one follows the will of God?
How does one's actions change when they are averse to pleasing God?
What is the consequence of following what angers God?
propositions: They followed whatever displeases Allah.
They hated whatever pleases Him.
He has rendered their deeds void because they were averse to doing what pleases Him.

source_text:
Verse: Or do those with sickness in their hearts think that Allah will not ˹be able to˺ expose their malice?

Tafsir: Or did those in whose hearts is a sickness suppose that God would not expose their rancour? that He would not bring to light their spite against the Prophet s and the believers.

hype_questions: Can Allah expose the malice in someone's heart?
Will God bring to light the spite against the Prophet and believers?
Is it possible for Allah to see into the hearts of people?
propositions: Those with sickness in their hearts think that Allah will not expose their malice.
God would not expose their rancour.
He would not bring to light their spite against the Prophet and believers.

source_text:
Verse: Had We willed, We could have truly shown them to you ˹O Prophet˺, and you would have certainly recognized them by their appearance. But you will surely recognize them by their tone of speech. And Allah ˹fully˺ knows your doings ˹O people˺.

Tafsir: And if We will We could show them to you We could have pointed them out to you the lām is repeated in the following fa-la-‘araftahum then you would recognise them by their mark. And you will certainly recognise them wa-la-ta‘rifannahum the wāw is for an omitted oath and what follows it fī lahni’l-qawl is its response by their tone of speech that is to say by the meaning thereof when they speak in your presence alluding as they do to what amounts to a scathing attack upon the Muslims; and God knows your deeds.

hype_questions: Can humans truly recognize others by their appearance?
How do people respond to the Prophet's presence?
Does Allah have complete knowledge of human actions?
propositions: Had We willed, We could have shown them to you.
You would have recognized them by their tone of speech.
Allah knows your doings.

source_text:
Verse: We will certainly test you ˹believers˺ until We prove those of you who ˹truly˺ struggle ˹in Allah’s cause˺ and remain steadfast, and reveal how you conduct yourselves.

Tafsir: And We will assuredly try you We will assuredly test you by way of commanding you to participate in the struggle and in other ways until We know with knowledge outwardly manifested those of you who struggle for God’s cause and those who are steadfast in adhering to the struggle and in other ways and We will appraise We will reveal your record in terms of whether you acted with obedience or disobedience in what concerns the struggle all three verbs may be read with the third person singular yā’ or with the first person plural nūn.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate test for believers?
How will Allah evaluate their actions in the struggle?
What does it mean to be steadfast in adhering to God's cause?
propositions: We will certainly test you until We prove those of you who truly struggle in Allah’s cause and remain steadfast.

We will assuredly try you by way of commanding you to participate in the struggle and in other ways until We know with knowledge outwardly manifested those of you who struggle for God’s cause and those who are steadfast in adhering to the struggle and in other ways.
We will reveal your record in terms of whether you acted with obedience or disobedience in what concerns the struggle.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who disbelieve, hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, and defy the Messenger after ˹true˺ guidance has become clear to them; they will not harm Allah in the least, but He will render their deeds void.

Tafsir: Indeed those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God the path of truth and defy the Messenger opposing him after the guidance this is the meaning of ‘the way of God’ has become clear to them they will not hurt God in any way and He will make their works fail He will invalidate them good works such as voluntary alms and the like and so they will not find any reward for it in the Hereafter — this was revealed either regarding those Meccan participants at the battle of Badr who provided food for the needy or regarding the Jewish tribes of Qurayza and al-Nadīr.

hype_questions: What happens when someone disbelieves and hinders others from following the right path?
Can defying the Messenger lead to harm for Allah?
How will Allah respond to those who provide no reward for their good deeds?
propositions: Those who disbelieve hinder others from the Way of Allah.
Defying the Messenger is opposing God's guidance after it has become clear.
God will render their deeds void and invalidate their good works without providing any reward in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not let your deeds be in vain.

Tafsir: O you who believe! Obey God and obey the Messenger and do not render your own works void by engaging in acts of disobedience for example.

hype_questions: What are some ways to ensure my actions align with God's will?
How can I avoid rendering my own works void through disobedient behavior?
What is the importance of obeying both Allah and the Messenger?
propositions: Believers must obey Allah.
Believers must obey the Messenger.
Engaging in acts of disobedience can render one's actions void.

source_text:
Verse: Surely those who disbelieve, hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, and then die as disbelievers; Allah will never forgive them.

Tafsir: Indeed those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God His path namely guidance and then die as disbelievers God will never forgive them — this was revealed regarding the men of the Well al-qalīb.

hype_questions: Can Allah forgive those who hinder others from His path?
What happens to those who die as disbelievers?
Is guidance a path that can be hindered?
propositions: Those who disbelieve hinder others from the Way of Allah.
Allah will never forgive those who die as disbelievers.
God's path is guidance.

source_text:
Verse: So do not falter or cry for peace, for you will have the upper hand and Allah is with you. And He will never let your deeds go to waste.

Tafsir: So do not falter do not be weak and do not call for peace read salm or silm that is to say a truce with the disbelievers should you encounter them when you have the upper hand al-a‘lawna the third letter of the triliteral root wāw has been omitted when you are the victors the vanquishers and God is with you helping and assisting and He will not stint you diminish you in the reward for your works that is to say of the reward for them.

hype_questions: What happens when you have the upper hand in a battle?
How does Allah assist and help believers in times of need?
What is the reward for doing good deeds?
propositions: Do not falter or cry for peace.
When encountering disbelievers, call for a truce if you have the upper hand.
God is with those who are victorious and will assist them in their works.

source_text:
Verse: This worldly life is no more than play and amusement. But if you are faithful and mindful ˹of Allah˺, He will grant you your ˹full˺ reward, and will not ask you ˹to donate all˺ your wealth.

Tafsir: The life of this world that is to say preoccupation solely with it is merely play and diversion; but if you believe and are wary of God both of which pertain to the goal of the Hereafter He will give you your rewards and will not ask you your wealth in return all of it rather only the alms that are required from it.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reward for those who are faithful and mindful of Allah?
Can one's faith and mindfulness guarantee a better life in the Hereafter?
How does one's wealth relate to their spiritual rewards?
propositions: This worldly life is play and amusement.
Faithful and mindful individuals will receive their full reward from Allah.
Allah will not ask for all of one's wealth, only the required alms.

source_text:
Verse: If He were to do so and pressure you, you would withhold and He would bring out your resentment.

Tafsir: If He were to ask you for it and press you demand it persistently you would be niggardly and this niggardliness would expose your rancour towards the religion of Islam.

hype_questions: What happens if God asks for something and pressures me to give it?
How would I react if God demands something from me persistently?
Can withholding something from God lead to resentment towards Islam?
propositions: If God were to ask you for something, you would withhold it.
Withholding something from God due to pressure would expose your rancour towards the religion of Islam.
You would be niggardly if you persistently refuse to give in to God's demand.

source_text:
Verse: Here you are, being invited to donate ˹a little˺ in the cause of Allah. Still some of you withhold. And whoever does so, it is only to their own loss. For Allah is the Self-Sufficient, whereas you stand in need ˹of Him˺. If you ˹still˺ turn away, He will replace you with another people. And they will not be like you.

Tafsir: Lo! there you are O those who are being called to expend in the way of God that which has been prescribed for you; yet among you there are those who are niggardly; and whoever is niggardly is niggardly only to his own soul one may say bakhila ‘alayhi or bakhila ‘anhu to mean ‘he was niggardly to someone’. For God is the Independent One without need of your expending; while you are the needy of Him. And if you turn away from obedience to Him He will replace you with another people that is to say He will bring them in your place and they will not be the likes of you in turning away from obedience to Him but they will be obedient to Him Mighty and Majestic is He.

hype_questions: What happens if I don't donate to the cause of Allah?
Will Allah replace me with another people if I don't obey Him?
How will the new people be different from me?
propositions: Some people are being called to donate to the cause of Allah.
God is the Independent One without need of your expending.
If you turn away from obedience to God, He will replace you with another people.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We have granted you a clear triumph ˹O Prophet˺

Tafsir: Verily We have given you We have ordained for you the conquest fath of Mecca and other places in the future by force as a result of your struggle a clear victory one that is plain and manifest;

hype_questions: What was the nature of the conquest granted to Prophet Muhammad?
How did the Prophet's struggle lead to a clear victory?
What places were conquered by force as a result of the Prophet's efforts?
propositions: We have granted you a clear triumph.
We have ordained for you the conquest of Mecca and other places in the future by force as a result of your struggle.
This is a clear victory that is plain and manifest.

source_text:
Verse: so that Allah may forgive you for your past and future shortcomings, perfect His favour upon you, guide you along the Straight Path,

Tafsir: that God may forgive you by virtue of your struggle what is past of your sin and what is to come of it so that your community might then desire to struggle like you — this verse also constitutes a justification of the concept of the infallibility ‘isma of prophets peace be upon them against sin by way of a definitive rational proof the lām in li-yaghfira ‘that He may forgive’ is for indicating the ultimate reason for the conquest so that the content of this latter statement constitutes an effect and not the cause and that He may perfect by way of the mentioned victory His favour to you and guide you thereby to a straight path upon which He will confirm you — and this straight path is the religion of Islam;

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reason for Allah's forgiveness?
How does the concept of prophetic infallibility relate to sin?
What is the straight path that Allah guides us upon?
propositions: Allah may forgive you by virtue of your struggle with past and future shortcomings.
The ultimate reason for Allah's forgiveness is indicated by the lām in li-yaghfira 'that He may forgive'.
Allah will perfect His favour upon you if you follow the straight path, which is the religion of Islam.

source_text:
Verse: and so that Allah will help you tremendously.

Tafsir: and that God may grant you therein a mighty victory one of glory involving no humiliation.

hype_questions: What does Allah mean by 'help' in the context of spiritual growth?
How can one achieve a 'mighty victory' that involves no humiliation?
What is the significance of glory in Islamic theology?
propositions: Allah will help you tremendously.
God may grant you therein a mighty victory one of glory involving no humiliation.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who sent down serenity upon the hearts of the believers so that they may increase even more in their faith. To Allah ˹alone˺ belong the forces of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: He it is Who sent down the spirit of Peace Divine reassurance into the hearts of the believers that they might add faith to their faith by way of their embracing of the legal stipulations of religion for every time He revealed one of these they would believe in it — including the command to struggle. And to God belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth and so if He wanted to bring victory to His religion by means of others He would have done so. And God is ever Knower of His creatures Wise in His actions in other words He is ever possessed of such attributes;

hype_questions: What is the role of faith in a believer's life?
How does Allah guide His believers through revelation?
Can anyone bring victory to Islam without Allah's will?
propositions: He sent down serenity upon the hearts of believers.
Allah revealed the spirit of Peace Divine reassurance into the hearts of believers.
Believers add faith to their faith by embracing legal stipulations of religion.
God belongs to the hosts of the heavens and the earth.
If God wanted to bring victory to His religion, He would have done so.

source_text:
Verse: So He may admit believing men and women into Gardens under which rivers flow—to stay there forever—and absolve them of their sins. And that is a supreme achievement in the sight of Allah.

Tafsir: so that He may admit li-yudkhila is semantically connected to an omitted clause that is to say amara bi’l-jihād ‘He has enjoined the struggle so that He may admit’ the believing men and believing women into gardens underneath which rivers flow wherein they will abide and that He may absolve them of their misdeeds; for that in God’s sight is a supreme triumph;

hype_questions: What are the rewards of believing men and women in Islam?
How does Allah absolve believers of their sins?
What is considered a supreme achievement in the sight of Allah?
propositions: He has enjoined the struggle so that He may admit believing men and women into Gardens under which rivers flow.
Allah will absolve believers of their misdeeds.
In God’s sight, a supreme triumph is achieved when believers are admitted to Paradise.

source_text:
Verse: Also ˹so that˺ He may punish hypocrite men and women and polytheistic men and women, who harbour evil thoughts of Allah. May ill-fate befall them! Allah is displeased with them. He has condemned them and prepared for them Hell. What an evil destination!

Tafsir: and so that He may chastise the hypocrites men and women and the idolaters men and women and those who make evil assumptions about God read al-saw’ or al-sū’ ‘evil’ in all three places; they assumed that He will not assist Muhammad (s) and the believers. For them will be an evil turn of fortune by way of abasement and chastisement; and God is wroth with them and He has cursed them He has banished them far from His mercy and has prepared for them Hell — and it is an evil destination! an evil place to return to.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of harbouring evil thoughts about Allah?
How will God respond to those who make false assumptions about Him?
What awaits those who are condemned by God?
propositions: Allah chastises hypocrites, polytheists, and those with evil thoughts.
God is displeased with those who harbour evil thoughts of Allah.
Those who make evil assumptions about God will face an evil turn of fortune.

source_text:
Verse: To Allah ˹alone˺ belong the forces of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And to God belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth; and God is ever Mighty in His kingdom Wise in His actions in other words He is ever possessed of such attributes.

hype_questions: What attributes does God possess?
How is God's kingdom described?
What does it mean for God to be wise?

source_text:
Verse: Surely those who pledge allegiance to you ˹O Prophet˺ are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. Allah’s Hand is over theirs. Whoever breaks their pledge, it will only be to their own loss. And whoever fulfils their pledge to Allah, He will grant them a great reward.

Tafsir: Truly those who pledge allegiance to you the ‘Pledge of Beatitude’ bay‘at al-ridwān given at al-Hudaybiyya in fact pledge allegiance to God — this statement is akin to Whoever obeys the Messenger verily obeys God Q. 480. The Hand of God is above their hands the hands with which they pledged allegiance to the Prophet in other words God exalted be He has observed their pledge of allegiance and will requite them in accordance with their adherence to it. So whoever reneges whoever breaches the pledge reneges — that is the evil consequences of his breach will eventually be — against his own soul; and whoever fulfils the covenant which he has made with God He will give him fa-sa-yu’tīhi; or read fa-sa-nu’tīhi ‘We will give him’ a great reward.

hype_questions: What happens when someone breaks their pledge?

source_text:
Verse: The nomadic Arabs, who stayed behind, will say to you ˹O Prophet˺, “We were preoccupied with our wealth and families, so ask for forgiveness for us.” They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, “Who then can stand between you and Allah in any way, if He intends harm or benefit for you? In fact, Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: Those of the Bedouins who were left behind around Medina — that is to say those whom God made to stay behind and not to accompany you when you had asked them to set out with you for Mecca fearing that Quraysh would attack you upon your return in the year of al-Hudaybiyya — will say to you ‘Our possessions and our families kept us occupied preventing us from going forth with you. So ask forgiveness for us!’ of God for our failure to go forth with you. God exalted be He exposes their mendacity by saying They say with their tongues that is to say in asking forgiveness and in the preceding statement of theirs what is not in their hearts and so they are lying in the excuse which they give. Say ‘Who can an interrogative meant rhetorically as a negation that is to say ‘none can’ avail you anything against God should He desire to cause you harm read darran or durran or desire to bring you benefit? Nay but God is ever Aware of what you do in other words He is ever possessed of such an attribute.

hype_questions: Can anyone stand between you and Allah if He intends harm or benefit?

Their possessions and families kept them occupied, preventing them from going forth with you.
None can stand between you and Allah if He intends harm or benefit.
God is ever Aware of what you do.
They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts.

source_text:

Verse: Those who stayed behind will say, when you ˹believers˺ set out to take the spoils of war, “Let us accompany you.” They wish to change Allah’s promise. The truth is: they can hardly comprehend.

Tafsir: Those mentioned who were left behind will say when you set forth after spoils namely the spoils of Khaybar in order to capture them ‘Let us follow you’ that we might also take a share of it. They desire thereby to change the words of God kalāma’Llāhi a variant reading has kalima’Llāhi in other words His promising of the spoils of Khaybar exclusively for those who were at al-Hudaybiyya. Say ‘You shall never follow us! Thus has God said beforehand’ that is prior to our return. Then they will say ‘Nay but you are envious of us’ lest we might acquire a share of the spoils and therefore you say this that you say. Nay but they never understood anything of religion all except a few of them.

source_text:
Verse: Say to nomadic Arabs, who stayed behind, “You will be called ˹to fight˺ against a people of great might, who you will fight unless they submit. If you then obey, Allah will grant you a fine reward. But if you turn away as you did before, He will inflict upon you a painful punishment.”

Tafsir: Say to those of the Bedouins mentioned who were left behind to test them ‘You shall be called against a people possessed of great might — these are said to have been the tribe of Banū Hanīfa the inhabitants of the region of al-Yamāma; but it is also said that these were the Persians and the Byzantines — you shall fight them tuqātilūnahum is a circumstancial qualifier referring to an implied future situation which constitutes that to which the ‘call’ will be made; or they will submit so that you will not have to fight. So if you obey the command to fight them God will give you a good reward; but if you turn away like you turned away before He will chastise you with a painful chastisement’.

Tafsir: And it is He Who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca at al-Hudaybiyya after He had made you victors over them for eighty of them surrounded your camp in order to inflict losses upon you but they were captured and taken to the Prophet s who pardoned them and set them free and this resulted in the truce.
