source_text:
Verse: They are the ones who persisted in disbelief and hindered you from the Sacred Mosque, preventing the sacrificial animals from reaching their destination. Had those ˹unknown˺ believers stood apart, We would have certainly inflicted a painful punishment on the disbelievers.

Tafsir: They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque that is barred you from reaching it and prevented the offering wa’l-hadya is a supplement to the suffixed pronoun –kum ‘you’ of saddūkum ‘they barred you’ which was detained ma‘kūfan is a circumstantial qualifier from reaching its destination that is from the place at which it is customarily sacrificed namely the Sanctuary itself an yablugha mahillahu is an inclusive substitution. And were it not for some of the believing men and believing women being present at Mecca alongside the disbelievers whom you did not know to be believers — lest you should trample them that is to say lest you should slay them together with the disbelievers had you been given permission to embark on the conquest an tata’ūhum is an inclusive substitution for –hum ‘them’ of lam ta‘lamūhum ‘whom you did not know’ and thus incur sin on account of them without your knowing it … the third person pronouns in both groups of people predominantly imply males; the response to lawlā ‘were it not’ has been omitted through ellipsis being something along the lines of la-udhina lakum fī’l-fathi ‘you would have been permitted to embark on the conquest’ but permission for this was not given at the time so that God may admit into His mercy whom He will such as those believers mentioned. Had they been clearly separated had they the believers been distinguishable from the disbelievers We would have surely chastised the disbelievers among them of the people of Mecca immediately thereat by permitting you to go ahead with the conquest thereof with a painful chastisement.

hype_questions: Would the believers have been punished if they had been clearly separated from the disbelievers?
What would have happened to the disbelievers if the believers had been distinguishable from them?
Why was permission for conquest not given at that time?
propositions: They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque.
Had those believers stood apart, We would have certainly inflicted a painful punishment on the disbelievers.

Were it not for some of the believing men and believing women being present at Mecca alongside the disbelievers whom you did not know to be believers — lest you should trample them that is to say lest you should slay them together with the disbelievers had you been given permission to embark on the conquest.

Had they been clearly separated had they the believers been distinguishable from the disbelievers We would have surely chastised the disbelievers among them of the people of Mecca immediately thereat by permitting you to go ahead with the conquest thereof with a painful chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember˺ when the disbelievers had filled their hearts with pride—the pride of ˹pre-Islamic˺ ignorance for they were better entitled and more worthy of it. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

Tafsir: When those who disbelieve alladhīna kafarū is the subject of the following verb ja‘ala nourished idh ja‘ala is semantically connected to ‘adhdhabnā in their hearts zealotry al-hamiyya means ‘disdain of something’ the zealotry of pagandom hamiyyata’l-jāhiliyyati substitutes for al-hamiyyata ‘zealotry’ namely their barring of the Prophet and his Companions from visiting the Sacred Mosque but then God sent down His spirit of Peace upon His Messenger and the believers and so they the disbelievers made a truce with them on the condition that they the believers would be allowed to return the following year and such zealotry would not overcome them the believers as it did the disbelievers then until they would come to fight them later and He made them the believers abide by the word of God-fearing kalimata’l-taqwā ‘there is no god except God and Muhammad is His Messenger’ it kalima ‘word’ is annexed to al-taqwā because it is the cause of it for they were worthier of it of the word than the disbelievers and deserving of it wa-ahlahā is an explanatory supplement. And God is ever Knower of all things that is to say He is ever possessed of such an attribute and among the things He knows is that they are worthy of it.

hype_questions: What is the nature of pride and its effects on individuals?

God has perfect knowledge of all things.
God sent down His spirit of peace upon His Messenger and the believers.
The believers made a truce with the disbelievers on the condition that they would be allowed to return the following year.
The word of God-fearing is the cause of taqwā, which means there is no god except God and Muhammad is His Messenger.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Allah will fulfil His Messenger’s vision in all truth: Allah willing, you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, in security—˹some with˺ heads shaved and ˹others with˺ hair shortened—without fear.

Tafsir: Verily God has fulfilled the vision for His Messenger in all truth The Messenger of God s saw in his sleep in the year of al-Hudaybiyya before his departure from Medina that he would enter Mecca together with his Companions safely whereafter they would shave completely or shorten their hair. He informed his Companions of this and they rejoiced. But when they set off with him from Medina and the disbelievers impeded them at al-Hudaybiyya such that they had to retreat which was distressing for them for some of the hypocrites began to have doubts about the Prophet’s sincerity this verse was revealed bi’l-haqqi ‘in all truth’ is semantically connected to sadaqa ‘fulfilled’ or it is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-ru’yā ‘the vision’ and what comes after it is the explanation thereof ‘You will assuredly enter the Sacred Mosque God willing — this is said to secure blessings — in safety to shave your heads that is all the hair or to shorten it to shorten some of the hair both muhalliqīna and muqassirīna are implied circumstantial qualifiers without any fear’ ever. So He knew there to be in the truce what you did not know in the way of reconciliation between the believers and the Meccans and assigned you before that entry a near victory namely the conquest of Khaybar — the vision was fulfilled in the following year.

hype_questions: Will I be able to enter the Sacred Mosque safely?
What is the significance of shaving or shortening hair in this context?

propositions: Allah will fulfil His Messenger’s vision in all truth.
The Messenger of God saw in his sleep that he would enter Mecca together with his Companions safely.
He informed his Companions of this and they rejoiced.
But when they set off with him from Medina and the disbelievers impeded them at al-Hudaybiyya such that they had to retreat which was distressing for them.
For some of the hypocrites began to have doubts about the Prophet’s sincerity.
This verse was revealed bi’l-haqqi ‘in all truth’ is semantically connected to sadaqa ‘fulfilled’ or it is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-ru’yā ‘the vision’

You will assuredly enter the Sacred Mosque God willing — this is said to secure blessings — in safety to shave your heads that is all the hair or to shorten it to shorten some of the hair both muhalliqīna and muqassirīna are implied circumstantial qualifiers without any fear’ ever.

He knew there to be in the truce what you did not know in the way of reconciliation between the believers and the Meccans and assigned you before that entry a near victory namely the conquest of Khaybar — the vision was fulfilled in the following year.

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. And those with him are firm with the disbelievers To those of them who believe and do good, Allah has promised forgiveness and a great reward.

Tafsir: Muhammad the subject is the Messenger of God its predicate and those who are with him that is his Companions from among the believers wa’lladhīna ma‘ahu another subject the predicate of which is the following ashiddā’u are hard tough against the disbelievers showing them no mercy but merciful among themselves ruhamā’u is a second predicate of wa’lladhīna ma‘ahu ‘and those who are with him’ that is to say they show mutual sympathy and affection for one another much like a father and a son. You see you observe them bowing prostrating in worship both rukka‘an and sujjadan are circumstantial qualifiers. They seek yabtaghūna is the beginning of a new sentence bounty from God and beatitude. Their mark sīmāhum is a subject their distinguishing feature is on their faces fī wujūhihim is its predicate this is a light and a radiance by which in the Hereafter they will be recognised as having been those who used to prostrate in this world from the effect of prostration min athari’l-sujūdi is semantically connected to the same thing to which the predicate is semantically connected that is to say kā’inatan ‘this being from the effect of prostration’; syntactically it is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of kā’inatan which is also the subject of the predicate sc. wujūhihim ‘their faces’. That mentioned description is their description mathaluhum is the subject in the Torah fī’l-tawrāti is the predicate thereof; and their description in the Gospel wa-mathaluhum fī’l-injīli is a subject the predicate of which is what follows is as a seed that sends forth its shoot read shat’ahu or shata’ahu and strengthens it read āzarahu or azarahu nourishing it and assisting it and it grows stout and rises firmly becoming strong and upright upon its stalk its roots sūq is the plural of sāq delighting the sowers that is to say those who planted it on account of its fairness. The Companions may God be pleased with them are being described in this way for at the outset they were weak and very few in number; but then their number grew and they acquired strength in the most wholesome way so that He may enrage the disbelievers by them li-yaghīza bihimu’l-kuffāra is semantically connected to an omitted clause which is suggested by what preceded that is to say ‘they are likened to this so that God may enrage the disbelievers’. God has promised those of them who believe and perform righteous deeds the Companions minhum ‘of them’ min ‘of’ is an indicator of the genus and not partitive for they are all possessed of the mentioned attributes forgiveness and a great reward — Paradise. Both of these rewards will also be given to those who will come after them as is stated in other verses.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Companions of Muhammad?
How do the Companions show mutual sympathy and affection for one another?
What rewards will be given to those who believe and perform righteous deeds?
propositions: Muhammad is the Messenger of God.
Those with him are firm against the disbelievers but merciful among themselves.
God has promised forgiveness and a great reward to those who believe and do good.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Do not proceed ˹in any matter˺ before ˹a decree from˺ Allah and His Messenger. And fear Allah. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Tafsir: O you who believe do not venture ahead of tuqaddimū derives from qaddama with the sense of the 5th form taqaddama that is to say do not come forward with any unwarranted saying or deed ahead of God and His Messenger the one communicating the Message from Him that is to say without their permission and fear God. Surely God is Hearer of your sayings Knower of your deeds this was revealed regarding the dispute between Abū Bakr and ‘Umar may God be pleased with them both in the presence of the Prophet s over the appointment of al-Aqra‘ b. Hābis or al-Qa‘qā‘ b. Ma‘bad as commander of his tribe.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him as you do to one another, or your deeds will become void while you are unaware.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding those who raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet s O you who believe do not raise your voices — when you want to speak — above the voice of the Prophet when he is speaking and do not shout words at him when you wish to confide in him as you shout to one another but speak lower than that out of reverence for him lest your works should be invalidated without your being aware that is to say for fear of this happening as a result of the raising of voices and the shouting mentioned.

hype_questions: What happens if you raise your voice above the Prophet's?
Why is it important to speak lower than usual when speaking to the Prophet?
How can speaking loudly affect one's deeds?
propositions: Believers should not raise their voices above the voice of the Prophet.
When speaking to the Prophet, believers should speak lower than they would to others out of reverence for him.
If believers shout at the Prophet, their works may become void without them being aware.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of Allah’s Messenger are the ones whose hearts Allah has refined for righteousness. They will have forgiveness and a great reward.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding those who used to lower their voices in the presence of the Prophet s such as Abū Bakr ‘Umar and others may God be pleased with all of them Truly those who lower their voices in the presence of God’s Messenger — they are the ones whose hearts God has tested for God-fearing that is to say He has tested them so that this fear of God may manifest itself in them. For them will be forgiveness and a great reward Paradise.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who lower their voices in the presence of Allah’s Messenger?
How does Allah refine the hearts of those who show reverence to His Messenger?
What is the ultimate goal of God testing the hearts of believers?
propositions: Those who lower their voices in the presence of Allah’s Messenger have their hearts refined for righteousness.
Allah has tested those whose hearts are God-fearing, so that this fear may manifest itself in them.
Forgiveness and a great reward await those who lower their voices in the presence of God’s Messenger.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, most of those who call out to you ˹O Prophet˺ from outside ˹your˺ private quarters have no understanding ˹of manners˺.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding a group of people who came to see the Prophet s during the midday resting period while he was in his house and called out to him Truly those who call you from behind the apartments the private chambers of his womenfolk hujurāt is the plural of hujra which is an area of ground on which stones are laid yuhjaru ‘alayhi to form a wall or the like and it happened that each one of them called out in that rough and crude Bedouin manner from behind one of the apartments as they did not know in which apartment he was most of them do not understand given the way in which they acted your exalted status and the reverence that befits it.

hype_questions: What is the significance of hujra in Islamic context?
How did the Prophet handle the rough and crude calls from his womenfolk's apartments?
What does the verse imply about the understanding of manners among those who call out to the Prophet?
propositions: Most people who call out to the Prophet from outside his private quarters do not understand the concept of manners.
The hujra refers to an area of ground on which stones are laid to form a wall or the like.
Those who call out to the Prophet from behind his womenfolk's apartments do so in a rough and crude Bedouin manner without showing reverence for his exalted status.

source_text:
Verse: Had they been patient until you could come out to them, it would have certainly been better for them. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: And had they been patient annahum ‘they’ has independent status on account of inceptiveness; alternatively it is said to govern an implied verb such as thabata ‘had their patience been maintained’ until you came out to them it would have been better for them; and God is Forgiving Merciful to those of them who repent.

hype_questions: What would have happened if the patient believers had been rewarded?
How does Allah's mercy apply to those who repent?
Can patience lead to a better outcome for believers?
propositions: Had they been patient until you came out to them, it would have certainly been better for them.
Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: O believers, if an evildoer brings you any news, verify ˹it˺ so you do not harm people unknowingly, becoming regretful for what you have done.

Tafsir: The following was revealed regarding al-Walīd b. ‘Uqba whom the Prophet had sent to the Banū al-Mustaliq in order to ascertain their loyalty to Islam. He already feared them on account of an old feud between him and them from the time of pagandom before Islam and so upon seeing them come out to him he returned and claimed that they had refused to give the voluntary alms and intended to kill him. And just as the Prophet s was making plans to raid them they came to him to disavow what he al-Walīd had said about them O you who believe if a reprobate should come to you with some tiding some piece of information verify it ascertain his truthfulness from his mendacity fa-tabayyanū a variant reading has fa-tathabbatū from al-thabāt ‘to ascertain’ lest you injure a folk an tusībū qawman an object denoting reason that is to say for fear of this happening out of ignorance bi-jahālatin is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb that is to say while you are ignorant; and then become remorseful of what you have perpetrated erroneously against that folk. After they had returned to their homelands the Prophet s sent Khālid b. al-Walīd to them who observed only obedience and goodness in them and later informed the Prophet of this.

hype_questions: What should I do if someone brings me false news?
How can I avoid harming people unknowingly?
What is the importance of verifying information before acting on it?
propositions: If an evildoer brings you any news, verify it so you do not harm people unknowingly.
The Prophet s sent al-Walīd b. ‘Uqba to the Banū al-Mustaliq to ascertain their loyalty to Islam.
You should verify the truthfulness of someone's words before believing them.
Lest you injure a folk and become remorseful of what you have perpetrated erroneously against that folk.

source_text:
Verse: And keep in mind that Allah’s Messenger is ˹still˺ in your midst. If he were to yield to you in many matters, you would surely suffer ˹the consequences˺. But Allah has endeared faith to you, making it appealing in your hearts. And He has made disbelief, rebelliousness, and disobedience detestable to you. Those are the ones rightly guided.

Tafsir: And know that the Messenger of God is among you so do not speak falsehood for God will inform him of the real state of affairs. If he were to obey you in many matters which you communicate contrary to reality so that the necessary evil consequences ensue you would surely be in trouble you would earn in addition to that sin the sin for the consequences that ensue from your error. But God has endeared faith to you adorning your hearts with it and He has made odious to you disbelief and immorality and disobedience an instance of suppletion with respect to import as opposed to lexical form; for the one to whom ‘faith has been endeared …’ and so forth will naturally be dissimilar in character to the mentioned reprobate. Those there is here a shift from the second to the third person address — they are the right-minded the ones firmly established upon the way of their religion;

hype_questions: What happens if I disobey Allah's Messenger?
How does Allah make faith appealing to us?
What are the consequences of speaking falsehood?
propositions: Allah’s Messenger is in your midst.
If he were to yield to you, you would suffer consequences.
God has endeared faith to you, making it appealing in your hearts.
Disbelief, rebelliousness, and disobedience are detestable to you.
Those who are rightly guided are the ones firmly established upon the way of their religion.

source_text:
Verse: ˹This is˺ a bounty and a blessing from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: that is a favour from God fadlan is a verbal noun in the accusative because of the implied verbal action that is afdala ‘He gives a favour’ and a grace from Him and God is Knower of them Wise in His bestowal of graces on them.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's blessings?
How does Allah bestow favors upon His servants?
What is the significance of God's grace in Islamic theology?
propositions: This is a bounty and a blessing from Allah.
Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
God gives a favour (fadlan) to His servants.
A grace from Him is bestowed upon them.

source_text:
Verse: And if two groups of believers fight each other, then make peace between them. But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight against the transgressing group until they ˹are willing to˺ submit to the rule of Allah. If they do so, then make peace between both ˹groups˺ in all fairness and act justly. Surely Allah loves those who uphold justice.

Tafsir: And if two parties of believers in tā’ifatāni mina’l-mu’minīna... to the end of the verse was revealed regarding a particular incident where the Prophet s was riding a donkey and happened to pass by Ibn Ubayy; the donkey urinated and so Ibn Ubayy held his nose whereupon ‘Abd Allāh Ibn Rawāhā said ‘By God the smell of the donkey’s urine is sweeter-smelling than your musk. Fighting then ensued between the two clans with fists sandals and palm branches being thrown about fall to fighting iqtatalū the plural is used on account of the plural import for each party is made up of several individuals; a variant reading has the dual form iqtatalatā make peace between them baynahumā the dual here takes into account the actual dual form of tā’ifatān ‘two parties’. And if one of them aggresses against the other fight the one which aggresses until it returns to God’s ordinance to the truth. Then if it returns reconcile them fairly and act justly. Surely God loves the just.

hype_questions: What happens when two groups of believers fight each other?
How should one respond if they are being aggressed against by another group?
What is the ultimate goal of fighting in the context of Islamic teachings?
propositions: If two groups of believers fight each other, make peace between them.
If one group transgresses against another, fight against the transgressing group until they submit to Allah's rule.
If a group returns to God's ordinance after fighting, reconcile with them fairly and act justly.

source_text:
Verse: The believers are but one brotherhood, so make peace between your brothers. And be mindful of Allah so you may be shown mercy.

Tafsir: The believers are indeed brothers in religion. Therefore always make peace between your brethren when they fall into dispute with one another a variant reading for the dual form akhawaykum ‘your two brethren’ has ikhwatakum ‘your brothers’ and fear God so that perhaps you might receive mercy.

hype_questions: What is the importance of making peace between brothers in Islam?
How can Muslims show mercy to one another?
What does it mean to be a brother in religion?
propositions: The believers are but one brotherhood.
Make peace between your brothers.
Be mindful of Allah so you may be shown mercy.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Do not let some ˹men˺ ridicule others, they may be better than them, nor let ˹some˺ women ridicule other women, they may be better than them. Do not defame one another, nor call each other by offensive nicknames. How evil it is to act rebelliously after having faith! And whoever does not repent, it is they who are the ˹true˺ wrongdoers.

Tafsir: O you who believe do not let any people that is any men among you deride yā ayyuhā’lladhīna āmanū lā yaskhar … to the end of the verse was revealed regarding the Banū Tamīm delegation when they derided the poor among the Muslims like ‘Ammār b. Yāsir and Suhayb al-Rūmī; al-sukhriya means ‘scorn’ and ‘disdain’ another people who may be better than they are in God’s sight; nor let any women from among you deride other women who may be better than they are. And do not defame one another do not cast aspersions on others and hence have aspersions cast on you that is let none among you denigrate another; nor insult one another by nicknames do not call another by a nickname which he detests such as ‘O degenerate one!’ or ‘O disbeliever!’. Evil is the name mentioned out of mockery derision and mutual reviling of immorality after faith! al-fusūqu ba‘da’l-īmāni substitutes for al-ismu ‘the name’ to indicate that it such naming of others is ‘immorality’ as it is an action which is usually repeated. And whoever does not repent of such immorality those — they are the evildoers.

hype_questions: What happens when believers ridicule each other?
How can believers avoid defaming one another?
What is the consequence of not repenting from immoral behavior?
propositions: Believers should not let men ridicule others, even if they may be better than them.
Women should not deride other women, even if they may be better than them.
Believers should not defame one another or call each other by offensive nicknames.
Acting rebelliously after having faith is evil.
Those who do not repent from immoral behavior are the true wrongdoers.

source_text:
Verse: O  believers! Avoid many suspicions, ˹for˺ indeed, some suspicions are sinful. And do not spy, nor backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of their dead brother? You would despise that! And fear Allah. Surely Allah is ˹the˺ Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: O you who believe shun much suspicion. Indeed some suspicions are sins that is to say it causes one to fall into sin. This suspicion may have many forms such as thinking ill of the good folk from among the believers — and such good folk are many — in contrast to the immoral individuals among them in whose case there is no sin so long as it the suspicion is in accordance with their outward behaviour. And do not spy tajassasū one of the two tā’ letters of tatajassasū has been omitted do not pursue the imperfections and faults of Muslims by searching them out; nor backbite one another do not speak of him by mentioning something which he is averse to having mentioned of himself even if it be true. Would any of you love to eat the flesh of his brother dead? read maytan or mayyitan. That is to say it would not be right for him to do so. You would abhor it. Thus to backbite him in life would be like eating his flesh when he is dead. This latter form of behaviour has been suggested to you and you were averse to it so be averse to the former too. And fear God that is His punishment for backbiting by repenting of it; assuredly God is Relenting accepting of the penitence of those who repent Merciful to them.

hype_questions: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of their dead brother?
What is the punishment for backbiting in Islam?
How can one repent from backbiting?
propositions: Believers should avoid many suspicions.
Some suspicions are sinful and can lead to falling into sin.
It is not permissible to spy on or pursue the imperfections of Muslims.
Backbiting, which involves speaking ill of someone behind their back, is forbidden in Islam.
To backbite someone is like eating their flesh when they are dead; it is abhorrent and should be avoided.
God is Relenting and accepting of the penitence of those who repent for backbiting.

source_text:
Verse: O humanity! Indeed, We created you from a male and a female, and made you into peoples and tribes so that you may ˹get to˺ know one another. Surely the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous among you. Allah is truly All-Knowing, All-Aware.

Tafsir: O mankind! We have indeed created you from a male and a female from Adam and Eve and made you nations shu‘ūb is the plural of sha‘b which is the broadest category of lineage and tribes qabā’il which are smaller than nations and are followed by ‘amā’ir ‘tribal districts’ then butūn ‘tribal sub-districts’ then afkhādh ‘sub-tribes’ and finally fasā’il ‘clans’; for example Khuzayma is the sha‘b while Kināna is the qabīla Quraysh is the ‘imāra Qusayy is the batn Hāshim is the fakhdh and ‘Abbās is the fasīla that you may come to know one another ta‘ārafū one of the two tā’ letters of tata‘ārafū has been omitted that you may acquire knowledge of the customs of one another and not to boast to one another of whose is the more noble lineage for pride lies only in the extent to which you have fear of God. Truly the noblest of you in the sight of God is the most God-fearing among you. Truly God is Knower of you Aware of your inner thoughts.

hype_questions: What is the true measure of nobility?
How can we acquire knowledge of one another's customs?
What is the source of pride in Islam?
propositions: Humans were created from a male and a female.
Nations and tribes were formed to promote mutual understanding.
The most noble among you is the most righteous and God-fearing.
Pride lies only in fearing God.
God is aware of human inner thoughts.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Some of˺ the nomadic Arabs say, “We believe.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “You have not believed. But say, ‘We have submitted,’ for faith has not yet entered your hearts. But if you obey Allah and His Messenger ˹wholeheartedly˺, He will not discount anything from ˹the reward of˺ your deeds. Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Tafsir: The Bedouins — a group of men from among the Banū Asad — say ‘We believe’ we affirm the truth in our hearts. Say to them ‘You do not believe; but rather say “We have submitted” we are outwardly compliant; for faith has not yet entered into your hearts’ hitherto; however it is expected of you. Yet if you obey God and His Messenger by embracing faith and in other ways He will not diminish for you read ya’litkum or yalitkum by making the hamza an alif anything of your deeds that is of the reward for them. God is indeed Forgiving to believers Merciful to them.

hype_questions: What does it mean to truly believe in Islam?
How can I show my submission to Allah and His Messenger?
What happens if I obey Allah and His Messenger?
propositions: The nomadic Arabs claim to have believed, but their faith has not yet entered their hearts.
Faith is not just about claiming belief, but also about submitting to Allah's will.
If the Arabs obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not discount anything from their deeds.
God is truly All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: The ˹true˺ believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger—never doubting—and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. They are the ones true in faith.

Tafsir: The true believers that is those who are true in their affirmation of faith — as He makes explicit in what follows — are only those who believe in God and His Messenger and then have not doubted they have not been uncertain of their faith and who strive with their wealth and their souls for the cause of God hence their striving manifests the sincerity of their faith. It is they who are sincere in their faith not those who say ‘We believe’ and from whom all that has been forthcoming is their submission to the religion.

hype_questions: What are the characteristics of true believers in Islam?
How do true believers demonstrate their faith?
What is the difference between those who claim to believe and those who truly submit?
propositions: The true believers are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger without doubting.
True believers strive with their wealth and lives for the cause of Allah.
Sincerity in faith is demonstrated through striving for the cause of God.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “Do you inform Allah of your faith, when Allah ˹already˺ knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.”

Tafsir: Say to them ‘Do you pretend to inform God about your religion read the doubled 2nd verbal form a-tu‘allimūna ‘do you inform’ in other words are you intimating to Him your religious status when you say ‘We believe’ when God knows all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth and even though God is Knower of all things?’

hype_questions: Does God need to be informed about one's faith?
Can humans claim to represent God in matters of religion?
Is God unaware of human beliefs and actions?
propositions: You do not inform Allah of your faith.
Allah already knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
Allah has perfect knowledge of all things.

source_text:
Verse: They regard their acceptance of Islam as a favour to you. Tell ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Do not regard your Islam as a favour to me. Rather, it is Allah Who has done you a favour by guiding you to the faith, if ˹indeed˺ you are faithful.

Tafsir: They deem it to be a favour to you that they have submitted without the need for any fighting unlike those others who submitted only after being fought. Say ‘Do not deem your submission to be a favour to me islāmakum ‘your submission’ has dependent accusative status because of the omission of the genitive preposition bi-which is also read as implicit before the an in both instances. Rather it is God Who has done you a favour in that He has guided you to faith if you are being sincere when you say ‘We believe’.

hype_questions: Does Islam bring a favour to the Prophet?
What is the difference between those who submitted after being fought and those who submitted without fighting?
How does one demonstrate sincerity in their faith?
propositions: Islam is not a favour to the Prophet.
Submission to Islam requires no fighting.
God guides individuals to faith if they are sincere.

source_text:
Verse: Surely Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and earth. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.”

Tafsir: Truly God knows the Unseen of the heavens and the earth that is He knows all that is hidden in both and God is Seer of what you do’ may be read either as ya‘malūna ‘they do’ or ta‘malūna ‘you do’ nothing of which can be concealed from Him.

hype_questions: Can anything be hidden from Allah?
Is Allah aware of our actions?
What is the nature of Allah's knowledge?
propositions: Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and earth.
Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.

source_text:
Verse: Qãf. By the glorious Quran!

Tafsir: Qāf God knows best what He means by this letter. By the glorious Qur’ān by the noble Qur’ān the disbelievers of Mecca have certainly not believed in Muhammad (s).

hype_questions: Does the Quran hold any significance for believers?
What is the relationship between Muhammad and the people of Mecca?
Can one truly understand the meaning behind a letter in the Quran?
propositions: The Quran is glorious.
God knows best what He means by this letter.
The disbelievers of Mecca have not believed in Muhammad (s).

source_text:
Verse: ˹All will be resurrected,˺ yet the deniers are astonished that a warner has come to them from among themselves ˹warning of resurrection˺. So the disbelievers say, “This is an astonishing thing!

Tafsir: Nay but they consider it odd that there should have come to them a warner from among themselves a messenger who is one of them to threaten them with the punishment of the Fire after resurrection. So the disbelievers say ‘This warning is an odd thing!

hype_questions: What is the significance of a warner coming from among themselves?
How does the concept of resurrection affect one's beliefs?
What is the nature of the punishment mentioned in the warning?
propositions: All will be resurrected.
A warner has come to them from among themselves warning of resurrection.
The disbelievers consider this warning an odd thing.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Will we be returned to life,˺ when we are dead and reduced to dust? Such a return is impossible.”

Tafsir: What! read a-idhā pronouncing both hamzas or not pronouncing the second but inserting an alif between the two in both cases When we are dead and have become dust? shall we return to life? That is a far-fetched return!’ an event that is extremely remote.

hype_questions: Can we be returned to life after death?
Is it possible for us to return to life when our physical bodies have decomposed into dust?
Is the concept of returning to life after death considered far-fetched or extremely remote?
propositions: When we are dead and reduced to dust, such a return is impossible.
What! shall we return to life? That is a far-fetched return!
That is an event that is extremely remote.

source_text:
Verse: We certainly know what the earth consumes of them ˹after their death˺, and with us is a well-preserved Record.

Tafsir: We know what the earth diminishes consumes of them and with Us is a preserving Book namely the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz which contains everything that has been ordained by God.

hype_questions: What happens to the earth after death?
Is there a record of our deeds?
How is our fate determined?
propositions: The earth consumes everything after death.
A well-preserved Record exists with God.
The Preserved Tablet contains everything ordained by God.

source_text:
Verse: In fact, they reject the truth when it has come to them, so they are in a confused state.

Tafsir: Nay but they denied the truth the Qur’ān when it came to them and so they with regard to the Prophet s and the Qur’ān are now in a confounded situation a troubled one. For on one occasion they said that he was ‘A sorcerer!’ cf. Q. 384 and that his statements were ‘Nothing but manifest sorcery!’ cf. Q. 3715 on another ‘A poet!’ cf. Q. 215 and ‘Poetry!’ cf. Q. 3669 and still on another ‘A soothsayer!’ cf. Q. 5229 and that his statements were nothing more than soothsaying cf. Q. 6942.

hype_questions: What happens when people reject the truth?
How do people react to accusations of sorcery?
Can poetry be considered a form of sorcery?
propositions: They rejected the truth when it came to them.
The Prophet s and the Qur’ān are in a confounded situation.
Some people accused the Prophet s of being a sorcerer or a soothsayer.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not then looked at the sky above them: how We built it and adorned it ˹with stars˺, leaving it flawless?

Tafsir: Have they not then looked with their own eyes at the heaven being above them in order to take heed by their own minds of the consequences for them when they deny the Resurrection how We have built it without supports and adorned it with planets and how there are no cracks in it? no fissures blemishing it.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Resurrection?
How was the heaven built without supports?
Why does it have no cracks or fissures?
propositions: We built the heaven without supports.
The heaven has planets on it.
There are no cracks in the heaven.

source_text:
Verse: As for the earth, We spread it out and placed upon it firm mountains, and produced in it every type of pleasant plant—

Tafsir: And the earth wa’l-arda is a supplement to the position of the words ilā l-samā’i ‘at the heaven’ how We have spread it out how We have rolled it across the face of the water and cast in it firm mountains to fix it in place and caused every delightful kind every delightful specimen causing delight by its very beauty to grow in it

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creating mountains on earth?
How does God spread out and roll out the earth?
Why does God cause every delightful kind to grow in it?
propositions: God spread out the earth.
God rolled out the earth across the face of water.
God fixed the earth with firm mountains.
God caused every delightful kind to grow in the earth due to its beauty.

source_text:
Verse: ˹all as˺ an insight and a reminder to every servant who turns ˹to Allah˺.

Tafsir: as an insight tabsiratan is a direct object denoting reason that is to say We did this to give an insight from Us and a reminder for every penitent servant who returns to obedience of Us.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Allah's reminder?
How does Allah guide His servants?
What is the nature of obedience to Allah?
propositions: We did this to give an insight from Us.
This insight is a reminder for every penitent servant who returns to obedience of Us.

source_text:
Verse: And We send down blessed rain from the sky, bringing forth gardens and grains for harvest,

Tafsir: And We send down from the heaven blessed water containing much blessing with which We cause to grow gardens orchards and the grain that is harvested

hype_questions: What are the blessings of Allah in the form of rain?
How do gardens grow with the help of blessed water from heaven?
What is the purpose of harvesting grains?
propositions: Allah sends down blessed rain from the sky.
The rain brings forth gardens and grains for harvest.
Blessed water from heaven causes gardens to grow.
Gardens are orchards that grow with the help of blessed water.
Grains are harvested as a result of the growth caused by blessed water.

source_text:
Verse: and towering palm trees ˹loaded˺ with clustered fruit,

Tafsir: and the date-palms that stand tall bāsiqātin is an implied future circumstantial qualifier with piled spathes one cluster of dates sitting on top of the other

hype_questions: What is a bāsiqātin?
How do date palms grow?
What are the benefits of date palms?
propositions: Date palms stand tall.
The date-palms are loaded with clustered fruit.
Bāsiqātin implies an implied future circumstantial qualifier.

source_text:
Verse: ˹as˺ a provision for ˹Our˺ servants. And with this ˹rain˺ We revive a lifeless land. Similar is the emergence ˹from the graves˺.

Tafsir: as provision for Our servants rizqan li’l-‘ibādi is a direct object denoting reason; and with it We revive a dead land baldatan may be followed equally by the masculine maytan or the feminine adjective maytatan. So like that manner of reviving shall be the rising from the graves so how can you deny it? the interrogative is meant as an affirmative; the meaning then is that they have indeed observed all of these things and are aware of what has been mentioned yet they disbelieve.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Allah's provision?
How does Allah revive a dead land?
Will those who deny the resurrection rise from their graves?
propositions: Allah provides for His servants.
Allah revives a dead land with rain.
Those who deny the resurrection will indeed rise from their graves.

source_text:
Verse: Before them, the people of Noah denied ˹the truth,˺ as did the people of the Water-pit, Thamûd,

Tafsir: The people of Noah denied before them kadhdhabat has a feminine person inflection because of the feminine gender of the import of qawm ‘people’ and so did the dwellers at al-Rass — this was the name of a well around which they dwelt together with their livestock; they worshipped idols and it is said that their prophet was one Hanzala b. Safwān; but some say that he was some other person — and Thamūd the people of Sālih

hype_questions: What was the name of the prophet of Thamūd?
Did the people of al-Rass worship idols?
Who is Hanzala b. Safwān?
propositions: The people of Noah denied the truth.
The dwellers at al-Rass worshipped idols.
Hanzala b. Safwān was a prophet.

source_text:
Verse: ’Ȃd, Pharaoh, the kinfolk of Lot,

Tafsir: and ‘Ād the people of Hūd and Pharaoh the brethren of Lot

hype_questions: What is the name of the tribe mentioned in the Quran as being destroyed by Allah?
Who are the people referred to as the 'brethren of Lot' in the Quran?
What is the name of the prophet who was sent to the people of Hūd?
propositions: ‘Ād were a tribe mentioned in the Quran.
Pharaoh is referred to as the brother of Lot in the Quran.
Hūd was a prophet sent to the people of ‘Ād.

source_text:
Verse: the residents of the Forest, Each rejected ˹their˺ messenger, so My warning was fulfilled.

Tafsir: and the dwellers in the wood a small forest — the people of Shu‘ayb — and the people of Tubba‘ — a king who ruled in Yemen; he had submitted to God and had summoned his people to the same submission to God but they denied him. Each of those mentioned denied the messengers as your tribe Quraysh have and so My threat became due the sending down of chastisement on all of them became incumbent so do not be anguished by Quraysh’s disbelieving in you.

hype_questions: What happens when a group rejects their messenger?
How does the rejection of messengers affect an individual's fate?
Can submission to God guarantee salvation?
propositions: The residents of the Forest rejected their messenger.
The people of Shu‘ayb and Tubba‘ denied their messengers despite being warned by a king who submitted to God.
Quraysh's rejection of Islam will not affect an individual's fate due to submission to God.

source_text:
Verse: Were We incapable of creating ˹them˺ the first time? In fact, they are in doubt about ˹their˺ re-creation.

Tafsir: Were We then wearied by the first creation? that is to say We were not wearied by it and likewise We will not be wearied by restoring it. Nay yet they are in doubt about a new creation which will be at the Resurrection.

hype_questions: Will Allah create new life after death?
Is the first creation tiring for Allah?
Can Allah recreate something that was lost?
propositions: We were not wearied by the first creation.
They are in doubt about a new creation which will be at the Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, ˹it is˺ We ˹Who˺ created humankind and ˹fully˺ know what their souls whisper to them, and We are closer to them than ˹their˺ jugular vein.

Tafsir: And verily We created man and We know wa-na‘lamu is a circumstantial qualifier with an implicit preceding nahnu what mā relates to the verbal action his soul whispers to him what it speaks to him the bi- of bihi ‘him’ is extra or it is required for the intransitive verb to become transitive and take a direct object; the suffixed personal pronoun in bihi ‘him’ refers to man; and We are nearer to him in knowing him than his jugular vein habli’l-warīdi the genitive annexation is explicative; al-warīdān are two principal veins on either side of the neck.

hype_questions: Does God have complete knowledge of human thoughts?
Can humans be closer to God than their physical bodies?
Is the relationship between God and humanity one of mutual understanding?
propositions: We created man.
We know what his soul whispers to him.
We are nearer to him in knowing him than his jugular vein.

source_text:
Verse: As the two recording-angels—˹one˺ sitting to the right, and ˹the other to˺ the left—note ˹everything˺,

Tafsir: When idh is dependent because of an implied udhkur ‘mention’ the two Receivers the two angels charged with recording a person’s deeds receive when they observe and record seated that is while both of them are sitting qa‘īdun ‘seated’ is the subject the predicate of which is the preceding clause on the right and on the left hand side of him —

hype_questions: What are the two recording angels?
How do they record a person's deeds?
Who are the Receivers of a person's deeds?
propositions: The two recording angels sit to the right and left of a person.
They receive a person's deeds when they observe and record them.
The Receivers are seated while recording a person's deeds.

source_text:
Verse: not a word does a person utter without having a ˹vigilant˺ observer ready ˹to write it down˺.

Tafsir: he does not utter a word but that there is beside him a watcher a guardian who is ready present both raqībun ‘watcher’ and ‘atīdun ‘ready’ are meant to indicate the dual.

hype_questions: Does God always watch over us?
Is there a guardian angel watching over me?
Can we ever be completely alone without being watched?
propositions: A person utters not a word without having a watcher ready to write it down.
There is beside every person a watcher who is always present.
The words of a person are accompanied by the presence of a guardian.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Ultimately,˺ with the throes of death will come the truth. This is what you were trying to escape!

Tafsir: And the agony of death its throes and distress arrives with the truth of the Hereafter such that the one who denied it sees it with his own eyes — and this is the distress itself. That namely death is what you used to shun what you used to flee from and be terrified by.

hype_questions: What is the nature of death in Islam?
How does denial of the Hereafter affect an individual?
What is the ultimate reality that awaits humanity?
propositions: Death arrives with the truth of the Hereafter.
The one who denied the Hereafter sees it with his own eyes.
Death is what one used to shun and flee from.

source_text:
Verse: And the Trumpet will be blown. This is the Day ˹you were˺ warned of.

Tafsir: And the Trumpet will be blown for resurrection. That namely the day of the blast is the Day of the Promised Threat of chastisement for the disbelievers.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Trumpet in Islamic eschatology?
How does the concept of Resurrection relate to the Day of Judgment?
What is the nature of the chastisement that will be inflicted on disbelievers?
propositions: The Trumpet will be blown for resurrection.
The Day of the Promised Threat of chastisement for the disbelievers is the Day of the blast.
There is a warning about the Day of Judgment.

source_text:
Verse: Each soul will come forth with an angel to drive it and another to testify.

Tafsir: And thereat every soul will come to the site for the Gathering accompanied by a driver an angel to drive it there and a witness to testify to its deeds namely the hands and the feet and others; and it will be said to the disbeliever

hype_questions: What will be the state of my soul at the time of the Gathering?
Will I be held accountable for my deeds?
How will my actions be judged?
propositions: Each soul will come forth with an angel to drive it.
Every soul will come to the site for the Gathering accompanied by a driver and a witness.
The hands and feet are among those that will testify to a person's deeds.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It will be said to the denier,˺ “You were totally heedless of this. Now We have lifted this veil of yours, so Today your sight is sharp!”

Tafsir: ‘Verily in the world you were oblivious of this that has befallen you on this day; So now We have removed from you your covering We have done away with your oblivion by what you witness on this day and so your sight on this day is acute’ it is sharp able to perceive what you used to reject in the world.

hype_questions: What happens when one's veil of ignorance is lifted?
How does one's perception change after witnessing a significant event?
What does it mean to have one's sight become sharp and acute?
propositions: You were totally heedless of this.
We have lifted this veil of yours.
Your sight is sharp today, able to perceive what you used to reject in the world.

source_text:
Verse: And one’s accompanying-angel will say, “Here is the record ready with me.”

Tafsir: And his companion the angel charged with him will say ‘This is what I have ready with me as testimony’ whereupon it will be said to Mālik the Keeper of the Fire

hype_questions: What is the record that one's accompanying-angel will say is ready with them?
Who is Mālik, and what role does he play in this context?
What is being kept by the Keeper of the Fire?
propositions: One's accompanying-angel will say, 'Here is the record ready with me.'
His companion the angel charged with him will say 'This is what I have ready with me as testimony'.
It will be said to Mālik the Keeper of the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It will be said to both angels,˺ “Throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever,

Tafsir: ‘Cast into Hell alqiyā meaning either alqi alqi ‘cast cast …’ to denote repetition or the emphatic form alqiyan ‘cast!’ which is the reading of al-Hasan al-Basrī in other words the final nūn has been changed into an alif every obdurate disbeliever obstinate to the truth

hype_questions: What happens to those who are obstinate to the truth?
Who will be cast into Hell?
What is meant by 'stubborn disbeliever' in this verse?
propositions: It will be said to both angels, 'Throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever'.
The final nūn has been changed into an alif to denote repetition or the emphatic form.
Every obdurate disbeliever is obstinate to the truth.

source_text:
Verse: withholder of good, transgressor, and doubter,

Tafsir: hinderer of good such as the payment of alms transgressor wrongdoer skeptic a doubter of his religion

hype_questions: What is the nature of a person who transgresses and doubts their religion?
How does one's transgression affect their relationship with Allah?
Can doubt in one's faith lead to spiritual harm?
propositions: The withholder of good is also a transgressor.
Doubt can hinder the payment of alms.
A person who is a wrongdoer and skeptic may be considered a doubter of their religion.

source_text:
Verse: who set up another god with Allah. So cast them into the severe punishment.”

Tafsir: who has set up alongside God another god! alladhī ja‘ala ma‘a’Llāhi ilāhan ākhara is the subject with an implicitly conditional import the predicate of which is the following. Cast him then into the severe chastisement’ the explanation of this dual form of the verb alqiyāhu ‘cast him’ is as above.

hype_questions: What happens when someone sets up another god alongside God?
Can you explain the punishment for those who do this?
How does Islam view the concept of setting up another god?
propositions: Who set up another god with Allah.
Allah has set up alongside God another god.

source_text:
Verse: One’s ˹devilish˺ associate will say, “Our Lord! I did not make them transgress. Rather, they were far astray ˹on their own˺.”

Tafsir: And his companion Satan will say ‘Our Lord! I did not make him a rebel I did not lead him astray but he himself was in extreme error’ and so when I invited him to disobedience he heeded my call — for this one had said ‘he Satan made me a rebel’ by way of his Satan’s invitation to him.

hype_questions: Does the Quran teach that humans have free will?
Can humans be led astray by Satan's invitation?
What is the nature of rebellion in Islam?
propositions: One’s devilish associate will say, “Our Lord! I did not make them transgress. Rather, they were far astray on their own.”
His companion Satan will say ‘Our Lord! I did not make him a rebel I did not lead him astray but he himself was in extreme error’.
This one had said ‘he Satan made me a rebel’ by way of his Satan’s invitation to him.

source_text:
Verse: Allah will respond, “Do not dispute in My presence, since I had already given you a warning.

Tafsir: He exalted be He will say ‘Do not dispute in My presence in other words disputing is of no use here for I had already given you in the life of the world the threat of chastisement in the Hereafter should you not believe and so it is now inevitable.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah responds to a dispute in His presence?
Can disputing with Allah lead to chastisement in the Hereafter?
How will believers be treated if they do not believe after receiving a warning?
propositions: Allah will respond to disputes in His presence.
Disputing with Allah is of no use.
Believers should not expect chastisement in the Hereafter if they do not believe after receiving a warning.

source_text:
Verse: My Word cannot be changed, nor am I unjust to ˹My˺ creation.”

Tafsir: The word that comes from Me in this respect cannot be altered and I am not unjust to servants’ that I should chastise them without any guilt on their part zallām means dhū zulm ‘one of injustice’ because of His words There will be no injustice today Q. 4017;

hype_questions: Can God's word be altered?
Is God unjust to His servants?
Will there be injustice today?
propositions: God's word cannot be changed.
God is not unjust to His creation.
There will be no injustice today.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Beware of˺ the Day We will ask Hell, “Are you full ˹yet˺?” And it will respond, “Are there any more?”

Tafsir: on the day yawma is in the accusative because of zallām ‘unjust’ when We will say naqūlu may also be read yaqūlu ‘He will say’ to Hell ‘Are you now full?’ this interrogative is for confirmation of His promise to fill it with mankind and jinn and it will say by way of an interrogative such as a question ‘Are there any more?’ that is to say ‘I Hell only have capacity for what I have been filled with’ in other words ‘I am full!’.

hype_questions: Will Hell be completely filled with humanity and jinn on the Day of Judgment?
Does Hell have any remaining capacity to hold more souls?
What will happen when Hell is full?
propositions: The Day of Judgment will ask Hell if it is full.
Hell responds by asking if there are any more souls to be added.
Hell has the capacity for only what it has been filled with.

source_text:
Verse: And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far off.

Tafsir: And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing to a place not far anymore from them and so they see it whereupon it will be said to them

hype_questions: What is the state of Paradise for those who are righteous?
How does proximity to Paradise change for God-fearing individuals?
What will be said to those who see Paradise?
propositions: Paradise is brought near to the righteous.
For the God-fearing, a place not far from them has been made available in Paradise.
They will see Paradise and it will be said to them something.

source_text:
Verse: ˹And it will be said to them,˺ “This is what you were promised, for whoever ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺ and kept up ˹His commandments˺—

Tafsir: ‘This that you see is what you were promised read tū‘adūna or third person plural yū‘adūna ‘they were promised’ in the world and what follows substitutes for li’l-muttaqīna ‘for the God-fearing’ — it is for every penitent one for every person reverting after sin to obedience of God who is mindful mindful of the bounds of God’s religion

hype_questions: What happens to those who constantly turn to Allah and keep up His commandments?
Who is promised in the afterlife for their devotion to God?
How does one achieve forgiveness from God?
propositions: This is what you were promised.
For whoever turned to Allah and kept up His commandments.
It is for every penitent one for every person reverting after sin to obedience of God.

source_text:
Verse: who were in awe of the Most Compassionate without seeing ˹Him˺, and have come with a heart turning ˹only to Him˺.

Tafsir: who fears the Compassionate One while He is in the Unseen the one who fears Him without having seen Him and comes with a penitent heart’ a heart eagerly applying itself to obedience of Him.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Compassionate One?
How can one fear the Compassionate One without seeing Him?
What does it mean to have a penitent heart?
propositions: There are those who fear the Compassionate One.
The Compassionate One is in the Unseen.
One fears the Compassionate One without having seen Him.
A penitent heart applies itself to obedience of the Compassionate One.

source_text:
Verse: Enter it in peace. This is the Day of eternal life!”

Tafsir: It will also be said to the God-fearing ‘Enter it in peace! that is to say secure from every fear or it means enter it with a greeting that is to say greet yourselves and enter. That day in which this entry takes place is the day of immortality’ of everlastingness in Paradise.

hype_questions: What does it mean to enter paradise with peace?
How can one ensure a secure entry into paradise?
What is the significance of greeting oneself before entering paradise?
propositions: Enter in peace.
This day is the Day of eternal life!
The God-fearing will be greeted and enter Paradise securely.

source_text:
Verse: There they will have whatever they desire, and with Us is ˹even˺ more.

Tafsir: Therein they will have whatever they wish; and with Us there is yet more as extra for what they did and for what they will request.

hype_questions: What will I have in paradise?
How much reward will I get for my deeds?
Will I be granted more than what I requested?
propositions: They will have whatever they desire.
There is yet more with Us as extra for what they did and for what they will request.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We destroyed before them, who were far mightier than them. Then ˹when the torment came,˺ they ˹desperately˺ sought refuge in the land. ˹But˺ was there any escape?

Tafsir: And how many a generation We destroyed before them that is before the disbelievers of Quraysh We destroyed many generations of disbelievers who were mightier than these in prowess and who then searched throughout the land wondering is there any escape? for them and others from death but they found none.

hype_questions: Can anyone truly find refuge from destruction?
What is the nature of torment and its effects on those who seek escape?
How do generations of disbelievers respond to the prospect of death?
propositions: We destroyed many peoples before them who were far mightier than them.
When the torment came, they desperately sought refuge in the land.
There was no escape from destruction for them and others.

source_text:
Verse: Surely in this is a reminder for whoever has a ˹mindful˺ heart and lends an attentive ear.

Tafsir: Assuredly there is in that which is mentioned a reminder an admonition for him who has a heart a mind or gives ear or listens to admonitions in full witness present in heart and mind.

hype_questions: What is the significance of being mindful and attentive in understanding the Quran?
How does one develop a heart that can receive reminders from Allah?
What role does listening to admonitions play in spiritual growth?
propositions: There is a reminder in the Quran for whoever has a mindful heart.
The Quran serves as an admonition for those who listen and heed its message.
Being attentive and receptive is essential for understanding the Quran's teachings.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six Days,

Tafsir: And verily We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days the first of which was Sunday and the last of which was Friday and no weariness no fatigue touched Us this was revealed as a refutation of the Jews’ claim that God rested on the Saturday and lay down upon the Throne. The preclusion of weariness in His case is absolute on account of His transcending of the attributes of creatures and the non-existence of any contiguity between Him and other beings His command when He wills a thing is just to say to it ‘Be’ and it is Q. 3682.

hype_questions: Does God rest?
What is the nature of God's creation?
Can God be described in terms of human attributes?
propositions: We created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six Days.
The first day was Sunday, and the last day was Friday.
God did not experience weariness or fatigue during creation.
God's command is to simply say 'Be', and it will be so (Q. 3682).
God transcends the attributes of creatures and does not have contiguity with other beings.

source_text:
Verse: So be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say. And glorify the praises of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset.

Tafsir: So endure patiently addressing the Prophet s what they the Jews and others say in the way of anthropomorphic comparisons and denials and glorify with praise of your Lord perform prayers with praise of Him before the rising of the sun in other words perform the morning prayer and before the sunset that is to say perform both the midday and the afternoon prayers;

hype_questions: What is the significance of patience in Islam?
How does glorifying one's Lord relate to prayer?
What are the different types of prayers mentioned in this verse?
propositions: The Prophet should endure patiently with what others say.
Glorify the praises of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset.
Perform morning, midday, and afternoon prayers.

source_text:
Verse: And glorify Him during part of the night and after the prayers.

Tafsir: and glorify Him at some part of the night that is to say perform the two evening prayers and after prostrations read adbār as the plural of dubur or idbār as the verbal noun from adbara ‘to pass’ in other words perform supererogatory prayers as prescribed by the Sunna after the obligatory ones; it is also said to mean the actual uttering of glorifications at these times with continuous praise.

hype_questions: What are the two evening prayers mentioned in the verse?
What does 'adbār' refer to in the context of Islamic prayer?
How do Muslims perform supererogatory prayers?
propositions: Glorify Him during part of the night.
Perform the two evening prayers after obligatory ones.
Read adbār as a form of continuous praise after prostrations.

source_text:
Verse: And listen! On the Day the caller will call out from a near place,

Tafsir: And listen — O addressee to My words — on the day when the caller namely the archangel Isrāfīl calls out from a place that is near to the heaven this is the Rock of the Holy House of Jerusalem the place on earth that is the nearest to the heaven. He Isrāfīl will say ‘O withered bones severed limbs torn flesh and scattered hairs! God verily commands you to come together for the passing of judgement’.

topics: Salah (calling out) in a spiritual context
hype_questions: What is the significance of Isrāfīl's call on Judgement Day?
How does God command individuals to come together for the passing of judgement?
What is the role of Jerusalem in Islamic eschatology?
propositions: The archangel Isrāfīl will call out from a place near the heaven on Judgement Day.
God commands individuals with 'withered bones, severed limbs, torn flesh, and scattered hairs' to come together for the passing of judgement.
Jerusalem is considered the nearest place on earth to the heaven in Islamic eschatology.

source_text:
Verse: the Day all will hear the ˹mighty˺ Blast in ˹all˺ truth, that will be the Day of emergence ˹from the graves˺.

Tafsir: On the day yawma substitutes for the previous yawma when they that is all creatures hear the Call of truth of the Resurrection — this will be Isrāfīl’s second blast and it may precede or follow his initial call — that day of the call and the hearing is the day of coming forth from the graves yawma ‘on the day is in the accusative because of an implied yunādī ‘when he will call’ that is to say they will come to know the consequence of their denial.

hype_questions: What will be the consequences of denying the truth on the Day of Resurrection?
Will Isrāfīl's second blast precede or follow his initial call?
How will all creatures come to know their fate on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: The Day of Resurrection is a day when all creatures will hear the Call of truth.
Isrāfīl's second blast may precede or follow his initial call.
On the Day of Resurrection, those who denied the truth will come to know their consequence.

source_text:
Verse: It is certainly We Who give life and cause death. And to Us is the final return.

Tafsir: Indeed it is We Who give life and bring death and to Us is the journey’s end.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate destination of all living beings?
Who has the power to give life and cause death?
What is the final return that all souls must face?
propositions: We are the ones who give life.
We are the ones who bring death.
The journey's end is with Us.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Beware of˺ the Day the earth will split open, letting them rush forth. That will be an easy gathering for Us.

Tafsir: On the day when yawma substitutes for the previous yawma with the intervening statement being a parenthetical the earth is split asunder read tashaqqaqu or tashshaqqaqu where the original second tā’ of tatashaqqaqu has been assimilated with it the shīn from them they will come hastening forth sirā‘an sirā‘ the plural of sarī‘ a circumstantial qualifier referring to an implied clause that is to say together they would read fa-yakhrujūna musri‘īna ‘they come forth hastening’. That is an easy gathering for Us dhālika hashrun ‘alaynā yasīr there is here a separation of the noun from its adjective by what is semantically connected to it for the purpose of specification — which is rhetorically unobjectionable; dhālika ‘that’ is meant to point out the signification of the ‘gathering’ which itself is also predicated by this demonstrative particle and this signification is the bringing back to life after extinction and the assembly for the exposition and the reckoning before God.

hype_questions: What will be the nature of the gathering on the Day of Resurrection?
How will people be brought back to life after extinction?
What is the purpose of the reckoning before God?
propositions: The earth will split open on the Day of Resurrection.
They will come forth hastening from their graves.
There is an easy gathering for Us.

source_text:
Verse: We know best what they say. And you ˹O Prophet˺ are not ˹there˺ to compel them ˹to believe˺. So remind with the Quran ˹only˺ those who fear My warning.

Tafsir: We know best what they the disbelievers of the Quraysh say and you are not to be a coercer of them so as to coerce them to embrace faith — but this was revealed before the command to struggle against these disbelievers. So admonish by the Qur’ān those who fear My threat namely believers.

hype_questions: What is the role of a prophet in relation to non-believers?
How should a prophet approach those who refuse to believe?
What is the purpose of reminding believers of the Quran?
propositions: You are not compelled to force others to believe.
The Qur'an serves as a reminder for those who fear My warning.
Believers are specifically mentioned in this verse.

source_text:
Verse: By the winds scattering ˹dust˺,

Tafsir: By the scatterers the winds that scatter dust and other things that scatter dharwan is a verbal noun; one may also say tadhrīhi dharyan ‘it blows it sweeping it away’;

hype_questions: What are the effects of wind on the environment?
How does dust affect human health?
Can winds be used to disperse pollutants?
propositions: The winds scatter dust.
Winds can also scatter other things besides dust.
Dharwan is a verbal noun that means 'to blow' or 'to scatter'.

source_text:
Verse: and ˹the clouds˺ loaded with rain,

Tafsir: and those that bear the clouds that bear moisture as a burden wiqran is the direct object of al-hāmilat ‘those that bear’;

hype_questions: What is the direct object of 'al-hāmilat'?
Who or what bears moisture as a burden?
What are the clouds that carry rain?
propositions: The clouds loaded with rain are a burden.
Those that bear the clouds bear moisture as a burden.

source_text:
Verse: and ˹the ships˺ gliding with ease,

Tafsir: and those that run the ships that run upon the surface of the water with ease yusran is a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial qualifier that is to say muyassaratan;

hype_questions: What does it mean for ships to glide with ease?
How do the ships move on the surface of the water?
What is the significance of ease in navigation?
propositions: The ships are moving smoothly.
Those who run the ships are doing so with ease.
The ships are gliding on the surface of the water.

source_text:
Verse: and ˹the angels˺ administering affairs by ˹Allah’s˺ command!

Tafsir: and those that apportion by command the angels who distribute provisions and the rains and other things across the lands and to all servants

hype_questions: What is the role of angels in administering affairs?
How do angels distribute provisions and rains across lands?
Who are the servants that receive provisions and rains from angels?
propositions: Angels administer affairs by Allah's command.
Angels distribute provisions across lands.
Angels distribute rains across lands.
Angels distribute other things across lands.
Allah commands angels to apportion provisions, rains, and other things.
Servants receive provisions from angels.
Servants receive rains from angels.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, what you are promised is true.

Tafsir: assuredly what you are promised mā ‘what’ relates to the verbal action in other words the promise given to them of resurrection and other matters is true is indeed a true promise

hype_questions: What does it mean for a promise to be true?
How can we trust in the promise of resurrection?
What are some other matters that are promised by God?
propositions: The promise given to them is true.
Resurrection and other matters are promised by God.
A promise is considered true if it is fulfilled.

source_text:
Verse: And the Judgment will certainly come to pass.

Tafsir: and assuredly judgement requital after the reckoning will take place! without doubt.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Judgment?
How does Reckoning relate to Judgment?
Will there be a reckoning after judgment?
propositions: The Judgment will take place.
Judgment is requital after the reckoning.
Reckoning will occur without doubt.

source_text:
Verse: ˹And˺ by the heavens in their marvellous design!

Tafsir: And by the heaven with all its tracks hubuk is the plural of habīka similar in pattern and meaning to turuq tarīqa ‘paths’ that is to say by the heaven that is created with tracks similar to tracks made in the sand

hype_questions: What is the meaning of 'hubuk' in this verse?
How does the design of the heavens relate to human-made tracks?
Can we apply the concept of 'tracks' to other natural phenomena?
propositions: The heavens have a marvellous design.
The heaven is created with tracks similar to those made in the sand.
Human-made tracks can be compared to the tracks on the heavens.

source_text:
Verse: Surely you are ˹lost˺ in conflicting views ˹regarding the truth˺.

Tafsir: indeed you O people of Mecca with regard to the matter of the Prophet s and the Qur’ān are of differing opinions some say of the Prophet that he is ‘a poet’ ‘a sorcerer’ or ‘a soothsayer’ and of the Qur’ān that it is ‘poetry’ ‘sorcery’ or ‘soothsaying’.

hype_questions: Does the Prophet's message have any basis in reality?
Is the Qur'ān more than just poetry?
Can the Prophet be trusted to convey God's message?
propositions: You are of differing opinions regarding the truth.
Some people consider the Prophet to be a poet, sorcerer, or soothsayer.
Others view the Qur'ān as poetry, sorcery, or soothsaying.

source_text:
Verse: Only those ˹destined to be˺ deluded are turned away from it.

Tafsir: He is turned away therefrom from the Prophet s and the Qur’ān that is turned away from believing therein who has deviated who has been turned away from guidance in God’s exalted be He.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are deluded and turn away from the truth?
How does deviation from guidance affect one's belief in God?
Can someone be turned away from guidance and still find their way back?
propositions: Only those destined to be deluded are turned away from it.
He is turned away from the Prophet, the Qur'ān, and from believing therein.
Whoever has deviated from guidance in God's exalted path is turned away from belief.

source_text:
Verse: Condemned are the liars—

Tafsir: Perish the conjecturers accursed be the liars those of differing opinions

hype_questions: What happens to those who spread false information?
How should we handle people with different beliefs?
Can we trust someone who contradicts our understanding of the Quran?
propositions: Lying is a grave sin.
Those who disagree are not necessarily liars.
We should focus on understanding and respecting differing opinions.

source_text:
Verse: those who are ˹steeped˺ in ignorance, totally heedless.

Tafsir: who are in a stupor in ignorance that has stupefied them heedless oblivious of the matter of the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What is the state of those who are ignorant and heedless?
How does ignorance affect a person's awareness of the Hereafter?
What is the nature of heedlessness in relation to spiritual growth?
propositions: Those who are steeped in ignorance are totally heedless.
Ignorance has stupefied them, making them oblivious to the matter of the Hereafter.
Heedlessness refers to a state of being unaware or indifferent to important matters.

source_text:
Verse: They ask ˹mockingly˺, “When is this Day of Judgment?”

Tafsir: They ask the Prophet asking him derisively ‘When is the Day of Judgement?’ in other words ‘when will it come?’ and the response given to them is that it will come

hype_questions: When will the Day of Judgement arrive?
What is the timeline for the Day of Judgment?
Will the Day of Judgment ever come?
propositions: The Day of Judgment will arrive.
The Prophet responded to those who asked about the Day of Judgment with a simple affirmation.
Those who ask when the Day of Judgment will arrive are met with a response that emphasizes its inevitability.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It is˺ the Day they will be tormented over the Fire.

Tafsir: on the day when they will be tormented in the Fire that is to say chastised in it and it will be said to them during the chastisement

hype_questions: What happens on the Day of Resurrection?
Will those who disbelieve be punished?
What is the nature of the punishment in the Fire?
propositions: The Day of Resurrection will bring torment over those who disbelieve.
The Fire is a place of chastisement where those who disbelieve will be punished.
During the chastisement, it will be said to them that they are being chastised in the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They will be told,˺ “Taste your torment! This is what you sought to hasten.”

Tafsir: ‘Taste this torment of yours this chastisement of yours. This chastisement is what you sought to hasten on!’ in the world in derision.

hype_questions: What happens when one seeks to hasten their own torment?
How does Allah respond to those who seek to hasten their own chastisement?
What is the nature of the torment that those who hasten it upon themselves will taste?
propositions: This is what you sought to hasten.
You sought to hasten on this chastisement in derision.
This chastisement is what you sought to hasten.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, the righteous will be amid Gardens and springs,

Tafsir: Truly the God-fearing will be amid gardens orchards and springs flowing therein

hype_questions: What is the state of those who are God-fearing in the afterlife?
How will the righteous be rewarded in Paradise?
What kind of environment can one expect to find in Paradise?
propositions: The righteous will be amid Gardens.
Gardens contain orchards.
Springs flow within the gardens.

source_text:
Verse: ˹joyfully˺ receiving what their Lord will grant them. Before this ˹reward˺ they were truly good-doers ˹in the world˺:

Tafsir: receiving ākhidhīna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person of the predicate of inna ‘truly’ what their Lord has given them of reward for indeed formerly before their entering Paradise they had been virtuous in the world.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the reward granted by Allah?
How do people's actions in the world affect their entry into Paradise?
What does it mean to be virtuous in the context of Islamic theology?
propositions: Allah grants a reward to those who enter Paradise.
People are considered virtuous if they were good-doers in the world before entering Paradise.
The reward granted by Allah is a consequence of one's actions in the world.

source_text:
