Verse: they used to sleep only little in the night,

Tafsir: Little of the night did they use to sleep mā is extra; yahja‘ūna is the predicate of kānū; qalīlan ‘little’ is an adverb in other words they used to sleep for a small portion of the night and perform prayers during most of it

hype_questions: How much did people sleep at night before?
What did they do with the rest of their time?
Did they pray during most of their nights?
propositions: They used to sleep little in the night.
They used to sleep for a small portion of the night and perform prayers during most of it.

source_text:
Verse: and pray for forgiveness before dawn.

Tafsir: and at dawns they used to seek forgiveness they used say ‘Our Lord! Forgive us’

hype_questions: What is the significance of seeking forgiveness before dawn?
How does the practice of praying for forgiveness at dawn relate to Islamic teachings?
What are the benefits of making du'a (supplication) at dawn?
propositions: Praying for forgiveness before dawn is a common practice among Muslims.
The phrase 'Our Lord! Forgive us' is often used in morning prayers.
Seeking forgiveness at dawn is considered an act of obedience to Allah's command.

source_text:
Verse: And in their wealth there was a rightful share ˹fulfilled˺ for the beggar and the poor.

Tafsir: and there was a share in their wealth assigned for the beggar and the deprived the latter being the one who does not beg because of his self-restraint.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of zakat in Islam?
How does self-restraint relate to poverty in Islamic teachings?
Who is considered deprived in the context of zakat?
propositions: There was a rightful share of wealth assigned for the beggar and the poor.
The deprived refers to the one who does not beg due to their self-restraint.
Zakat is fulfilled in the wealth of those who are able to give.

source_text:
Verse: There are ˹countless˺ signs on earth for those with sure faith,

Tafsir: And in the earth in the way of mountains seas trees fruits plants and other things there are signs indications of God’s power glory be to Him exalted be He and of His Oneness for those who know with certainty

hype_questions: What are the signs of God's power on earth?
How can we know God's Oneness with certainty?
What is the significance of mountains, seas, trees, fruits, and plants in understanding God's glory?
propositions: There are signs on earth for those with sure faith.
The earth contains signs of God's power, glory, and Oneness.
God's power and glory are evident in the natural world.

source_text:
Verse: as there are within yourselves. Can you not see?

Tafsir: and in your souls there are also signs from the beginning of your creation to its end and in the marvelous aspects of your creation. Will you not then perceive? all that and thus infer therefrom the Creator of it and His power.

hype_questions: Can we not see our own potential within ourselves?
Do we not perceive the signs of creation in our souls?
Can we infer the power and creator from these signs?
propositions: There are signs from the beginning of your creation to its end within yourselves.
You have the ability to perceive these signs in your souls.
The creator is inferred from these signs and their marvelous aspects.

source_text:
Verse: In heaven is your sustenance and whatever you are promised.

Tafsir: And in the heaven is your provision that is the rain from which results the vegetation that is your provision and there is also what you are promised in the way of the ultimate return reward and punishment in other words all of this is foreordained in the heaven.

hype_questions: What is promised to us in the afterlife?
How does our sustenance come from heaven?
Is everything foreordained in heaven?
propositions: In heaven, one's sustenance and provision are provided.
The rain in heaven results in vegetation, which serves as one's provision.
All aspects of life, including reward and punishment, are foreordained in heaven.

source_text:
Verse: Then by the Lord of heaven and earth! ˹All˺ this is certainly as true as ˹the fact that˺ you can speak!

Tafsir: So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth it that which you are promised is as assuredly true as the fact that you have power of speech read mithlu in the nominative as an adjective with the mā being extra; or read mithla in the accusative as being a compound with mā that is to say it is as true as your speech is in reality that is in your knowing it to be true necessarily by its issuing from you.

hype_questions: Does the power of speech imply truthfulness?
Can one's speech be a reflection of their inner conviction about something being true?
Is there an inherent connection between speaking and knowing something to be true?
propositions: You have the power of speech.
The fact that you can speak is as assuredly true as the promised event.
Your speech is a reflection of your inner conviction about the truthfulness of something.

source_text:
Verse: Has the story of Abraham’s honoured guests reached you ˹O Prophet˺?

Tafsir: Has the story reached you — addressing the Prophet s — of Abraham’s honoured guests? — these were said to be either twelve ten or three angels one of whom was Gabriel.

hype_questions: What were Abraham's honoured guests?
Who were the twelve or three angels that visited Abraham?
Was Gabriel one of Abraham's honoured guests?
propositions: The story of Abraham’s honoured guests has reached you.
Abraham’s honoured guests were either twelve or three angels, including Gabriel.
Gabriel was one of Abraham’s honoured guests.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember˺ when they entered his presence and greeted ˹him with˺, “Peace!” He replied, “Peace ˹be upon you˺!” ˹Then he said to himself,˺ “˹These are˺ an unfamiliar people.”

Tafsir: When idh is an adverbial qualifier of hadīthu dayfi ‘the story of the guests’ they entered upon him and said ‘Peace!’ — in other words they said these very words. He said ‘Peace!’ — also these very words — These are an unfamiliar folk whom we do not know — he said this to himself qawmun munkarūna is the predicate of an implicit subject such as hā’ūlā’i ‘these are’.

hype_questions: What does it mean to greet someone with 'peace'?
How do we recognize and respond to unfamiliar people?
Can we ever truly know someone's intentions?
propositions: When they entered his presence, they greeted him with 'Peace!'
He replied, 'Peace be upon you!'
These are an unfamiliar folk whom we do not know

source_text:
Verse: Then he slipped off to his family and brought a fat ˹roasted˺ calf,

Tafsir: Then he went aside to his family secretly and brought a fat calf — in sūrat Hūd it is said a roasted calf Q. 1169 —

hype_questions: What does the story of Hūd teach us about family secrets?
How did Hūd's family react to his secret visit?
What is the significance of a roasted calf in Islamic tradition?
propositions: He went aside to his family secretly.
He brought a fat calf.
A roasted calf was mentioned in sūrat Hūd (Q. 1169).

source_text:
Verse: and placed it before them, asking, “Will you not eat?”

Tafsir: and he placed it near them saying ‘Will you not eat?’ he invited them to eat but they did not respond.

hype_questions: Wouldn't you like to try some food?
Don't you want to eat?
Aren't you curious about what's being offered?
propositions: He placed the food near them.
He invited them to eat but they did not respond.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They did not eat,˺ so he grew fearful of them.

Tafsir: Then he conceived he kept secret in himself a fear of them. They said ‘Do not be afraid!’ we are messengers from your Lord. And they gave him good tidings of the birth of a knowledgeable boy one endowed with much knowledge and this was Isaac as mentioned in sūrat Hūd Q. 1171.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Isaac's birth in Islamic tradition?
How do messengers from God comfort those who are afraid?
What does the story of Hud and his son Isaac teach us about faith and knowledge?
propositions: He grew fearful of them.
They said 'Do not be afraid!' we are messengers from your Lord.
They gave him good tidings of the birth of a knowledgeable boy one endowed with much knowledge.

source_text:
Verse: Then his wife came forward with a cry, clasping her forehead ˹in astonishment˺, exclaiming, “˹A baby from˺ a barren, old woman!”

Tafsir: Then his wife Sarah came forward clamouring shouting fī sarratin is a circumstantial qualifier that is to say she came shouting and smote slapped her face and said ‘A barren old woman!’ who has never given birth to a child aged ninety-nine with Abraham being one hundred years old; or alternatively he was a hundred and twenty years old and she was ninety years old.

hype_questions: What is the age of Sarah when she gives birth to Isaac?
How old was Abraham when he gave birth to Isaac?
What is the age of Abraham and Sarah when Isaac is born?
propositions: Sarah came forward shouting.
Sarah slapped her face.
Abraham was one hundred years old.

source_text:
Verse: They replied, “Such has your Lord decreed. He is truly the All-Wise, All-Knowing.”

Tafsir: They said ‘So just like what we have said with regard to the good tiding has your Lord said. Indeed He is the Wise in His actions the Knower’ of His creatures.

hype_questions: Does Allah's wisdom and knowledge extend to all aspects of life?
Can we truly understand the reasons behind Allah's decrees?
Is Allah's wisdom and knowledge limited to His actions alone?
propositions: Allah has decreed something.
Allah is wise in His actions.
Allah is the Knower of His creatures.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Later,˺ Abraham asked, “What is your mission, O  messengers?”

Tafsir: He said ‘So what is your business O you who have been sent by God?’

hype_questions: What is the purpose of being a messenger from God?
How should one address a messenger from God?
What is the relationship between a messenger and their divine sender?
propositions: Abraham asked about the mission of messengers.
Messengers are sent by God.
God's messengers are on a specific business.

source_text:
Verse: They replied, “We have actually been sent to a wicked people,

Tafsir: They said ‘Lo! we have been sent to a guilty folk disbelievers — these were the people of Lot —

hype_questions: What is the nature of the people to whom the Prophet was sent?
How did the Prophet respond to those who rejected his message?
Who were the people of Lot, and what is their significance in Islamic history?
propositions: We have been sent to a wicked people.
These were the people of Lot, disbelievers.
The people of Lot were guilty folk.

source_text:
Verse: to send upon them stones of ˹baked˺ clay,

Tafsir: that we may unleash upon them stones of clay baked in fire

hype_questions: What is the Qiyamah?
What will happen to those who reject Allah on the Day of Judgment?
How will the Qiyamah be like?
propositions: We will send upon them stones of clay baked in fire.
The Qiyamah is a day of reckoning when Allah will judge humanity.
Those who reject Allah will face punishment on the Day of Judgment.

source_text:
Verse: marked by your Lord for the transgressors.”

Tafsir: marked bearing the name of the person at whom it will be hurled by your Lord ‘inda rabbika is an adverbial qualifier of musawwamatan ‘marked’ for the destruction of the prodigal’ for coming unto males in addition to their disbelief.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of transgressing against Allah?
How does Allah punish those who disbelieve and engage in sinful behavior?
What is the nature of the destruction that awaits those who reject Allah's message?
propositions: Your Lord has marked you for destruction.
The mark on you is from your Lord, indicating that you will be punished for your transgression.
You have been marked by your Lord as a prodigal, deserving of punishment for your disbelief and sinful behavior.

source_text:
Verse: Then ˹before the torment˺ We evacuated the believers from the city.

Tafsir: So We brought forth those in them that is in the towns of the people of Lot who were believers in order to destroy the disbelievers;

hype_questions: What is the significance of evacuating believers from a city in Islamic theology?
How does the Quran relate to the story of Prophet Lot and his people?
What is the purpose of destroying disbelievers according to Islamic teachings?
propositions: We evacuated the believers from the city before the torment.
Those in the towns of the people of Lot who were believers were brought forth by God.
The Quran destroyed the disbelievers as part of its plan.

source_text:
Verse: But We only found one family that had submitted ˹to Allah˺.

Tafsir: but We did not find therein other than one house of those who had submitted to God these were Lot and his two daughters. They have been described here with the terms ‘belief’ and ‘submission’ because they had affirmed faith in their hearts and used their limbs to perform acts of obedience.

hype_questions: What does it mean to submit to God?
How do people show their belief in God?
Who are the two daughters of Lot?
propositions: We found one family that submitted to Allah.
Lot and his two daughters were described as having believed and submitted to God.
Belief and submission refer to affirming faith in one's heart and performing acts of obedience with one's limbs.

source_text:
Verse: And We have left a sign there ˹as a lesson˺ for those who fear the painful punishment.

Tafsir: And We left therein after destroying the disbelievers a sign an indication of their destruction for those who fear the painful chastisement so that they may not do what these sinners did.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of leaving a sign for those who fear the painful punishment?
How does the destruction of disbelievers serve as an indication of their own destruction?
What lesson can be learned from the story of the sinners?
propositions: We left a sign in the earth as a lesson for those who fear the painful punishment.
After destroying the disbelievers, We left a sign that indicates their own destruction.
The purpose of leaving this sign is to warn others from doing what the sinners did.

source_text:
Verse: And in ˹the story of˺ Moses ˹was another lesson,˺ when We sent him to Pharaoh with compelling proof,

Tafsir: And a sign too in Moses wa-fī Mūsā is a supplement to fīhā ‘therein’ that is to say We also left a sign in the story of Moses when We sent him to Pharaoh vested with a clear warrant with a manifest proof;

hype_questions: What was the sign left by Allah in the story of Moses?
Why did Allah send Moses to Pharaoh with a clear warrant?
What is the meaning of 'fīhā' in this context?
propositions: Allah sent Moses to Pharaoh with compelling proof.
There was a sign left by Allah in the story of Moses.
The sign was vested with a clear warrant and manifest proof.

source_text:
Verse: but Pharaoh was carried away by his power, saying ˹of Moses˺, “A magician or a madman!”

Tafsir: but he turned away he rejected belief to his supports bi-ruknihi his hosts so called because to him they are like a support rukn saying to Moses that he Moses was ‘A sorcerer or a madman!’

hype_questions: Does Pharaoh's power lead to him rejecting belief?
What does Pharaoh call Moses, a magician or a madman?
How do Pharaoh's hosts relate to his rejection of belief?
propositions: Pharaoh was carried away by his power.
Pharaoh rejected belief and turned away from his supports.
Pharaoh called Moses 'A sorcerer or a madman!'

source_text:
Verse: So We seized him and his soldiers, casting them into the sea while he was blameworthy.

Tafsir: So We seized him and his hosts and cast flung them into the waters the sea and so they drowned for he that is Pharaoh was blameworthy guilty of what is blameworthy such as denying the messengers and claiming divinity.

hype_questions: What happens when one denies the messengers of God?
Can claiming divinity lead to blame and punishment?
How does one avoid being like Pharaoh, who was guilty of many wrongdoings?
propositions: We seized him and his hosts.
They were cast into the waters of the sea.
Pharaoh was blameworthy for denying the messengers and claiming divinity.
He was guilty of such actions as denying the messengers and claiming divinity.

source_text:
Verse: And in ˹the story of˺ ’ad ˹was another lesson,˺ when We sent against them the devastating wind.

Tafsir: And also in the destruction of ‘Ād was a sign when We unleashed against them a barren wind a wind which brings nothing of good for it does not bear any rain and does not pollinate any trees; this wind was the west wind al-dabūr.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the destruction of 'Ād in Islamic theology?
How does the barren wind relate to the concept of a sign from Allah?
What are the consequences of being affected by the west wind?
propositions: We sent against ‘Ād a devastating wind.
The destruction of ‘Ād was a sign from Allah.
The barren wind does not bear any rain and does not pollinate any trees.

source_text:
Verse: There was nothing it came upon that it did not reduce to ashes.

Tafsir: It did not leave anything any soul or property that it came upon without making it like decayed bones like something that is withered and in scattered pieces.

hype_questions: What happens to everything when a powerful force is unleashed?
How does destruction affect the material world?
Can anything survive the full force of a mighty power?
propositions: Nothing was left untouched by its power.
It reduced all things to decayed bones.
Everything was scattered into pieces.

source_text:
Verse: And in ˹the story of˺ Thamûd ˹was another lesson,˺ when they were told, “Enjoy yourselves ˹only˺ for a ˹short˺ while.”

Tafsir: And also in the destruction of Thamūd was a sign when it was said to them after the hamstringing of the she-camel ‘Enjoy yourselves for a while!’ until the end of your terms of life — as stated in the other verse ‘Enjoy yourselves in your dwellings for three days’ Q.1165.

hype_questions: What is the lesson from the story of Thamûd?
Why was the she-camel hamstringed?
How long should one enjoy themselves?
propositions: They were told to enjoy themselves for a short while.
The destruction of Thamūd was a sign after the hamstringing of the she-camel.
Their terms of life are determined by Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Still they persisted in defying the commands of their Lord, so they were overtaken by a ˹mighty˺ blast while they were looking on.

Tafsir: Then they defied they scorned the command of their Lord refraining from implementing it; so the thunderbolt that is the destructive cry seized them after the three days had passed as they were looking around in other words it seized them in the daytime.

hype_questions: What happens when one disobeys their Lord?
How does one's disobedience lead to reckoning?
What is the consequence of defying one's Lord?
propositions: They defied the command of their Lord.
The thunderbolt seized them after three days had passed.
It seized them in the daytime.

source_text:
Verse: Then they were not able to rise up, nor were they helped.

Tafsir: So they were unable to rise up they could not get up upon the sending down of the chastisement nor were they victors over the One Who destroyed them.

hype_questions: What happens when Allah sends down chastisement?
Can people rise up against Allah's punishment?
Who is the One Who destroys those who are punished?
propositions: They were unable to rise up.
The sending down of chastisement prevented them from getting up.
They were not victors over Allah, the One Who destroyed them.

source_text:
Verse: And the people of Noah ˹had also been destroyed˺ earlier. They were truly a rebellious people.

Tafsir: And the people of Noah read wa qawmi Nūhin as a supplement to Thamūda in other words ‘in the destruction of these two peoples by what destructive power exists in the heavens and the earth there is also a sign’; or read wa qawma Nūhin in other words ‘We also destroyed the people of Noah’ aforetime that is before the destruction of those mentioned. Indeed they were an immoral lot.

hype_questions: What destructive power exists in the heavens and the earth?
Did Allah destroy the people of Thamūda before or after the people of Noah?
What was the moral state of the people of Noah?
propositions: The people of Noah were destroyed by Allah.
The destruction of the people of Noah is a sign in the heavens and the earth.
The people of Noah were an immoral lot.

source_text:
Verse: We built the universe with ˹great˺ might, and We are certainly expanding ˹it˺.

Tafsir: And the heaven We built it with might and indeed We are powerful one says āda’l-rajulu or ya’īdu to mean ‘he is strong’; and awsa‘a’l-rajulu to mean ‘he has become capable dhū sa‘a and strong’.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's power?
How does Allah expand the universe?
What does it mean for Allah to be strong?
propositions: Allah built the universe with great might.
Allah is certainly expanding the universe.
Allah is a powerful one.
The term āda'l-rajulu means 'he is strong'.
The term awsa'ʿa'l-rajulu means 'he has become capable and strong'.

source_text:
Verse: As for the earth, We spread it out. How superbly did We smooth it out!

Tafsir: And the earth We spread it out We made it level what excellent Spreaders then! We are.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the earth's creation?
How did Allah create the earth?
What are some of the miracles of Allah in creating the earth?
propositions: Allah spread out the earth.
The earth was made level by Allah.
Allah is a superb Spreader.

source_text:
Verse: And We created pairs of all things so perhaps you would be mindful.

Tafsir: And of all things wa-min kulli shay’in is semantically connected to His following words khalaqnā We created pairs two kinds such as male and female heaven and earth sun and moon plain and mountain summer and winter sweet and bitter light and darkness that perhaps you might remember tadhakkarūna one of the two original tā’ letters of tatadhakkarūna has been omitted and hence realise that the Creator of pairs is Himself Singular that you might then worship him.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creating pairs in all things?
How can remembering the Creator help us worship Him?
What does it mean to remember the Creator?
propositions: We created pairs of all things.
The Creator of pairs is Himself Singular.
You should worship the Creator.

source_text:
Verse: So ˹proclaim, O  Prophet˺: “Flee to Allah! I am truly sent by Him with a clear warning to you.

Tafsir: So flee unto God that is to say away from His punishment toward His reward by being obedient to Him and not disobeying Him. Truly I am a clear warner to you from Him.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reward for obedience to Allah?
How can one avoid Allah's punishment through obedience?
What does it mean to be a clear warner from Allah?
propositions: Flee unto God.
Being obedient to Him brings His reward, while disobedience leads to His punishment.
I am truly sent by Him with a clear warning to you.

source_text:
Verse: And do not set up another god with Allah. I am truly sent by Him with a clear warning to you.”

Tafsir: And do not set up another god alongside God. Truly I am a clear warner to you from Him before fa-firrū ‘so flee’ one may read an implicit preceding qul lahum ‘Say to them’.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah?
Can humans be sent by Allah with a clear warning?
How should humans respond to a clear warning from Allah?
propositions: Do not set up another god alongside God.
I am truly sent by Allah with a clear warning to you.
Flee from the false gods.

source_text:
Verse: Similarly, no messenger came to those before them without being told: “A magician or a madman!”

Tafsir: Thus there did not come to those who were before them any messenger but they said that he was ‘A sorcerer or a madman!’ in other words their denial of you by saying that you are a sorcerer or a madman was like the denial of communities before them of their messengers by saying that same thing.

hype_questions: What is the typical response of people to a messenger before them?
How do communities typically respond to messengers from their past?
What does it mean when people deny a prophet by saying they are a sorcerer or madman?
propositions: No messenger came to those before them without being told that he is a magician or a madman.
The denial of a messenger by saying he is a sorcerer or madman is similar to the denial of communities before them of their messengers.
The response of people to a messenger is often characterized as denial, which can take the form of calling them a sorcerer or madman.

source_text:
Verse: Have they passed this ˹cliché˺ down to one another? In fact, they have ˹all˺ been a transgressing people.

Tafsir: Have they all enjoined this upon one another? an interrogative intended as a denial. Nay but they are an insolent folk a folk whose own proclivity to insolence has made them all say the same thing.

propositions: They have not passed this down to one another.
They are an insolent folk.
Their proclivity to insolence has made them all say the same thing.

source_text:
Verse: So ˹now˺ turn away from them ˹O Prophet˺, for you will not be blamed.

You have conveyed the Message to them.
Shun them.

source_text:
Verse: But ˹continue to˺ remind. For certainly reminders benefit the believers.

Tafsir: And remind admonish by the Qur’ān for reminding truly benefits believers these being those whom God knows that they will believe.

propositions: Reminders benefit believers.
The Qur'an admonishes by reminding.
God knows that those who are reminded will believe.

source_text:
Verse: I did not create jinn and humans except to worship Me.

Tafsir: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they may worship Me the fact that disbelievers do not worship God does not contradict this statement since a purpose does not have to be realised in an act for it to be valid as when you may say ‘I sharpened this pencil in order to write with it’ even though you might not actually write with it.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creating jinn and humans?
Can a purpose be valid without being realized?
Is worshiping God a necessary condition for the existence of jinn and humans?
propositions: I created jinn and humans to worship Me.
A purpose does not have to be realized in an act for it to be valid.

source_text:
Verse: I seek no provision from them, nor do I need them to feed Me.

hype_questions: Does Allah require anything from us?

propositions: I do not need any provision.
I am self-sufficient and do not require anything from others.
I do not desire that others should feed me or myself or others.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ is the Supreme Provider—Lord of all Power, Ever Mighty.

propositions: Allah is the Supreme Provider.
Allah is the Lord of Power.
Allah is Ever Mighty.
God is the Provider.
God is the Lord of Strength.

God is the Stern.

source_text:
Verse: The wrongdoers will certainly have a share ˹of the torment˺ like that of their predecessors. So do not let them ask Me to hasten ˹it˺.

Tafsir: And for those who have wronged their souls through disbelief from among the people of Mecca and others there will assuredly be a lot a share of chastisement like the lot the share of their counterparts who perished before them. So let them not ask Me to hasten on the chastisement should I give them respite until the Day of Resurrection.

hype_questions: Will those who have wronged their souls through disbelief be punished severely?

propositions: The wrongdoers will certainly have a share of the torment.
Those who have wronged their souls through disbelief will be punished severely.
Allah will not hasten the chastisement for those who have wronged themselves.

source_text:

propositions: There is a Day of Resurrection that has been promised.

source_text:

The mountain on which God spoke to Moses is called Ṭûr.

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: ˹It is˺ the Day they will be fiercely shoved into the Fire of Hell.

Tafsir: the day when they will be thrust with a violent thrust into Hell when they will be pushed violently this last clause yawma yuda‘‘ūna ilā nāri jahannama da‘‘an is a substitution for yawma tamūru ‘the day when the heaven will heave’ and it will be said to them in reproach

hype_questions: What happens on Judgment Day?

source_text:
Verse: Burn in it! It is the same whether you endure ˹it˺ patiently or not. You are only rewarded for what you used to do.”

Tafsir: Burn in it! And whether you endure it or do not endure your endurance and your anguish will be the same for you because your endurance will be of no use to you. You are only being requited for what you used to do’ that is to say only the requital for it.

hype_questions: What happens to a person's endurance and anguish in the afterlife?

propositions: You are only rewarded for what you used to do.
Your endurance will be of no use to you in the afterlife.

source_text:

hype_questions: What is the state of those who are righteous in the afterlife?

propositions: The righteous will be in Gardens and bliss.
God-fearing individuals will experience gardens and bliss in the afterlife.

source_text:
Verse: enjoying whatever their Lord will have granted them. And their Lord will have protected them from the torment of the Hellfire.

Tafsir: rejoicing delighting in what bi-mā relates to the verbal action their Lord has given them and that their Lord has shielded them from the chastisement of Hell-fire wa-waqāhum rabbuhum ‘adhāba’l-jahīmi is a supplement to ātāhum ‘what He has given them’ in other words rejoicing in their having been given this reward and shielded from Hell-fire.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reward for those who are righteous?

Their Lord has protected them from the torment of Hellfire.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They will be told,˺ “Eat and drink happily for what you used to do.”

Tafsir: And it will said to them ‘Eat and drink in full enjoyment hanī’an is a circumstantial qualifier that is to say muhanna’īna as a reward for what bi-mā the bi- is causative you used to do’.

hype_questions: What kind of enjoyment can one expect in the afterlife?
How does one's past actions affect their reward in the hereafter?
What is meant by 'full enjoyment' in this context?
propositions: They will be told to eat and drink happily.
The reward for what they used to do is eating and drinking in full enjoyment.
Hanī'an is a circumstantial qualifier that indicates full enjoyment as a reward.

source_text:
Verse: They will be reclining on thrones, ˹neatly˺ lined up ˹facing each other˺. And We will pair them to maidens with gorgeous eyes.

Tafsir: They will be reclining muttaki’īna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the concealed subject of God’s words fī jannātin ‘amid gardens’ on ranged couches arranged one next to the other and We will wed them zawwajnāhum is a supplement to jannātin ‘gardens’ meaning ‘We will couple them’ to beautiful houris of wide and beautiful eyes.

hype_questions: What is the state of those who will be resurrected?
How will they be paired in Paradise?
What are the beautiful houris like?
propositions: They will recline on thrones.
We will pair them to maidens with gorgeous eyes.
God will couple them to beautiful houris.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith, We will elevate their descendants to their rank, never discounting anything ˹of the reward˺ of their deeds. Every person will reap only what they sowed.

Tafsir: And those who believed wa’lladhīna āmanū the subject and whom We made to be followed wa-atba‘nāhum a variant reading has wa’ttaba‘athum ‘and there followed them’ as a supplement to āmanū ‘who believed’ by their descendants dhurrīyātihim a variant reading for this plural has dhurrīyatuhum young and old in faith on the part of the older ones and on the part of the parents in their young ones the predicate of the subject above is the following alhaqnā bihim We will make their mentioned descendants join them in Paradise so that they are in the same degree of reward even though they might not have performed the same meritorious deeds as them to deserve this equal status a way of honouring the parents by having their children join them again; and We will not deprive them read alatnāhum or alitnāhum We will not diminish them of anything min shay’in min is extra of their deeds in order to add it to the deeds of their children. Every man is subject to what he has earned of good or evil deeds and will be requited for evil and rewarded for good.

hype_questions: What happens to the descendants of believers after they pass away?
Will their children be rewarded equally for their good deeds?
How will the parents be treated in Paradise?
propositions: We will elevate the descendants of those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith.
Every person will reap only what they sowed.
We will make their mentioned descendants join them in Paradise so that they are in the same degree of reward.
We will not deprive them of anything from their deeds to add it to the deeds of their children.
Every man is subject to what he has earned of good or evil deeds and will be requited for evil and rewarded for good.

source_text:
Verse: And We will ˹continually˺ provide them with whatever fruit or meat they desire.

Tafsir: And We will supply them We will enhance for them their provision from time to time with fruits and meat such as they desire even if they do not request it openly.

hype_questions: Will Allah provide for me in this life?

propositions: Allah will provide for them whatever they desire.
Allah will supply them with fruits and meat from time to time.

source_text:
Verse: They will pass around to each other a drink ˹of pure wine,˺ which leads to no idle talk or sinfulness.

Tafsir: They will pass from one to another therein in Paradise a cup of wine wherein is neither vain talk which might come about between them as a result of drinking it nor cause for sin thereby that might befall them — in contrast to the case with the wine of this world.

hype_questions: What happens to people in Paradise when they drink wine?

Can drinking wine lead to sinfulness?
propositions: They will pass around a cup of wine in Paradise.
The wine in Paradise has no effect on people's behavior.
Drinking wine does not cause sinfulness.

source_text:
Verse: And they will be waited on by their youthful servants like spotless pearls.

Tafsir: And there will circulate from all around them for service youths delicate in demeanour of their own as if in terms of their beauty and immaculateness they were hidden pearls preserved inside shells because when it a pearl is inside it it is better than one that is not.

hype_questions: What is the significance of beauty in Islam?

What does the comparison between youthful servants and pearls signify?
propositions: The righteous will be attended to by their young servants.
The youths serving them are delicate in demeanor.
A pearl, when preserved inside a shell, becomes more valuable than one that is exposed.

source_text:
Verse: They will turn to one another inquisitively.

Tafsir: And some among them will turn to one another questioning each other — they ask one another about how they were in the past and what they have now attained in their delight and acknowledgement of the grace of God to them.

propositions: Some individuals will turn to one another questioning each other.
They ask about their past experiences and current accomplishments.
Their inquiry is driven by a sense of delight and acknowledgement of God's grace.

source_text:
Verse: They will say, “Before ˹this reward˺ we used to be in awe ˹of Allah˺ in the midst of our people.

Tafsir: They say as an intimation of the reason for this attainment ‘Truly before amid our families in the world we used to be ever anxious afraid of God’s chastisement;

hype_questions: What was it like for them before they received this reward?

propositions: They used to be in awe of Allah among their people.
Before receiving this reward, they were ever anxious and afraid of God's chastisement.
Their fear of God's chastisement was a significant aspect of their lives before receiving the reward.

source_text:
Verse: So Allah has graced us and protected us from the torment of ˹Hell’s˺ scorching heat.

Tafsir: but God showed us favour through His forgiveness and shielded us from the piercing chastisement al-samūm the Fire so called because it penetrates the pores al-masāmm; and they say also by way of intimation

hype_questions: What is the torment of Hell's scorching heat?
How does God show us favour through His forgiveness?
What is meant by al-samūm, the piercing chastisement?
propositions: Allah has graced us.
God showed us favour through His forgiveness.
He shielded us from the piercing chastisement of Hell's Fire.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, we used to call upon Him ˹alone˺ before. He is truly the Most Kind, Most Merciful.”

Tafsir: indeed before that is in the world we used to call on Him worship Him affirming His Oneness. Verily He is read innahu as the beginning of a new independent sentence even if it introduces the reason in terms of its import; or read annahu as a reason in terms of the syntactical order of the words the Benign the Beneficent the True to His promise the Merciful One of tremendous mercy.

hype_questions: What is the significance of affirming Allah's Oneness in worship?

propositions: We used to call upon Him alone before.
He is truly the Most Kind, Most Merciful.
Allah is read as the beginning of a new independent sentence or as a reason in terms of its import.
Verily He is the Benign, the Beneficent, the True to His promise.
The Merciful One of tremendous mercy.

source_text:
Verse: So ˹continue to˺ remind ˹all, O  Prophet˺. For you, by the grace of your Lord, are not a fortune-teller or a madman.

propositions: The Prophet is reminded by Allah.
Idolaters should not desist from being reminded.
A prophet is neither a soothsayer nor a madman.

source_text:
Verse: Or do they say, “˹He is˺ a poet, for whom we ˹eagerly˺ await an ill-fate!”?

Tafsir: Or am means bal do they say that he is ‘A poet for whom we may await the accidents of fate?’ the vicissitudes of time so that he will just die like other poets.

source_text:

source_text:

Or am in effect means bal ‘rather’ are they a rebellious lot? because of their obstinacy.

hype_questions: Do people's understanding prompt them to say this paradoxical statement?

They accuse someone of being a sorcerer, poet, soothsayer, or madman in reality.

source_text:
Verse: Or do they say, “He made this ˹Quran˺ up!”? In fact, they have no faith.

hype_questions: Does God create the Quran?
Is the Quran created by humans?
Can humans create something as perfect as the Quran?
propositions: God does not create the Quran.
The Quran is not created by humans.
Humans do not have the ability to create something as perfect as the Quran.

source_text:
Verse: Let them then produce something like it, if what they say is true!

Tafsir: Then let them bring a concocted discourse like it if they are truthful in what they say.

hype_questions: Can someone create something similar to this if their words are true?
What would happen if someone claims to be truthful but is not?

propositions: If someone claims to be truthful, they should be able to produce evidence or a similar discourse.
Truthfulness is not just about saying something, it's also about following through on one's actions and words.

source_text:
Verse: Or were they created by nothing, or are they ˹their own˺ creators?

Tafsir: Or were they created out of nothing? that is without a Creator. Or are they the creators? of themselves. It makes no sense for a created thing to have no creator nor can a thing that will cease to existent have the power to create. There must be a Creator of them and that is God the One so why do they not affirm His Oneness and believe in His Messenger and His Book?

hype_questions: Do humans have the power to create themselves?
Can a created thing truly have no creator?
Why do people not affirm God's Oneness and believe in His Messenger?
propositions: Humans were either created out of nothing or are their own creators.
A created thing cannot have no creator, nor can something that will cease to exist have the power to create.
There must be a Creator of humans, which is God, and yet many do not affirm His Oneness and believe in His Messenger.

source_text:
Verse: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? In fact, they have no firm belief ˹in Allah˺.

Tafsir: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Nor can any but God the Creator have created them so why do they not worship Him? Nay but they are not certain of Him for otherwise they would have believed in His Prophet.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's creation?
Why do people not worship their Creator?
How can one be certain of God's existence?
propositions: The heavens and the earth were created by God.
Only God, the Creator, has the power to create.
People should worship their Creator.
One cannot be certain of God's existence without faith in His Prophet.

source_text:
Verse: Or do they possess the treasuries of your Lord, or are they in control ˹of everything˺?

Tafsir: Or do they possess the treasuries of your Lord? in the way of prophethood provision and other matters so that they are able to assign what they will exclusively to whom they will? Or are they the ones in control? or are they the mighty ones who hold sway? the verb from musaytirūna is saytara similar in root form to baytara ‘to practice veterinary medicine’ or bayqara ‘to corrupt’ ‘to ruin’.

hype_questions: Do they have the power to decide who gets what?
Can they control everything?
Are they in charge of their own destiny?
propositions: They possess treasuries of your Lord for prophethood provision and other matters.
They are able to assign what they will exclusively to whom they will.

Verse: those who avoid major sins and shameful deeds, despite ˹stumbling on˺ minor sins. Surely your Lord is infinite in forgiveness. He knew well what would become of you as He created you from the earth So do not ˹falsely˺ elevate yourselves. He knows best who is ˹truly˺ righteous.

Tafsir: Those who avoid grave sins and abominations excepting lesser offences that is minor sins such as a look a kiss or a touch this constitutes a discontinuous exception in other words the meaning is but lesser offences are forgiven by the avoidance of grave sins. Truly your Lord is of vast forgiveness for such lesser sins and for accepting repentance. The following was revealed regarding those who used to say ‘What of our prayers our fasting and our pilgrimage!’. He knows you best from the time when He produced you from the earth that is to say when He created your father Adam from dust and when you were hidden fetuses ajinna is the plural of janīn in the bellies of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves do not praise yourselves that is in admiration; but if it is done in recognition of God’s grace then that is fine. He knows best those who are God-fearing.

God is infinite in forgiveness and knows best who is truly righteous.
Avoiding grave sins and abominations except for lesser offenses constitutes a means of forgiveness.
Human beings should not elevate themselves in pride but rather acknowledge God's grace.
God created humans from dust, including Adam, and knows their innermost thoughts since conception.

Verse: We unleashed upon them a storm of stones. As for ˹the believers of˺ Lot’s family, We delivered them before dawn

Tafsir: Indeed We unleashed upon them a squall of pebbles a wind hurling at them pebbles namely small stones a single one of these being no larger than the palm of the hand and they were destroyed; all except the family of Lot namely his two daughters together with him whom We delivered at dawn from among the dawns the morning time of an unspecified day had a specific day been meant for that mentioned dawn it sahar would have been treated as a diptote instead of the declined form saharin being a definite noun derived from al-sahar for with definite nouns one ought to use the preceding definite article al. So was the squall unleashed at first with the family of Lot still there? There are two opinions regarding this in the case of the former that it was unleashed upon them including the family of Lot the exception is understood as a continuous one while in the case of the latter opinion that they were delivered before the squall the exception is understood as a discontinuous one even if it ‘the family of Lot’ is actually subsumed by the collective noun ‘the people of Lot’ and so they were delivered as a kindness from God;

source_text:
Verse: Now, if you are not subject to Our Will ˹as you claim˺,

Tafsir: why then if you are not going to face a reckoning if you are not going to be requited by your being resurrected in other words why then if you are not going to be resurrected as you claim

source_text:
Verse: bring that soul back, if what you say is true.

Tafsir: do you not bring it back why do you not restore the spirit to the body after it has reached the throat if you are truthful? in what you claim the second law-lā ‘why … if’ is repeated to emphasise the first one; idhā ‘when’ is an adverbial particle qualifying tarji‘ūna ‘bring it back’ to which both conditions are semantically connected. The meaning is ‘Why do you not bring it back when in repudiating resurrection you are being truthful in this repudiation?’ That is to say ‘Let death also be repudiated as impossible in its case just as you claim that resurrection is impossible’.

hype_questions: Can we truly deny the possibility of both death and resurrection?
propositions: You do not bring back the soul if you are truthful about repudiating resurrection.
Death should also be considered impossible, just like resurrection.

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, for He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God that is to say all things exalt Him as being transcendent thus the lām of li’Llāhi is extra; mā ‘all that’ is used instead of min ‘all who’ in order to indicate what is the predominant sc. non-rational beings; and He is the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His actions.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's transcendence?

God is transcendent and exalted above all existence.
Allah is the Mighty in His kingdom.
Allah is the Wise in His actions.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And He is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; He gives life through His act of creation and He brings death thereafter and He has power over all things.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate source of creation?

propositions: Allah belongs to the kingdom of the heavens and the earth.
Allah gives life through His act of creation.
Allah brings death thereafter.

source_text:
Verse: He is the First and the Last, the Most High and Most Near, and He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

Tafsir: He is the First preceding everything but without His having any beginning and the Last succeeding everything but without His having any end and the Manifest through the proofs for Him and the Hidden from the perception of the senses and He has knowledge of all things.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's existence?

propositions: Allah is the First and has no beginning.
Allah is the Last and has no end.
Allah possesses perfect knowledge of all things.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, For Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.

Tafsir: It is He Who created the heavens and the earth in six days of the days of this world the first of which being Sunday and the last of which Friday then presided upon the Throne ‘arsh denotes the kursī a presiding that was befitting of Him. He knows what enters the earth of rain and dead creatures and what issues from it of vegetation and minerals and what comes down from the heaven in the way of mercy and chastisement and what ascends in it of righteous deeds and evil ones. And He is with you by virtue of His knowledge wherever you may be; and God is Seer of what you do.

hype_questions: What is the duration of Allah's creation of the heavens and the earth?
How does Allah preside upon His Throne?
Is Allah aware of all that happens on earth?
propositions: Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days.
The first day of creation is Sunday, and the last day is Friday.
Allah presides upon His Throne 'Arsh.
Allah knows what enters and issues from the earth, including rain, dead creatures, vegetation, minerals, mercy, chastisement, righteous deeds, and evil deeds.
Allah is with believers wherever they may be due to His knowledge.
God is Seer of all actions.

source_text:
Verse: To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And to Allah all matters are returned.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate authority behind creation?

source_text:
Verse: He merges the night into day and the day into night. And He knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.

Tafsir: He makes the night pass into He makes it enter the day so that it increases while the night diminishes and makes the day pass into the night so that it increases while the day diminishes. And He is Knower of what is in the breasts of what it contains of secrets and convictions.

hype_questions: What is the nature of time in Islam?

The night passes into day, increasing its duration while diminishing the day's duration.
The day passes into night, increasing its duration while diminishing the night's duration.
Allah is aware of what is in the hearts of believers and non-believers alike.

source_text:
Verse: Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and donate from what He has entrusted you with. So those of you who believe and donate will have a mighty reward.

Tafsir: Believe adhere to belief in God and His Messenger and expend in the way of God out of that over which He has made you successors out of the wealth of those mentioned whom you have succeeded for you will be succeeded in this wealth by those who will come after you this was revealed at the time of the ‘hardship’ campaign the campaign of Tabūk. For those of you who believe and expend — an allusion to ‘Uthmān b. ‘Affān may God be pleased with him — will have a great reward.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe and donate?
How will I be rewarded for my charity?
What does it mean to succeed in wealth?
propositions: Believe in Allah and His Messenger.
Donate from what Allah has entrusted you with.
Those who believe and donate will have a mighty reward.

source_text:
Verse: Why do you not believe in Allah while the Messenger is inviting you to have faith in your Lord, although He has already taken your covenant, if you will ever believe.

Tafsir: And why should you not believe — an address to the disbelievers — in other words there is nothing to prevent you from believing in God when the Messenger is calling you to believe in your Lord and a pledge has been taken from you reading it as ukhidha mīthāqukum; otherwise akhadha mīthāqakum ‘He has taken a pledge from you’ concerning it — that is to say God took this pledge from you in the world of atoms when He made them bear witness against themselves ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said ‘Yea indeed’ Q. 7172 — if you are believers? that is to say if your intention is to believe in Him then apply yourselves to this duty of faith.

hype_questions: What is the nature of faith in Islam?
How does Allah take a pledge from believers?
What is the significance of believing in one's Lord?
propositions: The Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord.
God has taken a pledge from you in the world of atoms when He made them bear witness against themselves 'Am I not your Lord?'
If your intention is to believe in Him, then apply yourselves to this duty of faith.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who sends down clear revelations to His servant to bring you out of darkness and into light. For indeed Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to you.

Tafsir: It is He Who sends down upon His servant clear signs the signs of the Qur’ān that He may bring you forth from the darkness from disbelief to the light to faith. For truly God is Kind Merciful to you in bringing you forth from disbelief to faith.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of receiving clear revelations from Allah?
How does Allah bring people out of darkness and into light?
What is the ultimate goal of faith in Islam?
propositions: Allah sends down clear revelations to His servant.
These revelations are signs of the Qur’ān that bring people forth from disbelief to faith.
God is Kind and Merciful to you in bringing you forth from disbelief to faith.

source_text:
Verse: And why should you not spend in the cause of Allah, while Allah is the ˹sole˺ inheritor of the heavens and the earth? Those of you who donated and fought before the victory ˹over Mecca˺ are unparalleled. They are far greater in rank than those who donated and fought afterwards. Yet Allah has promised each a fine reward. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: And why should you after having embraced faith not allā the nūn of an an-lā has been assimilated here with the lām of lā expend in the way of God when to God belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth with all that they comprise so that He will eventually receive all your wealth but without the reward for having expended of it for His cause as opposed to if you had expended and had hence been rewarded. Not equal to the rest of you are those of you who expended and fought before the victory at Mecca. Such are greater in rank than those who expended and fought afterwards. Yet to each of the two groups a variant reading for wa-kullan ‘yet to each’ has nominative wa-kullun as a subject God has promised the best reward Paradise. And God is Aware of what you do and will requite you for it accordingly.

hype_questions: What happens to the wealth of those who spend in the cause of Allah?
How does Allah reward those who fought and donated before the victory over Mecca?
What is the difference between the rewards of those who spent and fought before and after the victory?
propositions: Allah is the sole inheritor of the heavens and the earth.
Those who donated and fought before the victory are unparalleled in rank.
God has promised each a fine reward.
To spend in the cause of Allah means that one's wealth will eventually belong to God.
The reward for spending in the cause of Allah is not equal to the reward for spending afterwards.
Paradise is the best reward for those who spent and fought before the victory.

source_text:
Verse: Who is it that will lend to Allah a good loan which Allah will multiply ˹many times over˺ for them, and they will have an honourable reward?

Tafsir: Who is it that will lend God by expending his wealth in the way of God a goodly loan goodly by virtue of his expending it for God’s sake so that He may multiply it fa-yudā‘ifahu may also be read fa-yuda‘‘ifahu for him from tenfold up to more than seven hundredfold —as stated in sūrat al-Baqara Q. 2261 and so that there may be for him in addition to the multiplied reward a generous reward coupled with satisfaction and prosperity.

hype_questions: What is the nature of a good loan to Allah?
How does Allah reward those who lend to Him a good loan?
What are the benefits of lending to Allah a good loan?
propositions: Whoever lends to Allah a good loan will have that loan multiplied many times over.
The reward for lending to Allah a good loan includes a generous reward, coupled with satisfaction and prosperity.
Lending to Allah a good loan is an act of expending one's wealth in the way of Allah.

source_text:
Verse: On that Day you will see believing men and women with their light shining ahead of them and on their right. ˹They will be told,˺ “Today you have good news of Gardens, under which rivers flow, ˹for you˺ to stay in forever. This is ˹truly˺ the ultimate triumph.”

Tafsir: Mention the day when you will see the believing men and believing women with their light shining forth before them in front of them and it will also be on their right and it will be said to them ‘Good tidings for you on this day Gardens that is to say enter them underneath which rivers flow wherein you will abide. That is the great success’.

hype_questions: What are the Gardens that believers will enter in Paradise?
Will the rivers flow forever in the Gardens of Paradise?
What is the ultimate triumph for believers?
propositions: On the Day of Judgment, believing men and women will see their light shining ahead of them.
Believers will be told that they have good news of Gardens under which rivers flow.
The Gardens are a place where believers will abide forever.
This is truly the ultimate triumph for believers.

source_text:
Verse: On that Day hypocrite men and women will beg the believers, “Wait for us so that we may have some of your light.” It will be said ˹mockingly˺, “Go back ˹to the world˺ and seek a light ˹there˺!” Then a ˹separating˺ wall with a gate will be erected between them. On the near side will be grace and on the far side will be torment.

Tafsir: The day when the hypocrites men and women will say to those who believe ‘Look at us unzurūnā a variant reading has anzirūnā meaning ‘Give us a chance’ that we may glean something of your light!’ It will be said to them in mockery of them ‘Step back and seek light!’ So they step back then there will be set up between them and the believers a wall — this is said to be the wall of ‘the Heights’ cf. Q. 746 — with a gate the inner side of which contains mercy the side of the believers and the outer side of which the side of the hypocrites faces toward the chastisement.

hype_questions: What will happen to those who pretend to be believers but are actually hypocrites on the day of judgment?
How will the hypocrites be treated in comparison to the believers on that day?
What is the nature of the wall and gate mentioned in the Quranic verse?
propositions: On the Day of Judgment, hypocrites will beg believers for a chance to experience some of their light.
The hypocrites will be told to step back and seek light elsewhere.
A wall with a gate will be erected between the hypocrites and believers, with mercy on one side and torment on the other.

source_text:
Verse: The tormented will cry out to those graced, “Were we not with you?” They will reply, “Yes ˹you were˺. But you chose to be tempted ˹by hypocrisy˺, ˹eagerly˺ awaited ˹our demise˺, doubted ˹the truth˺, and were deluded by false hopes until Allah’s decree ˹of your death˺ came to pass. And ˹so˺ the Chief Deceiver deceived you about Allah.

Tafsir: They will call out to them ‘Did we not use to be with you?’ upon the path of obedience. They will say ‘Yes indeed! But you caused your souls to fall into temptation by engaging in hypocrisy and you awaited reversals of fortune for the believers and you doubted you were uncertain about the religion of Islam and false hopes greedy desires deceived you until God’s ordinance death came; and the Deceiver Satan deceived you concerning God.

hype_questions: Did we not use to be with you?
What is the nature of hypocrisy in Islam?
How can one avoid being deceived by false hopes?
propositions: They will cry out to those graced, 'Were we not with you?'
You chose to be tempted by hypocrisy eagerly.
Doubt the truth and were deluded by false hopes until Allah's decree of your death came to pass.
And so the Chief Deceiver deceived you about Allah.

source_text:
Verse: So Today no ransom will be accepted from you ˹hypocrites˺, nor from the disbelievers. Your home is the Fire—it is the ˹only˺ fitting place for you. What an evil destination!”

Tafsir: So on this day no ransom will be taken from you read tu’khadhu or yu’khadhu nor from those who disbelieved. Your abode will be the Fire it will be your guardian it is the place truly deserving of you and an evil destination!’ it is.

hype_questions: What happens to those who are taken hostage by Allah?
Will anyone be able to ransom themselves from the consequences of their actions?
What is the ultimate destination for those who reject Allah's message?
propositions: No ransom will be accepted from you.
Your home is the Fire.
The Fire is the place truly deserving of you.

source_text:
Verse: Has the time not yet come for believers’ hearts to be humbled at the remembrance of Allah and what has been revealed of the truth, and not be like those given the Scripture before—˹those˺ who were spoiled for so long that their hearts became hardened. And many of them are ˹still˺ rebellious.

Tafsir: Is it not time for those who believe — this was revealed concerning the matter of the Companions of the Prophet who had been overindulging in jest that their hearts should be humbled to the remembrance of God and to what has been revealed read as nuzzila; or read nazala ‘what has come down’ of the truth the Qur’ān and that they should not be lā yakūnū is a supplement to takhsha‘a ‘be humbled’ like those who were given the Scripture before? namely the Jews and the Christians. For the stretch of time the interval extending from them back to the time of the sending of the last of their prophets was too long for them and so their hearts became hardened unyielding to the remembrance of God and many of them are immoral.

hype_questions: Will believers' hearts be humbled at the remembrance of Allah?
Can those who were given the Scripture before be like believers in terms of humility?
Why do many of them remain rebellious?
propositions: Believers' hearts should be humbled at the remembrance of Allah and what has been revealed.
Those who were given the Scripture before have hardened hearts due to their prolonged exposure to it.
Many of those who were given the Scripture before are immoral.

source_text:
Verse: Know that Allah revives the earth after its death. We have certainly made the signs clear for you so perhaps you will understand.

Tafsir: Know — an address to the believers just mentioned — that God revives the earth after its death by bringing forth vegetation and likewise He is able to do with your hearts restoring them to humbleness. We have certainly made clear for you the signs that testify to Our power with this mentioned example and others that perhaps you may understand.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's power in reviving the earth?
How does Allah restore human hearts to humility?
What other signs has Allah revealed to demonstrate His power?
propositions: Allah revives the earth after its death.
Allah brings forth vegetation as part of this process.
Allah can restore human hearts to humbleness.
The signs of Allah's power have been made clear for believers.
Believers may understand these signs through reflection.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those men and women who give in charity and lend to Allah a good loan will have it multiplied for them, and they will have an honourable reward.

Tafsir: Indeed men who give voluntary alms al-mussaddiqīna derives from the infinitive al-tasadduq ‘to give voluntary alms’; the tā’ of the original mutasaddiqīna has been assimilated with the sād and women who give voluntary alms a variant reading for both has the softened form with a single sād musaddiqīna and musaddiqāti which derives from al-tasdīq ‘to affirm the truth of’ ‘to believe in’ and those of them who have lent God a goodly loan this refers back to both the men and women with the masculine plural of predominance; the supplementing of a verb aqradū ‘who lent’ to a noun of action al-mussaddiqāt at the point of the relative clause of the al- is because in that position it the noun functions as a verb; the mention of the ‘loan’ together with its qualification ‘goodly’ after the mention of ‘the giving of voluntary alms’ is intended to define it it will be multiplied yudā‘afu is also read as yuda‘‘afu namely their loan will multiplied for them and they will have a generous reward.

hype_questions: What happens to those who give in charity and lend to Allah a good loan?
How will their voluntary alms be rewarded?
What is the outcome for those who believe in the truth of God's goodness?
propositions: Those who give in charity will have it multiplied.
Men and women who give voluntary alms will receive a generous reward.
Their loan will be multiplied for them.

source_text:
Verse: ˹As for˺ those who believe in Allah and His messengers, it is they who are ˹truly˺ the people of truth. And the martyrs, with their Lord, will have their reward and their light. But ˹as for˺ those who disbelieve and reject Our signs, it is they who will be the residents of the Hellfire.

Tafsir: And those who believe in God and His messengers — they are the truthful al-siddīqūna those who go to the greatest lengths to be truthful and the witnesses with their Lord against the deniers of all communities; they will have their reward and their light. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs those signs that testify to the truth of Our Oneness — they will be the inhabitants of Hell-fire.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe in Allah and His messengers?
How do martyrs receive their reward and light?
What happens to those who disbelieve and reject Our signs?
propositions: Those who believe in Allah and His messengers are the truthful ones.
Martyrs will have their reward and their light with their Lord.
Those who disbelieve and deny Our signs will be the inhabitants of Hell-fire.

source_text:
Verse: Know that this worldly life is no more than play, amusement, luxury, mutual boasting, and competition in wealth and children. This is like rain that causes plants to grow, to the delight of the planters. But later the plants dry up and you see them wither, then they are reduced to chaff. And in the Hereafter there will be either severe punishment or forgiveness and pleasure of Allah, whereas the life of this world is no more than the delusion of enjoyment.

Tafsir: Know that the life of this world is merely play and diversion and glitter the frequent adornment of oneself and mutual vainglory in respect of wealth and children that is preoccupation with such things — but as for acts of obedience and incentives thereto these are the concerns of the Hereafter; as the likeness of that is to say it in the manner in which you admire it and in the manner in which it will disappear is as the likeness of rain whose vegetation which results from this rain the disbelievers the sowers admire; but then it withers it becomes dried-up and you see it turn yellow then it becomes chaff scatters vanishing with the winds. And in the Hereafter there is a severe chastisement for those who prefer this world to it and forgiveness from God and beatitude for those who have not preferred this world to it; and the life of this world that is to say the comfort enjoyed in it is but the comfort of delusion.

hype_questions: What happens to the worldly life after its fleeting nature is revealed?
How does one's preference for this world affect their fate in the Hereafter?
What is the true comfort of the life of this world?
propositions: The life of this world is play, amusement, luxury, mutual boasting, and competition.
The life of this world is like rain that causes plants to grow, but later they wither and become chaff.
The life of this world is a delusion of enjoyment.
Acts of obedience are the concerns of the Hereafter.
In the Hereafter, there will be severe punishment for those who prefer this world and forgiveness for those who do not.
The comfort enjoyed in this world is but the comfort of delusion.

source_text:
Verse: ˹So˺ compete with one another for forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. This is the favour of Allah. He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty.

Tafsir: Vie with one another for forgiveness from your Lord and a garden the breadth of which is as the breadth of the heaven and the earth if one were placed at the end of the other prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers. That is the bounty of God which He gives to whomever He will and God is dispenser of tremendous bounty.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe in Allah and His messengers?
How does Allah grant forgiveness to whomever He wills?
What is the nature of God's bounty?
propositions: Compete with one another for forgiveness from your Lord.
A Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth is prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers.
Allah grants forgiveness to whoever He wills.
God gives tremendous bounty to whomever He wills.

source_text:
Verse: No calamity ˹or blessing˺ occurs on earth or in yourselves without being ˹written˺ in a Record before We bring it into being. This is certainly easy for Allah.

Tafsir: No affliction befalls in the earth by way of drought for example or in yourselves such as illness or the loss of a child but it is in a Book meaning the Preserved Tablet al-lawh al-mahfūz before We bring it about before We create it — the same is said to be true of God’s graces — that is indeed easy for God

hype_questions: Does Allah have control over all events in the universe?
Can human beings influence their fate?
Is God's will always carried out?
propositions: No calamity occurs on earth or in humans without being written in a Record before it is brought into existence.
Allah's power and knowledge are all-encompassing, including the occurrence of natural disasters and human suffering.
God's grace and blessings are also predestined and cannot be changed.

source_text:
Verse: ˹We let you know this˺ so that you neither grieve over what you have missed nor boast over what He has granted you. For Allah does not like whoever is arrogant, boastful—

Tafsir: so that you may not kay-lā kay makes a verb subjunctive with the same sense as an as in an-lā ‘so that … not’ that is to say God informs you of this so that you may not grieve for what escapes you nor exult with a wanton exultation rather an exultation that is followed by a thanksgiving for the grace at what He has given you read thus as ātākum; or read as atākum meaning ‘at what has come to you from Him’. For God does not like any swaggering braggart swaggering in arrogance because of what he has been given boastful of it to people;

hype_questions: What happens when Allah informs us of something?
How does Allah feel about those who are arrogant and boastful?
What is the right attitude to have when we receive something from Allah?
propositions: Allah informs you of this so that you may not grieve for what escapes you.
God does not like whoever is arrogant, boastful—
At what has come to you from Him.

source_text:
Verse: those who are stingy and promote stinginess among people. And whoever turns away ˹should know that˺ Allah ˹alone˺ is truly the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

Tafsir: such as are niggardly in their duties and bid people to be niggardly in these too against such there is a severe threat of chastisement. And whoever turns away from what is his duty still God He is indeed huwa ‘He’ is a separating pronoun; a variant reading drops it the Independent without need of anyone other than Him the Praiser of His friends.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of promoting stinginess among people?
How does Allah respond to those who turn away from their duties?
What is the nature of God's independence and praise?
propositions: Those who are stingy and promote stinginess among people will face severe chastisement.
Allah is the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy, and independent without need of anyone else.
God is a separating pronoun that refers to Himself as 'He'.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and with them We sent down the Scripture and the balance ˹of justice˺ so that people may administer justice. And We sent down iron with its great might, benefits for humanity, and means for Allah to prove who ˹is willing to˺ stand up for Him and His messengers without seeing Him. Surely Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.

Tafsir: We have verily sent Our messengers the angels to prophets with clear signs with the definitive proofs and We revealed with them the Scripture and the Balance justice so that mankind may uphold justice. And We sent down iron We caused it to be extracted from mineral ores wherein is great might with which one may wage battle and many uses for mankind and so that God may know a knowledge of direct vision li-ya‘lama’Llāhu is a supplement to li-yaqūma’l-nāsu ‘so that mankind may uphold’ those who help Him by helping to uphold His religion through the use of instruments of war made of metal and otherwise and His messengers through the Unseen bi’l-ghaybi a circumstantial qualifier referring to the suffixed pronoun hā’ ‘Him’ of yansuruhu ‘who aid Him’ that is to say while He God is not seen by them in this world. Ibn ‘Abbās said ‘They help Him even though they do not see Him’ yansurūnahu wa-lā yubsirūnahu. Assuredly God is Strong Mighty without any need of being helped but such help benefits those who proffer it.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of sending down iron with great might?
How does Allah prove who stands up for Him and His messengers without seeing them?
What benefits do humans gain from using instruments of war made of metal?
propositions: We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and revealed the Scripture and the Balance of justice.
God caused iron to be extracted from mineral ores for its great might and many uses.
Those who help God by helping to uphold His religion through the use of instruments of war made of metal aid Him.
Assuredly, God is Strong Mighty without any need of being helped but such help benefits those who proffer it.

source_text:
Verse: And indeed, We sent Noah and Abraham and reserved prophethood and revelation for their descendants. Some of them are ˹rightly˺ guided, while most are rebellious.

Tafsir: And verily We sent Noah and Abraham and We ordained among their seed prophethood and the Scripture meaning the four Books the Torah the Gospel the Psalms and the Furqān all of which have been revealed among the seed of Abraham; and some of them are rightly guided and many of them are immoral.

hype_questions: What is the significance of prophethood and revelation in Islamic theology?
How do some descendants of Abraham receive guidance, while others are immoral?
What role do the four Books (Torah, Gospel, Psalms, Furqān) play in Islamic scripture?
propositions: We sent Noah and Abraham as prophets.
Prophethood and revelation were ordained among the descendants of Abraham.
Some descendants of Abraham are guided, while most are immoral.
The four Books (Torah, Gospel, Psalms, Furqān) have been revealed among the seed of Abraham.

source_text:
Verse: Then in the footsteps of these ˹prophets˺, We sent Our messengers, and ˹after them˺ We sent Jesus, son of Mary, and granted him the Gospel, and instilled compassion and mercy into the hearts of his followers. As for monasticism, they made it up—We never ordained it for them—only seeking to please Allah, yet they did not ˹even˺ observe it strictly. So We rewarded those of them who were faithful. But most of them are rebellious.

Tafsir: Then We sent to follow in their footsteps Our messengers and We sent to follow Jesus son of Mary and We gave him the Gospel and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him kindness and mercy. But as for monasticism namely abstention from women and seclusion in monasteries they invented it an innovation on their part — We had not prescribed it for them We did not enjoin them to it; but they took it on — only seeking God’s beatitude. Yet they did not observe it with due observance for many of them abandoned it and rejected the religion of Jesus and embraced the religion of their then king. However many of them did remain upon the religion of Jesus and they believed in our Prophet when he came. So We gave those of them who believed in him their reward; but many of them are immoral.

hype_questions: Did Jesus receive the Gospel from Allah?
What is the true meaning of monasticism in Islam?
How did the followers of Jesus respond to the message of Allah?
propositions: We sent Our messengers after the prophets.
Jesus son of Mary was granted the Gospel by Allah.
Allah instilled compassion and mercy into the hearts of his followers.
Monasticism was invented by humans as an innovation, not prescribed by Allah.
Many of those who followed Jesus abandoned monasticism and rejected his religion.
Those who believed in Jesus were rewarded by Allah.
Most of those who followed Jesus are immoral.

source_text:
Verse: O people of faith! Fear Allah and believe in His Messenger. ˹And˺ He will grant you a double share of His mercy, provide you with a light to walk in ˹on Judgment Day˺, and forgive you. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: O you who believe in Jesus fear God and believe in His Messenger Muhammad (s) and Jesus and He will give you a twofold portion share of His mercy for your belief in both prophets; and He will assign for you a light by which you will walk across the Path over Hell and into Paradise and forgive you; for God is Forgiving Merciful;

hype_questions: What is the reward for believing in Allah's prophets?
How will Allah guide us on Judgment Day?
Can we be forgiven by Allah?
propositions: Fear Allah and believe in His Messenger.
Allah grants a double share of His mercy to those who believe in both prophets.
God assigns a light for guidance across the Path over Hell and into Paradise.
God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: ˹This is so˺ that the People of the Book ˹who deny the Prophet˺ may know that they do not have any control over Allah’s grace, and that all grace is in Allah’s Hands. He grants it to whoever He wills. For Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty.

Tafsir: So that the People of the Scripture the Torah — those who did not believe in Muhammad (s) — may know in other words I inform you of this so that they the People of the Scripture may know that a of a-llā is softened in place of the hardened form an-lā its subject being the pronoun of the matter that is to say understand it as being annahum they have no power over anything of God’s bounty contrary to their claims that they are God’s beloved and those who deserve His beatitude and that all bounty is in God’s hand; He gives it to whomever He will and hence He has given the believers in the Prophet among them their reward twofold as stated above; and God is dispenser of tremendous bounty.

hype_questions: Does Allah grant His blessings to whoever He wills?
Can humans control Allah's grace?
What is the nature of Allah's bounty?
propositions: Allah grants His blessings to whoever He wills.
Humans have no power over Allah's grace.
Allah's bounty is in His hands.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, Allah has heard the argument of the woman who pleaded with you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning her husband, and appealed to Allah. Allah has heard your exchange. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

Tafsir: God has certainly heard the words of her who disputes with you her who consults you O Prophet concerning her husband who has repudiated her by zihār — he had said to her ‘You are to me as untouchable as the back of my mother’.
