She asked the Prophet s about this and he told her that she was thenceforth forbidden to him as was customary among them at the time of Jāhiliyya namely that repudiation by zihār results in permanent separation. She was Khawla bt. Tha‘laba and he was Aws b. al-Sāmit — and complains to God of her being alone and of her impoverishment while having young children whom if she were to leave with him they would go astray but whom if they remained with her would go hungry. And God hears your conversation your consulting. Assuredly God is Hearer Seer He is Knower.

hype_questions: Does God intervene in human disputes?
Can a woman's rights be violated through 'zihār'?
How does God respond to the pleas of those who are wronged?
propositions: Allah has heard the words of her who disputes with you concerning her husband.
Repudiation by zihār results in permanent separation.
God hears your conversation and responds accordingly.

source_text:
Verse: Those of you who ˹sinfully˺ divorce their wives by comparing them to their mothers ˹should know that˺ their wives are in no way their mothers. None can be their mothers except those who gave birth to them. What they say is certainly detestable and false. Yet Allah is truly Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving.

Tafsir: Those of you who repudiate their wives by zihār yazzahharūna is actually yatazahharūna in which the tā’ has been assimilated with the zā’; a variant reading has yazzāharūna and still another has yuzāhirūna similar in form to yuqātilūna; the same applies for the second instance of this verb below they are not their mothers; their mothers are only those who read allā’ī or without the final long yā’ allā’i gave birth to them and indeed they in repudiating them by zihār utter indecent words and a calumny a lie. Yet assuredly God is Pardoning Forgiving to the one who repudiates by zihār through an atonement which he must offer.

hype_questions: What is the meaning of zihār in Islamic law?
Can a husband divorce his wife by comparing her to her mother?
How does Allah respond to those who repudiate their wives through zihār?
propositions: Those who repudiate their wives by zihār are uttering indecent words and a calumny.
Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them.
God is Pardoning Forgiving to the one who repudiates by zihār through an atonement.

source_text:
Verse: Those who divorce their wives in this manner, then ˹wish to˺ retract what they said, must free a slave before they touch each other. This ˹penalty˺ is meant to deter you. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: And those who repudiate their wives by zihār and then go back on what they have said instead doing the opposite of this and retaining the woman divorced by zihār that which is contrary to the purpose of zihār in which a woman is characterised as being forbidden — then the penalty for them is the setting free of a slave an obligation upon him before they touch one another in sexual intercourse. By this you are being admonished; and God is Aware of what you do.

hype_questions: What happens if someone retracts their divorce statement after initially repudiating their wife?
Can a person who has divorced their wife through zihār still retain the woman and have sex with her?
Why is freeing a slave before reuniting with one's spouse considered a penalty?
propositions: Those who divorce their wives in this manner must free a slave before they touch each other.
The penalty for repudiating a wife through zihār and then going back on what was said is the setting free of a slave an obligation upon him before they touch one another in sexual intercourse.
God is Aware of what you do.

source_text:
Verse: But if the husband cannot afford this, let him then fast two consecutive months before the couple touch each other. But if he is unable ˹to fast˺, then let him feed sixty poor people. This is to re-affirm your faith in Allah and His Messenger. These are the limits set by Allah. And the disbelievers will suffer a painful punishment.

Tafsir: And he who cannot find the wherewithal to set free a slave then his redemption shall be the fasting of two successive months before they touch one another. And if he is unable to fast then the redemption shall be the feeding of sixty needy persons as an obligation upon him that is before they touch one another understanding the unrestricted prescription as having the same restriction as the restricted one. For every needy person he should give one mudd measure of the principal food of the town. This namely lightening of the atonement is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger. And these namely the rulings mentioned are God’s bounds; and for the rejecters of them there is a painful chastisement.

hype_questions: What are the alternatives to freeing a slave when financially unable?
How does fasting two consecutive months serve as redemption for not being able to free a slave?
What is the significance of feeding sixty needy persons as an obligation before touching another person?
propositions: If a husband cannot afford to set free a slave, he should fast two consecutive months before they touch each other.
If a husband is unable to fast, he should feed sixty poor people as an obligation before they touch each other.
The fasting of two successive months serves as redemption for not being able to free a slave.
Feeding sixty needy persons is an obligation before touching another person.
These rulings are God's bounds and serve to re-affirm faith in Allah and His Messenger.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who defy Allah and His Messenger will be debased, just like those before them. We have certainly sent down clear revelations. And the disbelievers will suffer a humiliating punishment.

Tafsir: Indeed those who oppose God and His Messenger will be abased humiliated just as those before them were abased for opposing their messengers. And verily We have revealed clear signs indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger and for those who disbelieve in the signs there is a humiliating chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens to those who oppose God and His Messenger?
Why do disbelievers suffer a humiliating punishment?
How can we trust the signs revealed by Allah?
propositions: Those who defy Allah and His Messenger will be debased.
We have certainly sent down clear revelations.
The disbelievers will suffer a humiliating punishment.

source_text:
Verse: On the Day Allah resurrects them all together, He will then inform them of what they have done. Allah has kept account of it all, while they have forgotten it. For Allah is a Witness over all things.

Tafsir: The day when God will raise them all together He will then inform them of what they did. God has kept count of it while they forgot it. And God is Witness to all things.

hype_questions: What will happen when Allah resurrects us?
Will Allah hold us accountable for our actions?
Can we be forgiven by Allah?
propositions: On the Day Allah resurrects them all together, He will then inform them of what they have done.
Allah has kept account of it all, while they have forgotten it.
For Allah is a Witness over all things.

source_text:
Verse: Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? If three converse privately, He is their fourth. If five, He is their sixth. Whether fewer or more, He is with them wherever they may be. Then, on the Day of Judgment, He will inform them of what they have done. Surely Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

Tafsir: Have you not seen have you not realised that God knows all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth? Not secret conversation of three takes place but He is their fourth companion by virtue of His omniscience nor of five but He is their sixth nor of fewer than that or more but He is with them wherever they may be. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Assuredly God has knowledge of all things.

hype_questions: Does Allah have knowledge of all things?
Is Allah present with humanity wherever they may be?
What will happen to humans on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
If three converse privately, He is their fourth companion by virtue of His omniscience.
Whether fewer or more, He is with them wherever they may be.
Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection.
Assuredly God has knowledge of all things.

source_text:
Verse: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret talks, yet they ˹always˺ return to what they were forbidden from, conspiring in sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you ˹O Prophet˺, they greet you not as Allah greets you, and say to one another, “Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?” Hell is enough for them—they will burn in it. And what an evil destination!

Tafsir: Have you not seen have you not observed those who were forbidden from conversing in secret but then returned to that they had been forbidden and all the while hold secret conversations tainted with sin and plans for enmity and disobedience to the Messenger? These were the Jews whom the Prophet s had forbidden them what they used to do in their secret talks that is their habit of conversing secretly with one another and giving the believers looks in order to cast doubt into their hearts about the faith. And who when they come to you they greet you O Prophet with that with which God never greeted you — namely their saying to the Prophet al-sāmu ‘alayka meaning ‘Death be upon you’ and they say within themselves ‘Why does God not chastise us for what we say?’ in the way of such a greeting and our saying that he is not a prophet if he truly were a prophet. Hell will suffice them! In it they will be made to burn — and what an evil journey’s end! it is.

hype_questions: Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?
propositions: Those who were forbidden from secret talks return to what they were forbidden from, conspiring in sin and aggression.
When they come to you, they greet you not as Allah greets you.
Hell is enough for them—they will burn in it.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! When you converse privately, let it not be for sin, aggression, or disobedience to the Messenger, but let it be for goodness and righteousness. And fear Allah, to Whom you will ˹all˺ be gathered.

Tafsir: O you who believe if you do talk in secret then do not talk in secret sinfully and in enmity and disobedience to the Messenger but talk secretly in piety and fear of God. And fear God to Whom you will be gathered.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of having sinful private conversations?
How can believers maintain piety in their secret discussions?
Who will be gathered on the Day of Judgment?
propositions: Converse privately for goodness and righteousness.
Fear Allah to Whom you will be gathered.
Talk secretly in piety and fear of God.

source_text:
Verse: Secret talks are only inspired by Satan to grieve the believers. Yet he cannot harm them whatsoever except by Allah’s Will. So in Allah let the believers put their trust.

Tafsir: Secret conversations tainted with sin and the like are of the work of Satan a result of his deception that those who believe may end up grieving; but he cannot harm them in any way except God’s leave that is except by His will. And in God let the believers put all their trust.

hype_questions: Can Satan truly harm believers without Allah's permission?
How do secret conversations with sinful elements affect a believer's faith?
What is the ultimate source of protection for believers in their relationships?
propositions: Secret talks are inspired by Satan to grieve believers.
Satan cannot harm believers except by Allah's Will.
Believers should put their trust in Allah.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! When you are told to make room in gatherings, then do so. Allah will make room for you ˹in His grace˺. And if you are told to rise, then do so. Allah will elevate those of you who are faithful, and ˹raise˺ those gifted with knowledge in rank. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: O you who believe when it is said to you ‘Make room’ during the assembly during the assembly convened with the Prophet s or for remembrance so that those arriving to join you may find room to sit al-majlis ‘assembly’ may also be read in the plural al-majālis then make room; God will make room for you in Paradise. And when it is said ‘Rise up’ stand up for prayer or for other good deeds do rise up a variant reading for unshuzū fa’nshuzū has anshizū in both instances sc. anshizū fa’nshizū; God will raise those of you who have faith thereby obeying this command and He will raise those who have been given knowledge by degrees in Paradise. And God is Aware of what you do.

hype_questions: What happens when we make room in gatherings?
How will Allah elevate those of us who are faithful and gifted with knowledge?
Will God raise those who obey His commands?
propositions: When you are told to make room in gatherings, then do so. Allah will make room for you.
If you are told to rise, then do so. Allah will elevate those of you who are faithful, and raise those gifted with knowledge in rank.
Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! When you consult the Messenger privately, give something in charity before your consultation. That is better and purer for you. But if you lack the means, then Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: O you who believe when you converse in secret with the Messenger when you wish to converse with him privately offer some voluntary alms before your secret talk. That is better for you and purer for your sins. But if you find nothing to offer as alms then God is indeed Forgiving of your secret conversation Merciful to you. In other words nothing will be held against you for holding a secret conversation without having offered some voluntary alms beforehand. However He God abrogated this later by saying

hype_questions: What is the recommended practice when consulting with the Messenger privately?
How can one make their private conversation with the Messenger more virtuous?
What happens if one cannot offer alms before a private consultation?
propositions: When consulting the Messenger privately, give something in charity beforehand.
If you lack the means to offer alms, Allah is truly All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.
God abrogated this later by saying

source_text:
Verse: Are you afraid of spending in charity before your private consultations ˹with him˺? Since you are unable to do so, and Allah has turned to you in mercy, then ˹continue to˺ establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: Do you fear read a-ashfaqtum either pronouncing both hamzas fully or by replacing the second one with an alif or not pronouncing it but inserting an alif between the one not unpronounced and the other one or without this insertion poverty when you fear to offer voluntary alms before your secret talks. So as you did not do this giving of voluntary alms and God relented to you waiving this requirement for you maintain prayer and pay the alms and obey God and His Messenger that is to say observe these duties regularly. For God is Aware of what you do.

hype_questions: What happens if I don't give voluntary alms before my private consultations?
How can I fulfill my religious duties when I'm afraid to offer charity?
Will God forgive me if I miss the opportunity to give alms?
propositions: You should establish prayer.
You should pay alms-tax.
You should obey Allah and His Messenger.

source_text:
Verse: Have you not seen those ˹hypocrites˺ who ally themselves with a people with whom Allah is displeased? They are neither with you nor with them. And they swear to lies knowingly.

Tafsir: Have you not regarded have you not seen those who — these being the hypocrites — fraternise with a folk — these being the Jews — at whom God is wrathful? They the hypocrites neither belong with you the believers nor with them the Jews but are suspended in between and they swear falsely in other words saying that they are believers while they know that they are lying in this.

hype_questions: What happens to those who ally themselves with a people that Allah is displeased with?
Can someone be considered a believer when they know they are lying about it?
How do hypocrites behave in relation to their own community and the disapproved group?
propositions: Those who ally themselves with a people that Allah is displeased with are neither with you nor with them.
Hypocrites swear falsely, claiming to be believers when they know they are lying.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Evil indeed is what they do.

Tafsir: God has prepared for them a severe chastisement. Evil indeed is that which they are wont to do in the way of acts of disobedience.

hype_questions: What punishment will Allah prepare for those who disobey Him?
How severe is the chastisement that God has prepared for those who act in disobedience?
What evil deeds are they wont to do in the way of acts of disobedience?
propositions: Allah has prepared a severe punishment.
God has prepared a severe chastisement.
They are wont to do evil deeds in the way of acts of disobedience.

source_text:
Verse: They have made their ˹false˺ oaths as a shield, hindering ˹others˺ from the cause of Allah. So they will suffer a humiliating punishment.

Tafsir: They have taken their oaths as a shield a means of protection for themselves and their possessions and so they bar thereby the believers from the way of God that is from engaging in a struggle against them thereby slaying them and seizing their possessions. So for them there will be a humiliating chastisement.

hype_questions: What happens when people use oaths as protection from the truth?
How do false oaths affect believers and their relationship with God?
What is the consequence of using oaths to hinder others from following God's path?
propositions: They have taken their oaths as a shield.
Their oaths serve as protection for themselves and their possessions.
Believers are barred from the way of God by those who take oaths as protection.
Those who use oaths to hinder others will suffer a humiliating chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Neither their wealth nor children will be of any help to them against Allah whatsoever. It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever.

Tafsir: Neither their possessions nor their children will avail them in any way against God against His chastisement. Those — they are the inhabitants of the Fire wherein they will abide.

hype_questions: What happens to those who rely solely on their wealth and children in the afterlife?
Can possessions or family ties protect someone from Allah's punishment?
What is the ultimate fate of those who are consumed by worldly desires?
propositions: Their wealth will not be of any help against Allah.
Their children will not be of any help against Allah.
Possessions and children will not protect someone from Allah's chastisement.
Those who rely on these things will be the residents of the Fire.
They will abide in the Fire forever.

source_text:
Verse: On the Day Allah resurrects them all, they will ˹falsely˺ swear to Him as they swear to you, thinking they have something to stand on. Indeed, it is they who are the ˹total˺ liars.

Tafsir: Mention the day when God will raise them all together whereupon they will swear to Him that they are believers just as they swear to you now and suppose that they are standing on something beneficial by swearing in Hereafter just as they supposed it to have been beneficial for them in this world. Yet assuredly it is they who are the liars!

hype_questions: What will happen to those who swear falsely on the Day of Resurrection?
Will they truly believe in Allah after death?
Can their false claims in this life be justified by their supposed benefits?
propositions: Allah will resurrect all beings.
They will swear to Allah as they do now, thinking they have a basis for their faith.
However, it is they who are the total liars.

source_text:
Verse: Satan has taken hold of them, causing them to forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of Satan. Surely Satan’s party is bound to lose.

Tafsir: Satan has prevailed upon them by their obedience of him and so he has caused them to forget the remembrance of God. Those are Satan’s confederates his followers. Yet it is indeed Satan’s confederates who are the losers!

hype_questions: What happens when one obeys Satan?
How does Satan's influence affect a person's remembrance of God?
Who are the followers of Satan and what is their ultimate fate?
propositions: Satan has taken hold of them, causing them to forget the remembrance of Allah.
Satan's party is bound to lose.
Satan prevails upon his confederates by their obedience to him.
Those who are Satan's confederates have forgotten the remembrance of God.
Satan's followers are indeed the losers.

source_text:
Verse: ˹As for˺ those who defy Allah and His Messenger, they will definitely be among the most debased.

Tafsir: Indeed those who oppose God and His Messenger — they will be among the most abased the vanquished.

hype_questions: What happens to those who defy Allah?
How do those who oppose God's messenger fare in the end?
Who are the most debased according to Islamic teachings?
propositions: Those who defy Allah and His Messenger will be among the most debased.
Opposition to God and His Messenger results in being among the most abased and vanquished.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has decreed, “I and My messengers will certainly prevail.” Surely Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.

Tafsir: God has inscribed in the Preserved Tablet or it means He has decreed ‘I shall assuredly prevail I and My messengers’ by means of definitive proof or the sword. Truly God is Strong Mighty.

hype_questions: Will Allah and His messengers ultimately triumph?
What is the nature of God's power and might?
How does God ensure the success of His messengers?
propositions: Allah has decreed that He and His messengers will prevail.
God is All-Powerful and Almighty.
God has inscribed in the Preserved Tablet or decreed 'I shall assuredly prevail I and My messengers' by means of definitive proof or the sword.
Truly God is Strong Mighty.

source_text:
Verse: You will never find a people who ˹truly˺ believe in Allah and the Last Day loyal to those who defy Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their parents, children, siblings, or extended family. For those ˹believers˺, Allah has instilled faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Him. He will admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. They are the party of Allah. Indeed, Allah’s party is bound to succeed.

Tafsir: You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving befriending those who oppose God and His Messenger even though they the opposers were their fathers that is to say the believers’ fathers or their sons or their brothers or their clan rather you will find that they intend to do them harm and they fight them over the question of faith as occurred on one occasion with some Companions may God be pleased with them. For those the ones who are not loving of them He has inscribed He has established faith upon their hearts and reinforced them with a spirit a light from Him exalted be He and He will admit them into gardens underneath which rivers flow wherein they will abide God being pleased with them for their obedience of Him and they being pleased with Him because of His reward. Those they are God’s confederates following His command and refraining from what He has forbidden. Assuredly it is God’s confederates who are the successful the winners.

hype_questions: What happens to those who defy Allah and His Messenger?
How do believers overcome opposition from non-believers?
What is the ultimate reward for those who follow Allah's command?
propositions: Allah instills faith in the hearts of believers.
Believers are strengthened with a spirit from Allah.
God is pleased with His confederates and they are pleased with Him.
God's party will succeed because they follow His command and refrain from what He has forbidden.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. For He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifies God that is to say all that is in them exalts Him as being transcendent the lām of li’Llāhi ‘God’ is extra; the use of mā instead of the personal min is meant to indicate a predominance of non-rational beings in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Mighty the Wise in His kingdom and in His actions respectively.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's transcendence?
How does Allah's wisdom manifest in His kingdom and actions?
What is the significance of the use of 'lām' in the phrase 'li'Llāhi'?
propositions: Whatever is in the heavens glorifies Allah.
Whatever is on the earth glorifies God.
All that is in them exalts Him as being transcendent.
The use of mā instead of the personal min indicates a predominance of non-rational beings in the heavens and the earth.
He is the Mighty.
He is the Wise in His kingdom and in His actions respectively.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who expelled the disbelievers of the People of the Book from their homes for ˹their˺ first banishment ˹ever˺. You never thought they would go. And they thought their strongholds would put them out of Allah’s reach. But ˹the decree of˺ Allah came upon them from where they never expected. And He cast horror into their hearts so they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take a lesson ˹from this˺, O  people of insight!

Tafsir: It is He Who expelled those who disbelieved of the People of the Scripture namely the Jews of the Banū al-Nadīr from their homelands from their dwellings at Medina at the first exile that is their exile to Syria the last exile being their banishment to Khaybar by ‘Umar during his caliphate. You did not think O believers that they would go forth and they thought that they would be protected māni‘atuhum is the predicate of an ‘that’ by their fortresses husūnuhum the agent of the verb māni‘atuhum with which the predication is completed from God from His chastisement. But God His command and His chastisement came at them from whence they had not reckoned from whence had never occurred to them from the part of the believers and He cast terror ru‘b or ru‘ub into their hearts by having their chief Ka‘b b. al-Ashraf slain destroying as they did read yukharribūna; or yukhribūna derived from 4th form akhraba their houses in order to take away with them what they valued of wood and so on with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed O you who have eyes!

hype_questions: What is the significance of Allah's banishment of disbelievers from their homes?
How did the disbelievers' strongholds fail to protect them from Allah's chastisement?
What lesson can be learned from the destruction of the disbelievers' houses by both themselves and believers?
propositions: Allah expelled those who disbelieved of the People of the Scripture from their homelands.
The disbelievers thought their strongholds would protect them from Allah's chastisement.
God cast terror into their hearts after slaying Ka‘b b. al-Ashraf.

source_text:
Verse: Had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would have certainly punished them in this world. And in the Hereafter they will suffer the punishment of the Fire.

Tafsir: And had God not prescribed had He not decreed banishment for them departure from their homeland He would have chastised them in this world by having them killed or taken captive as He did with the Jews of Banū Qurayza and in the Hereafter there is for them the chastisement of the Fire.

hype_questions: What would happen to those who are exiled by God?
How will the punishment of the Fire affect those who were banished from their homeland?
Can we learn from the fate of the Jews of Banū Qurayza?
propositions: Had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would have certainly punished them in this world.
And had God not prescribed had He not decreed banishment for them departure from their homeland
He would have chastised them in this world by having them killed or taken captive as He did with the Jews of Banū Qurayza
there is for them the chastisement of the Fire

source_text:
Verse: This is because they defied Allah and His Messenger. And whoever defies Allah, then Allah is truly severe in punishment.

Tafsir: That is because they defied they opposed God and His Messenger; and whoever defies God indeed God is severe in retribution against him.

hype_questions: What happens when someone defies God?
How does God punish those who defy Him?
What is the consequence of opposing God and His Messenger?
propositions: They defied Allah and His Messenger.
Allah is truly severe in punishment.
Whoever defies Allah will face severe punishment.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever palm trees you ˹believers˺ cut down or left standing intact, it was ˹all˺ by Allah’s Will, so that He might disgrace the rebellious.

Tafsir: Whatever palm-trees you cut down O Muslims or left standing on their roots it was by God’s leave He gave you the choice in this matter and in order that by giving you leave to cut them down He might disgrace those who are immoral the Jews in return for their objection that the cutting down of productive trees was deliberate spoiling of the land.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of cutting down palm trees according to Islamic teachings?
How does Allah's will relate to human actions in this context?
What is the significance of disgrace for those who are immoral?
propositions: Whatever palm-trees you cut down or left standing intact, it was by Allah’s Will.
God gave you the choice in this matter.
He might disgrace those who are immoral.

source_text:
Verse: As for the gains Allah has turned over to His Messenger from them—you did not ˹even˺ spur on any horse or camel for such gains. But Allah gives authority to His messengers over whoever He wills. For Allah is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: And whatever spoils God has given to His Messenger from these you did not O Muslims spur for it any min is extra horses or camels that is to say you did not suffer any hardship in securing it but God gives His messengers sway over whomever He will and God has power over all things hence you have no right to any of this booty rather it is exclusively for the Prophet s and those of the four categories mentioned with him in the next verse to be dispensed in accordance with the way in which he used to divide it up such that each would receive a fifth of the fifth and the rest being the Prophet’s s for him to do with as he pleases — thus he gave of it to the Emigrants and three from among the Helpers on account of their poverty.

hype_questions: What is the authority of a messenger from Allah?
How does Allah distribute booty among His messengers?
Who has the right to receive the Prophet's share of the spoils?
propositions: Allah gives authority to His messengers over whoever He wills.
God has power over all things.
The Prophet's share of the spoils is exclusively for him and his companions.

source_text:
Verse: As for gains granted by Allah to His Messenger from the people of ˹other˺ lands, they are for Allah and the Messenger, his close relatives, orphans, the poor, and ˹needy˺ travellers so that wealth may not merely circulate among your rich. Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it. And whatever he forbids you from, leave it. And fear Allah. Surely Allah is severe in punishment.

Tafsir: Whatever spoils God has given to His Messenger from the people of the towns such as al-Safrā’ Wādī al-Qurā and Yanbu‘ belong to God dispensing with it as He will and to the Messenger and to the near of kin the Prophet’s kin from among the Banū Hāshim and the Banū al-Muttālib and the orphans the orphaned children of Muslims those whose parents have died and who are impoverished and the needy those Muslims in need and the traveller the Muslim who may be cut off from all resources on a remote journey in other words they these spoils are the due of the Prophet s and those of the four categories divided up in the way that he used to where each category received a fifth of the fifth with the rest being his the Prophet’s so that these the spoils — this being the justification for the division of these spoils in this way do not kay-lā kay functions like lā with a following implied an sc. an-lā become a thing circulating handed round between the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger gives you of spoils or otherwise take it; and whatever he forbids you abstain from it. And fear God. Surely God is severe in retribution.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of distributing spoils among different categories?
Who are entitled to receive spoils from the Messenger?
Why should one fear Allah in relation to wealth distribution?
propositions: Spoils granted by Allah to His Messenger belong to God and the Messenger, his close relatives, orphans, the poor, and needy travellers.
The Messenger gives you spoils or other things, take them; he forbids you from something, leave it.
Fear Allah, for He is severe in punishment.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Some of the gains will be˺ for poor emigrants who were driven out of their homes and wealth, seeking Allah’s bounty and pleasure, and standing up for Allah and His Messenger. They are the ones true in faith.

Tafsir: At the poor Emigrants li’l-fuqarā’i is semantically connected to an omitted verb that is to say a-‘ajibū ‘What! Do they marvel at the poor Emigrants’ who have been driven away from their homes and their possessions that they should seek bounty from God and beatitude and help God and His Messenger? Those — they are the sincere in their faith.

hype_questions: What are the benefits for those who have been driven out of their homes and wealth?
How do the poor emigrants seek Allah's bounty and pleasure?
What does it mean to stand up for Allah and His Messenger?
propositions: Some of the gains will be for poor emigrants.
The poor Emigrants are driven away from their homes and possessions.
They seek bounty from God and beatitude.
They help God and His Messenger.
Those who have been driven out of their homes and wealth are true in faith.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who had settled in the city and ˹embraced˺ the faith before ˹the arrival of˺ the emigrants, they love whoever immigrates to them, never having a desire in their hearts for whatever ˹of the gains˺ is given to the emigrants. They give ˹the emigrants˺ preference over themselves even though they may be in need. And whoever is saved from the selfishness of their own souls, it is they who are ˹truly˺ successful.

Tafsir: And those who had settled in the hometown that is Medina and had abided in faith that is to say those who had embraced it with enthusiasm — these being the Helpers before them love those who have emigrated to them and do not find in their breasts any need any envy of that which those others have been given that is to say of what the Prophet s had given the Emigrants from the seized possessions of the Banū al-Nadīr a share which was exclusively theirs; but prefer others to themselves though they be in poverty in need of that which they prefer for those others to have. And whoever is saved from the avarice of his own soul its covetousness for acquiring possessions those — they are the successful.

hype_questions: What is the value of embracing faith and helping others in need?
How can one overcome selfishness and envy to achieve success?
What role do the Helpers play in supporting emigrants in their community?
propositions: Those who settled in Medina before the arrival of the emigrants love whoever immigrates to them.
They give preference to others over themselves, even when they are in need.
Whoever is saved from the selfishness of their own soul is successful.

source_text:
Verse: And those who come after them will pray, “Our Lord! Forgive us and our fellow believers who preceded us in faith, and do not allow bitterness into our hearts towards those who believe. Our Lord! Indeed, You are Ever Gracious, Most Merciful.”

Tafsir: And those who will come after them after the Emigrants and the Helpers up to the Day of Resurrection say ‘Our Lord forgive us and our brethren who preceded us in embracing the faith and do not place any rancour any spite in our hearts toward those who believe. Our Lord You are indeed Kind Merciful!’.

hype_questions: What is the significance of forgiveness in Islam?
How can believers avoid bitterness towards those who believe?
What is the nature of Allah's mercy and kindness?
propositions: Those who come after them will pray for forgiveness.
Believers should forgive their brethren who preceded them in faith.
Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful.

source_text:
Verse: Have you ˹O Prophet˺ not seen the hypocrites who say to their fellow disbelievers from the People of the Book, “If you are expelled, we will certainly leave with you, and We will never obey anyone against you. And if you are fought against, we will surely help you.”? But Allah bears witness that they are truly liars.

Tafsir: Have you not considered have you not seen the hypocrites who say to their brethren who disbelieve from among the People of the Scripture namely the Banū al-Nadīr their brethren in disbelief ‘If la-in the lām is for oaths in all four instances you are expelled from Medina we will assuredly go forth with you and we will never obey anyone against you to forsake you. And if you are fought against wa-in qūtiltum the prefatory lām of la-in has been omitted we will certainly help you’. And God bears witness that they are truly liars.

hype_questions: What happens to hypocrites if they are expelled from Medina?
Will hypocrites help their fellow disbelievers in a fight against others?
How do hypocrites respond when faced with the possibility of being fought against?
propositions: Hypocrites say they will leave with believers if they are expelled.
Hypocrites claim to never obey anyone against their fellow disbelievers.
If hypocrites are fought against, they claim to help them.
Allah bears witness that hypocrites are truly liars.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, if they are expelled, the hypocrites will never leave with them. And if they are fought against, the hypocrites will never help them. And even if the hypocrites did so, they would certainly flee, then the disbelievers would be left with no help.

Tafsir: For indeed if they are expelled they would not go forth with them and if they are fought against they would not help them. And even if they were to help them that is to say even if they came to help them they would surely turn their backs to flee the implied response to the oath suffices in place of the response to the conditional in all five instances — then they the Jews would not be helped.

hype_questions: What happens if a group of hypocrites is expelled along with believers?
How would the behavior of hypocrites change if they were to help believers in battle?
Would the presence of hypocrites hinder the success of believers' efforts?
propositions: If hypocrites are expelled, they will not leave with believers.
If hypocrites are fought against, they will not help them.
Even if hypocrites were to help believers, they would turn their backs and flee.
The implied response to an oath is sufficient in place of the response to a conditional statement.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, there is more fear in their hearts for you ˹believers˺ than for Allah. That is because they are a people who do not comprehend.

Tafsir: You indeed arouse greater awe fear in their hearts that is the hearts of the hypocrites than God — but only because He has deferred His chastisement to the Hereafter. That is because they are a people who do not comprehend.

hype_questions: What causes fear in the hearts of hypocrites?
Why do hypocrites not comprehend the reality?
How does Allah's chastisement relate to their understanding?
propositions: There is more fear in the hearts of believers than in the hearts of hypocrites.
Hypocrites do not comprehend because Allah has deferred His chastisement to the Hereafter.
Believers are not afraid of Allah's chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Even united, they would not ˹dare˺ fight against you except ˹from˺ within fortified strongholds or from behind walls. Their malice for each other is intense: you think they are united, yet their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people with no ˹real˺ understanding.

Tafsir: They that is the Jews will not fight against you together all in a single body except in fortified towns or from behind some wall jidār a variant reading has plural judur ‘walls’ some kind of protective fence. Their might their belligerence is great among themselves. You would suppose them to be all together united as a single body but their hearts are disunited scattered contrary to supposition. That is because they are a people who have no sense;

hype_questions: What is the reason behind the Jews' intense malice towards each other?
How do the Jews' hearts differ from their outward appearance of unity?
What characteristic defines the people who have no real understanding?
propositions: Even united, they would not fight against you except from within fortified strongholds or from behind walls.
Their malice for each other is intense: you think they are united, yet their hearts are divided.
That is because they are a people with no real understanding.

source_text:
Verse: They are ˹both just˺ like those who recently went down before them: they tasted the evil consequences of their doings. And they will suffer a painful punishment.

Tafsir: their likeness in relinquishing faith is as the likeness of those who recently before them a short time before — these being the idolaters from among those who fought at Badr — tasted the evil consequences of their conduct the punishment for it in this world by being killed or otherwise. And for them there will be a painful chastisement in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What happens to those who fight at Badr?
How do people who give up faith suffer in this world?
What is the punishment for idolaters in the Hereafter?
propositions: Those who recently went down before them tasted the evil consequences of their doings.
The punishment for it in this world by being killed or otherwise.
And for them there will be a painful chastisement in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: ˹They are˺ like Satan when he lures someone to disbelieve. Then after they have done so, he will say ˹on Judgment Day˺, “I have absolutely nothing to do with you. I truly fear Allah—the Lord of all worlds.”

Tafsir: In addition their likeness in heeding the words of the hypocrites and their forsaking of them is like Satan when he says to man ‘Disbelieve!’; so that when he man disbelieves he says ‘Lo! I am absolved of you. Indeed I fear God the Lord of the Worlds’ out of mendacity and dissimulation on his part.

hype_questions: What happens when someone disbelieves in Allah?
How does Satan's behavior compare to that of a hypocrite?
What is the significance of fearing God on Judgment Day?
propositions: Satan lures someone to disbelieve.
After disbelieving, Satan claims he has nothing to do with the person and fears Allah.
Hypocrites' words are like Satan's when he says 'Disbelieve!'
When someone disbelieves, they claim to be absolved of their previous beliefs due to hypocrisy.

source_text:
Verse: So they will both end up in the Fire, staying there forever. That is the reward of the wrongdoers.

Tafsir: So the sequel for both will be that is the sequel for both the one who leads astray and the one led astray a variant reading for ‘āqibatahumā has the nominative ‘āqibatuhumā as the subject of kāna ‘will be’ that they are in the Fire therein abiding. And that is the requital of the evildoers that is the disbelievers.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate fate of those who lead others astray?
How do wrongdoers get rewarded in the afterlife?
What punishment awaits disbelievers?
propositions: Both will end up in the Fire.
The reward of wrongdoers is to stay in the Fire forever.
Those who lead others astray and those who are led astray will be in the Fire abiding.
Evildoers and disbelievers will receive their requital in the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Be mindful of Allah and let every soul look to what ˹deeds˺ it has sent forth for tomorrow. And fear Allah, ˹for˺ certainly Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: O you who believe fear God and let every soul consider what it has sent ahead for tomorrow for the Day of Resurrection. And fear God. God is indeed Aware of what you do.

hype_questions: What happens to our deeds after we die?
How can we prepare for the Day of Resurrection?
Is God aware of our actions?
propositions: Believers should be mindful of Allah.
Every soul should consider its future deeds.
God is All-Aware of human actions.

source_text:
Verse: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. It is they who are ˹truly˺ rebellious.

Tafsir: And do not be like those who forget God those who neglect obedience to Him so that He makes them forget their own souls to forget to send ahead good deeds for its sake. Those — they are the immoral.

hype_questions: What happens when one neglects obedience to God?
How does forgetting Allah affect a person's soul?
Can good deeds be sent ahead for a righteous purpose?
propositions: Those who forget God neglect obedience to Him.
He makes them forget their own souls.
They are the immoral.

source_text:
Verse: The residents of the Fire cannot be equal to the residents of Paradise. ˹Only˺ the residents of Paradise will be successful.

Tafsir: Not equal are the inhabitants of the Fire and the inhabitants of Paradise. It is the inhabitants of Paradise who are the winners.

hype_questions: What determines success in the afterlife?
How do the inhabitants of Paradise differ from those of Fire?
What is the ultimate goal for those who reside in Paradise?
propositions: The residents of the Fire cannot be equal to the residents of Paradise.
Only the residents of Paradise will be successful.

source_text:
Verse: Had We sent down this Quran upon a mountain, you would have certainly seen it humbled and torn apart in awe of Allah. We set forth such comparisons for people, ˹so˺ perhaps they may reflect.

Tafsir: Had We sent down this Qur’ān upon a mountain and had it the mountain been endowed with a faculty of discernment like man you would have surely seen it humbled rent asunder by the fear of God. And such similitudes as those mentioned — do We strike for mankind that perhaps they may reflect and so become believers.

hype_questions: Can a mountain be humbled by the fear of God?
How does the Quran's revelation relate to human reflection and faith?
What is the purpose of using similitudes in religious texts?
propositions: Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have certainly seen it humbled.
We set forth such comparisons for people, so perhaps they may reflect.
And such similitudes as those mentioned — do We strike for mankind that perhaps they may reflect and so become believers.

source_text:
Verse: He is Allah—there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him: Knower of the seen and unseen. He is the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: He is God than Whom there is no other god Knower of the unseen and the visible what is secret and what is proclaimed — He is the Compassionate the Merciful.

hype_questions: What is Allah's nature?
How does Allah know the unseen and the seen?
What are the characteristics of Allah's compassion and mercy?
propositions: Allah is God than Whom there is no other god.
Allah is the Knower of both the seen and the unseen.
Allah is the Compassionate one.
Allah is the Merciful one.

source_text:
Verse: He is Allah—there is no god except Him: the King, the Most Holy, the All-Perfect, the Source of Serenity, the Watcher ˹of all˺, the Almighty, the Supreme in Might, the Majestic. Glorified is Allah far above what they associate with Him ˹in worship˺!

Tafsir: He is God than Whom there is no other god the King the Holy the One sanctified from what does not befit Him the Peace unblemished by any defects the Securer the One Who confirms the sincerity of His messengers by creating miracles for them the Guardian al-muhaymin derives from haymana yuhayminu meaning that one is watcher over something in other words the One Who is Witness to the deeds of His servants the Mighty the Strong the Compeller compelling His creatures to what He will the Exalted above what does not befit Him. Glorified be God — He is declaring His transcendence — above what partners they ascribe! to Him.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's transcendence?
How does Allah confirm the sincerity of His messengers?
What is the significance of Allah being the Watcher over all?
propositions: Allah is God than Whom there is no other god.
Allah is sanctified from what does not befit Him.
Allah confirms the sincerity of His messengers by creating miracles for them.
Allah is the Watcher over all.
Allah compels His creatures to what He wills.

source_text:
Verse: He is Allah: the Creator, the Inventor, the Shaper. He ˹alone˺ has the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth ˹constantly˺ glorifies Him. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: He is God the Creator the Maker the Originator from nothing the Shaper. To Him belong the ninety nine Most Beautiful Names cited in hadīth al-husnā is the feminine of al-ahsan. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorify Him and He is the Mighty the Wise — already explained at the beginning of this sūra.

hype_questions: What are the most beautiful names of Allah?
Why does everything in the universe glorify Allah?
Who is the creator and shaper of the universe?
propositions: Allah is the Creator, Inventor, Shaper.
Allah has the Most Beautiful Names.
The heavens and earth glorify Allah.
Allah is the Almighty, All-Wise.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Do not take My enemies and yours as trusted allies, showing them affection even though they deny what has come to you of the truth. They drove the Messenger and yourselves out ˹of Mecca˺, simply for your belief in Allah, your Lord. If you ˹truly˺ emigrated to struggle in My cause and seek My pleasure, ˹then do not take them as allies,˺ disclosing secrets ˹of the believers˺ to the pagans out of affection for them, when I know best whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal. And whoever of you does this has truly strayed from the Right Way.

Tafsir: O you who believe do not take My enemy and your enemy namely the disbelievers of Mecca for friends. You offer you communicate to them the Prophet’s plan s to attack them which he had confided to you and had kept secret at Hunayn communicating this to them out of affection between you and them. Hātib b. Abī Balta‘a sent them a letter to that effect on account of his having children and close relatives idolaters among them. The Prophet s intercepted it from the person to whom he Hātib had given it to deliver after God apprised him of this. Hātib’s excuse for this conduct of his was accepted by the Prophet; when verily they have disbelieved in the truth that has come to you that is in the religion of Islam and the Qur’ān expelling the Messenger and you from Mecca by oppressing you because you believe in God your Lord. If you have gone forth to struggle in My way and to seek My pleasure … the response to the conditional is indicated by what preceded that is to say understand it as being ‘then do not take them as friends’. You secretly harbour affection for them when I know well what you hide and what you proclaim. And whoever among you does that that is to secretly communicate the Prophet’s news to them has verily strayed from the right way he has missed the path of guidance originally al-sawā’ means ‘the middle way’.

hype_questions: Can taking an enemy as a friend lead to straying from the right path?
What is the significance of secrecy in struggling for Allah's cause?
How can one distinguish between seeking Allah's pleasure and harboring affection for enemies?
propositions: Believers should not take their enemies as trusted allies.
Those who emigrate to struggle in Allah's cause should not disclose secrets of the believers to pagans out of affection for them.
If you truly emigrate to struggle in My cause and seek My pleasure, then do not take them as allies.

source_text:
Verse: If they gain the upper hand over you, they would be your ˹open˺ enemies, unleashing their hands and tongues to harm you, and wishing that you would abandon faith.

Tafsir: If they were to prevail over you they would be your enemies and would stretch out against you their hands to kill and assault you and their tongues with evil intent with insults and reviling; and they long for you to disbelieve.

hype_questions: What happens when someone gains the upper hand over me?
How do people react when they are in a position of power?
What is the desire of those who want to prevail over others?
propositions: If they gain the upper hand over you, they would be your enemies.
They would unleash their hands and tongues to harm you.
They wish that you would abandon faith.

source_text:
Verse: Neither your relatives nor children will benefit you on Judgment Day—He will decide between you ˹all˺. For Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.

Tafsir: Your relatives and your children the idolatrous ones for whose sake you secretly communicated the news will not avail you against the chastisement in the Hereafter. On the Day of Resurrection you will be separated passive yufsalu; or read active yafsilu ‘He will separate you’ from them so that you will be in Paradise while they will be alongside the disbelievers in the Fire. And God is Seer of what you do.

hype_questions: What will happen to my relatives on Judgment Day?
Will my children benefit me in the Hereafter?
How will I be separated from those who rejected Allah?
propositions: Your relatives and your children are not beneficial to you on Judgment Day.
Allah will separate you from them on the Day of Resurrection.
You will be in Paradise while they will be alongside the disbelievers in the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: You already have an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, “We totally dissociate ourselves from you and ˹shun˺ whatever ˹idols˺ you worship besides Allah. We reject you. The enmity and hatred that has arisen between us and you will last until you believe in Allah alone.” The only exception is when Abraham said to his father, “I will seek forgiveness for you,˹” adding, “but˺ I cannot protect you from Allah at all.” ˹The believers prayed,˺ “Our Lord! In You we trust. And to You we ˹always˺ turn. And to You is the final return.

Tafsir: Verily there is for you a good example read iswa or uswa in both instances meaning qudwa in the person of Abraham in terms of his sayings and deeds and those who were with him of believers when they said to their people ‘We are indeed innocent of you bura’ā’ is the plural of barī’ similar in form to zarīf ‘charming’ and of what you worship besides God. We repudiate you we disavow you and between us and you there has arisen enmity and hate forever wa’l-baghdā’u abadan pronounce both hamzas fully or replace the second one with a wāw until you come to believe in God alone’ except for Abraham’s saying to his father ‘I shall ask forgiveness for you — this statement is excepted from ‘a good example’ so it is not right for you to follow his example in this respect by asking forgiveness for disbelievers. As for his saying but I cannot avail you anything against God’ — that is either against His chastisement or to secure for you of His reward — he Abraham is using it to intimate to his father that he can do nothing for him other than to ask forgiveness for him which saying is itself based on that former statement albeit excepted from it in terms of what is meant by it even if on the face of it it would seem to be semantically part of the good example to be followed Say ‘Who can avail you anything against God’ Q. 4811; his Abraham’s plea of forgiveness for him was before it became evident to him that he his father was an enemy of God as mentioned in sūrat Barā’a Q. 9114. ‘Our Lord in You we put our trust and to You we turn penitently and to You is the journeying these are the words of the Friend of God Abraham and those who were with him in other words they were saying

hype_questions: What is the significance of disavowing one's people in Islam?
How does Abraham's statement about seeking forgiveness for his father relate to the concept of tawhid?
What is the ultimate goal that believers are striving for, as mentioned in this verse?
propositions: The enmity between believers and disbelievers will last until they believe in Allah alone.
Abraham said to his father, 'I will seek forgiveness for you,' but he cannot protect you from Allah at all.
Believers turn to Allah in prayer and trust in Him.
God is the final return.

source_text:
Verse: Our Lord! Do not subject us to the persecution of the disbelievers. Forgive us, our Lord! You ˹alone˺ are truly the Almighty, All-Wise.”

Tafsir: Our Lord do not make us a cause of beguilement for those who disbelieve that is to say do not make them prevail over us lest they think that they are following the truth and are beguiled as a result in other words lest they lose their reason because of us; and forgive us. Our Lord You are indeed the Mighty the Wise’ in Your kingdom and Your actions.

hype_questions: What happens when believers are persecuted by disbelievers?
How can believers avoid being a cause of deception for others?
What is the ultimate goal of believers in their interactions with non-believers?
propositions: Our Lord, do not make us a cause of beguilement for those who disbelieve.
Forgive us, Our Lord, and You are indeed the Mighty, All-Wise.

source_text:
Verse: You certainly have an excellent example in them for whoever has hope in Allah and the Last Day. But whoever turns away, then surely Allah ˹alone˺ is the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

Tafsir: Verily there is for you O community of Muhammad (s) laqad kāna lakum is the response to an implied oath in them a good example for those of you who li-man kāna is an inclusive substitution for –kum of lakum ‘for you’ with the same preposition li- repeated anticipate God and the Last Day that is for those who fear these two or who expect reward or punishment. And whoever turns away by befriending the disbelievers should know that God is the Independent without need of His creatures the Worthy of Praise to those who obey Him.

hype_questions: What is the significance of having hope in Allah and the Last Day?
How should one respond to an implied oath, as exemplified by the community of Muhammad (s)?
What is the nature of God's independence from His creatures?
propositions: There is a good example for those who fear Allah and the Last Day in the community of Muhammad (s).
God is the Independent without need of His creatures.
Allah is the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

source_text:
Verse: ˹In time,˺ Allah may bring about goodwill between you and those of them you ˹now˺ hold as enemies. For Allah is Most Capable. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: It may be that God will bring about between you and those of them with whom you are at enmity from among the disbelievers of Mecca out of your obedience to God exalted be He affection by His guiding them to faith so that they then become your friends. For God is Powerful able to do that — and He did do this after the conquest of Mecca — and God is Forgiving to them of their past deeds Merciful to them also.

hype_questions: Can God bring about goodwill between enemies?
How can obedience to God lead to friendship with disbelievers?
Does God show mercy to those who have been at enmity?
propositions: Allah may bring about goodwill between you and those of them you hold as enemies.
God will guide them to faith through their obedience.
God is Powerful able to do that.
God is Forgiving to them of their past deeds.
God is Merciful to them also.

source_text:
Verse: Allah does not forbid you from dealing kindly and fairly with those who have neither fought nor driven you out of your homes. Surely Allah loves those who are fair.

Tafsir: God does not forbid you in regard to those who did not wage war against you from among the disbelievers on account of religion and did not expel you from your homes that you should treat them kindly an tabarrūhum is an inclusive substitution for alladhīna ‘those who’ and deal with them justly this was revealed before the command to struggle against them. Assuredly God loves the just.

hype_questions: What does Allah mean by 'dealing kindly and fairly'?
Why did Allah not forbid us from treating disbelievers with kindness?
How does God show love towards those who are just?
propositions: Allah does not forbid dealing kindly and fairly with those who have neither fought nor driven you out of your homes.
God loves those who are fair.
You should treat those who did not wage war against you from among the disbelievers on account of religion and did not expel you from your homes justly.

source_text:
Verse: Allah only forbids you from befriending those who have fought you for ˹your˺ faith, driven you out of your homes, or supported ˹others˺ in doing so. And whoever takes them as friends, then it is they who are the ˹true˺ wrongdoers.

Tafsir: God only forbids you in regard to those who waged war against you on account of religion and expelled you from your homes and supported others in your expulsion that you should make friends with them an tawallawhum is an inclusive substitution for alladhīna ‘those who’. And whoever makes friends with them those — they are the wrongdoers.

hype_questions: What happens when you befriend someone who fought against your faith?
Can making friends with those who expelled you from your homes be considered wrong?
How does God view friendships with those who waged war against you on account of religion?
propositions: Allah forbids befriending those who have fought against your faith.
Those who take such people as friends are the true wrongdoers.
God only prohibits making friends with those who waged war against you on account of religion and expelled you from your homes.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! When the believing women come to you as emigrants, ˹But˺ demand ˹repayment of˺ whatever ˹dowries˺ you had paid, and let the disbelievers do the same. That is the judgment of Allah—He judges between you. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: O you who believe when believing women come to you saying with their tongues that they are emigrating from the company of disbelievers — this was following the truce concluded with them the disbelievers at al-Hudaybiyya to the effect that if any of their number should go to join the believers that person should be sent back — test them by making them swear that they had only gone forth from Mecca because of their sincere wish to embrace Islam and not out of some hatred for their disbelieving husbands nor because they might be enamoured by some Muslim man that was how the Prophet s used to take from them their oaths. God knows best the state of their faith. Then if you know them if you suppose them on the basis of their oaths to be believers do not send them back to the disbelievers. They the women are not lawful for them nor are they the disbelievers lawful for them. And give them that is to say their disbelieving husbands what they have expended on them on such women in the way of dowries. And you would not be at fault if you marry them on that previous condition when you have given them their dowries. And do not hold on read tumassikū or tumsikū to the conjugal ties of disbelieving women your wives for your Islam automatically prohibits you from this or to the ties of those apostatising women who return to the idolaters for likewise their apostatising automatically prohibits you from marrying them and ask for demand the return of what you have expended on these women of dowries in the event of apostasy from those disbelievers to whom they are married. And let them ask for what they have expended on those women who have emigrated as explained above that it may be repaid to them. That is God’s judgement. He judges between you therewith and God is Knower Wise.

hype_questions: What happens to women who leave their disbelieving husbands and want to marry a Muslim?
Can I keep the dowry money if my wife leaves her disbeliever husband and wants to marry me?
How does Allah judge between believers and apostates in matters of marriage?
propositions: Believing women who come to you as emigrants demand repayment of their dowries.
The Prophet used to take oaths from these women, testing their sincerity.
You should not send back women who swear they are leaving for Islam and not out of hatred or desire.
You can marry these women on the condition that you have given them their dowries.
Islam prohibits marrying apostatising women who return to idolaters.
God judges between believers and apostates in matters of marriage, including repayment of dowries.

source_text:
Verse: And if any of your wives desert you to the disbelievers, and later you take spoils from them, then pay those whose wives have gone, the equivalent of whatever ˹dowry˺ they had paid. And be mindful of Allah, in Whom you believe.

Tafsir: And if you lose any of your wives that is to say if you lose one or more of them — or it means if you lose anything of their dowries — by their going to the disbelievers as apostates and so you retaliate you embark upon a raid and capture spoils from them then give those whose wives have gone from the spoils the like of what they have expended for their having lost it to the disbelievers. And fear God in Whom you believe. And indeed the believers did what they had been commanded to do in the way of paying back the disbelievers the dowries of their former wives and the believers the dowries of the women who had apostatised. Afterwards however this stipulation was annulled.

hype_questions: What happens if a Muslim husband loses his wife to the disbelievers?
How do Muslims compensate their wives who have been taken by the disbelievers?
What is the significance of paying back dowries in Islam?
propositions: If any of your wives desert you to the disbelievers, and later you take spoils from them, then pay those whose wives have gone, the equivalent of whatever dowry they had paid.
Be mindful of Allah, in Whom you believe.
The believers did what they had been commanded to do in the way of paying back the disbelievers the dowries of their former wives and the believers the dowries of the women who had apostatised.

source_text:
Verse: O Prophet! When the believing women come to you, pledging to you that they will neither associate anything with Allah ˹in worship˺, nor steal, nor fornicate, nor kill their children, nor falsely attribute ˹illegitimate˺ children to their husbands, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge, and ask Allah to forgive them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: O Prophet if believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not ascribe anything as partner to God and that they will not steal nor commit adultery nor slay their children as used to be done during the time of pagandom jāhiliyya when they would bury new-born girls alive fearing ignominy and impoverishment nor bring any lie that they have invented originating between their hands and their legs that is by bringing a foundling which they then falsely ascribe to the husband — it the lie is described in terms of a real child because when a woman gives birth to a child it falls between her hands and legs; nor disobey you in doing what is decent which is that which concords with obedience to God such as refraining from wailing ripping apart their clothes in grief pulling out their hair tearing open the front of their garments or scratching their faces then accept their allegiance — the Prophet s did this but in words and he did not shake hands with any of them — and ask God to forgive them; surely God is Forgiving Merciful.

hype_questions: What is the pledge that believing women make to the Prophet?
How does the Prophet handle the pledge of believing women?
What are the consequences of not following the guidance of the Prophet?
propositions: Believing women pledge to worship Allah alone and refrain from stealing, adultery, child murder, and false accusations.
The Prophet accepts the pledge of believing women but does not shake hands with them due to concerns about their sincerity.
God is All-Forgiving and Merciful, and the Prophet asks God to forgive those who follow His guidance.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Do not ally yourselves with a people Allah is displeased with. They already have no hope for the Hereafter, just like the disbelievers lying in ˹their˺ graves.

Tafsir: O you who believe do not befriend a people against whom God is wrathful namely the Jews. They have truly despaired of the Hereafter of attaining its reward — despite their being certain of its truth out of obstinacy towards the Prophet even though they know him to be sincere — just as the disbelievers have despaired — they themselves being — of those who are in the tombs that is to say those who are entombed and barred from the good of the Hereafter for they are shown both their would-have-been places in Paradise had they believed and the Fire for which they are destined.

hype_questions: What happens to those who ally themselves with a people against whom God is wrathful?
Can disbelievers attain the Hereafter despite their knowledge of its truth?
What are the consequences for those who refuse to believe in Allah's Messenger?
propositions: Believers should not form alliances with people against whom God is displeased.
The Jews have lost hope for the Hereafter due to their obstinacy towards Allah's Messenger.
Disbelievers are also denied entry into the Hereafter due to their disbelief.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. For He ˹alone˺ is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifies God that is to say everything proclaims His transcendence the lām of li’Llāhi is extra and mā has been used instead of min in order to indicate the predominance of non-rational creatures and He is the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His actions.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reality that transcends all existence?
How does God's power manifest in His kingdom?
What wisdom can be derived from Allah's actions?
propositions: Whatever is in the heavens glorifies Allah.
Whatever is on the earth glorifies God.
All that exists proclaims God's transcendence.
The lām of li’Llāhi indicates the extra aspect of God's nature.
Mā has been used instead of min to emphasize non-rational creatures' predominance.
God is the Mighty in His kingdom.
God is the Wise in His actions.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Why do you say what you do not do?

Tafsir: O you who believe why do you say in demanding to participate in the struggle what you do not do? for you retreated at Uhud.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of saying something you don't do?
Why did believers retreat at Uhud during a struggle?
How can one reconcile their words with actions?
propositions: Believers say they participate in struggles but do not act upon it.
You who believe retreated at Uhud despite demanding to participate in the struggle.
Retreating at Uhud indicates a lack of action on the part of believers.

source_text:
Verse: How despicable it is in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do!

Tafsir: It is greatly loathsome maqtan is for specification to God that you say an taqūlū constitutes the agent of the verb kabura ‘it is greatly’ what you do not do.

hype_questions: What are some common deceptions people make in their daily lives?
How can one ensure they are being obedient to Allah?
What are the consequences of not following Allah's commands?
propositions: It is despicable to say something you do not do.
Saying something without intending to perform it constitutes deception.
Deception is a grave offense in the sight of Allah.

source_text:
Verse: Surely Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ˹solid˺ ranks as if they were one concrete structure.

Tafsir: Indeed God loves He assists and honours those who fight for His cause in ranks saffan is a circumstantial qualifier in other words understand it as sāffīna as if they were a solid structure with all of its parts compacted together firm.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's love for those who fight in His cause?
How does Allah assist and honour those who fight for His cause?
What does it mean to be a 'solid structure' in the context of jihad?
propositions: Allah loves those who fight in His cause.
Allah assists and honours those who fight for His cause.
Those who fight in Allah's cause are like a solid structure with all its parts compacted together firm.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember, O  Prophet,˺ when Moses said to his people, “O my people! Why do you hurt me when you already know I am Allah’s messenger to you?” So when they ˹persistently˺ deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. For Allah does not guide the rebellious people.

Tafsir: And mention when Moses said to his people ‘O my people why do you harm me — for they had said that he had a hernia in his testicles which he did not have and they denied him — when certainly qad is for confirmation you know that I am the messenger of God to you?’ annī rasūlu’Llāhi ilaykum this sentence is a circumstantial qualifier and when you know that messengers ought to be respected. So when they deviated when they swerved away from the truth by harming him God caused their hearts to deviate He turned them away from guidance in accordance to what He had preordained since pre-eternity and God does not guide the immoral folk those who in His knowledge are disbelievers.

hype_questions: What happens when people reject a prophet?
How does Allah respond to those who harm or reject His messengers?
Can someone be guided by Allah if they are known to be disbelievers?
propositions: Moses said to his people, 'O my people! Why do you hurt me when you already know I am Allah's messenger to you?'
Allah caused their hearts to deviate after they persistedently deviated from the truth by harming Moses.
God does not guide the immoral folk who are known to be disbelievers in His knowledge.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹remember˺ when Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O children of Israel! I am truly Allah’s messenger to you, confirming the Torah which came before me, and giving good news of a messenger after me whose name will be Ahmad.” Yet when the Prophet came to them with clear proofs, they said, “This is pure magic.”

Tafsir: And mention when Jesus son of Mary said ‘O Children of Israel — he did not say ‘O my people’ as did Moses because he was not related to them in any way — I am indeed God’s messenger to you confirming what is before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger who will come after me whose name is Ahmad.’ God exalted be He says Yet when he brought them when Ahmad brought the disbelievers the clear signs the revelations and the indications they said ‘This namely what has been brought is manifest sorcery!’ sihrun a variant reading has sāhirun ‘a sorcerer’ meaning the one who has brought them is a manifest sorcerer.

hype_questions: Does the Torah confirm Jesus' prophethood?
What is the significance of Ahmad's name in Islamic theology?
How do believers respond to clear proofs and revelations?
propositions: Jesus said he was Allah's messenger to the children of Israel.
The Torah confirms what came before Jesus.
God exalted be He says Jesus brought good tidings of a messenger after him.
When Jesus presented his message, the disbelievers called it sorcery.
Ahmad is mentioned as a future messenger in Islamic theology.

source_text:
Verse: Who does more wrong than the one who fabricates lies about Allah when invited to submit ˹to Him˺? For Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

Tafsir: And who does — that is to say none does — greater wrong than he who invents lies against God by ascribing a partner and a child to Him and describing His signs as being sorcery when he is actually being summoned to submission to God? And God does not guide the wrongdoing folk the disbelieving folk.

hype_questions: What happens to someone who invents lies against God?
Who does greater wrong than someone who ascribes a partner and a child to God?
How does God guide people?
propositions: The one who fabricates lies about Allah when invited to submit to Him does more wrong.
God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
Inventing lies against God by ascribing a partner and a child to Him is greater wrong than any other wrong.
Describing God's signs as sorcery when being summoned to submission to God is also greater wrong.

source_text:
Verse: They wish to extinguish Allah’s light with their mouths, but Allah will ˹certainly˺ perfect His light, even to the dismay of the disbelievers.

Tafsir: They desire to extinguish li-yutfi’ū is in the subjunctive form because of an implicit an sc. an yutfi’ū the lām being extra the light of God His Law and His proofs with their mouths with their sayings that this is sorcery or poetry or soothsaying; but God will perfect He will manifest His light mutimmun nūrahu some have read this in the form of a genitive annextation mutimmu nūrihi though the disbelievers be averse to this.

hype_questions: Can God's light be extinguished?
What is the nature of li-yutfi'ū in Arabic?
How does God respond to those who seek to extinguish His light?
propositions: They wish to extinguish Allah’s light with their mouths.
Allah will perfect His light, even to the dismay of the disbelievers.
The light of God is His Law and His proofs.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who has sent His Messenger with ˹true˺ guidance and the religion of truth, making it prevail over all others, even to the dismay of the polytheists.

Tafsir: It is He Who has sent His Messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth that He may make it prevail that He may raise it over all other religions over all the religions which oppose it though the disbelievers be averse to this.

hype_questions: Does Islam have the power to overcome other religions?
Can a single religion be superior to all others?
Is it possible for a religion to prevail over polytheistic beliefs?
propositions: He has sent His Messenger with true guidance.
The religion of truth prevails over all others.
He may raise it over all other religions.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Shall I guide you to an exchange that will save you from a painful punishment?

Tafsir: O you who believe shall I show you a commerce that will deliver you read tunjīkum or tunajjīkum from a painful chastisement? It is as if they had replied ‘Yes’ so that He then says

hype_questions: Will this commerce save me from punishment?
