What is the nature of this commerce that will deliver me from chastisement?

propositions: God offers believers a commerce that will save them from punishment.
Believers are offered a commerce that will deliver them from painful chastisement.
If believers accept the commerce, God responds with a promise or reward.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It is to˺ have faith in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if only you knew.

Tafsir: You should believe you should maintain faith in God and His Messenger and struggle for the cause of God with your possessions and your lives. That is better for you should you know that it is better for you then do it.

hype_questions: What is the best way to live a virtuous life?
How can I prioritize my actions for the sake of God?
What does it mean to struggle in the cause of Allah?
propositions: Believe in Allah and His Messenger.
Strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives.
Maintaining faith is better than not knowing its value.

source_text:
Verse: He will forgive your sins, and admit you into Gardens under which rivers flow, and ˹house you in˺ splendid homes in the Gardens of Eternity. That is the ultimate triumph.

Tafsir: He will then forgive you yaghfir is the response to an implied conditional that is to say ‘if you do this He will then forgive you’ your sins and admit you into gardens underneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in the Gardens of Eden as a residence. That is the supreme triumph.

hype_questions: What are the rewards for those who seek forgiveness from Allah?
How does Allah's forgiveness manifest in the afterlife?
What is the ultimate triumph that awaits believers?
propositions: Allah will forgive your sins.
You will be admitted into Gardens under which rivers flow.
You will reside in splendid homes in the Gardens of Eternity.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He will also give you˺ another favour that you long for: help from Allah and an imminent victory. ˹So˺ give good news ˹O Prophet˺ to the believers.

Tafsir: And He will give you another grace which you love help from God and a victory near at hand. And give good tidings to the believers of assistance and victory.

hype_questions: What is the additional favor that Allah will give to believers?
How does Allah's help manifest in the lives of believers?
What is the nature of the imminent victory that Allah promises?
propositions: Allah will give believers another favour.
The favour is help from Allah.

Believers should be given good news about assistance and victory.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Stand up for Allah, as Jesus, son of Mary, asked the disciples, “Who will stand up with me for Allah?” The disciples replied, “We will stand up for Allah.” Then a group from the Children of Israel believed while another disbelieved. We then supported the believers against their enemies, so they prevailed.

Tafsir: O you who believe be helpers of God of His religion a variant reading of ansāran li’Llāhi has the genitive annexation ansāra’Llāhi just as said kamā qāla to the end of the statement means ‘just as the disciples were so’ as is indicated by what follows Jesus son of Mary to the disciples ‘Who will be my helpers unto God?’ that is to say who of you will be helpers alongside me turning to help God? The disciples said ‘We will be God’s helpers!’ These al-hawāriyyūn were the intimates of Jesus for they were the first to believe in him. They were twelve men of pure white complexion hawar; but it is also said that their epithet derives from the fact that they were bleachers qassārūn who bleached yuhawwirūna clothes. So a group of the Children of Israel believed in Jesus saying ‘He is indeed the servant of God who has been raised to heaven’ while a group disbelieved because they said that he was the son of God whom He had raised unto Himself. Thus the two groups waged war against one another. Then We strengthened those who believed of the two groups against their enemy the disbelieving groups and so they became the triumphant the victors.

hype_questions: Who will stand up with me for Allah?
What is the significance of the disciples' response to Jesus' question?
How did God respond to the conflict between believers and disbelievers?
propositions: O believers, stand up for Allah.
Jesus asked his disciples who would stand up with him for Allah.
The disciples replied that they would stand up for Allah.
A group of the Children of Israel believed in Jesus saying 'He is indeed the servant of God who has been raised to heaven'.
Another group disbelieved because they said that he was the son of God whom He had raised unto Himself.
God strengthened those who believed against their enemy, the disbelieving groups, and so they became the triumphant victors.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth ˹constantly˺ glorifies Allah—the King, the Most Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

Tafsir: All that is the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifies God all proclaims His transcendence the lām of li’Llāhi is extra; mā is used instead of min in order to indicate the predominance of non-rational beings the King the Holy the One Who transcends what does not befit Him the Mighty the Wise in His kingdom and in His actions.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's transcendence?
How do non-rational beings glorify God?
What does it mean for Allah to be the King and the Most Holy?
propositions: All that exists in the heavens and on earth glorifies God.
God's transcendence is proclaimed through the existence of non-rational beings.
Allah is the King, the Most Holy, and the One Who transcends what does not befit Him.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who raised for the illiterate ˹people˺ a messenger from among themselves—reciting to them His revelations, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, for indeed they had previously been clearly astray—

Tafsir: It is He Who sent to the unlettered folk among the Arabs ummī means ‘one who cannot write or read a book’ a messenger from among them namely Muhammad (s) to recite to them His signs the Qur’ān and to purify them to cleanse them from idolatry and to teach them the Book the Qur’ān and wisdom in the rulings that it contains though indeed wa-in in has been softened from the hardened form with its subject having been omitted that is to say understand it as wa-innahum before that before his coming they had been in manifest error.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Muhammad's message to the unlettered folk?
How did Allah purify and teach the people through the Qur'an?
What was the state of the people before Muhammad's arrival?
propositions: Allah sent a messenger from among the Arabs to recite His signs to them.
The Qur'an was used to purify and cleanse the people from idolatry.
Muhammad taught the people wisdom in the rulings of the Qur'an.

source_text:
Verse: along with others of them who have not yet joined them ˹in faith˺. For He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: And to others wa-ākharīna is a supplement to al-ummiyyīna ‘the unlettered’ that is to say those who are alive from among them and to those of them who will come after them who have not yet joined them with regard to precedence and merit; and He is the Mighty the Wise in His kingdom and in His actions those mentioned as coming afterwards are the Successors al-tābi‘ūna; and it suffices to mention these Successors in order to illustrate the greater merit of the Companions among whom the Prophet s was sent over all those others of humans and jinn to whom he was also sent and who believed and will believe in him up until the Day of Resurrection for every generation is better than the succeeding one.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Successors (al-tābi‘ūna) in Islamic succession?
How does the Prophet's message relate to different generations of humans and jinn?
What is the concept of merit in Islam, particularly in relation to the Companions?
propositions: He is the Almighty, All-Wise.
The Successors (al-tābi‘ūna) are those who come after the initial believers and are considered more meritorious due to their precedence.
Every generation is better than the succeeding one in terms of faith and belief.

source_text:
Verse: This is the favour of Allah. He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty.

Tafsir: That is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He will — such as the Prophet and those mentioned with him — and God is dispenser of tremendous bounty.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's favour?
Who receives Allah's bounty?
How does Allah distribute His blessings?
propositions: Allah grants favour to whoever He wills.
God gives bounty to whom He will — such as the Prophet and those mentioned with him.
God is dispenser of tremendous bounty.

source_text:
Verse: The example of those who were entrusted with ˹observing˺ the Torah but failed to do so, is that of a donkey carrying books. How evil is the example of those who reject Allah’s signs! For Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

Tafsir: The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah those who were charged with implementing it then failed to uphold it then failed to act in accordance with it in what pertains to the descriptions of the Prophet s and so did not believe in him is as the likeness of an ass carrying books in that it does not benefit from them. Evil is the likeness of the people who deny God’s signs those confirming the truth of the Prophet s — the object of rebuke is omitted but is implied to be hādhā’l-mathalu ‘this likeness’. And God does not guide the evildoing folk the disbelievers.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject Allah's signs?
How does one demonstrate faith in the Prophet s?
Can one benefit from knowledge if they do not act upon it?
propositions: Those who were entrusted with the Torah failed to uphold its teachings.
The Prophet s is an example of someone whose message is confirmed by Allah's signs.
God does not guide those who reject His signs and engage in wrongdoing.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O Jews! If you claim to be Allah’s chosen ˹people˺ out of all humanity, then wish for death, if what you say is true.”

Tafsir: Say ‘O you of Jewry if you claim that you are the favoured friends of God to the exclusion of other people then long for death if you are truthful’ in kuntum sādiqīna is semantically connected to tamannū ‘long for’; as for the two conditions the first is dependent on the second that is to say if you are truthful in your claim that you are the favoured friends of God and given that such a friend would prefer the Hereafter to this world and that it the Hereafter begins at death then long for it.

hype_questions: Would a truly chosen people prefer death over life?
Can one claim to be God's favored friends and still desire worldly life?
What would happen if someone claims to be God's chosen people but is not truthful?
propositions: If you claim to be Allah’s chosen people out of all humanity, then wish for death.
You are the favoured friends of God to the exclusion of other people only if you are truthful.
A truly chosen people would prefer the Hereafter to this world and that it begins at death.

source_text:
Verse: But they will never wish for that because of what their hands have done. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of the wrongdoers.

Tafsir: But they will never long for it because of what their hands have sent ahead in the way of their disbelief of the Prophet which itself is a necessary consequence of their denial; and God is Knower of the evildoers the disbelievers.

hype_questions: Will they ever desire to return to their previous state?
Can they be forgiven for their past wrongdoings?
What is the ultimate consequence of their disbelief?
propositions: Their hands have sent ahead in the way of their disbelief of the Prophet.
Their denial is a necessary consequence of their disbelief.
God is Knower of the evildoers and disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “The death you are running away from will inevitably come to you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the seen and unseen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”

Tafsir: Say ‘Assuredly the death from which you flee fa-innahu the fā’ is extra will indeed encounter you; then you will be returned to the Knower of the Unseen and the visible the Knower of what is kept secret and what is in the open and He will inform you of what you used to do’ whereat He will requite you for it.

hype_questions: What happens when we flee from death?
Will we be held accountable for our past actions?
What will the Knower of the seen and unseen reveal to us?
propositions: Death is inevitable.
We will be returned to the Knower of the Unseen and the visible after death.
The Knower will inform us of what we used to do.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! When the call to prayer is made on Friday, then proceed ˹diligently˺ to the remembrance of Allah and leave off ˹your˺ business. That is best for you, if only you knew.

Tafsir: O you who believe when the call for prayer is made on Friday hasten set off to the remembrance of God to the prayer and leave aside all commerce suspend all such contracts. That is better for you should you know that it is better for you then do it.

hype_questions: What happens when the call to prayer is made on Friday?
How should believers respond when they hear the call to prayer on Friday?
What is better for believers than leaving off business and proceeding to remembrance of Allah?
propositions: When the call to prayer is made on Friday, proceed diligently to the remembrance of Allah.
Leave off business when the call to prayer is made on Friday.
Suspend all contracts when the call to prayer is made on Friday.

source_text:
Verse: Once the prayer is over, disperse throughout the land and seek the bounty of Allah. And remember Allah often so you may be successful.

Tafsir: And when the prayer is finished disperse in the land this is an imperative denoting permissibility and seek provision through God’s bounty and remember God with remembrance frequently that perhaps you may be successful that perhaps you may be the winners.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of dispersing throughout the land after prayer?
How can seeking Allah's bounty lead to success?
What role does remembrance play in achieving success?
propositions: Once the prayer is over, disperse throughout the land.
Dispersing in the land is permissible and allows for seeking provision through God’s bounty.
Remembering Allah frequently can lead to success.
Seeking Allah's bounty is essential for achieving success.
Dispersion in the land after prayer enables individuals to seek provision from God.

source_text:
Verse: When they saw the fanfare along with the caravan, they ˹almost all˺ flocked to it, leaving you ˹O Prophet˺ standing ˹on the pulpit˺. Say, “What is with Allah is far better than amusement and merchandise. And Allah is the Best Provider.”

Tafsir: On one occasion the Prophet s was delivering the Friday sermon when a caravan arrived and so as was the custom drums were beaten to announce its arrival whereat the people began to leave the mosque to go to it all except for twelve men. The following verse was then revealed But when they sight some opportunity for business or a diversion they scatter off towards it that is towards the business since it is what they seek more than diversion and leave you during the sermon standing. Say ‘That which is with God in the way of reward is better for those who believe than diversion and commerce. And God is the best of providers’. They say that every person ‘provides for’ yarzuqu his dependants by which they mean that such a person does so by means of the provision given by God min rizqi’Llāhi exalted be He.

hype_questions: What is the best way to prioritize business and devotion?
How can one balance personal interests with religious obligations?
What does it mean to 'provide' for dependants in a spiritual context?
propositions: The Prophet was left standing alone during his sermon as people flocked to the caravan.
Allah is better than amusement and merchandise.
God provides for His believers in a way that is more valuable than worldly business.
People prioritize business over devotion when given the opportunity.
To 'provide' for dependants means to receive provision from God.

source_text:
Verse: When the hypocrites come to you ˹O Prophet˺, they say, “We bear witness that you are certainly the Messenger of Allah”—and surely Allah knows that you are His Messenger—but Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are truly liars.

Tafsir: When the hypocrites come to you they say with their tongues in contradiction of what is in their hearts ‘We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of God.’ And God knows that you are indeed His Messenger and God bears witness He knows that the hypocrites truly are liars in what they conceal that which is contrary to what they say.

hype_questions: What is the nature of hypocrisy in Islam?
How does Allah respond to those who claim to be believers but are not?
What is the relationship between one's words and actions in faith?
propositions: The hypocrites bear false witness that the Prophet is the Messenger of God.
God knows that the Prophet is indeed His Messenger.
The hypocrites are liars because their words do not match their hearts.

source_text:
Verse: They have made their ˹false˺ oaths as a shield, hindering ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah. Evil indeed is what they do!

Tafsir: They have taken their oaths as a shield as a means of protection for their possessions and their lives and so they have barred thereby from the way of God that is from using them for the struggle. Evil indeed is that which they are wont to do.

hype_questions: What happens when people use oaths as a shield to protect themselves from the truth?
How do false oaths affect one's relationship with God?
Can using oaths for protection lead to evil consequences?
propositions: They have taken their oaths as a means of protection.
Their oaths serve as a shield to protect their possessions and lives.
Using oaths for protection bars individuals from the way of God.
False oaths are a source of evil consequences.

source_text:
Verse: This is because they believed and then abandoned faith. Therefore, their hearts have been sealed, so they do not comprehend.

Tafsir: That namely their evil deed is because they believed by affirming faith only with the tongue then disbelieved in their hearts that is to say they persist in harbouring disbelief in it; therefore their hearts have been stamped sealed with disbelief. Hence they do not understand faith.

hype_questions: What happens when someone abandons their faith?
Why can't those who disbelieve in their hearts understand the true meaning of faith?
How does one's heart get sealed due to disbelief?
propositions: They believed and then abandoned faith.
Their evil deed is because they believed by affirming faith only with the tongue.
They persist in harbouring disbelief in their hearts.
Their hearts have been stamped sealed with disbelief.
Hence they do not understand faith.

source_text:
Verse: When you see them, their appearance impresses you. And when they speak, you listen to their ˹impressive˺ speech. But they are ˹just˺ like ˹worthless˺ planks of wood leaned ˹against a wall˺. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah condemn them! How can they be deluded ˹from the truth˺?

Tafsir: And when you see them their figures please you on account of their fairness; and if they speak you listen to their speech because of its eloquence. Yet they are by virtue of the enormous size of their figures yet in their lack of comprehension like blocks of timber read khushbun or khushubun that have been propped-up set reclining against a wall. They assume that every cry made like a battle-cry or one made to retrieve a lost camel is directed against them because of the extent of terror in their hearts lest something should be revealed deeming their blood licit. They are the enemy so beware of them for they communicate your secrets to the disbelievers. May God assail them! destroy them! How can they deviate? how can they be turned away from faith after the proofs for it have been established?

hype_questions: Can they be turned away from faith after the proofs for it have been established?
How can they deviate?
How can they be deluded from the truth?
propositions: Their appearance impresses you.
They think every cry is against them.
May Allah condemn them!
They assume that every cry made like a battle-cry or one made to retrieve a lost camel is directed against them because of the extent of terror in their hearts.
They communicate your secrets to the disbelievers.
May God assail them! destroy them!

source_text:
Verse: When it is said to them, “Come! The Messenger of Allah will pray for you to be forgiven,” they turn their heads ˹in disgust˺, and you see them ˹O Prophet˺ turn away in arrogance.

Tafsir: And when it is said to them ‘Come offer apologies and God’s Messenger will ask forgiveness for you’ they twist read lawwaw or lawū they turn their heads and you see them turning away rejecting this offer disdainful.

hype_questions: What happens when the Prophet is asked to pray for forgiveness on behalf of someone who refuses to apologize?
How do people react when they are offered a chance to make amends and seek forgiveness?
What does it mean to turn away in arrogance?
propositions: When the Prophet is asked to pray for forgiveness, some people refuse to apologize.
Those who refuse to apologize are turned away by the Prophet's message of forgiveness.
Turning away in arrogance means rejecting an offer of forgiveness and making it difficult for oneself.

source_text:
Verse: It is the same whether you pray for their forgiveness or not, Allah will not forgive them. Surely Allah does not guide the rebellious people.

Tafsir: It will be the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them a’staghfarta the interrogative hamza here has taken the place of the conjunctive hamza or do not ask forgiveness for them God will never forgive them. Indeed God does not guide the immoral folk.

hype_questions: Will Allah forgive someone if we pray for their forgiveness?
What happens to people who are rebellious and immoral?
Can God guide anyone?
propositions: If you pray for someone's forgiveness, Allah will not forgive them.
Allah does not guide the rebellious people.
God will never forgive those who have rebelled against Him.

source_text:
Verse: They are the ones who say ˹to one another˺, “Do not spend ˹anything˺ on those ˹emigrants˺ with the Messenger of Allah so that they will break away ˹from him˺.” But to Allah ˹alone˺ belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, yet the hypocrites do not comprehend.

Tafsir: They are the ones who say to their companions from among the Helpers ‘Do not expend on those who are with the Messenger of God from among the Emigrants until they scatter off’ until they part with him. Yet to God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth with what they contain of provision and so He is the provider for the Emigrants and others but the hypocrites do not understand.

hype_questions: What is the consequence of spending on emigrants with the Messenger of Allah?
Why do hypocrites not comprehend the concept of treasuries?
How does God provide for emigrants and others?
propositions: The hypocrites advise their companions to stop spending on those who are with the Messenger of Allah.
God belongs to the heavenly treasuries and the earth.
God is the provider for the emigrants and others.

source_text:
Verse: They say, “If we return to Medina, the honourable will definitely expel the inferior.” But all honour and power belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, yet the hypocrites do not know.

Tafsir: They say ‘Surely if we return from the raid against the Banū al-Mustaliq to Medina the powerful by which they meant themselves will soon expel from it the weaker’ by which they meant the believers. Yet the real might victory belongs to God and to His Messenger and to the believers but the hypocrites do not know that.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the power that will expel the believers from Medina?
Who is the 'power' that will bring about victory for the believers?
Why do hypocrites fail to recognize the true source of power and victory?
propositions: They say that if they return to Medina, the powerful will expel the weaker.
The real might and victory belong to God and His Messenger and the believers.
Hypocrites do not know this.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Do not let your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. For whoever does so, it is they who are the ˹true˺ losers.

Tafsir: O you who believe do not let your possessions and your children divert you distract you from the remembrance of God from the five prayers; for whoever does that — it is they who are the losers.

hype_questions: What happens when wealth and children distract us from remembrance of Allah?
How can we prioritize our relationship with God over material possessions and family ties?
What are the consequences of letting worldly attachments divert us from our faith?
propositions: Believers should not let their wealth or children distract them from remembering Allah.
The remembrance of God is a fundamental aspect of one's faith, especially during the five daily prayers.
Those who prioritize material possessions and family ties over their relationship with God are considered losers.

source_text:
Verse: And donate from what We have provided for you before death comes to one of you, and you cry, “My Lord! If only You delayed me for a short while, I would give in charity and be one of the righteous.”

Tafsir: And expend in alms of that with which We have provided you before death comes to any of you whereat he will say ‘My Lord if only law-lā means hal-lā ‘why do You not’; or the lā is extra and the law is optative You would reprieve me for a short time so that I might give charity assaddaq the original tā’ of atasaddaqa has been assimilated with the sād that I might offer alms and become one of the righteous!’ by making the Pilgrimage. Ibn ‘Abbās may God be pleased with both him and his father said ‘Every person who has fallen short of his duty regarding alms and the Pilgrimage will ask to be returned to this world at the moment of death’.

hype_questions: What happens to a person who fails to give charity and complete the Pilgrimage before death?
Can one be forgiven for not fulfilling their obligations of alms and Pilgrimage after passing away?
How will a person's actions in this life affect their fate in the afterlife?
propositions: Donate from what We have provided for you before death comes to one of you.
Expend in alms of that with which We have provided you before death comes to any of you.
Every person who has fallen short of his duty regarding alms and the Pilgrimage will ask to be returned to this world at the moment of death.

source_text:
Verse: But Allah never delays a soul when its appointed time comes. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: But God will never reprieve a soul when its term has come. And God is Aware of what you do ta‘malūna; also read as the third person plural ya‘malūna ‘they do’.

hype_questions: Will God ever delay a soul's death?
Is God aware of human actions?
What happens when a person's term has come?
propositions: But Allah never delays a soul when its appointed time comes.
Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

source_text:
Verse: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth ˹constantly˺ glorifies Allah. The kingdom is His, and all praise is for Him. For He is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifies God everything proclaims His transcendence the lām of li’Llāhi is extra; mā is used instead of min in order to indicate the predominance of non-rational beings. To Him belongs the Kingdom and to Him belongs all praise and He has power over all things.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's kingdom?
How does God's power manifest in the world?
What is the significance of glorifying God?
propositions: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah.
The kingdom belongs to Allah, and all praise belongs to Him.
Allah has power over all things.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who created you, yet some of you are disbelievers while some are believers. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.

Tafsir: It is He Who created you. Then some of you are disbelievers and some of you are believers in terms of your original disposition; then He makes you die and brings you back to life in that same disposition; and God is Seer of what you do.

hype_questions: Does Allah have the power to create and control human destiny?
Can humans truly choose their beliefs, or is it predetermined?
What is the nature of God's knowledge and observation?
propositions: He created you.
Some people are disbelievers while others are believers in terms of their original disposition.
God makes you die and brings you back to life in the same disposition.
Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.

source_text:
Verse: He created the heavens and the earth for a purpose. He shaped you ˹in the womb˺, perfecting your form. And to Him is the final return.

Tafsir: He created the heavens and the earth with the truth and He shaped you and made your shapes excellent for He made the human form to be the best of forms; and to Him is the journey’s end.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creation?
How was human form created?
What is the ultimate destination?
propositions: He created the heavens and the earth with the truth.
He shaped you and made your shapes excellent.
The human form is the best of forms.

source_text:
Verse: He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And He knows whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal. For Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.

Tafsir: He knows all that is in the heavens and the earth and He knows what you hide and what you disclose and God is Knower of what is in the breasts in terms of the secrets and convictions they contain.

hype_questions: Does Allah have knowledge of our innermost thoughts?
Can Allah see into the hearts of believers and non-believers alike?
Is Allah aware of our deepest secrets?
propositions: Allah knows all that is in the heavens and the earth.
Allah knows what you hide and what you disclose.
God is Knower of what is in the breasts in terms of the secrets and convictions they contain.

source_text:
Verse: Have the stories of those who disbelieved before not reached you ˹pagans˺? They tasted the evil consequences of their doings, and they will suffer a painful punishment.

Tafsir: Has there not come to you O disbelievers of Mecca the tidings the story of those who disbelieved before and thus tasted the evil consequences of their conduct? they tasted the punishment for disbelief in this world. And there will be for them in the Hereafter a painful chastisement?

hype_questions: What are the consequences of disbelief?
Will those who disbelieved suffer a painful punishment?
How will believers be affected by the actions of those who disbelieved?
propositions: The stories of those who disbelieved before have not reached you.
They tasted the evil consequences of their doings.
There will be for them in the Hereafter a painful chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: That was because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said ˹mockingly˺, “How can humans be our guides?” So they persisted in disbelief and turned away. And Allah was not in need ˹of their faith˺. For Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

Tafsir: That chastisement in this world is because bi-annahu contains the pronoun of the matter their messengers used to bring them clear signs manifest proofs for the validity of faith but they said ‘Shall mere humans basharan is meant as generic be our guides?’ So they disbelieved and turned away from faith and God was independent without need of their faith. And God is Independent without need of His creatures Praised praiseworthy in His actions.

hype_questions: Can humans be guides for others?
What is the significance of clear proofs in faith?
Is Allah independent of human faith?
propositions: Their messengers brought them clear signs and manifest proofs.
They said, 'How can mere humans be our guides?'
Allah was not in need of their faith.
God is Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers claim they will not be resurrected. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will certainly be informed of what you have done. And that is easy for Allah.”

Tafsir: Those who disbelieve claim that an is softened its subject having been omitted that is to say annahum they will never be resurrected. Say ‘Yes indeed by my Lord! You will be resurrected; then you will be informed of what you did. And that is easy for God’.

hype_questions: Will I be resurrected?
What will happen to me after death?
How will I be held accountable for my actions?
propositions: The disbelievers claim they will not be resurrected.
You will surely be resurrected, then you will certainly be informed of what you have done.
That is easy for Allah.

source_text:
Verse: So believe in Allah and His Messenger and in the Light We have revealed. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Tafsir: So believe in God and His Messenger and the Light the Qur’ān which We have revealed. And God is Aware of what you do.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's knowledge?
How does God reveal Himself to humanity?
What is the significance of the Qur'ān in Islamic theology?
propositions: Believe in Allah and His Messenger.
The Light refers to the Qur’ān which has been revealed by Allah.
God is All-Aware of human actions.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Consider˺ the Day He will gather you ˹all˺ for the Day of Gathering—that will be the Day of mutual loss and gain. So whoever believes in Allah and does good, He will absolve them of their sins and admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. That is the ultimate triumph.

Tafsir: Mention the day when He will gather you for the Day of Gathering the Day of Resurrection that will be the Day of Dispossession on which the believers will dupe the disbelievers by occupying what would have been their places in Paradise had they believed as well as appropriating their believing spouses. And as for those who believe in God and act righteously He will absolve them of their misdeeds and admit them into gardens underneath which rivers flow a variant reading for both verbs has the first person plural wherein they will abide. That is the supreme triumph.

hype_questions: What happens to those who believe in Allah and do good on the Day of Gathering?
How will believers outsmart disbelievers on the Day of Dispossession?
What is the ultimate triumph for those who believe in Allah and act righteously?
propositions: He will gather you for the Day of Gathering.
Believers will dupe disbelievers on the Day of Dispossession.
God will absolve them of their misdeeds and admit them into gardens underneath which rivers flow.

source_text:
Verse: As for those who disbelieve and reject Our revelations, they will be the residents of the Fire, staying there forever. What an evil destination!

Tafsir: And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — the Qur’ān — those they will be the inhabitants of the Fire wherein they will abide. And what an evil journey’s end! it is.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject the Quran?
Will they be punished forever in the Fire?
Is there an evil destination for those who disbelieve?
propositions: Those who disbelieve and reject Our revelations will be the residents of the Fire.
The Qur'ān is a source of signs that are denied by those who disbelieve.
The inhabitants of the Fire will abide there forever.

source_text:
Verse: No calamity befalls ˹anyone˺ except by Allah’s Will. And whoever has faith in Allah, He will ˹rightly˺ guide their hearts ˹through adversity˺. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

Tafsir: No affliction strikes except by the leave of God by His decree. And whoever believes in God in His saying that every affliction is by His decreeing it He will guide his heart to endure it patiently. And God is Knower of all things.

hype_questions: What happens when we have faith in Allah?
How does Allah guide our hearts during adversity?
What is the nature of Allah's knowledge?
propositions: No calamity befalls anyone except by Allah’s Will.
Whoever has faith in Allah, He will rightly guide their hearts through adversity.
Allah has perfect knowledge of all things.

source_text:
Verse: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger! But if you turn away, then Our Messenger’s duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.

Tafsir: And obey God and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away then the Messenger’s duty is only to communicate the Message clearly.

hype_questions: What happens when an individual obeys Allah and the Messenger?
Can a person's disobedience affect the Messenger's role in delivering the message?
How does one ensure they are on the right path by following Allah's commandments?
propositions: Obey Allah.
Obey the Messenger.
The Messenger's duty is to deliver the Message clearly.

source_text:
Verse: Allah—there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. So in Allah let the believers put their trust.

Tafsir: God — there is no god except Him. And in God let all believers put their trust.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah?
How should believers show their trust in Allah?
What is the significance of monotheism?
propositions: Allah is the only god worthy of worship.
Believers should put their trust in God.
God is the one and only deity.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Indeed, some of your spouses and children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon, overlook, and forgive ˹their faults˺, then Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: O you who believe! Indeed among your wives and children there are enemies for you so beware of them of obeying them in neglecting the performance of good deeds such as struggling or emigrating — because the reason why this verse was revealed was precisely their obedience of them in such matters. And if you pardon them for their impeding you from such good deeds justifying it on account of the distress that parting with you causes them and overlook such enmity and forgive then assuredly God is Forgiving Merciful.

hype_questions: What are some ways to deal with enemies in our daily lives?
How can we balance our relationships with family members who may be causing us harm?
What is the importance of forgiveness in resolving conflicts?
propositions: Some spouses and children may behave as enemies towards believers.
Pardoning and forgiving such individuals can lead to a more harmonious relationship.
Struggling or emigrating for good deeds can be hindered by the presence of enemies in one's life.
The reason behind this verse is their obedience to these enemies, causing believers to neglect performing good deeds.
God is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful, and forgiving others brings about a more positive outcome.

source_text:
Verse: Your wealth and children are only a test, but Allah ˹alone˺ has a great reward.

Tafsir: Your possessions and your children are only a trial for you distracting you from the concerns of the Hereafter and God — with Him is a great reward so do not forfeit it by preoccupying yourselves with possessions and children.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of having wealth and children?
How can I avoid being distracted from my spiritual concerns?
What is the ultimate reward for living a virtuous life?
propositions: Your possessions are only a test.
Allah has a great reward for those who live a virtuous life.
You should not forfeit this reward by preoccupying yourselves with worldly concerns.

source_text:
Verse: So be mindful of Allah to the best of your ability, hear and obey, and spend in charity—that will be best for you. And whoever is saved from the selfishness of their own souls, it is they who are ˹truly˺ successful.

Tafsir: So fear God as far as you can — this abrogates His saying Fear God as He should be feared Q. 3102 — and listen to what you have been enjoined to listening disposed to accept and obey and expend in obedience to Him; that is better for your souls khayran li-anfusikum is the predicate of an implied yakun ‘that is’ and the response to the imperative. And whoever is shielded from the avarice of his own soul such are the successful the winners.

hype_questions: What is the best way to live a virtuous life according to Islamic teachings?
How can one avoid the selfishness of their own soul and achieve success?
What is the importance of spending in charity in Islam?
propositions: Be mindful of Allah to the best of your ability.
Hear and obey, and spend in charity—that will be best for you.
Fear God as far as you can — this abrogates His saying Fear God as He should be feared.

source_text:
Verse: If you lend to Allah a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. For Allah is Most Appreciative, Most Forbearing.

Tafsir: If you lend God a good loan by giving voluntary alms out of the goodness of your hearts He will multiply it for you yudā‘ifhu a variant reading has yuda‘‘ifhu from tenfold up to seven hundredfold or more for each one — this loan being the giving of voluntary alms out of the goodness of the heart — and He will forgive you whatever He will and God is Appreciative rewarding of obedience Forbearing in refraining from always punishing disobedience;

hype_questions: What happens when you give voluntary alms to God?
How does Allah respond to our good deeds?
Can we expect forgiveness from God if we show appreciation for His blessings?
propositions: If you lend God a good loan by giving voluntary alms, He will multiply it for you.
God is Appreciative and Forbearing.
Allah forgives whatever He wills when we give voluntary alms out of the goodness of our hearts.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is the˺ Knower of the seen and unseen—the Almighty, All-Wise.

Tafsir: Knower of the Unseen the hidden and the visible the disclosed the Mighty in His kingdom the Wise in His actions.

hype_questions: What is Allah's knowledge of the unseen?
How does Allah's wisdom manifest in His actions?
What is the nature of Allah's kingdom?
propositions: Allah is the Knower of both the seen and unseen.
The unseen refers to that which is hidden from human perception, including the future and the hearts of creatures.
The visible refers to that which is apparent and tangible, such as the physical world and Allah's signs.
Allah's kingdom encompasses all of existence, past, present, and future.
Allah's wisdom is evident in His actions, which are guided by His knowledge and will.
Allah's wisdom is not limited to His actions, but also includes His attributes and nature.

source_text:
Verse: O Prophet! ˹Instruct the believers:˺ When you ˹intend to˺ divorce women, then divorce them with concern for their waiting period,

Tafsir: O Prophet meaning to address his community on account of what follows; or it means say to them when you men divorce women when you intend to effect a divorce divorce them by their prescribed period at the beginning of it such that the divorce is effected while she is pure and has not been touched sexually based on the Prophet’s s explaining it in this way as reported by the two Shaykhs al-Bukhārī and Muslim. And count the prescribed period keep record of it so that you may repeal your decision before it is concluded; and fear God your Lord obey Him in His commands and prohibitions. Do not expel them from their houses nor let them go forth from them until their prescribed period is concluded unless they commit a blatant act of indecency such as adultery read mubayyana or mubayyina corresponding respectively to buyyinat ‘one that has been proven’ and bayyina ‘blatant’ in which case they are brought out in order to carry out the prescribed legal punishment against them. And those mentioned stipulations are God’s bounds; and whoever transgresses the bounds of God has verily wronged his soul. You never know it may be that God will bring something new to pass afterwards after the divorce such as a retraction in the event that it was the first or second declaration of divorce.

hype_questions: Can a man divorce his wife during the waiting period?
What happens if a woman commits adultery during her waiting period?
Can God change His mind after a divorce is declared?
propositions: When divorcing women, men must follow their prescribed waiting period.
The waiting period should be counted and recorded to allow for potential retraction of the decision.
God's laws prohibit expelling women from their homes during this time unless they commit a serious act of indecency.
Indecency, such as adultery, is punishable by law after the waiting period has ended.
Transgressing God's bounds is considered a grave sin that harms one's soul.
God may bring about new developments or retraction of previous declarations after a divorce.

source_text:
Verse: Then when they have ˹almost˺ reached the end of their waiting period, either retain them honourably or separate from them honourably. And call two of your reliable men to witness ˹either way˺—and ˹let the witnesses˺ bear true testimony for ˹the sake of˺ Allah. This is enjoined on whoever has faith in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for them,

Tafsir: Then when they have reached their term when they are near the end of their prescribed period retain them by taking them back honourably without coercion or separate from them honourably leave them to conclude their waiting period and do not compel them to go back to you. And call to witness two just men from among yourselves to witness the retraction or the separation and bear witness for the sake of God and not merely for the sake of what is being witnessed or for the sake of the man. By this is exhorted whoever believes in God and the Last Day. And whoever fears God He will make a way out for him from the distress of this world and the Hereafter;

hype_questions: What happens when someone reaches their waiting period?
How should one handle the waiting period with a companion?
Can God intervene on behalf of someone who fears Him?
propositions: When someone has reached their waiting period, they can be retained honourably or separated from them honourably.
Retaining or separating from someone during their waiting period is a matter of personal choice.
Believing in God and the Last Day is obligatory for everyone.
God will make a way out for whoever fears Him.
The waiting period is a prescribed period that must be completed before any action can be taken.

source_text:
Verse: and provide for them from sources they could never imagine. And whoever puts their trust in Allah, then He ˹alone˺ is sufficient for them. Certainly Allah achieves His Will. Allah has already set a destiny for everything.

Tafsir: and He will provide for him from whence he never expected from whence it never occurred to him. And whoever puts his trust in God regarding his affairs He will suffice him. Indeed God fulfils His command His will a variant reading for bālighun amrahu has the genitive construction bālighu amrihi. Verily God has ordained for everything even things such as comfort and hardship a measure a fixed time.

hype_questions: What are the sources from which Allah provides for His servants?
How does Allah fulfill the needs of those who put their trust in Him?
Is God's will fixed and predetermined, or can it change?
propositions: Allah provides for His servants from sources they could never imagine.
Whoever puts their trust in Allah is sufficient for them.
God fulfills His command and achieves His Will.
God has ordained a destiny for everything, including comfort and hardship with a fixed measure of time.

source_text:
Verse: As for your women past the age of menstruation, in case you do not know, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated as well. As for those who are pregnant, their waiting period ends with delivery. And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make their matters easy for them.

Tafsir: And as for those of your women who read allā’ī or allā’i in both instances no longer expect to menstruate if you have any doubts about their waiting period their prescribed waiting period shall be three months and also for those who have not yet menstruated because of their young age their period shall also be three months — both cases apply to other than those whose spouses have died; for these latter their period is prescribed in the verse they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days Q. 2234. And those who are pregnant their term the conclusion of their prescribed waiting period if divorced or if their spouses be dead shall be when they deliver. And whoever fears God He will make matters ease for him in this world and in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What is the waiting period for a woman who has not menstruated due to her young age?
How does pregnancy affect a woman's waiting period after divorce or spousal death?
Will Allah make matters easy for someone who fears Him?
propositions: The waiting period for women past the age of menstruation is three months.
For those who are pregnant, their waiting period ends with delivery.
Allah will make matters easy for whoever fears Him in this world and in the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: This is the commandment of Allah, which He has revealed to you. And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will absolve them of their sins and reward them immensely.

Tafsir: That which is mentioned regarding the prescribed waiting period is God’s command His ruling which He has revealed to you. And whoever fears God He will absolve him of his misdeeds and magnify the reward for him.

hype_questions: What is the prescribed waiting period in Islam?
How does Allah absolve individuals of their sins?
What is the reward for those who fear God?
propositions: This is the commandment of Allah.
Allah will absolve individuals of their sins if they are mindful of Him.
Allah will reward individuals immensely if they are mindful of Him.

source_text:
Verse: Let them live where you live ˹during their waiting period˺, according to your means. And do not harass them to make their stay unbearable. If they are pregnant, then maintain them until they deliver. And if they nurse your child, compensate them, and consult together courteously. But if you fail to reach an agreement, then another woman will nurse ˹the child˺ for the father.

Tafsir: Lodge them that is the divorced women where you dwell that is to say in some part of your dwellings in accordance with your means min wujdikum is an explicative supplement or a substitution of what precedes it with the repetition of the same preposition min and with an implied genitive annexation in other words something like amkinat sa‘atikum ‘house them in the places of your means and not otherwise’ and do not harass them so as to put them in straits with regard to accommodation such that they would then need to go elsewhere or be in need of maintenance to provide for themselves so that they are forced to ransom themselves from you. And if they are pregnant then maintain them until they deliver. Then if they suckle for you your children whom you have from them give them their wages for the suckling and consult together with them honourably with kindness for the sake of the children by mutual agreement on a fixed wage for the suckling. But if you both make difficulties regarding the suckling with either the father withholding payment of the wage or the mother refraining from performing it then another woman will suckle the child for him for the father and the mother should not be compelled to suckle it.

hype_questions: What is the Islamic ruling on supporting divorced women and their children?
How should a father compensate a woman for nursing his child?
What happens if a father and mother cannot agree on compensation for suckling?
propositions: Let them live where you live during their waiting period according to your means.
Do not harass them to make their stay unbearable.
If they are pregnant, then maintain them until they deliver.
If they nurse your child, compensate them and consult together courteously.
But if you fail to reach an agreement, then another woman will nurse the child for the father.

source_text:
Verse: Let the man of wealth provide according to his means. As for the one with limited resources, let him provide according to whatever Allah has given him. Allah does not require of any soul beyond what He has given it. After hardship, Allah will bring about ease.

Tafsir: Let the affluent man expend on the divorced or the suckling woman out of his affluence. And let he whose provision has been straitened restricted for him expend of what God has given him in accordance with his means. God does not charge any soul save except with what He has given it. God will assuredly bring about ease after hardship — which He indeed did by way of the Muslim conquests.

hype_questions: What is the Islamic obligation for those with wealth to distribute?
How should individuals with limited resources contribute to society?
Will Allah ever bring about ease after hardship?
propositions: The affluent man should expend on the divorced or the suckling woman out of his affluence.
He whose provision has been straitened should restrict himself and expend of what God has given him in accordance with his means.
God does not charge any soul save except with what He has given it.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Imagine˺ how many societies rebelled against the commandments of their Lord and His messengers, so We called each ˹society˺ to a severe account and subjected them to a horrible punishment.

Tafsir: And how many ka’ayyin the kāf is the genitive prepositional particle which has been added to ayy ‘which’ to give the meaning of kam ‘how many’ a town — that is to say many a town meaning its inhabitants disobeyed the command of its Lord and His messengers then We called it in the Hereafter — even if it has not yet arrived God says so because of the fact that it will surely come to pass — to a severe reckoning and chastised it with a dire chastisement read nukran or nukuran namely the chastisement of the Fire.

hype_questions: What happens to societies that disobey their Lord and His messengers?
How will the Hereafter be dealt with those who have disobeyed?
What is the nature of the chastisement that awaits those who disobey?
propositions: Many societies rebelled against the commandments of their Lord and His messengers.
We called each society to a severe account and subjected them to a horrible punishment.
God says so because of the fact that it will surely come to pass — to a severe reckoning.

source_text:
Verse: So they tasted the evil consequences of their doings, and the outcome of their doings was ˹total˺ loss.

Tafsir: So it tasted the evil consequences of its conduct the punishment for it and the consequence of its conduct was utter loss failure and destruction.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of one's actions?
How does Allah punish those who disobey Him?
What is the ultimate outcome for those who fail to follow His guidance?
propositions: The evil consequences of their doings were tasted.
The punishment for their conduct was utter loss, failure, and destruction.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has ˹also˺ prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O  people of reason and faith. Allah has indeed revealed to you a Reminder,

Tafsir: God has prepared for them a severe chastisement the reiteration of the threat is for emphasis. So fear God O people of pith O possessors of intellect you who believe! this is a description of the vocative or an explication of it God has certainly revealed to you a source of remembrance that is the Qur’ān;

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's punishment for those who disbelieve?
How does Allah reveal His message to believers?
What is the significance of the Qur'ān as a source of remembrance?
propositions: Allah has prepared a severe chastisement for those who disbelieve.
You should fear Allah, O people of reason and faith.
God has revealed to you a source of remembrance, namely the Qur'ān.

source_text:
Verse: ˹and sent˺ a messenger reciting to you Allah’s revelations, making things clear so that He may bring those who believe and do good out of darkness and into light. And whoever believes in Allah and does good will be admitted by Him into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. Allah will have indeed granted them an excellent provision.

Tafsir: a messenger that is Muhammad (s) rasūlan is in the accusative because of an implied verb that is to say wa-arsala ‘and He sent you a messenger’ reciting to you the clear signs of God read mubayyanāt or mubayyināt as explained above that He may bring forth those who believe and perform righteous deeds after the arrival of the remembrance and the Messenger from darkness the disbelief to which they adhered to light the faith that was established in them after a life of disbelief. And those who believe in God and act righteously He will admit them a variant reading has the first person plural nudkhilhu ‘We will admit them’ into gardens underneath which rivers flow wherein they will abide forever. God has verily made a good provision for him namely the provision of Paradise the bliss of which never ends.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reward for those who believe in Allah and do good deeds?
How will Allah admit those who believe and act righteously into Gardens under which rivers flow?
What is the nature of the provision granted to those who are admitted into Paradise?
propositions: Allah sent a messenger reciting to you His revelations.
He may bring those who believe and do good out of darkness and into light.
God will admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever.
Allah has granted them an excellent provision in Paradise.
The bliss of Paradise never ends.

source_text:
Verse: Allah is the One Who created seven heavens ˹in layers˺, and likewise for the earth. The ˹divine˺ command descends between them so you may know that Allah is Most Capable of everything and that Allah certainly encompasses all things in ˹His˺ knowledge.

Tafsir: God it is Who created seven heavens and of earth the like thereof that is to say seven earths. The command the revelation descends between them between the heavens and the earth Gabriel descends with it from the seventh heaven to the seventh earth that you may know li-ta‘lamū is semantically connected to an omitted clause that is to say ‘He apprises you of this creation and this sending down that you may know’ that God has power over all things and that God encompasses all things in knowledge.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's creation?
How does Allah's command descend between the heavens and earth?
What does it mean to know Allah's power and knowledge?
propositions: Allah created seven heavens.
The divine command descends between the heavens and the earth.
Gabriel descends with the revelation from the seventh heaven to the seventh earth.
Li-ta‘lamū means 'He apprises you of this creation and this sending down'.
God has power over all things.
God encompasses all things in knowledge.

source_text:
Verse: O Prophet! Why do you prohibit ˹yourself˺ from what Allah has made lawful to you, seeking to please your wives? And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: O Prophet! Why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you in terms of your Coptic handmaiden Māriya — when he lay with her in the house of Hafsa who had been away but who upon returning and finding out became upset by the fact that this had taken place in her own house and on her own bed — by saying ‘She is unlawful for me!’ seeking by making her unlawful for you to please your wives? And God is Forgiving Merciful having forgiven you this prohibition.

hype_questions: What is the significance of Māriya in Islamic teachings?
How does Allah's mercy apply to human actions?
What are the implications of a husband's prohibition on his wife?
propositions: The Prophet prohibits himself from what Allah has made lawful for him.
God laid down no restrictions on marriage with Coptic handmaidens.
A husband cannot prohibit his wife from marrying another man without justification.

source_text:
Verse: Allah has already ordained for you ˹believers˺ the way to absolve yourselves from your oaths. For Allah is your Guardian. And He is the All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Tafsir: Verily God has prescribed He has made lawful for you when necessary the absolution of your oaths to absolve them by expiation as mentioned in the sūrat al-Mā’ida Q. 589 and the forbidding of sexual relations with a handmaiden counts as an oath so did the Prophet s expiate? Muqātil b. Sulaymān said ‘He set free a slave in expiation for his prohibition of Māriya’; whereas al-Hasan al-Basrī said ‘He never expiated because the Prophet s has been forgiven all errors’. And God is your Protector your Helper and He is the Knower the Wise.

hype_questions: Can a prophet expiate for his mistakes?
What is the value of expiating for a handmaiden in Islam?
Does God forgive all errors committed by prophets?
propositions: Allah has ordained believers the way to absolve themselves from their oaths.
God has made lawful for believers the absolution of their oaths when necessary, with expiation.
The Prophet s did not expiate for his prohibition of Māriya'.
Muqātil b. Sulaymān said that the Prophet s set free a slave in expiation for his prohibition of Māriya'.
Al-Hasan al-Basrī said that the Prophet s has been forgiven all errors.
God is your Guardian, Protector, Helper, and Knower of the Wise.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Remember˺ when the Prophet had ˹once˺ confided something to one of his wives, then when she disclosed it ˹to another wife˺ and Allah made it known to him, he presented ˹to her˺ part of what was disclosed and overlooked a part. So when he informed her of it, she exclaimed, “Who told you this?” He replied, “I was informed by the All-Knowing, All-Aware.”

Tafsir: And mention when the Prophet confided to one of his wives namely Hafsa a certain matter which was his prohibition of Māriya telling her ‘Do not reveal it!’; but when she divulged it to ‘Ā’isha reckoning there to be no blame in doing such a thing and God apprised him He informed him of it of what had been divulged he announced part of it to Hafsa and passed over part out of graciousness on his part. So when he told her about it she said ‘Who told you this?’ He said ‘I was told by the Knower the Aware’ namely God.

hype_questions: Can a prophet's confidence be breached without divine permission?
How does a prophet balance the need for secrecy with the need to inform others?
What role does God play in guiding a prophet's actions?
propositions: The Prophet confided a matter to Hafsa, prohibiting her from revealing it to Māriya.
Hafsa divulged the information to Ā'isha, who believed there was no blame in doing so.
God apprised the Prophet of the situation and informed him of what had been disclosed.
The Prophet announced part of the information to Hafsa while overlooking a part due to his graciousness.
Hafsa asked the Prophet who told him about the matter, to which he replied 'I was informed by God'.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It will be better˺ if you ˹wives˺ both turn to Allah in repentance, for your hearts have certainly faltered. But if you ˹continue to˺ collaborate against him, then ˹know that˺ Allah Himself is his Guardian. And Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels are ˹all˺ his supporters as well.

Tafsir: If the two of you namely Hafsa and ‘Ā’isha repent to God … for your hearts were certainly inclined towards the prohibition of Māriya that is to say your keeping this secret despite knowing the Prophet’s s dislike of it which is itself a sin the response to the conditional ‘if the two of you repent to God’ has been omitted to be understood as ‘it will be accepted of both of you’; the use of the plural qulūb ‘hearts’ instead of the dual qalbayn ‘both your hearts’ is on account of the cumbersomeness of putting two duals together in what is effectively the same word; and if you support one another tazzāharā the original second tā’ of tatazāharā has been assimilated with the zā’; a variant reading has it without this assimilation tazāharā against him that is the Prophet in what he is averse to then know that God He huwa a pronoun for separation is indeed his Protector His supporter and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers Abū Bakr and ‘Umar may God be pleased with both of them wa-Jibrīlu wa-sālihu’l-mu’minīna is a supplement to the syntactical locus of the subject of inna sc. ‘God’ who will also be his supporters and the angels furthermore further to the support of God and those mentioned are his supporters assistants of his in supporting him to prevail over both of you.

hype_questions: What happens when two people repent to Allah?
Who are the supporters of Allah in this situation?
What is the consequence of not supporting one another?
propositions: If you both turn to Allah in repentance, it will be better.
Your hearts have faltered due to your keeping the secret of Māriya despite knowing the Prophet's dislike of it.
Allah Himself is his Guardian and Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels are his supporters as well.

source_text:
Verse: Perhaps, if he were to divorce you ˹all˺, his Lord would replace you with better wives who are submissive ˹to Allah˺, faithful ˹to Him˺, devout, repentant, dedicated to worship and fasting—previously married or virgins.

Tafsir: It may be that if he divorces you that is if the Prophet divorces his wives his Lord will give him in your stead read yubaddilahu or yubdilahu wives better than you azwājan khayran minkunna is the predicate of ‘asā ‘it may be’ the sentence being the response to the conditional — the replacement of his wives by God never took place because the condition of his divorcing them never arose — women submissive to God affirming Islam believing faithful obedient penitent devout given to fasting — or given to emigrating in God’s way — previously married and virgins.

hype_questions: What are the qualities of a good wife in Islam?
How does God replace a divorced woman with better wives?
What are the conditions for a man to be rewarded with better wives?
propositions: If he divorces you, his Lord will give him better wives who are submissive, faithful, devout, repentant, and dedicated to worship and fasting.
The replacement of his wives by God never took place because the condition of his divorcing them never arose.
Women who are submissive to God, affirming Islam, believing, faithful, obedient, penitent, devout, given to fasting, or emigrating in God's way, are considered good wives.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, overseen by formidable and severe angels, who never disobey whatever Allah orders—always doing as commanded.

Tafsir: O you who believe! Guard yourselves and your families by enjoining obedience to God against a Fire whose fuel is disbelieving people and stones such as those idols of theirs made of that stone — the meaning is that it is extremely hot fuelled by the above-mentioned unlike the fire of this world which is fuelled by wood and the like — over which stand angels its keepers — numbering nineteen as will be stated in sūrat al-Muddaththir Q. 7430 — stern a sternness of the heart mighty in their power of assault who do not disobey God in what He commands them mā amarahum is a substitution for His Majesty ‘God’ in other words they do not disobey the command of God but do what they are commanded — this is reiterated for emphasis; the verse is meant as a threat to deter believers from apostatising and for hypocrites who believe only with their tongues and not with their hearts.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Fire that Allah warns against?
How do angels relate to this Fire, and what is their role?
What is the significance of obedience to God in avoiding this Fire?
propositions: Believers should protect themselves and their families from a Fire.
The Fire is fueled by disbelieving people and stones, including idols.
Angels oversee the Fire and are stern in their power.
Obedience to God is essential for avoiding this Fire.
Hypocrites who only claim faith with their tongues will be deterred from apostasy by this warning.

source_text:
Verse: ˹The deniers will then be told,˺ “O disbelievers! Make no excuses this Day! You are only rewarded for what you used to do.”

Tafsir: ‘O you who disbelieve! Do not make any excuses today — this is said to them upon their entering the Fire — in other words because this excusing will be of no use to you. You are only being requited for what you used to do’ that is only the due requital thereof.

hype_questions: What happens when someone disbelieves in God?
Can excuses be made on the Day of Reckoning?
How are people requited for their past actions?
propositions: The deniers will be told to make no excuses on the Day of Reckoning.
Disbelievers are only rewarded for what they used to do.
Excusing oneself on the Day of Reckoning is of no use.

source_text:
Verse: O believers! Turn to Allah in sincere repentance, so your Lord may absolve you of your sins and admit you into Gardens, under which rivers flow, on the Day Allah will not disgrace the Prophet or the believers with him. Their light will shine ahead of them and on their right. They will say, “Our Lord! Perfect our light for us, and forgive us. ˹For˺ You are truly Most Capable of everything.”

Tafsir: O you who believe! Repent to God with sincere repentance read nasūhan or nusūhan a truthful repentance so that one does not return to committing that sin again nor have the desire to return to it. It may be that your Lord ‘asā an expression denoting ‘a hope’ that will be realised will absolve you of your misdeeds and admit you into gardens orchards underneath which rivers flow on the day when God will not let down by admitting into the Fire the Prophet and those who believe with him. Their light will be running before them in front of them and it will be on their right. They will say yaqūlūna this denotes the beginning of a new syntactically independent sentence ‘Our Lord! Perfect our light for us towards Paradise — whereas the hypocrites their light will be extinguished — and forgive us Our Lord. Assuredly You have power over all things’.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate goal of sincere repentance?
How will believers be treated on the Day of Judgment?
What is the difference between the light of believers and hypocrites?
propositions: Believers should turn to Allah with sincere repentance.
Allah may absolve believers of their sins and admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow on the Day of Judgment.
The Prophet and believers will be admitted into Paradise, where their light will shine ahead of them and on their right.
Believers' light will be perfect and running before them, while hypocrites' light will be extinguished.
Allah forgives believers and has power over all things.

source_text:
Verse: O Prophet! Struggle against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be firm with them. Hell will be their home. What an evil destination!

Tafsir: O Prophet! Struggle against the disbelievers with the sword and the hypocrites by the tongue and with argument and be stern with them in rebuke and hatred. For their abode will be Hell — and what an evil journey’s end! it is.

hype_questions: What happens to those who struggle against believers?
How do hypocrites respond to criticism?
What is the ultimate destination of those who reject faith?
propositions: Struggle against disbelievers with the sword and by argument.
Hypocrites are opposed by the tongue and rebuke.
Hell is their abode.
The journey to Hell is an evil one.

source_text:
Verse: Allah sets forth an example for the disbelievers: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. Each was married to one of Our righteous servants, yet betrayed them. So their husbands were of no benefit to them against Allah whatsoever. Both were told, “Enter the Fire, along with the others!”

Tafsir: God has struck a similitude for those who disbelieve the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants yet they betrayed them in their religion for they both disbelieved — Noah’s wife called Wāhila used to say to his people that he was a madman while Lot’s wife called Wā‘ila used to tell his people the whereabouts of his guests when they stayed with him at night by lighting a fire and during the day by making smoke. So they that is Noah and Lot did not avail the two women in any way against God against His chastisement and it was said to the two women ‘Enter both of you the Fire along with the incomers’ from among the disbelievers of the peoples of Noah and Lot.

hype_questions: What happens when a believer's wife betrays them?
How do disbelievers respond to righteous servants?
Can anyone escape Allah's chastisement?
propositions: Allah sets forth an example for the disbelievers: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot.
Both were told, 'Enter the Fire, along with the others!'
Noah's wife called Wāhila used to say to his people that he was a madman.
Lot's wife called Wā‘ila used to tell his people the whereabouts of his guests when they stayed with him at night by lighting a fire and during the day by making smoke.
So they that is Noah and Lot did not avail the two women in any way against God against His chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: And Allah sets forth an example for the believers: the wife of Pharaoh, who prayed, “My Lord! Build me a house in Paradise near You, deliver me from Pharaoh and his ˹evil˺ doing, and save me from the wrongdoing people.”

Tafsir: And God has struck a similitude for those who believe the wife of Pharaoh — she believed in Moses her name was Āsiya; Pharaoh chastised her by tying her hands and feet to pegs and placing a huge millstone on her chest and having her laid out in the sun; but when those in charge of her would leave her the angels would come to shade her — when she said during her torture ‘My Lord build for me a home near You in Paradise — so He disclosed for her a veil of the Unseen and she saw it which in turn alleviated for her the torture — and deliver me from Pharaoh and his work his torture and deliver me from the evildoing folk’ the followers of his Pharaoh’s religion whereat God took unto Himself her spirit in death. Ibn Kaysān said ‘She was raised to Paradise alive where she eats and drinks’.

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who believe in Allah?
How did the wife of Pharaoh endure her torture?
What happened to the spirit of the wife of Pharaoh after death?
propositions: Allah sets forth an example for the believers: the wife of Pharaoh.
The wife of Pharaoh prayed to Allah to build a house in Paradise near Him.
Pharaoh chastised the wife of Pharaoh by tying her hands and feet to pegs and placing a huge millstone on her chest.
When the angels came to shade her, she saw a veil of the Unseen which alleviated her torture.
God took unto Himself her spirit in death.

source_text:
Verse: ˹There is˺ also ˹the example of˺ Mary, the daughter of ’Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her ˹womb˺ through Our angel ˹Gabriel˺. She testified to the words of her Lord and His Scriptures, and was one of the ˹sincerely˺ devout.

Tafsir: And Mary wa-Maryama is a supplement to imra’ata Fir‘awna daughter of ‘Imrān who preserved the chastity of her womb so We breathed into it of Our Spirit namely Gabriel — when he breathed into the opening of her shirt by God’s creation of this action of his which reached her womb thus conceiving Jesus — and she confirmed the words of her Lord His prescriptions and His revealed Scriptures and she was of the obedient one of the obedient folk.

hype_questions: What is the story of Mary, the daughter of Imran?
How did Gabriel play a role in Mary's life?
What was Jesus' conception like?
propositions: Mary, the daughter of 'Imran, guarded her chastity.
We breathed into Mary's womb through Our angel, Gabriel.
Mary testified to the words of her Lord and His Scriptures.
God created the action of Gabriel breathing into the opening of her shirt.
Jesus was conceived in Mary's womb through this divine action.
Mary confirmed the words of her Lord and followed His prescriptions.

source_text:
Verse: Blessed is the One in Whose Hands rests all authority. And He is Most Capable of everything.

Tafsir: Blessed exalted above the attributes of created beings is He in Whose hand at Whose disposal is all sovereignty all authority and power and He has power over all things.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate source of authority?
Who holds sovereignty over all things?
What are the limits of God's power?
propositions: God is the one in whose hands rests all authority.
God has power over all things.
All sovereignty and power belong to God.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is the One˺ Who created death and life in order to test which of you is best in deeds. And He is the Almighty, All-Forgiving.

Tafsir: He Who created death in this world and life in the Hereafter — or both of them in this world since the sperm-drop is imbued with life life being that power by which sensation becomes possible death being the opposite of this or the non-existence of it — these being two alternative opinions; in the case of the latter life in the Hereafter ‘creation’ implies ‘ordainment’ — that He may try you that He may test you in this life to see which of you is best in conduct which of you is most obedient to God and He is the Mighty in His vengeance against those who disobey Him the Forgiving to those who repent to Him;

hype_questions: What is the purpose of death and life in Islam?
How does God test His creation?
What happens to those who disobey God?
propositions: God created death and life.
Death is the opposite of life.
God tests His creation to see which one is best in conduct.
God is the Mighty in His vengeance against those who disobey Him.
God is the Forgiving to those who repent to Him.

source_text:
Verse: ˹He is the One˺ Who created seven heavens, one above the other. You will never see any imperfection in the creation of the Most Compassionate. So look again: do you see any flaws?

Tafsir: Who created seven heavens in layers one above the other without any contact between them. You do not see in the Compassionate One’s creation of these or of other things any irregularity any disparity or discordance. Then cast your eyes again turn them toward the heaven Do you see in it any fissure? any cracks or ruptures?

hype_questions: Does the creation of the Most Compassionate have any flaws?
Can we see imperfections in the creation of God?
Is there any irregularity or disparity in the creation of heaven?
propositions: The Most Compassionate created seven heavens one above the other.
There is no contact between the seven heavens.
The creation of the Most Compassionate has no irregularities or disparities.
You do not see any fissures or cracks in the heaven.
