source_text:
Verse: Then look again and again—your sight will return frustrated and weary.

Tafsir: Then cast your eyes yet again once and then twice and your sight will return to you humbled abject on account of it not perceiving any fissure and wearied unable to see any fissure.

hype_questions: What happens when we repeatedly look at something without finding what we're searching for?
How does repeated failure affect our perception and attitude?
Can patience lead to humility?
propositions: Your sight will return frustrated and weary.
Your sight will return humbled, abject, and wearied due to not perceiving any fissure.
You will be unable to see any fissure.

source_text:
Verse: And indeed, We adorned the lowest heaven with ˹stars like˺ lamps, and made them ˹as missiles˺ for stoning ˹eavesdropping˺ devils, for whom We have also prepared the torment of the Blaze.

Tafsir: And verily We have adorned the lowest heaven the one closest to the earth with lamps with stars and made them missiles against the devils should they attempt to listen by stealth in which case a meteor of fire detaches itself from the star just like a brand is taken from a fire and either kills that jinn or deprives him of his senses it is not that the star itself is displaced from its position; and We have prepared for them the chastisement of the Blaze the ignited Fire.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of adorning the lowest heaven with lamps and stars?
How do devils attempt to listen by stealth, and what happens to them?
What is the chastisement prepared for devils who disobey Allah?
propositions: Allah adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and stars.
The purpose of adorning the lowest heaven is to serve as missiles against devils who attempt to listen by stealth.
When a meteor of fire detaches itself from a star, it either kills the jinn or deprives him of his senses.
Allah has prepared the chastisement of the Blaze, which is ignited Fire.

source_text:
Verse: Those who disbelieve in their Lord will suffer the punishment of Hell. What an evil destination!

Tafsir: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord there is the chastisement of Hell and what an evil journey’s end! it is.

hype_questions: What happens to those who reject their Lord?
Will those who disbelieve in Allah face punishment?
What is the fate of those who refuse to believe in their Creator?
propositions: Those who disbelieve in their Lord will suffer the punishment of Hell.
Disbelievers in their Lord will receive the chastisement of Hell.
There is the punishment of Hell for those who reject their Lord.

source_text:
Verse: When they are tossed into it, they will hear its roaring as it boils over,

Tafsir: When they are flung into it they hear it blaring producing a horrid sound like that of an ass as it seethes

hype_questions: What is the sound of Qiyamah?
How will people react when they are flung into Qiyamah?
What is the nature of the torment in Qiyamah?
propositions: When someone is tossed into Qiyamah, they will hear a loud roaring sound.
Qiyamah produces a horrid sound similar to that of an ass braying.
The torment in Qiyamah is characterized by a severe and unpleasant noise.

source_text:
Verse: almost bursting in fury. Every time a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them, “Did a warner not come to you?”

Tafsir: almost exploding tamayyazu a variant reading has the original form tatamayyazu ripped apart with rage in wrath against the disbelievers. Whenever a host a group of them is flung into it its keepers ask them an interrogation of rebuke ‘Did there not come to you a warner?’ a messenger to warn you of God’s chastisement.

hype_questions: Did a warner not come to warn you of God's chastisement?
What is the chastisement that God has in store for those who reject His warnings?
How will God punish those who refuse to listen to His messengers?
propositions: A group cast into hell will be asked if a warner did not come to them.
God's chastisement is a warning given to those who reject His message.
Those who reject God's warnings will face punishment from God.

source_text:
Verse: They will reply, “Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied and said, ‘Allah has revealed nothing. You are extremely astray.’”

Tafsir: They will say ‘Yes a warner did indeed come to us but we denied and said “God has not revealed anything; you are assuredly in great error”’ this last words may be the words of the angels spoken to the disbelievers when they are told of the denial or they may belong to the words of the disbelievers spoken to the warners.

hype_questions: What is the nature of a warner in Islam?
How do believers respond to a warner?
What are the consequences of denying the revelation?
propositions: A warner did come to us.
We denied the message of Allah.
Allah has not revealed anything.
You are assuredly in great error.

source_text:
Verse: And they will lament, “If only we had listened and reasoned, we would not be among the residents of the Blaze!”

Tafsir: And they will say ‘Had we listened that is listening so as to understand or comprehended that is comprehension entailing reflection upon the truth we would not have been among the inhabitants of the Blaze’.

hype_questions: If only we had listened to guidance, would we be saved from punishment?
What happens when we fail to understand divine messages?
Can reflection on truth lead us away from destruction?
propositions: They will lament if they had listened and reasoned.
Listening and reasoning could have saved them from the Blaze.
Understanding divine messages is crucial for salvation.

source_text:
Verse: And so they will confess their sins. So away with the residents of the Blaze!

Tafsir: Thus they will confess when confession is of no avail their sin which was their denial of the warners. So away suhqan or suhuqan with the inhabitants of the Blaze! so far away may they be from God’s mercy.

hype_questions: What happens to those who deny the warners?
How far away are the inhabitants of the Blaze from God's mercy?
Can confession be of any avail for those who have denied the warners?
propositions: They will confess their sins.
Confession is of no avail for those who deny the warners.
The inhabitants of the Blaze are far away from God's mercy.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those in awe of their Lord without seeing Him will have forgiveness and a mighty reward.

Tafsir: Assuredly those who fear their Lord in secret while they are absent from people’s eyes being obedient to Him in secret such that openly before people it is all the more likely that they fear their Lord — there will be for them forgiveness and a great reward namely Paradise.

hype_questions: What is the condition for receiving forgiveness and a mighty reward in Islam?
How can one ensure forgiveness and a great reward from Allah?
What is the ultimate goal of fearing one's Lord?
propositions: Those who fear their Lord without seeing Him will have forgiveness and a mighty reward.
Fear of Allah is obligatory for believers, both in secret and openly.
Paradise is the ultimate reward for those who fear Allah sincerely.

source_text:
Verse: Whether you speak secretly or openly—He surely knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.

Tafsir: And whether you keep secret O people your speech or proclaim it He indeed exalted be He is Knower of what is in the breasts of what they contain so how much more so is He Knower in the case of what you utter openly — the reason for the revelation of this verse was that the idolaters said to one another ‘Speak secretly and Muhammad’s god will not hear you’.

hype_questions: Does Allah know what's in our hearts?
Can we hide the truth from Allah?
What happens when we speak openly about our faith?
propositions: Allah knows best what is hidden in the heart.
Allah is aware of what is in the breasts of those who contain it.
Allah is more knowledgeable about what is uttered openly than what is kept secret.

source_text:
Verse: How could He not know His Own creation? For He ˹alone˺ is the Most Subtle, All-Aware.

Tafsir: Will He Who has created not know? what you keep secret in other words will His knowledge of things be precluded by such secret speech? And He is the Subtle in His knowledge the Aware therein.

hype_questions: Can a creator be unaware of their own creation?
Does secrecy limit one's knowledge?
Is the creator's awareness affected by human concealment?
propositions: God is aware of His creation.
God's knowledge is not limited by human secrets.
God's subtlety and awareness are inherent in His nature.

source_text:
Verse: He is the One Who smoothed out the earth for you, so move about in its regions and eat from His provisions. And to Him is the resurrection ˹of all˺.

Tafsir: It is He Who made the earth tractable for you easy for you to walk on; so walk in its flanks and eat of His provision that has been created for you; and to Him is the resurrection from the graves for the Requital.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of Allah's creation of the earth?
How should humans interact with the earth according to Islamic teachings?
What is the ultimate goal of human existence in Islam?
propositions: Allah smoothed out the earth for humans.
Humans should walk on the earth and eat from its provisions.
The resurrection is a reality in Islam.

source_text:
Verse: Do you feel secure that the One Who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you up as it quakes violently?

Tafsir: Are you secure read a-amintum pronouncing both hamzas fully or by not pronouncing the second one inserting an alif between it and the other one or without the insertion but replacing it with an alif instead in thinking that He Who is in the heaven that He Whose authority and power is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you an yakhsifa substitutes for man ‘He Who’ while it quakes? while it moves underneath you and rises above you?

hype_questions: Will the earth swallow me up if God is in heaven?
What happens when God moves underneath and above me?
Is God's authority limited to his power in heaven?
propositions: The One Who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you up.
God's authority and power are in the heaven.
He Who quakes will move underneath and above you.

source_text:
Verse: Or do you feel secure that the One Who is in heaven will not unleash upon you a storm of stones. Only then would you know how ˹serious˺ My warning was!

Tafsir: Are you secure in thinking that He Who is in the heaven will not unleash an yursila substitutes for man ‘He Who’ upon you a squall of pebbles? a wind hurling pebbles at you. But you will soon come to know upon seeing the chastisement with your own eyes the nature of My warning My warning of chastisement in other words you will soon see that it was true.

hype_questions: Will the One Who is in heaven unleash a storm of stones upon me?
What will happen to me if I don't take precautions?
How will I know that My warning was serious?
propositions: The One Who is in heaven may unleash a storm of stones upon you.
You should be patient and prepared for the chastisement.
You will soon come to know the nature of My warning with your own eyes.

source_text:
Verse: And certainly those before them denied ˹as well˺, then how severe was My response!

Tafsir: And verily those communities who were before them denied then see how was My rebuttal! how was My rebuttal of them in destroying them when they denied in other words how it was true.

hype_questions: What happens to those who deny the truth?
How does God respond to those who reject Him?
What are the consequences of denying God's existence?
propositions: Those communities before them denied the truth.
God responded to their denial with severe consequences.
God destroyed those communities when they denied Him.

source_text:
Verse: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Most Compassionate. Indeed, He is All-Seeing of everything.

Tafsir: Or have they not seen the birds above them in the air spreading their wings and closing? their wings after spreading them? in other words read wa-yaqbidna as wa-qābidātin similar to sāffātin ‘spreading’. Nothing sustains them from falling either when they are spreading them or closing them except the Compassionate One by His power. Indeed He is Seer of all things. The meaning is have they not inferred from the fact that the birds are able to remain in the air that We have the power to do with them what has been mentioned above as well as inflicting upon them other kinds of chastisement?

hype_questions: Can a creator be held accountable for the actions of their creations?
Is there a limit to a creator's power?
What is the nature of a creator's relationship with their creations?
propositions: The Most Compassionate One sustains all things.
Nothing sustains birds from falling except the Compassionate One by His power.
We have the power to do with them what we will, as well as inflicting upon them other kinds of chastisement.

source_text:
Verse: Also, which ˹powerless˺ force will come to your help instead of the Most Compassionate? Indeed, the disbelievers are only ˹lost˺ in delusion.

Tafsir: Or who am-man the subject is it hādhā its predicate that alladhī a substitution for hādhā ‘is it’ will be an army supporters for you lakum belongs to the relative clause of alladhī ‘that’ to help you yansurukum is an adjectival qualification of jundun ‘an army’ besides the Compassionate One? that is to say other than Him who is there that will be able to avert His chastisement from you in other words you have no helper. The disbelievers are in nothing but delusion Satan has deluded them into believing that the chastisement will not befall them.

hype_questions: What force can help me instead of Allah?
Will anyone be able to avert Allah's chastisement from me?
Can I avoid Allah's punishment?
propositions: There is no force that will come to your help instead of the Most Compassionate.
The disbelievers are only lost in delusion.
You have no helper besides the Compassionate One.

source_text:
Verse: Or who is it that will provide for you if He withholds His provision? In fact, they persist in arrogance and aversion ˹to the truth˺.

Tafsir: Or who is it that will provide for you if He the Compassionate One withholds His provision? that is to say if He withholds the rain from you the response to the conditional has been omitted but is indicated by what preceded it namely the statement to the effect ‘who will provide for you?’ and so the response would be you have no provider other than Him. Nay but they persist in disdain and aversion moving away further from the truth.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate source of provision for humanity?
How does one's behavior reflect their relationship with the divine?
What happens when individuals turn away from the truth?
propositions: If Allah withholds His provision, who will provide for you?
Allah is the sole provider for humanity.
When Allah withholds rain, it signifies a response to the question of who will provide for you.
Despite being reminded of their dependence on Allah, people persist in arrogance and aversion to the truth.

source_text:
Verse: Who is ˹rightly˺ guided: the one who crawls facedown or the one who walks upright on the Straight Path?

Tafsir: Is he who walks cast down fallen on his face more rightly guided or he who walks upright on a straight path? the predicate of the second man ‘who’ has been omitted but is indicated by the predicate of the first namely ahdā ‘more rightly guided’; the similitude refers to the believer and the disbeliever and to which of the two is more rightly guided.

hype_questions: Is walking upright on a straight path considered more righteous than crawling facedown?
Which one is more rightly guided, the believer or the disbeliever?
What does it mean to be 'more rightly guided' in this context?
propositions: The one who crawls facedown is not more rightly guided than he who walks upright on the Straight Path.
He who walks upright on a straight path is more rightly guided than he who walks cast down fallen on his face.
A person is more rightly guided if they are a believer rather than a disbeliever.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “He is the One Who brought you into being and gave you hearing, sight, and intellect. ˹Yet˺ you hardly give any thanks.”

Tafsir: Say ‘It is He Who created you and endowed you with hearing and sight and hearts. Little do you thank!’ mā tashkurūna mā is extra; the sentence itself is a new independent one informing of how extremely little they give thanks for these graces.

hype_questions: What are some things that people often take for granted?
How do humans typically respond to blessings from a higher power?
Can gratitude be cultivated and strengthened?
propositions: The Prophet says, 'He is the One Who brought you into being'.
He gave you hearing, sight, and intellect.
You hardly give any thanks for these graces.
It is He Who created you.
He endowed you with hearts.
Little do you thank!

source_text:
Verse: ˹Also˺ say, “He is the One Who has dispersed you ˹all˺ over the earth, and to Him you will ˹all˺ be gathered.”

Tafsir: Say ‘It is He Who multiplied you created you on earth and to Him you will be gathered’ for the Reckoning.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creation?
How will we be held accountable for our actions?
What happens to us after death?
propositions: He multiplied you.
You were created on earth.
To Him you will be gathered.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Still˺ they ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”

Tafsir: And they say to the believers ‘When will this promise be fulfilled the promise of the gathering if you are truthful?’ about it.

hype_questions: Will the threat come to pass?
When will the promise be fulfilled?
What is the meaning of the gathering?
propositions: They ask when this threat will come to pass.
The believers say that the promise of the gathering will be fulfilled if they are truthful.
This promise refers to a future event.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “That knowledge is with Allah alone, and I am only sent with a clear warning.”

Tafsir: Say ‘The knowledge of its coming is only with God and I am but a plain warner’ one whose warning is plain.

hype_questions: What is the nature of knowledge in Islam?
Who is responsible for conveying divine messages?
What does it mean to be a 'plain warner'?
propositions: Knowledge is exclusive to Allah.
The Prophet Muhammad was sent as a clear warning.
A plain warner conveys a message in an uncomplicated manner.

source_text:
Verse: Then when they see the torment drawing near, the faces of the disbelievers will become gloomy, and it will be said ˹to them˺, “This is what you claimed would never come.”

Tafsir: But when they see it that is the chastisement after the gathering near at hand the faces of those who disbelieved will be awry blackened and it will be said that is the keepers of Hell will say to them ‘This is that chastisement which the warning of which you used to make claims about’ claims to the effect that you would not be resurrected — this is the narration of a situation that will take place in the future and which has been expressed using the past tense in order to confirm that it will actually take place.

hype_questions: What happens when the disbelievers face their torment?
Will those who claim they will not be resurrected actually face judgment?
How do the keepers of Hell respond to the disbelievers?
propositions: When the torment approaches, the faces of the disbelievers become gloomy.
The chastisement after the gathering near at hand is what the disbelievers claimed would never come.
Those who claim they will not be resurrected will actually face judgment.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Consider this: whether Allah causes me and those with me to die or shows us mercy, who will save the disbelievers from a painful punishment?”

Tafsir: Say ‘Have you considered If God destroys me and those with me of believers by His chastisement as you would have it or has mercy on us and does not chastise us who then will protect the disbelievers from a painful chastisement?’ in other words they will have no protector from it.

hype_questions: What would happen to disbelievers if Allah shows mercy on believers?
Who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?
Would destroying believers be better than showing them mercy?
propositions: Allah causes destruction or shows mercy.
Those with the Prophet are either destroyed by Allah's chastisement or shown mercy.
The disbelievers have no protector from a painful chastisement if they are not shown mercy.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “He is the Most Compassionate—in Him ˹alone˺ we believe, and in Him ˹alone˺ we trust. You will soon know who is clearly astray.”

Tafsir: Say ‘He is the Compassionate One; we believe in Him and in Him we put our trust. And assuredly you will soon know sa-ta‘lamūna is also read sa-ya‘lamūna ‘they will know’ upon seeing the chastisement with your own eyes who is in manifest error’ is it us or yourselves or them?

hype_questions: What is the nature of compassion in Islam?
How does faith and trust relate to one's understanding of God?
What happens when individuals are faced with the consequences of their actions?
propositions: We believe in Allah as the Most Compassionate One.
We put our trust in Allah alone.
You will soon know who is clearly astray upon seeing the chastisement with your own eyes.

source_text:
Verse: Say, “Consider this: if your water were to sink ˹into the earth˺, then who ˹else˺ could bring you flowing water?”

Tafsir: Say ‘Have you considered If your water were to sink deep into the earth who then will bring you running water?’ which hands and buckets would be able to reach like they do your water in other words none but God exalted be He would be able to bring it so how can you reject that He will resurrect you? It is commendable for one to say Allāhu rabbu’l-‘ālamīna ‘God Lord of the Worlds!’ after ma‘īn ‘running water’ as is stated in a hadīth. This verse was recited before a certain tyrant who then replied ‘Hatchets and pickaxes will bring it!’ whereupon the water of his eyes dried up and he became blind. We seek refuge with God against that we should be insolent towards Him or His verses.

hype_questions: What would happen if God were to resurrect me?
How can I trust in the power of God?
What is the nature of God's sovereignty?
propositions: If your water were to sink deep into the earth, who will bring you running water?
None but God exalted be He would be able to bring it.
It is commendable for one to say Allāhu rabbu’l-‘ālamīna after ma‘īn.
Hatchets and pickaxes will not bring running water.

source_text:
Verse: Nũn. By the pen and what everyone writes!

Tafsir: Nūn one of the letters of the alphabet God knows best what He means by it. By the Pen with which He has inscribed the records of all creatures in the Preserved Tablet and what they inscribe that is the angels of good and righteousness.

hype_questions: What does the letter Nūn represent in the alphabet?
Who inscribed the records of all creatures on the Preserved Tablet?
What are the angels of good and righteousness?
propositions: Nūn is one of the letters of the alphabet.
God knows best what He means by the letter Nūn.
The Pen with which God inscribed the records of all creatures is on the Preserved Tablet.
Angels are the ones who inscribe what people write.

hype_questions: What is prophethood?

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers would almost cut you down with their eyes when they hear ˹you recite˺ the Reminder, and say, “He is certainly a madman.”

Tafsir: Indeed those who disbelieve would almost throw you down to the ground read la-yuzliqūnaka or la-yazliqūnaka with their looks looking at you in a severe way almost hurling you to the ground or making you fall from your place when they hear the Reminder the Qur’ān and they say out of envy ‘He is truly a madman!’ on account of the Qur’ān that he has brought.

hype_questions: What happens when a person recites the Quran and disbelievers react with anger?

Those who disbelieve would almost throw you down to the ground when they hear the Reminder.
They say out of envy 'He is truly a madman!' on account of the Qur'ān that he has brought.

source_text:
Verse: But it is simply a reminder to the whole world.

Tafsir: Yet it namely the Qur’ān is just a Reminder an admonition for all the worlds of both humans and jinn and cannot be the cause of any dementia.

hype_questions: Can the Qur'an cause dementia?
Is the Qur'an a reminder for all beings?
What is the purpose of the Qur'an?
propositions: The Qur'ān is a reminder.
The Qur'ān is an admonition for humans and jinn.
The Qur'ān cannot cause dementia.

source_text:
Verse: The Inevitable Hour!

Tafsir: The Reality the Resurrection in which is realised the truth of all that was rejected in the way of the raising from the graves the reckoning and the requital or it means the Resurrection which will manifest all of that.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Resurrection?
How will the reckoning and requital be realised?
What truth will be revealed in the Resurrection?
propositions: The Resurrection will manifest all that was rejected.
The Resurrection will realise the truth of all that was rejected.
The Resurrection is the reality in which the reckoning and requital are realised.

source_text:
Verse: What is the Inevitable Hour?

Tafsir: What is the Reality? ma’l-hāqqa an interrogative to emphasise its enormity; this is the subject as well as the predicate of the previous al-hāqqa ‘the Reality’.

hype_questions: What will be the reality after the inevitable hour?
What is the nature of the inevitable hour?
Will anyone be able to escape the inevitable hour?
propositions: The Inevitable Hour is a reality.
The Reality refers to the subject and predicate of the previous al-hāqqa 'the Reality'.
The Inevitable Hour has enormous significance.

source_text:
Verse: And what will make you realize what the Inevitable Hour is?

Tafsir: And how would you know what the Reality is? repeated as an extra emphasis of its enormity; the first mā of the previous verse is the subject the second one its predicate; the second mā and its predicate also function as the second direct object of the verb ‘knowing’.

hype_questions: What is the Inevitable Hour?
How can I know Reality?
What makes me realize the enormity of Reality?
propositions: You will realize what the Inevitable Hour is.
You would know what Reality is.

source_text:
Verse: ˹Both˺ Thamûd and ’Ȃd denied the Striking Disaster.

Tafsir: Thamūd and ‘Ād denied the Clatterer the Resurrection because its terrors cause the hearts to clatter.

hype_questions: What is the Striking Disaster?
Will there be a Resurrection?
How does the Clatterer affect human hearts?
propositions: Thamūd and ‘Ād denied the Resurrection.
The terrors of the Resurrection cause the hearts to clatter.

source_text:
Verse: As for Thamûd, they were destroyed by an overwhelming blast.

Tafsir: As for Thamūd they were destroyed by the overwhelming Roar an excessively severe cry.

hype_questions: What was the cause of destruction for Thamud?

propositions: Thamûd were destroyed by an overwhelming blast.
Thamūd were destroyed by the overwhelming Roar
Thamūd were destroyed by an excessively severe cry.

source_text:
Verse: And as for ’Ȃd, they were destroyed by a furious, bitter wind

Tafsir: And as for ‘Ād they were destroyed by a deafening intensely clamorous violent wind that was powerful and severe in its assault upon ‘Ād despite their power and might.

hype_questions: What was the fate of ‘Ād?
How did 'Ād meet their end?
What kind of wind destroyed ‘Ād?
propositions: ‘Ād were destroyed by a violent wind.
'Ād had power and might, but it was not enough to withstand the assault.
The wind that destroyed 'Ād was powerful and severe.

source_text:
Verse: which Allah unleashed on them non-stop for seven nights and eight days, so that you would have seen its people lying dead like trunks of uprooted palm trees.

Tafsir: He forced it upon them for seven nights and eight days the first of which was the morning of Wednesday eight days before the end of the month of Shawwāl and this was at the height of winter successively one after the next husūman it the action of the wind is likened to the repeated actions of a hāsim ‘one cauterizing a wound’ time and again until it the blood has been cut off inhsama so that you might have seen the people therein lying prostrate lying dead on the ground as if they were the hollow collapsed trunks of palm-trees.

hype_questions: What was the duration of the punishment unleashed by Allah on a particular group?
How did the wind's action likened to cauterizing a wound affect the people?
Why were the people lying dead like trunks of uprooted palm trees?
propositions: Allah unleashed non-stop punishment on them for seven nights and eight days.
The first day was Wednesday, eight days before the end of Shawwāl.
The wind's action is likened to cauterizing a wound repeatedly until blood has been cut off.
People were lying prostrate and dead on the ground as if they were hollow collapsed trunks of palm-trees.

source_text:
Verse: Do you see any of them left alive?

Tafsir: So do you see any remnant of them? min bāqiyatin this is either the adjectival qualification of an implicit nafs ‘soul’ or the final suffixed tā’ is for hyperbole in other words understand it as fa-hal tarā lahum min bāqin ‘any one remaining?’ No!.

hype_questions: Are there any survivors left?
Is there anyone remaining?
Has anything survived?
propositions: Do you see any remnant of them?
There is no one remaining.
No one has survived.

source_text:
Verse: Also, Pharaoh and those before him, and ˹the people of˺ the overturned cities ˹of Lot˺ indulged in sin,

Tafsir: And Pharaoh and those of his followers man qibalahu a variant reading has man qablahu that is to say those disbelieving communities who came before him and the Deviant cities that is their inhabitants — these being the cities of the people of Lot — brought iniquity they committed deeds that were iniquitous.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Pharaoh's followers?
How did the people of Lot contribute to iniquity?
What are some examples of iniquitous deeds?
propositions: Pharaoh and his followers were disbelieving communities who came before him.
The cities of the people of Lot brought iniquity through their actions.
Deeds that were iniquitous were committed by Pharaoh's followers and the people of Lot.

source_text:
Verse: each disobeying their Lord’s messenger, so He seized them with a crushing grip.

Tafsir: Then they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord namely Lot and others so He seized them with a devastating blow one surpassing others in its severity.

hype_questions: What happens when one disobeys their Lord's messenger?
How severe is the punishment for those who disobey their Lord's messenger?
Can anyone escape the wrath of their Lord's messenger?
propositions: Each person who disobeys their Lord's messenger will be seized.
The messenger of their Lord was Lot and others.
The punishment for disobedience is a devastating blow.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, when the floodwater had overflowed, We carried you in the floating Ark ˹with Noah˺,

Tafsir: Truly when the waters rose high when they rose above all things including mountains and otherwise at the time of the Flood We carried you meaning your forefathers you being in their loins in the sailing vessel the ark which Noah built and by which he and those with him were saved while all the others drowned

hype_questions: What was the Ark used for?
Who built the Ark?

propositions: The floodwater overflowed, and Allah carried Noah and his forefathers in the Ark.
The waters rose high above all things, including mountains, during the time of the Flood.
Noah built the Ark, which was used to save himself and those with him while all others drowned.

source_text:
Verse: so that We may make this a reminder to you, and that attentive ears may grasp it.

Tafsir: so that We might make it namely this act the saving of the believers and the destruction of the disbelievers a reminder a lesson for you and that receptive ears ears which remember what they hear might remember it.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of this verse in the Quran?
How does this verse relate to the concept of salvation and destruction?
What is the significance of receptive ears in understanding this verse?
propositions: We will make this act a reminder for you.
This act will be the saving of believers and the destruction of disbelievers.
Receptive ears that remember what they hear will grasp this lesson.

source_text:

source_text:

hype_questions: What happens to our secrets on Judgment Day?

source_text:
Verse: As for those given their records in their right hand, they will cry ˹happily˺, “Here ˹everyone˺! Read my record!

Tafsir: As for him who is given his book in his right hand he will say addressing those around him on account of the joy that has come to him ‘Here take and read my book! kitābiyah both hā’ūmu ‘here is’ and iqra’ū ‘read’ compete for government of this direct object.

hype_questions: What is the significance of being given one's book in the right hand?

propositions: Those who are given their records in their right hand will be joyful.
He who is given his book in his right hand will say to those around him, 'Here take and read my book!'
The act of reading one's own record brings joy and a desire to share it with others.

source_text:

source_text:

propositions.text: I am unaware of my reckoning.

source_text:

hype_questions: Would death be the ultimate end?

source_text:
Verse: My authority has been stripped from me.”

Tafsir: My authority my strength my argument has gone from me’ the final hā’ in kitābiyah ‘my book’ hisābiyah ‘my account’ and sultāniyah ‘my authority’ is for consonantal quiescence; and it is retained when reciting with a pause as well as without a pause in accordance with the authoritative version of the Qur’ānic text and the transmitted reports; some elide it when reciting without a pause.

hype_questions: What happens to one's authority when reciting with a pause?
How does the elision of 'sultāniyah' affect the recitation without a pause?

propositions: My authority has been stripped from me.
My authority, my strength, and my argument have gone from me.
The final hā' in 'kitābiyah' is for consonantal quiescence when reciting with a pause or without a pause.

source_text:

source_text:

hype_questions: What is the length of a chain used in the Fire?
How long are the arms of an angel's forearm?

propositions: The Fire uses a chain seventy cubits long.
An angel's forearm is one cubit in length.
The verb 'admitting' is semantically connected to the preceding adverbial clause despite the fā’ of fa’slukūhu.

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: and none of you could have shielded him ˹from Us˺!

Tafsir: and not one of you ahadin is the subject of mā min being extra used to emphasise the negation; minkum is a circumstantial qualifier referring to ahadin could have defended him hājizīna is the predicate of the preceding mā and it is used in the plural because ahad when employed in a negatory context denotes a plural sense; the suffixed pronoun in ‘anhu refers to the Prophet in other words there is none to prevent Us from punishing him.

hype_questions: Can anyone defend God from punishment?

propositions: None of you could have shielded him.
Ahadin is the subject of mā min being used to emphasise the negation.
Hājizīna is the predicate of the preceding mā and it refers to the Prophet.

source_text:

source_text:
Verse: Surely your Lord knows that you ˹O Prophet˺ stand ˹in prayer˺ for nearly two-thirds of the night, or ˹sometimes˺ half of it, or a third, as do some of those with you. Allah ˹alone˺ keeps a ˹precise˺ measure of the day and night. He knows that you ˹believers˺ are unable to endure this, and has turned to you in mercy. And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Tafsir: Assuredly your Lord knows that you stand vigil less than two thirds of the night or at times a half of it or a third of it if read wa-nisfihi wa-thuluthihi then these constitute a supplement to thuluthay ‘two thirds’; if read wa-nisfahu wa-thuluthahu then a supplement to adnā ‘less than’ — his keeping vigil in the way mentioned is in accordance with what was enjoined on him at the beginning of this sūra — along with a group of those with you wa-tā’ifatun mina’lladhīna ma‘aka constitutes a supplement to the subject of the verb taqūmu ‘you stand vigil’ but it may also constitute although it is not certain a separating clause. The keeping vigil by some of his companions in this way indicates their emulation of him. Some of them could not tell how much of the night they had spent in prayer and how much of it had remained and would therefore keep vigil all night as a precaution; and so they used to keep vigil in this way for a whole year or more with their feet swollen until God alleviated matters for them. He exalted be He says and God keeps measures He keeps count of the night and the day. He knows that an softened in place of the hardened form its subject having been omitted that is to say annahu you will not be able to keep count of it that is the length of the night so that you may perform the vigil at the time in which it is required unless you stay up all night which is hard on you and so He has relented to you making you revert to what is easier. So recite as much as is feasible of the Qur’ān during prayer by performing as much prayer as is feasible. He knows that an softened in place of the hardened form that is to say annahu some of you will be sick while others will be travelling in the land seeking the bounty of God seeking of His provision through commerce and otherwise and others will be fighting in the way of God for each of the three groups mentioned the keeping of nightly vigil is hard and so God has alleviated things for them by enjoining on them what is feasible.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of standing vigil in prayer?
How does Allah alleviate the difficulties faced by believers who stand vigil?
Why is it hard for some to keep count of their time during prayer?
propositions: Your Lord knows that you stand vigil less than two-thirds of the night.
Allah keeps a precise measure of the day and night.
He knows that you are unable to endure this, and has turned to you in mercy.
Seek Allah's forgiveness.
His keeping vigil is in accordance with what was enjoined on him at the beginning of this sūra.
Some of his companions could not tell how much of the night they had spent in prayer and would therefore keep vigil all night as a precaution.
He exalted be He says and God keeps measures He keeps count of the night and the day.

He knows that you will not be able to keep count of it that is the length of the night so that you may perform the vigil at the time in which it is required unless you stay up all night which is hard on you and so He has relented to you making you revert to what is easier.
So recite as much as is feasible of the Qur’ān during prayer by performing as much prayer as is feasible.

source_text:
Verse: We have appointed only ˹stern˺ angels as wardens of the Fire. And We have made their number only as a test for the disbelievers, so that the People of the Book will be certain, and the believers will increase in faith, and neither the People of the Book nor the believers will have any doubts, and so that those ˹hypocrites˺ with sickness in their hearts and the disbelievers will argue, “What does Allah mean by such a number?” In this way Allah leaves whoever He wills to stray and guides whoever He wills. And none knows the forces of your Lord except He. And this ˹description of Hell˺ is only a reminder to humanity.

Tafsir: And We have appointed only angels as wardens of the Fire in other words and so they cannot be withstood as these disbelievers are wont to imagine; and We have made their number so only as a stumbling-block a cause for error for those who disbelieve when they then say ‘Why are there nineteen of them?’ so that those who were given the Scripture namely the Jews may be certain of the sincerity of the Prophet s in saying that they are nineteen for this concords with what is in their Scripture; and that those who believe from among the People of the Scripture may increase in faith in affirmation of the truth given that what the Prophet s has said concords with what is in their Scripture and that those given the Scripture and the believers those other than these Jews may not be in doubt concerning the number of these angels and that those in whose hearts there is a sickness an uncertainty those in Medina and the disbelievers in Mecca may say ‘What did God mean by this number as a similitude?’ mathalan they referred to it thus as a mathal on account of it being a curious matter; in terms of syntax it mathalan is a circumstantial qualifier. Thus that is just as the one who rejects this number is led astray and the one who affirms the truth of it is guided God leads astray whom He will and guides whom He will. And none knows the hosts of your Lord namely the angels none knows them in terms of their strength and their assistants except Him. And it that is Saqar is nothing but a reminder for humans.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the number of angels guarding the Fire?
How does Allah's description of Hell serve as a reminder to humanity?
What is the role of faith and doubt in understanding the nature of Allah's power?
propositions: Allah has appointed only angels as wardens of the Fire.
The number of angels guarding the Fire is a test for disbelievers.
Those who believe will increase in faith upon hearing this description.
None knows the forces of Allah's power except Him.
This description of Hell serves as a reminder to humanity.

Tafsir: and the moon is eclipsed darkening its light disappearing

hype_questions: What happens to the moon during an eclipse?
Why does the moon disappear during an eclipse?
How is the light of the moon affected by an eclipse?
propositions: The moon is eclipsed.
The moon's light disappears during an eclipse.
An eclipse darkens the moon's light.

source_text:
Verse: and the sun and the moon are brought together,

Tafsir: and the sun and the moon are brought together so that both of them will rise from the west; or it means when the light of both of them disappears — and this will be on the Day of Resurrection —

hype_questions: Will the sun and moon rise from the west on the Day of Resurrection?
What happens to the light of the sun and moon when they disappear?
Is the Day of Resurrection a time when the sun and moon will be brought together?
propositions: The sun and the moon are brought together so that both of them will rise from the west.
When the light of both the sun and the moon disappears, it will be on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: on that Day one will cry, “Where is the escape?”

Tafsir: on that day man will say ‘Where is the escape?’

hype_questions: What happens to humans after death?
Will there be an escape or judgment?
How will people react when they face their final reckoning?
propositions: On that Day, one will cry out in despair.
Man will say on that day, 'Where is the escape?'
There will be a final reckoning for humanity.

source_text:
Verse: But no! There will be no refuge.

Tafsir: No indeed! — a deterrent against seeking to escape — There is no refuge no shelter to seek protection in.

hype_questions: What happens when we try to escape from our problems?
Is there a place of safety where we can hide from our troubles?
Can we truly find refuge in this world?
propositions: There is no refuge or shelter to seek protection in.
Seeking to escape is discouraged.
No place can provide true protection or safety.

source_text:
Verse: On that Day all will end up before your Lord.

Tafsir: On that day the recourse will be to your Lord the final recourse of all creatures whereupon they will be reckoned with and requited.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate destination for all beings on Judgment Day?
How will individuals be held accountable for their actions?
What is the final reckoning that awaits all creatures?
propositions: All beings will end up before your Lord on Judgment Day.
The final recourse of all creatures is to your Lord, where they will be reckoned with and requited.

source_text:
Verse: All will then be informed of what they have sent forth and left behind.

Tafsir: On that day man will be informed of what he has sent ahead and left behind he will be informed of the his first and last deeds.

hype_questions: What will I be held accountable for on the Day of Judgment?
How will my past actions be evaluated?
Will I be rewarded or punished for my deeds?
propositions: Man will be informed of what he has sent ahead.
Man will be informed of what he has left behind.
Man will be informed of his first and last deeds.

source_text:
Verse: In fact, people will testify against their own souls,

Tafsir: Rather man has insight into his own soul for his limbs will speak of his deeds the hā’ sc. the tā’ marbūta in basīratun is for hyperbole and so he must be requited

hype_questions: Does a person's body betray their true intentions?
Can one's limbs speak of their inner state?
What happens to a person when they are held accountable for their actions?
propositions: People will testify against their own souls.
A person has insight into his own soul, which is indicated by the limbs speaking of his deeds.
The phrase 'tā' marbūta in basīratun' is used hyperbolically to emphasize the importance of accountability.

source_text:
Verse: despite the excuses they come up with.

Tafsir: though he should offer his excuses ma‘ādhīr is the plural of ma‘dhira but following a different pattern from the usual ma‘dhira ma‘ādhir that is to say whatever excuse he offers will not be accepted from him.

hype_questions: What happens when someone offers excuses?
Can excuses change the outcome of a situation?
How does one handle situations where excuses are not accepted?
propositions: Despite excuses, they will not be accepted.
Ma‘ādhir is the plural form of ma‘dhira used in this context to indicate that excuses will not be accepted.
Whatever excuse he offers, it will not be accepted from him.

source_text:
Verse: Do not rush your tongue trying to memorize ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran.

Tafsir: God exalted be He says to His Prophet Do not move your tongue with it with the Qur’ān before Gabriel is through with reciting it to hasten it fearing to lose it.

hype_questions: What is the significance of reciting the Quran with patience?
How can one avoid losing the revelation of the Quran?
What role does Gabriel play in the recitation of the Quran?
propositions: God exalted be He says to His Prophet not to move his tongue with the Qur'an before Gabriel is through with reciting it.
The Prophet should hasten the recitation of the Quran fearing to lose it.

source_text:
Verse: It is certainly upon Us to ˹make you˺ memorize and recite it.

Tafsir: Assuredly it is for Us to bring it together in your breast and to recite it your reciting of it that is its flowing off your tongue.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of memorizing and reciting the Quran?
How does Allah bring the Quran to life in our hearts?
What is the significance of reciting the Quran on our tongues?
propositions: It is upon Us to make you memorize and recite it.
Assuredly it is for Us to bring it together in your breast.
Your reciting of it that is its flowing off your tongue.

source_text:
Verse: So once We have recited a revelation ˹through Gabriel˺, follow its recitation ˹closely˺.

Tafsir: So when We recite it to you by means of Gabriel’s recital follow its recitation listen to its recitation thus the Prophet s would listen to it and then repeat it.

hype_questions: What is the correct way to follow the recitation of a revelation?
How does one demonstrate obedience to God's message?
What role does Gabriel play in conveying divine revelations?
propositions: When a revelation is recited, it should be followed closely.
The Prophet s would listen to and repeat the recitation of a revelation.
God's message should be obeyed and repeated by those who receive it.

source_text:
Verse: Then it is surely upon Us to make it clear ˹to you˺.

Tafsir: Then it is for Us to explain it by making you comprehend it the connection between this verse and what preceded it is that those verses before imply turning away from God’s signs whereas this one implies applying oneself to them by memorising them.

hype_questions: What does it mean to apply oneself to God's signs?
How does memorizing the Quran relate to turning away from God's signs?
What is the connection between this verse and what preceded it?
propositions: It is upon Us to make it clear.
This verse implies applying oneself to God's signs by memorising them.
Those verses before imply turning away from God’s signs.

source_text:
Verse: But no! In fact, you love this fleeting world,

Tafsir: No indeed! kallā is for commencement with the sense of alā Rather you love the transitory life this world both verbs here and below may be read in the second or third person plural

hype_questions: Does one's love for this fleeting world surpass their devotion to a higher power?
Can the transitory nature of life be seen as a test of faith?
How does one reconcile their attachment to worldly pleasures with spiritual aspirations?
propositions: You love the transitory life.
This world is both fleeting and loved by you.
The commencement of something is indicated by kallā in this context.

source_text:
Verse: and neglect the Hereafter.

Tafsir: and forsake the Hereafter thus neglecting to work towards attaining bliss in it.

hype_questions: What is the Hereafter?
How can one attain bliss in the Hereafter?
What are the consequences of neglecting the Hereafter?
propositions: The Hereafter refers to the afterlife.
Attaining bliss in the Hereafter requires effort and dedication.
Neglecting the Hereafter leads to missing out on eternal bliss.

source_text:
Verse: On that Day ˹some˺ faces will be bright,

Tafsir: Some faces on that day that is on the Day of Resurrection will be radiant fair and resplendent

hype_questions: What will happen to our faces on the Day of Resurrection?
Will we be judged fairly on that day?
How will our actions be evaluated on the Day of Resurrection?
propositions: Some faces on the Day of Resurrection will be radiant and fair.
The Day of Resurrection is a specific, future event.
Our actions will be evaluated on the Day of Resurrection.

source_text:
Verse: looking at their Lord.

Tafsir: looking upon their Lord in other words they will see God glorified and exalted be He in the Hereafter.

hype_questions: What is the state of one's Lord in the Hereafter?
How does looking at one's Lord relate to God's glorification?
What happens when one looks upon their Lord?
propositions: They will see God.
God is glorified and exalted.
Looking at their Lord means seeing God.

source_text:
Verse: And ˹other˺ faces will be gloomy,

Tafsir: And other faces on that day will be scowling glowering frowning terribly

hype_questions: What will be the state of faces on the Day of Judgment?
How will people react to seeing Allah's face?
What is the expected behavior of human faces when they see Allah?
propositions: Other faces on the Day of Judgment will be scowling.
The faces on that day will be gloomy and frowning terribly.
Allah's face will be seen by all on the Day of Judgment.

source_text:
Verse: anticipating something devastating to befall them.

Tafsir: certain that a spine-crushing calamity will fall on them a great catastrophe one that ‘crushes the spine’ fiqār.

hype_questions: What kind of calamity will befall them?
Will a great catastrophe crush their spirits?
How severe will the devastation be?
propositions: A spine-crushing calamity will fall on them.
This calamity is certain to happen.
The calamity will have a devastating impact.

source_text:
Verse: But no! ˹Beware of the day˺ when the soul reaches the collar bone ˹as it leaves˺,

Tafsir: No indeed! kallā in the sense of alā When it the soul reaches up to the collar bones

hype_questions: What happens to the soul when it leaves the body?
At what point does the soul depart from the body?
When will the Day of Judgment arrive?
propositions: The soul reaches up to the collar bones as it leaves the body.
No indeed, in the sense of alā (God's permission).
The Day of Judgment is a real event that will occur when the soul reaches its destination.

source_text:
Verse: and it will be said, “Is there any healer ˹who can save this life˺?”

Tafsir: and it is said and those around him the dying one say ‘Where is the enchanter?’ to perform incantations on him and cure him

hype_questions: Can a healer save this life?
Where is the enchanter to perform incantations and cure the dying one?
Can miracles be performed on the dying?
propositions: There exists a healer who can save a life.
Those around the dying person ask where the enchanter is to perform incantations and cure them.
Miracles can be performed on individuals, including those who are dying.

source_text:
Verse: And the dying person realizes it is ˹their˺ time to depart,

Tafsir: and he suspects he the one whose soul has reached this stage that it is the time of parting the parting with this world

hype_questions: What happens to a person's soul when it reaches a certain stage?
When is the time of parting with this world?
What does it mean for someone's soul to reach a certain stage?
propositions: The dying person realizes it is their time to depart.
He suspects he is the one whose soul has reached this stage that it is the time of parting the parting with this world.

source_text:
Verse: and ˹then˺ their feet are tied together ˹in a shroud˺.

Tafsir: and the shank is intertwined with the other shank that is one of his shanks will be intertwined with his other shank at the moment of death; or it means the distress of parting with this world is intertwined with the distress of the arrival of the Hereafter;

hype_questions: What happens to a person's shanks at the moment of death?
How is the distress of parting with this world related to the distress of the arrival of the Hereafter?
Can a person's shanks be intertwined in any other way?
propositions: Their feet are tied together in a shroud.
The shank is intertwined with the other shank at the moment of death.
The distress of parting with this world is intertwined with the distress of the arrival of the Hereafter.

source_text:
Verse: On that day they will be driven to your Lord ˹alone˺.

Tafsir: on that day to your Lord will be the driving of the souls al-masāq means al-sawq; this indicates the operator of the above idhā ‘when’ the meaning being ‘when the soul reaches the throat it will be driven towards the judgement of its Lord’.

hype_questions: What happens to a person's soul when they reach the throat?
Will the souls be driven towards their Lord on Judgement Day?
What is the meaning of 'al-masāq' in this context?
propositions: On that day, the souls will be driven towards the judgement of their Lord.
The term al-masāq refers to the throat.
Al-masāq indicates the operator of the idhā 'when' the meaning being 'when the soul reaches the throat'

source_text:
Verse: This denier neither believed nor prayed,

Tafsir: For he man neither affirmed the truth nor prayed

hype_questions: Does denial of faith lead to a loss of spiritual benefits?
Can one who denies the truth still be considered a believer?
What are the consequences of not praying for someone who denies their faith?
propositions: This person neither believed nor prayed.
He did not affirm the truth.
He did not pray.

source_text:
Verse: but persisted in denial and turned away,

Tafsir: but he denied the Qur’ān and he turned away from faith

hype_questions: Does denial of the Qur'ān lead to spiritual loss?
Can turning away from faith result in a loss of divine guidance?
How does denying the Qur'ān affect one's relationship with Allah?
propositions: He denied the Qur'ān.
He turned away from faith.
Denying the Qur'ān leads to spiritual loss.

source_text:
Verse: then went to their own people, walking boastfully.

Tafsir: then went off to his family swaggering strutting about in self-conceit.

hype_questions: Does boasting lead to a stronger sense of identity?
Can excessive pride in one's heritage be a source of strength or weakness?
How does swaggering affect relationships with others?
propositions: He went to his family.
He walked boastfully.
He strutted about in self-conceit.

source_text:
Verse: Woe to you, and more woe!

Tafsir: Woe be nearer to you there is a shift from the third to the second person address here; the term awlā is a noun of action with the following lām being explicative in other words ‘what you are averse to is now near to you’ and nearer that is because you are more deserving of it woe than anyone else

hype_questions: What does 'woe' signify in this context?
How does the speaker's address change from third to second person?
What is the significance of the lām in the word awlā?
propositions: Woe signifies a state of great misfortune or suffering.
The term awlā is a noun of action that means 'to be averse' or 'to dislike'.
The lām in the word awlā is explicative, meaning it clarifies what you are averse to is now near to you.

source_text:
Verse: Again, woe to you, and even more woe!

Tafsir: then may woe be nearer to you and nearer! — repeated for emphasis.

hype_questions: Will woe be closer to me?
Is the speaker expressing more emphasis than usual?
What does the repetition of 'woe' signify?
propositions: Woe is nearer to you.
The speaker emphasizes that woe is even closer to them.
The repetition of 'woe' adds to its proximity.

source_text:
Verse: Do people think they will be left without purpose?

Tafsir: Does man suppose that he is to be left aimless? left to his own devices without being obligated to the prescribed laws let him not suppose that!

hype_questions: Will I be given a purpose in life?
Am I left to my own devices without any obligations?
What is the significance of following prescribed laws?
propositions: People think they will be left without purpose.
Man is not supposed to be left aimless or without being obligated to the prescribed laws.

source_text:
Verse: Were they not ˹once˺ a sperm-drop emitted?

Tafsir: Was he not — that is indeed he was — a drop of emitted semen? read yumnā or tumnā deposited into the womb.

hype_questions: Did not all creation begin from a single drop of semen?
Is the creation of humans linked to the emission of semen?
What is the origin of human life?
propositions: He was a sperm-drop emitted.
A drop of semen was deposited into the womb.
The creation of humans began from a single drop of semen.

source_text:
Verse: Then they became a clinging clot ˹of blood˺, then He developed and perfected their form,

Tafsir: Then it the drop of semen became a clot; then He God created from it man and proportioned him making the parts of his body upright

hype_questions: What is the process of human creation in Islam?
How does God create humans with a perfect form?
What are the parts of the human body that God has proportioned?
propositions: Then it became a clot.
God created man from a drop of semen.
He perfected and proportioned the human body.

source_text:
Verse: producing from it both sexes, male and female.

Tafsir: and made of it of the drop of semen that became a blood-clot then an embryo a small mass of flesh the two sexes the two kinds the male and the female at times coming together and at times each being on their own.

hype_questions: How does creation involve both sexes?
What is the process of creating a blood-clot from semen that becomes an embryo?
Why do the two sexes come together and sometimes exist separately?
propositions: It produces both male and female.
A drop of semen transforms into a blood clot, which then forms an embryo.
The male and female sexes are created simultaneously and can coexist independently.

source_text:
Verse: Is such ˹a Creator˺ unable to bring the dead back to life?

Tafsir: Is not such a Doer of all these things able to revive the dead? — the Prophet s would say ‘Yes indeed!’

hype_questions: Can a creator bring back to life those who have died?
Is the one who does all these things able to revive the dead?
What is the nature of the power of Allah?
propositions: A Creator is unable to bring the dead back to life.
The Doer of all these things can revive the dead.
The Prophet s affirmed that the one who does all these things can indeed revive the dead.

source_text:
Verse: Is there not a period of time when each human is nothing yet worth mentioning?

Tafsir: Has there ever been — there has indeed been — for man Adam a period of time forty years in which he was a thing unmentioned? — he was during this period a fashioned in clay and not mentioned; alternatively what is meant by insān ‘man’ is the generic noun and by hīn ‘a period of time’ the period of gestation.

hype_questions: Is there a moment in human existence when we are not worth mentioning?
Can humans be considered insignificant at any point in their lives?
What does it mean to be 'unmentioned' in the context of human existence?
propositions: There was a period of forty years during which Adam was fashioned in clay and not mentioned.
The term 'man' is often used as a generic noun, referring to humanity as a whole.
The phrase 'unmentioned' can be interpreted as referring to the gestation period of human life.

source_text:
Verse: ˹For˺ indeed, We ˹alone˺ created humans from a drop of mixed fluids, ˹in order˺ to test them, so We made them hear and see.

Tafsir: Verily We created man the species from a drop of mixed fluid from a mixture that is from the seminal fluid of the man and the ovarian fluid of the woman that have mixed and blended so that We may test him trying him with the moral obligations of religion nabtalīhi is either a new sentence ‘We will test him’ or an implied circumstantial qualifier meaning ‘intending to test him when he is ready’. So We made him for that very reason hearing seeing.

hype_questions: What is the purpose of creating humans?
How do we test humans?
What moral obligations does religion impose?
propositions: We created humans from a drop of mixed fluids.
The purpose of creation is to test humans.
Humans are tested with moral obligations of religion.

source_text:
Verse: We already showed them the Way, whether they ˹choose to˺ be grateful or ungrateful.

Tafsir: Verily We have guided him to the way We have pointed out to him the path of guidance by sending messengers to mankind whether he be grateful that is to say whether he be a believer or ungrateful both shākiran and kafūran are circumstantial qualifiers referring to the direct object; in other words We have pointed out to him in both presupposed states whether his gratefulness or his unthankfulness; immā is used to list the ‘states’.

hype_questions: Does guidance from Allah guarantee salvation?
Can ungratefulness lead to spiritual loss?
What is the role of messengers in guiding humanity?
propositions: We have guided him to the way.
We have pointed out to him the path of guidance.
He can be grateful or ungrateful.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, shackles, and a blazing Fire.

Tafsir: We have assuredly prepared for the disbelievers chains with which they are dragged through the Fire and fetters around their necks to which the chains will be attached and a hell-fire a fire set ablaze burning fiercely in which they shall be chastised.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of disbelief?
How will the disbelievers be punished in the afterlife?
What is the nature of the hellfire mentioned in the Quran?
propositions: We have prepared chains for the disbelievers to be dragged through the Fire.
The disbelievers will be fettered around their necks with chains attached to them.
A blazing fire has been prepared as a place of chastisement for the disbelievers.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, the virtuous will have a drink ˹of pure wine˺—flavoured with camphor—

Tafsir: Truly the righteous abrār is the plural of barr or bārr namely the obedient ones will drink from a cup ka’s is a vessel for drinking wine and this wine will be in it; what is meant is that they will drink from ‘wine’ a case where the actuality is referred to by the name of the locus in which it is found; min ‘from is partitive whose mixture that with which it is mixed is camphor;

hype_questions: What does the Quran say about the virtuous and their drink?
How do the righteous relate to the concept of 'wine' in Islamic theology?
What is the significance of camphor in the context of wine?
propositions: The virtuous will have a drink of pure wine flavored with camphor.
The righteous are those who obey and will drink from a cup called ka.
The 'wine' referred to in the Quran is actually the locus where it is found, mixed with camphor.

source_text:
Verse: ˹from˺ a spring where Allah’s servants will drink, flowing at their will.

Tafsir: a spring ‘aynan substitutes for kāfūran containing the scent thereof from which the servants of God His friends drink making it gush forth plenteously directing it to wherever they wish of their dwellings.

hype_questions: What is the name of the spring mentioned in the verse?
Where do Allah's servants drink from this spring?
How does the servant direct the flow of the spring?
propositions: There is a spring where Allah’s servants will drink.
The scent of kāfūran is substituted by 'aynan in the verse.
Allah's friends drink from 'aynan plenteously.
The servant directs the flow of 'aynan to their dwellings.

source_text:
Verse: They ˹are those who˺ fulfil ˹their˺ vows and fear a Day of sweeping horror,

Tafsir: They fulfil their vows pledged in obedience to God and fear a day the evil of which will be widespread.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Day of sweeping horror?
How do people fulfill their vows in obedience to God?
What is the significance of fearing a widespread evil day?
propositions: They fulfil their vows.
They fear a Day of sweeping horror.
The evil of which will be widespread.

source_text:
Verse: and give food—despite their desire for it—to the poor, the orphan, and the captive,

Tafsir: And they give food despite their love of it that is to say despite their love of food and their craving for it to the needy the poor and the orphan who does not have a father and the prisoner meaning the one who has been rightly imprisoned.

hype_questions: What is the Islamic obligation to provide for those in need?
How does Islam define a 'needy' person?
What is the significance of providing for orphans and prisoners?
propositions: They are obligated to give food despite their desire for it.
The needy, poor, and orphan are entitled to receive food.
A prisoner who has been rightly imprisoned is also deserving of food.

source_text:
Verse: ˹saying to themselves,˺ “We feed you only for the sake of Allah, seeking neither reward nor thanks from you.

Tafsir: ‘We feed you only for the sake of God seeking His reward. We do not desire any reward from you nor any thanks this contains the reason for the giving of the food. Now do they actually say this or is it that God knows this to be true of them and has thus praised them by mentioning it? The two are different opinions regarding this matter.

hype_questions: Does Allah reward the sincerity of our actions?
Can we truly be certain of our intentions before Allah?
What is the nature of Allah's knowledge and praise?
propositions: We feed you only for the sake of Allah.
Seeking neither reward nor thanks from you.
God seeks His own reward, not ours.
We do not desire any reward from you nor any thanks.
This is the reason for the giving of the food.
Now do they actually say this or is it that God knows this to be true of them and has thus praised them by mentioning it?

source_text:
Verse: We fear from our Lord a horribly distressful Day.”

Tafsir: Indeed we fear from our Lord a day of frowning one in which faces scowl in other words a horrid day to observe on account of its severity calamitous’ severe in that respect.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Day of Judgment?
How will our Lord judge us on that day?
What can we expect from our Lord's judgment?
propositions: We fear a horribly distressful Day from our Lord.
Our Lord has a day of frowning in which faces scowl.
This day is severe and calamitous.

source_text:
Verse: So Allah will deliver them from the horror of that Day, and grant them radiance and joy,

Tafsir: God has therefore shielded them from the evil of that day and has granted them radiance fairness and resplendence in their faces and joy.

hype_questions: What will Allah grant to those who are saved from the horror of that Day?
How does Allah shield people from the evil of that Day?
What is the radiance and joy that Allah grants to those who are saved?
propositions: Allah will deliver them from the horror of that Day.
God has therefore shielded them from the evil of that day.
Allah has granted them radiance, fairness, and resplendence in their faces.
God has granted them joy.

source_text:
Verse: and reward them for their perseverance with a Garden ˹in Paradise˺ and ˹garments of˺ silk.

Tafsir: And He has rewarded them for their patience for their steadfastness in refraining from disobedience with a Garden into which they are admitted and silk which they are given to wear;

hype_questions: What is the reward for those who persevere in their faith?
How does Allah show appreciation for patience and steadfastness?
What is the nature of the Garden that Allah rewards with?
propositions: Allah has rewarded those who persevere with a Garden in Paradise.
Patience and steadfastness are rewarded with a Garden into which they are admitted.
The reward for patience includes silk to wear.

source_text:
Verse: There they will be reclining on ˹canopied˺ couches, never seeing scorching heat or bitter cold.

Tafsir: reclining muttaki’īna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the implicit verb udkhilūhā ‘they are admitted into it’ therein upon couches arā’ik are beds inside canopies. They will not find lā yarawna is a second circumstantial qualifier therein either sun or bitter cold neither heat nor cold; but it is also said that zamharīr means ‘the moon’ and so in other words it means that it will be bright without any sun or moon.

hype_questions: What is the state of comfort in Paradise?
How does one experience comfort in Paradise?
Is there any mention of light or darkness in the description of Paradise?
propositions: They will be reclining on couches inside canopies.
There will be no scorching heat or bitter cold in Paradise.
The state of comfort in Paradise is characterized by its brightness, without any sun or moon.

source_text:
Verse: The Garden’s shade will be right above them, and its fruit will be made very easy to reach.

Tafsir: And close dāniyatan is a supplement to the syntactical locus of the clause lā yarawna in other words it is a supplement to the import ghayra rā’īna over them will be its shades its trees and its clusters of fruits will hang low its fruits will brought close so that they are reached by the one standing the one sitting or the one lying down.

hype_questions: What will be the accessibility of the Garden's fruit?
How will the shade of the Garden be utilized?
What benefits can one expect from being in the shade of the Garden?
propositions: The Garden's shade will be above them.
Its fruit will be easily accessible.
The shade, trees, and clusters of fruits will hang low to make it easy for anyone standing, sitting, or lying down to reach them.

source_text:
Verse: They will be waited on with silver vessels and cups of crystal—

Tafsir: And they will be waited upon from all around them in it with vessels of silver and goblets akwāb are cups without handles of crystal —

hype_questions: What is the state of those who enter Paradise?
How will they be treated in Paradise?
What kind of vessels and cups will they be served with?
propositions: They will be waited on with silver vessels.
They will be served cups of crystal.
They will be waited upon from all around them.

source_text:
