Tafsir: And what will show you what will make known to you O Muhammad (s) what the Night of Ordainment is? — intended to emphasise its great status and to provoke marvel at it.

hype_questions: What is the Night of Glory?
How will you realize the significance of the Night of Glory?
What makes the Night of Glory special?
propositions: The Night of Glory is a significant event.
O Muhammad (s) is referring to the Night of Ordainment.
The Night of Ordainment has great status and deserves marveling at it.

source_text:
Verse: The Night of Glory is better than a thousand months.

Tafsir: The Night of Ordainment is better than a thousand months in which there is no Night of Ordainment for a righteous deed on that Night is better than one performed for a thousand months without it.

hype_questions: What is the significance of the Night of Glory in Islam?
How does performing righteous deeds on the Night of Ordainment compare to doing them for a thousand months without it?
What is the value of the Night of Ordainment in Islamic theology?
propositions: The Night of Glory is better than a thousand months.
A righteous deed performed on the Night of Ordainment is better than one performed for a thousand months without it.

source_text:
Verse: That night the angels and the ˹holy˺ spirit descend, by the permission of their Lord, for every ˹decreed˺ matter.

Tafsir: The angels and the Spirit namely Gabriel descend tanazzalu one of the two original tā’ letters of tatanazzalu has been omitted in it on that night by the leave of their Lord by His command with every command that God has decreed from that year to the following one min is causative functioning as bi ‘with’.

hype_questions: What is the role of angels in relation to God's decrees?
How does the Spirit (Gabriel) function in relation to God's commands?
What is the significance of the tā’ letters in the context of divine decree?
propositions: The angels descend by the permission of their Lord for every decreed matter.
God has decreed a command that is executed by Gabriel, with the leave of their Lord.
The tā’ letters are part of the original text used in the revelation.

source_text:
Verse: It is all peace until the break of dawn.

Tafsir: It is peaceful salāmun hiya a predicate preceding the subject until the rising of the dawn read matla‘ or matli‘ until the time it rises it is peaceful because of the numerous salutations of peace salām spoken in it by the angels who every time they come across a believing man or believing woman bid him peace.

hype_questions: What is the significance of salutations of peace in Islam?
How do angels interact with believers?
What is the meaning of 'peaceful' in the context of dawn?
propositions: Salāmun hiya a predicate preceding the subject until the rising of the dawn.
The numerous salutations of peace spoken by angels bring about peace.
Believers are bid peace by angels upon their encounter.

source_text:
Verse: The disbelievers from the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist ˹from disbelief˺ until the clear proof came to them:

Tafsir: The disbelievers from among min explicative the People of the Scripture and the idolaters that is the idol-worshippers wa’l-mushrikīna is a supplement to ahl ‘the People of’ were not going to leave off munfakkīna is the predicate of yakun ‘were’ that is to say they were not going to abandon their ways until the clear proof namely Muhammad (s) should come to them that is until it came to them;

hype_questions: What is the nature of disbelief in Islam?
How do polytheists respond to the message of Islam?
What is the significance of Muhammad's prophethood?
propositions: The disbelievers from among the People of the Scripture and the idol-worshippers were not going to leave off their ways until the clear proof came to them.
The clear proof namely Muhammad (s) should come to them.

source_text:
Verse: a messenger from Allah, reciting scrolls of ˹utmost˺ purity,

Tafsir: a messenger from God rasūlun mina’Llāhi substitutes for al-bayyinatu ‘the clear proof’ namely the Prophet s reciting pages purified of all falsehood

hype_questions: What is the role of a messenger from God?
How does the Prophet's recitation relate to the concept of clear proof?
What is meant by 'purified pages' in this context?
propositions: A messenger from Allah exists.
The Prophet recites scrolls of utmost purity.
Al-bayyinatu refers to the clear proof, which is the Prophet's recitation.

source_text:
Verse: containing upright commandments.

Tafsir: wherein are upright precepts written rulings that are upright that is to say one who recites what contains all that and that is the Qur’ān. Thus some of them believed in it while others disbelieved.

hype_questions: What is the primary source of guidance for Muslims?
How did people initially respond to the revelation of the Qur'ān?
What is the significance of reciting the Qur'ān?
propositions: The Qur'ān contains upright commandments.
Some people believed in the Qur'ān, while others disbelieved it.
Reciting the Qur'ān means following its precepts.

source_text:
Verse: It was not until this clear proof came to the People of the Book that they became divided ˹about his prophethood˺—

Tafsir: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided regarding belief in him the Prophet s except after the clear proof had come to them namely the Prophet s — or the Qur’ān which he brought as his miracle. Before his s arrival they had all agreed to believe in him when he would come; then those who disbelieved in him from among them became envious of him.

hype_questions: What is the clear proof that led to the division among the People of the Book regarding his prophethood?
How did those who were given the Scripture initially react to the Prophet's arrival?
What was the reason behind those who disbelieved in the Prophet becoming envious of him?
propositions: The clear proof came to the People of the Book.
Those who were given the Scripture agreed to believe in the Prophet before his arrival.
Those who disbelieved in the Prophet became envious of him after his arrival.

source_text:
Verse: even though they were only commanded to worship Allah ˹alone˺ with sincere devotion to Him in all uprightness, establish prayer, and pay alms-tax. That is the upright Way.

Tafsir: And they were only commanded in their Scripture the Torah and the Gospel to worship God illā li-ya‘budū means illā an ya‘budū an having been omitted and the lām added devoting religion purely to Him free of any idolatry as hanīfs upright in following the religion of Abraham and the religion of Muhammad (s) when he would come — so how is it that they disbelieved in him? and to establish prayer and pay the alms. That is the upright religion the upright creed.

hype_questions: What is the upright way of worshiping God?
How can one establish a pure and upright religion like Abraham's?
What is the significance of paying alms-tax in Islam?
propositions: They were commanded to worship Allah alone with sincere devotion.
The Torah and Gospel were only meant to worship God without any idolatry.
Establishing prayer and paying alms-tax are essential parts of the upright religion.
Abraham and Muhammad (s) followed a pure and upright religion.
Disbelieving in Muhammad (s) despite being commanded to follow his example is puzzling.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who disbelieve from the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, to stay there forever. They are the worst of ˹all˺ beings.

Tafsir: Truly the disbelievers from among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters shall be in the fire of Hell to abide therein khālidīna an implied circumstantial qualifier in other words it will be decreed for them by God exalted be He to abide therein — those are the worst of creatures.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate fate of those who reject God's message?
How do polytheists and disbelievers from the People of the Book end up in Hell?
What is the nature of the punishment for idolaters?
propositions: Those who disbelieve from the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell.
The disbelievers from among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters shall be in the fire of Hell.
It will be decreed for them by God to abide therein.

source_text:
Verse: Indeed, those who believe and do good—they are the best of ˹all˺ beings.

Tafsir: Truly those who believe and perform righteous deeds — they are the best of creatures al-bariyya means al-khalīqa.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be the best of beings?
How do righteous deeds impact one's status in Islam?
Can faith and good actions guarantee a high standing in the afterlife?
propositions: Those who believe are the best of beings.
Believing and performing righteous deeds are essential for being considered the best of creatures.
The term 'al-bariyya' refers to God's creation, emphasizing the importance of faith and good actions.

source_text:
Verse: Their reward with their Lord will be Gardens of Eternity, under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. This is ˹only˺ for those in awe of their Lord.

Tafsir: Their reward with their Lord will be Gardens of Eden as a residence underneath which rivers flow wherein they shall abide forever. God is pleased with them because of their obedience of Him and they are pleased with Him because of His reward. That is the reward for him who fears his Lord for him who fears His punishment and hence desists from disobeying Him exalted be He.

hype_questions: What is the ultimate reward for those who fear their Lord?
How does God's pleasure relate to human obedience?
What motivates someone to desist from disobeying their Lord?
propositions: Their reward with their Lord will be Gardens of Eternity.
Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him.
God is pleased with them because of their obedience of Him.
They are pleased with Him because of His reward.
That is the reward for him who fears his Lord.
Hence desists from disobeying Him exalted be He.

source_text:
Verse: When the earth is shaken ˹in˺ its ultimate quaking,

Tafsir: When earth is shaken when it is rocked for the rising of the Hour with its final quake with its most violent rocking one that befits its magnitude

hype_questions: What is the Hour?
How will the earth behave during the final quake?
What magnitude of shaking can be expected?
propositions: The Earth will experience its ultimate quaking.
The Hour is approaching, causing the earth to rock violently.
The earth's final quake will be a violent one that matches its magnitude.

source_text:
Verse: and when the earth throws out ˹all˺ its contents,

Tafsir: and the earth brings forth its burdens its hidden treasures and its dead casting them onto its surface

hype_questions: What will happen to the earth on the day of resurrection?
Will the earth be punished or rewarded?
How will the earth's contents be revealed on that day?
propositions: The earth will throw out all its contents.
The earth brings forth its burdens, hidden treasures, and dead to cast them onto its surface.

source_text:
Verse: and humanity cries, “What is wrong with it?”—

Tafsir: and man the disbeliever in resurrection says ‘What is wrong with it?’ — in denial of that situation.

hype_questions: Does the concept of resurrection exist?
Is it possible to deny the reality of resurrection?
What are the consequences of denying the existence of resurrection?
propositions: Humanity is in a state of distress and questioning.
A person who disbelieves in resurrection is in denial of its reality.
The concept of resurrection is a fundamental aspect of human existence.

source_text:
Verse: on that Day the earth will recount everything,

Tafsir: On that day yawma’idhin substitutes for and is the response to idhā ‘when’ it shall relate its chronicles it shall inform of the good and evil deeds committed in it

hype_questions: What will be the earth's account on the Day of Judgment?
How will the earth relate its chronicles on that day?
What deeds will the earth inform about on that day?
propositions: The earth will recount everything on the Day of Judgment.
Yawma'idhin substitutes for and is the response to 'when'.
The earth shall relate its chronicles, informing of good and evil deeds committed in it.

source_text:
Verse: having been inspired by your Lord ˹to do so˺.

Tafsir: for its Lord will have inspired it that is He will have commanded her to do this — in a hadīth it is stated ‘It the earth shall testify to every single deed committed by every servant and handmaiden upon its surface’.

hype_questions: Will the earth testify to every single deed committed by every servant and handmaiden?
What is the significance of a hadīth stating that the earth shall testify to every single deed?
How does this verse relate to the concept of accountability?
propositions: The Lord inspired someone to do something.
The Lord commanded someone to do something.
The earth will testify to every single deed committed by every servant and handmaiden.

source_text:
Verse: On that Day people will proceed in separate groups to be shown ˹the consequences of˺ their deeds.

Tafsir: On that day mankind shall issue forth they will depart from the site of the Reckoning in separate groups divided up so that those taking it their book by the right hand will go to Paradise while those taking it by the left hand will go to the Fire to be shown their deeds that is the requital for them in either Paradise or the Fire.

hype_questions: What happens to individuals after they pass away?
How are people judged on their deeds in the afterlife?
What is the ultimate destination for those who follow a righteous path?
propositions: On that Day, mankind will depart from the site of the Reckoning.
Those taking their book by the right hand will go to Paradise.
Those taking their book by the left hand will go to the Fire.

source_text:
Verse: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it.

Tafsir: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good shall see it he shall see its reward

hype_questions: What happens if I do a small act of kindness?
How will I be rewarded for my good actions?
Can doing good things bring me benefits?
propositions: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.
Doing good deeds will result in seeing its reward.

source_text:
Verse: And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.

Tafsir: and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil shall see it he shall see its requital.

hype_questions: What happens if I do a small amount of good or bad?

propositions: Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.
The act of doing an atom's weight of evil is equivalent to seeing its requital.

source_text:
Verse: ’ By the galloping, panting horses,

Tafsir: By the chargers the steeds that charge in attack and snort with a snorting — this being the name of the sound which they emit from inside them when they charge;

hype_questions: What is the name of the sound horses make when charging?
How do horses prepare to charge?
Why do horses snort when they are about to attack?
propositions: The steeds that charge in attack emit a specific sound.
This sound is called the 'name' of the sound which they emit from inside them when they charge.
Horses prepare to charge by charging
Horses snort when they are about to attack

source_text:
Verse: striking sparks of fire ˹with their hoofs˺,

Tafsir: by the strikers the steeds that strike fire by way of sparks with their hoofs when they gallop across rocky terrain by night;

hype_questions: What is the phenomenon that occurs when horses gallop across rocky terrain at night?
How do horses strike fire by way of sparks with their hoofs?

propositions: Horses strike fire by way of sparks with their hoofs when they gallop across rocky terrain at night.
The steeds that strike fire are those that gallop across rocky terrain by night.
Striking sparks of fire refers to the phenomenon of horses striking fire by way of sparks with their hoofs.

source_text:
Verse: launching raids at dawn,

Tafsir: by the dawn-raiders the steeds that make raids against the enemy at dawn at the hands of their riders

hype_questions: What are the dawn-raiders?
Who makes raids against the enemy at dawn?
At what time do the steeds make raids against the enemy?
propositions: The steeds that make raids against the enemy at dawn are called dawn-raiders.
Raids against the enemy at dawn are made by their riders.
Dawn-raiders are the ones who make raids against the enemy.

source_text:
Verse: stirring up ˹clouds of˺ dust,

Tafsir: raising stirring up therein in the place of their charge or at that time of dawn a trail of dust by the power of their movement

hype_questions: What is stirring up in the clouds?
How does the movement create a trail of dust?
Why is the dust being raised?
propositions: The clouds are filled with dust.
Their movement creates a trail of dust.
Dust is being stirred up by their movement.

source_text:
Verse: and penetrating into the heart of enemy lines!

Tafsir: cleaving therewith with the dust a host of the enemy that is to say cutting right into their centre! the verb is supplemented to the noun in the above instances because it serves to explain the verbal action in other words wa’llātī ‘adawna fa-awrayna fa-agharna ‘by those that charge then strike sparks then raid’.

hype_questions: What is the effect of penetrating into enemy lines?
How does the verb 'cleaving' relate to the noun 'dust' in this context?
What does it mean to strike sparks and raid?
propositions: Penetrating into enemy lines has a significant impact on their military strategy.
The verb 'cleaving' is used to explain the action of cutting through the dust, which serves as a supplement to the noun.
Those who charge and strike sparks are likely to raid enemy positions.

source_text:
Verse: Surely humankind is ungrateful to their Lord—

Tafsir: Verily man the disbeliever is ungrateful to his Lord thankless denying the reality of His graces exalted be He

hype_questions: What is the nature of ungratefulness towards one's Lord?
How does disbelief affect an individual's relationship with their Lord?

propositions: Humankind is ungrateful to their Lord.
The disbeliever is ungrateful to his Lord due to denial of His graces.
Man is ungrateful to his Lord because of his disbelief.

source_text:

propositions: He is a witness bearing witness against himself to his own actions.
Ingratitude leads to self-witness.
One's own actions can be a witness against them.

source_text:

hype_questions: What happens when one prioritizes material gain over spiritual growth?

source_text:
Verse: Do they not know that when the contents of the graves will be spilled out,

Tafsir: Does he not know that when that which is in the graves in the way of the dead is strewn when it is turned over and brought out that is to say that when they are raised

hype_questions: What happens when the contents of the graves are spilled out?
How do the dead come back to life?
What is meant by 'the way of the dead'?
propositions: The contents of the graves will be spilled out.
That which is in the graves, in the way of the dead, will be strewn when it is turned over and brought out.
When they are raised

source_text:
Verse: and the secrets of the hearts will be laid bare—

Tafsir: and that which is in the breasts the hearts of disbelief or faith is obtained when it is revealed and examined

hype_questions: What happens to our inner selves when God reveals the truth?

propositions: The secrets of the heart will be revealed.
Faith or disbelief is obtained when it is revealed and examined.
God examines the hearts to determine whether they are filled with faith or disbelief.

source_text:
Verse: surely their Lord is All-Aware of them on that Day.

Tafsir: on that day their Lord will indeed be Aware of them Knower of them and will requite them for their disbelief the pronoun reverts to the plural because of the collective import of the term ‘man’; this sentence indicates the direct object of the verb ya‘lamu ‘does he not know’ that is to say ‘We will requite him at the time mentioned’; khabīrun ‘Aware’ is semantically connected to yawma’idhin ‘on that day’ even though in fact God is ever Aware because that is the Day of Requital.

hype_questions: Will Allah be aware of our deeds on the day of reckoning?
What is the nature of Allah's awareness on that day?
How will Allah requite us for our disbelief?
propositions: Their Lord is All-Aware of them on that Day.
Their Lord will indeed be Aware of them, Knower of them, and will requite them for their disbelief.
God is ever Aware because that is the Day of Requital.

source_text:
Verse: The Striking Disaster!

Tafsir: The Clattering Blow the Resurrection that will make hearts clatter by its terrors.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Resurrection?
How will the Resurrection affect human hearts?
What terrors can be expected on the Day of Judgment?
propositions: The Resurrection is a striking disaster.
It will bring about a clattering blow.
Hearts will be affected by its terrors.

source_text:
Verse: What is the Striking Disaster?

Tafsir: What is the Clattering Blow? — intended to emphasise its awesomeness mā’l-qāri‘a both of these elements constitute a subject and a predicate and together the predicate of the first al-qāri‘a.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Striking Disaster?
How does the Clattering Blow relate to the Striking Disaster?
What significance does the al-qāri‘a hold in understanding the Striking Disaster?
propositions: The Striking Disaster refers to a significant event.
The Clattering Blow is an intense and awe-inspiring phenomenon.
Al-qāri‘a serves as a crucial element in describing the Striking Disaster.

source_text:
Verse: And what will make you realize what the Striking Disaster is?

Tafsir: And what will show you what will make known to you what the Clattering Blow is? — additional emphasis of its awesomeness the first mā is a subject and what follows it is its predicate; the second mā and its predicate also function together as the second direct object of the verb adrā ‘show’.

hype_questions: What is the nature of the Striking Disaster?
How will it be revealed to us?
What is the significance of the Clattering Blow?
propositions: The Striking Disaster will be realized through a specific event.
The Clattering Blow will be shown to us through a demonstration of its power.
The first mā serves as the subject, and the second mā functions as the direct object of the verb adrā.

source_text:
Verse: ˹It is˺ the Day people will be like scattered moths,

Tafsir: The day yawma that which renders it accusative is the verb indicated by al-qāri‘a in other words by the implied taqra‘u ‘it clatters’ mankind will be like scattered moths like a throng of scattered locusts surging into each other in confusion until they are summoned to the Reckoning

hype_questions: What will be the state of humanity on Judgment Day?
How will people behave during the final reckoning?

propositions: The Day of Reckoning is near.
Mankind will be like scattered moths on the Day of Judgment.
People will surge into each other in confusion until they are summoned to account for their deeds.

source_text:
Verse: and the mountains will be like carded wool.

Tafsir: and the mountains will be like tufts of wool like carded wool in terms of the lightness with which it floats in the air until it comes to settle upon the earth.

hype_questions: Will mountains be like carded wool?

propositions: The mountains will float in the air.
The mountains will settle upon the earth.
Carded wool is very light.

Faith grows through prioritizing good deeds over bad ones.

source_text:
Verse: they will be in a life of bliss.

propositions.text: His home will be the Abyss.

source_text:

source_text:

propositions: You will visit your graves either at the time of your death and burial or to the extent that you consider the dead as equals.

source_text:

propositions: You will come to know.
No indeed!
a disavowal.

source_text:

Verse: and ˹so will˺ his wife, the carrier of ˹thorny˺ kindling,

Tafsir: and his wife wa’mra’atuhu is a supplement to the person of the verb yaslā ‘he will enter’ separated by the clause of the direct object and its qualification — and this was Umm Jamīl — the carrier read hammālatu or hammālata of firewood cactus and thorns which she used to fling into the path of the Prophet s.

hype_questions: What was Umm Jamīl's role in the Prophet's life?
How did Umm Jamīl prepare firewood cactus and thorns for the Prophet?
Why is Umm Jamīl mentioned in this verse of the Quran?
propositions: His wife will be a companion to him.
She was carrying firewood cactus and thorns.
The Prophet s. encountered her on his journey.

source_text:
Verse: around her neck will be a rope of palm-fibre.

Tafsir: with a rope of palm-fibre around her neck fī jīdihā hablun min masadin is a circumstantial qualifier referring to hammālata’l-hatab which in turn is either a description of imra’atahu ‘his wife’ or the predicate of an implied subject.

hype_questions: Does a husband have any rights over his wife?
Can a wife be described as 'his wife' in a literal sense?
What does the phrase 'a rope of palm-fibre around her neck' imply about marriage?
propositions: A rope made of palm-fibre is placed around a woman's neck.
The term 'hammālata’l-hatab' refers to a wife in a literal sense.
Marriage involves the concept of ownership and control.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “He is Allah—One ˹and Indivisible˺;

Tafsir: Say ‘He is God One Allāhu is the predicate of huwa ‘He is’ and ahadun is its substitution or a second predicate.

hype_questions: What does it mean to be one and indivisible?
How does the concept of tawhid relate to Islamic theology?
What is the significance of using 'Allah' as a predicate in Arabic?
propositions: He is Allah
Allah is One
Allah is Indivisible

source_text:
Verse: Allah—the Sustainer ˹needed by all˺.

Tafsir: God the Self-Sufficient Besought of all Allāhu’l-samad constitute a subject and a predicate al-samad means the One Who is always sought at times of need

hype_questions: What does it mean to be self-sufficient?
How does Allah's self-sufficiency relate to human need?
Can humans ever be completely self-sufficient like Allah?
propositions: Allah is the Sustainer needed by all.
Al-samad means the One Who is always sought at times of need.

source_text:
Verse: He has never had offspring, nor was He born.

Tafsir: He neither begot for no likeness of Him can exist nor was begotten since createdness is precluded in His case.

hype_questions: What is the nature of Allah's creation?
Can anything be compared to Allah?
Is Allah's existence dependent on something else?
propositions: Allah has never had offspring.
Allah was not born.
Nothing like Allah can exist.
Allah was not begotten.

source_text:
Verse: And there is none comparable to Him.”

Tafsir: Nor is there anyone equal to Him’ neither match nor comparison lahu ‘to Him’ is semantically connected to kufuwan ‘equal’ but precedes it because it is the object of the intended negation; ahadun ‘anyone’ which is the subject of yakun ‘is there’ has been placed after the predicate of the latter kufuwan ‘equal’ in order to retain the harmony of the end-rhyme of the verses.

hype_questions: What is the nature of God's uniqueness?
How does the Quran emphasize God's oneness?
What implications does this concept have for Islamic theology?
propositions: There is no one comparable to God.
God is not equal to anyone or anything.
The concept of God's uniqueness is a fundamental aspect of Islamic theology.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak

Tafsir: Say ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak the morning

hype_questions: What is the significance of seeking refuge in Allah?
How does seeking refuge in Allah relate to patience and salah?
What is the Lord of the Daybreak in Islamic context?
propositions: The Prophet seeks refuge in Allah, the Lord of the daybreak.
Seeking refuge in Allah is a form of patience.
Allah is the Lord of the Daybreak.

source_text:
Verse: from the evil of whatever He has created,

Tafsir: from the evil of what He has created of obligated animate beings and non-obligated ones and from all inanimates such as poison and so on;

hype_questions: What is the source of evil in creation?
How does Allah define 'evil' in His creation?
Can inanimate objects be considered 'evil'?
propositions: Allah has created something that contains evil.
The evil in creation refers to obligated and non-obligated animate beings, as well as inanimates such as poison.

source_text:
Verse: and from the evil of the night when it grows dark,

Tafsir: and from the evil of darkness when it gathers that is from night when it becomes dark and the moon when it is absent

hype_questions: What happens to darkness when it gathers?
How does night become dark?
What is the effect of the moon's absence on darkness?
propositions: Darkness grows when it gathers.
Night becomes dark when it grows dark.
The moon's absence causes darkness to grow.

source_text:
Verse: and from the evil of those ˹witches casting spells by˺ blowing onto knots,

Tafsir: and from the evil of the women-blowers sorceresses who blow on knots which they knot into strings blowing into them certain words but without spittle; however al-Zamakhsharī says ‘with this spittle’ — sorceresses such as the daughters of the said Labīd —

hype_questions: What is sorcery?
How do women use sorcery in Islam?
Who are the daughters of Labīd?
propositions: Sorceresses blow on knots to cast spells.
The knots are tied into strings and blown into with certain words but without spittle.
Al-Zamakhsharī says that sorceresses use spittle in their spells.

source_text:
Verse: and from the evil of an envier when they envy.”

Tafsir: and from the evil of an envier when he envies’ when he manifests his envy and behaves in accordance with it — such as the mentioned Labīd from among the Jews who were envious of the Prophet s; the mention of these three elements of evil which are already subsumed by the statement ‘of what He has created’ is because of the severity of their evil.

hype_questions: What are the consequences of envy in a person's life?
How does envy affect one's behavior and relationships?
Can envy lead to severe evil actions?
propositions: The evil of an envier is from the evil of envy.
When someone manifests his envy, he behaves in accordance with it.
Labīd was envious of the Prophet s.

source_text:
Verse: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I seek refuge in the Lord of humankind,

Tafsir: Say ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind their Creator and their Possessor they mankind have been singled out for mention here in order to honour them and a preface to seeking refuge from the evil of the one who whispers in their hearts;

hype_questions: What is the significance of seeking refuge in the Lord of mankind?
How does the concept of being singled out for mention relate to honouring individuals?
What is the purpose of a preface in seeking refuge from evil thoughts?
propositions: The Prophet seeks refuge in the Lord of mankind.
The Lord of mankind is their Creator and Possessor.
Mankind has been singled out for mention to honour them.
Seeking refuge is a preface to avoiding the evil of one's heart.

source_text:
Verse: the Master of humankind,

Tafsir: the King of mankind

hype_questions: What is the title given to Allah in Islam?
Who is considered the ruler of humanity in Islamic theology?
What is the name of Allah's role as the supreme authority in human life?
propositions: Allah is referred to as the Master of humankind.
The King of mankind is a title given to Allah in Islamic theology.

source_text:
Verse: the God of humankind,

Tafsir: the God of mankind both maliki’l-nās and ilāhi’l-nās are either substitutions or adjectival qualifications or explicative supplements; the repetition of the annexed word al-nās is meant as an additional explication

hype_questions: What does it mean to be the God of mankind?
How do the terms maliki’l-nās and ilāhi’l-nās relate to each other?
What is the significance of the repetition of al-nās in this context?
propositions: The God of mankind refers to a single entity.
Maliki’l-nās and ilāhi’l-nās are either substitutions or adjectival qualifications for the same concept.
The repetition of al-nās is an additional explication meant to clarify its meaning.

source_text:
Verse: from the evil of the lurking whisperer—

Tafsir: from the evil of the slinking whisperer Satan — he is referred to by the name of the action waswasa on account of his repeated engaging in it — who slinks away and recoils from the heart whenever God is mentioned

hype_questions: What is the name of Satan's action that he is referred to by?
How does Satan behave when God is mentioned?
Why is Satan referred to as 'the slinking whisperer'?
propositions: Satan is referred to by the name of the action waswasa.
Satan slinks away and recoils from the heart whenever God is mentioned.

source_text:
Verse: who whispers into the hearts of humankind—

Tafsir: who whispers in the breasts of mankind in their hearts — whenever they neglect to remember God

hype_questions: What is it that whispers to humans?
Who or what is responsible for reminding humans of their creator?
How can humans ensure they never forget about God?
propositions: There exists a thing that whispers in the hearts of humans.
Humans are prone to neglecting their remembrance of Allah.
Neglecting one's remembrance of Allah has consequences.

source_text:
Verse: from among jinn and humankind.”

Tafsir: of the jinn and mankind’ mina’l-jinnati wa’l-nāsi an explication for the whispering Satan being of the jinn and also of the humans similar to God’s saying the devils of humans and jinn Q. 6112; or mina’l-jinnati ‘of the jinn’ is an explication for him Satan wa’l-nāsi ‘and of mankind’ being a supplement to al-waswās ‘the whisperer’. Both explanations apply to the evil of the mentioned Labīd and his daughters; the objection to the first opinion is that humans do not ‘whisper’ in the hearts of other humans but that it is the jinn who whisper in their hearts I would respond by saying that human beings also ‘whisper’ in a manner appropriate to them beginning externally whereafter their whispers reach the heart and establish themselves in it in the way in which this customarily happens. But God knows best what is correct and to Him shall be the return and the final destination and may God bless our Master Muhammad and his family and Companions and grant them all much peace forever and always. God suffices for us and what an excellent guardian is He! And there is no power or might except in God the Sublime the Tremendous.

hype_questions: Does Satan whisper in the hearts of humans?
Can humans also 'whisper' in a manner appropriate to them?
What is the nature of the evil mentioned in the verse?
propositions: Satan is of the jinn and mankind.
The devils of humans and jinn are similar to God's saying.
Humans do not 'whisper' in the hearts of other humans, but it is the jinn who whisper in their hearts.
Human beings also 'whisper' in a manner appropriate to them beginning externally.
God knows best what is correct and to Him shall be the return and the final destination.
